Ascending the hall, the mountain monk was reading the "Golden Lion Chapter" of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, specifically the ninth section, "The Door of Skillful Accomplishment through the Turning of the Mind.
It further explains: "It is like a mirror one foot square that reflects myriad images in successive layers. If this is so, one may say it exists; one may say it does not exist;
one may say it is neither; one may say it is both. Nevertheless, even though this is so, one must still..."
Know that there is a single aperture at the top of the staff. If you do not understand this, the staff will pass through the lanterns and enter the Buddha hall;
it will strike Śākyamuni and knock Maitreya over, while the pillar claps its hands and laughs out loud. Now tell me: what do you say?
"What are you laughing at? He struck the meditation staff and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he held up the meditation staff and said: "Panshan said, 'The path leading upward is slippery. Nanyuan said, 'It is as precipitous as a thousand-fathom cliff.
Linji said, 'Stone sparks and lightning are dull. Yangshan had a phrase that settles heaven and earth. Each of them..."
"Keep your eyes open! Keep your eyes open! [The Master] strikes the meditation staff and descends from the seat.

Compiled by Xingyue of Loudong, Abbot of Lian’an Chan Temple at the Eighteen Gullies in Wulin.
Based on the lecture hall discourse of Chan Master Dagu Zhi: “Dagu received the Great Hero’s grandson; the cloud-and-water travelers from the Five Lakes vie for precedence.”
Rushing! They rush headlong in competition. What gate is there? Striking the arrow, how could one know that withered wood remains? That withered wood remains;
in one year, it has indeed seen spring twice. Spring twice; pearls from within the curtains are scattered to others. Scattered to others;
even upon reflection, this is merely a longing for Western Qin.

Ascending the hall: A single strike rings out with crystalline clarity; its thunderous resonance pervades the universe. As soon as those who know the sound tilt their ears, it is like Xiang Yu crossing the river to the east.
To understand it in such a way is precisely to mistake the bridge of a donkey’s saddle for one's father’s chin.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Vertically exhausting the three periods of time and horizontally pervading the ten directions—when picked up, even Śakra is startled;
when set down, even the Earth Deity trembles with fear. When neither picked up nor set down, what do you call it? He himself replied: "A frog."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know it exists; the cat and the white ox, however, do know it exists.
He then picked up his whisk and said, "The cat and the white ox are both here, emitting light and shaking the earth. Why is this so?
Because there are two distinct parts."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Standing in ranks at the bottom of the great ocean, the second from the front has graying hair.
Why does he not say that the first has graying hair? Do you understand? Golden stamens and silver filaments form the jade dew; the eminent monk does not sit upon the Phoenix Terrace."
Ascending the hall, when the assembly had gathered, he said: "To exert oneself for the sake of the multitude brings calamity to one's private door.

He then descended from his seat. He addressed the assembly, holding up the incense case and saying: "It fits at the bright end; it fits at the dark end. If you can speak thus, you may roam freely throughout the world.
If you cannot speak thus, then close it and descend from your seats. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To find no oil in the sand is a pitiable matter; Cuiyan chews his rice and feeds it to an infant.
When you understand the root of good and evil at that time, you will realize for the first time that your face was once covered in dust. He struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall.

Chan Master Fahua Ju ascended the hall and said: "If Śākyamuni had not appeared in the world and Bodhidharma had not come from the West, the Buddha-dharma would pervade the world, yet no one would open their mouths to discuss the profound mystery."
Ascending the hall: The bells toll and the drums resound; the magpies chirp and the crows caw. For all of you, I have already expounded upon Prajñā and lectured on Nirvāṇa.
Do you believe this? Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva manifests great supernatural powers right before you.
If you cannot believe it, he will depart for other realms to save sentient beings from suffering and benefit their lives.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To open one's mouth is to produce redundant words; not to open one's mouth is to produce superfluous words.
He then added: "The decree of the Golden Wheel Emperor: the house style of the thatched shop is unique."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Buddhas of the three periods have their mouths hung upon the wall. How can the old monks throughout the land find a place to set their hands?
When you all go to various places, how will you bring this up? My speaking thus is merely the result of long-standing habituation;
my lips have grown accustomed to it. He let out a shout.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients said, 'If I were to exclusively exalt the religious teachings, the grass in the Dharma Hall would grow a fathom deep.
Yet, one cannot lock the gate of the monks' hall for you, O *śrāmaṇera*.
Even so, it is like a tortoise playing with dust on dry land."
Ascending the hall, he said: "To speak of the gradual is to return to the ordinary and accord with the Way; to discuss the sudden is to leave no trace behind.
Even if one were to discuss the sudden and return to the ordinary, this would still be a matter of forcing it."
Chan Master Fushan Yuan ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas appear in the world and establish gates of transformation, yet they do not depart from the wisdom-eye of the three bodies (*trikāya*).

It is like the three eyes of Maheśvara: for what reason? One eye is so tightly sealed that not even a drop of water can pass through, making it difficult for the ordained and the laity to distinguish;

one eye is fully open across the great earth, with the ten directions flowing freely; and one eye takes a single glance at high and low alike, such that all myriad things are simultaneously perfected."
Zhan said: "Even so, if one is a monk of the fundamental division, only when meeting on a common road with another who possesses the extraordinary, heaven-penetrating true eye will it be possible.
Therefore it is said: 'The Buddhas of the three periods do not know what exists; the cat and the white ox, however, do know.
But tell me, what is it that the cat and the white ox know? Do you wish to understand? Deep autumn: rain upon the curtains of a thousand homes."
"The setting sun over the pavilions, a single flute in the wind.
Master Baoying Zhao ascended the hall and said: "Throughout the twelve periods of the day, I allow you one period of 'cessation of study'—this is precisely what it means to study the Buddha-dharma.
Have you not seen how Ānanda, though foremost in erudition, was nonetheless expelled by Kāśyapa and was not permitted to participate in the compilation of the scriptures?"
Only now do you realize that your cleverness, vast learning, memory, and conceptualization are outward-seeking pursuits;

they have no connection with the awakened, numinous mind. You cannot break through the shell of the five aggregates. When circumstances accord with your desires, you give rise to joy; when they oppose them, you give rise to anger. Covered by such profound layers, you entangle and bind yourself;
there is no liberation as you drift through the cycle of birth and death. The six sense faculties become a source of affliction, and manifold sufferings arise.
Being constrained by these, one has no freedom; yet the deluded mind presides over them as its master. A true man of great character should seize this opportunity early on.
(He lets out a shout and says: "Investigate! (Chán).
Ascending the hall: The Treasure Response Gate is fraught with peril; those who enter lose their entire bodies. What is the phrase for emerging?
If you cannot speak it, thirty years from now—
Chan Master Daguan Ying addressed the assembly, saying: "As soon as one involves the lips and palate, one falls into conceptual thought;

all such things are dead ends and none are living paths. Even if one manages to break through, one still remains within the depths of samsara. Do not let your lifelong efforts go to waste by vainly passing this life.
If you wish not to let your life be in vain, [take up the staff]—he struck it once—and said: 'You must simply not...'"
Only when you are deceived by this staff can you truly understand. Look! Look!
This staff pierces through the skulls of all of you and leaps right into your nostrils. (He strikes once more.)
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "The lineage of this mountain monk is distinct; I have already altered the tracks of all other quarters.

To extract the wedge from Mañjuśrī’s eyes, I instruct Samantabhadra to cease chewing the iron in his mouth. I urge you to loosen the hand that grips the slithering snake and, for you, I shall hew away the hitching post for the donkey.
If you pause to dwell upon it with calculation, I shout: 'Squeeze! Squeeze! Study!"
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "In my life, I have always been fond of sumo wrestling, yet I have found no one to match me.

Today, I shall wrestle with the Head Seat. Roll up your kashaya! He descended from his seat, challenged the Head Seat to a match, and as soon as the Seat stepped out, the Master said, "A fall on level ground! and returned to his quarters.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time are servants; the entire Great Canon of teachings is but snot and spittle. After a long silence, he asked:
"Tell me, whose servants are the Buddhas of the three periods? He then took his whisk and drew a line, saying: "The Buddhas of the three periods are on this side of the line.
He then asked: "Tell me, whose snot and spittle is the Great Canon? The Master then spat once himself.
Ascending the hall, he said: “The scale-weight suddenly floats to the bottom of the well; The old rat has been transformed into an ox for many years.
Hui-kong saw this and clapped his hands in laughter: ‘A three-legged monkey is more extraordinary than a common ape.’”
Ascending the hall, he said: "The five thousand scriptures are the constant discourse of all Buddhas; the eighty thousand afflictions are the wondrous function of sentient beings.
Yet even these are not yet the Vajra Eye. What is the Vajra Eye? After a long silence, he said: "Blind."

Ascending the hall, when the assembly had gathered and settled, a monk just as he stepped forward to prostrate, the Master said: "If you wish to understand the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should contemplate the conditions of time and season.
The monk then asked, "What are the conditions of time and season? The Master immediately descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "In other quarters, the hook is curved and the bait is fragrant; they swarm together like bees clustering around a queen.
Here in this Sage’s place, the hook is straight and there is no bait at all—it is like submerging a gourd in water. Raising his staff and making the gesture of fishing, he said:
"Taking fish from deep waters, one relies entirely on destiny; never have I offered wine to the River God. He then cast down the staff.

The Seat. Chan Master Danning Kuan ascended the hall and said: "The wondrous secret of Shaolin is the ancestral style of the Buddhas of antiquity. Its application adapts to conditions, unfolding and rolling up with effortless mastery.
It is like a fist becoming an open palm—the opening and closing occur at their own time; it is like water forming bubbles—arising and ceasing without fixed duration. Movement...
In stillness, speech and silence are both fully revealed; in the spontaneous manifestation of myriad functions, there is no need for mental exertion.
Reaching this point is called "letting the boat drift with the current. But tell me, who is the skilled hand that rows against the wind?
After a long pause, he said: "To play in the tide, one must be a player of the tide. With a shout, he said: "Take care!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Taking non-thought as the school, taking non-abiding as the foundation, taking true emptiness as the essence, and taking wondrous existence as the function.
Thus it is said: 'The entire earth is true emptiness; throughout the dharma-realm is wondrous existence. Now tell me, who is it that can employ this?
The four seasons operate, and the sun and moon shine eternally. The Dharma is fundamentally unchanging, and the Way has no fixed location. Following conditions, it manifests of itself."
Whether rising or sinking as one pursues external objects, or entering the state of ordinary beings or sages in this land or other realms—though it be so, tell me:
how do you express the phrase "entering the local customs"? After a long silence, he said: "The Sanskrit language of the Western Heavens; the Tang language of this land."
Chan Master Yunfeng Yue ascended the hall and said: "Carrying staff and wooden sounding-blocks wherever you go, you perform your play upon meeting the occasion.
Although this is so, one hand alone cannot clap. Is there among the assembly any masterful Chan guest or monk of the fundamental lineage who will come forth to join in this song?
Is there anyone? At that time, a monk came forward and bowed. The Master said: "Vague and indistinct, like a melody just barely worth hearing. Then he added: "Furthermore..."
Blown by the wind into a different tune, he immediately descended from his seat.
Entering the hall, he said: "The practice of Samantabhadra and the wisdom of Mañjuśrī—on Mount Potalaka a pure breeze arises; a blind donkey follows the herd and encounters Silla.
The tongue of the Jiaoliao extends three thousand li."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "Holding the alms bowl toward the world of Fragrant Accumulation—why is there no way to emerge?
Carrying the sun and moon upon the tip of the staff—why are those with eyes as if blind?

Even when it reaches the point where the wind blows and the grass bows, where the resonance follows the sound and harmony prevails, leaving not even a speck of dust behind—this is still a dharma of contention. What is it?"
"Birth is a dharma that does not involve contention. [The Master] struck the meditation staff and descended from his seat.
He ascended the hall and said: "In the teachings it is said that all various forms of grasping and rejecting are samsara.

To attempt to discern Perfect Enlightenment without having escaped samsara is for that nature of Perfect Enlightenment to be identical with the cycle of transmigration; there is no such possibility. You all..."
When people arrive here, how do they discern Perfect Enlightenment? After a long silence, he said: "The lotus leaf is round and round, as round as a mirror;
the water chestnut is pointed and pointed, as pointed as an awl. He then struck the meditation seat with his whisk.
Chan Master Dazheng Zun ascended the hall and said: "Those who come up do not question; those who go down do not doubt. I do not know whether this is so or not.
If it is so, then it is truly marvelous. He then descended from his seat.

Chan Master Zhenshou Renshou ascended the hall and said: "Clearly and brightly there is no awakening; to have a dharma is itself delusion. When the sun rises without clouds, it shines beautifully upon the heavens;
when there is no film before the eyes, space is fundamentally free of flowers. Do not speak erroneously before those without wisdom. Investigate!"
Cuiyan Zhen Chan Master ascended the hall and said: "The former sages said that this matter is like cracking a tortoise shell to see its pattern.

If it cracks, a sign is formed; if it does not crack, it remains dull. Whether it cracks or not, one must grasp it directly and immediately. At Shanglan, however, it is otherwise: there is no fixedness and no necessity.
It is like horses running through empty space or boats sailing on dry land; clouds rise on the South Mountain and rain falls on the North Mountain. He then took up his staff.
The staff said: "This walking staff transforms into a Celestial Great General to patrol the four continents. There are those who maintain their integrity and those who do not;
there are those with virtuous conduct and those without. He reports all this at once to Śakra-devānām-indra, and then lets out a shout."
A man of spirit naturally possesses the will to pierce the heavens; do not walk where the Tathāgata has walked.
*He strikes once.* He ascends the hall and cites the verse of Longya: "Studying the Way is like drilling for fire: When smoke appears, do not yet cease.
Only when the golden star manifests Will you have reached home at last. Shending said: "Studying the Way is like drilling for fire: When smoke appears, one should immediately cease."

"Do not wait for the appearance of the morning star; you will burn your feet and then your head. The Master said, "If we speak of the sudden (sudden enlightenment), Longya is still only halfway there.
If we speak of the gradual, Shending still lacks full realization.
As for this matter, what then? O worthy ones, this year there are many fallen leaves; at how many places will they be swept back home?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "To resist the enemy on the battlefield without fear of life or death is the courage of a general.
To enter the mountains without fear of tigers and rhinoceroses is the courage of a hunter. To enter the waters without fear of crocodiles and dragons is the courage of a fisherman."
"What is the courage of a patch-robed monk? Holding up his staff, he said, "This is the staff.
If you can pick it up, hold it, and move it, the three thousandfold world-system will shake all at once.
If you cannot pick it up, cannot hold it, and cannot move it, then Mañjuśrī remains Mañjuśrī and liberation remains liberation. Study!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an anecdote: A monk asked Baling, "What is the Way? Baling said, "A person with clear eyes falls into a well.
Again, a monk asked Baoying, "What is the Way? Baoying said, "Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion. Again, a monk asked Shoushan, "What is the Way?"
Mountain said, "Three feet deep beneath one's feet. These are three turning words: one phrase stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high; one phrase is rowing a boat on dry land;
one phrase is the mutual interpenetration of guest and host. Is there anyone among you who can discern them? Come forward and speak!
If there is none, then practice the compassion of an Arhat to destroy the thieves of the fetters; practice the compassion of a Bodhisattva to bring peace to all sentient beings.
Practice the Tathāgata’s compassion, for you have attained the Suchness of phenomena.
Zen Master Wuquan Zheng ascended the hall: "At the Huangmei assembly, there were a thousand monks; the one who received the Dharma and transmitted the robe was the laborer at the mill.

If this is so, it is like the red sun rising in the west; if not, it is like the lunar disc ascending in the east. Examine!"* *Note: This is a classic Zen koan concerning the identity of the person who received the Sixth Patriarch's robe.*
Chan Master Shuangfeng Hui addressed the assembly: "A man from South India sails upon a boat; a man from the north of the Great Wall brandishes his lances.
A Persian enters the Great Tang; Mount Sumeru performs a dance. What kind of talk is this?"
Chan Master Daowu Zhen ascended the hall and said: "The sun and moon of ancient and modern times are as they were; the mountains and rivers remain as they are.
If you can understand this, then the Buddhas of the ten directions all share the single path to Nirvana. If you cannot understand it, you slander this sutra and shall incur such retribution."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The lion cub roars; the dragon-horse colt leaps and bounds. The mirror of the ancient buddhas is bright; the solitary moon over the three peaks is radiant.
He then performed a dance and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he raised [the precedent] of Dongshan’s saying: “On Mount Wutai, clouds steam rice; before the steps of the Buddha Hall, it is a dog-urine sky;
atop the flagpole, a hammer is being fried; three monkeys winnow coins at night. The Old Monk says it is not so:
“The three-faced marten treads upon the moon; The two-headed white ox grasps smoke in its paws; A crowned blue hare stands upon the courtyard cypress.”
The shelled turtle has shed its skin and flown into the sky. This old monk’s tangles have all been seen through by you people.
The old man Dongshan was truly extraordinary; nevertheless, he could only manage three or four steps, and did not go beyond seven jumps and eight leaps.
Tell me, where does the crux lie? Today, this old monk will not begrudge [his life].
He gave away his eyebrows all at once. After a long while, he said: "Repeated entreaties only diminish one's virtue; silence truly achieves merit.
Let the vast ocean change as it may, I shall never speak for you."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The ancients said, 'If you recognize it, as before it is not. This is truly difficult to understand. The soil-dweller has a profusion of beard and whiskers beneath his chin;
the Persian has deep-set eyes and large nostrils. How extraordinary! In a sudden flash, he has passed through the borders of Silla."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The wheat ripens before the mountain; the price of rice in Luling; the radishes of Zhenzhou—and yet there is something more. After a long silence, he said:
"At times one gathers wild greens and boils them with their roots; at times one hews fresh firewood and burns it with its leaves."
Ascending the hall: Puhua’s striking in the light and striking in the dark;布袋 (Baidai) scattering horizontally and scattering vertically;
the Stone Chamber Attendant treading the pestle—why has he forgotten how to set his foot down?
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an old case: A monk asked Shoushan, "What is the Buddha? Shoushan said, "The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it.
The Master said: "Hand in hand with the nose-ring, foot on the tail; looking up at the sky, listening to the flowing water;
at daybreak, sent out by the roadside; when night falls, returning to the thatched hut."
Chan Master Baizhang Zheng ascended the hall and said: "Master Yantou paid three copper coins to obtain a wife;
she only knew how to dredge for shrimp and clams, yet she did not know how to give birth to sons or raise daughters. To this very day, her lineage has been cut off.
If you, the assembly, wish to recognize Master Huo’s wife, today Baizhang will not begrudge his lips and teeth to show you all."
People’s commentaries have shattered it. Wild hair and thorn-bridle hairpins are rare in this world; the coarse cloth skirt is still the dress from her wedding day.
Chan Master Daowei Qian ascended the hall: “Mountain flowers are like brocade—Mañjuśrī has struck his eyes.
Deep birds warble—Avalokiteśvara has blocked his ears. You worthy ones, what more is there to contemplate? Last night at the third watch...”
"I could not sleep. Turning over in bed, I seized Puxian and banished him to the Land of Non-arising. One stretch of consciousness lasted until dawn.
This morning, I have again met you all to speak of my dream. Alas! What kind of talk is this? He struck his staff on the ground and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Guangfayuan ascended the hall and said: "If you discuss this matter, do not speak of it at all; to speak of it is to give rise to horns.
A monk stepped forward and said, "Horns have arisen! The Master said, "A calamity! The monk said, "I am at fault.
The Master said, "A dragon's head with a snake's tail. "Please take care," he added.
Chan Master Dinghui Xian ascended the hall and said: "If you recognize prajñā, you are bound by prajñā;
if you do not recognize prajñā, you are also bound by prajñā. Setting aside both recognition and non-recognition, I ask you all:
what is the essence of prajñā? Go to the meditation hall and investigate."
Ascending the hall: A clay snake bites a stone tortoise; the incense burner pillar chirps and squeaks. A blow is struck upon Mount Sumeru;
Old Yama laughs heartily. *Chan*. Ascending the hall:
The song of the oriole fades; the sound of the cicada hastens. The turtle entering the water does not get its head wet. The egret flies into the reeds.
Flower clusters. The combined brilliance of snow and moon cannot compare to it.

HŪṂ. Master Chan Shi Fang of Jiangshan ascends the hall: "Passing through clouds but not crossing waters; crossing waters but not passing through clouds. Holding fast to heaven and earth yet not holding them fast;
letting emptiness go forth yet not letting it go forth. Horizontal threes and vertical fours, parting and joining again and again. Taking this up—
"Lengthening the long to compensate for the short" does not concern you people. "The rice is made from grain"—this one phrase is difficult to speak of.
After a long silence, he said: "Private matters cannot be recompensed by official means."
Ascending the hall, he said: "It is not that one can speak of it or cannot speak of it; everywhere people take this to be something extraordinary.
Hanshan burns fire and his head is full of ash, yet Fenggan laughs and reviles him as an old thief."
Chan Master Bailu Duan ascended the hall and said: "Kāśyapa Matanga entering the Han was like carving a sore upon flesh; Zhu Fashang coming to Wu was like adding grit to one's eyes.
Bodhidharma sitting in wall-contemplation for nine years was the origin of a demonic specter; the Second Patriarch standing in the snow seeking his mind ended up becoming undisciplined.
When you all arrive here, how will you express yourselves? If you can speak it, then [you shall be] beyond the seas."
He walked across. When he found no way through, he lay alone among the trees and struck the meditation seat once with his staff.
Master Fuyan Zong ascended the hall and said: "When the World-Honored One took seven steps, his lifting of his feet was entirely contrary [to the Way].

When he looked toward the four quarters, he encountered obstructions at every turn. The golden robe was passed on, bringing calamity upon descendants; the jade verses were transmitted, hanging from people's lips."
Kissing [the moon]: the wind-blown banner reveals that awakening-nature has not yet departed from the dust of form. Dropping a needle into the bowl-water is entirely a limited perspective.
The Patriarch sat facing the wall for nine years without seeing so much as a hair’s breadth; Master Lu transmitted the robe through six generations seeking only minor gain.

The "Single Roar" of Jiangxi does not understand guarding the beginning; Deqiao’s total application does not know how to protect the end. Nanshan’s pointing at the turtle’s nose is but a vain indication of the tracks.
In the Northern Courtyard, withered pines vainly display their elegance; at Yunmen’s glance in the mirror, there is "two" and "three";
at Linji’s total upholding, there is "seven" and "eight. To speak of the five ranks of ruler and minister is like paper horses crossing a river;

to further push the mutual interpenetration of guest and host is just like a clay figure bathing. To transcend the realm of forms alone is not merely catching the hare or letting the hawk fly; it is to blend...

Within the traces of the mundane dust, you are no more than a dog gnawing at a pig—how is this any different from fleeing a pit only to fall into a ditch, or avoiding drowning only to throw oneself into a snare?
Such an understanding remains within the common run of things. How can one who is a man of the Way beyond the ordinary explain it?
Have you not seen that even the worldly fellow Tao Qian could perceive the situation and seize the opportune moment? Now, as descendants of the Patriarchal Hall, you must not merely be skin-deep.
"No blood. [He] lets out a shout.
Zen Master Jingyin Zhen ascends the hall and, holding up his staff, says: "This staff of jílù wood is well able to discourse on the Buddhas and patriarchs.
Since the deaf have now heard, even the mute understand speech. It points to white stone as jade; it transforms gold into..."
"Earth. If you understand it in such a way, you have not yet been granted permission by him. Since you have not been granted permission, do not be reckless.
"Beating the drum on the south street while dancing on the north street.

When National Teacher Neng of Mount Heng ascended the hall, as soon as the ancestral wind was raised, the clouds over ten thousand miles were cleared away; when the Dharma command was put into practice, [the myriad phenomena were revealed].
The color of the peaks is cold. Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, white waves surge to the heavens; amidst the billows of the great ocean, red dust fills the earth.

One should reflect upon Huangmei in days of yore and Shaoshi in former times: unable to yield to others, they were thus compelled to answer Huike’s resolve by pounding chaff and repay his heart by severing an arm.
How does this compare to the millet rice from the mountain fields here at Mount Heng—just a single bucket, without salt?
The soup: suffering and joy dwell together, following the high to reach the low. It is not a matter of buying at a high price in the south and selling at a low price in the north.
It is such that Mañjuśrī must bow his head and Kāśyapa knit his brows; Nāgārjuna and Aśvaghoṣa must swallow their voices and suppress their breath;
even Maudgalyāyana and Śāriputra could not do it for them. Why is this so? Observe closely the Dharma of the Dharma King; the Dharma of the Dharma King is just like this.
Stone Buddha Master Zhong ascended the hall and said: "When the time has not yet come, black and white are not yet distinguished;
when the time arrives, though one may point it out, it is like mixing mud with water. Let the pillar leap into the lantern for all you care, but why are your eyebrows trailing beneath your heels?
Even if you were to understand this clearly, it would still be like a monkey wearing a bamboo hat."
This point remains unclear; how is it any different from a crooked meal or a boot with holes? Nevertheless, those who laugh at me are many, while those who pity me are few.
Chan Master Daomiao Zhe ascended the hall and said: "The ancient Buddha said that in the past, at Vārāṇasī, he turned the Dharma wheel of the Four Noble Truths."
Having fallen into a pit and dropped into a ditch, he now turns the most wondrous, unsurpassed Great Dharma Wheel once more—this is like adding mud upon soil.
Is there anyone present here who, without traversing the steps, can transcend all things alone? After a long silence, he said: "Look out from atop the heavens."
"Who is the one who stands within this circle?
He ascended the hall and said: "A-la-la! What is it? I recall that year when I struck the 'Broken Oven' (Pozhuo) with my staff; suddenly, he was hit!"
"Only now do I realize you have let me down. Striking the incense altar once with his staff, he said, "Fall!
Fall! He ascended the hall and said: "Rubbing the void to chase after echoes exhausts your spirit. When dreaming ends and one awakens, realizing it was not real—what further matter remains?
The old man Deshan is upon the eyebrows and eyelashes of you all. Do you perceive him yet? If you perceive him..."
"Waking from a dream, one realizes it was not real. If you have not yet awakened, groping in empty space and chasing echoes will yield no end to your efforts.
Even if you were to attain such bold clarity here, it would still be like climbing a mountain to present tribute at court. Is there anyone who transcends all things alone?
After a long silence, he said: 'For now, do not feign clarity.'"
Ascending the hall, he said: "White clouds are limpid; waters flow into the vast ocean. All phenomena are fundamentally at rest—what further matter is there?
Therefore it is said: there is the provisional and there is the real; there is illumination and there is function. When you people arrive here, how do you proceed? After a long silence, he said:
"As long as there is a path that can be ascended, those who are superior will also walk upon it."
Ascending the hall, he said: "This mountain monk has no accumulated possessions; I simply have enough gruel and enough rice.
When I am weary, I fall asleep immediately, letting myself go wherever I may wander."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancient worthies said: 'First, Śākyamuni; second, Yuanhuo; third, Buddha. All others are merely bowl-dropping ghosts (wǎn-tuō-chōu).
Huiguang does not think so. First, Śākyamuni; second, Yuanhuo; third, Buddha—all are nothing but bowl-dropping ghosts.
Do you all know where Huiguang’s point lies? If you do, I grant that you possess iron eyes and copper pupils."
[The Master] said, "If you do not know this, do not say: 'Having weathered many treacherous winds and waves, my small boat has once traveled across the Five Lakes.
He ascended the hall, picked up his staff, and said, "As soon as a single speck of dust arises, the entire great earth is fully contained within it.
He struck the ground with the staff and said, "The World of Wondrous Joy is shattered into a hundred fragments. Now tell me, where is the Tathāgata of Immovability right now? If anyone...
If you recognize it, you may be said to have ascended to wondrous enlightenment without moving a step.
If you do not yet recognize it, then enter nirvana within the eyebrows and eyelashes of everyone here. He then struck the ground once more.

Ascending the hall, he raised his staff and said: "This staff of Zhikai sometimes acts as the Vajra King’s precious sword, sometimes acts as a crouching lion, sometimes acts as a probing pole or a shadow-grass, and sometimes does not function as a staff at all.
Do you all understand this thoroughly? If you do understand it, you will be like a dragon gaining water or a tiger relying on a mountain—appearing and disappearing, rolling up and unfolding at will."
As for the free and total application [of the Dharma], if you have not yet been entrusted with it, it is much like trying to escape one's shadow in broad daylight.
Chan Master Puyongping ascended the hall and said: "This mountain monk does not understand the Buddha-dharma; my efforts to benefit others are entirely without basis.
At times I half-open and half-close; at other times I fully release and fully withdraw. It is just like standing in the midst of ten thousand people, coldly tossing [the ball]."
This is a stone. Suddenly, if you strike upon one, you will for the first time know that it flows everywhere, reaching all places.
Entering the hall, he raised the case of Panshan, who addressed the assembly, saying: "Like the earth supporting a mountain, one does not know the mountain's towering loftiness;
like a stone containing jade, one does not know the jade's flawlessness. When the ancients spoke thus, they were very much like those who embrace their own plunder while crying out for injustice.
Everyone under the guidance of Master Zhikai was resolute and spirited; they could capture tigers and rhinoceroses alive and seize fierce dragons in hand.
They could accommodate Mount Sumeru within their eyes and the great ocean waters within their ears. Then, picking up his staff, he said: "This is not to show off my skills to others;

Chan Master Qingshan Long ascended the hall and said: "Flowers in clusters, brocade in clusters; for years, salt and sauce have been sufficient for every affair.

Chan Master Xiangshan Yuan ascended the hall and said: "The wine shops and fish markets are all treasured sites; the cawing of crows and the chirping of magpies are each sublime sounds.
He struck his staff and said, "Tell me, what kind of Buddha-work is this? There is no small amount of disorder here!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Patriarch Xiangshan has a 'head-word' that fills the four great continents.

If one were to critique it using the principles of the Buddha-dharma, it would be like mistaking a horse for an ox. Since you all do not critique it through the Buddha-dharma, what principle is it ultimately?
(He strikes the whisk. A lockless chest never tires of being shaken; at midnight, one must reach for the pillow."

"Use it! Now tell me, what do they usually employ under Huangbo?—*he gives a shout*.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The phrase exists, the phrase does not exist—like a vine leaning against a tree. For now, let everyone nod their heads.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "When the master craftsman has not yet emerged, jade and stone cannot be distinguished; when the skilled smelter is absent, gold and sand are mixed together.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Sometimes I open the gate to wait for a man of knowledge, yet the man of knowledge does not come to pass by.

Is this not like those who seek out their own kind? If you have it, take one step forward from the top of a hundred-foot pole;
if you do not, it will be a cause for laughter before the peak of Shaoshi.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The mind is identical to the realm of empty space; it manifests dharmas equal to empty space. When the realization of empty space is attained, there is neither 'is' nor 'non-is.

"Playing with you from the start, not violating the clear waves—the meaning is naturally distinct.

Furthermore, the sentient beings therein are neither aware nor do they know that those beings are riding donkeys and entering into the eyes of all people;
the people likewise are neither aware nor do they know it. Do you understand? To offer this body and mind to every dust mote and land—this is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Before a single bubble has arisen and the ancient sail has not yet set forth, the wind-signal does not arrive and no one raises the oars.
At such a time as this, how can the currents of the water be discerned? Do you not see where the old Yunmen lowered his hand—vast and clear waves leave no path to pass through?

Return! Do not blame us for meeting yet not recognizing one another; let it be so that ten thousand ages remain vast and dark.
Ascending the hall, he said: "When Mazu ascended the hall, Baizhang rolled up his mat. Later generations, unable to grasp the source of the wind, all say they left no trace behind.

If there is no such person, then for now, take up the fisherman’s flute and leisurely blow it by the seashore.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The wind whistles and the tree leaves fly; The wild geese do not come, and news is scarce.
There is no one to blow the 'Song of Returning Home'; It leaves me clapping my hands in vain hesitation."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "As for a reflection in a mirror, some say it exists; yet you cannot grasp it, for it does not fill the hand. As for a reflection in a mirror, some say it does not exist;
yet it appears as clearly as a formal portrait. Therefore, it cannot be grasped and cannot be relinquished; within that which cannot be obtained, it is simply obtained. Do you understand?"
He was not Vimalakīrti, yet he resembled Fu Dashi. He ascended the hall and said:
"The profound Way cannot be attained through the exertion of effort; sagely wisdom cannot be known with a calculating mind;
the ultimate truth cannot be realized by maintaining a sense of 'I'; and supreme merit cannot be achieved through the pursuit of worldly affairs. Ancient...
It is not possible for a person to simply provide medicine according to the illness throughout their single lifetime.

If one is a man of true character, they will govern the world when they emerge from seclusion, and withdraw and preserve it within themselves when they do not. If you always act in harmony with the sound, I shall reject you in every direction;
if you manifest in wine shops and brothels, I shall sleep alone upon a solitary peak. Tell me, where is this?
This Huanglong was the eye of humanity.
Zen Master Yunju You ascended the hall and said: "The Tathāgatas of the past do not subject you to further examination;
the Bodhisattvas of the present cannot simply let you off the hook; those who practice and study in the future must not be deceived by even a single point. Therefore, the teaching says:"
The Middle Way. If one wishes to thoroughly understand all Buddhas of the three periods of time, one should contemplate the nature of the Dharma-realm:
that all things are created solely by the mind. Nevertheless, under the gate of Yunju, this is precisely like gold dust falling into one's eyes.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The vision of the ordinary and the vision of the sage are like spring clouds and flashing lightning; true speech and false speech are like flowers in the sky and the moon reflected in water.
This brings me back to remember Changzi seeing Shitou, who could say: 'A single speck of snow on a red-hot furnace. [He] struck the meditation seat and descended."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Using tortoise hair as an arrow and hare fur as a bow, Nanda the Terrible shoots and pierces through empty space.

[He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it.

What a true message! Rely on you gentlemen to examine it closely. The former master Huanglong threw himself down completely—can anyone lift him up? If the patriarchs and ancestors..."
[The Master] finished. "The calamity shall reach your descendants.
He struck the meditation seat and descended from it. Entering the hall, he said: "All sounds are the Buddha’s voice. With his whisk, he struck the meditation seat and said:

"This Brahma-sound is profound and far-reaching, causing those who hear it to rejoice. He further said: "All forms are the Buddha’s form. Thereupon, picking up the whisk, he said: "Now the Buddha emits..."
This radiance assists in bringing forth the meaning of the true nature (*dharmatā*). Those who have already attained it should receive it upon their heads and practice accordingly;
those who have not yet attained it should understand it thus and believe it thus. Having struck the meditation seat, he descended from his position.
Chan Master Huangbo Sheng ascended the hall and said: "Linji’s shout and Deshan’s staff are left for practitioners to serve as models.
Guizong’s grindstone and Xuefeng’s ball—this kind of teaching style is for receiving those of superior capacity. But if it were Huangbo, it would not be so."
There is no shout, nor is there a staff; neither is there grinding, nor is there rolling a ball. Before you is the front mountain; behind you is the main mountain.
They block your eyes and squeeze your face until it breaks. If you can see this, you will attain the stage of non-retrogression and, until the end of the future, you shall not seek elsewhere.
If you cannot see this, the supreme flavor of *amṛta* (clarified butter) turns instead into poison.
It forms a toxic medicine.
Entering the hall for instruction: "Silent and desolate; the moon shines brightly down into the empty valley. Vast and expansive; the brilliant sunlight streams forth across the four seas.

Even if you can realize it here with such clarity and decisiveness, that is not yet the livelihood of a patch-robed monk.
A true great man must strike the shackles and break the chains within the dark prison; set fire to the ranks of hungry ghosts and seize their gruel;
topple the Tower of Maitreya and shatter the Hall of the Empty King; uproot the auspicious sprouts and rare grasses by their very roots, leaving them strewn across the ground.
Thorns grow. Chan Master Kaiyuan Qi ascended the hall and said: "Space has no interior or exterior; phenomena and principle have their long and short.
To follow them is to realize Bodhi; to oppose them is to produce affliction. The lantern always dozes off; the pillar also feels vexed. The Great Way lies..."

"On all four sides there are no gates; in the ten directions there are no walls. Hair disheveled, ears flapping—every one of you is a great man.

He gave rise to the Way. After a long silence, he said: "Treading through grass shoes, walking barefoot. Master Fuyan Gan ascended the hall and said:

Yellow and variegated intermingled—on what can the Chan practitioner rely? After a long silence, he said: "Zha! Master Zhizhi of Yungai ascended the hall and said:

Shoes-money. Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Zhaozhou asked a monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "To pick tea. Zhaozhou said, "Idle. The Master said:
"Whether one speaks it or does not speak it, where can it be grasped? Behind is the dragon’s scales; in front are the donkey’s hooves. A flip of the body reveals the sinews."
A single star. A solitary cloud, a wild crane. A-he-he!
Master Baozi Ying ascends the hall. The Master throws down his staff and calls out to the assembly, saying, "The staff has already swallowed the Patriarchs;
who is there to speak of Chan? Is there anyone who can save it? He lets out a shout.
"Ho! Chan Master Baoning Ji ascended the hall and said: "The spring rain falls gently; all things are as they should be. The grain sprouts and flourishes, and the vegetables grow in their season.
Ānanda joins his palms, and Kāśyapa also furrows his brow. Even if one were at the assembly on Vulture Peak, [to grasp] the holding up of the flower..."

Chan Master Qingyin Yuan ascended the hall and said: "My late teacher first served Xiyan Yi and Letan Cheng for twenty years.

When the Duke painted a dragon, the dragon appeared and he was immediately struck with fear.

He then cast down his whisk. At that moment, a monk picked it up from the ground and blew upon it.
The Master then shouted, "Who would have known that the ember of a continuing fire would have its smoke extinguished by this fellow?"

Master Huanglong Xin ascended the hall and said: "Profound, firm, secluded, and remote—no one can reach it.

After the evening at Yuhua, the Phoenix brought it back.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The eminent traveler opens his sack; he sets down his bowl-bag and discards his list of dietary prohibitions.
He must reach where one person is; he must reach where half a person is; he must personally reach even where no person is."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "If you break the staff, with what will you climb mountains and cross waters?
If you set aside the bowl, spoon, and chopsticks, with what will you eat porridge and rice? It would be better to cast lots east and west at the crossroads;
if you suddenly hit upon it, you all will have the credit. If you do not hit upon it, you cannot blame Yunyan."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Mañjuśrī rides a lion; Samantabhadra rides the Elephant King; Old Śākyamuni treads upon red lotuses.
But tell me, what does Huanglong ride? After a long silence, he said: "Lately I have grown old; every step is a true step."
Ascending the hall, he said: "When a pure pearl is cast into turbid water, the turbid water cannot fail to become clear.

When mindfulness of the Buddha is directed toward a distracted mind, the distracted mind cannot fail to become the Buddha. Since the Buddha is not distracted, the turbid water naturally becomes clear. Now that the turbid water is clear, to whom does the merit belong?
After a long silence, he said: "How many times have black winds overturned the great ocean? Yet I have never heard it said that a fishing boat has capsized."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Sometimes he breaks two into three; sometimes he brings three back to one; sometimes the three and the one are merged together;
sometimes he does not fall into numerical categories. Now tell me, where is Huanglong’s place for benefiting people?
After a long silence, he said, "Take care."
Chan Master Letan Qing ascended the hall and said: He cited Master Fushan Yuan, who said:

"If you wish to obtain the heroic and outstanding, you must further ensure that four things are all prepared before the path of the patriarchal master can be revealed. What are they? The first is the 'whiskers' of the Patriarchs."
Second, one must possess the vajra eyes; third, one must have the claws and fangs of a lion; fourth, one must obtain the monk’s staff that governs both killing and giving life.

Only when these four conditions are met can one move freely in all directions, manifesting transformations at will, rolling up or unfolding as the occasion demands, towering above gods and humans, standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
If it is not so, then for those who merely "guard the good path until death," it is a sign of defeat in battle. Why? Because striking stone with a staff [yields no result].

People value the discussion of actual facts. Therefore, arriving at this point, one must not fail to cultivate the following: the vast expanse where the river flows with clarity, the clouds gathering over the great fields;

the green bamboo holding mist, and the blue mountains locking in their verdancy. When wind and clouds are of one accord and water and moon are viewed as equal, a single phrase encompasses all, already manifesting what remains of the decayed.
The Master said: "Today Huanglong has appeared in the world. The times belong to the final age, when the Buddha-dharma is diluted."
One need not employ the patriarch’s nostrils; one need not employ the adamantine eyes; one need not employ the lion’s claws and fangs; one need not employ the staff that kills or gives life.
There is only this single fly-whisk as the path. With it, one can manifest纵横 transformations at will, rolling up and unfolding according to the natural flow;
one can soar high above the heavens and humans, standing like a thousand-fathom cliff. At times, when encountering the strong, one yields weakness.
At times, when encountered with the noble, it becomes base; when lifted up, the hosts of demons vanish and the Buddhas and Patriarchs hide their tracks.

When set down, water mingles with mud and the holy and the ordinary share the same path. Tell me, is it better to lift it up or to set it down? "The thread on the tip of the pole is for you to play with;
by not disturbing the clear waves, its meaning is naturally unique."
Cen Master Shuangfeng ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said: "Held horizontally or used upside down, it is the tiger’s stride and dragon’s gait of all quarters.

Master Kaixian Ying ascended the hall and said: "To discuss the profound and explain the subtle is like painting a cake to satisfy hunger. To enter the holy and transcend the mundane is much like a moth flying into a flame.
