Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Yangqi’s one essential point is the same wondrousness as that of the thousand sages. I bestow it upon the great assembly.
He struck the meditation seat once and said, "As expected, you have lost your vision. "Investigate!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Yangqi’s one phrase—look with quickened eyes! While on the long benches, picking up the spoon and grasping the chopsticks.
Ascending the hall again, he took up his staff and said: "The one is all; all is the one. He drew a line and said:
"Mountains, rivers, the great earth, and all the old masters under heaven—all shattered to pieces! What, then, are the nostrils of you all? After a long silence...
He said, "The sword leaves its precious sheath because it is not at peace; the medicine comes from the golden jar to save the sick. He gave a shout and struck the meditation seat once.
Entering the hall, he said: "Yangqi has no core meaning; he tills the fields to earn his rice to eat. As for the old Gautama who speaks of dreams, where can one find him?"
[He makes a] trace. [With a] shout, he strikes the meditation seat once.

He ascends the hall and says: "Living at Yangqi with meager merit, my strength has declined over the years. The cold wind withers the fallen leaves; yet I am still glad that an old friend has returned.
*Lao-lao-li!* Taking up this head of dead firewood, let us for now settle in where there is no smoke or flame."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The matter of Yungai is not like speaking of Chan; it is like swallowing a chestnut. If you can understand it at this point, the distance between the Buddha-dharma and the mundane world will be as vast as heaven and earth."
Ascending the hall, he threw down his staff and said: "Old Śākyamuni tripped and fell; he stole a laugh at Yungai’s rambling talk.
Although the world is level and plain, it is still a case of making up for one's shortcomings with diligence."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "When body and mind are pure, all objects are pure; when all objects are pure, body and mind are pure.
Do you know where the old man of Yangqi has landed? When money is lost in the river, one must fish for it in the river."
Chan Master Baiyun said in an address to the assembly: "A bird has two wings; it flies whether far or near. The Way issues from a single corner; it is practiced whether before or after.
You monks, in your daily lives, when picking up your spoons and setting down your bowls, all say you 'know it.
Yet when you reach the mountain pass, why do you suddenly become short of breath? Have you not heard that for a practitioner, if there is no foresight, there will surely be immediate anxiety?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Within the realm of heaven and earth, amidst the universe, there is a treasure hidden within the mountain of form.
Great assembly, the eyes are above the nose and the feet are below the belly; tell me, where is this treasure? After a long silence, he said:
"One knows not where the human face has gone; the peach blossoms still smile upon the spring breeze."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The ancients said, 'To offer this profound mind to every dust mote and land is what is called repaying the Buddha's kindness.
But Yuantong is not like this: at times he picks wild vegetables at night and boils them with their roots; he hews fresh firewood and burns it with its leaves still attached."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The river moon shines; the pine wind blows. At this point, is there anyone who has escaped the net? After a long silence, he said:
"Heaven has no partiality."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Entering the forest without moving the grass; entering the water without disturbing the waves; entering among birds without confusing their flight. O Great Assembly!
This is the hand and foot for casting off the anchor and setting sail. But tell me, how should a member of the *sōngjia* (patch-robed monk) act?
[He] struck the meditation seat with his hand and said: "Turning over mountains and seas to seek a true friend; shaking the cosmos to see the peace of the world."
Ascending the hall, he said: "By naturally restricting what one eats, various ailments are diminished; yet having many attachments cannot avoid occasional weariness.
Living in poverty, every movement results in either opposition or compliance; thus, one attains the singular excellence of pure leisure.
Although this is so, do not say that a 'mindless' state is the Way—for even 'mindlessness' still leaves behind a further barrier."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The clay Buddha does not cross water; the wooden Buddha does not cross fire; the golden Buddha does not cross the furnace;
the True Buddha sits within. "Great assembly! This old man Zhaozhou has at once cast his twelve joints of bone and eighty-four thousand pores into the laps of everyone here.
Today, Yuantong, seeing injustice on the road, acts on behalf of the ancients."

A man came out and, slapping the meditation seat with his hand, said: "One must know that the seas and mountains submit to the enlightened sovereign; one cannot yet believe that heaven and earth would trap a virtuous person.
He then ascended the hall. Śākyamuni Buddha has the Four Great Vows, which say: "Sentient beings are boundless; I vow to deliver them all. [The text continues: "Afflictions..."
I vow to sever afflictions that are inexhaustible; I vow to study the Dharma gates that are immeasurable; I vow to accomplish the unsurpassed path of the Buddha.
The Lotus Sūtra also contains the four great vows: When hunger comes, one must eat; When cold arrives, one adds clothing;
When weary, one stretches out the legs to sleep; In the heat, one longs for a breeze.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "When the ancients left behind a single word or half a phrase, as long as it had not been penetrated, it was like bumping into an iron wall.
Suddenly, one day, after seeing through it, one finally realizes that one's own self is the iron wall.
How do you penetrate it now? He added: "The iron wall! The iron wall!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "If you can truly break into a sweat once, then even upon a single blade of grass you will manifest jeweled towers and palaces of jade.
If you have not yet broken into a sweat once, then even if there were jeweled towers and palaces of jade, they would be covered over by a single blade of grass.
How do you get yourself to break into a sweat? There is already a pair of hands that are destitute; they have never permitted anything to enter."
The *Yi* dances upon the three stages.
Ascending the hall: "If one can advance in every subtle interest, yet ultimately find no place of return;

if one can act daily with a receding body until the impulse is exhausted—suddenly, one shall behold one's original father and mother. What is this original father and mother? He then said: "Ten thousand..."
"Fo! He then descended from his seat and addressed the assembly, saying:
"When I press my finger, the Ocean-Seal Samādhi radiates light. Raising his staff, he said:
"Mountains, rivers, the great earth, waterfowl, and forest trees—all things with sentience and without sentience—today all manifest the Great [Dharma] upon the tip of this *dharmaparyāya* staff."
The Lion’s Roar: Expounding the Mahāprajñāpāramitā. But tell me, what Dharma-gate did Tiantai and Nanyue expound?
Nanyue spoke of the five ranks of practice in the Dongshan tradition, where ruler and subject, father and son, each find their proper place.
"Do not linger by the cold crag while the strange grasses turn green; sit amidst the white clouds, for this lineage is not inferior. Tiantai spoke of the three [mysteries] under Linji.
The Three Essentials of the Mysterious and the Four Kinds of Critical Examination: with a single shout, host and guest are distinguished and illumination and function are exercised simultaneously.
To understand the meaning within this, it is like striking the third watch at midday. Lushan stepped forward and said, "You two are right in the midst of a tangle of vines."
"I have not seen anyone who, wishing to avoid incurring karma of the Avīci Hell, would slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma.
O Great Assembly, judging these three men by the scale of a true monk, one weighs eight *liang*, one weighs half a *jin*, and one is not worth even half a copper coin.
Now tell me, which one is not worth even half a copper coin?"
After a long silence, he said: "I only wish that the spring breeze would exert its full strength, blowing all at once into my gate. He struck his staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Baoning Yong ascended the hall and said: "For over twenty years, this mountain monk has carried his bag and bowl, traveling across the vast seas."
Among the ten or so fellow practitioners who were my internal spiritual friends, none possessed any personal insight;
they were like inert stones. The venerable masters we studied under likewise had no superior qualities to benefit us.

Consequently, for the rest of my life, I remained a person who understood nothing at all—a truly pitiable state of affairs. Suddenly, however, driven by the winds of karma, I was blown to the riverbank.
Ningfu was unexpectedly deceived by others and pushed to the crossroads. He took up residence in a dilapidated temple as a master of gruel and rice, receiving guests from all quarters.
Having no other recourse, he provided salt and vinegar as best he could, ensuring there was enough gruel and rice to get by.
Thus he passed his time; as for the Buddha-dharma, he had never even seen it in a dream.
Ascending the hall, after the attendant had finished burning incense, the Master pointed to the attendant and said, "The attendant has already preached the Dharma for everyone.
Ascending the hall again, he said, "Look, look! This mountain monk is entering the Hell of the Plucked Tongue. He pulled his tongue with his hand and cried out, "A-yi!"
Ājñā. Ascending the hall: When scolding one another, there are no good words;
when striking one another, there are no good fists. Great assembly, you must act in this very way before you can succeed.
Every word cuts to the quick; every punch lands with solid force. Suddenly striking this faceless fellow, it is truly exhilarating—truly lethal.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The autumn wind is cool; the pine tones are long. The traveler who has not yet returned thinks of his hometown. But tell me, who is this traveler who has not yet returned?
Where is that hometown? After a long silence, he said: "On the long benches, there is porridge and rice."
Ascending the hall, he said: "In the heavens there is no Maitreya; beneath the earth there is no Maitreya.
Having shattered the vast void, how can one fail to find him? He then lowered one foot and said: "Great assembly, where have you gone?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "If one speaks of the Buddha-dharma to provide for the assembly, one cannot avoid the falling out of eyebrows and beard.
If one speaks of worldly dharmas to provide for the assembly, one enters hell as swiftly as a shooting arrow. Setting aside these two paths, tell me: what should Baoning say today?
A three-inch tongue has no place to be used; a pair of empty hands do not form a fist."
Ascending the hall: That which belonged to the ancients is used by those of today; that which belongs to those of today was practiced by the ancients.
There is no front or back between past and present—how many people, ancient or modern, understand this? *Yā*! *Ī*! One nine and two nines—when they meet, they do not even lift their hands.
Ascending the hall, he said: "It has hands and feet, yet it has no front or back. Even those with clear eyes cannot see it. Heaven revolves to the left; earth revolves to the right.
He struck his knee and said: "A gust of west wind comes; two or three leaves fall."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The wind whistles through the branches; the rain breaks up the clods of earth. At dawn, the sound of orioles on the pillow is shattered.
Frogs and earthworms cry out all at once. Miaode and Śāriputra do not understand. They do not understand. Three form a group; four make a troupe."
Deep and secluded; drifting and soaring. Heading north, south, east, and west, he plucks a few blossoms of pear and plum—one sashful, two sashfuls—and ascends the hall.
"Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking of it. To speak of it is to give rise to horns. "O Assembly, as for these horns..."
It has been born. Is it an ox? Is it a horse?
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The night is still and the moon is bright; the water is clear and the fish appear. A golden hook is cast—where shall one seek its trace?
Raising his staff, he said: "Examine closely, examine closely!"
He addressed the assembly, saying: "There is a fellow who is strange and ugly; his eyes are bulging and his nose is crooked. Facing south, he looks at the Big Dipper;
he knows how to make the golden crow cry at noon and the iron ox bellow at midnight. Heaven and earth spin, mountains and rivers run;
the feathered tribes and hairy multitudes lose their way. It is so that Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra emerge here and vanish there, leaping seven ways and crossing eight paths in a thousand directions."
Giving rise to myriad perceptions, one suddenly encounters that Yellow-Faced Gautama.
Not sparing his own eyebrows, he repeatedly strokes the person’s head and bestows a prophecy upon them, saying: "Excellent, excellent! You perform great Buddha-work; rare indeed, rare indeed!
At this, one is left feeling utterly abashed and disconcerted, shrinking back in trepidation with head tucked and hands withdrawn. [The Master] calls out: "Great Assembly, as for this story..."
"Great practice! Why must you wait another thirty years?
[The Master] addressed the assembly, saying: 'The Old Śākyamuni preached the Dharma for forty-nine years without ever uttering a single word.
Upagupta filled his chamber with counting-slips yet never ordained a single person. Bodhidharma did not dwell at Shaoshi. 6.
"The Patriarch did not dwell at Caoxi; who then is the descendant, and who is the one first awakened?
Since this is so, 'if he has no wound himself, do not inflict one upon him. He struck his knee and looked at the assembly, saying, "I am glad to see that all under heaven is at peace."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The True Form is formless, yet it manifests form and displays characteristics. A thousand wonders and ten thousand transformations are revealed from this.

When joyful, light radiates across the face; when angry, the two brows suddenly stand erect. Neither ordinary nor holy, perhaps right and perhaps wrong—it is unfathomable to humans and beyond the reach of even the heavens.
To grasp this directly is not yet to be called a true man; if one does not turn back upon being called, then..."
Do not misunderstand.
Zen Master Wuzu Yan addressed the assembly: "In this way, in this way—the shrimp cannot leap out of the basket.
Not in this way, not in this way—cleverness turns into clumsiness. Soft as iron, hard as mud. Twelve taels of the diamond eye. The patched robe...
The monk’s hand holds the scale; the head is low. There is a price, yet no room for deliberation. Those without nostrils—what do they use to smell the fragrance?
Ascending the hall, he said: "Difficult, difficult! How many kinds? Easy, easy! No handle to grasp. Good, good! It hastens one toward old age. Silent, silent! Follow along."
This is attained. Having passed through the four heavy barriers, the people of Sizhou see the Great Sage.
[The Master] enters the hall and says: "If you wish to move with sevenfold freedom and eightfold ease, look at this old monk beating the drum and ascending the hall.
At seventy-three or eighty-four, I will take my staff and strike you right in the mouth! Although it is thus, I shall remove the mounting platform at the gate.
"Only by cutting away the five-colored cords can one finally attain peace and happiness.
Entering the hall, [the Master] said: "The ancients said: 'If I were to speak to you, my tongue would fall out;
if I were not to speak to you, my mouth would be mute. Tell me, is there still a way to benefit others? Sometimes Si-mian intended to act for them..."
"You swallowed it, but it was obstructed by your front teeth. I intended to spit it out for you, but my throat is too narrow.
He then said, "From all four directions, Liu Xiaohui comes of his own accord."

Ascending the hall, he said: "White Cloud does not know how to speak of Chan. The three gates open toward both sides. If someone touches the pivot, the two panels swing one to the east and one to the west."
Ascending the hall: A thousand peaks stand in verdant array; willows by the banks hang with golden grace. Woodsmen sing their songs; fishermen beat the drum.

Flutes and pipes resound through the earth; birds warble in soft harmony. Fair ladies in crimson robes and elegant young gentlemen—each one, for all of you, has manifested the highest vehicle and opened the Eye of the True Dharma.
If you can realize this right here, the Golden-Clothed Dhūta has no room for you.
As for the body’s location: if you do not understand, I shall allow you to be pierced through from every side as you eat your congee and rice.
Entering the hall: This very thing supports the heavens above and props up the earth below; Mount Wan serves as its eyes, and Mount Wan serves as its nose.
Taiping steps back three paces to let all of you breathe freely.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The man of the Tàipíng era was a thoroughgoing fellow; he has passed through every single matter. Thus it has been for thirty years.
There have been those who praised him, but tell me, what did they praise? He was a fine, thoroughgoing fellow indeed."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Where there is a Buddha, you must not dwell; this will exchange your heart, liver, and five viscera.
Where there is no Buddha, run past quickly; like a wild goose passing that leaves its cry behind. Even if you encounter someone three thousand *li* away, do not misquote [the teaching].

To step out the door is already an error. If it were so, then one would not go at all—planting millet yet having beans grow. Plucking the willow blossoms, plucking the willow blossoms, one does not realize the day has passed again."
Night. How can one teach others when they are still young?
Ascending the hall: Awakening is the same as non-awakening; returning home, seek the old path. One character is one character; one phrase is one phrase.
Since childhood, I have never uttered empty words; at two years of age, I learned to take steps. A lotus flower grows from still water; it takes a year to grow.
Once, he ascended the hall and said: "Fortunately, there is not a single thing; one who travels on pilgrimage ought to study Chan. Yet one is instead vexed by the appearance of Chan.
Without penetrating the Patriarch’s barrier, how can one do so? What is the Patriarch’s barrier? 'Carrying fire into the cowpen.'"
Ascending the hall, the mountain monk said: "Yesterday, when I entered the city, I saw a stage of puppet theater and could not help but approach to watch.

Sometimes I saw figures of dignified and extraordinary appearance; sometimes I saw those so ugly as to be unbearable. I watched them move, walk, sit, and gesture, noting every detail of their blue, yellow, red, and white colors.
When I looked closely, however, I realized that there were people behind the blue cloth curtains. The mountain monk could no longer restrain his amusement."
He then asked, "What is the High Official’s surname? The other replied, "Old Monk, you have already seen him; why do you ask what his surname is?
"O assembly, when the mountain monk was thus questioned by him, I was left with no words to respond and no principle to defend.
Is there anyone here who can speak for me? Yesterday I fell at the joints; today I pull up the very roots."
Ascending the hall, he preached the Dharma, brandishing the mallet and raising the whisk—ten thousand miles of white clouds. When Deshan entered the gate, he struck;
when Linji entered the gate, he shouted—ten thousand miles of white clouds. Yet, after that, it cannot be done this way, nor can it be done that way;
even if both this way and that way are not permitted, there are still ten thousand miles of white clouds. Suddenly, there is one who...
Han came forth and said: "Elder, for you to speak thus is like ten thousand miles of white clouds.
This talk is called "the dwarf watching a play, rising and falling with the others. Thirty years from now, it will be a laughable scene.
But tell me, what is there to laugh at? One laughs at the "ten thousand miles of white clouds."
Addressing the assembly: The Patriarch said, "I have come to this land to transmit the Dharma and save deluded beings; when the flower blooms, the five petals unfold, and the fruit ripens naturally.
Master Bodhidharma came with his feet leading him and spoke with his mouth leading him, yet the descendants of later generations have mostly fallen into calculating deliberations.
Do you wish to understand the place where the flowers bloom and the fruit ripens? Pears from Zhengzhou, dates from Qingzhou—among all things, there is none [that does not bear fruit].
Excellent in its departure from conventional origins.
Addressing the assembly: The Buddhas of the ten directions, the six generations of patriarchs, and all the good spiritual friends in the world—all share this very same tongue.
If you can recognize this tongue, only then will you understand the "great empty deception," whereby you will say that the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are [it].
“The Buddha. Grasses, trees, thickets, and forests are the Buddha. If you have not yet recognized this tongue, you will merely achieve a minor deception and delude yourself;
there is much more to come tomorrow and the day after. When the Fifth Patriarch spoke thus, was there anything substantial in it?
He himself said there was. What is that substantial point? “Go back to the hall and drink tea.”

Addressing the assembly: Every day since rising, I have wielded Linji’s staff, blown the Yunmen flute, responded to Zhaozhou’s clapping, carried Yangshan’s spade, and drove Moshan’s ox to plow the fields of White Cloud.
Over these seven or eight years, I have gradually established my household. I further appeal to you all:
each of you extend a hand to assist me in singing the village field music of coarse soup and plain rice.
Let us pass our days in this manner. Why? Simply because we pray that the silkworms and wheat may ripen this year, so that Rāhula’s child may be given a single coin.
Addressing the assembly, he raised the case of Master Deshan. Once, a monk asked him: "By what Dharma do the sages of all ages instruct people? Deshan—
"I say that my school has no words or phrases, nor do I give a single dharma to anyone. Hearing this, Xuefeng attained a realization.
Later, a monk asked Xuefeng, "Master, what did you obtain upon seeing Deshan that you then ceased [seeking further]?
Xuefeng replied, "At that time, I went empty-handed and returned empty-handed. Baoyun now speaks this for those who have not yet penetrated it: there is one...
A man came from Tokyo. When asked where he had come from, he replied that he had come from Suzhou. When asked how things were in Suzhou, he said they were all quite ordinary.
Even so, he could not deceive Baiyun. Why? Because: [He was merely repeating what he had heard; his own experience remained hidden.]
It is simply because their spoken sounds differ. Ultimately, how is it? "Water chestnuts from Suzhou; lotus roots from Shaobu.
Master Benchan of Yungai ascended the hall, called out loudly to his attendant, and the attendant responded, "Yes?
The Master asked, "Has the assembly gathered yet? The attendant replied, "The assembly has already gathered. The Master said, "Why does that one person not come?"
He went to attend the assembly. The attendant remained silent. The Master said, "Upon arrival, there is no greeting.
He ascended the hall and said: "Filled the mouth, yet words cannot issue forth; every phrase is utterly clear. Filled the eyes, yet one cannot see; mountain upon mountain, layers of chaotic green.
If the sound of the drum is still not understood, how much less so the tolling of the bell! He gave a shout.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The patriarch was eminent and outstanding; his descendants are cramped and petty. There is a place to hide their heads, yet no place to expose their horns.
I ask you monks: how do you go about searching for them?"
Ascending the hall, he held his staff horizontally and said: "Teeth like swords and blades, a face like iron; eyes emitting flashes of lightning that never cease.
Grasping ten thousand catties of thorny brambles in hand, he casually knocks down the moon from the edge of the sky. He struck once.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Those who depart have their nostrils reaching to the heavens; those who come tread upon solid ground.

But tell me, where does the Patriarch’s intention lie? After a long silence, he said: "I have always lamented that spring departs with no place to be found; I know not how it has flowed into this very midst."
Ascending the hall: The core of the high platform—open your mouth and it is right there. If it were already right there, what core would there be? The moon is cold, the wind is high;
the water is clear, the mountains are verdant.
Ascending the hall: “Using a wedge to extract a wedge—how can there be any rest? If you wish to attain rest, use a wedge to extract a wedge. *Shouts.* Ascending the hall:
“Head wearing Mount Sumeru, feet treading the four great oceans; with every breath, wind and thunder arise; in every movement, the five colors are born.
If you can recognize this one, let the years and months pass as they may. But tell me, who is it that recognizes this one? *Shouts.*
One shout: "Yun-tian Ku-nu!
Chan Master Wensheng of Shousheng ascended the hall, held up his staff, and said: "This wooden *zhilu* of Huazang is casually brought forth at random.

It is not that he is unwilling to let go of it; it is simply that the mountain man has no fixed attachments. When he points to a mountain, the mountains tremble; when he stirs the water, the waters ripple."
Yi suddenly seized hold of him, and for every matter he applied the rules and regulations. Where he wanted to be obstinate, one could not be obstinate;
where he wanted to be submissive, one could not be submissive. He suddenly called out to the assembly, saying: "Do not say that there is an eye on the tip of the staff as bright as the sun;
the radiance upon it is entirely lacquer. With these words, he struck once.
Ascending the hall: One thrust, one jab—bone meets skin; one grasp, one lift—hands stick and feet adhere. A flash of lightning, a spark from flint—the head droops and the tail droops.
Like an arrow split in flight, chasing the wind—half-alive, half-dead. To collide and strike against it, what eyebrows can you find?
Whether facing bright or facing dark, what eyes are these? If you do not act in either of these ways, you are precisely halfway there. Even if...
The entire mechanism has not yet reached the further shore. Even if one were utterly naked and bare, with nothing to grasp, there would still be a trace of attachment.
When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, tell me: what is it that you call "speaking"? After a long silence, he said: "Heh! Keep some for eating."
Chan Master Yixi of Shangfang ascended the hall. "Shide carries firewood; Hanshan burns the fire. Only Fenggan sits coldly within his cave.
Now tell me, what excellence does Fenggan possess? After a long silence, he said: "If a household has no minor servants, one cannot be considered a gentleman."
Chan Master Kaifuning ascended the hall and said: "The autumn sun shines across the vast sky; the autumn river reflects the empty azure.
Alas for those outside the gate, who seek Maitreya everywhere. Suddenly lifting their heads along the road, they meet him yet do not recognize him. O virtuous Chan practitioners!"

Since we have met face-to-face, why do you not recognize me? I have clipped away all the bamboos before the frost; standing by the stream, I do not transform into a dragon. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Pervading the entire world, there has never been anything hidden; my whole body is without shadow or form. Do not be surprised that our meeting is so utterly foolish;
from kalpas past until now, I have had no skillful means. No skillful means—few people know it. Generally speaking, it is because his flesh and bone are naturally excellent. How...
One must approach a mirror to paint the brows of a beauty.
Great Master Jingsu of Suizhou ascended the hall and said: "The sovereign is clear-sighted; the generals are alert. Once victory is achieved, the six states are brought to peace."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the dialogue concerning Linji’s visit to Huangbo. Master Baiyun Dan had composed a verse on it which says:
"A single punch knocks down the Yellow Crane Tower; A single kick overturns the Parrot Isle. When there is spirit, one adds more spirit;
Where there is no elegance, there is still elegance. The Master said: "Dasuì, it is not so. At seventy years of age, I am an old, clumsy fellow. My eyes..."
The eyes are clear and bright, and the ears do not go deaf. Suddenly someone comes along to bully me; with a single punch, I knock them down past the pass of Guandong.
Entering the hall: One’s own fields and gardens are plowed at ease; the ancestral foundation must be defended with effort. To awaken, one must sit atop the heads of a thousand sages;
to act, one must walk beneath the depths of the three miserable realms.
Chan Master Jingyin Cheng ascended the hall and said: "The Kunlun slave wears iron trousers; with every blow of the staff he takes a step forward.
How does this compare to fishing for turtles in fire or hiding ice in the sun? Shadows and reflections turn into *wangliang* spirits; empty space is bound with hempen rope."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Sound is in the nose, fragrance is in the ear; saltiness and blandness are in the eye, while the tongue distinguishes black and yellow.
The mind can perceive touch, and the body makes discriminations. In an ice chamber it is like spring; in the ninth month of summer it is cool.

If you see it thus, you will know that when one enters meditative concentration within a man’s body, one emerges from concentration within a woman’s body. The sunflower turns with the sun; the rhinoceros-patterned horn gazes upon the moon.
A fragrant maple tree transforms into an old man; a moth becomes a wasp. If you do not know this, how bitter it is, O Buddha!
I grant you a single eye.
Chan Master Wanshou Su ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great thousandfold world-system is utterly destroyed.

I wonder, is this [the True Self] also destroyed? Wanshou said, "It is destroyed. Xiu the Mountain Master said, "It is not destroyed. "I wonder which of you is right and which is wrong," [the monk] asked.
The Master said, "One is destroyed, one is not destroyed. It makes Avalokiteśvara laugh to death. A lion suddenly bites a person; a mad dog..."

He chased him all the way until he dropped the clod of earth. [The monk] asked again, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "A lacquer bucket that is not clever enough.
Chan Master Letan Ying ascended the hall and, looking over the assembly, said: "The green mountains are layered upon layers; the green waters resound with a murmuring flow.
He then took up his staff and said, "Before reaching the edge of the precipice, lift your head and look closely. With a thud, he struck the ground once.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The noble ones of Baofeng rarely arrive. Before the crags, snow weighs down the withered pines until they fall.
Before the ridges and behind them, wild monkeys cry. A single ancient path is swept clean by the pure breeze. Zen practitioners, although it is thus, tell me: how long is this mountain monk’s staff?
He then lifted it up and said, "When long, it is used for its length; when short, it is used for its brevity. He struck the ground once.

Descending from his seat, he ascended the hall and looked over the assembly, saying: "The crags of Shimen are treacherous and the iron gates are secure; every eye raised meets ten thousand fathoms of height.
If the hornless iron ox can break through them, it will stir up waves within the ocean of Vairocana. But tell me, what is it that does not involve itself in these waves?"
"Master Tao, how would you say it? After a long silence, he said: "A single phrase was not sufficient for Wuzhuo’s question;
even now, he remains a monk wandering in the wilds.
Chan Master Wenduoshuo ascended the hall and said: "The lion yawns and stretches; the elephant king roars. Yunmen [is] within the Big Dipper."
The body is hidden. Why did Baiyun call it "the hand"? The Buddhas of the three periods cannot know it; yet the tabby cat and the white ox do.
But tell me, what is this matter of their knowing it? Rain beats the pear blossoms as butterflies fly;
the wind blows the willow catkins as they roll away like balls of fur.
Chan Master Chuchan of Longhua ascended the hall and said: "When a rooster sees another, it fights; when a dog sees another, it bites.
The *chīwen* (gargoyle) on the roof of the hall faces its counterpart all day long—why does it never get angry? He then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Yuyang ascended the hall and said: "Deshan’s 'staff upon entering the gate' mostly leaves one's tracks buried within the leather bag;
Linji’s 'shout upon entering the gate' entirely involves appearing and disappearing within the realm of sound. If you are a truly heroic monk,"
"You must simply let the wind rise from beneath your feet and transcend the tracks of past and present. He brandished his staff, struck once, and gave a shout, saying:
"As for this very thing, what is it like? If you call it a 'stick' or a 'shout,' you are still asleep and have not yet awakened.
If you do not call it a 'stick' or a 'shout,' you do not yet know Deshan or Linji. After all, how is it? He struck once more and said: "It cannot be grasped at all."
He moved. He ascended the hall and said: "The entire earth is the eye of the śramaṇa; throughout the ten directions is one's own light.

Why is it that when the drum is beaten in Pūrvavideha in the east, it is not heard in Aparagoyānī in the west? When the lamp is lit in Jambudvīpa in the south, [it is not seen] in Uttarakuru in the north."
"Transcending darkness and sitting. Even if you were able to speak with complete mastery here, it would still be a livelihood within the realm of light and shadow.
[The Master] struck the whisk and said, "It is all shattered into a hundred fragments. What is the single path for emerging? Throw down the whisk—study!"

Ascending the hall, he said: "To move is for shadows to appear; to awaken is for ice to form. Even if you remain unmoving and unawakened, you are still like the rattle of a chariot wheel from the Qin dynasty.
Reaching this point, one must have a subtle illumination amidst a thousand differences so that ten thousand doors open simultaneously.
With a single turn of the pivot at the tip of a hair, the life-vein does not sink into the sea of poison. At times awakening is like still water; at times movement is like stars flying."
At times, both movement and awareness are forgotten; at other times, illumination and function are sovereign. Tell me, at such a moment as this, is it movement?
Is it awareness? Is it illumination? Is it function? Is there anyone who can distinguish them? An iron ox blocks the ancient road;
when touched, one’s very bones and hair turn cold.

Ascending the hall, he said: "When acting, there is no trace of action; when speaking, there is no mark of speech. If action and speech reach their destination, one sets up a target that invites the arrow.

If action and speech are not yet clarified, the divine blade cuts through with a stroke. Even if one’s speech is without leakage and one’s actions do not lose their direction, one still remains stuck within the shell and leakages.
Only when one is like the great golden-winged garuḍa, flapping its wings across hundreds of thousands of *yojanas*, does it cast ten shadows."
A divine steed gallops across the four quarters and the eight extremities; it does not graze haphazardly, nor does it bury itself wherever it happens to be.
Moreover, it relies on nothing at all. Is there still a portion for treading upon? Every moment and every speck of dust is the essential ford.
Ascending the hall, he said: "It is easy to fill a vast chasm, but difficult to fill a leaking cup. Yet if one possesses the capacity for sustained practice, there is neither ease nor difficulty.
If you set aside the entire earth, it is spacious and more than sufficient; if you let go even a hair’s breadth, there is no path left for obstruction.
Suddenly, if you neither set it aside nor let it go, where will you tread? Sharing in sincerity, we share in joy and sorrow; even drinking water must nourish you."
Chan Master Daowei Tai ascended the hall and said: "Pushing to the limit of the Real, the Real has no marks; exhausting the delusory, the delusory has no form.
When both Real and delusory are non-existent, the eyes are revealed in vast openness. Now that the eyes are revealed, what do you see? The morning sun melts the snow upon the cliffside;
the northern wind blows open the winter plum blossoms."
Ascending the hall, he said: "When the precious sword is drawn, it is used immediately; how could there be any hesitation? When the eyebrows are raised, one walks forth;

there is no turning back or evasion. In every place, it illuminates the present and radiates through antiquity; in every place, it cuts through all nets and cages. It does not touch the blade’s edge, nor does it reflect in a mirror.
Setting aside for a moment the matter of its solitary transcendence beyond all things—what of the time when the myriad functions have been utterly exhausted? August."
"Where is it hot in autumn? He ascended the hall and said: "In Nirvana there is no divergent path; expedient means have many doors. Raising his staff, he said: "Look! Look!
This mountain monk’s staff has swallowed up the waters of the West River in a single draught. The carp of the Eastern Sea leap thirty feet into the air!"
For three days, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, grew enraged and struck Mount Sumeru with a single blow, shattering it to pieces. The Earth Goddess Sthāvarā joined her palms and praised him, saying:
"Observe well the Dharma of the Dharma King; such is the Dharma of the Dharma King. Then, striking his meditation seat with his staff, he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To realize the emptiness of persons and the emptiness of phenomena does not yet accord with the ancestral style of the Buddhas.
To embody total function and total illumination is likewise not the essential subtlety of a patch-robed monk. You must directly shatter the sturdy barrier and recognize that single aperture above.
What is this single aperture above? The spring chill is biting; it freezes the youth to death."
Ascending the hall: Vast and remote, it encompasses the ten directions; level and expansive, it transcends form and appearance.
The eyes wish to see, yet the pupils wither; the mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail. Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra have no skill at all;
Linji and Deshan do not hesitate to proclaim the teaching. A tortoise swallows the iron ox of Shanfu; a snake bites the great elephant of Jiazhou. Terrified—!
The carp of the Eastern Sea has remained bloated until this very day.
Hehe! Entering the hall: Opening one’s mouth is sometimes wrong; opening one’s mouth is sometimes right. Whether coarse words or subtle speech, all return to the primary meaning.
The old Śākyamuni’s bowl rings out; Bodhidharma’s coming from the West is a stench of excrement. Only that which is before the mountain...
Water-buffalo! Its body emits white light that illuminates heaven and earth.

Entering the hall, he said: "Attaining mindfulness or losing mindfulness—there is nothing that is not liberation. What kind of talk is this? "Establishing dharmas or destroying dharmas—all are called nirvana.
This is a mere guess; it has no connection to the reality. "Wisdom and folly are both universally the Prajñā. This is a coarse and superficial Buddha-nature.
The dharmas accomplished by Bodhisattvas and non-Buddhists are all but a mere trifle compared to Bodhi.
Nevertheless, even so, it is like Emperor Yang losing his camel.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "If you wish to know where the Buddha has gone, it is simply this sound of my voice. *Duh!* "Master Fu did not recognize good from evil;

he taught people to pursue that which is bright and luminous, thereby ruining the men and women of their families. Being addressed with a shout by Master Zhigong, who said, "Great Master, do not speak thus!
Try saying something else," the Great Master then spoke a verse: "Holding a hoe in empty hands, I walk along the path of weeds. The weeds are deep and thick, Yet I find no place to rest."
Walking, he rides a water buffalo; a person passes over the bridge. The bridge flows, yet the water does not flow.
Master Zhigong laughed heartily and said: "The beginning was still somewhat bearable, but the end is even more distressing."
Ascending the hall, he said: "I recall in days past when I traveled as a wandering monk, I obtained two things: one was a vajra-hammer, and the other was the bones of a thousand sages.
Carrying them through the universe, my spirit and bearing were loftily prominent.
Thus for thirty years, I used them as my standard. But now that I am old, what do I know of these things? I cast down the vajra-hammer and smash the bones of the thousand sages to pieces."
The holy bones are cast upon the four-way crossroads; they can no longer be cherished. One passes through this floating life at will:
taking south for north, calling a tortoise a soft-shelled turtle, and calling beans millet. Let those with clear eyes laugh at me for being without the guiding line.
National Teacher Huo: "The team of fellows before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja were off by seven or eight;
the team of fellows after King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja were off by two or three. But as for this current team of fellows, they sit and stand with solemn dignity.
Now tell me: are they off by seven or eight, or off by two or three? Can you still determine which it is? He raises his whisk.
The Master said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ!
He ascended the hall and said: "The wild jackal howls; the lion roars. Eyes wide open, mouth agape, he moves the Southern Star and stumbles past the Northern Dipper."
"Great assembly, do you know where this falls? A diamond vajra squats at the foot of the steps; a divine tortoise runs through the fire.
Master Yuan of Lingyin ascended the hall and said: "A monk asked Muzhou, 'I do not ask about removing one layer after another;
but when there is no removing of one layer after another, what then? Muzhou replied, 'Yesterday I planted eggplants; today I am weeding.'"
He was planting melons. The Master said: "The questioner asks well, yet does not understand the answer; the respondent answers well, yet does not understand the question.
Today, this mountain monk shall snatch meat from the talons of a hungry eagle and cast my body across the mouth of a fierce tiger to show you all a model.
The robe of the ascendant ritualist is light; though his incantatory power may be exhausted, the Dharma remains ever new. [His] thumb..."
He splits open heaven and earth’s darkness; the serpent’s head falls, and ghosts and spirits tremble.
Master Huazang Min ascends the hall: “The multitude sell flowers, yet I alone sell pines. Their green hues are not as red as mine.
Calculated, they ultimately do not harmonize with the times; let us return to the midst of the verdant mists. One cannot help but laugh at the ancients for being thus.
"What do you say? This is much like fleeing from a mountain peak to a ravine, or avoiding drowning only to throw oneself into fire.
How could it compare to accepting one's lot and seeking out one or half of a person at the edge of the eight-foot staff and the five-inch hoe? Even so, Bao Ning does not want even half of one."
Why is this? "The wealthy lament that a thousand mouths are too few;

the poor resent that a single body is too many. Master Ren of Central India ascended the hall and said: "Of the spring's ninety days, half have already passed. The weather for nurturing flowers is perfectly harmonious.
On the branches of the rhododendron, the song of the oriole is fine. Do those who follow the worldly trends perceive this? Although it is thus, nevertheless— and so forth.
"How do you express it in a single phrase that penetrates both sound and form? 'The golden-reined horse neighs on the fragrant grasslands;
the jade-towered person is drunk beneath the apricot-blossom sky.
Master Huayan Jue ascended the hall and said: "When the Venerable Shishuang passed away, the assembly requested the Head Seat to succeed him."
Regarding the public case (gong'an) asked by Attendant Qian, the Master said: "The sphere of action of a true teacher is like fire melting ice;

he passes through the barrier of right and wrong, and with his full capacity, he forgets gain and loss. Everyone says that the Head Seat is stuck in 'one color,' yet the Attendant’s insight surpasses his master.
This can be called 'losing the essence while missing the source, utterly confused about direction and orientation. Little do they realize that the Head Seat is like a heron..."
The sparrows standing in the snow are of diverse species. One attendant is like a phoenix soaring through the crimson heavens, unentangled by golden nets;
one stands high atop a mountain peak, while another walks deep within the ocean floor. Each comes from their own direction, yet they meet together within the nine-layered city.
Do you wish now to recognize these two? Raising his whisk, he said: "A dragon lies coiled in the azure depths."
The wind on Mount Tan was piercingly cold. Lowering his whisk, he said: "A crane returns to the Milky Way, its back brushing the heavens.
When Master Tiansi of Tianning ascended the hall, he overturned the sea of birth and death and kicked over the shore of nirvana.
On this world there are no living people; in the Yellow Springs there are no dead men. He then took up his staff and said: "Today, Master Ne’s staff has—"
"This is the place of entrustment. Is there anyone who can take it up? Come forth and bear this burden! Is there anyone? Is there anyone?
After a long silence, he threw down his staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Those who know it exist are eating porridge and rice; those who do not know it exist are also eating porridge and rice.
How can one directly verify whether they have it or not, whether it is right or wrong, whether it is this or that?
If you cannot verify this, the work of study is still far from being accomplished. He gave a shout and descended from his seat.
Chan Master Jue of Mount Jun ascended the hall and said: "The more one looks up at it, the higher it rises; the more one drills into it, the firmer it becomes.

Looking for it, it seems to be in front; suddenly, it is behind. Do you all recognize it? If you do not recognize it, I shall explain it for you: 'The more one looks up at it, the higher it rises'—there is not even a hair’s breadth of separation.
At the vital ford, the passage is cut off, such that even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot escape. 'The more one drills into it, the firmer it becomes'—the true body is itself..."
Indeed! The birds sing and the flowers smile before the emerald cliffs. Looking toward them as being "in front," they are neither central nor partial;
they cut off the ten directions and their majesty subdues the great chiliocosm. Suddenly they are "behind"—a total exposure of the leak! How laughable that Yunmen hides his body in the Big Dipper!
*Du!* (A shout of realization.)
Chan Master Baohua Xian ascended the hall and said: "The rice gruel has been eaten; to place a head upon a head is to add feet to a snake by washing the bowl.
If you ask further how it is, you will only bring about your own defeat. After a long silence, he called out loudly to the assembly.
When the assembly raised their heads, the Master said, "Return to the hall for tea."
Chan Master Nanhua Bing ascended the hall and said: "This matter is most extraordinary; it is not obstructed by direct speech.
The old farmer from the eastern neighbor’s house has, according to custom, received a single piece of wood. It not only penetrates sound and form, but also accords with the times.
If you ask what school this belongs to, the eight strokes do not even touch a slant. He struck the meditation seat and descended.
Ascending the hall, he said: "I speak of it day after day; I bring it up from time to time. It is like the earth supporting a mountain—how much effort is required?
The parrot of Longxi is beloved by all, yet it is mostly for its ability to speak. Cease your deliberations; keep your companions. When the wise hear even a little, they should seize it with vigor.
There is another thing that is truly marvelous: the cat is uniquely adept at catching mice."
Ascending the hall, he stirred the air with his staff, saying, "He stirs the long river into butter and milk; yet the shrimp and crabs still have their eyes shut with rheum.
He struck the ground once and said, "He transforms the great earth into gold; yet the pauper remains as before, bare-boned and destitute."
Is it that you yourselves lack the capacity? Or is it that you are unwilling to take responsibility?
Among you, there may be a man capable of bearing this burden, yet how many have lost their wealth and incurred blame! Striking the desk once more, he said: "Do you understand?
When you reach the mountain of jewels, you must open your eyes; do not let yourself return in haste with empty hands."
Chan Master Longya Cai ascended the hall and cited the small assembly discourse of Master Sishin, which said: "If one discusses this matter, it is like a family that has three sons.
The first son is intelligent, wise, and filial; he receives guests, attends to visitors, and manages the family estate.
The second son is fierce, stubborn, and cunning; he is lustful and addicted to wine, lying prostrate in the streets and alleys."
He ruined the family estate. The third son was blind, deaf, and mute, unable to distinguish between beans and wheat; he could not even manage the basic task of eating his meals.
Among these three, Huanglong intended to select one for use. There is another fourfold set of possibilities: there is life within death.
"In life there is death; in death there is constant death; in life there is constant life. Use these four lines to test the monks of the world.
The Master said, "What do you call these 'four lines'? What are the surnames and names of the three people?
If you can recognize them, you will walk hand-in-hand with Huanglong, without the slightest interval between you. If this is not yet so, I cannot help but borrow water [to wash your face].
Offering flowers, they depart. The three persons share a single essence; their function is not a function. The four lines share a single resonance; they are both empty and not empty.
If you wish to recognize these three persons and the four lines: as the golden sun first rises, it is a mass of red.
Chan Master Penglai Qing ascended the hall and said: "A phrase and no-phrase are like a vine leaning against a tree; let the various quarters nod their heads as they will.
But when the tree falls and the vine withers, there is no plan to soar toward the heavens above, nor any scheme to sink into the earth below.
A person of keen intelligence who can fix a single eye upon this will see it moving freely in all directions—seven ways and eight ways. He raised his whisk and said: "Look!"
Look! One song, two songs—no one understands them. After the rain, the night pond’s autumn waters are deep.
Entering the hall, he said: "Within the cry of the cuckoo, the spring light fades; fallen flowers cover the ground, yet none can stay.
Upon the crystal palace, all traces of passage are gone; who can understand how to plant a rootless tree? Raising his staff, he said: "This here is the rootless one."
Now tell me, was the flower untied? After a long silence, he said: "Only because of the rain all night, another spring has passed.
Chan Master Heshan Xun ascended the hall and said: "The wheel that crushes and the axe that dwells on the mountain—when Buddhas and Patriarchs appear, they are not lightly granted [to others]."
Even if the world were filled with *amṛta* (the finest essence), if you have no precious vessel, how can you take it? Aha-ha! The God Mountain beats the gong;
Daowu performs the dance. The sweet melon is sweet all the way to its stem; the bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip.
Chan Master Guyshan ascended the hall and said: "To speak once and not again is already to fall into the second or third [level].

To meet face-to-face without raising an eyebrow turns into contrived fabrication. Even if one could strike a different chord to discern the future from the past, or see the whip's shadow and immediately set forth—"
If you turn back after merely gazing at the flagpole of the Buddha-land, I shall give you thirty blows right under your heels.

How much less can you hope to grasp the spark of a flint or catch a flash of lightning here? Your efforts are in vain; it is all a trivial matter. It would make the blue-eyed barbarian from the West laugh to tears.
(He strikes his staff and descends from the seat.)
Master Longxiang Gui ascended the hall and said: "Where the myriad functions do not reach, the eyes see forms and the ears hear sounds.
A single phrase stands forth in the open: the head wears the heavens, the feet tread upon the earth.

You all know only that today is the first day of the fifth month, yet you do not realize that the golden crow (the sun) hastens away in the dead of night, while the jade hare (the moon) ascends the eastern sea at dawn. He struck with his whisk.
Descending from his seat on the meditation platform, he ascended the hall and said: "Clearly there is no awakening; to have a dharma is delusion. You people cannot stand here;
you people cannot dwell here. If you stand, you are precarious; if you dwell, you are blind. You must simply ensure that your mind does not rest in the profound."

Sentences do not halt the mind; their application does not halt the mechanism. Once these three are clarified, there is no need for supervision or maintenance in any situation, as [the truth] manifests naturally;
there is no need for watchfulness, as it is naturally understood.
Even so, one must further know that there is a matter beyond this. Long rain, no clearing. Tsk!
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The eastern house lights the lamp; the western house sits in darkness.
The monk asked, "I do not understand the intent of this. The Master said, "When it is a horse, it is saddled;
when it is a donkey, it is made to grind. The monk bowed. The Master said, "A truly clever patch-robed monk needs only one [of these]. He then continued, "The horse is saddled; the donkey grinds."
A sharp-witted monk can only digest one. Even if the neighbor to the east lights his lamp clearly, it does not necessarily mean the neighbor to the west sits in the dark.
When asked about the meaning of the Westward Journey, the talkative teacher brings calamity upon himself.
Chan Master Yunju Wu ascended the hall and said: "The wall-gazing at Shaolin conceals the East Land within its breast;
ascending the hall at Mount Ouyang in the West, it fills the four quarters and the zenith and nadir.

This causes the mountains to be majestic while the palm of the hand remains level, the waters to be dark yet ever naturally clear, flowers to bear fruit in the void without being colorful, and a single leaf to fall without the wind shaking it. People have no dharma."
Thus one may receive instruction and inquiry. The Buddha has no mind, yet he can further accomplish it. With wild vegetables and plain rice, one extends the days;
letting things go as they are and following conditions, the Way is naturally efficacious. After all, how is it? At midday, strike three watches.
Chan Master Huanglong Zhong ascended the hall and said: “Lord Zhang drinks the wine and Lord Li gets drunk; Consider it carefully—it is inconceivable.
When Lord Li awakens from his drunkenness, he asks Lord Zhang: ‘Just now you made Lord Zhang feel quite ill-tempered.
Feeling ill-tempered? It would be better to go home and take a nap.’”

Chan Master Wugu ascended the hall and said: "The Buddha spoke of the three vehicles, the twelve divisions of scripture, and the sudden, gradual, partial, and complete teachings—do not speak of dreams before a fool.
The Patriarch came from the West to point directly to the human mind, to see one's nature and become a Buddha—do not speak of dreams before a fool.
Linji’s Three Mysteries, Yunmen’s Three Statements, and Dongshan’s Five Ranks—do not speak of dreams before a fool."
"One must not speak of dreams in the presence [of others]. When Nanming spoke thus, did he avoid being subject to scrutiny?
Therefore, the ancients said: 'If a stone man’s wit were like yours, he too would know how to sing a folk song. If you were like a stone man...'"
"The Snow Song should also be harmonized. "Is there anyone who can harmonize the Snow Song? "If there is, call him here to wash the old monk's feet.
He ascended the hall and, citing Zhaozhou’s address to the assembly, said: "The old monk sets aside the two times for meals and gruel; this is the use of a distracted mind."
At that place, the Master said: "Today is the first day of the sixth month. The attendant strikes the drum and the Elder ascends the hall.
You all come here together to employ your minds in a confused manner."
Master Baiyang Shun ascended the hall and said: "The rooster crows at the dawn moon; the dog barks at the withered stump.

These can only be realized in silence; they are difficult to enter through deliberation. Where the eye cannot see, the earth trembles and light is emitted; where words cannot reach, heaven and earth are dark and yellow.
A six-foot-tall official document from Fucheng originally comes from Qingjiang. O assembly, though clearly spoken, it is difficult for people to perceive."
Last night at the third watch, the moon shone through the window.
Entering the hall, he said: "The wind blows against the thatched roof, leaking from the ridge; the rain beats upon you, O *śrāmaṇeras*, and your eyes grow wet.
Though it is so clear, you do not realize it; instead, you come here and stand with bowed heads."
Chan Master Xian of Guizong ascended the hall and said: "Now, how do you speak the first phrase?

If you can speak it when the world has not yet been formed, before your parents were born, before the Buddha appeared in the world, and before the Patriarch came from the West—then even that would already be the second phrase.
How, then, do you speak the first phrase? Even if you could speak it with total perfection," he continued.
One cannot help but move from left to right. [Master] Zhuo struck his staff and descended from the seat.
Dharma Master Jing of Husheng ascended the hall and said: "The essential points for studying the Way do not go beyond what the former Nantang spoke of as the 'first phrase' and the 'last phrase.
Those who can pass through these have finished their work for a lifetime. If this is not yet the case, I shall further divide them up for you."
Having established these ten gates, have you each individually verified them within your own mind so that you may attain stability?
First, you must believe in the separate transmission outside the teachings. Second, you must know that there is a separate transmission outside the teachings.

Third, you must realize that the preaching of the insentient and the preaching of the sentient are non-dual. Fourth, you must see your nature as clearly as observing an object in the palm of your hand. One—

1. One must have a stable and secure foundation. 2. One must possess the eye that discerns the Dharma. 3. One must traverse the mysterious path of the birds. 4. One must be proficient in both civil and martial arts. 5.
One must suppress the heterodox and manifest the orthodox. 6. One must possess great capacity and great function. 7. One must act among those of different species.
Whoever wishes to perpetuate the lineage of the Dharma must exhaust these essential principles; only then can they sit upon the curved and low couch.
Zhangzi has received the prostrations of all people under heaven and dares to act as a teacher to the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
If he had not reached such a state, he would have been nothing but empty-headed all along; at some future time, Old Yama will certainly not let you off.
Chan Master Daochang Bian ascended the hall and said: "Picked up from the mouth of a fierce tiger; placed upon the head of a venomous snake.
Without further lashing out the mooring stake or rowing the oars, one turns the head to find another way of life. The old woman has been seen through by me;
there is a village feast at the Great Compassion Temple."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The five eyes are purified; the golden spring colors well up as evening falls. The five powers are attained; they blow down the emerald peach blossoms.
Only through realization can one know that it is difficult to fathom. He struck the meditation staff and said: "Who has obtained this single fragment? It flows through a hundred thousand households."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Third Patriarch said, 'Simply do not harbor hatred or attachment, and all will be clearly and transparently manifest. If I, this old monk, had seen him at that time, I would have given him a slap.
Tell me, was that hatred or was it attachment? Lately, the boundaries have become somewhat stricter; we no longer permit the use of false names or the subletting of land."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Touzi, “When a person who has undergone the great death returns to life, what then?

Touzi said, “Night travel is not permitted; one must reach the destination at first light. The Master said: “I suspect this is the essence of a thousand-year-old azure jade, transformed into a single slab of autumn-water bone.
The Sea God wished to protect it but could not; suddenly, one day, the head of the giant turtle lifted it forth.”
Master Jiaochongguang ascended the hall and said: "A phrase, no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree. Why do you act so foolishly?
When the tree falls and the vine withers, where does the phrase return? I know that all of you will ultimately fail to find its head or nose.
Why is this so? It is simply because when clarity reaches its peak, it causes what is attained to be delayed."
Chan Master Yan of Donglin ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to know the mind of all Buddhas, simply recognize it within the thoughts and actions of sentient beings.
If you wish to know the eternally abiding, unfading nature, simply realize it in the midst of the shifting and changing of the myriad things. Do you recognize it yet?
If you wish not to incur karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata."
Ascending the hall: It is the severe cold of mid-winter; there is no peace within the three realms. The wealthy enjoy happiness, while the poor suffer from hunger and cold.
Failing to recognize the profound essence, they mistakenly fixate on the shape of the platter. Why is this so? To place the ox’s head upon its tail, and to look southward at the Big Dipper.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Drop by drop of water, drop by drop of ice. The heavens are cold, the people are cold. The wind moves, the banner moves.
Yunmen’s fan leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens, striking the nostrils of Śakra. A sea bream from the Eastern Ocean receives a blow, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin.
This is none other than what you all constantly utilize throughout the twelve periods of the day."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The gateway of universal penetration is opened wide in eight directions. If you enter through the gate, you are unfit for conversation;
you must enter the gateless gate before you can sit within the inner sanctum. Therefore it is said: 'All Tathāgatas of the past have already perfected this gate;
all Bodhisattvas of the present now each enter its perfect luminosity; those of the future shall likewise do so.'"
Students, you should rely upon such a Dharma. Fortunately, there exists such a vast tradition from the various sages of the past;
yet, being unable to inherit it, you would rather shamefully abandon yourselves, like thieves breaking through walls—how unmanly!
I dare ask the assembly: how does one enter the gateless gate? After a long silence, he said: "Not only Avalokiteśvara, but I too have realized it from within."

Ascending the Hall: Long have I lingered in this guest house, At the edge of my hometown where the evening sun sets. Rain hangs from the eaves for three months; Water submerges the lotuses of both lakes.
The cauldron leaks as the oil lamp burns low; Wood grows thick, filling the hearth with smoke. I have already forgotten thoughts of north and south; Looking out, the horizon is entirely level plains.
Chan Master Zhongji ascended the hall and said: "Ten thousand ages of eternal sky; a single day of wind and moon.

One must not allow the wind and moon of a single day to obscure the eternal sky of ten thousand ages, nor must one fail to illuminate the wind and moon of a single day through the eternal sky of ten thousand ages.
But what is this 'wind and moon of a single day'? All people dread the heat, yet I love the length of summer days. [He burned incense.]

The wind comes from the south; the halls and pavilions give rise to a subtle coolness. Whether you understand it or not, you must by all means avoid taking it upon yourself as something to be grasped.
Chan Master Xiujian of Jianfu ascended the hall and said: "Words are uttered, yet they are not sounds—what is this? Before form, there is no object—do not confuse the needle and the chisel.
Having passed through the Dragon Gate, the winds and waves are even more perilous. Tsk!"
Chan Master Guifeng Guang ascended the hall. "For several days now, the summer heat has been like burning; there is nowhere for this whole body to find rest.

To dwell upon this is already a source of affliction for people, yet this is not yet the true affliction. There is something further: if one does not clarify the matter within one's own person, that is affliction.
This is why Great Master Bodhidharma was afflicted—he wished to swallow it for the sake of all of you."
Yet it was caught by the narrowness of the throat; wishing to spit it out for the sake of all people, it was obstructed by the teeth.

Unable to grasp it and unable to let it go, he suffered in affliction for nine years. Had he not encountered the Second Patriarch and spared his own life, he would have often found no way to turn back, suffering until death.
This is what is meant by "if the ancestors do not resolve their karmic debts, the calamity will reach their descendants. Later, [it was resolved by] the Lotus...
The Abbot reached this point and was vexed, refusing to stay; Master Nanyue Huizhong reached this point and was vexed, refusing to go down the mountain.
Furthermore, Linji and Deshan exhausted their own efforts—like prying with a wooden wedge—but were vexed by the fact that the alms bowl has no handle.
Today at Guifeng, I shall for their sake increase their ignorance over these idle matters, and for all of you, I shall explain them from the beginning.
He broke [the staff] and struck it once against the desk, saying: "One person has his cheek exposed behind the head; another has no teeth before the gate.
Furthermore, several others have one side of their nostrils missing. There is no need for further investigation. You all should stop standing here drowsing;
you do not realize that the rice baskets and cooking pots in your own homes have all been lost at once. If you..."
"I do not believe it; simply go home and investigate for yourself.
Chan Master Kai Shan Xian ascended the hall and said: "Standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high—where the Buddhas of the three periods have no place to set foot.
This is so, yet it is far too unapproachable for human sentiment. Let down a single thread of the Way, and the oceans of lands in the ten directions emit light and shake the earth."
It is indeed so. But what can be done about this "muddying the clay and mixing the water"? You must know that where a single thread-way is penetrated, there stands a wall ten thousand fathoms high;

where a wall stands ten thousand fathoms high, there is a single thread-way. Grasping sideways and using upside down, pressing straight and lifting from the side—like a flash of lightning or a crash of thunder, like a cliff collapsing and stones shattering—it is indeed so.
Yet, it still falls within the gate of transformation. Here, even standing on a wall ten thousand fathoms high is required.

There is no engagement. Even passing through a single thread of the Way, there is no engagement. Being unapproachable to human sentiment, muddying the waters and blending with the clay—there is no engagement in any of this.
This very "no engagement" is itself "no engagement. It is so; yet it lacks the principles of the Buddha-dharma.

If you wish to understand it now, simply go ask Yunmen about the "dry shit-stick."
Chan Master Yuwang Guang ascended the hall and said: "Seven hands and eight feet, three heads and two faces; ears hear not, eyes see not.
Suffering and joy, adversity and favor, are forged into a single whole. Now tell me, what is it? When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it;
carry it home in a bottomless basket."
Chan Master Zhaojue Bian ascended the hall for a discourse: "A hair’s breadth of error and heaven and earth are separated.

Even if they can speak with words arising like clouds and appearing like rain, they are merely toads transforming into dragons;

One turn of phrase: for now, rejoice that there is no connection. Do you understand? How shameful! The World-Honored One—his face being red is not as good as straightforward speech. Great or small?"

The Venerable Yue’s mouth was like a millstone; today, while lecturing on the sutra for this questioning monk, he unwittingly revealed the entire commentary all at once, and then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "I shall silence my own mouth, yet I must speak; I shall block your ears, yet you must listen. Do not, by any means, let this pass you by.
Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and said that the Great Sage of Sizhou was sitting in meditation at Hongzhou, selling his wares in the middle of the crossroads.
What is this? It is a root-cutting straw sandal and a peaked-brim bamboo hat."
Master Jing of Xichan ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to correctly grasp the guiding thread, you must first let the great earth fall into ruin.
If you wish to come forward and strike with a snow-blade, you cannot avoid exposing its sharp edge.
At such a time, setting aside for a moment the question of whether Śākyamuni could have shown his head, how would you all explain this: what is it like to hide one's body within a horse's stirrup?"

Ascending the hall, he said: "One who excels at combat does not look back for his own head; one who excels at war surely secures the merit. Once that merit is secured, peace prevails as a matter of course.
When peace prevails, one rests on high pillows without anxiety. Lay aside the three-foot sword; cease playing with the single bow.
Return the horses to the southern slopes of Mount Hua; release the oxen into the wilds of Peach Grove. Let the winds blow according to the seasons..."
The rains fall in their proper season; the fisherman sings and the woodcutter dances. Even so, there still remains the transformative influence of sovereigns such as Yao and Shun.
How can this compare to the fact that Heaven and Earth cannot be contained, and even Yao and Shun do not know their names? The entire household takes no account of matters of rise or fall;
they simply love to occupy the Lake Dongting together with the clouds.
Chan Master Jianfu Ben ascended the hall and said: "I would give thirty blows of the staff to one who bows high to Śākyamuni but does not prostrate to Maitreya.
Why? Because he only knows how to climb higher step by step, but does not know how to let go from emptiness.
I would give thirty blows of the staff to one who pulls the plow for the eastern neighbor and drags the harrow for the western neighbor. Why? Because he only knows how to let go from emptiness..."
"Down! One does not climb higher with every step. When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, is there any fault in it?
Is there anyone among you who can point out the error? If you can point it out, we shall walk hand-in-hand to the south side of Mount Sumeru."
If you cannot discern this through inspection, then the old crow in the sack, though alive, is as good as dead.
[Ascending the hall: Śākyamuni shut his room in Magadha; Vimalakīrti sealed his mouth in Vaiśālī;
Subhūti proclaimed non-speaking to manifest the Way; Śakra and Brahmā transcended sight and hearing while raining down flowers. O Great Assembly! This lot is no match for anything!

"Liú Hàn! Without cause, you have taken the ancestral fields and private lands, drawn up private contracts, and demarcated their boundaries according to the four limits—square, round, long, or short—all at once.
This has resulted in your descendants for a thousand years hence having not a single tile to cover their heads above, nor a place to set a needle-point below.
If Boshan had seen this at the crossroads at that time..."
Dig a bottomless, deep pit at the head of the road and call them all to be buried therein at once, so as to spare them from mutual obstruction. Why is this?
Have you not seen that "a family prospers when there is a filial son, and a state becomes hegemonic when it possesses a strategic minister"?
Chan Master Xing of Lingyan ascended the hall and said: "To have already seen through [the matter] yet let it pass—that is the straw sandals of a patch-robed monk.
To manifest the form of an asura and perform a woman’s prostration—that is the bewitchment of a wild fox spirit.
To draw a circle and drop a dot within the void—that is the trickery of a child. To strike the cheek with a palm and then sweep the sleeves and depart—this is precisely karma."
Consciousness is vast and boundless, with no fundamental basis upon which to rely.
Even if you were to cut it off completely at the moment before the black bean has sprouted, you would still not have earned the right to receive Lingyan’s staff. I ask the assembly:
tell me, where does the crux of his teaching lie? Do you understand? Since the spring colors came to Songshao, the thirty-six peaks have remained green.
Now, Chan Master Chong of Jingci ascended the hall. "The World-Honored One spoke what was not spoken; Kāśyapa heard what was not heard. He struck the meditation staff and said:
"Where do the flowing waters and yellow leaves come from? An ox, trailing crows of the cold season, passes through a distant village."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised up the words of his late teacher, Wan’an: “Sitting on the Buddha’s throne, he hacks at the Buddha’s feet;

he does not revere Confucius of the Eastern House, but instead goes to a foreign land to practice ritual and music. The Master said, “It is not that our late teacher did not enter the mud and the water, but alas, the cicada clings to the withered wood;
its weeping is exhausted, yet it looks back not once. He struck the meditation staff and said, “Truly, there is no looking back!”
From the depths of my heart, Jingci bows three prostrations to you, Xiangshengzi.
Entering the hall for the discourse: The Buddhas of the three periods speak of existence within non-existence—like picking up a flower-needle from a heap of weeds.

The Patriarchs of the six generations seek non-existence within existence—like a monkey reaching for the moon reflected in water. Setting aside these two paths, how shall one explain this? I, this fellow, do not concern myself with it.
Throughout the day, he gazes upon the clouds over Lake Dongting as he contemplates the affairs of rise and fall.
Zen Master Yuan of Zhaojue ascended the hall and said: "Melting bottles, basins, hairpins, and bracelets into a single gold; churning buttermilk, curd, and clarified butter into a single flavor.
Thus, guest and host harmonize their paths, the internal and external are at peace, and the five ranks of ruler and subject are all thoroughly penetrated."
These four kinds of discernment form a single thread. If one lets go, there is a fine drizzle and a rustling autumn wind;
if one holds fast, all is empty and void—who would dare look upon it with a direct eye? Tell me, is it better to let go for the sake of others, or is it better to hold fast for the sake of others?
He spoke again: "Casually, it is as if the autumn wind has arrived; unintentionally cooling others, people cool themselves."
Chan Master Huazang Quan ascended the hall and said: "Zen, Zen—without faction, without partiality. When deluded, one is separated by a thousand miles;
when awakened, it is right at the edge of the lips. Thus, when a monk asked Shishuang, 'What is Zen?
Shishuang replied, 'A brick for a deer. Again, a monk asked Muzhou, 'What is Zen? Muzhou replied, 'Fierce fire frying oil. And again, a monk asked Shoushan..."
"This is Zen. Shanshan said, "A monkey climbing a tree, its tail trailing behind its head. "O Great Assembly! There is no cross-path on the Way; the place one stands is solitary and perilous.
These three great elders traveled upon a living path before sound, employing spiritual mechanisms beyond kalpas.

Yet, if one were to examine them with the authentic eye of a monk, there would be no lack of distinctions in their excellence. One was like Zhang Liang entering the fray; the other was like Xiang [Yu]..."
Regarding the use of troops by Yu, if one person can discern the enemy as Kongming did, they may stand shoulder to shoulder with the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Even so, should a monk suddenly come forth and say, "Elder, you have split the discourse into two separate pieces," what then?
Just now you said that the Way has no crossroads, no factions, and no partiality; yet now you have again divided it into so many degrees of superiority and inferiority.
How will you respond to this? Do you understand? "Holding hands while climbing the mountain, we exert our strength together; the breath passing through the throat is known only by oneself."
Chan Master Daomian of Daguang ascended the hall and said: "The trees have shed their leaves and the sky is empty; the heavens are cold and the waters are frozen.
