When the lotus leaves move without a breeze, there is certainly a fish swimming beneath.
The Outline for Recitation:
Chan Master Qun of Yuanwu Preaches on Ascending the Hall to View the Tripitaka. Auspicious smoke swirls and auspicious qi mingles.
The public case is already perfected; who will strike upon it? He then said: "The great scripture within the dust has unfathomable boundaries. With clear wisdom and purity..."

Only those with the eye of wisdom can extract it. It is such that the ocean of the Dharma-nature is like the interlacing net of Indra, and the divine light of intelligent illumination is like the fierce flames of a great furnace.
Today, fortunately, we encounter the vast sway of imperial grace and the level path of the Emperor’s Way;
there is a donor of great mind who triggers the mechanism for you, causing everyone to open wide their eight-character gates, until the crimson sash [of realization] is attained.
When the jade tablets are unfurled and the scrolls are spread, the patterns and colors are already manifest; each should be taken up accordingly.
Yet, how do you speak that single phrase which does not fall into the realm of written words? "The wind is cold and still within the hall; the intent of a thousand ages is clear."

The Patriarch ascended the hall for the assembly: "Upon the crown of the thousand sages, the ocean of lands can be contained; within the life-vein of the patch-robed monks, no true mechanism is permitted.
Yet, let us open one further path: from Buddha appearing as Patriarch, and from Patriarch realizing Buddhahood. Seal upon seal is without error; mechanism upon mechanism is perfectly realized.
At Vulture Peak, the golden-colored monk held up a flower to show the assembly, thereby establishing this very school’s tradition. The golden-colored *dhūta*.
Having received the sublime instructions, [the lineage] has extended from the four groups and seven patriarchs of India to the two groups and three patriarchs of this land.

Since the dispersal of the assembly at Caoxi, for several hundred years, monasteries have stood side by side; each has grasped the jewel of the spiritual serpent, and every person has embraced the jade of Mount Jing.
Possessing both illumination and function, as well as skillful means and reality, they have upheld the lofty winds of the ancestral school and maintained the True Dharma Eye.

In the Treasury [of the Dharma], it is essential that though the hundred rivers flow in different currents, they all return to the great ocean; though there are a thousand layers and a hundred enclosures, they do not emerge from anything other than a single source.
Therefore, it is said: "The twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven were thus; the sixth patriarch of the land of Tang was thus;
the various elder masters throughout the world’s monasteries were thus; and this mountain monk is also thus. Now tell me, what is the matter of being "thus"?
How will you deliberate upon this? Can you bring it forth? Can you distinguish the black from the white with clarity?
This mountain monk, without sparing even two strands of his eyebrows, shall break it open for you all. He then took up his staff and said: "Do you see?
All the Buddhas of the three periods, the patriarchs of successive generations, and the old monks of the world—all are emitting a great light from the tip of this staff."

Clarifying: the manifestation of expedient means, the manifestation of reality, the manifestation of the capacity [of the practitioner], and the manifestation of the environment. These list the five ranks of ruler and subject and open up the essential mysteries of the three patriarchs.

When capacity and environment meet, they are like the tips of arrows meeting point-to-point. A single word contains three phrases; though they share the same source, the circular forms and their respective conditions differ.
If you understand this thoroughly, you will bring all affairs of your life to rest upon the tips of the hundred grasses, leaving not even a trace of the root or trunk behind. Thus it is heard.
"Pure sound and external phrases—do not seek them within the words. Should this not yet be so, this mountain monk cannot help but once again wade through the mud and water.

"If Bodhidharma had not come to the Eastern Land and the Second Patriarch had not gone to the Western Heaven, every person would stand like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, and each individual would have their constant radiance ever-present.
[He struck his staff once and descended from the seat.]

Ascending the hall at the Lotus Assembly: Before Vipaśyin, a thousand petals manifested as an auspicious omen; the God among Gods appeared amidst the earth as a rare Udumbara flower displaying its grace.
Thus it was that the entire realm was never concealed, yet his whole body was without shadow or form, manifesting as the Great Lotus King.
Surrounding it are a thousand lotus seats; on each petal is a Śākyamuni, and on each filament is a Maitreya.
Thus it is in every atom, in every land, in every place, and in every thought-moment. A single atom lifts up the entire earth, and a single flower blooms as the world arises.
This may be called the most supreme among the supreme, the doubly marvelous among the marvelous. It moves the compassionate spirit so that auspicious vapors condense before the stupa.
The true countenance is revealed by the side of the Arhat Cave; the Dharma assembly is solemn as humans and devas gather from all quarters.

Arriving at this point, what should one discuss? Is it permissible to speak of the profound and the subtle? Is it permissible to speak of Buddhas and Patriarchs? Is it permissible to cite the ancients and the present?
Can manifesting activity and manifesting function be separated? All of this has been brought forth by the great masters of the past and future.
Right now, it is better not to stir anything at all, but simply to present this one ready-made koan.

If you can realize it, the flower of the human mind will blossom and shine, illuminating the lands of the ten directions everywhere. At this very moment, when things are thus, credit is attributed to the source.
How do you express it in a single phrase? Do you understand? "All under heaven celebrates the Sage who returns to the light;
may we see the Yellow River clear for the hundredth time.
Master Yuan of Longmen, for the sake of his donor, ascended the hall to recite the *Buddhapiṭaka-hṛdaya-sūtra*: *Oṃ cili cili*.
"Oṃ bulim oṃ bulim. Great assembly, what kind of words are these? What is their meaning? Is there anyone who can understand them?
If you say they are words, they do not constitute words; if you say they possess a principle, they do not constitute a principle.
It may be said that they are beyond the reach of verbal expression and the scope of conceptual discrimination. The sages of old called them 'esoteric words' (guhyavākya)."
It is also called "True Word" (Mantra), for all sounds and voices arise from it, and all speech and teachings issue forth from it.
While I was recently reading the scriptures, I obtained the Seven-Syllable Dhāraṇī, which can extinguish a thousand calamities and accomplish ten thousand virtues.
Now, before you all, I shall recite this Seven-Syllable Dhāraṇī once. Listen attentively, everyone. [He then remained silent.]
Then, he silently bent his fingers from the first to the seventh and asked, "Do you all hear me?
Fearing that some might not have heard, he raised them once more. Again, he silently bent his fingers from the first to the seventh and asked, "Do you hear me, Great Assembly?
Only Buddhas and Buddhas can know this; all other sentient beings are utterly at a loss. There is a skillful means called...
He spoke again, reciting a verse: "Now I shall further set forth the three sections to clearly explain this seven-character mantra, titled the *Buddhōṣṇīṣa-hṛdaya Sūtra*.
Great assembly, do you understand its essential meaning? Wait while I, this mountain monk, offer an explanation for you."
Each and every word must be known for its point of descent. If one speaks of the Buddha, it is simply the person themselves; there is nothing else.

If one speaks of the Crown (the *uṣṇīṣa*), day and night it radiates light, illuminating the realm before one. If one speaks of the Mind, when observed it is without form, yet when functioning it is profound. If one speaks of the Sūtra...
Understanding speech and being able to speak is not the sound itself. If one discusses the fast (*zhāi*), all that is done and enacted is perfectly harmonious.

If one discusses the vow (*yuàn*), it is as if one’s body were within the Dragon Gate courtyard. If one discusses realization (*liǎo*), there is no anxiety and no doubt; the mind is luminously clear. The mind is luminously clear.
It increases blessings and longevity while diminishing calamities; when measured, its merits are vast and inconceivable. Mount Sumeru is not large by comparison, and the vast ocean is but small.
What the mountain monk has just spoken is the True Word (Mantra). Worldly people know only the words, but do not know the Truth.
If one does not know the truth, all that is spoken is false. What is called "True Speech" (mantra)? It is called True Speech because it can give rise to the myriad schools.
It is also named the King of Samādhis; it is also named the Summit of Ten Thousand Characters; it is also named the Subtle and Wondrous Phrases; it is also named the Great Secret Dhāraṇī.
To receive and uphold it with a sincere heart brings great spiritual efficacy. This is what is known as the Seven-Character Mantra of the Mountain Monk.
Then, counting on his fingers, he said: "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. Chanting and upholding [the mantra] is entirely secret;
it is like a person personally entering a mountain of jewels, from which all manner of rare treasures emerge. He stood for a long time.

Chan Master Qiji of Dongshan ascends the hall at the invitation of his dharma friends from the Lotus Society: Gradually the skin becomes like chicken skin and the hair like crane feathers; the father is young while the son is old.
Look at those walking steps—limping and unsteady—they would put even Wood Seat (Muzhuo) to shame.

Even if gold and jade fill the hall, one must still watch out for the thief who steals in broad daylight. How can one escape decay, decline, aging, and illness? This is precisely when you should exert your full brilliance. Let it be as you will.
A thousand kinds of happiness—this fellow ought to be free. Impermanence will inevitably arrive; return to the hall and go for tea.
There is only the path of cultivation; as before, strike and circle around it. Simply recite the name of Amitābha Buddha;
if you cannot achieve salvation through such recitation, he said again: "Agh! This living path has already been pointed out directly and straightforwardly by Master Shandao."
It is so. You all come and go every morning and evening along this very path; why then do you pass Amitābha Buddha right before your faces?

If you can realize it here, you may immediately eliminate the obstacle of delusion, pull out the arrow of hesitation, cut through the net of doubt, cross the river of ignorance and craving, fell the dense forest of the mind, wash away the turbidity of mental defilements, rectify the mind’s crookedness, and sever the mind’s [entanglements].
After traversing birth and death, one then turns toward that other shore. Raising one’s feet, one takes a step toward the place where even Buddhas and Patriarchs have not trodden;
opening one’s mouth, one utters a single word toward the place where even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot reach through verbal explanation.
This calls back Master Shandao to seek a different path for practice. Otherwise, one will continue as before, abandoning one’s father to flee and wander lost in foreign lands.
"Clashing to the east and bumping against the west—how bitter it is, Amitābha Buddha!
This was the Dharma hall discourse delivered by Chan Master Yuansou Duan upon the conclusion of the imperial viewing of the Tripiṭaka.
"Within the treasury of Vairocana is a great scripture, its measure equal to the three-thousandfold world system; it records all matters within that three-thousandfold world system."
All [the worlds] were exhausted without remainder. Now, the Emperor, the Son of Heaven, with his pure celestial eye, beheld this great sutra scroll within a single atom.

He earnestly dispatched an envoy to bestow imperial incense and commanded the monastic officials throughout the realm to break open this atom and bring forth this sutra scroll, so that all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm may know that within every single atom there exists such a sutra scroll.
Each and every fascicle of the sutra contains such passages; each and every passage contains such wondrous meanings;
each and every wondrous meaning possesses such marvels, such excellence, such vastness, and such sovereignty.
This morning, following the ritual of scattering flowers, I have been commanded to ascend this seat as a mountain monk to proclaim the unsurpassed Prajñā and manifest its significance.
I repent for the aforementioned merits: the ocean of wisdom of all various dharma-gates; the ocean of the marks and virtues of all various causes and effects;
the ocean of all various practices, conducts, and vows; the ocean of all various skillful means of instruction; the ocean of the ultimate perfection of all various environments and inhabitants;

May the four quarters be relieved of the anxieties of war, and may the myriad people delight in the occupations of farming and sericulture.

This place is its boundary.

"There is no Sangha. He planted his staff on the ground and said, "Mountains, rivers, the great earth, grasses, trees, and forests all enter into equality within this very place.
Those who have not yet attained liberation shall attain liberation; those who have not yet attained nirvana shall attain nirvana.
Although this resides within the domain of the patch-robed monk, it is like water in a household afflicted by a venomous spirit—one must not let even a single drop touch it. He leaned against it.
[The Master] leaned on his staff and descended from the seat.
To the Imperial Decree for Viewing the Tripitaka, he ascended the hall [and said]: "The hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates all return to the single square inch of the mind;

the wondrous virtues as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are all contained within the source of the heart. Those of great merit cultivate them; those of great merit receive them. Therefore, throughout the lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges..."
Without receiving their majestic spiritual power, even the grasses, trees, insects, and creeping things all rely upon their transformative nourishment.

Now, as this Dharma assembly is opened wide and the treasury of teachings is grandly revealed, there are layer upon layer of gates of merit and various oceans of life-span. Like heaven universally covering, like earth universally supporting;
like the sun universally shining, like the wind universally blowing. Confucius said, "I have long been praying. He spoke again, raising [his voice]:
Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty once entered a monastery and asked a monk, "What sutra are you reading?
The monk replied, "The *Benevolent Kings Sutra for the Protection of the State*. The Emperor said, "Since this is my own sutra, why has it ended up in your hands? The monk was unable to respond.
Later, Xuedou spoke on his behalf, saying: "The August Heaven has no favorites; it assists only those with virtue. The Master said:
"If one were to ask Yongzuo, he would simply respond with 'Ten-thousand years! Ten-thousand years! as prescribed in the scripture for receiving the imperial crown."

Ascending the hall to preach on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra: Throughout the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below, in every atom and every world-system, there is nothing that does not belong to this Flower Treasury World-Ocean. There is high and low, broad and narrow;
there is complete and incomplete, equal and unequal; there is pure and impure; there is short life and long years. Now tell me: what is it?
The Tathāgata Vairocana is currently preaching the Dharma in the world-system of Anāga.
Furthermore, what Dharma does he preach? Does he preach the Dharma of the Three Vehicles? Does he preach the Dharma of the One Vehicle? Does he preach the Dharma of the Unsurpassed Vehicle?
Or is there nothing at all that is preached? Try to say it! If you can say it, I grant you the power to purify Buddha-fields and sport with supernatural faculties, O sentient being.
Sentient and insentient beings alike realize and enter [this state]. If you say you cannot attain it, you will drift and sink within the sea of birth and death.
When the donor looks upon the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* during the formal assembly, he realizes the wondrous principle and possesses constant, clear knowledge.

With a single, even-minded composure, he remains perpetually without leakage. Putting on clothes and eating food are merely ordinary matters; seeing forms and hearing sounds are like being deaf and blind. Only...

One may enter the Buddha’s realm but must not enter Māra’s. Once one has penetrated the ten kinds of Zen barriers and emerged from the domain of the five aggregates (*skandhas*), there is nothing that is not the work of the Buddha in every place, and every single thing is a site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). In wine shops and brothels, there is no hindrance whatsoever;
one may pass freely through dragon palaces and tiger dens. Thus, one may enter Māra and may also enter the Buddha; thereafter, both Buddha and Māra are...
Sentient beings and sages are both discarded; neither nirvana is grasped nor samsara is inhabited. I declare that my great task is finished.
Since the staff is no longer here, I shall give you thirty blows with the handle of the broom.
Chan Master Da’an Zhuang ascended the hall for the Dharma Flower Assembly. “For a long time I have kept this matter hidden and did not strive to speak of it quickly;
now I shall speak of it, so each of you should listen well. After a long silence, he said: “I do not dare to slight you;
you shall all become Buddhas.”

Chan Master Zhuo’an was invited by the Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport and Pacification Commissioner, the Marquis of Gongshun, Layman Wu Shizai, to the Wéntōng Pagoda Temple in Huai City to inaugurate a Huayan Dharma Assembly;
he then ascended the hall and addressed the assembly: "The realm of a great man is not known except by a great man;
such extraordinary causes and conditions do not occur except through extraordinary coincidence. This mountain monk has traveled far from Yuanshui to arrive here."

Huang Quai. On this journey, he passed through prefectures, commanderies, counties, and districts, as well as rivers, lakes, streams, and seas. The total distance traveled exceeded one thousand *li*, and the journey took fifteen days.
Throughout it all, there was no perception of coming or going, no perception of duration or brevity, and no perception of adversity or favor.

There is no characteristic of motion or stillness. Thus it is said: "By observing the directions one knows that there is going; yet the goer does not arrive at any direction. It is further said: "In going, there is truly no going;
in coming, there is truly no coming. And again: "The two characteristics of motion and stillness are clearly seen as not arising.
If you can see through this point, you will be able to interweave worldly and world-transcending dharmas, attaining mastery over motion, stillness, going, and coming. It is thus.
Thus, since this mountain monk has arrived here, he has not departed from the patriarch’s chamber; yet even before arriving here,

there was not a single day that he did not walk hand-in-hand with the Great Governor, Layman Shiweng, nor a single day that he did not traverse the Flower Treasury World (*Huazangjie*) together with the honorable officials and virtuous friends present before us—
wherein phenomena are unimpeded, principle is unimpeded, phenomena and principle are mutually unimpeded, and each phenomenon is unimpeded within every other phenomenon.

Unobstructed. This is what is called the extraordinary causes and conditions of the Great Being’s realm, which have been fully realized and perfected one by one long before this discourse was even raised.
Since this is so, tell me: regarding the establishment of this *bodhimaṇḍa* and the reopening of the Universal Radiance Assembly (*Samantaprabhā-parṣad*) right now—whose affair is this?
It flings wide the eyes of all living beings across the great earth, until they are moved to sing in joy.
On the road, Master Mochun Men, Full of Huayan, ascends the hall. "The Dharma-realm of the Avatamsaka is the non-obstruction of principle and phenomena;
repentance for transgressions and the elimination of calamities are like winning both colors at once. He suddenly picks up his staff and says, "Assembly, Venerable Dushun is coming!"
Holding his staff, he murmured: "In Huai State, the ox eats the grain; in Yi State, the horse has a bloated belly.
Seeking a physician throughout the world, one applies moxibustion to the left shoulder of a pig. Do you all see this? If you do see it, you cannot avoid adding a head atop a head.
If you do not see it, your daily life is grand and open, without concealment; fundamentally, we are all one with the body of Vairocana.
The Opening Address for the Water and Land Assembly:

Chan Master Ying’an Hua ascends the seat at the request of Wang, the Official of the Mechanisms (Ji Yí), who is the younger brother of the State Councilor (Shūmì Xiānggōng), to perform the Water and Land rites.
The Master addresses the assembly, saying: "A great person possesses great vision; one of great wisdom attains great function. Ascending to the Hall of Great Liberation, he expounds..."

This is the meaning of Great Liberation. Therefore, although the Lord Privy Councilor, the Grand Chancellor, manifests coming and going for the sake of worldly beings, his ultimate essence is utterly unmoving and unchanging.
Thus, he does not abide when enticed, nor does he turn back when called;
neither Buddhas nor patriarchs can arrange him, and to this day he has no fixed location. In every atom and every world-system, he universally manifests majestic radiance.
In every object and at every point, the supreme form is fully manifested. Most excellent among the excellent, most extraordinary among the extraordinary.
Other realms and this world are entirely the pure land of the mind; the human realm and the heavens are one and the same true state. At such a time as this, tell me:
where is the State Councilor, Grand Marshal, and Senior Minister, the Palace Attendant, right now? In his hand he holds the golden wheel that governs both killing and giving life.
A sharp sword—dare anyone look directly at it?

At the Beiji Assembly, the Master ascended the seat and called to the assembly, saying: "Great wisdom is profoundly clear; its essence has neither coming nor dwelling. Its brilliance surpasses the sun and moon; its vastness is like the great void.
Heaven and earth rely on this for their covering and supporting; the sun and moon rely on this for their shining and presiding. The mountains..."
The mountains are made majestic by this; the rivers and lakes are made to flow by this. The sages and saints are made awe-inspiring and numinous by this;
ordinary people find peaceful sustenance in this. Those who died in battle achieve transcendence through this;
enemies and foes attain liberation through this. The Buddhas manifest themselves through this; the Patriarchs transmit the single dharma through this. All people [attain realization] through this.
Compassionate Rescue. Guangxiao used this as a skillful means. He suddenly picked up his staff and said:
"The Old Man Śākyamuni is right now emitting a great radiance from the tip of this mountain monk’s staff. This light is pure, indestructible, and unmixed;
its rays interlace one another without distinction between front and back. It enters universally into every atom and is fully manifested in every world-system. Thereafter, it becomes immeasurable."
Each and every one becomes immeasurable; within the great, the small appears, and within the small, the great appears. Upon the tip of a single hair, he manifests a jeweled royal land;
sitting within a speck of dust, he turns the Great Dharma Wheel. Now tell me, where do you all see Old Śākyamuni?
If you see him on the head of this staff, you have not yet seen him. If you see him within the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, you have not yet seen him either.
Nor have they yet seen him present. Since it is not like this, after all, where can one see Old Śākyamuni?
[The Master] strikes the ground once with his staff and says: "May he now attain the fruit and become a Treasure King, again delivering as many beings as there are sands in the Ganges."

Chan Master Yuansou Duan ascended the seat at Jinshan Temple in the imperial court for the Water and Land (Shuilu) ceremony. Having finished offering incense and making prayers for the Emperor, he said:
"The entirety of worlds as numerous as unspeakably unspeakable atoms is this very adamantine essence—purely naked and beyond all grasping.
The entirety of worlds as numerous as unspeakably unspeakable atoms is this very treasure..."

Awaken to the true mind; it is radiantly bare, without any deficiency. It is like the sky universally covering, like the earth universally supporting, like the sun universally shining, and like the wind universally blowing.
There is not a single moment when it is not pervasive; there is not a single place where it does not reach; there is not a single principle that is not complete.

There is not a single thing that is not fully present; in every atom and every world-realm, it is brilliant and unobstructed from all eight directions. In every object and at every point, the ten directions are thoroughly permeated.
One may take a single blade of grass and manifest it as the sixteen-foot golden body of the Buddha, or take that sixteen-foot golden body and treat it as a single blade of grass.
Within the belly, billions of Jambudvīpa worlds appear; within a single room, thirty-two thousand lion thrones surge forth. Seven times advancing, eight times retreating...

Manifesting a thousand transformations and myriad changes, turning left and right with nothing that is not permissible, the Buddhas of the three periods of time have, by means of this true body and this true mind, sat upon the precious lotus flower to achieve equal and perfect enlightenment.
They ferry across the four modes of birth and serve as a bridge and boat for the nine realms of existence.
The six generations of patriarchs, by means of this true body and this true mind, opened the gate of ambrosia to widely deliver the multitudes.
This chapter enlightens the blind and deaf and brilliantly illuminates the ignorant and muddled.

For generations, world-rulers and sovereign emperors have taken this true body and this true mind to establish the ultimate standard for the people and to open the foundation of great peace for the world, rescuing the common folk from the depths of suffering and turmoil.

The entire world is placed upon a bedrock foundation. The present Emperor, Sovereign of the Great Yuan World, by means of this orthodox embodiment and this sincere mind, has been able to inherit the great design and ascend to the Great Treasure Throne.

Throughout ten billion Mount Sumerus and ten billion seas of fragrant water, wherever the sun and moon shine and the wind and rain reach, all submit to his majestic spirit and return to his transformative nurture—even unto this...

On this day, a special imperial edict was issued, earnestly dispatching an envoy to Jinshan Guzeshen Temple to perform, in accordance with the ritual protocols of Emperor Wu of the Liang Dynasty, the Great Water-Land Assembly for the Spirits of Heaven and Earth and the Living and the Dead over seven days and nights.

Various kinds of incense were burned, various kinds of lamps were lit, various kinds of exquisite food and drink were prepared, and various kinds of superior garments and regalia were provided. Gold...
They made offerings of silver, coral, pearls, agate, and various other kinds of supreme and wondrous treasures.
They commanded fifteen hundred monks to recite the secret scriptures and true expositions of the Tripiṭaka, the Five Vehicles, and the Twelve Divisions of the Canon— whether provisional or real,
sudden or gradual, partial or complete, biased or perfect— all interlacing and reflecting one another like strands of precious silk.
This net serves above to assist and protect the Imperial Mandate, and below to nurture the fundamental basis of the people.

We, the subject-monk Xingduan of Jing Mountain, together with the venerable and eminent masters of the three schools—Teaching, Chan, and Vinaya—with this true body and this sincere mind, reverently receive the imperial decree to ascend the precious throne.
We shall expound the unsurpassed profound purport of all Buddhas and manifest the unsurpassed secrets of all Buddhas.

Tradition holds that whether hidden or manifest, saintly or ordinary, flying or submerged, moving or stationary, all universally rely upon these wholesome causes and equally receive these wondrous benefits.
May calamities and misfortunes be dispelled throughout the four quarters; may the myriad people delight in the occupations of plowing and sericulture;

may they together attain benevolence and longevity, and share in the peace of an era of prosperity. At such a time, principles are perfected and matters are comprehensive; the fruit is full and the merit is complete. Directly...

How can one ultimately uphold and display this single phrase of no private self? [The Master] strikes the whisk and says: "Transformations unfold beyond the mountains and rivers under the sun of Shun;
people dwell within the rain and dew of the heaven of Yao. He then speaks a verse: "To grasp a ruler and measure empty space, One can never exhaustively determine its extent.
To hold a ladle and fathom the sea, How could one ever understand its source? The essential body of our Sovereign’s original mind Is vast and great."
It is likewise so. If one seeks its limit, it can ultimately never be found. The lifespan of Your Majesty is identical to this essence of mind;
if one seeks its exhaustion, that too cannot be found. The source of Your Majesty’s merit is identical to this lifespan;
if one seeks its end, that too cannot be found. This applies equally to the Empress Dowager, the Crown Prince, and the consorts.
The retinues, the essence of mind, and the source of merit are all without distinction. In every single atom there is a Buddha-field; in every Buddha-field there is a Śākyamuni.
Each manifests a broad and long tongue and together proclaims the matters mentioned above. Even among hundreds of thousands of millions of [beings], not even one can equal this.
The various classes of beings—gods and humans, those in the hells, hungry ghosts, animals, and all sentient beings throughout the ten directions within the three realms—[are all encompassed therein].
"O assembly of sentient beings, you should know that the essence of this mind has been such in its fundamental nature from the beginning.
Chan Master Yuejiang Yin ascended the seat at Jinshan Temple in the imperial court for the Water and Land Assembly.

"In the past, the Tathāgata cultivated boundless practices within the ocean of Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, just as a torrential rain clears away the heat of summer and universally washes away all impurities."
Born amidst the heat of afflictions, he manifests in the world through the power of his vows of great compassion.
He is the Great Teacher of the three realms and the compassionate father of the four modes of birth; he appears but once in an age, like the udumbara flower.

At times, he manifests a jeweled royal land upon the tip of a single hair, sitting within a mote of dust to turn the Great Dharma Wheel. Or he becomes a Wheel-Turning Sage King, ruling over the four continents under the thousand [suns].
The son was surrounded by the adornments of the seven treasures and lived for eighty thousand years. He traveled through the air with sovereign ease, meeting no obstacles wherever he went.
His country was prosperous and joyful, its people flourishing; his majestic virtue was preeminent and beyond compare.
All of this was manifested through the power of the vows of great compassion. Thus, the power of the vows of great compassion is like the great ocean—profound and bottomless.
Its foundation: the power of the great compassionate vow is as vast and boundless as great empty space; the power of the great compassionate vow is like the great sun-disk rising in the sky;
the power of the great compassionate vow is like Mount Sumeru raining down all manner of jewels;

the power of the great compassionate vow is like the wish-fulfilling gem that fulfills the aspirations of sentient beings; the power of the great compassionate vow is like the bright lamp of the world, illuminating everywhere.
Truly so! The power of the Great Compassionate Vow is like a canopy of space, universally shading all living beings.
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, takes great compassion as his very essence. It is because of sentient beings that great compassion arises; it is because of great compassion that the bodhicitta is born.
Through the bodhicitta, one attains equal and perfect enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*). It is like a great king of trees in a vast wilderness:
if its roots receive water, its branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits all flourish and grow profusely. The Bodhi-tree king is likewise;
all sentient beings constitute its roots, while the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas constitute its flowers and fruits. If these Bodhisattvas, by means of the Great...
The water of compassion benefits sentient beings, thereby enabling the fulfillment of the flowers and fruits of the Buddhas' wisdom.
If Bodhisattvas benefit sentient beings with a mind of great compassion, they can then achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Therefore, enlightenment belongs to sentient beings; without sentient beings, no Bodhisattva could ever achieve unsurpassed, perfect awakening.
Therefore, I, the Sage of the Buddha-mind of the Great Yuan, share the same root and the same branches and leaves as Śākyamuni Tathāgata, the Wheel-Turning Sage King.
Riding upon the power of great compassionate vows, I manifest in the world to serve as a great sovereign king and lord of the realm.
Possessing both civil and martial virtue, being sagacious and enlightened, my legacy shall be perpetuated through the Dharma, as I gaze upon the sentient beings of the four seas.
Like a newborn infant, he ruled as a Golden Wheel-turning King, unifying the lands of the ten directions into a single family.

Possessing the mind and body of a Bodhisattva of the Ten Stages, his lifespan surpassed that of the four types of wheel-turning kings. In the leisure between attending to myriad affairs of state, he devoted himself to the Buddha-dharma;

he governed the people with the Right Dharma, whereby the radiance and vigor of the Buddhist teachings flourished twice as much as before. With a heart of great compassion, he brought benefit to all sentient beings.
He opened the gate of the ambrosia to extensively deliver all classes of beings.
Consequently, he established at the Yangtze River the "Jinshan Ocean Assembly of Ten Thousand Monks," where he performed the great *shuilu* (water-land) feast of unimpeded liberation.

There, he perused the venerable scriptures in their five thousand and forty-eight fascicles and expounded upon the inconceivable, wondrous Dharma of direct pointing in both Chan and the doctrinal teachings, using ten billion suns and moons as lamps.
As candles, they cause all sentient beings to realize the samādhi-gate of radiance.
As fragrant offerings made of ten billion Mount Sumerus, they cause all sentient beings to be fully satiated and to realize the bliss of the joy of Dharma and the delight of dhyāna.
As clarified butter, cream, and curd made from ten billion seas of fragrant water, they cause all sentient beings to immediately cease their hunger.

Virtue! Because one has gained entry into the Tathāgata’s pure ocean of Dharma, one offers as alms the seven treasures of ten billion four-continent worlds, so that all sentient beings may forever be free from the suffering of poverty and all attain the wealth and happiness they desire.
Therefore, one takes as one's retinue the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the past, present, and future, numbering as many as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Ganges Rivers.
It belongs to [this purpose]: so that all sentient beings may find reliance upon virtuous spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), he has made the trichiliocosm into a sutra scroll;
so that all sentient beings may constantly turn such a sutra, it reaches upward to the Peak of Existence (*bhavāgra*) and downward to the wheel of emptiness (*ākāśa-cakra*).
Whether obscure or manifest, all are liberated from the wheel of suffering; whether gods or humans, all receive its grace.
All powers without exception flow forth from the pure, subtle, and wondrous power of the Great Compassionate Vow of the Buddha-Mind, the Holy Sovereign.
Above, they accord with the fundamental, wondrously enlightened mind of all Buddhas; below, they share in the same sorrow and longing as all sentient beings.
By this we pray for the Sage’s longevity, may his life be as immovable as Mount Sumeru;

by this we extend the Sage’s blessings, may his merit be equal to the profound ocean of the Flower Treasury (Kusumatalagarbha). To govern the state thereby ensures the people are healthy and all things flourish;

to bring peace to the world thereby ensures the seas are calm and the rivers clear. How is this any different from what is rarely encountered in ten billion kalpas or what is seldom seen throughout the lands of the ten directions?

Śākyamuni has appeared in the world and Maitreya is born; the realms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are all brought within his domain, and the ninety-six types of heterodox paths have all returned to the true transformation.
How majestic! How vast! It is beyond measure and beyond conception.
Now, at this very moment, sovereign and subjects rejoice together as the Buddha-dharma shines forth. How do you speak of knowing gratitude and repaying kindness?
The two wheels of sun and moon shine impartially; the universe is unified in the joy of Great Peace. Again, it is recounted that Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty dreamed of a divine monk who told him:
"Among the six realms and four modes of birth, those imprisoned in obscurity are many. Why not establish the Great Water-Land Feast to deliver and uplift them?
Upon waking, the Emperor issued an edict for ten eminent monks to search through the Tripitaka and compose the ritual texts. This was the beginning...
This great assembly was established at Mount Jinshan. During the first watch of the night, all lamps and candles were extinguished. The Emperor personally attended the banquet and prayed, saying:
"If this ritual procedure accords with the will of both the sages and the common people, may the lamps and candles illuminate themselves as I bow and rise.

If I have not yet attained the favor of the sages, let the candles remain as dark as before. With his first bow, the lamps and candles all became bright; with his second bow, the palace shook; and with his third—

Upon prostrating to Heaven, rain fell of precious flowers; at that time, such spiritual wonders were beyond counting. As for the successive dynasties’ restorations and constructions, the manifest miracles have been even more numerous.

Now, His Majesty the Buddha-Mind Emperor, taking the heart of Emperor Wu of the Liang Dynasty as his own, has specially bestowed imperial incense and seven-jeweled fine silks to provide offerings for the vegetarian feast and establish this Great Assembly.
The Chancellor and the hundred officials have graced the Dharma assembly with their presence.
The eminent masters of the various mountains together expound the profound resonance. Mundane and sagely beings merge, and humans and devas interact.
It is such that the Sāgara Dragon King surges forth from the sea to personally offer a precious jewel, and Śakra Devendra rains flowers from mid-air, offering earnest praise.
As the monk-official ascends the jeweled throne to proclaim the vehicle of the school, the vast merit thus gathered is solely for [the sake of...].

I pray for the prolongation of Your Majesty’s celestial years. I have further composed this verse: The eight-colored eyebrows of Yao illuminate the universe; The double pupils of Shun shine upon the four quarters.
At the peak of Mount Zijin, the sun stands at its zenith; The myriad worlds of the great chiliocosm look up to Your gracious radiance.
Your Excellency has stood long; I humbly entreat you to cherish yourself well.
On the eleventh day of the ninth month in the first year of the Hongwu era, Chan Master Chu-shih Qi ascended the seat at the Water and Land Assembly in Jiangshan Chan Temple by imperial decree.
The realm of true suchness is pure; it is entirely extinguished and has never existed as a thing.
Yet, according to conditions of defilement or purity, it subsequently manifests as the ten dharma realms. These dharma realms are the minds of sentient beings. The minds of sentient beings are...
The Buddha-mind. How great is this mind! Formless and signless, it pervades the ten directions; spanning from antiquity to the present, it encompasses all existence.
Yet, within the realm of sentient beings, its exclusively defiled functioning is called ignorance (*avidyā*);
within the realm of the Buddhas, its exclusively pure functioning is called Buddha-nature (*buddhadhātu*). Both ignorance and Buddha-nature are equally empty. Nevertheless, sentient beings...

Failing to understand emptiness and deluded by ignorance, they have proceeded from immeasurable kalpas until the present life, giving rise to greed, anger, and delusion through body, speech, and mind.
Those whose conduct is dominated by greed number twenty-one thousand; those whose conduct is dominated by anger number twenty-one thousand.

Those whose conduct is dominated by delusion number twenty-one thousand; those whose conduct is balanced among the three poisons number twenty-one thousand. Together they create eighty-four thousand karmas of affliction.
Born into this world, they encounter royal punishments; dying, they fall into the hells.

They pass through kalpas without any prospect of escape. As the ancient masters have said: "All bitter fruits of suffering are experienced because of karma. Once the retribution is exhausted, it returns to nothingness—what suffering is there?"
Is it not seen in the *Mind-King Inscription* by Master Fu of the Liang Dynasty, which says: "Observe the Mind-King; subtle and wondrous, it is difficult to fathom.
Formless and signless, it possesses great supernatural power. It can extinguish a thousand calamities and accomplish ten thousand virtues.
Although its essential nature is empty, it can bestow the Dharma rules. When observed, it has no form; when called upon, it has a voice. It acts as the General of the Dharma—the Precept of the Mind."
The Transmission of the Sūtras says: "The taste of salt in water, the blue pigment within lacquer—these are certainly present, yet their forms are not seen.

It further states: "If you wish to seek Buddhahood, do not defile yourself with a single thing. Although the nature of the mind is empty, the substance of greed and anger is real. Enter this Dharma gate."
Sitting upright, he attained Buddhahood. He suddenly raised his whisk and said, "Do you see?

The World-Honored One Amitāyus is right now upon the tip of this whisk, emitting a great radiance that universally illumines the ten directions—throughout the entirety of empty space and the Dharma-realm, beyond words, beyond words, again beyond words, as numerous as the atoms of three thousand great thousandfold world-systems. [He spoke of] ten billion...
There were ten billion suns and moons, ten billion sets of the four continents, ten billion great oceans, ten billion Mount Sumerus,

ten billion celestial palaces of the desire realm, ten billion celestial palaces of the form realm, and ten billion celestial palaces of Buddhas within the form realm. Within each of these worlds, inside every celestial palace,
there were assemblies of Bodhisattvas surrounding [the Buddha] like an ocean, who preached the Dharma according to the capacities of beings.

The dharmas are each distinct: there are sudden teachings and gradual teachings, ultimate teachings and provisional teachings; vertical teachings and horizontal teachings, explicit teachings and concealed teachings.
Whatever is taught, it is all the teaching of this mind. What principle is not complete? What phenomenon is not encompassed?
What single atom is not included? What single world-system is not subsumed? If you can see it here—[it is not yet...]
Those who have not yet crossed over, let them cross over. Those who have not yet been liberated, let them be liberated. Those who have not yet reached the other shore, let them reach the other shore.
Those who have not yet realized nirvana, let them attain nirvana. Thus, the Imperial Grace and the Buddha’s Grace shall be repaid all at once.
If this were not so, I would add further annotations. (He strikes the whisk. Do you hear? If you hear here, everyone’s ears are present in this single sound.
A single sound universally reaches the ears of all people; this is the Great Being Avalokiteśvara’s Dharma-gate of Perfect Penetration (*pariṣphuṭa*).

When drums are struck simultaneously in the ten directions, they are heard at once in ten places; this is the reality of perfection (*pūrṇatva*). One hears sounds through a wall, and they are audible both near and far;
this is the reality of penetration (*vyāpti*). Since sound does not exist, it is not extinguished; since sound exists, it is not born. Birth and extinction—
The second is the detachment from conditions; this is the eternal reality. Therefore, the Buddhas attain this and achieve equal and perfect enlightenment throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Bodhisattvas attain this and fulfill the six perfections and myriad practices.

Pratyekabuddhas attain this and penetrate the clear understanding of the twelve links of dependent origination. Śrāvakas attain this and realize the eight liberations through the three knowledges and six supernormal powers.
Liberation. Through this, the devas attain it and transcend the ten stages; through this, human beings attain it and become fully endowed with all virtues;
through this, asuras attain it and forever sever their arrogance; through this, those in the hells attain it and are all released from the wheel of suffering.
Even down to the hungry ghosts, animals, and all sentient beings of the four modes of birth and nine categories, through this—
Upon attaining this, there is none who does not awaken to the Buddha within their own mind and realize the Buddha of their own mind. As the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā* states:
"The past mind cannot be apprehended; the future mind cannot be apprehended; the present mind cannot be apprehended. Since the mind cannot be apprehended, [how can there be a Buddha outside it?]
The Buddha is also unattainable. The bodhisattva is also unattainable. The pratyekabuddha is also unattainable.
The śrāvaka is also unattainable. The devas are also unattainable. Human beings are also unattainable. The asuras are also unattainable.
The hungry ghosts, animals, and all sentient beings of the four modes of birth and nine categories are also unattainable. This is unattainable.
"Attainment, too, is unattainable. As the Great Being of Yongjia said: "Clearly seeing, there is not a single thing; there is no person, and there is no Buddha.
The great trichiliocosm is but a bubble on the sea; all sages and worthies are like a flash of lightning.
Thus, when the Second Patriarch Shen Guang visited the First Patriarch Bodhidharma, he said: "My mind is not at peace; I beg the Master to pacify my mind. The First Patriarch—
Xuefeng said, "Bring forth your mind and I shall settle it for you. Shenguang said, "I have searched for my mind, but it is ultimately unattainable.
The First Patriarch said, "I have finished settling your mind for you. With his whisk, he drew a line and said, "This cuts through the tangle.
At this very moment, when the fruit is full and the function is perfected—how do you speak this one phrase? "Offer this profound mind to the dust-motes and lands; this is what is called..."

To repay the grace of the State: We humbly observe that Your Majesty, the Emperor, is heroic, martial, benevolent, and sagacious. Having pacified the realm within the seas, you have nurtured the myriad people as your own children.
The nine tribes and eight barbarians all submit without exception; thus, they ascend mountains to present tribute and cross the oceans to offer precious gems.

In the first year, a great amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire, suffusing all with generous grace. Even the innocent and the wronged were granted deliverance. You have specially bestowed silver...
The Imperial Household (Tangming) ordered the Shan-shi Yuan to perform a seven-day and seven-night *shuilu* great vegetarian feast at Jiangshan Chan Temple.
Within this, various Buddhist rites were performed to make offerings to the Buddhas, sages, and saints, as well as to the deities of heaven and earth and the spirits of the three realms.

Furthermore, the monk Fanqi was summoned to proclaim the teachings of the *zongmen*. The merit accumulated therein was dedicated to the transcendence and deliverance of all beings within the four modes of birth and the six destinies.
Those who were innocent yet falsely accused were all liberated from the dark realms and reborn in Buddha-lands, where they achieved Bodhi.

Their aspirations were fulfilled as the wish-fulfilling jewel shattered the cavern of ignorance, and the sword of wisdom severed the roots of birth and death. Through the Great Dharma, they awakened to the mind;
proceeding to the Land of Bliss, they beheld the Buddha. Furthermore, it is recounted that Emperor Wu of the Liang Dynasty invited the Great Master Fu to expound the sutras. The Great...
The Master ascended the seat. Waving his measuring rule once, Master Baogong addressed the Emperor, saying, "Your Majesty, do you understand?
The Emperor remained silent. The Bodhisattva said, "The Great Being has finished preaching the sutra. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented:

"Today, by the Imperial Grace, I, the monk Fanqi, have been commanded to ascend this seat to proclaim the primary truth (paramārtha-satya). May all beings in the stream of delusion together achieve the Buddha-way."
The great Dharma-gate that Śākyamuni could not exhaustively expound in forty-nine years has been entirely revealed at once by Master Fu.
But tell me, where does the crux lie? The conditions for the Great Water-Land Feast for the Dead and the Living pervade the three thousandfold world-systems and the great chiliocosm;
the golden crow flies eastward and the jade hare races westward, reaching upward to the limits of the azure void.

Descending to the Yellow Springs, they forever cast off the ocean of karmic consciousness and ignorance; ascending high upon the Tathāgata’s wondrous jewel lotus, how could one repay such profound kindness as Mount Sumeru?
May we pray for the Emperor’s sacred longevity to endure for ten thousand years.
On the thirteenth day of the third month in the second year of the Hongwu era, I received by imperial decree the command to ascend the seat at the Water and Land Assembly in Jiangshan Chan Temple.
To thunder the Dharma-thunder, to beat the Dharma-drum, to spread the clouds of compassion, and to sprinkle the nectar of immortality.

Now, the Dharma-thunder has already thundered, the Dharma-drum has already been beaten, the clouds of compassion have already spread, and the nectar has already been sprinkled. Tell me, what shall this mountain monk say?
What kind of dharma is it? Is it a dharma that leads toward the vehicle of the śrāvakas? Is it a dharma that leads toward the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas?
Is it a dharma that leads toward the vehicle of the bodhisattvas? Is it a dharma that leads toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?

Or is it a dharma that leads toward the realm of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana*)? Within the teaching of the Middle Way, within the *dharmadhātu*, there is no dharma named "leading toward the vehicle of the śrāvakas" or "leading toward [the vehicle of] the pratyekabuddhas."
One turns toward the vehicle of awakening, toward the bodhisattva vehicle, and toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

There is no dharma that can be named "turning toward the realm of ordinary beings. There is no dharma that can be named "turning toward defilement," "turning toward purity," "turning toward saṃsāra," or "turning toward nirvāṇa.
Why is this? Because all dharmas are non-dual, like space. Whether in the past, future, or present, they cannot be found when sought; yet it is not...
"There is no empty space. Speaking according to reality, this very empty space has already been driven in as a stake.

Yunmen’s fan in his hand leaps up to the thirty-third heaven and touches the nostrils of Śakra; a sea bass from the Eastern Ocean receives a blow of the staff, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin.
How do you all understand this? After a long silence, he said: "Not a single fiber is stirred."
With a mind of diligent cultivation, one is always sovereign within the light of formlessness. It is further said: "It is not the mind, it is not the Buddha, it is not a thing.
What is it? This has already been clearly stated; why seek further commentaries? This matter does not reside in words.
To interpret it through ten pairs and five groups of words—how bitter! How grievous! As Master Xiangyan said:
It is like a person climbing a tree whose hands do not grasp the branches and whose feet do not tread upon them.

If someone comes beneath the tree and asks about the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, to answer him would be to lose one's body and life; yet to not answer him would be to violate the question he has asked.
If one answers, it is not answering; if one does not answer, it is correct. Master Dahuai said:
"The Chan here is like a mass of fire. If you touch it, it will burn you to death; if you turn your back on it, it will freeze you to death.
As for Master Yongjia’s two lines that "give the thief a ladder to climb over"—what do they say? "Looking at one's form in a mirror is not difficult to see."
"Grasping at the moon in the water—who can seize it? It is as level as a mirror’s surface, yet as treacherous as a precipice.
At the place where Vajra takes the mud, there dwells one of my own household. To those who know this, I shall add another ancient saying:
My fourth patriarch, the Venerable Upagupta, once had a youth of noble lineage who left the home life. One night, he went to stay overnight at the Devakula Monastery. Thereupon, the Venerable One..."
He then manifested a yakṣa carrying a dead man, while another yakṣa arrived empty-handed. The two spirits disputed with one another;
the first said, "I brought this dead man here," and the second said, "I brought this dead man here.
The first spirit said, "I have a witness: this person saw me bring the dead man here. At that moment, the person thought to himself: "I..."
"Now he will certainly die; you should speak the truth. After speaking, he said to the latter ghost: "This dead man was brought here by the former ghost; it is not your portion.
The latter ghost became greatly enraged and tore off one of his arms. The former ghost reattached the dead man's arm as it was before.
The latter ghost again tore off another arm, and the former ghost once more tore a dead man's arm from him to restore the place. The latter...
The demons pulled out his two legs; the demons in front then replaced them with the legs of a dead man so that they were restored as before.
Thus, the two demons together devoured the freshly pulled flesh and immediately departed. At this, the son of good family attained sudden and great enlightenment, realizing:
"Today the Sage Emperor universally delivers those in the dark realms, commanding me, the monk Fanqi, to preach the Dharma to deliver all the Buddha-sons. This is my hope."
Upon a single word, all doubts were resolved and dispersed. One knows that all dharmas are the self-nature of the mind;
thus, one accomplishes the body of wisdom without needing further awakening. It is like suddenly waking from a dream, or like a lotus flower opening. At such a moment, how can it be expressed?
The one hundred and fifth day approaches Qingming; the Shangyuan Festival is certainly on the fifteenth day of the first month.
Again, it is cited that in the past there was a scholar who composed a "Treatise on the Non-existence of Ghosts. A ghost manifested its form and said, "I am here! The scholar had no reply.
Later, Master Wuzu Yan, acting on his behalf, joined both hands together in the shape of a pigeon’s beak and said, "Gu-gu-ghua. The Master (Zhaozhou) comments: "Wuzu harmonized with him."
This may still be called that which is plucked from the crowns of a thousand sages and pointed out from amidst ten thousand people;
it is where speech and silence fail to reach, and where intellectual understanding cannot attain. How can one deliberate upon this phrase that points directly upward? One constantly recalls:
"In the third month of Jiangnan, where the partridges cry, the hundred flowers are fragrant."
Record of the Essential Teachings of the Successive Patriarchs, Volume Sixteen;
Record of the Essential Teachings of the Successive Patriarchs, Volume Seventeen.
Compiled by Xingyue of Loudong, Abbot of Lian’an Chan Monastery at Shiba Jian in Wulin.
Master Wude of Fenyang once addressed the assembly, saying: "Last night I dreamed that my deceased parents were seeking wine, meat, and paper money.
Unable to refuse their request, I followed worldly custom and prepared offerings for them. I had the items prepared in the storehouse and set up an altar just as one does in the secular world."

The ritual of pouring wine and distributing meat was completed, followed by the burning of paper money. The administrative officers (*zhishi*) were ordered to gather and distribute the remaining dishes.

The officers refused them, yet Wude sat alone at the banquet table, eating and drinking as if nothing were amiss. The assembly of monks remarked, "How can a monk who consumes wine and meat be fit to serve as a teacher of the Dharma?
Consequently, they all departed with their packs on their backs, leaving behind only Ciming, Dayu, Quan, Da Dao, and others.
Only six or seven people remained by his ear. On the following day, Wude ascended the hall and said:

"All these many idle spirits and wild ghosts can be sent off with nothing more than a single platter of wine and meat, along with two bundles of paper money. He then quoted the *Lotus Sūtra*: "This assembly has no branches or leaves;
there are only those who are real. Having finished, he descended from his seat.
Cen Master Xuedou Xian addressed the assembly on account of a certain matter:

"To shut out the ears and eyes within the shell of the womb, and to conceal the profound celestial signs beyond the heavens—yet to demand distinctions in the musical notes of *gong* and *shang*, and to argue over the differences between black and white; who is this person? Do you know him yet?"
That one. This one. Together with the original three—letting these pass by one step—he then descended from his seat.

On account of a certain matter, he addressed the assembly: "The stone is naturally vast and spacious; the jade is of its own accord coarse and unpolished. From antiquity to the present, how swift is this [truth]!"
A lion does not bite a qilin; a fierce tiger does not eat raw meat. Have you not seen? On a solitary island in Lake Dongting, the misty waves run deep.
Does anyone recognize the wooden horse that chases the wind?
On account of a certain matter, he addressed the assembly: "A guest comes from afar, leaving me a jade disc an inch across. Within it are four characters;

character after character, no one recognizes them. Purely containing the vastness of the whale-ocean, Coldly piercing the narrowness of the moon’s orb. Today I present them for you to behold; I ask you to speak the final word."
Chan Master Xueyan Qin, on account of certain matters and to express his gratitude to the Head Seat, writes: Before the fifteenth day, there was thunderous sound but no raindrops at all;
after the fifteenth day, the times were clear and the way was prosperous, and the state and the family were at peace.
On this very fifteenth day, we respectfully wish that each and every one of you may enjoy ten thousand blessings in your health and daily life. But in the end, how is it? [In the] Hall.
The Head Seat is the Eye of Humanity and Heaven.
Chan Master Gaofeng Miao ascended the hall for a discourse on a certain occasion: "The salty taste in water and the blue pigment in color definitely exist, yet their forms are not seen.
Holding up his whisk, he said: "Now that you see its form, you have lost the eyes of an entire village of people before the mountain."
Master Tianru Ze addressed the assembly on account of a certain matter. Striking the left side of the meditation seat with his whisk, he said:
