Following this sequence from youth to old age, even when one reaches the point where the illness has penetrated the vital organs and the divine physician folds his hands in helplessness, all maladies are cast off and the true essence is directly realized as suchness. Yet, one must further turn toward that other side."

Subsequently, through practice in accordance with the Dharma and practice following the Dharma, the banner of the Dharma is established wherever it may be. Thus, one is able to reveal the ailment of being unable to reach the bottom when things are gathered together;

this directly causes even the thousand sages to be unable to find its point of origin. It universally enters into the bodies of all sentient beings, taking the very illnesses of sentient beings entirely into the gate of great liberation.
Only by realizing the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) can one finally provide a ferry for the four classes of birth and serve as a ladder.

I navigate through the nine realms of existence. If it were not so, for what purpose would there be this "sickness of emptiness"? I venture to ask you all: suppose this mountain monk has been ill for a long time;
tell me, is this illness the same as or different from the illness I spoke of just now? If you say they are the same—
If you say it is something else, you still have not seen the old monk. Why? "When the ocean dries up, its bottom will finally be seen;
when a person dies, their mind remains unknown."
When Chan Master Huisi of Huanglong was ill and had retired to Huìtáng, he gave a night instruction. Holding up his whisk, he said: "Look! Look!
The whisk is the sickness of the body; the whisk is the sickness of the mind. The whisk settles the sickness of the body; the whisk settles the sickness of the mind.

The whisk pierces through the sickness of the mind; the sickness of the mind pierces through the whisk. At this very moment, if you call it the whisk, it is again the sickness of the mind. If you call it...
"Dead Heart" is also a whisk. Ultimately, what would you call it? After a long silence, he said: "Do not bring right and wrong to judge me;
the fabrications of this floating life are irrelevant."
Master Milmam Je ascended the hall after recovering from illness and said: "A single leaf drifts through the void; ten thousand trees turn autumnal.
Reflecting back on this fleeting time, it rushes like a flowing river. If one can recognize the meaning within this, one will cut off all diversities at the ultimate source.
For these past few days, this mountain monk has been as if ill yet not ill, as if at ease yet not at ease, as if dead yet not dead—discharging excrement right here in the abbot’s quarters."
Urine. With eyes wide open, he rambles and mutters in his sleep; he simply cannot distinguish east from west or north from south.

He seeks life but cannot find it, and seeks death but cannot attain it. Śākyamuni, the compassionate father of the four modes of birth and the physician-king of the three realms, could not find the origin of this illness even while searching.
At this very moment, if anyone can save this mountain monk, let them light a single lamp.
"Peppermint decoction and Ishoku (Isa-ku). If you cannot save yourself, it will be like people climbing a mountain, each striving for themselves.
King Yama is not your father; at that time, he will strike your ghost-bone buttocks with a rope to collect his rice-money.
Do not say he did not warn you."
Master Dianyuyuan of Dianiu ascended the hall after recovering from illness. He cited Mazu Daoyi’s “Sun-Face Buddha, Moon-Face Buddha,” and then quoted the verse by Master Dongshan Shouyan:
“A young girl paints her eyebrows; Before the phoenix-mirror stand, her words are like those of a madwoman.
She says her jade face has no peer, Yet she goes back to the rack to put on her silken robe. The Master said, “Dongshan...”
The old man’s full-mouthed praise is indeed as it seems; yet, when scrutinized, it cannot be said that he is entirely free from local bias.
Yunyan, however, was not like this: "Kill the yellow oriole; let it not sing upon the branch. How many times has it startled my dreams?"

"One must not go to Liaoxi. Master Chan Baiyang Shun, while ill, addressed the assembly: "I have been ill for a long time, yet I have never moved my wooden pillow. When people come, they mostly ask, 'How is it?
I, this mountain monk, answer according to the circumstances as they arise. Outside the window, the yellow oriole’s voice is even more abundant. As for the seven..."
"Where does this one-chi frame suffer its ailment? Let those among you who possess the true eye try to point out the source of the illness for this mountain monk.
When the assembly offered their responses, none were in accord. The Master clapped his hands once, made a sound of retching, and said, "What a fine wooden pillow!"

Chan Master Foxincai ascended the hall after recovering from illness. "A single Dharma has form that encompasses all things moving and stationary; the hundred rivers rush and surge, vying to flow toward the source.
The Shao zither remains unstrung as the clouds and sky grow dim; one can only imagine the old, ailing elder of Vaiśālī. When Vimalakīrti was ill, it was Shangfeng who was ill;
when Shangfeng was ill, it was the staff that was ill; when the staff was ill, it was the myriad phenomena of the universe."
The sickness of the elephant. When the myriad phenomena of the universe are sick, both the ordinary and the sage are sick.
Do you all perceive the place where the root of this sickness arises? If you do perceive it, the sentient and the non-sentient are of one body; everywhere is the same true Dharma-realm.
If this were not yet so, then the sweet melon is sweet all the way to its stem, and the bitter gourd is bitter down to its roots.
When Chan Master Xinwen Ben rose from illness and ascended the hall to teach, Vimalakīrti, while ill, exhausted every principle;
Longxiang, while ill, coughed incessantly. He coughed incessantly while exhausting every principle, and exhausted every principle while coughing incessantly. You—
Do you all still recognize the essential meaning within this? Originally, it was the Yangtze River that encountered the cold wind;
yet now, the pillar is made to suffer from a headache.
Master Shiwu Hong, rising from illness, ascended the hall and cited the Ancestor of Tiaoxi, who addressed the assembly, saying: "I have a great..."
This illness cannot be cured by the physicians of the world. Later, a monk asked Caoshan, "I wonder what kind of illness this is?
Caoshan said, "It is the illness of being unable to gather [the mind] together. The monk asked again, "Do all sentient beings have this illness as well?
Caoshan said, "I myself am currently searching for its point of origin and cannot find it. The Master said, "This monk is one who has already passed through the illness; he is truly searching."
He does not let it go, even down to the tips of one's hair. Had it not been for Caoshan knowing its point of descent, others would have found it difficult to open their mouths.
He then composed another verse to present to the assembly: "A hundred bones ache and throb, crowded together in pain; One bout of fever is followed by another chill.
Searching for its place of origin, one finds nothing at all; The medicinal cauldron and the wind-fueled stove are both overturned."
Master Jiefeng Yuchan ascended the hall due to an eye ailment. "The Buddha’s illness, the Patriarchs’ illness, and the illnesses of all beings—I set these aside.
The elixir, the wondrous medicine, the medicine of the immortals—I cast these to one side. Departing from this illusory body of the four elements, tell me:
what is the illness and what is the medicine? If you can realize it here, I grant that you all possess [the true eye]."
A single eye. If you have not yet realized this, I, the old monk, shall clearly point out the source of the illness for all of you to see:
when the four elements disperse, where will you find a place to settle and establish your life? This is the phrase of having the illness but no medicine:
"The radish of Zhèngzhōu," "the cypress tree," "a dried piece of excrement," and "three pounds of hemp. This is the phrase of having the medicine but no illness: "All phenomena return to..."
"Where does each one return? Zhaozhou said, "When I was in Qingzhou, I made a cotton shirt that weighed seven *jin*.
This is a phrase for treating a disease with medicine; it is not mind, not Buddha, not a thing, and there is no Buddha-nature in a dog.

This is the phrase where both medicine and illness are forgotten. It is intended to cure all the illnesses within the minds of sentient beings—the afflictions, toils, delusions, attachments, and the five desires and eight winds.
The entire Great Canon of the Teachings is a medical prescription for saving the world;
the seventeen hundred *gong'an* of the patriarchs are all efficacious elixirs and wondrous medicines. When there is illness, one should take the medicine; when there is no illness—
The medicine is returned and the ailment dispelled. Suppose someone were to come forth from among the assembly and say, "If the Master cannot cure his own self, what use is it to treat others?
To him, one would simply say: "I have kept a pair of blue and white eyes, laughing as I watch the countless people coming and going."
Chan Master Wumen Can rose from his illness and ascended the hall to teach. "The illness of all you people is my own illness; my illness is the illness of all you people.
Where you people suffer pain, I am able to endure it; where I suffer pain, you wish to endure it but cannot. He struck the meditation staff once.
This single dose of a singular prescription brings immediate harmony and peace; there is no need to go to the roots of pines to gather *fùgǔ* (pachyma).
Ling. Chan Master Shuzhong Yun, suffering from eye disease, ascended the hall and said: "For several days now, my monk’s diseased eyes have been dark and blurred;
I cannot distinguish east from west, nor north from south. Yet, within this state of non-distinction and non-discrimination, there is nevertheless something."
[The Master] said, "It is clear. A monk asked Jiufeng, "What is the eye that holds fast to heaven and earth? [Jiufeng] snapped his chopsticks and stirred the Dragon Gate.
Jiufeng said, "It is held fast right here; it is like a beggar playing with a rice bowl. The monk said, "Where is the eye of heaven and earth? [Jiufeng] said, "A second offense is not tolerated.
Jiufeng said, "This is precisely the eye of heaven and earth; it is buying high and selling low. The monk said, "Does it still shed light?"

There is a profound failure of illumination. Feng said, "Without borrowing the power of the three luminaries, my tongue drags upon the ground. The monk asked, "If you do not borrow the power of the three luminaries, by what means do you illuminate?

[Feng] called it the "Eye of Heaven and Earth. [The Master said,] "A dog biting a dry bone. Feng said: [Note: The dialogue continues with the Master's response to the monk's challenge regarding the source of illumination.]
If it were not so, then seeing ghosts before one’s own skull would truly be the talk of one who sees ghosts.

Jiufeng’s long blowing and slow beating, though he claimed his own skill was supreme, could not prevail against this monk, who had long frequented the halls of practice and whose exchanges were flawless.
Even with the "eye that holds fast heaven and earth," one has still not seen him. Today, I am not merely interjecting or seizing the market; it is because...
One who is frequently ill is well-versed in the nature of medicines. Do you know the "eye that grasps and stabilizes heaven and earth"? (He plants his staff.
When the light of dawn has not yet parted, all gaze; yet once daybreak comes, it is but ordinary.

Chan Master Chushi Qi ascended the hall after recovering from illness and said: "I, Shoushan, do not know how to speak of Chan. Having risen from sickness, my bones are exposed and my skin is pierced through.

I have judged the Old Man Yama, who one day will come to demand payment for his meals. The Sword Trees and Knife Mountains cannot be avoided; the boiling cauldrons and burning furnaces will sear us all.
Furthermore, we shall enter the wombs of donkeys and horses, and it is unknown when we shall be liberated. Why is this so?"
It is thus. This is the daily fare of those who dwell in the Way.

Chan Master Liaoyu, having recovered from illness, ascended the hall and said: "Yesterday there was illness; the day before yesterday there was illness. Illnesses follow one another in succession, yet they possess no inherent nature (*svabhāva*).
This cuts off the tongue of Vimalakīrti and turns back the orthodox command of Mahākāla. He struck his whisk and shouted, "Wild fox!"
A *śarabha* is born within a cave; monkeys each wear the mirror of Xuanyuan.
Entering the hall, Master Yan of Dongshan said: "Illness upon illness, skin clinging to bone—truly startling! Shaking oneself free and rising, there is not a single thing;
yet it is still somewhat lacking. Unable to take a step, the voice is low; even if one tries to depict it, it cannot be captured."
It is not a painting; the painting is not completed. Yet the nostrils remain high and prominent. "Hitting it, bumping into it—excellent!
O assembly, the ancients brought their realization to a point where there was nothing left to manifest; it truly shook heaven and moved earth, surpassing the past and transcending the present.
Since the beginning of this summer, I, this mountain monk, have been ill and ill again. Having recovered from my illness, I see no four elements or five aggregates within;
I see no mountains, rivers, or the great earth without; I see no Buddhas above; I see no sentient beings below; and I see no self in between.
Purely naked and starkly clear, there is nothing to grasp. How fortunate! How fortunate indeed!
Pity these living beings! Without cause, the attendant has left this one case unresolved. Today is the full moon;

those who offer incense shall offer incense, those who bow to guests shall bow to guests, those who dip their brushes shall dip their brushes, and those who request the Dharma shall request the Dharma.
I simply wish for the mountain monk to write the four characters "Long Live the Emperor" across the great void of space. Is there anyone who will do this for me?
[The Master] asks, "Who is the scribe? He raises his whisk and says, "Civilization aligns with the North Pole; sagacious calculation equals the Southern Mountain.
He lowers the whisk and descends from the seat.
Master Miyun Wu, rising from illness, ascends the seat and says: "I, this mountain monk, am sixty-five years old. Counting back, it has not involved..."
Regarding delusion and enlightenment: for three years I suffered from chronic dysentery until my entire body was reduced to skin and bone.

If one can realize and verify this in such a manner, one will surely transcend both Buddhas and patriarchs. Throughout the twelve periods of daily life, ensure there is no further deviation or confusion.
If you can practice in this way, you will certainly realize the adamantine solidity. Just look at the person treading the pestle in the mortar house; throughout the entire day, they have never—
"Try taking even a single step. Suzhou City has six gates, and at each gate there is a path leading through to the city streets;
it is a pity that no one examines them to know their total number. Then he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Zhuo’an ascended the seat after recovering from illness. The Master said:
"The three hundred and sixty joints and eighty-four thousand pores of the body—shaking them all thoroughly, one cannot find even a trace of where the illness arose.
When wind, cold, heat, and dampness press in from all four sides, tell me, where do you lodge it? You who are accustomed to passing before the Five Phoenix Pavilion..."
[The Master] passed away. Holding a golden whip in his hand, he celebrated the Great Peace. Suddenly, a monk came forward and said, "Does the Master still act as the host?
At this, the mountain monk could not help but dance with his hands and stamp with his feet.
Today, for the first time, my rambling has begun and it still does not cease. [He] gave a shout and descended from the seat.
Master Tianru Weize of Yan-shi established a retreat based on the *Complete Enlightenment Sutra* for a period of one hundred and twenty days.
He wrote a verse upon the door to address the assembly: "A firm barrier stands upon level ground; Even if a Buddha comes, there is no path to meet him. [He] divided [the retreat]...
Clarity lies only in the ordinary. As if separated by a thousand peaks and ten thousand crags, Master Jianxin Fu addressed the assembly while in retreat:
"My body is like withered wood, a hundred thoughts reduced to ash; The mountain monkeys and wild cranes suspect me with distress.
I close my door alone amidst the rain upon the green pines; Even when meeting people, my smiling mouth is too weary to open."

Chan Master Wququ (Wuqu) of the Empty Hall closed his retreat and addressed the assembly: "For over thirty years, I have visited and sought instruction from the patriarchs and masters of the ten directions.

Whenever I asked about the Dharma, they all said, 'There is nothing to say. Whenever I asked about the Buddha, they all said, 'He has no marks. Fortunately, by attaining this state of no-marks and no-speech, I unconsciously realized that my clever artifices were suddenly empty.
Reflecting on the past, I see that I had lost my advantage at the very root; today, I rejoice that my eyebrows are finally back where they belong."

Above. From this point on, cast away the straw sandals and immediately snap the staff in two. With both hands empty, enter the Mysterious Barrier and sit watching the waxing and waning of Yin and Yang.
The verse says: The impoverished son returns to the elder’s mansion; Sudhana has finished his pilgrimage through the groves of the *Avataṃsaka*.
The great trichiliocosm is gathered within the tip of a hair; He pushes out the void and slams the gate shut.
Chan Master Rui Bai Xue sealed the pass for Elder Cheng. He locked the head of his staff and tied the mouth of his cloth bag.
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth were churned into a single mass; light and dark, form and emptiness, were squeezed into one cluster.
On Mount Lu, not a shred of cloud hangs; on Mount Qinwang, how could there be even a trace of mist? At such a moment, what is the phrase for entering the pass?
The Way. After a long silence, he said: "A wooden man beats a felt board in the clouds; a stone woman sings a tea song atop the mountain.
Master Shiyufang performs the rite for the walking corpse and seals the barrier of the mustard-seed city. The sea is vast and the sky is open; the wise do not dwell therein."
An iron wall and a silver mountain—fools do not recognize them. Thus, it is like a mirror reflecting a mirror; there is no hindrance between this side and that side.

Since the resolve for death is already firm, the intention to be buried alive must likewise be steadfast. Nevertheless, if you wish to understand the meaning of these words, you must wait and see after three years.
Opening the Barrier and Grasping the Mainstay:
Chan Master Wunü Kōng’s Instructions upon Opening the Barrier to the Assembly. I myself bound the profound barrier; I myself buried myself alive.
It was I who closed it, and it is I who open it. With a single blow, I shatter the aperture of the profound barrier, releasing the man who has been here all along.
Chan Master Yuzhi opened the gate and addressed the assembly: "For three years in my chamber, I have sat and cut off the ten directions of the world;
in a single thought upon this meditation cushion, the ten ages of past and present are suddenly perfected.

It is like being within Maitreya’s tower—opening and closing as one pleases—but ultimately, within the realm of Samantabhadra, one must see that which survives after total extinction. Therefore it is said: 'If you hold fast, all is dry.'"

The Earth (Kun) loses its color. If one lets go, even rubble and debris will radiate brilliance; the heavens and the Milky Way stretch across all directions. How could the dark cypress trees fail to harbor the brilliant phoenix?
Amidst the vast surging of wind and thunder, how could the azure pool allow the blue dragon to remain coiled in slumber?

If this is so, then how do you speak the single phrase for "releasing the Lord of Guanzhong"? *Ei!* When the gate opens, the sun rises from the west at the hour of Mao; amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed.
Chan Master Shiyu opened the gate for Zhengheng, saying: "The entire great earth is this very gate-house; fundamentally, there is no coming or going.
It is only because of delusion that one speaks of 'passing through' the gate upon the gate, which is merely the meaning of delusion upon delusion.

People today think only of seeking enlightenment, yet they do not understand delusion at all. Since they do not understand delusion, from where could enlightenment be obtained? Therefore, I, the old monk, always say:"
Regarding the human path: there are ten parts of delusion and ten parts of awakening. Today, opening the gate—how could this belong to either delusion or awakening?
Listen to this verse: "There is entering and exiting, yet no door or gateway; There is no opening or closing, yet there is a secure seal.
If you are one with the power of a fragrant elephant cutting through the current, you will never seek a way from another. Now, he raises the key. Tell me, what is it? Try opening it and see.
Welcoming the Venerable Elder, the Master Shixing led him to the seat and presented the outline of the discourse.

Because he had previously studied under his fellow practitioner, Chan Master Rongjing, he ascended the hall, took the staff in his right hand, leaned it against his left side, and after a long silence, said:
"If this matter were not handled by my elder brother, Master Rongjing, it would be truly difficult."
Having fully understood this, he descended from his seat.

When Chan Master Fanchang Yu and Chan Master Huanglong Nan arrived for the morning assembly, [Fanchang] ascended the hall and said: "Seizing the clouds and grappling with the waves—countless as hemp seeds.
Once the coppery eyes are struck, they immediately blossom into flowers. Apart from the head and horns of the Yellow Dragon, everything else is nothing but vermilion spots."
Snake. At Fachang, this small monastery is situated where the roads are distant and the mountains remote; the scenery is desolate and few travelers venture there.
I dare say that Master Huanglong’s gracious visit has not only brought radiance to these springs and rocks, but has also brought joy to humans and devas alike.
Yet, as clouds move and rain falls from antiquity to the present, alas, in the smelting furnace there are still many pieces of dull iron. A skilled physician...
In this gate, the illness of those who come grows ever more severe. To cure an illness, one must seek the divine medicine; to dissolve stubbornness, one must rely on the golden hammer.
Within this place of Fachang, how many are there—those teachers who merely evade the root? Their illness lies deep in the vital organs; their stubbornness has penetrated to the very marrow.
Had it not been for the arrival of the old man Huanglong, they would all have lived in vain and died in delusion. (He picks up his staff and says: "If you want..."
Do you understand? To make noodles, one must use the wheat of that specific region; to sing a song, one must be a person from the imperial capital.
When Chan Master Baoning Yong was giving a formal lecture upon the arrival of the Changlu Abbot, he said: "Gold is tested by fire; water is tested by a staff.
But, O Great Assembly, what if gold were not tested by fire, and water were not tested by a staff? Is there anyone who can discern this?"
"Mò. If you can discern it, then whether it be true or false, deep or shallow—you will know. If you cannot discern it, then entrust it to those with clear eyes.
Master Chan Master Zhenjing Wen ascended the hall, and Elder Longqing addressed the assembly: "The scriptures state that when the Buddha entered parinirvāṇa..."
Those who later become spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) all perceive them as the coming of the Buddha.
Nevertheless, such spiritual friends are not easily encountered, nor should they be treated with contempt. This is what Master Longqing meant.
The old monk, together with the administrators, the head seat, and the assembly, shares in this great joy. Then, he gave a shout and said:
A lineage of the Huxi school and descendants of Longshan; the Great Opening of the Chan Gate at Longqing in Jizhou.
As the ancients said, "That which enters through the gate is not the family treasure. Suddenly raising his staff, he asked, "Is this the family treasure, or is it an external object?
I ask the assembly to let Master Longqing of Longqing Monastery decide for us. He then threw down the staff and descended from his seat.
Chan Master Xuedou Xian, because Senior Monk Zong arrived, led the assembly forward, saying: "Venerable assembly, today’s Senior Monk Zong of Xuedou was formerly the Great Elder Han of Taiyang.
Possessing great insight and vision, he concealed his traces and hid his brilliance.
Now, wishing to propagate the spirit of our school, I pray that he will graciously ascend this seat."
Chan Master Baiyun said: "Nine times nine is eighty-one; how many people can calculate this?
Two pieces of five hundred cash—originally they are but one string. At this point, can you add even a single coin?
If you could add a single coin, then light would shine along the entire road, surpassing both past and present. Yet, alas, from antiquity until now, [how few have done so]!"
"One person, ten thousand people. I only love the white clouds at the tips of their feet. Today, for your sake, I shall add to this view. He then said, "Descend from the seat;
let the administrators, the head seat, and the assembly invite Master Zhongfeng to ascend the seat once more."
Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin invited Chan Master Jue of Changlu to ascend the hall. Before the Many-Sons Stupa, he shared half his seat;
he cut off the flow of all streams. At Shaolin, he sat in dignified stillness for nine years, standing like a wall ten thousand fathoms high. He now stirs the furnace and bellows of a true master.
Bestowing the upward-pointing tongs and hammer, he manifests great function and great capacity, fully bringing forth life and fully executing death;

he extracts nails and pulls out wedges for all people, ungluing the sticky and removing bonds, so that every person on this great earth may, like a lion cub, display its prowess, roar, and crouch upon the ground with a backward leap.
Therefore it is said: "The Dharma-King’s Dharma-power transcends all living beings; he constantly bestows the wealth of the Dharma upon one."
All-pervasive! Having long accumulated pure karma, you are called Immeasurable; because you lead the multitudes to tranquility, I bow my head to you.

Thus it is that one extends a hand over a precipice ten thousand fathoms high, where both the "knocking" and the "singing" are present; one advances further atop a hundred-foot pole, where host and guest interchange roles.
At this very moment, how is it? When the dragon roars, long mist arises; when the tiger shouts, the wind is born. He further said:
"When meeting a fellow traveler on the path, they pass each other shoulder to shoulder; the lifelong task of study is then complete. Today, fortunately, we have encountered the Great Teacher."
The "Treasure Flower King Throne" is brought forth to highlight this.
Zen Master Longmen Yuan, while presiding over the assembly at Wuzu Heshang’s temple, said: "The Great Master of Caoxi transmitted the robe and returned to Lingnan.
Later, Reverend Rang received the Dharma and bestowed it upon the Great Master Ma. The Great Master Ma then received Baizhang."
Baizhang received Huangbo; Huangbo received Linji; Linji received Xinghua; Xinghua received Nanyuan; Nanyuan received Fengxue;
Fengxue received Shoushan; Shoushan received Fenyang; Fenyang received Master Ciming.
Master Ciming personally received one person, Master Yangqi. Now, I shall cite what he attained.
Look at this! This Old Man [Linji] said, "In my place, it is like climbing a pole in a bustling marketplace;
everyone sees it. Can you deceive their eyes? Later, this Old Man of Yangqi succeeded in receiving only one person, Master Duan.
This was where Laozi once resided. There is a verse that says: "When the pearl at the bottom of the sea stirs, The moon in the clouds appears again.
On a cool night without a wild wind, The pure light is all one piece. Later, Master Duan succeeded our former teacher as his sole heir.
Our former teacher had said: "From the moment one bites through this single iron pastry, one attains the hundred flavors."
It is complete. This is why this Old Man [Linji] was throughout his life stubborn of mouth and fond of speaking harsh words.

Since the time our former teacher entrusted him with the Dharma and the Great Teaching has been transmitted, at the very end, Dongshan suddenly handed it over to the present Abbot of the Fifth Patriarch’s Hall.
Today, fortunately, before this vast assembly of humans and devas, I request that you, out of your compassionate generosity, reveal it once more for us.
I declare: it would be a great fortune indeed if our former patriarchs were to have a foothold here and our Way were further clarified.
When Master Ganlu ascended the hall upon the mountain, he said: "If Bodhidharma had not come to the land of Tang, heaven and earth would endure forever;

if the Second Patriarch had not gone to the Western Heaven, the mountains would remain green and the waters blue. The dragon roars and mist rises; the tiger sighs and the wind is born. Autumn rains hang from the void."
Floating clouds obscure the sun. Do those who possess eyes still see? Do those who possess ears still hear? Since they are endowed with seeing and hearing, what is delusion and what is awakening?
What serves as the condition and what serves as the counterpart?

If you wish to know the principle of delusion and awakening, rising and sinking, you must ultimately return to the teacher of your own original portion—the Way of the Buddhas of the past. As for the physical form, it belongs to the four great elements; as for the nature of the mind—

They return to the six sense objects. The four great elements are each separate in substance; who is it that brings them together? O Great Assembly, since body and mind are already like this, what exactly is it that exists now?
Lately, those who study the Way have all been rushing about with words and phrases, debating the past and present, yet they are entirely unenlightened regarding their own fundamental task.
For this reason, the True Teaching has grown thin and the Way of the Dharma has become diluted.

I am deeply moved. Fortunately, we have encountered the arrival of the Venerable Master. We humbly beseech you to thunder forth the sound of the Dharma and reveal the true essence; to tear away the heavy cataracts and manifest the pearl within the robe.
The fourfold assembly turns its heart with utmost sincerity; we cannot bear to refrain from our earnest entreaty.
Chan Master Ying’an Hua, upon the arrival of Master Xuedang of Wujushan, ascended the hall and said:
"Linji received three severe blows of the staff and realized his homecoming on the rapids of Gaoyuan. At the staff of Dajue, Xinghua deeply clarified the intent of Huangbo."
Although there are not many among us brothers in the mountains, each of us suffers from a malady deep within the vital organs.

Had it not been for the arrival of you, Reverend Uncle, how would Mingguo have dared to rashly convey this news? In a short while, we shall descend from our seats and, together with the administrators, the heads of the community, and the assembly, extend our formal invitation.
We humbly beseech you to look upon us with compassion and graciously administer the medicine that will cure us.
When Wanshan Heshang arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "The large is large, the small is small; the long is long, the short is short;
the curved is curved, the straight is straight; the square is square, the round is round; the correct is correct, the deviant is deviant.
Is this a Buddha? Is it a Bodhisattva? Is it an Arhat? Is it a Holy Monk? Is it a ghost or spirit? Or is it a deva?"
"O Immortal, I have heard this Dharma in the past and have never spoken it falsely. To say 'this is the meaning' or 'this is not the meaning' is to fall into following the meaning.

To say 'it is neither meaning nor non-meaning' or 'it is neither non-meaning nor not non-meaning' is to fall into following the phrasing. If one engages in such deliberations regarding the Buddha-Dharma, the single school of Daruma will be wiped out like dust.
If one does not engage in such deliberations regarding the Buddha-Dharma, this old monk will live trapped in hell. You all—"

Can people return to their original state, both monastics and laypeople alike? If this is not yet the case, shortly after I descend from the seat, the administrative officers and heads of the community shall join in inviting the new Abbot of Wanshan to explain it for the assembly.
When Chan Master Dahui of Jing Mountain ascended the hall, he said: "I originally had no mind to seek anything, yet now this great treasure of the Dharma King has arrived spontaneously.
Now that the great treasure of the Dharma King has arrived, you all must quickly sharpen your wits. As the saying goes:
'If you do not seize it when you see it, it will be a thousand miles away when you think of it. Have you not seen Master Da Sui?"
"Dao! I have studied under more than seventy spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). Among them, those who possess the Great Eye are but one or two;
the rest all possess right knowledge and vision (*samyagjñānadarśana*). In this world today, the only true spiritual friend who possesses the Great Eye is my Dharma-uncle, the Master alone.
With his pitch-black bamboo staff, he overturns the seas and mountains, striking from head to foot."
Although this is like treating a dead horse with medicine, it contains within it the essential subtlety. When Huangbo struck Linji with his staff, did Jiangshan not possess one as well?
It is simply because the land is vast and people are few. Yunmen’s "One Tune" was played on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month;
how could it be blown and sung today on the sixteenth? [The Master] suddenly grasps his staff, strikes once, and says: "Empty space can be measured, and the wind can be..."
[This matter] is bound up [in the nature of reality]. No one is able to exhaustively describe the Buddha’s merits.

Furthermore, I recall that while at Huqiu, I heard my late teacher recount how his late uncle Fuyan first served as a *huashu* (conversion officer) in Wuweijun. While on the road, he suffered a fall and attained a moment of realization.

Upon returning, he reported this to the Master. Later, the Master appointed him as the guest prefect (*zhiké*). One night, while sitting by the fire, he suddenly attained a profound awakening. Although...
It was thus. Every time he entered the room, he was unable to penetrate deeply into its innermost recesses;
he would then calmly request further instruction from the Great Master. The Patriarch said, "I shall give you a parable. It is just like a man leading an ox through a window lattice."
Both horns and all four hooves have already passed through; only the tail cannot pass. The Master said, "These words have long resided within my belly.
I know for certain that in these present times, no one is able to comprehend them. Therefore, I have kept them hidden at the 'three inches' [between the eyebrows].
Had it not been for the arrival of you, the venerable Dharma-uncle, this nephew would have had no cause to bring them forth in his entire life. I venture to say:
I ask the assembly: "Since the main body has already passed through, why is it that the tail cannot? Tell me, where does the crux lie?

Today, this little nephew brings this forth before the multitude as an offering to my Dharma-uncle, the Great Master Abbot, praying only that his longevity may equal that of Zhaozhou, that he may act as a great advocate for the Buddha-dharma, and cause all under heaven...

This humble monk has thoroughly penetrated this one extraordinary and momentous matter. Having descended from the seat, he, together with the administrative officials, the head officers, and the great assembly, earnestly prostrates and requests:
we humbly hope that, out of compassion, you will deign to grant us your instruction.
Chan Master Wuyong Kuan, at the request of Master Zhongfeng of Tianmu, led the assembly: "Vividly clear is the head of every blade of grass; vividly clear is the meaning of the Patriarchs.
On Mount Tianmu, the ancient Buddha shines upon both heaven and earth. A tiger bites a tiger; a snake swallows a turtle’s nose.
He threw down his staff and said, "It comes straight down—quickly, look with your eyes! He descended from the seat, and the assembly held incense in their sleeves.
"I humbly request the Great Monk Huanzhu to compassionately grant us instruction. Having spoken thus, he descended from his seat.
Master Qiyan Chang and Master Daoyuan of Guifeng ascended the hall for the formal discourse: "When masters meet, how could it depend on forms or words?
We strike the drum and ascend the hall merely to present this offering. We offer it to our Guifeng Master, who has condescended to descend from his exalted position..."

Venerable Sir: Formerly, at the conclusion of the Master Ying’an’s expression of gratitude to Dahuì, he said: "The void may be measured and the wind may be bound, yet no one can fully describe the Buddha’s merits.
Now, as we descend from our seats, I join the assembly in respectfully requesting the Honorable Compassion of the Abbot to grant us an instruction.
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun, the Reverend Mengtang of Ruelong, ascends the hall and says: "The great person possesses great vision;
with great wisdom, they attain great function. With a black lacquer bamboo whisk, they overturn mountains and seas; with a *bājiāo* staff, they strike at empty space."
It is such that Śākyamuni and Maitreya must fold their hands in submission, while Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra find no place to hide their bodies.
Therefore it is said: "To kill a person, one must have the sword that kills; to bring a person to life, one must have the blade that gives life.
If one has the blade that gives life but lacks the sword that kills, all living beings cannot die. If one has the sword that kills but lacks the blade that gives life, all [living beings]...
A dead person cannot be made to live. To make a dead person live is to kill a living person. Even so, one still falls into the trap of merit and achievement, burying the fundamental principle.
Have you not seen how one day Master Fuyong visited his fellow student, Master Shixing?
Shixing ascended the hall, took a staff in his right hand, leaned it against his left side, and after a long while said, "If this matter were not..."
"Brother Fuyong has indeed spoken with great difficulty and full detail," he said, and then descended from the seat. Shixing spoke thus:

"Li Xiang bites at the red edge. In this present age, one who can bare his shoulders to bear the burden and hold it up with a bare hand—transcending all triviality and cutting through like a nail being driven home or iron being severed—is none other than my brother, Master Ruelong alone.
Do not say that because the land is vast and people are few, one must keep this secret."

Do not let it leak away. We only pray that you will loosen the constraints of the formal path and accommodate the needs of the times, so that those who merely receive the words and remain stuck in phrases may thoroughly realize this singular, extraordinary matter of the direct pointing and single transmission. Would this not be most fitting?
Having descended from the seat, together with the Head Seat and the assembly, we extend our prostrations and request that you graciously propagate it for us.
Chan Master Chushi Qi, upon the arrival of Master Zhuquan of Lingyin, ascended the hall and said: "I cite Master Guanghui Lian’s words:
'In the assembly of my former teacher, I saw him raise a bamboo cane and ask the monk Xing: "If you call it a bamboo cane, you commit an offense;
if you do not call it a bamboo cane, you turn your back on the truth. What do you say? Xing stepped forward, snatched the cane away, and threw it to the ground.'"
The Master above asked, "What is this? Xiangyan (the former master) replied, "Blind. From this, Xing asked for enlightenment and entered through it.
I say that although Xing, that fellow from Liangzhou, attained enlightenment, he was indeed enlightened to a great extent; yet, he still did not exhaust the full intent of his former master.
The Master said, "How can you say such a thing, Guanghui? Did the former master truly have no intent? Take a torch and look: how thick is his skin? Below.
The slope does not move; a swift opportunity is difficult to encounter. If one is to be upheld in the supreme sense, one must first return my bamboo spring to Elder Brother Shi.
Chan Master Hongjue Mǎn and Chan Master Tōngxuán Qí arrived and led the assembly. Unexpectedly, Biéfēng personally encountered [the karmic retribution].
A rope of force. Without cause, one sees Mount Sumeru. How could this be a matter of excessive concealment? From of old, the direct blow values the indirect strike.
Have you not seen how Danxia visited National Teacher Zhong? Danxia asked the attendant, "Is the National Teacher in? The attendant said, "He is indeed here;
he simply does not see guests. Danxia said, "How profoundly deep! The attendant said, "Not only you, Venerable Sir, but even the Buddha..."
Even with one's eyes, one cannot see it. Danxia said, "The dragon gives birth to dragon cubs; the phoenix gives birth to phoenix chicks.
When the National Teacher woke from his sleep, the attendant reported this to him. The National Teacher then struck the attendant twenty blows and expelled him from the monastery.

Upon hearing of this, Danxia sighed and remarked, "He is truly not falsely called the National Teacher of Nanyang. Was this not Danxia striking from the side to manifest the National Teacher’s direct blow?

It was because the National Preceptor’s direct striking revealed that there was nothing hidden; once it was known that there was nothing hidden, the Great Function naturally manifested with a chilling majesty.
Only then could the ancestral seal be held high and the "blow-off" sword be laid across the breast.

He eradicates the manifest proclamations of the present age and brings forth the ancestral style of the predecessors. He rouses and elevates the simultaneous practice of "knocking" and "singing," suddenly seizing the opportunity for the mutual exchange of host and guest.
When host and guest exchange places, clouds obscure the vast fields and mists lock the long sky.

When knocking and singing proceed together, the melody issues from the blue heavens and the wind arises throughout the assembly. It reaches the point where the mountains, rivers, and the great earth all become the sound of the lute.
The grasses, trees, and groves lean low in accordance with the direction of the wind. At this very moment, what is the matter that leaves nothing hidden?
[He] strikes the meditation staff and says: "Do you wish to understand? Descending from the seat, I join in requesting Master Tongxuan to clearly point it out for the sake of all of you."
Master San-yi of Huashan arrived and led the assembly. At Mengchang’s gate, there were three thousand men with pearl-adorned shoes;

in the Jin-gu Garden, there were eight hundred women in embroidered robes. Yet for a monk like me, who has come to partake of this fragrant meal and offer sustenance to the myriad sages within these same halls, three transformations have purified the monastery and gathered all emanations into a single place.
Therefore, to take even one step forward causes the earth to tremble.
Throughout the infinite network of worlds, taking a single step back would sever ten billion great wind-wheels;

neither advancing nor retreating, the authentic command is enacted, cutting off all ten directions in its seat. Even if it were thus, it would still not be the total functioning of a patch-robed monk.
Do you wish to see this total functioning? Raising his whisk, he said: "Look! Look! The King of Space."
The Buddha, the Buddha Prabhūtaratna, the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū, and the forty thousand Buddhas named and titled Candrasūryapradīpa—
all of them, upon the tip of this mountain monk’s whisk, blow the great Dharma conch and beat the great Dharma drum.
He expounds the great Dharma and performs great Buddha-works; each and every Buddha-work pervades the entire Dharma-realm.

That is to say, a single hair manifests spiritual transformations, and all Buddhas speak of them together until the end of future kalpas, yet one cannot find their limit. Holding his whisk upside down, he said:
"As for turning the handle upside down, even the Buddhas of the three periods and the ancestral masters of successive generations ultimately [could not reach it]."
Even I have groped about my own mind and found nothing; how much less could you all possibly know the secrets of the eggplant and the gourd?

This morning, by great fortune, we have encountered the arrival of the Honored One Heshang Huashan, whose majestic carriage graces us and whose celestial discernment looks down upon us from on high. Upon descending from the seat, let us together offer this invitation:
may he compassionately provide detailed instruction for the sake of everyone present.

Compiled by Xingyue of Loudong, Abbot of Lian’an Chan Monastery at Shiba Jian in Wulin.
Welcoming the Venerable Elder and Expressing Gratitude for the Outline of the Teaching.
Upon the arrival of fellow practitioners, Chan Master Shishuang Yuan addressed the assembly from the high seat: "The winds rustle through the cool scenery; Fellow seekers visit this secluded place.
We boil water from the mountain springs for tea; We burn firewood from the caves to heat the cauldron. Take care."
Chan Master Yangqi Hui: Elder Yangqi Quan came to the hall for the formal discourse. [The Master] said: "The transmission of the flower carries a grievance against those present.
Facing the wall for nine years, speaking in barbarian tongues and Chinese alike—within the scope of one's own nature, this cuts off heaven and earth.
But tell me, what is the phrase that cuts off heaven and earth? Is there anyone who can speak it? If not, Yungai has lost."
Benefit.
Zen Master Wuzu Fayan addressed the assembly of elders and abbots upon ascending the hall: "When Linji entered the gate, he immediately shouted—what kind of bowl is that making such a sound?
When Deshan entered the gate, he immediately struck with his staff—forcing the crooked to become straight. Yunmen’s three phrases, Caodong..."
The Five Ranks. To have one's eyes wide open and yet be dreaming—why is this so? "In the state of Guoqing, the talent is noble; in a wealthy household, the child is spoiled.
When Master Shitai and his disciples ascended the hall, he spoke on the verse by our former master concerning Linji’s three blows of the staff, saying: "A single punch..."
With a single fist, he toppled the Yellow Crane Tower; with one kick, he overturned the Parrot Isle. When there is spirit, he adds to that spirit;
where there is no elegance, he creates elegance. O assembly, if you arrive at the gate of Baiyun, you must surely require the support of all to lend him a hand.
Chan Master Zhenjing Wen ascended the hall because Elder Xiaoyao had arrived. "A person from deep within the green mountains comes here into my midst of red dust.

In this red dust, we happen not to see one another; there are only white clouds and flowing streams. What distinction can there be between the ears and eyes? What use for floating fame and fleeting profit?
Is it that the red dust is false, or is it that the green mountains are true? Between these two paths of right and wrong, how many [are lost]?"
It has not yet come to an end. Fortunately, we have encountered a person of leisure who can eloquently expound upon the profound principle.
[The Master] descends from his seat. Because an elder from Shuanglin came to the hall, [the Master said]: "A Treasure Mountain is not easily reached; having reached it, do not return empty-handed."
"Is there anyone here who does not turn back empty-handed? He then threw down his staff and asked, "What is this?
After a long silence, he said, "I have not seen the old Śākyamuni of the Twin Trees, nor have I heard that Maitreya has descended to be born. With a shout, he descended from his seat.
Elder Zhangjiang came to ascend the hall. He raised the following case: A monk asked Yunmen, “What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?
Yunmen said, “Water flows uphill on the Eastern Mountain. Letan, however, is not like this. If someone were to ask me, “What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?
I would simply tell them: “Far removed from Hongjing, one enters deep into the Jewel Mountain. Great assembly, tell me: what do you say?
"Is it the same? Is it different? Suddenly, if a monk were to come forth and say, "What place is this to be discussing sameness and difference?
that would be truly rare. One must actually arrive at this ground before one can succeed; if you have not yet arrived, you must not act with such haste.
Elder Yonggu ascends the hall: Deeply secluded and far-reaching, no one can reach it. Yet when one arrives, the mountains are green and the waters are lush;

it is a realm entirely distinct from the human world. How excellent, O virtuous Chan practitioners! The river moon shines, the pines rustle in the breeze; throughout the eternal night and the clear sky, what is there to do?
One cannot help but find strange the cuckoo that, though the spring mountains are boundlessly beautiful, still cries out, "It is not as good as returning home."

Because Elder Qingliang arrived, [the Master] ascended the hall. "When the heat and afflictions are exhausted, cool clarity manifests; when conceptual discrimination does not arise, empty luminosity shines of itself.
Only then shall I press my fingers and the Ocean-Seal Samādhi emit its light. If you momentarily raise your mind, the dust of worldly toil arises first.
He then shouted, "I would strike down all Buddhas of the three periods of time with a single blow! I would fill the ditches and block the ravines, casting them east and west!"
"West! Leave it to everyone to see. Suddenly, he took up his staff and said, "The Buddhas of the past were like this;
the Buddhas of the present are like this; the Buddhas of the future will be like this. He then threw the staff down and said, "Look!"
Because Elder Kuaishan had ascended the hall, the Great Way of Kuairang was right before one's eyes.
Though he moved back and forth across the crossroads, as if lingering there, he then looked at the assembly for a long time, let out a shout, and descended from his seat.
Because the Master of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra had arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "The Dharma-realm is the fundamental substance of the body and mind of all sentient beings.

He then picked up his staff and said: "This is not the Dharma-realm; it is the wondrous essence of all of you—the numinous clarity, vast penetration, and great, empty stillness that has existed from time immemorial.
Therefore, whether this land or other realms, the heavens or the hells, the six paths of ordinary beings or the four..."
The Sage’s mind and the insentient are one and the same—without distinction, without destruction, and without admixture.

It is like the luminous pearls of Indra’s net, mutually penetrating and interpenetrating one another; thus it may be said that the realms of infinite lands are not separated by even a hair’s breadth between self and other.
Throughout the ten ages of past and present, from beginning to end, nothing is ever apart from the tip of this staff.

If this is so, then it is more than merely casting the great trichiliocosm beyond the four quarters or containing Mount Sumeru within a mustard seed. Now, the ten billion suns and moons, the ten billion Mount Sumerus, and the ten billion worlds are all contained within this very staff.
[The Master] then throws it down and says: "I cast it right onto the faces of you all!"
"Did you see it just now? Do you believe it? The inconceivable power of liberation, the playful manifestation of spiritual penetrations and wondrous functions, are all present before you.
They do not depend on any external arts; they are simply the constant nature of our own mind. With a shout, he descended from his seat.
The Great Master Huacheng ascends the hall. "The three realms offer no peace; they are like a burning house.

Having escaped the burning house but not yet reached the precious destination, one remains in the conjured city. Today we meet at this conjured city, yet we do not see where the precious destination lies.
It turns out it is simply the former Elder Yuan. Assembly, it turns out that from the very beginning, everyone here is but the people of old. [He] prostrates.
Please take care of yourself.
Zen Master Dahui Puguang, at the request of Master Shi of Xuedou, ascended the hall.
Regarding Yangshan’s saying, "If Master Uncle Dongsi were here, Huiji would not suffer in silence," Yangshan knew only himself and was unaware of others. —Jingshan.
This is not so. Had the Master Xuedou been alive, the monks of the world would not have suffered such desolation.
Why? Have you not seen that ancient Xuedou said: "The cold wood held in the palm—how laughable is this total mechanism! The autumn waters held crosswise—how extinguishable is this partial raising!
This caused those who gaze upon the limits of the eight directions not to vie for balance; seeing such a man, they were brought under his command.

Aṅgē. Zen Master Huā of Yìng’ān ascended the hall at Chánglú. "The wind blows and the grass bends; the water flows and the channel forms. Those who were enemies in past lives now enter and exit the same gate together.
Hearing of Zen, hearing of the Way, is like a duck listening to thunder; seeing the Buddha, seeing the Patriarchs, is like the wind [passing through].
Passing by the trees, he saw the flagpole across the river and immediately turned back. He deserves thirty blows beneath his heels for failing to appreciate the view.
One must truly knit their eyebrows together to live and die as one. Now tell me, how do you explain the phrase "The Five Heinous Offenses Hearing Thunder"?
After a long silence, he said: "The Great Man Above; Qiu Yi Ji."
