"Tomorrow there is a great assembly at Mount Tai; will you go for the meal, Master? Mañjuśrī, like a leper seeking companions, lay down as if sleeping.
Mazu followed the heterodox and pursued the evil; Mañjuśrī then went out and said, "Tsk! Even if you were to seize it and run off, it would still be like Hanlu the hound chasing after a clod."
Master Changer Qianyan ascended the hall. Master Yuxi of Shuanglin addressed the assembly: "In the heavens there is no Maitreya; on the earth there is no Maitreya.
A thousand gates and ten thousand doors stand open; the wheel-hammer strikes but once. He descended from the seat.
When Master Youyun of Shuanglin ascended the hall for the morning service, he said: "Meeting a fellow traveler on the road, we pass each other shoulder to shoulder;
the lifelong task of study is finished. But tell me, what serves as proof? He held up his staff, struck once, and said: "Empty-handed, yet holding a hoe."
The guest arrives at the hall; donning his robes, he ascends the Dharma seat. This man of the Way is a high monk—initially, one might think him full of wonders.
Yet, in truth, he is capable of nothing. A west wind blows a fine rain; fallen leaves fill the empty courtyard. When a guest comes to visit, the green mountains themselves welcome and see him off.
Chan Master Tianru Ze, while roasting yams as an offering for guests who had arrived amidst the snow, addressed the assembly:
"Lan Can caught me roasting my yams; Envious of my deep seclusion, he compared me to Damei. A guest came unbidden to ask: 'When will the one flower and five petals bloom?
'Suzhou fool! Suzhou fool! Outside the gate, the snow piles high; To the bone, he leaves you frozen."
Once, when an old fellow practitioner went up to the hall for the sermon, [the Master] said: "A golden fish that has passed through the net—how could it be as good as one that never entered?
Suddenly, if you can realize a point of entry, even if you are not a fellow practitioner, it will still be quite difficult.

The Abbot of Jiangshan arrived and addressed the assembly: "Full presentation and partial presentation; the complete treasury and the half-treasury. Ten inches make one foot; ten feet make one fathom.
A foot has the form of a foot; a pair of scissors has the pattern of scissors. Even a whisk is used to strike a circular diagram."
Carrying his staff across his shoulder, he does not look back at others. How could Master Zhigong be a mere idle monk?
When Zen Master Tianmu Li and Master Yunchao Yan ascended the hall, they cited an ancient worthy who, upon the arrival of an old friend, said:
"We meet, yet no brow is raised; you go east, and I go west. Crimson clouds pierce the azure void; the white sun circles the celestial pivot."
"Mi, today Master Rui Guang has arrived at Nanhu. How do you see him? Without raising an eyebrow:
'You go east and I go west; crimson clouds pierce the azure void; the white sun circles Mount Sumeru. Nevertheless, I am not the same as the ancients."
Master Shuai-an Zong ascended the hall for the morning service. Last night, a tiger on the South Mountain bit a great beast;
its life was not spared. Today, Vajra and the clay deity rub each other’s backs; with a single squeeze, the bone comes out.

But as for Xuefeng’s three visits to Touzi and his nine ascents to Dongshan—how is that? Where there is no seeking, human relations are pleasant; where one does not drink, one follows others’ example.
The price of wine is high.
Chan Master Yuansou Duan ascends the hall to express his gratitude to Baozhong Yuan, the Chief Librarian. He cites Master Dazhu, who said:
"I have heard the Master of Jiangxi say that within one's own precious treasury, everything is fully present; its use is entirely free and at one's command. Not...
If you seek it externally, from this moment on, let it rest. Even throughout the entirety of the ten directions of the world, there is not a single speck of dust that is not your own treasure.
The Master said: "Master Ma spoke thus for a time; Dazhu heard thus for a time, never forgetting it until the end of his life, thereby attaining great utility.
Were it not for deep and firm faith, how could one penetrate to the very crown of the head?"
It is thus. In years past, the Abbot of Zhongyuan manifested this very Dharma-gate within the ancient Mount Mù.
Is there anyone who possesses deep faith and firm resolve, thereby attaining great benefit? On this day, you have graciously deigned to visit; I hope you will kindly remain with us for a while.
When Chief Seat Duanjiang came to ascend the hall, the mountain monk [the abbot] recalled how, in years past during his travels, he had stayed at this mountain.
Master Heixuan of Yewang sent him a verse which said: (Qingxi) Long and short sounds, I lean alone against the corridor pillar.

The three periods of time do not come; A single sheet of cold spring water. Not only are there no sentient beings, There is no Buddha, and no self either. This short verse is paired with the long one.
Poem: To dispel worldly concerns and find contentment. Midnight frost flowers fall; the sun is at its zenith.

Within the vastness of heaven and earth, there is only Hanshan. Good assembly, since the time of the Patriarchs, they have upheld that one stroke upon the crowns of our monks—like a spark from stone or a flash of lightning.
Whether you grasp it or fail to grasp it, you cannot avoid losing your life. All.
This old monk cannot be let out. Today, because his dharma-heir and foremost disciple, Chan Master Duanjiang, has come to visit, I bring this up for you all; everyone, realize it!
Ascending the hall to express gratitude to Elder Jixiangxiang: Bodhidharma exerted his full strength to uphold the Dharma, yet he could say nothing more than "I do not know.
The Sixth Patriarch took up the entire burden, yet he could say nothing more than "I do not understand.

Those of small roots and small capacity, with frivolous and arrogant minds, rely on their teachers' lineages, scholastic learning, and superficial entanglements; how can they dare to give rise to such vain expectations? — Your Dharma Nephew, Dongling.
Having long dwelt among the assembly, you are deeply familiar with this matter. How do you express the single phrase for responding to conditions and benefiting beings?
"The golden lock is snapped; the celestial qilin is raised high, and the iron whip strikes three hundred times."
When Chan Master Yuyan Ji and Master Guding of Baotuo went up to the hall, [Yuyan] raised the case of Longya, who said:

"My senior brother Yunju attained the second phrase; I have attained the first phrase. The Master said: "Great indeed is Longya, knowing only how to open his mouth wide, yet failing to realize his tongue is dragging on the ground.
Now, I, this mountain monk, have received the grace of my Dharma-brother, the Venerable Master of Baotuo..."

I am honored that you have condescended to visit this empty mountain with your carriage and elephants. I only regret that my place is so desolate and neglected that I have nothing to offer you in worship. How could I dare to falsely communicate any news?
"The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara bought some wheat cakes with money; when he let go of his hand, they turned out to be steamed buns"—this is the second phrase.
But what is the first phrase? [He gave a shout and descended from his seat.]
The attendants of Lingyin and Tiantong went up to the hall for the formal discourse. [The Master] raised the following case:

When Attendant Guang said to Xuan Sha, "If you, my uncle, can realize Chan, I, your nephew, shall forge an iron boat and sail it into the sea. After Xuan Sha took up residence there, he sent someone with a letter to inquire of Guang, saying, "Have you finished forging the iron boat yet?
Guang had no reply. Later, Fenyang Zhao spoke on his behalf, saying, "I see only the awl."
Touli said, "I do not see the squareness of the chisel's tip. Xuangjue said, "Xuan Sha was merely a poor man thinking of old debts.
The Master said, "Whether great or small, Xuan Sha and Attendant Guang have not yet forgotten self and others; they alternately bring disgrace upon their own house.
Even after a thousand years, they will be subjected to scrutiny by others. I, Cuiping, will never follow those ancients; everything is simply as it always has been. Yesterday I received..."

The attendants from Lingyin and Tiantong have come to visit me. After the initial greetings of the season were concluded, we burned incense and shared tea. Upon finishing the tea, they were escorted back to their guest quarters.

Naturally, the host and guests found their paths in harmony, and the formalities between uncle and nephew were forgotten. Today, as I ascend the hall, I briefly set forth these matters, hoping for your enlightened understanding.
Chan Master Wumen Can thanked Baoyan upon ascending the hall: "Without stirring a single speck of dust, without revealing a single mechanism—like brocade wrapping a rock, or cotton padding a weight.
Having seen this, Kaixian directly adorns it with a hundred jewels and bears it upon his head."
Why is this? There are wandering ghosts who do not recognize it, and mindless people who do not know it.
Chan Master Shuzhong Yunchen thanked National Master Qingliang of Kaiyuan Temple for presiding over the assembly on the high seat:

"The one path that transcends all is not transmitted by the thousand sages; before you have even set foot upon it, you are already separated from it by a great trichiliocosm. Within Mount Qingliang dwell ten thousand bodhisattvas."
Dragging plows and hauling harrows—yet within Fangguang Temple, the Venerable Banzhian set out offerings for the midday meal;
only the Kaiyuan Stone Buddha remained stubbornly firm, such that the wind could not enter it and the rain could not wet it.
More than five thousand scrolls, each word distinct, have all come from the Dragon Palaces and the Ocean Treasuries.
The Head Seat Zhongfu and the Abbot Yunchang ascend the hall. When the wind blows, the grass bows; when the water arrives, the channel is formed.
Once the true command is exercised, the ten directions are cut off at once. Muzhou pressed people until their feet broke; Yunmen cast down a chip of firewood.
Though these were indeed unconventional and transcendent of the school, they could not avoid being "wrapped in hemp and paper. This is truly laughable and truly pitiable—at the crest of Wushan Ridge.
The matter of meeting face-to-face: those who know the sound know it; after this, who else will know?
When Master Duofu Qiujiang arrived with his attendants, he ascended the hall. Penetrating the school and penetrating the path, carrying the essence and following the way:
a single phrase fully raised, and ten thousand functions respond at once. A monk asked Duofu, "What is the one [Dharma] of Duofu?"
“Thick bamboo. Fuyun said, “One stem, two stems, leaning askew. A monk said, “I, this student, do not understand. Fuyun said, “Two stems, four stems, bent.
How strange! O Zen adepts: This is a nose-rope for an ox; this is a bit of iron in a horse’s mouth.
To hold the seal of the wondrously luminous mind and employ the vital mechanism beyond the formal categories—it requires great merit to achieve this. Now, as for that monk—
If one asks in such a manner, is there still any sense of betrayal? The golden rooster cries upon the jade balustrade; with a single cry, it penetrates straight through to the summit of Mount Sumeru.
—Written by Chan Master Yujie in gratitude to Librarian Ru of Jian-nan, Librarian Qing of Yun-gu, and Librarian Wuze of Zhen-chang.
The Master ascends the hall. He cites the Ancestral Master Baiyun’s words upon opening the hall and offering incense, which said:
"Among you, there may be fellow practitioners of the robe and bowl who have offered even a single word or half a phrase that has benefited me; together we shall extend our gratitude.

Now that this mountain monk has newly taken up residence, two or three old friends have come from afar to offer their congratulations. These are not merely words or half-phrases—how could I not have a piece of incense as an offering?"
Nurturing. Burning *fengxiang* (Cinnamomum camphora) is a matter pertaining to the periphery of Bodhi; burning *huangshu* (yellow ripe wood) is a matter pertaining to the Buddhas and Patriarchs.

Yet now, with a single fierce blaze in the incense burner, he wishes for everyone throughout the entire earth to know that this is the true ground of the plains and fields within the jurisdiction of Jiaxing Prefecture in Western Zhejiang.
But tell me, what kind of incense is being burned? After a long silence, he said: "It does not descend from the pavilion."
Chan Master Chushi Qi, with the Record Clerk Xuechuang Guang of Jingci Monastery, ascended the hall for the formal discourse:
"Superior man! Qiu Yiji! He transformed three thousand; seventy scholars. You, young student! Eight or nine disciples. Excellent work on benevolence! One may thereby know the rites."
He summoned the assembly, saying: "What kind of talk is this? None of the disciples of Confucius recognized it; the blue-eyed barbarian monk smiled and nodded his head.

When the various mountains ascend to the hall, a single flower blooms and the great earth is filled with spring; a single leaf falls and the whole world is autumn. A movement on the strings distinguishes the melody."
In music, one prizes the connoisseur. A blink of an eye or a raising of an eyebrow has already missed the mark.
Thus, the command not to err seizes the vital ford; the flavorless discourse blocks the mouths of men.

Deshan’s staff, Linji’s shout, Guizhi’s raised finger, Luzu’s wall-gazing, Guizong’s slaying of the snake, Daisui’s slash-and-burn, Shigong’s drawing of the bow, and Zihu’s watching of the dog—whether it be these,
Thus, there may be level fields and shallow grass; or iron walls and silver mountains; or flashing lightning and crashing thunder; or mud and water mixed together.
Fully upholding the true seal and alone shaking the great framework—yet when examined, there is inevitably leakage.
Therefore, "this very mind is Buddha" is, for the present age, not yet entry into the profound mystery; "neither mind nor Buddha" is still merely pointing out the tracks.

Ultimate! The path that goes beyond has not been transmitted by a thousand sages. Students exhaust their bodies like monkeys grasping at shadows; is there even a trace of "entering into" it? Where the level marshes end, there are green mountains; the traveler is further beyond the green mountains. Again, a monk asked Master Huanglong Ji, "What is the meaning of Chan? Ji said, "Slander is its meaning. The Master [said]: [The Master] said: "If you wish to understand this matter, you must first abandon all conceptualization.

If you do not abandon conceptualization, you will never see your own face. Even if you can speak of the myriad dharmas with eloquence as vast as the ocean, it is merely adding frost to snow. If you can cut off the flow of thought and speech, then the ten directions are all empty space, and the three periods of time are but a single moment. At this point, there is no place for the mind to dwell, and there is nothing for the intellect to grasp. This is what is called 'the great function of the Way. It is not something to be sought through study or deliberation;

it is only to be realized through the direct pointing of a teacher. Therefore, the ancients said: 'The Way is not far; it is simply that people themselves create complications. If you can let go of all attachments and cast away all views, then you will naturally accord with the Way. Do not seek it outside; do not look within. If you try to find it within, you will lose it; if you try to grasp it outside, you will miss it. It is like the moon reflected in water—neither the water nor the moon can be grasped. When the clouds disperse and the sky clears, the moon shines forth of itself. This is the ultimate meaning of Chan."
It is said: "If someone asks what the Chan of Nanhu takes as its meaning, tell them it takes 'praise' (zan) as its meaning.

But tell me, is that which is slandered the same as that which is praised? To see with the eyes is blindness; to hear with the ears is deafness; to speak with the mouth is dumbness; to think with the mind is exhaustion.
Ten feet of snow bury the rocks at the edge of heaven; several pines snap in the cold at the cave entrance.
Wumeng Eji ascends the hall for the formal teaching. He cites Master Baiyun Yuan: "Having written out a thousand sheets of paper, it is merely a weariness of heart and hand;
human sentiments are like Mount Taihua—how can they compare to the loftiness of the Way-spirit?
The Master says: "Even the great Baiyun still has this lingering. Yongzuo received a visit from his elder brother, Master Wumeng; with coarse tea and plain talk, they sat in stillness.
Sit in forgetfulness and let go of all concerns. If there were even a single trace of the fundamental self, neither you nor I would find ease. Why? When people are at peace, they do not speak;
when water is level, it does not flow.
When Daojiu arrived at the hall for the formal lecture, he recited: "The wind whistles through the cool scenery; Fellow seekers visit this desolate place. Tea is brewed by the mountain stream;
Firewood is burned by the cave’s edge. The Master said: "Old man Baimu, you are poor and cannot afford vegetarian fare. I am busy and have no time for cursive script.
It is simply that it is improper to take the property of the Sangha for one's own personal use."
When the various mountain lecture masters ascend the hall, they say: "The former sages taught that all phenomena are not born of themselves, nor are they born from another;

they are not born from both together, nor are they born without cause. Therefore, it is said they are unborn. The entire earth is a sesame cake; you may bite it horizontally or vertically as you please.
At Nālandā Monastery in the Western Heavens, some ten thousand monks each get to eat of it. There was only Mā...
The Great Deity Hākarā could not eat it; he struck Mount Sumeru with a single blow, shattering it into a hundred fragments, and Śakra leaped up to the Brahma Heaven.
Dongshan Shouzhi ascended the hall. He related the story of Quandai Daowen visiting Ciming. Ciming said, "A single cloud spans the mouth of the valley;
from where does the traveler come? Daowen said, "What fire came last night? It has burned out the graves of the ancients.
Ciming said, "Not yet—speak further! Daowen then let out a tiger’s roar. Ciming struck him with his sitting mat, and Daowen pushed Ciming onto the meditation platform.
Having clarified this, Ming made a tiger’s roar. Quan said, “I have seen over eighty virtuous teachers (kalyāṇamitra), but only you have succeeded in carrying on the Linji tradition.
The Master said, “You have used a term incorrectly. At that time, how could Ciming have tolerated such a madman speaking like this?
He gave him another blow with his sitting cloth. Let us see what kind of trickery he will perform next—just as his eyes [met].
As soon as his eyes flickered, Linji struck him with his staff and drove him out. The Dharma lineage of Linji had not yet reached its current state of decline.

When Master Liaohan retired from Lingyan, he returned to deliver a lecture of thanks. He said: "One who acts as a true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) drives away the plow and seizes the food, transforming the ordinary into the sacred.
For one who encounters such a spiritual friend, it is like seeing a blue lotus; the faculty of the eye becomes pure."
It is pure. Those who hear the Dharma taught by a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) are like those who eat the food of the Land of Fragrant Accumulation;

their pores are all filled with fragrance—this is what Master Lingyan meant. Having returned once more to Xielǐ, my humble heart is deeply satisfied. It is my good fortune to have the company of these dragon-like and elephant-like sages;
I hope you will cherish yourself.
Former Chan Master Nan Shiyou, before [Master] Tianxi of Nanyue at Jingxi, ascended the hall for the formal discourse.
He cited the case of Chan Master Datian Tong: when Master Shuikong arrived, Datian seized his sitting cloth and said, "No need for greetings."
Nor does one employ the conventional greetings of arrival. Xingkong said, "If you intend to act in such a manner, I fear human sentiments will not be satisfied.
He threw out his hands and said, "Are they satisfied yet? Xingkong picked up his sitting mat and said, "If you employ conventional greetings, I fear you will lose track of where you came from."
Dian said, "There is no harm in meeting for a brief moment.

Today at Lingyan, having received the arrival of Venerable Nanyue Tiansi, after exchanging greetings regarding the weather, [Lingyan] said, "You have come from Huqiu specifically to offer congratulations; you have not lost your way."
Human sentiments are fully satisfied; yet everyone remains unaware. Fortunately, there is the pillar to bear witness.
When Master Zhongxu of Guangxiao ascends the hall, Yangqi pulls the plow and Jiufeng drags the harrow—idle talk!
Daowu performs a dance and Xuefeng rolls the ball—idle talk! As for Master Zhongxu of Guangxiao:
"Not so. The Go-board Stone atop Mount Lingxiao is spread out at my gate for sale to anyone. Who would say that the market is sparse these days?
Every time it is brought up, it is ever new. Then he asked, "But tell me, what will Lingyan do?
He planted his staff and descended from the seat.

When Chan Master Liaoyuan Yu ascended the hall for the assembly, he said: "The Tathāgatas of the three periods of time share one tongue; within the Great Canon of the Teachings, there is no dharma to be spoken.
In the hands of the patch-robed monk lies the zero-point of the balance scale: ten thousand miles of vast sky, a solitary moon shines bright.
The Head Seat has his own excellence, yet he does not follow the beaten tracks; he walks freely through the thicket of brambles, uprooting the root-nails of the people of this age."
The Wedge. Elder Miaozhi ascends the hall: "Gautama’s tongue has no bone; Miaozhi’s skin has blood beneath it.
In the Western Heaven, they understand how to keep a wax man from freezing; in this Eastern Land, the 'goose-guarding snow' is unheard of. Turning my thoughts back, Baizhang had three secrets."
"Enjoy your tea; be careful; return to the hall and rest. How many Dharma masters and monks know this? Wandering aimlessly, they employ cleverness only to turn it into clumsiness.
*Shouts.* Chief Seat Xi ascends the hall:
"The bright sun shines in the heavens; the blind man gropes upon the ground. For a monk of true substance, there is nowhere [to go]."
He let out a breath of relief. Did you not see how one day when a fellow practitioner arrived, as soon as he stepped onto the Dharma Hall, Xinghua shouted;
the monk also shouted. Xinghua shouted again; the monk shouted once more. Xinghua said, "Look at this blind fellow, still acting as the master!
As the monk hesitated, Xinghua seized his staff and drove him straight down from the hall. An attendant remarked, "This monk has offended the Master."
Huayan said: "He just now possessed both the provisional and the real; he possessed both illumination and function.
Yet, as soon as I crossed my hands twice before him, he was unable to move. For a blind fellow like this, when would I wait to strike him?
Aha-ha! The lion cub turns back; the dragon horse foal leaps and bounds. Smash it!"
At this ultimate barrier, both host and guest fail to maintain their awareness.

Some might say, "At that moment, it would have been better to give another shout," or else, "Otherwise, one should overturn the meditation seat and leave with sleeves flapping. What room is there for conversation?
This mountain monk does not open his fist unless he encounters someone extraordinary. Now that Great Master Dadao has come from afar, I intend to let the assembly here before me see him through.
The ancients both attained the mutual vision; do you understand this thoroughly? "The green mountains do not lock in their soaring momentum;
the vast blue sea surely knows the height from which they come.
When Chief Seat Yongfu Ying arrived, he ascended the hall [and said]: "Beyond the four propositions, transcending the hundred negations—Mahāyāna Dharma is preached within a dream."
Hold this up. I venture to ask the great assembly: Are dream and waking the same or different?

If you can speak with such bold clarity, not only will there be no place for Little Śākyamuni to hide his form, but you may take the three hundred li of water on the Poyang Lake and contain it within a single drop of the Yuanyang Lake; it would be neither too wide nor too narrow, lacking nothing.
The rest? Do you understand it thoroughly yet? To startle the multitude, one must be a man of heroic spirit; to match the victor, one must be the lion’s cub.
At the West Hall of Jiazu, ascending to the Dharma Hall: before the peak of Jiazu, the wind is still;

beneath the hall of Śākyamuni, the waves cling to the sky. Leaping upward, he brushes past the azure heavens; a single melody of the *huqia* flute has not yet reached its end. For these few days, this mountain monk has cast [aside]...
Having departed from the great assembly, I returned last night and was able to meet with Venerable Kāśyapa.
Since it is said that when emotions forget self and other, the Way naturally harmonizes host and guest, he raised up an old tangle that is truly impossible to pull apart.
Is there anyone among the assembly who can cut it through with a single stroke? After a long silence, he said: "Even if there were such a person, they would still be but a fellow of the weeds."

The West Hall Abbot of the Final School ascends the hall to offer thanks to the heads of the community. What does the entire Great Canon of the Teachings say? "Thus have I heard" was already mistaken from the start.
Before the Hall of Broad Blessing, the true command is enacted: a millstone in the void develops eight corners. Host and guest exchange roles;
granting and seizing are applied according to the moment. Turning over the great ocean, leaping down upon Mount Sumeru. *Striking the whisk:* Lake Tai.
Thirty-six thousand *qǐng*. When the moon is in the heart of the waves, to whom does it speak?
Master Wúxiǎng Zhòngmóu ascended the hall. Xinghuá received his fellow student; salt was wasted and vinegar was still required. Běnjué met a kindred spirit;
the Way exists when there is mutual witnessing. Since neither staff nor shout were employed, how could provisional and ultimate truth be applied? The Stone.
Above, with the pine roots, facing one another, my mind is naturally satisfied. Is it that the ancients were wrong, or is it that we of today are right?
Reaching this point, there is no need to debate right and wrong; ultimately, ancient and modern are of one essence. Striking a golden bell upon the summit of Mount Sumeru.
The pure breeze continues to blow without ceasing. (A shout. Venerable Yuan ascends the hall:
"From two comes one; do not cling even to that one. When the single mind does not arise, the myriad dharmas are without fault.
Since the Head Seat possesses such excellence, why need he open his mouth further? At the summit of a ten-thousand-fathom peak, he holds his fishing rod. (A shout.)
Drawing back the six dragons, they frequently fall into one’s hands; among the pines and upon the rocks, there is no hindrance to lingering for a while.

Within the rank of Buddhas and Patriarchs, it is simply a matter of pushing the door and entering the white hall. Do you all understand? The precious sword of Fengcheng has not yet emerged from its scabbard, yet night after night its cold light pierces the Dipper and Ox constellations.
When the Chief Seat was invited to ascend the hall, Fachang struck the drum with all his might, while Gongchen Wanxiang preached Chan.

These two elders were like Xu Liu carrying a single plank; they could not avoid each seeing only one side. I, Benjue, have readied my empty mind to observe the world, leaving everything to its own natural course.
Sometimes I steer against the wind, and sometimes I sail with the current; in either case, nothing is amiss. Therefore:
The Way is silent and desolate, yet not within; it is vast and expansive, yet not without. That it is silent and desolate, yet not within, means that a single hair pierces through all the apertures.

That it is vast and expansive, yet not without, means that all the apertures are gathered within a single hair. Have you not seen how, under Zhaozhou, two monks pushed each other aside, refusing to accept the position of the First Seat?
When the administrator informed Zhaozhou of this, Zhaozhou said, "Let them both be made the Second Seats. The Master [said]: [Note: The provided text ends with the Master's quote.]

Is this not "the head straight and the tail straight"? The Master then called to the assembly, saying: "Huangbo and Linji, father and son—when they open their mouths, it is not from their tongues.
Yangshan and Daowei of Mount Shishuang—divining with a ladle and listening to empty sounds. Old Ying’an splits open Mount Taihua and lets it loose."
He emerged from the Yellow River. Old Man Shishiweng held a torch made of ox-horn to illuminate the dark blue sea. The place where King Aśoka saw it must be known by all people.
One person pointed south, causing his influence to spread through Wu and Yue. In the vast emptiness of space, there is no need for a peg to be driven.

Riding a great Peng within the hollow of a lotus fiber, he casually knocks down the moon at the edge of the sky. Having stood for a long time before the assembly, I humbly pray that you will take care of yourself.
Chan Master Chaozong Ren arrived at Huangbo and requested him to ascend the hall. This is the place where Duanji emerged; it is the ancient path of Huangbo.

"Wherever one arrives, who says one has come as a guest? Everywhere is one's hometown. Thus, out of the fellowship of former fellow practitioners, I, a mountain monk, came to visit my Dharma nephew at Huangbo.
I was received with a hundred-li journey by a messenger sent to welcome me from afar, and I was further honored by the assembly’s earnest invitation to preach the Dharma.
Though it be a sincere heart, one cannot avoid mutual neglect. Why is this so? When masters meet, their mouths are already stumped;
what business is there for "this morning's person"? Generally, when one wishes to speak, words have already perished.
Ascending the Dharma seat, all join in joyful acclaim. Words having perished, what is there to acclaim? After a long silence, he said: "When meeting, there is naturally knowing."
[The Master] said, "To know sound, why must it be a pure breeze moving heaven and earth? He descended from his seat. (The host was Master Yinyuan.

When Chan Master Ruohan arrived at Ba’en, Master Yulin invited him to ascend the hall. The Rector proclaimed the memorial: [...]* *Note: The ellipsis indicates the omission of the specific text of the proclamation.*

I, your younger brother in the Dharma, consider myself fortunate to have shared the dais with my esteemed elder brother, the Great Abbot Ruo’an, for ten years. While I am but thirty years of age, my brother has already reached the stage of "not being confused" (forty).

His gracious visit brings great joy and celebration to the entire assembly. As I am currently observing the *jinzu* retreat to care for my parents, I am unable to personally lead the formal invitation before the multitude.
I therefore respectfully present this single robe of my late teacher. I pray that you, my esteemed elder brother, the Great Abbot, [will graciously accept it].
Never forgetting that he had long since entered the chamber of his former master, he had already caused a thunderous resonance throughout this region.

I respectfully request that you don the robe of the former master and sit upon the seat of the former master, revealing the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye so that all who see and hear may together illuminate the single aperture of the Ultimate.
This shall allow ignorant and inferior juniors like myself to sleep peacefully in our small rooms; it is not that I dare emulate the ancients by closing the door and striking the bell.
The Master of Sleep also somewhat admired the legacy of the High Ancestor’s “Deadly Barrier,” and that was all. When the Master received the draft, he said, "Does the assembly understand?
Our head monk, the Great Monk Dharma-brother Yulin, has already settled matters for everyone with a single blow.
Those who are clever need not hesitate; please come forward and stir up the discussion before the assembly. After the assembly had finished their questions, the Master spoke again.
He then said: "Let this dialogue cease for now. What kind of place is this? Everyone intends to point east and draw west here, speaking of long and short.
In years past, our late Master established the banner of the Dharma here;
subsequently, my Dharma-brother, the Venerable Yulin, expanded this vast gateway, truly renewing the ancient legacy. Now, tell me, Upāsaka—"

The day has arrived; it is truly beyond the reach of praise. How much more so when one ascends his precious throne before the great assembly of devas and humans to beat two pieces of leather, deceiving the Hu and mocking the Han!

Recalling my time with the Senior Monk (Wen Shangzuo), for twenty years since first seeing my late teacher, he has never, even for a single thread or speck of dust, deceived himself regarding this matter. Formerly, while in the meditation hall at Qing Shan...

I personally attended my late teacher to receive his instruction, enduring the full force of his hammer and tongs and remaining as steadfast as ice and snow; thus, I truly did not dare to deceive myself.
When I arrived at Baoyun Temple to assist my late teacher, I joined the water and mixed the mud, bearing the burden upon my entire being;

how could there ever have been even a hair’s breadth of self-deception? Later, after my late teacher passed away and the funeral arrangements were settled, I took up my staff and departed for other lands.
For eight or nine years now, Master Shan, if there had been even a single thread of self-deception within me, how would I dare to meet my Dharma brother, Venerable Yulin, face-to-face today?

Since you have honored me by inviting me to this seat to expound this matter for the assembly, I must not allow even a single thread of self-deception to deceive you, my worthy friends. Look to the left...
The Master said: "Now tell me, what is this matter? Where is the point where you, Elder, do not deceive yourself?
Do you know? If you do know, then clearly it is the supreme pivot of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; it is the vast, open treasury of the true Dharma eye for humans and devas.
If you do not know, I hope that when you descend from your seats shortly, all of you gentlemen will proceed together to the Abbot’s quarters."
I earnestly entreat the Abbot, the Venerable Master, not to be sparing with his efforts, but to bestow his compassion by applying the deep, piercing probe of the painful hammer.
This humble report is submitted, hoping it will meet with your discerning gaze.

Descending from the seat, he proceeded to Wanshou Temple, where he was invited to ascend the hall by the Venerable Master Sanyi. Host and guest exchanged roles as the master responded to the occasion through the shifting interplay of the biased and the correct, locking both in a double bind.
The golden needle traverses freely in wondrous harmony; before the hall of the ancient Buddhas, no trace is left. Upon the golden throne, one stands far beyond distinctions of high and low.
This is the point where Master Wanshou could never ordinarily be outwitted by others.

If you seek a standard within words, you bury your own spiritual brilliance; if you further seek external support beyond the phrases, you disgrace the former sages. Have you not seen what the former masters said?
The Way is indeed a most formidable Way; its continuity is exceedingly difficult. Today, this mountain monk shall borrow this board-beater to briefly open a single thread for you all.
(He strikes the ground with his staff. "Let you play with the line on the tip of the pole;
without disturbing the clear waves, the meaning is naturally distinct."
Record of the Essential Teachings of the Successive Patriarchs, Volume Eighteen;
Record of the Essential Teachings of the Successive Patriarchs, Volume Nineteen.
Compiled by Xingyue of Loudong, Abbot of Lian’an Chan Monastery at the Eighteen Streams in Wulin.
The patron invited the Master to ascend the seat and deliver the formal discourse.
At the provincial capital of Dingzhou, Chan Master Cui was invited by Provincial Commander Wang Lingong to the official residence to ascend the seat.

Holding up his staff, the Master said, "I will strike you if you come forward; I will strike you if you do not come forward. A monk stepped forward and asked, "What about Cui Chan? The Master threw down his staff.
He said: "The Duke has stood for a long time; I humbly pray that you will take care of yourself.
Chan Master Xuefeng Zhao was invited by the Magistrate of Yingzhou to ascend the seat. He said: "The Mind-Seal of the Patriarchs resembles the mechanism of an iron ox:
if it moves away, it is sealed; if it stays still, it is broken. But as for neither moving nor staying—how can it be sealed?"
"Not sealing it is precisely it. Is there anyone here who can say anything about this? At that time, the Elder Lupi came forward and asked, "This student possesses the faculty of the Iron Ox;

I request that you Master do not apply the seal. The Master said, "I am accustomed to hooking whales and leviathans in the vast depths, yet I sigh for the frog's stride as it struggles in the mud and sand.
Lupi stood there lost in thought. The Master shouted, "Elder, why do you not offer a word? Lupi hesitated.

[The Master] deliberated. He then struck [Baoche] once with his whisk and asked, "Do you still remember this critical phrase? Try to bring it up. As Baoche was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him again with the whisk.
The Herdsman said, "I now know that the Buddha-dharma and the King's law are one and the same. The Master asked, "What principle do you see?
The Herdsman replied, "If one hesitates to act when a decision must be made, one will instead invite chaos. He then descended from his seat.

Chan Master Fushan Yuan was invited by Duke Ouyang to expound the Dharma by means of the game of Go. He then ascended the seat and said: "If one discusses this matter, it is like two parties playing a game of Go.
Why is this so? It requires an opponent who understands the art; when the opportunity arises, one must not yield.

If you are trailing by five points or leading by three, you must open up another path before you can succeed. There are those of a certain sort who only know how to secure their own position by closing off their territory."
One does not snatch the corner to rush through the pass; the hard joints and the tiger’s mouth manifest together. Once the position is broken, it is merely laborious to manipulate the pieces.

Thus it is said: "Fat edges are easy to obtain, but a lean belly is difficult to seek. If one thinks before acting, one often loses the connection; if the mind is coarse, one constantly bumps one's head.
Do not boast of being a national master, nor speak in vain of being an immortal. Whether winning the game or losing the stakes is yet to be seen.
Tell me, before black and white were yet distinguished, where did that one move fall? After a long silence, he said:
"From of old, there have been nineteen paths; how many people have been deluded or awakened?"
Zen Master Wuzu Yan ascended the hall at the invitation of Guo Chaofeng Xiangzheng. Before the Dharma seat, Chaofeng burned incense and said:
"This single offering of incense, as it is burned into the censer, becomes clouds of radiant light that pervade the entire Dharma realm.
I offer it to my elder brother, the Zen Master of this hall. I humbly pray that from within these clouds, upon this vast and expansive seat, you will split open your face."
The Master had the likeness of his late teacher displayed at the gate for people to copy. Why was this so? "An old acquaintance by the cliffs of Baiyun;
Things of yesteryear and today are not the same. The night is still and the water cold, the fish do not bite;
A single brazier of incense drifts away from White Lotus Peak. The Master then said: "Namo Satvatāpratyai. Such and such—how many times?"
Crossing the White Cloud Brook and gazing upward: yellow plum blossoms open amidst the snow. Not so, not so.

The tender willow twigs are golden threads; they simply require their timely arrival. Have you not seen how Layman Pang asked Master Mazu, "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as his companion?
Master Mazu said, "Wait until you can suck the Western Ocean dry in a single gulp."
The River Water has already spoken to you, O Great Assembly. To swallow up the waters of the West River in a single draught, one must reach the very bottom of a ten-thousand-fathom deep pool.
A rickety footbridge is no Zhaochuan Bridge; how can bright moon and clear breeze be compared [to this]?
Chan Master Foyin Yuan was invited by Guo Gong, the Judicial Intendant, to ascend the seat. Guo Gong offered incense and said: "How early we have met on the ground of awakening!
The 'falcon-smelling' robe is now cast off. If you wish to recognize the single mysterious phrase of Yunju, take care:
the donkey in the back garden is eating grass. He then called to the assembly, saying: "This one portion of incense rises to heaven and scorches the earth! The Master [continued].

[The Master] said, "Today you were not quick enough; you have been smeared right in the face by this fellow. He then struck him and said, "Thank you, sir, for coming from a thousand li away to visit me.
We shall talk together of the deep bamboo paths of the Eastern Mountain. I lend you a dragon to ride out of the cave; should you encounter a drought, let it bring down the rain.
He threw down his staff and descended from his seat. As the official rose to bow, the Master asked, "Have you caught the dragon? The official—
[The Master] said, "He is already right here. The Master asked, "How do you ride? The official made a waving gesture with his hand, danced, and then departed.
The Master clapped his hands and said, "Only this fellow has some measure of excellence."

Chan Master Baoning Yong was invited by Governor Guo, the Judicial Intendant, to ascend the seat. Governor Guo held up the incense and said, "The Dharma drum has already sounded and the precious incense has just been lit;
at the gate of Yangqi’s crown, I request the Master to drive in the wedge once more.
The Master struck his staff once and said, "The wedge has already been driven in; the assembly bears witness. He struck it once more and then descended from the seat.

When the Provincial Commissioner and layman Wujin Zhang Shangying was touring the administrative districts and passed through Fenning, he invited the five elders of the monasteries to preach the Dharma at Yunyan.
The Master was the last to ascend the seat; holding his staff crosswise, he said:

"Just now, all you virtuous friends have held it horizontally, set it upright, stood it straight, and tossed it askew; you have shifted your steps, moved your bodies, and concealed your heads while revealing yourselves."
Jue, having each admitted defeat before the scholars, could not avoid receiving a heavy blow from the hand of Doushuai.
At this point, it matters not whether one is willing or unwilling. Why? Because when one sees an injustice, how can one bear to endure it?
A monk must exercise his own rightful authority. (He strikes the meditation staff and descends from the seat.)
Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin ascended the hall at the invitation of Chancellor Lü and said: "A single phrase is entirely in accordance with the rules;

it issues forth the seal of the void. A single kind of function cuts off the myriad streams; it penetrates the barrier of the patriarchs. If one is a person of clear eyes, they have already passed through three thousand miles.
Should one still linger in viewing and listening, remaining stuck on the surface, one cannot avoid falling into the secondary."
The gateway of meaning is once again discussed. Therefore it is said: "To know illusion is to be detached from it; no expedient means are required. To be detached from illusion is awakening;
there is also no gradual progression. The heart-essence of Śākyamuni and the Buddhas of the three periods of time is revealed all at once and instantaneously.
Simply accept it as such: the whole mind is Buddha, and the whole Buddha is the mind. Mind and Buddha are non-dual; what more is there to doubt?
At this very moment, how would you express it? For ten thousand ages, all is dark and vast;
ditches and ravines are filled, yet no one understands.
Master Chen requested to ascend the hall. He said: "The phrase with meaning and the phrase without meaning—originally there were no two ends.
Like a vine leaning against a tree, they are struck into a single whole. When the tree falls and the vine withers, Hanlu the hound, unable to restrain his impatience, lets out a great laugh.

As for the golden-maned lion, if one possesses iron eyes and copper pupils and perceives it thoroughly in the presence of all, one can then block the vital passageways, allowing neither ordinary nor sage to pass."
Ultimately, one must never make a nest within the words of others, nor allow oneself to be ensnared by the realm of sensory objects and circumstances.
Therefore it is said: "Words do not unfold the reality; speech does not meet the occasion. Those who rely on words perish; those who linger in phrases are deluded.

Not falling into language and not establishing mechanical devices, one spreads a net across the heavens to strike the fish leaping through the waves; one lowers a hook ten thousand li long to halt the black steed galloping from a thousand li away.
One must also return to those who are truly great masters before one can succeed. Thus, Zhaozhou’s place of penetration serves as a skillful means;
Xuansha’s place of missing the mark tests the adept; Xuefeng’s rolling the ball, Yunmen’s looking into the mirror, and Muzhou’s seeing it as already accomplished all do the same.
Juzhi’s single finger was as if cast from raw iron, penetrating from top to bottom. He sought only a person of true capacity.
But if suddenly none were so, what then? Do you understand? Realize that the ordinary mind is the Way:
when hungry, eat; when weary, sleep. He further composed a verse: "The very mind is the Buddha—this reveals the Mind-Seal. Neither Buddha nor mind."

Treading upon the Great Way, he manifests his body in hundreds, thousands, and billions of forms right where he stands. From the Hall of Universal Radiance, he emits rays of light from between his brows.
Chan Master Dahui Gaoming was invited by County Magistrate Chen to ascend the seat. He said: "The Patriarch said: 'To penetrate the mind of the fundamental Dharma...'"
There is neither dharma nor non-dharma. Awakening is the same as non-awakening; there is no mind and likewise no dharma.
Since there is neither mind nor dharma, what then can be called the "original dharma"? And how, furthermore, is this original dharma to be realized? The Old Man with the Yellow Face said:
"The mind does not falsely grasp at past dharmas, nor does it crave or cling to future events, nor does it dwell upon the present."
As for that which abides: one thoroughly realizes that the three periods of time are entirely empty and quiescent.
Do you all understand this clearly? If you have not yet understood it clearly, I shall explain it for you in detail. Not abiding in the present—this is called concentration (*samādhi*).

Not clinging to the future—this is called wisdom (*prajñā*). Not grasping at the past—this is called knowledge (*jñāna*). It is also called the Tathāgata-dhyāna, and it is also called the Patriarchal [Dharma].

Master Chan: If one can thus penetrate and thus awaken within the twenty-four hours of daily life, then this concentration, this wisdom, and this insight will each be like space, without limit or boundary.

Since concentration, wisdom, and insight are without limit, then the supernormal powers and radiant light of the person in their daily life will likewise be without limit. Since supernormal powers and radiant light are without limit...
There is no limit. The various *pāramitās* and the various gates of liberation (*vimokṣamukha*) are likewise without limit.
Since the *pāramitās* and gates of liberation are without limit, this mind of non-abiding is also without limit.

Since the mind of non-abiding is without limit, today at Jing Mountain, by means of this limitless mind, I shall preach this limitless Dharma. I offer it for the sake of the ministers and their subjects, Chen...
The Assistant Minister prays for our Sovereign’s longevity, that it may endure as long as the earth and heaven, without limit.
At such a time, how do you express the phrase "in accordance with the seasons"? [The Master] raises his whisk and says: "Offer this body and mind to serve every dust-mote world."
This is what is called repaying my Emperor. [The Master] descended from his seat.
Chan Master Ying’an Hua ascended the hall at the request of Professor Yan. Regarding the meaning of the five hundred laborers lifting the rock:
Walking with hands let go before the ten-thousand-fathom cliff, The entire world of the ten directions is a single ring of iron; White fur grows upon the back of empty space. Directly!
Even if you were to cast off your greasy cap and strip away your rank-smelling cloth robe, you would still deserve a blow from the staff at the gate of Baoen.
Why? Because rising in the dead of night and sitting with knees bent, the Star of Hairs appears before the patch-robed monk.
Chan Master Dongshan Yungding ascends the hall at the request of the Daoist Guandao of Jiulong and three laymen.

In the Confucian school, they paint the Eight Trigrams and create contracts, yet these do not save one from the cycle of rebirth in the six realms. In the Daoist school, they worship the Nine Sovereigns and refine the true qi.

They do not comprehend the numerical cycles of the three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas*. Our Śākyamuni World-Honored One, however, penetrates the cycles of the three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* and delivers beings from the saṃsāra of the six realms.

With great vows, he gathers in humans and devas, just as the wind-wheel sustains the sun and moon; with great wisdom, he shatters birth and death, like the kalpa-fire consuming even the finest autumn hair.
Those who enter my gate naturally transform heaven and earth and clearly perceive ghosts and spirits.

To cause Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains, the great earth, and the vast oceans to enter into a single pore, while all sentient beings remain unaware and unknowing—this Dharma-gate I speak of is like space, which contains all myriad phenomena. One is immeasurable, and the immeasurable is one.
If a person attains this one, then all matters are complete. Take heed!
Chan Master Qianyan Chang was invited to ascend the seat by the layman Cao.

The lay practitioner Cao Renqing of Wuzhou, together with his entire family and honored relatives, hosted a vegetarian feast at the temple and presented offerings, requesting the old monk to ascend the seat and preach the Dharma. The old monk replied, "Yes."
Do you understand? The entire earth is this old monk; the entire earth is this Dharma seat. What further seat would you have the old monk ascend?
What Dharma would he preach? I recall that five or six years ago, when crossing the bridge, I already came to your residence to receive a meal and alms.
Today, three or four hundred people in the mountains are eating a meal and receiving alms, and everyone is joyful.
Joyful, indeed joyful! This very joy and jubilation will increase your virtue by how much and extend your lifespan by how much, O Field of Merit!
The Elder has already proclaimed this for you from the Dharma-seat. I, this old monk, shall simply partake of the meal and receive the offerings;
there is no need to draw legs upon a snake. It will naturally be accomplished when the water arrives at the channel. Have you not seen?
Zen Master Wuzu Fayan said: "Sitting upright while receiving offerings, the donor shall long enjoy peace and happiness.
Zhaozhou said: "The old monk sits here; what more need be said of 'Buddha-dharma' or 'ignorance'? When there is a way, follow the way; when there is no way, follow the precedent.
Suddenly, if a man were to come forth and say, "Monk, you are sitting here dividing the spoils," he would one day become... [a person of great realization].
What can be used to repay the donor? One simply says: "If not a cow, one will surely be a donkey.
Why is this so? For a great man to walk among the various species is no small matter.

Master Gulinmao ascends the hall at the request of his patrons. Buddha to Buddha, hand is passed to hand: the boundless realms of all lands are not separated by so much as a hair’s tip from self and other.
Patriarch to Patriarch, the Dharma is transmitted: ten thousand generations of past and present never depart from this very moment of thought.

The upward path has not been transmitted by a thousand sages. Even if one were to sit and sever the heads of both the Reward-Buddha and the Transformation-Buddha, one would still inevitably fall into a heap of sound and form.

To further seek to alone rouse the profound wind beyond the limit of Vairocana, or to solely clarify the self before the empty kalpa, is much like using a fist through a boot to scratch an itch; what joy is there in it? Therefore it is said: "The multitude..."
The numinous single source is provisionally named "Buddha. Its essence is exhausted and its form dissolves, yet it does not perish; like gold flowing and ore dispersing, it remains eternally present.
The common people use it daily without knowing it; the Buddhas always know it and alone employ it.

By means of this principle of solitary employment free from partiality, they eternally abide before all phenomena with form. By means of this mind that uses it daily without knowing it, they transcend the realm of the True.
The manifestation of the Truth is without before or after, without ancient or modern. Self and other are merged as one; the sage and the ordinary person are no different.
At such a time as this, how is it? "The green mountains do not lock in their soaring momentum; the vast blue seas surely know their source is high.
[He strikes the whisk and descends from the seat.]
At the request of Shi Checheng Chan Master, Magistrate Huang Yuankong, and others, [the Master] ascended the hall. "A single phrase cuts off the current: the whole mind is Buddha.
Ten thousand functions do not reach it: the whole Buddha is the mind. Reaching this point, both mind and Buddha are forgotten—what, then, is this?
He let out a shout: "The sweet melon is sweet to the very stem; the bitter gourd is bitter to the very root."
Chan Master Zhuo’an was invited by various officials to ascend the hall for a discourse. To follow the waves and drift with the current, not leaving behind a single drop;
to cut off all streams, not retaining even a hair’s breadth. To swallow the Western River in a single gulp, and not to be a companion to the myriad dharmas.
Tell me, is this following the waves and drifting with the current, or cutting off the streams? Layman Pang said: "The ten directions gather together as one; every single person..."
Study non-action (*wuwei*). This is the field for selecting Buddhas. With an empty mind, one returns having passed the imperial examination;
everyone here is present. Is this not passing the examination with an empty mind? But how does one study non-action? Upon the waters of the Long River, the waves surge to the heavens.
How can the bright moon and clear breeze be compared [to this]?

Great Minister Jin invited the Master to ascend the hall. The Master said: "In the ground of ultimate reality, not a single speck of dust is admitted; in the gateway of myriad practices, not a single dharma is abandoned.
If one were to admit a single speck of dust, from where could the Wheel of Dharma be turned? If one were to abandon a single dharma, the Buddha..."
From what source does this undertaking arise? Thus, great beings of power act as ferries and bridges within the bitter sea of the *kalpa*-turmoil;
whether they move against or with the current, their ways are entirely unfathomable. Only such a person can turn the celestial gates and revolve the earth’s axis, capable of bearing such a burden.

They breathe the springtime of vitality into what has already been consumed by fire, establishing the fortune of prosperity where it is just beginning to rise, thereby forming a most extraordinary moment.
This is the condition for a union of the worthy and good that shall endure for a thousand years. When wind and clouds meet, the "knocking" and "singing" ride upon the occasion;
through this extraordinary cause, this extraordinary condition, this extraordinary vow, and this extraordinary merit, one does not forget the entrustment.
To raise it up and know it immediately—to hold hands and present it—is to leap directly beyond and penetrate from head to tail in a single stroke. One phrase!
How do you say it? It relies entirely on the hand that lifts the cauldron and stirs the soup to turn the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata.

On the occasion of the celebration of Master Yuanwu Keqin’s birthday, at the request of Imperial Censor Zhou, he ascended the hall for the discourse: "The profound mechanism is transcendent and liberated; it merges the myriad phenomena within the eye."
The preceding [passage] concerns the sublime and luminous ultimate truth, which unifies a thousand differences beyond all phenomena. When one is enlightened, all are enlightened;
when one sees, all are seen; when one acts, all act; when one speaks, all speak. This directly cuts through to the root and is manifest before one’s very eyes.
If you can penetrate this thoroughly, the great matter beneath your own heels will be as clear as the bright sun—vast and expansive.

If one can take the great void as the means to cultivate the body, realize one's nature, offer prayers for the longevity of another, and plant seeds for superior causes in the future, then this is why Śākyamuni held up a flower on Vulture Peak and Kāśyapa smiled, and why Bodhidharma faced the wall at Shaolin and Huikong transmitted the mind-seal.
Within this interval, it is like a spark struck from stone or a flash of lightning; it requires nothing less than a person of extraordinary caliber.
This clarifies the matter of one's own fundamental portion. To know this fundamental portion, one must rely upon an extraordinary person.

Right now, how would you express that single phrase of the extraordinary fundamental portion? "The sunflowers and hellebores alike incline their heads upward; we offer high prayers for ten thousand years of spring."
Zheng Taishi requested the Master to ascend the hall. He then said: "Before the spiritual light had manifested, the myriad phenomena contained the Great Void.

Once the single breath was revealed, the world arose with its blossoming flowers. All Buddhas of the past, all Buddhas of the present, and all Buddhas of the future have appeared from within this very place.
Whether gods, humans, or the various classes of living beings, there are none who do not flow forth from this center. By means of this one...

Abiding in illumination, hundreds and thousands of places radiate brilliance; with a single movement of the mechanism, thousands and tens of thousands of mechanisms unfold in profusion. Thus it is said:
"The body of the pure dharma-realm fundamentally has no appearing or disappearing; through the power of great compassionate vows, it manifests birth.

Yet, regarding this compassion, these vows, and this power—if one has previously received a numinous root and possesses the seed-wisdom of transcendence—then at the very moment of birth, [one realizes them].
Having already let out the lion’s roar and being fully endowed with great supernormal powers, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down;
whether letting go or holding fast—there is nothing that does not proceed from the ten-directional cross-pattern upon the crown of the heads of all the Sages.
Even the enjoyment of blessings, longevity, wealth, and noble progeny is entirely sustained by their majestic power. It is precisely thus...
At such a time, how do you speak this single phrase? Layer upon layer, auspicious vapors manifest; one by one, golden lotuses surge forth. Again, he offers this verse:
Before the Era of Awesome Sound, the spiritual sprouts were exquisite; To this day, their radiance grows ever more fresh. The myriad flowers are fragrant and the scenery is lovely;
Mount Longevity soars high unto the age of the Great Cinnamon Tree.
Chan Master Dahui Zonggao ascends the seat at the request of Vice Minister Rong on his birthday.
A monk asks, "Why does Yangqi’s donkey have only three legs? The Master says, "Because it eats little water and grass.
The monk advances, saying, "If that is so, then you present yourself face-to-face with no evasion. The Master says, "Do not pretend to be clear-headed. The monk advances, saying, "Since it is Pan..."
Pānláng returns riding backward. Why did he fall and break his neck? The Master said, "It is not within your realm.
The student asked, "What can be done about this very moment? The Master said, "Do not let me down. The student said, "Great kindness is difficult to repay," and then prostrated himself.
The Master then said, "Yangqi has a donkey that has only three legs. Pānláng returns riding it backward."
The Yellow Barbarian Chuo was killed by a fall; this is the commentary on Miaoxi from thirty years ago.
Today, that monk has given him a thorough dismantling before the assembly of gods and men, something far more than a minor matter.
It is enough to make Master Yangqi clap his hands and laugh heartily, while the mountains, rivers, the great earth, and the myriad phenomena all dance together at once. At such a time as this—
Tell me, who is it that provides the witness? Therefore it is said: "True in every place, true in every place;
in every dust mote is the person of original nature. When spoken of as reality, no sound appears; the majestic, upright essence has caused the body to vanish. What is this majestic, upright essence?
Before leaving Tuṣita Heaven, he had already descended into the royal palace; before emerging from his mother’s womb, he had already saved sentient beings.
It is finished. Is this not the majestic, upright body? If you understand it as the majestic, upright body, you betray the Old Śākyamuni;
if you do not understand it as the majestic, upright body, you betray yourself.
Since you have betrayed yourself, with what will you meet the Old Śākyamuni? If you can find a single thread of a path here—
Only then do we know that when Śākyamuni was in Tuṣita Heaven, riding upon the fragrant elephant of the sun-wheel to descend into the womb of Lady Māyā,
it was merely a manifestation of the timing of his birth. Even his pointing one finger to heaven and one finger to earth,
saying, "In all the heavens above and the earth below, I alone am honored," was likewise merely a manifestation made for the sake of all people.
This is the very model of the arising of phenomena. If you can see it within this, you will not only be avenging the Old Śākyamuni, but you will also be avenging your own biological parents.
Not only will you be avenging your biological parents, but you will also be avenging all sentient beings.
At this very moment, tell me: by whose power of grace do you receive this? (After a long silence)
It is said: "To brandish the sword and cleave open self and other is easy; to push a mountain and block off right and wrong is difficult.

"The dharmas born of causes and conditions adorn the appearances of the world. Those who realize their nature is empty—such people possess the true eye. All.

Is it Mount Sumeru? The vast ocean? The great earth? The grasses, trees, and forests? If one were to take Mount Sumeru as his longevity, Mount Sumeru is high yet has a summit.

The earth serves as their life-span; the great earth is thick and possesses wheels. If one were to take grasses, trees, thickets, and forests as their life-span, such grasses, trees, thickets, and forests are numerous yet finite.

Only by taking the clouds of fragrant incense, clouds of flowers, clouds of banners and pennants, clouds of music, and clouds of jeweled canopies within this Flower Treasury World-realm of our Great Perfect Enlightenment—whether citing one, two, a hundred, or... [is the life-span truly inexhaustible].

From one thousand, up to hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, millions, and billions, if one were to select even a single mote of dust from among these numbers, it would all be equal to sentient and insentient beings alike, and equal to Vairocana.
All of these may be used to offer blessings for a layperson's long life. Nevertheless, this being so:
I cannot help but provide a side-transmission of this message for the lay practitioner. What is this side-transmitted message?
Within the Flower Treasury World, a single thought-moment is already ten thousand years in Jambudvīpa. Be careful.
Chan Master Zhuo’an ascends the seat for his birthday celebration. Today is the occasion when the Grand Historian Dayu, not sparing a single hair on his brow, reveals both his head and face.
This elder personally received the final instructions of Śākyamuni Buddha at the Vulture Peak assembly twenty centuries ago;
without leaving that very spot he has already arrived in Jambudvīpa, and without emerging from his mother’s womb he has already attained perfection.
“Perfectly Awakened One! Today, since you have not forgotten the entrustment, this mountain monk shall offer a single incense stick as a witness for you.

Do you understand? If you do, then you will see that the mountains, rivers, the great earth, the grasses, the trees, the sentient, and the insentient—all together raise their voices in praise to wish you long life. Now tell me, what about this mountain monk’s staff?”
How does one offer praise? [The Master] strikes the meditation staff once and says: "The Southern Mountains are unceasingly lush and verdant; From the Eastern Sea rises the brilliant, rosy dawn.
For long, the crags and valleys have been bathed in spring’s abundance; A misty new rain moistens the blossoms of the forest."
On the donor’s birthday, the Sangha was invited to ascend the seat for offerings. Light clouds spread like dark brow-ink; thin mists delineate the azure. Auspicious vapors rise in mist;
crimson clouds part to reveal the morning sun. The lapis lazuli fields shimmer with the luster of white jade; the red waters gleam with the hue of dragon pearls.
When person and environment meet, and phenomena merge with principle, one is then able to erect the most supreme banner within the Hall of Universal Radiance and plant the monument of merit.
In the land of Universal Fragrance, the Vairocana Hall is not small, the great trichiliocosm is not vast, the Bohai Sea is not many, and a puddle in a hoofprint is not minute.

With this same body and mind, these same lands and kalpas, these same practices and vows, and these same merits and virtues—precisely at such a time, how do you speak that single phrase of birth? (He strikes the whisk and says: "One night, the heavens..."
The fragrance of the cassia seeds is heard; autumn deepens as it returns once more to the home of Ge Hong.
[The Master] descends from his seat. Layman Zhou requests the Master to ascend the hall. Today, the Tathāgata Amitāyus emits light and shakes the earth upon the tip of this mountain monk’s staff.
He addresses the great assembly, speaking this verse: "All dharmas are unborn; all dharmas are..."
"Extinction. When arising and extinction have both ceased, they are exhausted; quiescent extinction is constantly manifest. Venerable Kauṇḍinya could not contain his amusement at the side.
Placing his palms together over his chest, he knit his brows and glared, saying: "The Ancient Buddha Tathāgata thought there was some extraordinary samādhi here.
To speak in such a manner does not even escape the master’s conceptual trap; how can it suffice as the cause for today?"
In the ritual of fasting and celebration, the Tathāgata Amitāyus suddenly emerges from the mountain monk’s staff,

manifesting eighty-four thousand Buddha-lands. He universally transforms the fragrant food within those eighty-four thousand Buddha-lands and arranges eighty-four thousand lion thrones made of jewels,
making offerings to the eighty-four thousand great Bodhisattvas throughout.
It perfumed the eighty-four thousand pores of all the great Bodhisattvas;
within each and every pore, there were individually present eighty-four thousand immeasurable and boundless adornments of merit.

Having performed this single cycle of Buddha-activity, the staff-bearer requested an inquiry from the Great Being Mañjuśrī, and the Great Being Mañjuśrī requested an inquiry from the Elder Vimalakīrti. The assembly...
Is there anyone here who recognizes kindness and repays virtue? If so, come forth now to repay the cost of the meal!
If this is not yet the case, then let the staff be returned to the staff; let Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva be returned to Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva;
let the Elder Vimalakīrti be returned to the Elder Vimalakīrti. Do not say that silence is best. (He strikes the ground with his staff.)

On the occasion of the auspicious birthday celebration of Vice Minister Jin Dae-jung, he was invited to ascend the seat. The Master said: "Auspicious clouds encircle the seat; auspicious vapors swirl through the void.
Grasping the pivot of affairs, you glorify the transforming sun. Only by possessing the strategy to rectify the age can one unfold the resolve for the higher path;
only by establishing world-transcending merit can one fulfill the function of the Great Mechanism. Thus, the Great Man performs great deeds, and with great wisdom..."

Attaining great power, great material resources lead to the accomplishment of great merit; great virtue necessarily entails a long life. Three thousand *li* away, one lays the Mohe sword across one's lap;

killing and giving life are fully manifested as essence and function are exercised together. One exerts divine power amidst tangled roots and knotted branches, and brings order to the chaos on days when armor is donned and spears are brandished.
To gather and concentrate [the forces] is to take full command within the tent while devising strategy from behind the curtain.

Upon his release, a hundred offices were renewed, and the seas and mountains shall forever rely upon him. This is because the Great High Commissioner and Layman Qi Weng have long harbored such aspirations in his life and cultivated them through many kalpas;
since receiving his prediction at Vulture Peak, he has manifested in the body of a civil official, possessing the deeds of a great being.
It is as it is said: "To practice worldly dharmas with a mind that transcends the world; to be able to accomplish [enlightenment] without destroying worldly dharmas."
The supramundane mind. When this mind is applied to the state, the Chancellor today has achieved the Way and perfected his virtue, becoming secure, wealthy, honored, and dignified.
When this mind is applied to the family, the Chancellor today is like the auspicious qilin and the auspicious phoenix—capable of yielding and capable of reverence.
When this mind is applied to the world, the Chancellor today presides over the realm within the imperial domain and wields authority beyond the borders, expanding the territory.

Opening up new frontiers to benefit the people and stabilize the state—when this mind is put into practice for a single moment today, the myriad capacities of both monastics and laypeople before us are stilled and harmonized, and one stands uniquely honored in the eyes of all.
They are inspired by the brilliance of the enlightened age and sing praises of the auspicious fortune.
Yet tell me, at such a time as this, how would you express the single phrase for celebrating longevity? "Mount Sumeru stands towering, coeval with heaven and earth—for ten million kalpas and beyond."

The year begins with the dawn of Great Peace. Again, he composes a verse: "The rains and dew from the Nine Heavens are freshly pervasive; I am specially appointed to the pivot of state affairs, a grace of profound favor.
The realm of longevity is cleared and leveled as the sun of transformation rises; We shall soon behold the dragon and tiger meet the wind and clouds."
Chen Xingzhi requested the Master to ascend the seat to offer blessings for his mother’s birthday. The Master said, "Xingzhi is offering blessings for his mother’s birthday;
what Dharma can this mountain monk possibly speak? If there were words to be spoken, thought would easily exhaust them; if there were no Dharma, it would be beyond calculation or limit.

Everyone should partake of the meal according to custom; each person looks up in vain expectation. Since you look up in vain expectation, tell me, what is so extraordinary about it? He then raised his whisk.
The staff-bearer said: "Yesterday, a tiger on the South Mountain bit a great beast; a carp from the East Sea turned over once and leapt into the depths of the waves of Lake Tai.
Suddenly, with a thunderous crash, everything became indistinct and ethereal. Two peaks facing each other nodded their heads and said, 'A most auspicious news!
But the local deity of the Three-House Village, unable to contain his indignation, laughed from the side and said, 'Long—'"
"Old Elder, you are far too talkative. You country bumpkin love to speak of 'easy' Chan.
Why do you needlessly cause such a great stir and tie yourself up in knots? Little do you realize that once this staff has reached this point, it cannot be let go.
He strikes the ground with the staff and says: "Adept at fishing for whales and leviathans in the vast depths, yet pitying the frog’s stride as it rolls through the mud."
[The Master] lets out a shout and speaks again: "Today, Chen Xingzhi has invited me to offer congratulations on his mother's birthday.
One person is so joyful that he does not know where his words will lead. Everyone, it is clear: Chen Xingzhi has invited me to offer congratulations on his mother's birthday.
This mountain monk is not speaking of anything other than this. Long standing, take care."
Chan Master Muchunmen ascends the hall on the first day of the New Year for the birthday celebration of Mr. Dong. On this first day of the year, the light wind blows and the sun shines clear.

Good assembly, from before the time of Vipaśyin Buddha until the present moment, whether there have been buddha-worlds or no buddha-worlds, within them there have been unspeakably unspeakable days and months, and unspeakably unspeakable years.
In unspeakably unspeakable lands, there is not one who does not follow the radiance flowing from this single day.
Thus, the imperial wind sweeps vast and boundless across the eight directions; the village elders sing songs of joy throughout the myriad regions without end.
Now, suppose a person appears in the world and happens to encounter such a day—what then? Having received the legacy of ritual, music, the Odes, and the Documents, they will certainly...
To those who wear crowns and gird their waists:

Master Wuxiang Zhen, Holding the Mainstay, Responds to the Lay Patron’s Prayer for Offspring; Invited by a Dānapati, He Addresses the Assembly at Mount Qingliang.
The myriad bodhisattvas within are all people of my own household. Cherish this autumn light as it departs;
how many times does the autumn moon wax full and wane? Come and go in peace without haste; from the ends of the earth to the furthest horizons, such encounters are not easily found.
You must believe that as soon as Sudhana withdraws his thoughts, he is once again present to the east of the city of Vairambhya. That a dragon and a tiger are born together is truly extraordinary.
As soon as he was born, he already possessed the spirit of an ox-eater. When the *campaka* groves are deep and the autumn moon is full, a single breeze of fragrance stirs heaven and earth.
Chan Master Nan Shi Xiu ascends the hall for a meal-offering arranged by Chen Congdao of Qin River, who seeks progeny. "When hungry, eat rice."
When weariness comes, one strikes for sleep; treading the ordinary path, such a monk is truly rare indeed.
Yet those who take broad strides atop a ten-thousand-fathom peak, or turn their bodies amidst a thicket of brambles, are not one in ten thousand.
When Mazu let out a shout, Baizhang was deaf for three days straight; Huangbo, hearing of this, could not help but stick out his tongue. Now tell me, what was it?
The ordinary path is a broad stride atop a ten-thousand-fathom peak. Sandalwood trees are surrounded by sandalwood;
lions give birth to lion cubs.
Zen Master Zhuo’an was requested by a donor seeking progeny to ascend the seat. He said: "The summer retreat is completed; the season has concluded."
Full. With the tip of his staff, he travels all around the four continents;

yet upon turning once, it is found that he has been merely tossing and turning back and forth beneath the three rafters and before the seven-foot mat within his own house. There is not the slightest bit of anything extraordinary about it.
Although it is merely one’s own house, there is nonetheless nothing extraordinary about it. Yet, how can one deny that the head is the head and the bottom is the bottom;
that the donkey is a donkey and the horse is a horse; that the old monk is the old monk and the *dàolǐ* (teacher) is the *dàolǐ*.
When it is cold, one freezes to death; when it is hot, one scorches to death. How many instances of such blundering and confusion can there possibly be? Where would you find eggplants and gourds?

"I have learned that today happens to be the end of the summer retreat (*varsā*). A patron has entered the mountains to provide offerings, requesting that I, a mountain monk, pray for him to obtain an heir.
If I call it 'praying for an heir,' it is also the end of the summer retreat for everyone; if I call it 'the end of the summer retreat,' it is also for his sake to pray for an heir.
Ultimately, how can one make these two correspond? [The Master] picks up his staff and says: 'From the Cinnabar Mountains is born the phoenix.'"
When a lion gives birth to a *śarabha*, it is naturally a fine cub, regardless of its eyebrows or whiskers. [The Master] held up his staff and said:
"If you want one, you get one; if you want two, you get two. From the beginning, my words have never been uttered in vain. Each of you, take this clearly to heart.
He then descended from his seat.
