Master Baoning Yong of Tiegang raised his staff as he ascended the hall for a meal offering to the Sangha provided by a patron. A monk asked, "Since [the offerings] are inexhaustible," the Master replied, "The answer is likewise infinite."

If one relies on the tradition of the ancestral patriarchs, there was originally no such thing as this. Yet, within the gate of transformative teaching, the skillful means employed according to circumstances are truly vast indeed.
Yongjia said: "Alas for the Dharma of the final age! Alas for this evil era! Sentient beings have meager merit and are difficult to discipline.
The Sages are far removed and false views run deep; demons are strong and the Dharma is weak, resulting in much resentment and harm. Yongjia spoke thus.
Furthermore, it is not permissible to merely yield temporarily to human sentiment; for beneath the weight of a thousand ages, one will inevitably be scrutinized by others.
Why? Because, in my house, there has never been such a thing. Even the Buddhas have never appeared in the world;
there is no Buddha to be realized, no Dharma to be taught, no sentient beings to be delivered, and no afflictions to be severed. Nor is there...
Enlightenment is not to be sought, nor is there any nirvana to be realized. There is no prior limit, middle limit, or subsequent limit;
there is no True Dharma, Semblance Dharma, or Final Dharma. When seeking the true nature of all phenomena, it is entirely unattainable.
Therefore, time neither comes nor goes, and phenomena neither arise nor cease. One does not perceive a path; all phenomena are non-arising. All...
The Dharma is not extinguished. If one can understand it in this way, the Buddhas are constantly manifest before one.
Thus, Changsha said: "The entirety of the ten directions of the world is the single eye of the śramaṇa; the entirety of the ten directions of the world is the whole body of the śramaṇa;
the entirety of the ten directions of the world is the true human body; the entirety of the ten directions of the world is the gate of liberation. It is thus.
Reaching the point where Buddhas, sentient beings, and all things— whether animate or inanimate, possessing nature or lacking nature— are of one substance, one nature, and one characteristic;
and wherein there is no longer any conceptual differentiation by various forms of cognition regarding internal or external, middle, grasping or abandoning, love or hatred, permanence or annihilation,
arising or ceasing, defilement or purity, going or coming— if one can be thus, then the three realms cannot contain them.
The Way cannot encompass it. It functions throughout all places, coming and going without dwelling or attachment. Manifesting forms in response to things, it attains great mastery.
Whether as ordinary or as sage, whether right or wrong, whether acting contrary to or in accordance with the norm, even the heavens cannot fathom it.
This is why Yongjia could not bring himself to act here. Furthermore, I recall Benjing saying: "The essence of the Way is fundamentally without cultivation;
by not cultivating, one naturally accords with the Way. To cast aside the single true nature and enter into the clamor of the world—if you encounter a cultivator of the Way, first do not speak of it.
These are truly words of sincerity. Baoning follows this approach as well.
Just as the square becomes round. Yet, even so, those who laugh at me are many; those who smile at me are few.
The market towns invite him to ascend the hall; the chamber of Magadha is not closed. The gate of the Abbot’s quarters opens once more. For one who does not spare his eyebrows—
He stretched out his body and invited them to enter, saying: "In the cycle of the three realms and six paths of rebirth, the mirror of karma does not fail to conceal either beauty or ugliness.
There is no need to linger further in the affairs of others; all is but what one has done for oneself and must receive for oneself.
Now, within the sphere of each of you, there is a mirror of karma of your own, clear and vividly manifest. Tell me, is it beautiful or ugly? Please, turn back and look."

[The Master] looked at himself in a mirror. Furthermore, a non-Buddhist asked the World-Honored One, "What Dharma will you preach today? The Honored One replied, "I shall preach the Dharma of certainty.
On the following day, he asked again, "What Dharma will you preach? The Honored One replied, "I shall preach the Dharma of uncertainty. The Way-farer asked, "Why was it certain yesterday?"

"Why is it not fixed today? The Venerable One replied, "It was fixed yesterday; today it is not fixed. O worthy ones, you should know that the Buddha-dharma has no fixed characteristic and no non-fixed characteristic.
It is established according to capacity and applied according to the occasion. To say 'it exists' is permissible; to say 'it does not exist' is also permissible.
To say 'it is fixed' is permissible; to say 'it is not fixed' is also permissible. It is like the vast, empty sky."
Unimpeded. One may freely penetrate and traverse in all directions with ease. Suppose today someone were to ask Baoning, "What Dharma will you preach today?
one would say, "I am preaching the indeterminate Dharma. Or suppose on the following day they asked, "What Dharma did you preach yesterday? one would say, "I was preaching the determinate Dharma.
Or if they were to ask, "Why was it indeterminate yesterday, and why is it determinate today? one would say, "Yesterday it was not..."
"Fixed. "Fixed today. Someone asked, "What about yesterday’s 'not fixed'? He replied, "I have not yet finished my thanks to the Prefect.
Someone asked, "What about what is fixed today? He replied, "The market households have already finished the tea ceremony.
Having completed his thanks, he said: "Leading forth and withdrawing, I hide away; my will does not follow. Where in this world can I find acceptance? Relying on... (text ends).
Advancing and retreating, he enters the dust and mud; in every thing and at every head, the ancestral source is revealed. [He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Master Wuzu Yan, on the occasion of a meal offering, ascended the hall and said: "Not cold, not warm, joyfully wandering in spring; men and women incline their hearts to prepare for the future.
One realizes for oneself that a lifetime is like a dream; only then does one know that a hundred years are like a floating bubble. The *subing* (cuckoo) cries.
Abiding in the true message, when the peony blooms, the rustic interest is profound. Who can understand this gate-style?
In ordinary negligence, one has whitened the head of youth.
At the request of the Gao residence of Tongshu, he ascends the hall. Gao Ping-shi of Tonglin: fortunately, his family enjoys official emolument; by nature, he is tranquil and fond of [the Dharma].
Our school is as warm and gentle as fine jade. We have submitted this petition to request that the various monasteries prepare vegetarian feasts to plant seeds of great merit.

Two elders converse together on the profound mystery; it is precisely the second month of the Yanghe season. Thirsty deer drink from the stream, mistaking ice for water; wild monkeys cry in the trees, where the fog forms smoke.
On the road of the Yellow Plum, there are many who know our way; today we shall all board the Prajñā boat together. Board!
"The boat is certainly not absent; but tell me, what matter is being discussed? Fortunately we have encountered the brilliant clarity of the three springs;

thus, while traveling, one may even swing one's arms without hindrance. *Lalala lalala!* [He clapped his hands and laughed loudly, saying: "What tune is this? It is the 'Ten Thousand-Year Joy' (*Wannianhuan*)."
Ascending the hall for the mid-month vegetarian feast: In the second month of spring, all phenomena are fresh; throughout the sands of worlds, it is one and the same sky.
Mossy green is washed by rain, clearing away last winter’s snow; Wildfire and wind drift away the smoke of yesterday night.

On perilous ridges, the cry of monkeys is heard at dawn; Upon the long river, travelers are seen boarding boats. How many times in human life does one encounter such a scene? It is well to cultivate fields of merit with a sincere heart.
Chan Master Zhennjingwen ascended the hall due to a patron’s offering: “The Buddha expounds the Dharma with a single voice;
sentient beings each attain understanding according to their kind. With a mind of equality toward monastics and laypeople, men and women alike, each and every one realizes the Dharma-realm as one.”
Chan Master Meng’an Xin, due to the request of a group of virtuous friends who had entered the monastery to establish the conditions for a gruel offering, ascended the seat.
He recalled that in the past, when the lay practitioner Gan-zhi entered Nanquan Monastery to provide a gruel offering, he requested the Venerable Nanquan to perform the recitation.
Nanquan said, "If you recite the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* for a wildcat or a white ox, Ganji will come out. Ganji then came out.
After the porridge was served, Nanquan asked the steward where Ganji was. The steward replied, "He left right then and there. Nanquan said, "Go break the porridge pot!
The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Ganji prepared the porridge; his merit was not bestowed in vain."—Nanquan.
Reciting the mantras is not without its intimacy; at that time, the rice pot was smashed. How do you all practice and perform the rites now?
Even so, when you all prepare the gruel and suddenly invite this mountain monk to recite the mantras, tell me, to what should you dedicate the merit?
If you say it is for the sake of the cats and the white oxen, you are merely following after their heels. If...
To say that the Way is the lantern or the pillar is no more than copying a cat by following the model.
To say it is for the donor to increase their field of merit is to conceal the virtue of others. Yet, if one simply leaves it at that, the offering has nowhere to go.
Tell me, how should one dedicate the merit? [He strikes the ground once with his staff and says: "May this be offered universally to all."
Chan Master Milmun Je ascended the hall at the request of his patrons.

Taking his seat, he looked left and right, then suddenly raised his staff and said, "Now the Buddha emits a radiance to assist in revealing the meaning of the true mark. He struck it once and said, "How rare, O bhikṣus!
Within this, it is difficult to find an analogy. Again, he lifted the staff and asked, "Do you see Jiangshan’s staff? Morning.
Having traveled to the Western Heaven at dusk, he returns to the Eastern Land. He says to the assembly: "In some worlds, the Buddha-work is performed through sound;
in some worlds, the Buddha-work is performed through fragrant food; in some worlds, the Buddha-work is performed through inhalation and exhalation.
Then, striking once, he says: "Now tell me, in this world, what is used to perform the Buddha-work? He then throws down his staff.
"Alala! In the four directions and eight corners, all is lively and agile.

Chan Master Chushi Qi addressed the assembly upon the arrival of Lady Anren of the Yang family and the two lay practitioners Shenzhu and Shanju, who had entered the mountains to provide a vegetarian feast for the monks.
"O śramaṇas and sons of the Śākya, you wear the roofs of your donors upon your heads, tread upon the ground of your donors with your feet, and eat the food of your donors with your mouths."
Eating rice, wearing the robes of a donor—how can one repay the donor? If one enters the Way without penetrating its principle, one merely returns to consuming the faithful offerings of others.
At eighty-one years of age, the tree no longer sprouts.

If one eats all day long without ever biting through a single grain of rice, and wears clothes all day long without ever being attached to a single thread of silk, then even while walking, one does not see walking.

Establishing oneself, one does not see establishment. Throughout the twelve hours of the day, do not rely upon or depend on a single thing. Do not see a giver, do not see a receiver, and there is no gift itself.
Such a view is precisely that of a person of overweening pride; it creates a separate hell for you to dwell in.
When none of this is the case, how is it? Everyone, return to the hall and go drink tea.
Master Nanxiu ascends the hall for a meal of gruel and rice provided by a lay donor. "Abundant activity is great function; every action must fully manifest the True.

When Vimalakīrti filled thirty-two thousand bodhisattvas with a single bowl of rice, and when the lay practitioner Ganqi served gruel and Nanquan smashed the cauldron—tell me, was this abundant activity and great function, or was it not? It is all so ordinary.
"Recognizing the face of the east wind, the myriad purples and thousands of reds are all spring.
At the request of the donor of the vegetarian field, Master Xushan Xingchan, the donor of the Shu-xi vegetarian field invited him to ascend the hall. "Each person has one sitting mat."

Its squareness and roundness remain solemnly as they were in the past and present; its posture, whether walking or sitting, never shifts. Through the cold of the ages, even the kalpa-stone is worn away, yet it no longer belongs to the realm of yin and yang.

Furthermore, it does not contribute to grain taxes or labor service; since its four boundaries are clearly defined, the deeds and contracts are personally and thoroughly verified. Thus, the field and land are further authenticated.
Great Sovereign Rest: what could be more complete? Its enjoyment is inexhaustible; such as this I bestow upon you—how can you fail to be grateful?
It nurtures the seeds of the Buddhas of the ten directions and constantly produces the food of great wisdom; it is further bestowed upon all ordinary beings and sages.

Inconceivable merit is not attained through intentional seeking, nor is it gained through a state of non-seeking; one must awaken to the meaning of the spring breeze and not merely recognize the greenness of the spring mountains.
This unsurpassed great cause and condition requires that you acknowledge its grace and reflect upon its origins; since cause and effect are without deviation, [the result follows].
One should fully employ the power of the Way and compare it to the merit of its source. Whether it be soup or rice, or even molten bronze and iron, cut them off abruptly.

Within the three spheres of existence, which are as empty as space, who can seek out their traces? The lanterns and the pillars remain as they were; the autumn harvest is still piled high like mountains and peaks. (He plants his staff upright and says:
"Willow catkins follow the wind; sunflowers turn toward the sun."
The Offering to the Arhat:
A Framework for the True Chan Master Wuxiang The Offering to the Arhat: Addressing the Assembly The True Man worthy of offerings casts his gaze far and high;

He travels back and forth across the seas and mountains, never wearying of toil. One knows that wherever he brings auspicious omens, He causes celestial flowers to fall upon his coarse woolen robe. The Stone Beam.
The path to Fangguang is not far; within the Campaka Hall, he beckons with an open hand. Among the thousand venerable ones, who is the master?
The clouds over sea and heaven have stilled, and the lunar orb rises high.
Chan Master Zhenjing Wen ascended the hall for a meal offering to the Arhats. He said, "Master Fang is today acting as the donor to provide offerings for the Arhats.
Now tell me, have the Arhats come or not? If they have come, where are they? If they have not come, then why do you make offerings to them?
He then looked toward the assembly and said, "Do you wish to recognize the true Arhat? It turns out that all of you..."

While [the master] was here, he called out again, saying: "Does the Venerable Fang see it? It is precisely right for making offerings. Coming, there is no place from which it comes; going, there is no place to which it goes.
Each and every thing is neither born nor extinguished. Its nature is true, wondrous, and luminous, eternally abiding within the world."
"Pure and fundamental from the beginning, pervading the entire Dharma-realm. If it were thus, even ten thousand ounces of gold could be digested;
if it were not thus, even a drop of water would be difficult to digest. This old monk eats his fill according to custom, and he can even buy straw sandals for three coins."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Today the Monastery Gate makes offerings to the Arhats, to repay the heart's vows of donors from the ten directions, so that the deceased may be reborn in heaven and the living may obtain blessings.
He called out, 'Assembly! Simply follow the custom and eat your fill; do not inquire about the shortness or length of life in the human world.
Again, picking up his staff, he said: 'My births have been exhausted; the holy life has been established.'"

"Having accomplished what was to be done, no longer subject to further existence, the three realms can do nothing against him—one who is worthy of receiving offerings from devas and humans—this band of forest-dwelling monks deserves twenty blows of the staff each. [The Master] lets out a shout and descends from his seat."
Offering to the Arhats, he ascended the hall and said: "The three realms are but mind; the myriad dharmas are but consciousness.
There is not a single dharma that does not arise from the mind. If the mind were extinguished, all dharmas would be extinguished. Therefore, the past mind cannot be apprehended."
"The future mind cannot be apprehended; the present mind cannot be apprehended. Since the three periods of time do not exist, from what could a single mind arise?
O Great Assembly! Only when all floating thoughts are exhausted is one realized as an Arhat. If floating thoughts are not exhausted, one remains entirely subject to the wandering of birth and death.
With a shout, he descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Today we offer sustenance to the Arhats. Last night, eminent guests from the four quarters recited the 'Chapter on the Peaceful Practices' of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* once.
Great assembly, what is this 'Peaceful Practice'? If you conceive of it with a deliberate mind, you have already ceased to be at peace.
Then he gave a shout and said: 'Is this not the Peaceful Practice? What is the penetration of the Dharma?"
The phrase "hiding the body within the Big Dipper"—is this not the practice of peace and joy?
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"—"The cypress tree in the courtyard"—is this not the practice of peace and joy?

"What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and Patriarchs?"—"A steamed bun"—is this not the practice of peace and joy? Thus, down to the monastics and the lay assembly, each and every one is pure radiance.

Is maintaining clarity not itself the practice of peace and bliss? From a single Buddha, two Bodhisattvas, each Arhat, and each Pratyekabuddha, there is none that does not dwell in the pure reality-mark (*dharmatā*), which is what is called the practice of peace and bliss.
O Great Assembly! It is only the jewel within the topknot that I do not give away recklessly. Although I do not give it, you all possess it fully within yourselves.
Throughout the twelve periods of the day, the radiance is brilliantly blazing. Who lacks this? Do you understand? Return to the hall for tea.
(He lets out a shout and descends from his seat.)
Offering to the Arhats, he ascends the hall and addresses the assembly: "All phenomena are the Buddha-dharma;
all minds are the Buddha-mind; all speech is the Buddha-speech; all paths are the path of the Arhats.
As for these phenomena, minds, speech, and paths—tell me, are they one? Are they two? Are they the same? Or are they different? Two...
Do not cling even to the "one" or the "existence. When the single mind does not arise, the myriad dharmas are without fault.
Chan Master Chushih Qi ascended the hall for a meal offering to the Arhats, saying: "The wind stirs in the ancient halls; the moon turns through the winding corridors.

Fragrant smoke swirls all around; lamps and candles shine brightly. The Venerable Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja partakes of offerings throughout the four worlds, yet there is not a single place where he is not present."
"Not yet. "Have you come here? "What place is this that you say I have not arrived?
He joined his palms and said, "The three virtues and six flavors are offered to the Buddha and the Sangha," and then descended from his seat.
The Outline for Releasing Living Creatures:
Chan Master Xuedou Xian’s Teaching to the Assembly upon Releasing a White Crane Red crest, green plumage, snow-white feathers— Though you do not approach the phoenixes, your intent is lofty.
I release you into the forested clouds; do not look back. Where now is the office of the immortals?
Chan Master Wuxiang showed the assembly the fish brought by a donor for release. "Sinking in dead water is not yet being a master;
turning one's body in the great ocean is truly free and easy. Today at Lushan, I open up a single thread of the Way;
it must be valued that each attains freedom. Do not greedily covet others' fragrant bait. If you can believe with full confidence, even a thousand-fathom fishing line will not entangle you."
Abiding. Who dares to cast a vast, sky-reaching net? With a single leap, one passes through the Dragon Gate; fearing neither the overturning of heaven nor the shaking of the earth.
When a great drought strikes, one becomes a rain-cloud; with focused intent, one bestows grace upon all living beings. Ten thousand celestial sons stand together beneath the wind;
even the angry sea-monsters and *kūṇapeng* dragons look up but cannot reach him. After a long silence, he said: "If you reach this state..."
"You would be failing this old monk.
Master Zhongfeng Ben held a memorial service for the late Commissioner Qu at the Bhaiṣajyaguru Ritual Hall, releasing living beings.
Beside the red peonies, butterflies dance; within the green wutong trees, orioles sing. The Great Way before one’s eyes is without obstruction; it is simply that the multitude...

Traveling along the path of birth and death, today the Medicine Master Tathāgata, being in close proximity, has caused Senior Official Gu of the Two Zhe Circuits and the Commissioner of Transport—holding the rank of Lesser Minister—to give rise to a great *dharma-maṇḍala* upon the tip of a single hair. He performs the Buddha-activity adorned with a hundred jewels.
For this reason, the Abbot [Zhen] celebrates this feast and, for the sake of all sentient beings, points out the very head of the path. Thus he teaches:
The Middle Way: Since there are no phenomena within the three realms, where can one seek the mind? The mind cannot be sought; how then can phenomena find a locus?
Thereupon, one sees that the worlds of the ten directions are the pure Dharma-body, and the worlds of the ten directions are the ocean of the twelve vows of the Medicine Master Buddha.
It is truly so. Those with wings may soar high; those with feet are not hindered from traveling far.
Those clad in armor may hide in the deep abyss; those bearing scales may roam freely in the vast ravines.

There is not a single sentient being who does not attain perfect enlightenment, nor a single sentient being who does not enter into perfect clarity. Even so, as the ancients said: "To emerge from within the gate."
Easy. It is difficult to leave the body behind. Tell me, how is it to be that which transcends both ease and difficulty?

What is the phrase for being utterly liberated and alone? Then, releasing the living beings, he said: "Wherever one breaks through, all is the path to the heavens; wherever one penetrates, there is nothing but the gate of liberation."
Chan Master Zhuo’an addresses the assembly on the liberation of living beings at West Lake: Clouds rise from the southern mountain, and rain falls upon the northern peak.
The autumn colors fill the lake as gulls and egrets dance. Suddenly, the staff transforms into a dragon, and all living beings throughout the great earth lose their fundamental footing.
Many bystanders are implicated; they beat their breasts, crying out in grievance and suffering. The mountain monk blinks his eyes, and a smile breaks across his face.
In a single instant, we enter together the path of non-arising. How about this? "If I head toward the mountain of blades, the mountain of blades shall collapse of its own accord;
if I head toward hell, hell shall extinguish itself. Clapping his hands, he said: "The golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net does not linger in the water."
A swift falcon soars through the clouds toward the heavens.

Ascending the seat at the ceremony for releasing living beings on the lake, the Master said: "The net is spread across the sky; those who wish to enter cannot enter, and those who wish to exit cannot exit.
Even if you were able to turn your body around, your skin would already be pierced and your flesh torn. If you wish to seize the nine-thousand-mile clouds,"
"To travel ninety thousand *li*, one must do so without legs yet moving, without wings yet flying.
After a long silence, he said, "Only by not craving the taste of fragrant bait does one become a dragon of the azure pool.

Today, on behalf of the faithful of this entire city who have formed a society for the release of living beings, we pray for the imperial domain and beseech the cessation of martial calamities; may there be peace throughout the world and the eternal laying down of arms."
How can one express this in a single phrase? Listen to this verse: The hawk flies of its own accord, and the fish leaps of its own accord. Why should the hunter covet them?
Why should the fish be startled by the hook? Together we gaze upon the hue of the lake and mountains, looking up to bathe in the vast and boundless benevolence of the Imperial Grace.
Regarding the Offering of Dharma Robes, Chan Master Baiyun Yuan said: "When a dragon wears even a single thread, the golden-winged bird cannot swallow it.
Had he swallowed it all at once then and there, would not the world have been at peace? But tell me, which is that which cannot be swallowed?"
[The Master] picked up a corner of his dharma robe and showed it to the assembly, saying: "Is this not that which cannot be swallowed? Do you see it?
To casually hang it upon one's shoulder surpasses the people of this age wearing brocade robes."

Chan Master Zhenjing Wen ascended the hall as a donor presented him with a Dharma robe. The Master said, "When the Buddhas appeared in the world, they all donned this robe to preach the Dharma and save sentient beings.
Today, Dongshan likewise dons this robe to preach the Dharma and save sentient beings.
He then picked up a corner of the robe and called to the assembly, "Is there anyone here who will not be splashed with foul water? After a long silence, he said, "The moon..."
The sky reaches the white heart of the heavens; the waves return to the sea’s clarity.

The Dharma robe was offered by a donor; the assembly, listen! The Dharma robes of all Buddhas—those who obtain them transcend the three realms, leave behind the five desires, realize the Great Way, and deliver sentient beings.
He then held up the robe and said: "Lifted up, the bitterness of hell ceases."
Luo Xi zhan puts it down. Emperors and Śakras shake their heads; the devas cease their music.

Neither raised nor lowered, the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm—sentient and non-sentient alike—attain the Buddha-way together. I do not know what one who bestows a Dharma robe has accomplished.
After a long silence, he says: "Since Old Lu gathered it back in, you must believe that everyone possesses it."
Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin ascended the hall when a donor offered him a Dharma robe, saying: “Kāśyapa carried it to Chicken Foot Peak; Old Lu took it over the Dayu Ridge.
Now, I don this upon the precious flowered seat; its solitary radiance shines far and wide atop the high peak.
Tell me, is this the same or different? A young lord in brocade robes is noble; a man of the way beneath the forest trees is lofty.”
Chan Master Ying’an Hua was invited by Zhao Zhongda of Guangde Commandery to give a small-scale sermon (xiaocan) upon the offering of a Dharma robe.
The Master then cited a passage from the teachings: "If one sees me in form, or seeks me in sound, this person walks a deviant path and cannot see the Tathāgata.
He then let out a shout and asked, "Do you all hear it? Yet it is not sound. He then raised [the robe].
[The Master] said, "Regarding the corner of the *kāṣāya*: do you all see it? It is certainly not color. Since it is not to be distinguished through sound or form, where do you see the Tathāgata?

If you say that you see the Tathāgata during the twenty-four hours of the day—whether moving or still, speaking or silent, in every turn, step, bow, or gesture—that is to mistake a thief for one's own son. If you say..."

Throughout the two periods of six hours [day and night], whether moving or still, speaking or silent, turning or walking, bending or looking up—discriminating in all such states is precisely "a madman running outside.
Here, if one is a man of clear eyes, not even a single point can be deceived. Have you not seen how Master Benren said:
"Ordinarily, I do not wish to dally with the sons and daughters of others before sounds or after phrases; yet, nevertheless..."
"Sound is not sound; form is not form. At one time, someone asked, "What is meant by 'sound is not sound'?
Ren said, "Can you call it form? [The questioner] asked, "What is meant by 'form is not form'? Ren said, "Can you call it sound? Now tell me:
was this spoken for you, or was it an answer to your question? If you can discern this, you will undoubtedly have something within the Buddha-dharma.
Regarding this point of entry, Xuedou took it up and said, "Benren is truly extraordinary; yet, he is preoccupied with gazing at the heavens.

Since this is neither prior to sound nor subsequent to words, through what door does one enter? The Master (Zhaozhou) took it up and said, "At this point, even though Xuedou exhausts all his spiritual powers, there is no place for him to insert a hand.
As for saying, 'Since it is neither prior to sound nor subsequent to words, through what door does one enter?'"
Often, five out of ten miss the mark. Do you know where Jianfu has landed? One arrow brings down two vultures.
The Venerable Liaozhi has come from Guangde, carrying the generous offerings of the Grand Governor to provide for the monks on this day and to perform various Buddhist rites.
Furthermore, he has offered a Dharma robe to me, the mountain monk, to receive.
On this occasion, he has commanded a small-scale sermon (*xiao can*) to exalt the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye and the Sublime Mind of Nirvāṇa.
He gathers these boundless superior virtues to pray for the extension of the Count’s longevity and that of his entire noble family, so that their merit and blessings may flourish beyond measure.

May the four debts of gratitude be fully repaid, the three realms of existence be universally sustained, and all sentient beings within the *dharmadhātu* together perfect the seed-wisdom (*bīja-jñāna*). Although the Great Official of the Prefecture...
I have not yet had the opportunity to meet you in person. I have heard in confidence that you possess profound realization regarding this great matter;
though we are separated by more than a thousand li, there has never been a gap of even a single hair’s breadth between us—truly what is called "the same breeze blowing over a thousand miles.

Since you act as an external protector of the Zen school and remain tireless in this Way, I know for certain that throughout the past immeasurable kalpas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, [you have cultivated this].
When the habitual tendencies have reached maturity, as soon as one emerges from the head [of the coffin], one turns it all around with a single stroke; how could this depend on much talk?
Nevertheless, there is no other technique for practicing the work than simply possessing the great faculty of faith and being endowed with the great seed-wisdom.

Knowing that such a thing exists, during the two periods of six hours (the twelve periods of the day and night), whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, you must earnestly and repeatedly call it to mind and examine what its principle is. But...
Pushing it back and forth in this manner until you reach a state of total non-reliance, you suddenly encounter it without expending even a hair’s breadth of effort;
this is precisely that which came from your mother’s womb. It has never been anything other than what was given to you, shared in common enjoyment with all the Buddhas and Patriarchs of antiquity.
It is just like cutting a skein of silk: as one cut is made, one strand is severed.
It is completely severed. Just as when one thread of dyed silk is dyed, all are dyed; the boundaries of past and future are cut off, and the three great kalpas are empty.
If one seeks that emptiness, it is utterly unattainable. The entire body is this very adamantine essence, entirely devoid of appearing or disappearing.
Upon the portion of the Buddhas, not a single hair’s breadth has been added; within the bodies of ordinary beings, not a single hair’s breadth has been subtracted.
It is like water washing water, or gold exchanging for gold. At times, one takes up a blade of grass and makes it the sixteen-foot golden body;
at other times, one takes the sixteen-foot golden body and makes it a blade of grass. Seizing and releasing are sovereign; killing and giving life are free.

This very *huatou* has descended from the time of the Yellow-Faced Old Man at the assembly on Vulture Peak in antiquity. From Buddha to Buddha and from Patriarch to Patriarch, they have transmitted it mind-to-mind;
until this day, there has never been so much as a single hair’s breadth of error. It is called the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye and the Subtle Mind of Nirvana.
It existed before heaven and earth, before the sun and moon, and before the human relations of society.
Prior to this, this mind already pervaded the void. When heaven and earth were first divided and the sun, moon, and human relations came into being, this mind likewise pervaded the void.
Therefore it is said: "Birth is thus, and death is thus. Yet, fundamentally, birth and death cannot encompass it. Why?
Because at every step, there is a path for it to emerge. Have you not seen?
He teaches the Middle Way. If he is among householders, he is honored as the foremost among householders and preaches the supreme Dharma for them.

If he is among lay devotees, he is honored as the foremost among lay devotees and severs their greedy attachments. If he is among the kṣatriyas, he is honored as the foremost among the kṣatriyas and instructs them in patience.
If he is among the brāhmaṇas, he is honored as the foremost among the brāhmaṇas and eliminates their pride. If he is among the ministers... [he is honored as the foremost among the ministers...]
O Venerable One, you teach by means of the True Dharma. If among princes, you are the most honored among princes, showing them loyalty and filial piety;

if within the inner palace, you are the most honored among those of the inner palace, transforming the palace women with correctness; if among the common people, you are the most honored among the common people, causing them to give rise to the power of merit;
if among the Brahmā devas, you are the most honored among the Brahmā devas, instructing them in supreme wisdom; and if among Śakra, you are the most honored among Śakras.
World-Honored One, you manifest impermanence; yet if you are among the World-Protectors, you are the most honored among the World-Protectors, protecting all sentient beings.
This is surely because from within the pure and subtle fundamental wisdom, you have extensively brought forth such a supreme and wondrous gate of great liberation through skillful means.
It is also called the adamantine true essence (*vajra-svabhāva*); it is also called the King-Crown Samādhi (*mūrdha-rāja-samādhi*);
it is also called the Ocean of Buddha-lands of the Floating Banner King; and it is also called the Ultimate Truth (*paramārtha*).

As for Master Yangqi’s use of the "adamantine circle" (*vajra-maṇḍala*) and the "chestnut thorn" (*liji pong*) to reveal the Way to students, he clearly illuminated the origins of the direct pointing of Shaoshi (Bodhidharma). His skillful adaptation was unconventional, transcending all measure.

Attaining great mastery, he extracts nails and pulls out wedges for all people, ungluing what is stuck and unbinding what is bound, causing each and every one to personally realize the ultimate penetration from top to bottom.
Furthermore, this cannot be known by the mind, nor can it be cognized by consciousness. As the Master of Changsha said:
"If I were to expound the teachings of our school, the grass before the Dharma Hall would grow ten feet deep; having no other choice, I [speak thus]."
I have previously told people: the entire world of the ten directions is the śramaṇa’s eye; the entire world of the ten directions is the śramaṇa’s whole body;
the entire world of the ten directions is one's own radiance; the entire world of the ten directions is contained within one's own radiance;
and throughout the entire world of the ten directions, there is not a single person who is not oneself. I have often said this...
"O people of the world! All Buddhas of the three periods of time, throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm, are this light of Mahāprajñā.
Before this light has yet been emitted, where do you all turn for refuge? Even before the light is emitted, there is no news of Buddha or sentient beings.
Since there is no news of Buddha or sentient beings, tell me: what of the great earth, mountains, rivers, sun, and moon?"
From where do the stars, humans, livestock, grasses, and shrubs—whether minute or vast, long or short—originate? Do you know their place of descent?
In the heavens, all stars bow toward the North; among men, there is no water that does not flow toward the East.
Chan Master Zhuo’an asked about the robe presented by a donor and addressed the assembly. Holding up a corner of the Dharma robe, the Master said:
"This is that which the Yellow-Faced Old Man has transmitted from generation to generation. For what reason, today, does it instead come from the house of a faithful patron?
Since this mountain monk neither stores it away nor uses it as a covering, I shall simply present it before this assembly of devas and humans."
Once I have brought it up for you, do you understand? When brought forth, not even an inch of thread separates it; a single expanse of cloud and mist, brilliant and unrestrained.
When one has spirit, let spirit increase; when one attains elegance, let there be elegance.

Offering Dharma robes for the ascent to the hall: [made of] Shu brocade and Wu silk, with clustered flowers and intricate patterns, blazing reds and radiant purples, overflowing with color and increasing in brilliance.
They seize the light from beneath the neck of the black dragon and pluck the sharpness from the whiskers of the fierce tiger.
Every monk of our school has teeth like sword-trees and a mouth like a blood-basin; who would be willing to surrender their stratagem and pay tribute? Therefore it is said: "Descending from Heaven."
Below, there is poverty; emerging from the earth, one becomes wealthy and noble. The great treasure of the Dharma King is manifest and accomplished; it arrives spontaneously without being sought.
Entering a desolate field, one does not discriminate; with a trusting hand, one simply picks it up. Face-to-face, they present it to one another. When one is raised, two are not raised.
Reaching this point, one sheds precious royal robes to don tattered, soiled garments; having attained the wondrous, one turns back to enter the marketplace.

Regarding the phrase "Hanging down one's hand," how would you say it? "The bamboo pole follows the body; wherever the stage is found, there is the play. At the tip of every blade of grass, one sees the Patriarch.
When the attendant offered the Dharma robe, he ascended the hall, donned the Tathāgata’s robe, sat upon the Tathāgata’s seat, and performed the Tathāgata’s work. Three.
A frog on one's feet wears a brocade apron; the wind blows, yet the tree before the steps does not move.
Mazu pinches his nose; the wild duck has nowhere to go. Baizhang rolls up the mat; when the Great Function manifests, there are no fixed rules.

How laughable is the Old National Teacher of Nanyang, who says "I owe you" and "I owe myself," pointing at his finger as a note. To point is not to arrive; to arrive is not to be pointed at. For thirty years...
Henceforth, do not say that here at Mount Jinshan there is injustice but no place to cry out.

*Record of the Essential Teachings of the Patriarchs*, Volume Twenty.
The Abbot of Lian-an Chan Temple at the Eighteen Gullies in Wulin, Xingyue of Loudong, has assembled offerings for a Dharma robe.
High Peak Master Miaozhao, Chan Master Tongning, and the Hermit Zhian present the Dharma robe. Ascending the hall, he says: "Cut from Shu brocade."
Cut from Wu-ling silk, draped with white jade, interspersed with gold; when forged into a single whole, even a needle cannot pierce it.
Where the warp and weft knot at the corners, the seams are difficult to find. Nevertheless, it is just like Xifeng, who took the emptiness of all dharmas as his seat.
Pointing his staff at his robe, he asked: "Can you wear this? Leaning on his staff, he said: "The fragrance of heaven disperses among the moss."
Moss-covered rocks; five-leafed flowers bloom in the campaka groves.
Chan Master Changer Qian of Qianyan addressed the assembly regarding a Dharma robe bestowed by the Prince of Ning: "The spring clouds have just rolled away, and the spring rain has newly cleared.

Flowers are red and willows are green; waters are emerald and mountains are azure. Purple swallows and yellow orioles discourse deeply on the true mark (*dharmatā*). Among the thickets and grasses..."
The entire wood resonates with the sound of a lute. It thrusts forth the nostrils of Śākyamuni and wide-opens the eyes of Bodhidharma.
Just as it is today, regarding this single dharma-cloak offered by Lady Zhang Dezhen of Qijun: upon it is a scroll of the Heart Sūtra.
To call it a scroll of the Heart Sūtra is yet another way of calling it a dharma-cloak; and to call it a dharma-cloak is yet another...
This one scroll of the Heart Sutra has golden flames flickering and brocade layers unfolding. Its interlocking corners and lattice patterns are successive precious seals;

its vertical and horizontal ten directions are clusters of pearl necklaces. Since the adornments are so wondrous, the marks of virtue increase all the more. Each and every character flows forth from the hearts of the honored ladies;
each and every one is perfectly luminous within the sphere of the Buddhas. I, this old monk, have received [the transmission] from all of you.

[The Master] divided [the property]. Once the people had received their portions, the old monk was left with no share. It would have been better to strike it down and return it to the permanent residence (the monastery).

For a thousand years, ten thousand ages, let the true lamp shine! Let the true lamp shine! On what else could it rely? Sometimes hung upon the Flower King’s throne, it is far superior to the black-lacquered screens found elsewhere.
Master Yuan of Foyan, a descendant of Baogai Digan, ascended the hall for the offering of a precious canopy by Mr. Guo, a retired government official. He raised the following case:

When Master Muping was traveling on pilgrimage, he asked Luopu, "What is it like before even a single bubble has arisen? Luopu replied, "Move the boat and you will know the currents. He raised [this case].
Setting out his oars upon the waves, Mupyeong found no resonance and so went to ask Panlong. Panlong said, "If you move your boat, you will not discern the water;
if you raise your oars, you will lose the source. At these words, Mupyeong attained great enlightenment. Later, he resided at Mupyeong.
When King Yi summoned him to Jinling to inquire about the Way, Fayuan had a verse that said: "The man from within Mupyeong Mountain has an ancient appearance and his speech is likewise..."
Few indeed. We gaze upon one another on the same road; discussing our hearts, the autumn moon is bright. The thread for his tattered robe does not come from silkworms;
there are birds that assist his singing. The city walls have come today; he has long since understood the "single bubble. Truly, these words are so!
How will you clarify the matter of his awakening beneath the words of Panlong? If someone asks: "Before the single bubble had yet arisen at Longmen—"
"How is it? he asked. Longmen found it truly difficult to speak, yet after a long silence, he finally said: "When the single bubble has not yet arisen, The jeweled canopy hangs toward the void.
Auspicious colors rise and drift, And fragrant breezes blow gently. What need is there to lift the robe lightly? There is no need to slightly raise an eyebrow.
Five hundred [monks] once presented this in person; The Tathāgata gave his seal of approval. In the past, at the city of Vaiśālī, five hundred..."
The sons of the elders each took a parasol made of the seven treasures and came to where the Buddha was.

Before the Buddhas appeared in the world and before Bodhidharma came from the West, everyone possessed the raw jade of Jing Mountain, and every individual cherished the pearl from the Red Water.

Yet, once the five petals of the Dharma-flower have blossomed and the thousand lamps have continued their flame, we see life and death alternating and cold and heat shifting in succession—just as in the wealthy households of the northern districts.

Yesterday there was song, today there is weeping. Jiangshan’s announcement is much like moving flowers and the butterflies arriving with them, or buying stones and finding oneself with an abundance of clouds.
If you all can examine this well, you will surely find yourselves sitting and lying down all day long amidst sounds and forms, yet sounds and forms will be unable to defile you;

'I cannot help but borrow his nostrils to breathe. [He] strikes the ground with the staff and says: 'Opening the gate of ambrosia. [He] draws a line and says: 'Revealing the sweet dew.'"
The Flavor of Dew. All sentient beings of the great earth have suddenly transcended the ten stages;
only the elder Juecheng, who prepared this vegetarian feast to offer merit for the spirits of his deceased parents, is not included therein. Why? [He] throws down his staff and says:
"Clearly, a pair of golden bones; there is no need for sandalwood to be intricately carved."

Innumerable flowers fill the lotus palaces and Buddha-fields; raise your eyebrows and observe them closely. The Master [Zhaozhou] said: "Observing is not non-existent."
"What do you call 'one thing'? He gave a shout.

A swift falcon or a keen eagle cannot overtake it; a sudden clap of thunder or a flash of lightning cannot catch up. Leaping upward, one brushes past the Great..."

How do you all understand this? (He strikes the whisk. A white egret descends the field—a thousand dots of snow;

What this mountain monk offers is entirely in accordance with reality. [The assembly] descends from their seats.

Before the world had taken form and before heaven and earth were established, where could names be assigned to Buddhas, ordinary beings, or sages? Now that the world has taken form and heaven and earth are established, the Buddha...
Ordinary beings and sages each find their proper place. Thus it is said: "This dharma abides in its own station; the characteristics of the world are eternally constant.
What is this dharma? [The Master] holds up his whisk and says: "This is the whisk. What is the station of dharma? [The Master] strikes the whisk and says:
"It cannot be called a whisk, yet it cannot not be called a whisk. Herein...
One attains the single eye; by this, heaven and earth find their proper places, and by this, the myriad things are nurtured.
The ruler attains it and governs the myriad states; the minister attains it and assists the nine realms.

Fathers, sons, elder brothers, younger brothers, and wives attain it, whereby filial piety, compassion, friendship, and harmony are established within a single household. Friends attain it, whereby righteousness, trust, loyalty, and integrity are sworn in alliance.

The square inch of the heart is the eternal principle that remains unchanged for ten thousand generations; it is the supreme nature that endures through antiquity and the present without being worn away.

If this principle is not destroyed for a single day, the world will not perish for a single day. If this nature does not cease for a single breath, heaven and earth will not shift for a single breath.
Do not say that the eras of the Yellow Emperor and Yao have suddenly vanished; how is the present any different from the beginning of the kalpa?

Today, this mountain monk, on behalf of the Dharma-protecting lay devotee Shi Zixiang, has specially requested to ascend the seat to proclaim the Dharma for the sake of those spirits who sacrificed their lives in service to righteousness.
From the sovereign and regional princes above, down to the generals, officials, and common clerks below—may they all be remembered.
Whether remembering or forgetting, whether dwelling vividly within or drifting outward; across different times and separate worlds, self and other are not divided by so much as a hair’s breadth.
Whether living or dead, ascending or sinking, beginning and end never depart from the present moment. Returning to the root and shedding the leaves, the essence is revealed in the golden wind.
Raising one's spirit and lifting the brow, even when the body is struck by a white blade, the precious lotus seat is already lowered with medicinal grace.
The branches emit a wondrous fragrance. O virtuous ones, do you believe this? Have you not seen it stated in the teachings:
"If I go toward the mountain of blades, the mountain of blades shall naturally crumble; if I go toward the cauldrons of fire, the cauldrons of fire shall naturally dry up;
if I go toward hell, hell shall naturally be extinguished; if I go toward the realm of hungry ghosts, the hungry ghosts shall naturally be satiated"? If I go toward...
Asuras! Asuras, you must tame yourselves. If I were to turn toward other species, each would attain great wisdom.
At such a time as this, how shall we guide and deliver these wandering souls? Listen to this verse: Warm blood transforms into water of merit;
The grievances of the netherworld coalesce into clouds of wondrous fragrance. Upon coral branches, the bright moon is hooked; From the azure void, the soul of Shu is summoned back.
[The Master] struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
He then invited the Governor for his wife, Lady Jin, to ascend the seat. "Spiritual light shines alone, utterly transcending the sense bases and their objects.
Its essence reveals true permanence, unbound by words and letters. The nature of mind is undefiled, fundamentally perfect and complete. Simply by parting from delusive conditions, one is as such."
As the Buddha taught: false conditions are not real; all is but mind alone. If the mind and its objects are empty, from where could all false conditions arise?
In delusion, one falsely perceives birth and falsely perceives death, giving rise to various evil karmas and creating obstacles of sin within the cycle of birth and death.
When one is free from delusion, birth is like a bubble drifting by, and death is like a phantom dissolving. In this fundamental state...
Within the state beyond birth and death, evil karma is fundamentally empty and karmic obstacles are fundamentally pure.

Thus, the Buddhas of antiquity have said: "The body is provisionally formed by borrowing the four great elements; the mind is fundamentally unborn, arising only because of external objects. If the external object is absent, the mind is likewise non-existent.
Transgressions and blessings are like illusions—they arise and they perish. In this way, the body, the mind, the sensory dusts, the external objects, transgressions, and blessings [are all empty].

They arise and they cease, being equal to illusions. Although they are equal to illusions, at the very moment an illusion arises as a single thought and suddenly dwells upon an illusory object, there are unspeakably unspeakable realms throughout kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Whether it be love or hatred, kindness or enmity, there is nothing that is not fully present within the minds of sentient beings. At the very moment one such [thought] suddenly arises...

When one suddenly awakens to the thought being like an illusion, then throughout unspeakably unspeakable numbers of kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—whether regarding love or hatred, kindness or enmity—all are, within the mind of non-arising, like the sun shining upon the great void, penetrating all darkness;
or like snow falling upon a red furnace, where all obstructions melt away. Thus one knows that this single thought is equal to them all.

To transform the mundane into the sacred and to turn delusion into awakening—the distinction between the illusory and that which is like an illusion—is precisely what constitutes the vast difference between the sacred and the mundane, and between delusion and awakening.
Now, the Great Layman Shiweng, Minister of the Grand Council, having long since inherited the power of his vows, this very nature remains undeluded.
Because his wife has passed away, he has dispatched a letter from a thousand li away earnestly requesting that I, this mountain monk, come specifically to Huai.
The attendants personally acted as proxies for the deceased, elevating [the merit] to provide for their posthumous blessings and using Prajñā to wash away transgressions.
The moment the layman raised this thought, the lady had already ascended to the Pure Realm. When one thought is pure, every subsequent thought is pure.
When one person is purified, many people are purified; when one world is purified, many worlds are purified. The boundless realms of lands—self and other—are not separated by even the tip of a hair;
the ten periods of past and present, from beginning to end, do not depart from the present moment of thought.
How much more so for Lady Zhi, who, by means of this single thought-moment, empties all outflows and purifies all karmic conditions. Through many lifetimes of kin and across kalpas...
There is not one among enemies or kin who does not, by means of this single thought-moment, attain the stage of great liberation and enter the gate of the great samādhi of stillness.

Even down to all sentient beings throughout the world, by virtue of this single thought-moment of the Great Overseer, each and every one awakens to the fact that the body is like an illusion, the mind is like an illusion, and the environment is like an illusion; thus, O Layman, this thought of yours is likewise [self-arisen].

Benefiting both self and others, we shall together achieve fulfillment. Reaching down to the profound depths of the mysterious and soaring upward beyond the limits of all realms, this is surely not merely the formation of a single occasion’s prajñā-affinity;
it is truly the seed of bodhi across kalpas as numerous as motes of dust. Now tell me:
as the mountain monk ascends today to this precious seat specifically to proclaim it, is it ultimately an illusion, or is it not an illusion? Is it a false condition, or is it the truth?
"Is it the limit? Listen to this one verse: Sudden emptiness, yet there is existence; the illusory is neither illusory nor real. It shatters emotional conditions—emptiness and non-emptiness alike.
The Jade Maiden has already departed into the celestial expanse; there is no need for sorrow over the wind of the fifth watch.
With his whisk, he drew a circle, gave a shout, and descended from the seat.

After Mother Wu, the Senior Lady, had lit the spirit-tablet, she ascended the seat, held her staff horizontally across her lap, and said: "Stoically sitting, he cuts off the paths of mountain and stream;
beneath the hundred billion Mount Sumerus, all is cold to the core. The eight directions naturally return to the realm of rectitude;

birth and death, like dreams and illusions, do not interfere with one another. Since they do not interfere, one must discern the Master. If you can discern him, my question shall be answered like water poured from one vessel to another."

Like clouds arising, they carry their staffs and wood with them, performing their play as the occasion demands. They become lost by a hair’s breadth beneath words and confused by the slightest glimmer of reflection.
Exhausting the world’s pivotal mechanisms, they display all manner of profound sophistry; yet these are all but the mad wandering of fools, with skulls filling every realm.
Every person possesses a living path that pierces the heavens; every individual has a wondrous skill that carves the earth. Not even a single atom can be added to this.
It cannot be diminished by even a hair’s breadth. Brightly casting oneself into the dark, essence and function are mutually appropriate.
Whether one possesses the wisdom of Śāriputra or the eloquence of Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra, there is no point of intersection whatsoever within the sphere of ordinary people.

Linji’s Three Mysteries and Three Essentials, Dongshan’s Five Ranks of Ruler and臣 (Minister), Yunmen’s Single-Character Barrier, and the ninety-six circular diagrams of the Miao-yang school—these are like hanging a notice at the gate of the realm of ghosts.
Deceiving and intimidating the common folk, he twists the upper pivot and hurls the Flower Treasury World (Avataṃsaka-dhātu) upside down.

Completely transcending the sages and worthies of past and present, he no longer leans on the door or peers through the window. From the bare lump of flesh, the True Person of No Rank (wù-wèi zhēn-rén) suddenly emerges;
from within his own breast, it flows forth, covering heaven and earth. He calls Maitreya a slave and regards Śākyamuni as a maid-servant—as for all other fellows who sell straw sandals!
To find a place where one can emerge, the matter must be such a matter, and the person must be such a person.
The supreme flavor of clarified butter (*ghṛta*) is prized by the world; yet, if it does not meet the right person, it turns into poison.
Today, I have lifted the lid from my skull and laid it bare for all of you. It is clearly no different [from before]; it is authentically transmitted. Total guest is total host. Total...
The host is the guest; shatter the city of nirvana and travel together across the ocean of liberation. Now, regarding this one phrase that transcends directly—how do you speak it?
He raises his staff and says: "The green mountains do not lock in their soaring momentum; the vast blue seas surely know the height from which they come.
With a shout, he strikes the ground with his staff.
Chan Master Chaozong Ren ascends the hall to pray for blessings and to offer memorial services for his deceased wife. First is the prayer for blessings; second is the memorial for the deceased.

Below, one does not loathe the hells; above, one does not rejoice in the heavens. Suddenly emerging in the midst of reality, it stands forth majestic and manifest. Where the partridge cries, the hundred flowers bloom.
Xiang gave a shout. He then cited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, saying: "If one sees that all marks are no-marks, then one sees the Tathāgata. The Master said:

At the request of the Imperial Commissioner Shen Zhitai, who dispatched an official to the mountain to offer memorial services for the fallen soldiers, the Master ascended the hall and said:
"Taking the four elements as a body—within this, there is ultimately no self. If one can achieve liberation in a single thought-moment, then the teachings will be fully manifested in every dharma."
All things are fully present; he alone is honored throughout the three realms. The sword-trees and knife-mountains vanish into nothingness;
from where do the banners, streamers, and precious canopies arise? Therefore it is said: "If I go toward the mountain of knives, the mountain of knives collapses of its own accord;
if I go toward the cauldron of fire, the cauldron of fire extinguishes of its own accord. By sitting and cutting off the path of both sin and merit, one naturally transcends directly beneath. Now...
When the Sun-canopy was about to sink, Grand Marshal Shen was commissioned by imperial decree to suppress the Yao rebels. Within a single year, all eight mountain ranges were pacified.

Now, at this moment of celebrating victory, a sorrow for our shared essence has suddenly arisen. An official has been dispatched with funds to enter the mountains to perform rites of repentance and establish a vegetarian feast.

One must know that a single application of the Dharma-rain reaches directly into the netherworld; a single hearing of the Dharma-sound immediately transcends to the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
To rouse oneself against the raiders of the mind, one dons the armor of patience and the demonic armies are instantly shattered.

To establish the rank of a Marquis, one wields the sword of wisdom against delusive thoughts and the Buddha-way is swiftly accomplished. Although it is thus, this is still merely the Great Marshal’s act of pitying the multitude.
"Understand. Furthermore, regarding the phrase 'First, we offer congratulations upon the Imperial Grace'—how would you say it? 'The eight directions are moistened by the rain of non-action;
throughout the four seas, songs of joy celebrate Great Peace. Descend from your seat."
Chan Master Yuan of Longmen returned to Dongshan to pay his respects; at the request of the assembly, he was asked to give a small discourse (*xiao can*).

Having briefly descended from Lotus Peak, I have lightly counted my fingers; time has passed in an instant, and it is already three years. Although not separated by even a hair’s breadth, how can this compare to personally arriving before the seat?
I, [Name], have been in the company of Chan Master Taiping on his majestic carriage as we once again ascended Lotus Mountain since several days ago.
Returning to serve the Great Monk, my teacher, while gazing upon his compassionate countenance, you must know that there is a matter of "meeting.
I dare ask the assembly: what is this matter of meeting? It cannot be that you see me and I see you—that would be meeting.
If it were so, there would be no place where the Buddha-dharma exerts its power. Why? Because in the various realms of the mundane world...
We see one another, yet we constantly remain within the cycle of birth and death, having not yet found a place of liberation.
Therefore, Master Xuefeng said to people: "I have already met you at Wangzhou Pavilion; I have already met you at Wushan Ridge;
I have already met you before the Sangha Hall. If one relies on such indications, why wait for [anything else]?
When voices and countenances meet and speech and breath intermingle, this is what constitutes "meeting.
O venerable elders, one who is a student of the Way must truly have a place to go before it is attained. Do you understand?

Nowadays, I dare say that meeting while sharing the same breeze across a thousand li is easy to comprehend, yet meeting face-to-face is difficult to know. Why is it difficult to know? Old Man Jia Shan said:
At present there is no *ācārya*; on this seat there is no old monk. All you who have gathered as the great assembly are here; how do you perceive this?
The Master, the Great *Upādhyāya*, is seated in the hall before the assembly to bear witness. How do you see that there is no old monk on the seat?
You must not let this pass in indifference; otherwise, you will treat it as a trivial matter and be seen through day and night.
Hearing the wind that blows and stirs, one is bound by the faculties, objects, aggregates, elements, and sense bases, unable to attain freedom.

The matter of birth and death is great; one must find a point of entry through awakening before it can be resolved. Although this is so, those who transcend the ordinary bounds truly meet with strange laughter.
Why? You must know there is a further step beyond. Wait for another day or time, and I shall explain it separately for you.

The people pointed this out to him. He then recalled that in the past, the two venerable masters Nanquan and Zhaozhou were both men whose realization transcended the mundane world and whose fame spread throughout the realm.
At that time, there was a monk who went into the mountains and saw a Chan master sitting in a hermitage on a flat rock.
The monk asked him, "Nanquan has appeared in the world with such great renown; why do you not go to him?"
The monk inquired, "Why do you sit empty-handed? The hermitage master replied, "Do not speak of Nanquan appearing in the world;
even if a Buddha were to appear in the world, I would not go. When the monk took these words to Nanquan, Nanquan was greatly astonished. He then sent Zhaozhou to investigate and verify the matter.
Zhaozhou went to the abbot’s quarters; he walked from east to west, but the abbot paid him no heed. Zhaozhou then walked from west to east, yet the abbot still paid him no heed.
Zhaozhou finally stood directly in front of the door and said, "Abbot, you have lost! Even so, the abbot paid him no heed.
He then pulled down the curtain and walked away; the master of the hermitage likewise paid him no heed. "O Great Assembly, how do you understand this causal occasion?
Is it that Zhaozhou and Nanquan failed to reach the master’s domain, and were instead exposed by the master, falling into his 'trap for tigers'?
Or is it that although the master had no [intention to deceive], [he was nonetheless caught]?"
Regarding its application: if one does not understand how to adapt and exchange it according to the occasion, there is no difference between this and being a corpse on level ground.

Gentlemen, this is simply not the way. Generally speaking, a traveler on the path must have clear insight into the Way before they can succeed; if their insight into the Way is not clear, [they will fail].
"You have simply had your eyes changed by Nanquan, Zhaozhou, and the Hermitage Master—there is not even a trace of anything corresponding [to reality].
If your eye of the Way were clear, then Nanquan, Zhaozhou, and the Hermitage Master would be you;
there would be no difference whatsoever. Do you still grant this approval? Have you not heard it said: 'Having experienced the great ocean, one need no longer boast of water'?"
"Except for Mount Sumeru, everything else is but dust. [He stood for a long time.
Zen Master Dahuì Gǎo, having ascended from Tǔqiū to visit Yúnjū and preside over the whisk, said:
"In the past at Yímén, he displayed the family’s private flaws; he brought forth the boundless *lìjípéng* thorn. Today, atop the solitary peak of Òufēng, fortunately there is nothing to do."
Again we meet. Setting aside this meeting for a moment, what is the matter within it?
If there is anyone who can utter a single phrase, then please each return to the hall. If you cannot speak it, you will merely be weaving a web of complications to deceive all people.
Before the Buddhas appeared in the world, there was already this present "bar-nabi" (the essential core); it shines as a great jewel-light upon the crown of every person's head.
Since his passing into the world of transcendence, there has been no news at all. Under the feet of each and every one, the crossroads run both lengthwise and crosswise.
Where there is a Buddha, one may not dwell; where there is no Buddha, one must pass by in haste. When pressed, they cannot come; even from three thousand *li* away, their nostrils are pierced.
Reaching this point, even if you were to place the realms of infinite lands upon the tip of a single hair—this very hair alone.

From where does the head come? To place ten billion Mount Sumerus within a single grain of millet—where exactly is that single grain of millet placed? If it is thus, it is easy; if not thus, it is difficult.
Do not seek it in words; do not seek it in the mind. If it is thus, it is difficult; if not thus, it is easy. Recognize it!
The meaning of the hook’s tip: do not fixate on the zero point of the scale. When a monk picks up his staff, he walks away immediately;
one must by all means avoid driving a stake into level ground and rowing a boat there. Therefore it is said: "The divine light is never obscured; its glorious legacy endures for ten thousand ages.

Having entered this gate, do not harbor conceptual understanding. As for the entire Tripitaka, which speaks of the provisional and the real, the sudden and the gradual—[how can these be grasped through intellect?]
Whether speaking of existence or non-existence—even including the various words and diverse actions of all the patriarchs and masters of India and this land, from past to present—tell me:
are these intellectual understandings, or are they not?
If you can resolve this, the master of the whisk has suffered a total defeat; if you cannot resolve it, I shall pour on a second ladle of foul water.
(He lets out a shout and says: "What is it? There is illumination and function, but no facing or turning away.
It is permitted only for the Old Barbarian to know; it is not permitted for the Old Barbarian to understand. Muzhou always carried a single board; Zhaozhou buys high and sells low.
To sell [this teaching] alone—there is only this blind donkey of the Three Sages who has been subjected to the ridicule and strangeness of people until now.
Setting aside for a moment the fact that Mount Sumeru thrusts out from the corners of everyone’s foreheads and the great ocean waters pour into the nostrils of everyone, Master Mazu said:
"Since the time of the 'huluan' [the chaotic period], for thirty years there has never been a lack of salt and sauce.
How do you deliberate upon this? Do you understand it yet? No one asks about the calendar of many years; suddenly brought forth, it brings grief unto death. He let out a shout.

When Chan Master Tan-yi of Yuquan visited Master Dahui at Xiaoxi, Dahui ascended the seat for him.
