"Simply call it a 'cane' (*zhuzhangzi*). When walking, simply walk; when sitting, simply sit. You must not touch upon anything at all.

Huiyun said, "I am not like the old man Yunmen, who carves a hollow in empty space. He then suddenly picked up his cane and said, "This cane does not belong to existence, nor does it belong to non-existence;
it does not belong to illusion, nor does it belong to emptiness. He struck the ground once and said, "Ordinary people and those of the Two Vehicles..."
Pratyekabuddhas and Bodhisattvas all turn toward this very place, each according to their own capacity, and therein they all find its full utility.
Yet, within the domain of the monk, it acts as a destroyer and an adversary: when one wishes to walk, one cannot walk; when one wishes to sit, one cannot sit.
To take a single step forward, one is bewildered by the staff and loses the way; to retreat a single step, one has the nostrils pierced by the staff.
"Is there anyone here now who is not satisfied? Come forth and meet this staff!
If there is none, next year there will be new branches; the spring wind will continue to stir them without end. At such a time as this, what should be done?

[The Master] descends from his seat and requests the Elder of Yüquan to bring forth [the meaning] for the assembly. Having finished his expressions of gratitude upon ascending the seat, he then proceeds with the discourse.
The previous discourse said: "Just now, the Abbot’s critique was much like a weary fish confined to a pond or a sick bird perched on a reed.
At Yuquan, it is not so. [He] takes up his staff and says: "This staff can exist, can be non-existent, can manifest illusions, and can be empty.
Ordinary people, those of the two vehicles, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas—" [He] strikes once and says: "Right here!"
A hundred fragments scattered. Only within the realm of the patch-robed monk is it like a dragon finding water or a tiger relying on a mountain:
when he wishes to walk, he walks; when he wishes to sit, he sits. To take one step forward, heaven and earth tremble; to take one step back, the grass bows and the wind blows.
But tell me, how do you speak that phrase of neither advancing nor retreating? After a long silence, he said: "Holding a scripture in hand."
Leaning against a pine tree, he stood and asked with a smile, "Where have you guests come from?

When the letter of succession arrived, he took up the general principles of Master Huanglong Nan’s letter of succession to the Fourth Patriarch Changzhuo Yan and ascended the hall. The mountain monk’s talent is slight.
With such meager virtue, how could one be fit to be a teacher of men? It is simply that I have not been oblivious to my original mind and have not deceived the sages.
Where others had not yet escaped birth and death, I have now escaped birth and death; where others had not yet left the cycle of saṃsāra, I have now left the cycle of saṃsāra;

where others had not yet attained liberation, I have now attained liberation; where others had not yet attained self-mastery, I have now attained self-mastery. Therefore, when the Greatly Awakened World-Honored One was in the presence of Dīpaṃkara Buddha, he did not possess even a single...
"The Dharma can be attained. But what did the Sixth Patriarch transmit at Huangmei in the middle of the night? He then spoke this verse:
"Attained or not attained, transmitted or not transmitted— When one returns to the root and grasps the essential meaning, what more is there to say? I recall that at Xiangshan I once let it slip:
The daughter-in-law rides the donkey, while the mother-in-law leads."
The special messenger Wenxiang arrived from Master Duan of Dongshan bearing a letter of succession.
Before the Dharma seat, the Master received the letter and, holding it up, asked the messenger, "This is [the seal] of Sifan; where is yours, O *śrāmaṇera*?
The messenger replied, "It is being verified right before your eyes. The Master said, "I almost failed to question you on this point. He then ascended the seat and said, "A fine matter indeed!"
"Hard to encounter! Why do you not come forth so that we may all join in the song? He spoke again: "O Assembly! The Elder from the Four Directions has a letter;
before the assembly, it must be read aloud. "The great lacquer barrel from the Four Directions—Master Xiang divided it into two halves.
Under White Lotus Peak, it opened up and perfumed my nostrils. Tell me, why is it so? There is no place for you to breathe out."
A special messenger from Zifu Temple arrived bearing a letter of Dharma succession. The Master received the letter in the Dharma Hall and, picking it up, asked the messenger:
"It has no name; from where did you obtain this? The messenger hesitated. The Master said, "By whom was it brought here?
He then ascended the seat and cited the story of Shitou asking Changzi, "Where have you come from? Changzi replied, "From Lingnan."
Shitou said, "Has the work of merit at the head of Dayu Ridge been completed? Xishi replied, "It has been accomplished for a long time;
it only lacks the dotting of the eyes. Shitou asked, "Do you wish for the eyes to be dotted? Xishi said, "Please do so immediately.
Shitou lowered his foot, and Xishi prostrated himself. Shitou asked, "What principle have you perceived that you prostrate yourself?"

[The student] bows. Baizhang says, "A beard like a single speck of snow upon a red furnace. The Master says, "A single speck of snow on a red furnace—does the one who knows it perceive it instantly or not?
A fan made of tortoise hair fans a mud ox; a single drop of blood."
Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin ascends the hall upon the arrival of a letter from his dharma heir, Chi, of Dongshan in Xiazhou.

At the assembly on Vulture Peak, a thousand leaves spread their fragrance; at the peak of Shaoshi, a single branch stands alone in excellence. Even before the birth of Buddhas was conceived, its coiled roots were already visible.
On the other side of the kalpa of emptiness, patterns and colors manifest; the whole mass cannot be split apart. It strikes the nose even more fragrantly;

it is naturally resonant on all eight sides. The entire body turns dense and subtle. Setting aside for a moment the meeting of arrow-points and the fitting of needles and mustard seeds—how do you speak that single phrase of solitary liberation?
Suddenly wind and clouds meet; vast and open, heaven and earth are spring. He spoke again: "Sit."

Beholding the ancient wind of Mount Dongshan, the eye atop the head possesses complete efficacy. Wielding the Diamond Sword of Linji, one handles the thorny *liji* pomegranate of Yangqi with bold audacity.
Through iron walls and silver mountains, there must be active function; even within the demon palaces and tiger dens, the Dharma flows on.
Gathering the infinite lands of the fragrant waters, they are all cast together into the furnace and forge of the hammer.
Chan Master Tianmu Li’s Letter of Succession from Elder Cuiyan Zhen, presented upon ascending the hall:

By the side of the Hongya Well, within the precincts of Cuiyan Temple, the mountains hide half the moon and the river obstructs the slanting sun. This is neither the eye of the Buddhas nor the nostrils of the Patriarchs.
Addressing the special messenger, he said: "Do you understand? Return to Tengwang Pavilion, roll up the pearl curtains, and look."
Seizing the head of the Eighteen Rapids, the smoke and waves boil over.
When the letter of succession from Chan Master Yuyan and Elder Tong of Shanquan arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "Since the time of chaos..."
For thirty years, there has been no lack of salt and sauce. Only after the snowfall does one come to know the steadfast character of the pines and cypresses.
Let you be neither mind nor Buddha; I simply maintain that "mind is itself Buddha. It is only when faced with difficulty that the heart of a true man is revealed.
Some will say, "The news from Jiangxi has arrived," or "The plum on Damei has ripened. Such is indeed the skillful means of Shanguan. But as for this—
Shitou said: "The letter does not reach, and the message does not pass. How will you all explain this?
Even if you could speak it directly right now, the adze has not yet arrived with you."

When the letter from his Dharma relatives arrived, Chan Master Zhenjing Wen of Tiegang ascended the hall to express his gratitude for Huangbo’s prior dispatch, saying: "Branching out and forming lineages, we together propagate the ancestral tradition;
fully upholding the Patriarchal Command, each responds according to the occasion. Like the single rain of Huanglong, the withered tree flourishes once more. He continued: [He] succeeded...
The traces of the Ultimate Limit have been preserved; the true lamp flares up once more, its light illuminating those who have awakened before and advancing those who follow.
I cannot bear to contain my joy and celebration. I, [Name], am one of the unworthy; how could I have anticipated that the Venerable One would leave the Vulture Peak and enter deeply into Dongshan?

I have repeatedly dispatched letters to express my gratitude for the milk of the Dharma you have bestowed upon me; I am deeply moved by your constant kindness and my sense of indebtedness knows no end.
Again, he took up his staff and called to the assembly, saying: "Truly, it is said that though we were born from the same root, we shall not die from the same root.
A-la-la! How extraordinary! Calculatedly, we are both sons of men; when sleeping, we share the same bed, yet each dreams alone. Thus it has been from ancient times to the present.
This principle is known by few; it is known by few. Entrusted to Xianchi, may it be transmitted back to Vulture Peak.

I shall clearly present it to you, Master. From the letter of Chan Master Yulin to Chan Master Ruohan: "Upon receiving the letter, the single feather soars halfway to heaven, and my double brows are briefly relaxed.
Amidst the biting cold wind, I am glad to have received a letter from an old friend. "Great Assembly, tell me: what does the letter say?"
"What? He then descended from his seat.
When the letter of succession arrived, Master Fashi [Foyin Liaohui] delivered a formal address;
Master Wenyuan Qinquan, upon hearing the news of the Fifth Patriarch’s passing, ascended the hall and said: "At the head of Mount Dayu, laughter turned into weeping. Chong...
Why is it that weeping at the gate turns instead into laughter? It is because one drinks from the spring water to honor the vital earth-vein;
furthermore, one must ensure the true eye flows freely so that the ancestral wind does not fall. As it is said: "The laws of impermanence and birth-and-death have nothing to do with me.
If you can see in this way, there is no need to wail to the blue heavens. Since there is no need to wail to the blue heavens, how then shall we communicate the message? I ask the assembly.
[The Master] holds up the incense and says: "Two colors, one match. He descends from his seat.
Upon the arrival of the posthumous letter from Master Wuzu Yan regarding the passing of Zen Master Longmen Yuan, he ascends the hall and says:
"Yesterday was the twenty-sixth of the sixth month. The hornless iron ox has grown four feet. With a single roar, none yet know it— It shakes the very earth."

The heavenly gate and the earth’s axis [have shifted]; with but a single sandal, he has returned to the West. Having finished singing the song of the Hu family, how pitiable that his final words were so clear!
His boundless pure voice resounded throughout the valleys and streams. My late master was active in the world for over forty years;

in the two prefectures of Shu and Jin, he presided over four great monasteries. Bestowing compassion and speaking with earnest urgency, he attended to beings and benefited living things without a moment’s leisure. At...
On the morning of the twenty-fifth, he ascended the seat to address the assembly. By evening, he had shaved his head and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
On the morning of the twenty-sixth, he passed away peacefully. From beginning to end, from first to last, his conduct was perfect and complete; he was a true spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*).
I, Qingyuan, having been the recipient of his guidance and instruction, find my grief immeasurable. As the ancients said: "Offer this profound mind to the dust..."
This is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness. Formerly, when Dàmé was about to pass away, he ascended the hall and, upon hearing the cry of a flying squirrel, said:
"It is this very thing; it is not another thing. You must preserve and uphold it well; I am now about to depart. My former teacher also ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying:
"The wealthy lament that a thousand mouths are too few; the poor regret that a single body is too many. Comparing the present with the past, there is not even a hair’s breadth of difference.
There is no difference. Do you all know where the two old masters, Damei and Dongshan, have gone?

If you can know this, you will not have disgraced your former teacher. If you do not yet know, there are cold and heat that shorten one’s lifespan, and there are ghosts and spirits that envy one’s fortune.
[Descend from the seat.]
Upon the arrival of the late Master’s testamentary letter, the assembly raised their voices in mourning and offered incense.
Regarding the Dharma words for the raising of mourning and the offering of incense by Chan Master Dahui Zonggao for Master Yuanwu, he pointed to the portrait and said:
"This old master spent his life with too much talk, causing turmoil within the monastic community. I have recently heard that he has already passed away in Shu. Moreover—"
I rejoice in the peace of the world. Although Yunmen approached him in years past, he never once heard that fellow utter so much as a single word of the Dharma.
Therefore, today I have prepared this offering, poured out this cup of tea, and burned this stick of incense to perfume his nostrils.
This is not to repay his virtue or requite his kindness; it is simply to humiliate him. [He] summons Da...

The assembly said: "Since you have not heard him utter even a single word of the fundamental principle (*yuan*), and there is no kindness or virtue for which you can repay him, why have you made yourself such a laughingstock out of thin air?
Do you understand? An offense has its source, and a debt has its owner. It was merely by chance that he tripped and fell;
yet to this day, his resentment runs deep into the marrow of his bones. Thereupon, he burned incense.
Chan Master Hongluo of Huqiu expressed his grief for Master Yuanwu, saying: "Śākyamuni has already passed away and Maitreya has not yet been born;
it falls precisely upon this day that the transmission of the true pulse of the Buddhas and Patriarchs rests entirely upon our Great Monk, Chan Master Yuanwu.

He has truly attained the seven seals of authority over the precious monasteries, taking the three realms as his home; his fame spreads across the four seas, acting as a refuge for all living beings."

The eyes of the world lament that the Dharma banner has been toppled and the Buddha-sun has obscured its light; those who have come after have nothing to hear from, and the monastic groves have lost their refuge.

Nevertheless, even so, all such concerns fall within the realm of the present moment. Why? Have you not heard it said: "The body of the Pure Dharma-realm fundamentally neither appears nor disappears"?
Since there is no appearing or disappearing, the Master does not die now; why should I harbor any doubt? O Great Assembly, since this is so...
He has passed away. Do you know where Old Man Yuangwu has gone? If you can discern his destination, there is no need for further instruction.
If this is not yet the case, then look up to the Master’s Way, which shall endure as long as earth and heaven; please, before the image, let us all burn incense together.
Again, pointing to the True [Self], he said: "Do you see? At the outskirts of the city of Kuśinagara, a great event was once enacted;
now, at the head of the River of Washed Brocade, he follows the old tracks once more, emitting light and manifesting auspicious signs to gather and transform beings as he returns to the Truth.

Though the pearl of the Dharma has sunk and the Eye of Humans and Gods has been extinguished—even so, within suchness there is that which is not suchness; within that which is not suchness, there is yet suchness."
Thus, within the state where there is neither birth nor death, he manifests birth and death; within the state where there is neither coming nor going, he manifests coming and going.
Nevertheless, fundamentally, there are no marks of birth, death, coming, or going. Therefore, our Great Master Yuanwu Chanshi’s river of Chan is vast and profound, its ferrying across boundless;
his fame moved the Sovereign and his Way filled the world. Moreover, his great task was already complete.
With his single sandal, he returned to the West, sitting steadily in the hall of his home. As for the final word—how do you speak it?
If you can speak it here, the Elder Yuanwu is still present. If not, I shall speak it for you all.
After a long silence, he looked back at his attendant and asked, "What did you say?

He then raised his voice in mourning: "The letter from Chan Master Wu’an Jizhao has arrived; we raise our voices in mourning and offer incense. The fifth transmission of Miaoxi is the most radiant flame;
Jizhao is the dewy gate of an entire era. To casually touch this is to have one’s liver and brain split open; ice and frost suddenly—"
It creates a springtime warmth. I think back to the day my nostrils were lost; what kind of breath remains even now?
The celestial wind blows from the north as the year draws to a close; why seek traces in the void with a flash of lightning?
Upon receiving the news of the passing of Chan Master Xushan Xing and Master Quanshi, I raised my voice in mourning and offered incense.
When the sons of heaven in the thirty-three heavens die, they all feel grief; when the people of Uttarakuru in the north die, they all raise cries of joy.
To have both grief and joy is entirely a matter of attachment and aversion. For a monk’s coming and going, it is like fire burning through ice—do you know where the former master has entered?
From what kind of practice does one emerge from the prison? When there is equality, there is the Path. Today is not extinguished; yesterday was not born.
But tell me, how does Shushan’s wayward son repay his filial debt? [He] beats his breast with his hand and says: "Pāpīyān rests; the world is at peace."
Again, they raised their voices in lamentation, crying, "Heaven! Heaven!
A letter from his parents arrived at the Tiangang Heze Chan Master’s assembly.
One day, a message from his hometown arrived reporting that his parents had passed away. The Master ascended the hall and struck the wooden mallet himself.

He said, "Both my parents have passed away; I request that the assembly recite the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra. Just as the assembly had gathered, the Master struck the mallet again and said, "I trouble the assembly with this request."

Upon returning to visit his preceptor and receive his formal ordination, Guling praised Chan Master [Tianhuang] Daowu. When the Master returned from visiting Baizhang, his preceptor gathered the assembly and requested him to ascend the seat.

The Master cited Baizhang’s instruction to the assembly, saying: "The numinous light shines alone, utterly transcending the sense bases and their objects; its essence reveals true permanence, unconstrained by words."
"Your very nature is undefiled and fundamentally perfected from the beginning. Simply by detaching from delusive conditions, you are the Buddha of Suchness.
Upon hearing these words, the master of his studies attained realization.
Later, when Chan Master Dahui Gaofeng returned to his home monastery, the assembly requested him to give a small lecture (*xiaocan*). "When I was a young boy," the mountain monk said, "once—"
Reflecting on this, I know that leaving the household life is excellent; it was for this reason that I shed my white robes at this monastery. Today I have returned to be called an Elder.

After the turmoil of war, those who perished were many, yet the venerable seniors present here rejoice in being free from affliction. By honoring the superior and humbling oneself before the inferior, one departs from the notions of self and other.
All together, I entreat you to proclaim the Unsurpassed Way. Those born later should rouse a heart of fierce vigor; they should seek a teacher throughout the four seas.
"Pushing through the grass"—Jingshan’s words of exhortation were not in vain. To discern the mouth of Vimalakīrti, one must rely on a complete overturning.
Chan Master Xing of Shushan returned to Hongxi in Liyang; at the request of the assembly of his former preceptor, he ascended the hall and struck his whisk, saying:
Furthermore, is there anyone who can discern the thickness of the late master’s skin? Since there is none, let us watch as this mountain monk pursues the wind and captures the shadow.
My native place is Nanxu, Jintan County; I received my training at Danyang Dashi Monastery.
Originally, I was a man of no affairs, yet I stubbornly sought to study Chan and attain right view. In my youth, I traveled on foot to Tianmu, where I met Shizi...
Having personally encountered poison before the crags, he traveled through all quarters and then returned home. He declared that his lifelong aspirations were fulfilled;
he dwelt high in a hermitage at the mouth of Hong Creek. Braving snow and frost for many years, he cultivated fields to earn his food, emulating the style of the ancients.
From beginning to end, never falling behind others; for fifty years, he has waited by the stump for the hare.
Carrying a single plank, he lacks the affinity of men; meeting on a narrow path, Li Bai-ba appears. Buying a hat to fit the head is an old-world grievance. At eighty-six, his worldly ties have ended;
east surging and west sinking, he rests in the *nāga-samādhi*. Who can evaluate this one phrase that stands before us? He sits, cutting off heaven and earth.
There is not the slightest remainder. Contemplating and understanding, one smiles but does not weep. When the string snaps, who can join it with *luangiao* glue?
Amidst the thicket of thorns, he reveals the essential ford; beneath the shadowless tree, he chants the wind-song. How could this compare to the self-awakened ones of quiescent extinction?
One must surely take up the true lamp to illuminate the deep darkness. May you return once more to the boundless sea of suffering and re-settled the old public case of Zhongfeng. Restore!
Nanquan once raised this story: while serving a meal for Mazu, he asked the assembly, "If you say that our late teacher has come today, what proof do you have?
If you say he has not come, then the Buddha-dharma lacks efficacy. At that moment, Dongshan, who was among those present, stepped forward and said, "He comes when he has a companion.
Nanquan said, "I am not asking about the ancients; tell me, has our late teacher come today or not?"
[The Master] approached. After a long silence, he spoke on his own behalf: "When I first met Xushan as a mere child. He then looked toward the assembly and asked, "Do you understand?
He raised his staff, struck the incense table, gave a shout, and said, "The former master has arrived! Thereupon, he descended from the seat.

The Dharma Words for Accepting the Invitation and Ascending the Seat to Present the Robe, by Chan Master Yangqi Huai.
Upon receiving the invitation from Jiufeng, he presented the robe to the assembly, saying: "Do you understand? If you do not yet understand..."
Today, without cause, you have wandered into the herd of water buffalo. Do you know? At Juyang Jiuchu, Pingshi, and Yangqi, Chan Master Yong of Baoning received the minor ordination at Jiangshan.
When a monk presented him with his dharma robe, the Master held it up upon his body.
Kāśyapa said: "Great assembly, tell me: which one is this, and which one is that? If you say this one is it, what can you do about that one?
If you say that one is it, what can you do about this one? He then looked at the assembly and said:
"Now, there is no choice but to change my head and face before this great assembly; I shall cast off one and take up another. Thereupon, he removed his *kāṣāya* and donned [the other].
Regarding the Dharma robe:
Zen Master Wuzu Fayan received a certificate from Baiyun. Holding up the Dharma robe, he said:
"Since it could not be lifted at the head of Mount Dayu, why is it here? Tell me, which one is 'here' and which one is 'there'? Thereupon—
He said: "Carrying the water jar, he draws cool, clear water; then, donning the *kāṣāya*, he acts as host. He then threw on his robe.
Zen Master Yuanwu Qin, having been invited by Zhaojue, held up the Dharma robe and said: "The ancients had no choice but to hang their worn and soiled robes.
Now, unable to decline the invitation, they enter in a great throng. At the head of Dayu Ridge, they hide.
It is not permitted. Nevertheless, I must let everyone know.
On the day Chan Master Taiping Qin was invited [to the abbacy], Wuzu presented him with the Dharma robe. The Master received it, held it up to show the assembly, and said:
"In the past, Śākyamuni Buddha draped his sixteen-foot golden cassock over the body of the thousand-foot Maitreya Buddha."
The Buddha’s body is not long, and the *kāṣāya* robe is not short. Do you understand? It is this very pattern;
there is no other pattern.
[This refers to] Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin receiving the imperial decree at Jiangshan. Holding it up, he showed it to the assembly, saying: "Great assembly, do you see? The Dragon..."

The flying phoenix dances as it descends from the ninefold heavens; the fundamental principles of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are all contained herein. Now, please request the Rector to proclaim this to the assembly.
While residing at Mount Jinshan, the Master received an imperial edict at Qianming Temple. Holding it up to show the assembly, he said: "Do you see it? When it was held up, ten days [passed]."
Shining universally, its brilliance illuminates the thousand worlds; descended from the heavens of the Nine Palaces, it was personally entrusted into the hands of the Prime Minister.
I dare not conceal or cover it away, but request that the Vinaya Master Daeil (Sengjeong-i) proclaim it for us.

When the Master residing at Yunju received his official appointment at Jinshan, the imperial edict was issued the following day. Holding up the edict, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Personally bestowed within the nine-layered capital;
a single ray of divine light illuminates the great void. Within the ultimate truth (paramārtha-satya), it is the true ultimate truth;
amidst a cluster of a thousand petals, a lotus blossoms. To understand this in a single stroke—how much effort is saved! If you have not yet reached this realization, please listen further."
[The Master] proclaimed his transgressions.
Chan Master Dahuì Gǎo returned to reside at Jìngshān and subsequently accepted an invitation to Yùwáng Monastery. Holding up the imperial decree (*chìhuáng*), he addressed the assembly, saying:
"Bodhidharma did not come to the Eastern Land, and the Second Patriarch did not go to the Western Heaven. The constant radiance is ever-present for every person; each and every one..."
"Standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. Now tell me, from where did this come? If you know its source, its enjoyment will be inexhaustible.
If not yet so, then please, Venerable Karmadāna, announce it clearly so that everyone may know it exists.

Chan Master Chang’eng Jing was commanded by imperial decree to ascend and reside at Tiantong. Holding up the imperial edict, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The clouds part to reveal the nine heavens.
Raising it up, he said: "Behold! A magnificent phoenix brings it forth. Now tell me, how do you understand this? 'Swift as a divine command.'"
Imperial Decree:
Chan Master Mimang Jie is appointed to reside at Mount Jing. Having received the invitation at Huazang Monastery, the Master held up the imperial decree and addressed the assembly, saying:

"The Phoenix Palace has issued its proclamation; all living beings prick up their ears. As it is now brought forth in the presence of all, it reaches across the earth and fills the heavens, calling back the withered wood."
The Dragon’s Roar: This is a distinct springtime in a single jar. If you can perceive it, the imperial grace and the Buddha’s grace will both be repaid at once.
Should this not yet be so, we request that the Rector clearly proclaim it.
While residing at Lingyin, the Master was invited to Mount Jing. Holding up the imperial decree (*chihuang*), he addressed the assembly, saying:
"Descended from the Ninefold Heavens above, it is brought forth before the Hall of Good Dharma. It is as clear as the bright sun and as vast as the great void.

It gloriously upholds the ancestral style of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and transmits the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye. If you can see it thus, you are worthy to repay the unrepayable debt of gratitude. If you have not yet..."
Nevertheless, the Rector clearly exposed the truth.

Taking up the Dharma discourse on the *Hufa shu* (Commentary on Protecting the Dharma) bestowed by Wuzu Yan Chan Master at Shimian Mountain, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The army follows the seal; the general pursues the talisman."
[The Master] proceeded. "Please, Your Honor, explain this clearly.

Residing at Dongshan, the Master accepted the invitation at Haihui Monastery; picking up the ceremonial document (shu), he showed it to the assembly and said, "An eighty-year-old old man rolling an embroidered ball," and then he handed it to the Rector (Weina).

After Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin took up residence at Jinshan and received the imperial edict, he next held up the ceremonial document (shu) and said: "The jeweled temple upon the tip of a hair is the sovereign authority beyond the pass;
it has its rolling up and unfolding, its illumination and its function. Every character rolls like a pearl and turns like jade;
each stroke obeys like grass bowing to the wind. Although the literary brilliance is already manifest, I ask you all to please pick it up and present it anew."
Chan Master Ying’an Hua was invited by Miaoyan to preside over the ceremony. The Left Vice Director of the Provincial Administration Office presented a memorial.
The Master held it up and addressed the assembly, saying: "This is the Left Vice Director’s gift with both hands; it is called the 'Inexhaustible Treasury' and the 'Crown King Samādhi.
Every word reveals the ultimate truth, and every phrase flows toward the source. If you can understand this, there is no need for me to further recite verses. But if you have not yet..."
"Understood. Please trouble the monastic officials to read this proclamation before the assembly.
Chan Master Miam Jie accepted the invitation and, holding up the document, said:

"Where the Buddhas have failed to reach in their teachings, and where the Patriarchs have been unable to lift it up—this samādhi of language, with its interlaced patterns and knots, flows forth entirely from within this very place, its brilliance illuminating both past and present."
It does not fall into the extremes of nihilism or eternalism; it is intended for the fourfold assembly to know together. What harm is there in explaining its refutation again? The commentary states:
Two thousand years ago, at the assembly on Vulture Peak, the "Yellow-Faced Old Man" entrusted a single phrase to kings and great ministers.
It has been disseminated throughout heaven and earth, continuing without interruption. Those with eyes see it; those with ears hear it.
Having heard this, once hearing and seeing have both been opened up, you must plug your ears and listen even more attentively.
This is the donor’s preface for Chan Master Yuansou Duan: "Atop a solitary peak, heaven knows not and earth cares not;
why then has he been enticed out by this? For incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*) in the past, he has practiced together with the eminent talents of the entire district."
The unsurpassed fruit of Buddhahood and Bodhi.
Residing at Fengshan, he accepted an invitation at the Laṅkā Hall of Mount Jing to present the temple’s formal petition.

This was personally entrusted to him by the various officials of the Xuanzheng Yuan; it is called the "Vajra Secret Samādhi. By means of this, demons and heretics are eradicated, and the True Lineage is upheld.
By means of this, it is made radiant and manifest.
Master Nian’s Postscript on Dharma Words:

He could not be pulled out in the past, yet now he has been pulled out. He did not dwell in the monastery in the past, yet now he dwells there.

He detested being a Buddha in the past, yet now he acts as one. He detested preaching the Dharma in the past, yet now he preaches it. Setting aside for a moment whether he was pulled out or not, and whether he dwelt or not, I ask you all:
what kind of Buddha is it that he acts as? Is it Śūnyarāja Buddha? Or is it Dīpaṃkara Buddha?
"Is it Śākyamuni Buddha? Is it Maitreya Buddha? What kind of Dharma are you expounding? Is it the fundamental Dharma?
Is it the Dharma of non-arising? Is it a worldly dharma? Or is it a world-transcending dharma? Is there anyone in this assembly who has attained the Way?"
"If you can speak thus, this mountain monk’s work in appearing in the world is finished. If it is otherwise, do not misrepresent [the teaching] when meeting people.
He gave a shout and descended from his seat.
On the day Master De Shan Qiong accepted an invitation, he ascended the hall and said: "The master craftsman casts his net, yet they refuse to stay; though called and summoned..."
Turning back. Why? From east to west. [The Master] spoke on his own behalf, saying: "Look after five days.
On the day Chan Master Tian Tong Jiao was invited to ascend the hall, he said: "Alas! The Yellow-Faced Old One entrusted the Buddha-dharma to kings and ministers."
"A mindless guest beneath the forest trees is being driven to his death by an official's summons. Is there anyone who knows the bottom of my heart who can save me from this?
If not, I shall simply take what is wrong and make it right. Thereupon, he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Baoshou De was invited to Nanhua during the winter. He addressed the assembly, saying: "In the new winter, there is the new Baoshou;
yet what he says is the same as his words from the past. If you would understand the meaning of the Westward Journey, it is like a Persian boarding a ship."
When the State Censor Liu Zhonggu held the governorship of Changsha, he sought to establish the Dharma wheel by inviting Master Zhong of Muan from the general consensus of the assembly.
The Master shook his head and paid no heed. The Governor further intended to welcome him by vacating the seat at Shengye Monastery and issued a formal summons to all Chan masters to entreat him.
Upon hearing this, the Master fled under the cover of night. The Governor pursued him to the Dingming Hermitage, where he beat the drum in the hall and extended his invitation.

The Master sat upon his seat; monks and laypeople prostrated themselves before him for more than an hour without ceasing. The Master sighed deeply and spoke this verse: "Alas, you yellow-faced old man!
You entrust the Dharma to kings and ministers. I am but a mindless guest beneath the forest trees, Yet official summons drive me to my death.
In the past I heard these words; today I see these deeds. Having said this, he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Zhuo’an was invited by Jinshan Longyou Chan Temple to ascend the seat at Zhulin.

With the first proclamation of the Dharma-treasury, the Three Baskets cease their explanations; from antiquity to the present, the mallet does not move. As the wind blows, the grass bows; as the water flows, the channel forms.

This is the natural unfolding of time, season, and conditions, wherein every eye beholds the full manifestation of supreme excellence—simultaneously killing, simultaneously enlivening, and simultaneously granting freedom.
They are identical in their seizing, identical in their illumination, identical in their function, identical in their host, and identical in their guest.

They uphold the sublime Way that points upward and together display the "barb-nose" (the vital core) of the monk. When there is spirit, they add to that spirit; it cannot be increased by even a fraction.

Where there is no elegance, they are elegant nonetheless; it cannot be diminished by even a fraction. Where increase is impossible, they diminish by a fraction; where diminution is impossible, they increase by a fraction.
One immediately perceives the practice of the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma; the banner of the Dharma is established wherever one stands.

It is like a blind turtle encountering a floating log, or like a fragrant elephant crossing a river—where the waves reach the heavens, its entire body emerges and submerges; it cuts through the current, passing over according to the depth or shallowness as appropriate.

At the heart of the Yangtze River, the transformative sun rises; atop the peak of Mount Miaogao, the needle and awl are revealed. How could there ever have been even the slightest need for external seeking? It resides only here.
Advancing further on the tip of the staff. At this very moment, when the soldier follows the seal and the general pursues the talisman, and rhythm and beat support one another—how do you speak of it?
When the nine-myriad-li Peng bird first spreads its wings, the three-thousand-year-old crane immediately soars aloft.

Furthermore, a verse says: The wind through the bamboo in the courtyard cannot be kept out; A single long note from the flute reaches the river. Vastly expanding the legacy of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
The decree before the pivot: leaning toward the right, one travels amidst surging waves.
Having received the invitation from Louze, the Master accepted the document and said: "Before a single word is uttered, the wind is the same across a thousand miles.
If you wish to add flowers to brocade, you must clearly reveal it before this assembly of devas and humans. Great assembly, do you understand? No.

One might say that the army follows the turning of the seal and the general proceeds according to the talisman; yet one cannot say that as soon as power is in one's hand, all commands are immediately executed.
You must know that there is a "transcendental aperture" above this before you can succeed. But what is this transcendental aperture?
In the past, on Vulture Peak Mountain, [the Buddha] personally transmitted it to Kāśyapa, as well as to kings, princes, ministers, and the multitude.
We entreat you to propagate and protect [this teaching], transmitting it to future generations so that it shall not be severed.

We, the Great Minister Qi Weng, lay devotee, together with the great Dharma-protectors, the dignitaries of the current administration, and the gentry of the entire prefecture, submit this joint memorial.

By reopening this ancient temple and establishing a site for the Way, how does this single assembly differ from Vulture Peak? Since there is no distinction between the present and the past, it follows that...
The sound is harmonious and the resonance follows; on the peaks of a thousand mountains he raises compassion, yet this does not hinder him from extending his hand at the crossroads.
Extending his hand at the crossroads, one must see him raising compassion on the peaks of a thousand mountains. "Is it truly so, great assembly? He then raised his whisk and said:
"A crane may have its wings, yet it is hard to soar to the nine heavens; a horse may lack the thousand-mile stride, yet it vainly pursues the wind. Having stood for long, take care.
Having again accepted the invitation,
Chan Master Yong of Baoning received the Baoning notice and ascended the hall. He clapped his hands three times, pointed to his mouth, shook his hand three times,
and then descended from the seat.
Chan Master Dahuigao ascends the seat once again at Yuyang Monastery by imperial decree from Mount Jing: Before the Hall of Good Dharma, auspicious vapors arise anew;
An imperial edict has arrived from the nine-layered capital. Relying solely on these words of impartiality, I offer my highest prayers for the Emperor’s ten thousand million springs.

On the evening of his formal reception, Chan Master Zhenjing Wen gave a small-scale sermon (xiaocan) on the essential principles of the teaching. He said: "The ancient caves of Xin'feng are crowded by ten thousand layers of peaks;
the true source of awakening is thronged by a thousand forests. This is a preeminent site throughout antiquity and the present, where Buddhist activities have always flourished. Therefore..."
In the past, Great Master Wuben once proclaimed: "There is only the Buddha-bodhi; this is the true place of reliance.
He then let out a shout and said: "There is still this 'going' and 'staying'! "Virtuous ones," [he asked], "just as the Great Master said..."
It is like this: the very act of going is the very place of being. But tell me, what is the meaning? Do you know where it lands?

There are many in the monastic communities who speculate on this. Some say that hearing the Buddha or hearing the Dharma is like encountering an enemy; how much more so when there is still something to rely upon?
For this reason, they were scrutinized by Master Wuben. Others say that Wuben simply wants people to stop.
"Cease! Some say that Wuben saw only the sharpness of the chisel’s tip and did not see the squareness of the chisel’s handle.
To match it in such a way—how could he have even dreamed of those ancients? Since it is not like this, then how is it? O Virtuous Ones!"
This matter requires great care and attention; one must not be coarse-minded.

Whether it be Chan meditation or the exhaustive study of the teachings, the various schools of the Zen tradition differ in a thousand ways and follow diverse paths of concealment and manifestation. Only those of great wisdom can clarify them.
Beyond this point, their depths are unfathomable. Nowadays, most people merely hold onto a child who does not cry or beat a clean ball, letting out the anchor.
A boatman embraced the bridge pillar to bathe; who among us men has not had their share of such moments?

If one were to depart with clear understanding, it would be like driving away the oxen of a plowman or snatching food from a starving person. Entering fire, one is not burned; entering water, one is not drowned.

Remaining nowhere yet present in all places—whether manifesting as the solitary brilliance of the numinous light, shining forth with extraordinary distinction—it may truly be called vast and boundless.
Vast and expansive! Unfurling sails to reach the shore, he maneuvers the boat that ferries beings across.
Amidst the white-capped waves within the sea of birth and death, he appears and disappears, coming and going with ease and freedom. Then he roars: "Let them slander me; let them criticize me.
With my bamboo hat and raincoat, I now take leave for a moment of the moon at Haimen Port; carrying my fish, I shall return to the marketplace."
Descend from your seats. Zen Master Wuzu Yan accepted an invitation to Dongshan. That evening, he gave a small discourse (xiaochan): "One phrase leads to three; three phrases lead to seven.
A *jujube* tree by the banks of the sheep-pasture embankment; a 'Wangfu' (Waiting-for-Husband) rock by the Juema River. Striking the gavel with a stone; drawing a winnowing fan with red earth."
Ji: "Let the Eye-instruction fold over delusion. He further said: "Thirty years in the Huai fields; now I am an old Huangmei.
The good matter is clearly explained; let the ducks listen to the thunder."
Chan Master Mingjue Xian accepted the invitation from Xuedou. That evening, he gave a small-scale sermon (xiaocan), saying: "O worthy ones!

There has never been one who acts constantly without abiding, nor one who abides constantly without acting. Whether in antiquity or today, each has their own destination. Furthermore, this monastery is situated in a remote corner;
were it not for the thought of repaying the Buddha’s kindness, there would be no reason for those from the four quarters to dwell here. I fear that the mountain..."
Since Master Sengjin has departed, the Dharma seat has been left vacant. We now appoint the Bodhisattva Master Sugu to succeed him as abbot.
We hope that the assembly will show compassion and join together in exhorting him to accept this invitation.
On the evening of his arrival at Jinshan Longyou, as he was receiving the imperial decree to reside there, Chan Master Yuanwu gave a small-scale sermon (xiaocan).
"The Patriarchal Heart-Seal is like the mechanism of an iron ox; the secret words of the Buddhas are just like a poison-coated drum.

Before you can even conceive of a conjecture, you have already missed the mark; the moment you begin to deliberate, you are separated by a thousand mountains. You must have eyes like shooting stars and a mind..."
It is like iron and stone. Thus, from of old, the guiding principles that uphold the upward-tending纲 (gāngzōng) have consisted of only three phrases:
sometimes they bite off; sometimes they bite and hold fast; sometimes they do not go at all; and sometimes they do not stay at all. For those with clear eyes, there is no fixed nest or trap.
If one speaks of battle, everyone’s strength lies in the point of turning; yet taking things as the object is superior to pursuing things.
This is for those of lesser capacity. One must first decisively sever the path of both the ordinary and the sage so that not even a hair’s breadth remains.

Only then can one raise a single hair and exhaustively encompass the boundless seas of fragrant water, reaching everywhere through the seven paths and eight openings; speaking a single phrase, it reaches the depths of the dragon palaces and fills the treasuries of the ocean.
This is still merely talk of ultimate principles; it is not yet the "bar-nabi" (the core essence) of a patch-robed monk.

If one speaks of the actual utilization of a patch-robed monk, even if they strike like raindrops falling and shout like thunder crashing—ranking all the sages beneath their wind and standing atop the crown of Vairocana;
even with the spark struck from flint and the flash of lightning, swift hawks and eagles cannot catch up to them. One must, however, correctly realize all-knowing wisdom.
Upon seeing this, one realizes great liberation; there is nothing that is not distinct and nothing that is not penetratingly free.

Thus, in heaven one is the same as heaven, on earth one is the same as earth, with things one is the same as things, and with the self one is the same as the self. One realizes all-knowledge and clarifies all paths;
there is nowhere it does not accommodate, and no capacity for which it is not perfectly realized. At this very moment, each of you should reflect back upon yourselves.
In its fundamental nature, has there ever been a shift of even a single hair’s breadth? This is what is called the perfect integration of ten ages and the full realization of the ten aspects.
Now tell me: how do you express that single phrase which does not fall within the realm of causal conditions? To meet face-to-face, one must require the true eye of the school;
when the occasion arises, one must cut off the tracks of both sage and ordinary.

Taking his leave of the assembly, Chan Master Baiyun Da'an ascended the hall at the invitation of Fahua. He said: "The Buddha-body fills the Dharma-realm, universally manifesting before all sentient beings.
Responding to conditions and meeting with stimuli, there is nowhere it does not reach; yet it eternally abides within this Bodhi."
"Assembly, how do you explain the principle of responding to conditions and manifesting according to needs?

In the mere space of a single snap of the fingers, the capacities and roots of all sentient beings throughout the entire world may be fully and simultaneously responded to, yet without ever moving so much as a hair’s breadth.
This is precisely what is called 'responding to conditions and manifesting according to needs while always remaining in this seat. It is just like this monk here—"

This person accepted the invitation for the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* assembly. In succession, he took his leave of the great assembly; only after going to the interior of Susong County and opening the hall did he return to the monastery.
Now tell me: did he depart from this seat or not? If you say he departed, then you are merely propagating worldly conventions.

If the Way is not separate, how can you see that which is not separate? Is it that "the realms of boundless lands are not separated from one another by so much as a hair’s tip, and the ten ages of past and present do not depart from this very moment"?
Or is it that "all things, being without mind, are simultaneously and spontaneously pervasive"? If it were like that, you would be no different from striking at the moon with a swinging staff.
Upon reaching this point, you must awaken; only then will it be attained. After awakening, you must further encounter a person; only then will it be attained.
You say that once one has awakened, one simply stops—why then would one need to encounter a person?

If one who has awakened encounters a person, then at the time of extending a hand in skillful means (*upāya*), there shall naturally be a path for emergence at every turn, not blinding the eyes of the student. If one merely awakens...
Those who obtain only the dried radish head not only blind the eyes of students, but moreover, as soon as they move, they first strike their own blades and wound their hands.
Look at how my late master Yangqi asked the venerable teacher Ciming:
"When the dark birds warble and chatter, leaving the clouds to enter the chaotic peaks—what is this? He replied: "I walk amidst the wild weeds; you, however, have entered..."
"In a deep village. Jìn said, "The official does not allow even a needle to pass; let me ask one more question. The Master struck him with a shout.
Jìn said, "A fine shout! The Master shouted again. The former Master also shouted. The Master then followed suit and shouted twice in succession. Thereupon, the former Master bowed.
"Great assembly, you must know that one who has attained awakening meets people at the crossroads of the street, yet holds hands atop a thousand peaks;
one meets people atop a thousand peaks, yet holds hands at the crossroads of the street.
Therefore, I, this mountain monk, have often composed a verse: 'Where others dwell, I do not dwell; where others walk..."
"I shall not go. It is not that I find it difficult to dwell together with others; rather, it is simply that the monastic and the lay must be clearly distinguished.
As this mountain monk departs now, I have untied the mouth of my sack and scattered its contents all at once before you.
Those with eyes, do not mistake me for anything else. Take care."
Chan Master Zhenjing Wen was at Jiufeng in Junzhou when he accepted the invitation from Guizong. At the evening assembly, he ascended the hall to take his leave of the congregation.
Holding up his whisk, he said: "In the past, when the World-Honored One held up a flower, Kāśyapa smiled.
Tonight, as Guizong holds up this whisk, the great assembly is silent. Is it this silence that is the smile? Or what else is it?"

Consider this: Is Guizong’s raising of the whisk the same as the World-Honored One’s holding up the flower, or is it different? If you say they are the same, there is no such thing as a "sameness" among dharmas.
If you say they are different, how could there be two distinct things? Those who have long studied under the former masters understand immediately upon hearing them mentioned;

however, those of later generations and beginners must examine this closely. After a long silence, he said: "Every dharma returns to the source; when facing the situation, one must adapt with skillful means. This is the Lingyuan (Spiritual Source).
The Master Mingjue Xian, who is the impartial master of this wondrous place, took his leave of Cui Feng while ascending the hall.
This mountain monk, having suppressed my own inclinations to comply with his request, finds it difficult to linger longer;

I have packed my belongings and am announcing my departure, feeling nothing but deep attachment and gratitude. Furthermore, during my long stay, I have greatly troubled the veteran monks and fully recognized the passage of the years.

It is cold. I hope each of you will strive diligently in the Way to repay my sincere prayers. Among those who have followed these noble gentlemen, some have traveled over a thousand li and others have come from as near as a hundred *li*.

Should you suddenly find yourselves short of rice gruel or provisions, or if your boats and carts prove too cramped, I hope you will yield to one another so that you may find sustenance through the joy of meditation (*dhyāna-prīti*).

If you can thus provide for yourselves, then traveling throughout the Buddha-lands will not be considered far. Why is this? O virtuous practitioners of meditation, your coming and going are not constrained by—
Because they are like phantoms, there is no vessel that does not take form; because movement and stillness do not depend on the mind, there is no stimulus that is not answered.
Thus, the mind arises from having a mind, and phantoms emerge from having forms. Since these phantoms do not emerge from me, metal and stone may be melted without being scorched;
since these forms do not arise from me, they are used daily without weariness. The profusion of phenomena comes from elsewhere—what can it do for me? Please [understand this].
"May all you gentlemen hoist your sails and depart; I cannot bear to part with you.
Chan Master Yuansou Duan accepted an invitation from Zhongtianzhi Temple in the Hangzhou Prefecture. Taking his leave of the assembly, he ascended the hall and said:
'In my past years at Mount Yufquan, for four years and eight months, I beat the drum and played with the monkeys, never knowing rest by day or night. [The Emperor] bestowed an imperial edict.
The public way has opened; those with clear wisdom have been assigned their stations. Calamities are remedied and greed eliminated; the worthy and the heroic are sought and selected.
Why, then, at the Peak of India, was this entrusted to one so dull and clumsy? An official was dispatched to force a man to death, allowing no further explanation.
Packing my bundle, I set out on the road ahead to part from the multitude for a while. A thousand-year-old Chan rock leaps up into the sky; in the sixth month, the fire-clouds fly.
Auspicious Snow.

Chan Master Zhuang Da’an, having been selected by eminent monks, took leave of the assembly and ascended the hall to speak: "I have resided here in Yunzhong for five years, as fleeting as a shifting candle.
What I delight in are illusory conditions; heart-mind after heart-mind, I know this for myself. Empty fame cannot be avoided; the imperial decree arrives."
Arriving at an empty valley, he laughs as he gazes upon a broken-legged cauldron. Left behind, who will continue its use? He strokes his seven-foot rattan staff; its glossy lacquer dazzles the eyes.
When used or set aside, each has its own time. Whether departing or staying, to what constraints are we bound? "Be careful, you fellow travelers! Let us together sing the *Qingping* melody.
Suddenly, picking up his staff, he calls to the assembly, saying: "Tell me, in what tune is this *Qingping* melody?"
He gave a shout and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Yuguan went to Mount Jing; addressing the assembly before ascending the hall, he said:

"I have served as a placeholder at Nanjiang for exactly three years, and now I again exercise my transformative influence at Lingxiao. Having settled the old case of my former master, when hungry I eat, and when weary I sleep."
"Furthermore, how did the former masters resolve their public cases? [He] struck the meditation seat and descended.
The Head Monks of Renown and Virtue accepted the invitation to borrow the seat and ascend the dais (the Abbot first leads them to the seat and presents the outline).
Chan Master Baiyun Cuan, while serving as the Head Seat, was invited by the Four Directions. The Master ascended the hall and said: "Year after year, the autumn heat..."
It is just as at the beginning. What matter is it that the coolness is so exceptionally abundant? It is entirely the resonance within the minds and grounds of those present;

it is not in vain that we are holding hands here in Longshu. But tell me, how do you speak this one phrase of "holding hands"? After a long silence, he said: "When walking, one reaches the end of the water;
sitting, one watches the clouds arise."
Chan Master Baoning Yong ascends the hall for the departure of Elder Shouning.
One night at Caoxi was truly groundless; three blows from Huangbo were merely mutual neglect. The meditation cushions and Zen boards have oppressed the person within.
To ask for fire to burn them would still be somewhat better. Today, Baoning has nothing else to offer as a parting gift; Elder Shouning, take up your staff.
He said: "I have only this single black-lacquered staff; I will not conceal it further. I now entrust it to you all with both hands.
Having cast down the staff, he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Yuanwu Qin delivered a sermon upon receiving the official appointment from Master Min of Baoning:
"To dwell alone on a solitary peak, gazing at the clouds and the sky—though this does not fail to preserve the ancestral wind, is it not perhaps too high?

To stand at a crossroads with a dusty face and ashes on the head, benefiting others and responding to circumstances—though this does obscure one's own self, is it not perhaps too much of a compromise?"
How much more so for the enlightened person, who possesses the eye upon the crown of the head and holds the talisman beneath the elbow;

one who attains great mastery in appearing and disappearing, or rolling up and unfolding [the mind], moving like drifting clouds and resting like the spirit of the valley. Such a one may sometimes dwell alone on a solitary peak, yet must not soil their face or smear their head with ash;
or they may soil their face and smear their head with ash, yet must not dwell alone on a solitary peak. Within such states, there is that which is not...
"Thus it is. Yet within that which is not thus, there is indeed "thusness. For now, how would you express the phrase for being timely and attuned to the season?
After a long silence, he said: "Auspicious vapors meet a fortunate era; the spiritual sprouts find spring everywhere."
Chan Master Ying’an Hua ascended the hall at the request of Elder Longbao Jue and said:
"The Unsurpassed Dharma King possesses a great *dhāraṇī* gate called Perfect Enlightenment (*yuanjue*), from which flow forth all pure *tathatā*, *bodhi*, and *nirvāṇa*.
[He] suddenly took up his staff, struck it once, and said: 'Everyone, please enter here! Hearing the sound, realize the Way; seeing..."
"Form is clarity; mind is clarity. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva bought a sesame cake with his money, but when he let it go, it turned out to be a steamed bun.
Again, he took up his staff, struck it once, and said: "If you enter through this, you will blind people's eyes;
if you do not enter through this, where else will you enter? A clever person turns around at a single push, yet they must further know how to exit."
"The single path for emerging from the body. I venture to ask the great assembly: "What is this single path for emerging from the body? Then, striking the ground once more, he said:
"Lifting one's head to gaze beyond the heavens—who is there like me?"
Chan Master Meng’an Xin received a letter from the Pacification Commissioner Shao of Danyang, requesting that Chan person Song take up residence at Gongde Monastery in Xiaogan.
Consequently, he led him to the seat for an introduction: "To thoroughly explore the tiger’s den, one must possess heroic spirit;
to alone pluck the pearl from the dragon’s head, how could there not be someone extraordinary? Since you have harbored such a resolve, you must surely respond to such a request. But tell me—"
Regarding such matters, how are they to be applied? Those who know the Way, though a thousand miles apart, offer their counsel:
please bring this forth for me so that all may see.
A special messenger from Qingxian in Nandang, Lin’an Prefecture, has come to the hermitage to invite Chan Master Jian to serve as abbot. For this reason—
[The Master] introduces the assembly: "The waters of Qiantang flow vast and wide, reaching to the Bohai Sea. Casting bait and lowering the line cannot be done in haste.

Do not be like one who returns with an empty boat carrying only the moon; plunge deep into the misty waves to seek and investigate. When the *kūn* and *jīng* fish finally take the hook, you will not have wasted your time following the currents and mingling with the flow.
Before the Hundred-Fathom Mountain, what business shall we accomplish? First, let us take up our fishing pipes upon the small boat. [He then] turns to the left.
Looking back to the right, he said: "Fortunately, there are those who understand; I shall now bring this forth.
Chan Master Kentang Chong, at the request of Master Yuan'an, ascended the seat and said: "On South Mountain there is an old demon king.
His piercing eyes flash with lightning; his mouth is like a blood-basin as he scolds the Buddhas and Patriarchs, and his fangs are like swords."
Shu Ma reviles all directions; how many times has the wind of karma blown him without moving? Only when blown by the wind at the side of Mount Yunhuang does he move.
Together with Sengtou Tuo and Master Fu Dashi, they broke through the door with a single fire.

Still the same Meng Bala, deceiving countless ignorant men and women, opening their eyes wide as they enter the boiling cauldron. Suddenly, if there is a monk who comes forth and says, "Since this is goodness..."
"Knowledge! Why does it lure people into the boiling cauldron? To this, he simply replied: "This is not your realm.
When Chan Master Chushih Qi and Master Liaohan set out for Lingyan, he ascended the hall and said: "Sansheng said, 'Whenever I meet someone, I come forth;
yet when I come forth, I do not act for the sake of others. Xinghua said, 'Whenever I meet someone, I do not come forth; yet when I come forth..."
Thus he becomes a human being. Look at the descendants of Linji: they are like mercury falling to the ground; the large ones are perfectly round and the small ones are perfectly round.
One can never find their head or nose. The newly installed Abbot Lingyan balances the Buddhas and Patriarchs and smelts and forges the holy and the ordinary.
For the sake of the Chan practitioners throughout the four seas, he sweeps away the boastful proclamations of all quarters. Upon the surface of Lake Dongting, he stands firm.
The Vajradhvaja arises; within Mount Zhijian, the Eye of the True Dharma opens wide. Ultimately, upon what does one rely?
He brandishes his staff, strikes it once, and descends from the seat.
Chan Master Yuansou Duan presided over the assembly for the Venerable Fushan of Xin Ruiyan in Mingzhou.

Controlling the great pivot of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and fixing the true eye of heaven and earth, those who have occupied the "curved wooden seat" since time immemorial are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
yet, when one investigates their ultimate aim, there is truly not one in ten thousand who has attained it. Therefore it is said: "It is like the *qin*, *se*, *konghou*, and *pipa* lutes."
Though there be a wondrous sound, without wondrous fingers it can never be produced. (He strikes the whisk. Before the twelve peaks, the moon is as if cut;
its clear light, shared across a thousand miles, lingers on with mutual affection.
To commemorate the late Master Liaotang, the presiding master leads the assembly: He opens the lotus flower in the month of December; he causes flakes of ice to fall upon a scorching sky.
He clarifies the source and flow of the authentic lineage and shatters the stagnant nests of heterodox teachers. Holding the withered tree in his grasp, his total function is laughable;
wielding the autumn waters across his chest, his partial lifting can extinguish all. Thus, those who gaze at the zenith throughout the eight directions shall no longer contend with one another.
Heng: "I shall go to see this man; he drives the carriage with its high and gnarled branches. (He strikes the whisk. "The monastic groves are now desolate everywhere;
listen to the Second Zen of the Western Mountain."
Chan Master Yuguan and Secretary Yan went to Puqing Temple for the morning assembly. "If you wish to understand the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should contemplate the conditions of time and season.
Have you not seen how Mazu asked Youshan, "What is your current realization?"
Shan said, "The skin and flesh have all fallen away; there is only the one true reality.

The Patriarch said, "What you have attained may be called 'harmonizing with the essence of the mind and extending it to the four limbs. Since this is so, take three strips of bamboo to bind your belly and go dwell in the mountains wherever you please.
Shan said, "Who am I that I would dare say I will dwell in the mountains? The Patriarch said, "Not [so]."
However, there has never been one who travels long distances without stopping, nor one who dwells for a long time without moving.
To seek benefit is to find no benefit; to act is to have nothing to do. You ought to become a vessel for crossing over; do not remain here for long.
That Ma Boji was indeed a shrimp bowing for its offspring—nevertheless, when the season arrives, the principle reveals itself naturally. At such a time as this, how would you explain it?
"This is the principle that manifests of itself. Suddenly picking up his staff, he called to the assembly, saying, "Tomorrow, go and see this Way among Mount Pujing.
The Elder shall clearly explain it for the sake of all people. He struck the ground with his staff and gave a shout.
Zhangzhu Yan went to Qianqing for the ascending-to-the-hall discourse. He cited an ancient worthy who said:
"This plot of land has been entrusted to you for a long time; I stand here waiting for you to grasp it. Fayen said:
"This plot of land has been entrusted to you for a long time; I sit here waiting for you to grasp it. Foguo said: "This plot of land..."
It has been entrusted for a long time. I shall now offer you a direct celebration and praise: one is three, and three is one.
Because perspectives differ, there is mutual gain and loss. Jing Mountain said: "This plot of land has been entrusted for a long time;
it is simply that you have failed to grasp it. Today, I entrust it to Elder Yuyu, who holds it with bare hands and reveals it openly.
Carrying the burden upon their shoulders, they cast seed here and there amidst the thousand-acre clouds, plowing deep and sowing shallow.
They plant forests of thorns, bloom the flowers of the three poisons, and bear the fruit of ignorance. They transform the stalks of rice into ears of millet and change rubble into gold.
Truly, Śākyamuni and Maitreya clap their hands in joy; Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra join their palms in praise.

Following the statutes and precedents of a hundred generations, he revives the monastic assembly of this region. Holding up his staff, he says: "If you wish to recognize true gold, look for it in the fire;
the eye upon the staff is as bright as the sun."
Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun acted as the introducer for Master Me’An of Fengsheng.
To transmit the Buddha’s Mind-essence is no small matter; to shoulder the Great Dharma requires the right person.

Thus, Shoushan and Fengxue dwelt alone in thatched huts for thirty years, yet the flourishing of their Dharma path exceeded that of ten thousand disciples and a thousand foundations. Later, Zhenjing...
Furthermore, he said: "In my late teacher’s time at Huangbo, the assembly did not exceed a hundred people, yet those with clear eyes accounted for nearly half.

Although the numbers today are three times what they were then, there are barely one or two such individuals. It can truly be said that while a thousand soldiers are easy to find, a single general is difficult to seek."
Today, an imperial envoy arrived specifically to invite the First Seat to reside as abbot of this mountain. To retain him would disappoint the purpose of his mission;
to let him go would deprive this assembly of its support. Can you all determine what is right?

If you can determine it, then you will see the thousand leaves wafting their fragrance at the assembly on Vulture Peak, and a single branch standing uniquely prominent before the peak of Shaoshi. If you have not yet reached this realization—
Listen further as this staff conveys a message. *He strikes once* and says: "Silver mountains and iron walls allow no evasion;
where the grass bows and the wind blows, one attains freedom. He then raises the case of Yangqi, who was invited by Jiufeng.
Upon descending from his seat, Master Jiufeng Qinqin seized him and said, "I am glad to have found a fellow practitioner. Yangqi asked, "What is the matter regarding being a 'fellow practitioner'?"
Shengfeng said, "Jiuping pulls the plow; Yangqi drags the harrow. Yangqi asked, "At this very moment, is Yangqi in front or Jiuping in front?
As Jiuping hesitated, Yangqi pushed him aside and said, "I thought we were fellow practitioners; it turns out you are not."
The Master said: "Yangqi and Jiufeng played the *xun* and *chi* flutes in alternation; such a thing has rarely been heard in antiquity or today.
Today at Longxiang, I raise this up before the assembly so that everyone may know it. But tell me, what is it that they know? The ancestral estate is not very large;
strive with one heart, you two brothers."

The former Hall Head Seat went to Baoning to request an address from the High Seat. "Opening the flower of ignorance and binding the fruit of the three poisons, the evil karma of the Mara-king manifests before one;
driving the plowman’s ox and seizing the hungry man’s food—his 'white-thief' (stealthily taking) skills are particularly high.
This is why when Baizhang visited Mazu for a second time, Mazu displayed his majestic power with a single shout that left him deaf for three days. Huangbo heard of this..."

Unconsciously he stuck out his tongue, whereupon he first realized that great capacity and great function do not depend on the transmission of a teacher; that the subtle and profound skill of the tongs and hammer belongs to the person themselves.
Such is my younger brother, Fawang, whom our former master revered and feared. Recently, he took leave of the famous monasteries by the sea.
He humbly served as a model for those within the mountains. Now, having received the command of the Prime Minister, he has gone to respond to the invitation from Baoning.

This is what is meant by "the Dharma follows the practice of the Dharma" and "the banner of the Dharma is erected wherever one is. He is a furnace that melts the ordinary and forges the sage, smelting gold;

his brilliance illuminates the past and soars through the present. He beats the phoenix and nets the dragon with a web of tortoise hair, covering the heavens and pervading the earth, until there is no path left to travel and no door to enter.
"You may enter. I, this mountain monk, shall provide a skillful means for all of you. He brandished his staff, cast it down, and said:
"How many have lost their bodies and forfeited their lives? Watch out for the turtle-nosed snake of the South Mountain!"
