Compiled by Xingyue of Loudong, Abbot of Lian’an Chan Monastery at the Eighteen Streams in Wulin.
The Renowned and Virtuous One Accepts the Invitation, Takes His Seat, and Presents the Outline.
Chan Master Yangqi Huai was invited to ascend the seat at Jiufeng in Junzhou. After the question-and-answer session concluded, he said:
"Is there anyone else who wishes to ask a question? Come forward from the assembly and let us see you. Today, Yangqi’s very life depends on you."
In the hands of all people, let them drag you about or pull you down as they please.
Why is this so? A true man of great capacity must make a decisive judgment in public; do not act like someone pushing a gourd under water in secret.
When tested before the assembly, do not be put to shame. Is there anyone? Is there anyone? Come forward and make your decision! If there is none, Yangqi has lost his advantage.
As soon as the Master descended from his seat, Master Jiufeng Qin seized him and said, "Today I am delighted to meet a fellow practitioner.
The Master asked, "What is this matter of being a fellow practitioner? Jiufeng said, "Jiufeng plows the furrow; Yangqi drags the harrow.
The Master said, "At such a time as this, who is in front—Yangqi or Jiufeng? As Jiufeng hesitated, the Master pushed him aside and said, "Take [this]!"
This refers to fellow practitioners; originally, it was not so.
Chan Master Yunfeng Yue, while at Tong'an, accepted an invitation from Cuishan and ascended the seat, saying:
"Today, this mountain monk has met his downfall on level ground. Do you all know where the failure lies? For the public administration, even a needle cannot pass; for private matters..."
The carriage and horses passed through. [The Master] struck the meditation seat and descended.
Zen Master Xuedou Xian was at Lingyin Monastery when he accepted the invitation from Cuifeng. The assembly requested him to ascend the seat, saying:

"This is the most supreme site of enlightenment under heaven; it is the vast seat of the Master of Lingyin. We temporarily borrow this humble monk to ascend, yet we truly feel ashamed that his talent is insufficient."
How could I dare, before these five hundred monks, preach upon the Buddhas and Patriarchs or extol the ancients and the present?

To flaunt my own knowledge and feel shame at the works of others—were I to speak until the heavens rain down the four flowers and the earth shakes in six ways, not even a single point of such utility would suffice on the path of Caoxi.
Why? Because high-minded practitioners who travel the road possess the capacity to grasp the entire world within their palms.
This is indeed the eye of heaven and earth; who would dare err by even a hair’s breadth? Those who possess this knowledge will surely understand it together.
When Chan Master Haoyuanyuan of Yuyuan was at Lumen, he accepted an invitation from Dayang and ascended the seat. [The Master said: "I have been at Lumen for ten years."
"I have never drunk a single drop of water from Lukmon, nor chewed a single grain of rice from Lukmon.
If you do not understand, come to Dayang and I shall break it open for you. Carrying his staff, he descended from the seat.

Chan Master Baoben was invited to take up residence at Tiyan Monastery; he ascended the hall and said: "I have been summoned by Shengshou Temple on Wujiang to serve as its abbot, yet I am at a loss as to whether to accept or decline.
For now, I shall follow my karmic conditions. All of this is due to the constant guidance, instruction, and encouragement provided from beginning to end by our Head Monk (the Abbot).
According to the strict standard of today, if I were to exercise the true command, I would strike you all dead with a single blow of my staff—how could I possibly tolerate anything less?"
He stood before the seat. Although it is thus, only by raising a child does one come to know a father’s compassion.
Regarding the request for a seat and the evening *xichan* (small lecture) given by the Master Yunfeng Yue while at Tong’an, after the questions and answers were concluded, he [said]:
[The Master] was invited by Cuiyan while staying at Tong’an; on that evening, he gave a *xiaochan*. After the question-and-answer session was finished, he...
He said: "Are there no other masters among the Chan guests or fellow monks of the fundamental lineage? What prevents you from coming forth to provide mutual verification? Is there anyone?
Even a needle in a sack would be quite excellent if it did not poke its head out. Generally speaking, to uphold the Dharma-lineage, one must indeed be such a person.
If you have not yet attained that state where the mind flows like a rushing torrent, passing through the blade like a spark of flint or a flash of lightning—"
The eyes—no need to bring them forth. When Master Linji and Deshan were sitting together, Deshan said, "I am tired today.
Linji said, "Old man, why do you speak in your sleep? Deshan was about to raise his staff when Linji overturned the meditation seat.
The Master said, "How extraordinary! All you practitioners, look at these two masters: one pressing, one nudging, briefly revealing their style."
"It is very much like holding a high mountain in one's hands. Although this is so, it cannot avoid the laughter of onlookers.
But tell me, who is the onlooker? With a shout, he struck the meditation seat and descended.
The Master Yunfeng Yue, renowned for his virtue, took leave of the assembly to depart from Tong’an.
Before ascending the hall to bid farewell, he said: "This mountain monk’s way is shameful for its meagerness; I consider myself unworthy.
Yet, how could I have expected that the summons would travel so far and the monks would request my presence like clouds gathering? This is surely due to the affection of our Head Monk."
The depth of our feelings is fully expressed and the Way is vast; we shall only strive with the resolve of one treading on thin ice, never daring to forget our sincerity in repaying your grace.
Furthermore, the special envoy Yixing of Cuiyan is nearby, and within these few days, some forty or so people have caused considerable clamor and disturbance.
My feelings of gratitude and shame converge within my heart. Furthermore, Master Xing, who accompanies me, is one of high virtue;
he already possesses the beauty of character and further cultivates a mind of resolute determination. As we traverse this long journey, may you both cherish and protect one another.

Yet, for those who have left the household life and attained the Way, benefiting others is their primary responsibility. Their movement is like drifting clouds, and their stillness is like the spirit of the valley—how could they ever...
It is when the mind is concerned with this or that, and the emotions are bound to movement or stillness.
Since there is no concern for this or that, and no attachment to coming or going, why should these manifold phenomena from "that" side concern me?

If it is thus, I hope that you, O venerable superiors, will hoist your golden mendicant staffs high, lightly roll up your cloud-like robes, and set out tomorrow; wherever you go, how could it not be auspicious?

Dharma Words for Incense Offerings at the Three Gates (The Ritual of Offering Incense upon Entering the Monastery) Chan Master Miam Jie points to the three gates of Jiangshan: These are the gates of unimpeded liberation, Layer upon layer, like precious pavilions.
Without exerting effort to collect the mind, open wide with eight characters; simply walk where your feet lead, and naturally the sound will harmonize with its echo.
If you hesitate, you will find yourself bumping into walls and crashing into barriers.
Chan Master Xueyan Qin pointed to the triple gate at Longxing Temple and said: "The entire great earth is this courtyard.
Tell me, from which door does one enter? It is wide open—blue sky and bright sun."
Guarding the three gates of the Sage, he spans the threshold of the universal realm and demonstrates the pivotal mechanism of the world. Placing his hand to his forehead, he asks, "Who is this?
Yangshan [replies], "My three gates here are a door that reaches to the heavens; the entire earth is caught in a single net. If it were a *xianglin* (auspicious qilin), [he would let it pass].
Auspicious Phoenix! Let it wear horns and lift its head as it pleases. Even so, all such talk belongs to the side of the conceptual.
As for Chan Master Yuan’an’s three gates at Shengshou Monastery on Fulong Mountain: before crossing the Dragon Gate, one’s feet already tread upon solid ground;
once having crossed the Dragon Gate, one’s feet still tread upon solid ground. He strides forward and says: "With a single clap of thunder, wind and clouds arise."
Chan Master Yuansou Duan points to the three gates of Fengshan: the gate of inexhaustible treasury of spiritual powers, the gate of inexhaustible treasury of liberation.
Today, at this very place, he opens wide the eight characters: the toad leaps up to the Brahma Heaven;
the earthworm passes straight across the Eastern Sea.
Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun opened the gates of the three-tiered tower of Central India in the space of a single finger-snap;
the nine bends of the Yellow River flow forth from Mount Kunlun.
Chan Master Wuwen Can points to the main gate of Jianfu Monastery: "Red lotuses stand at the entrance; green willows wind along the path.
The new Jianfu has opened wide with eight characters. If you can enter here, you may roam freely throughout the world.
Huizang points to the three gates: if there is no place of entry, it drives people to their deaths; if there is a place of entry, it obstructs people to their deaths.
[The Master] snaps his fingers once and says: "The heavy barrier is smashed to pieces! From where does the very word 'entry' come?"
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun’s Inscription for the Main Gate of Guangfu Monastery: A single phrase upon entering the gate—how difficult it is to see!
To stir the mechanism, the eastern door flaps and the western door flaps. (He lets out a shout.)
Regarding the three gates of Ruiyan: "The entire earth is the gate of liberation; I hold out my hand to pull you in, yet you will not enter.
Xuefeng spoke thus, but Ruiyan does not speak thus. [He] lets out a shout.

Chan Master Guyan Ji points to the three gates of Mount Jing: "Mount Jing under heaven, the Dragon Gate under heaven—swallowing and spitting out the sun and moon, encompassing and covering heaven and earth."
The Southern Chan Master Shi Xi’s Inscription for the Main Gate of Guangxiao Temple: "The Dharma-gate is vast and great; only those who arrive know it.
Red clouds pierce the azure void; the white sun encircles Mount Sumeru."
The Gate of Ten-Thousand-Year Longevity. This is the Dharma-gate of no gate, entering directly by a single leap. A swift horse chasing lightning cannot catch up.

Master Tianguan Shu’s "Gate of Universal Carrying" is the Great Gate of Liberation; like the earth that universally carries all, one enters with a confident step, where there is ultimately no distinction between interior and exterior.
Chan Master Shiwu Hong points to the main gate: "The doors and windows stand wide open; who is facing the hall? He lets out a shout.

How many are there who enter the monastery to look at the plaque? He then asks, "What is it? and enters.
The three gates of Fengshan: the East Gate, West Gate, South Gate, and North Gate. Each gate has a road; where does the end of the road lie?
Before the Five-Phoenix Pavilion.
The three gates of original enlightenment have not yet opened their hibernation chambers; the dragon lacks its dragon-sentence. Shattering the void, the whole body is revealed.
He further said: "Step."
The Three Gates of Kuangxiao are gates that have no gate; enter them by not entering. Clouds hang over the four fields, and waters fill the twin lakes.
If you wish to traverse the world with ease, you must arrive there in person at least once.
Chan Master Liaoyuan Yu pointed to the three gates at Kaifu Temple and said, "This Dharma-gate of mine is for going straight out and entering straight in;
those of inferior capacity can only look up at it from afar. He let out a shout.
"Original enlightenment points to three gates; each gate has its own path. Even those who have attained realization remain deluded. To turn back the pivot of heaven—who knows that it exists?
(He lets out a shout.)

Lingyan points to the triple gate; he pushes open the barrier beyond. He sweeps away the tracks of the holy and the profane; for all eternity, heaven and earth are, in a single morning, wind and moon.
Chan Master Zhuang of Da’an at Yunju points to the triple gate: he grandly opens the heavy barriers and fully upholds the orthodox command. Waters flow toward...
Clouds rush forth; the golden bell tolls and the jade chime responds.
Dajue points to the triple gate: "This Dharma-gate of mine is as vast as heaven and as broad as the earth.
You people who enter and exit within it must know that there is a 'key' for the upward path before you may succeed. He lets out a shout.
Chan Master Yuejiang Yin pointed to the triple gate of Yewang Temple and said, "The Great Gate of Liberation has been flung wide open.
He snapped his fingers and let out a shout; all of this was unnecessary.

To manifest the three gates of Master Zhun’s universal compassion—the gate of hundreds of thousands of spiritual powers and the gate of hundreds of thousands of wondrous functions—all of these fall into the second meaning.
What, then, is the first meaning? (He snapped his fingers once.)
Chan Master Zhuo’an asked at the main gate of Jinshan: "Jade halls and crystal palaces; crystal palaces and jade halls.
Ten billion transformation gates—each gate has eyes. It is opened wide, eight characters flung apart, and the waves splash against one’s face. Reaching this point, you must advance further.
Everyone, look! Having said this, he entered.
The Leuze (Leakage-Overflow) has three gates; of these, this one alone is narrow and small. Yet, once you can enter it, the ground becomes vast and the heavens wide.
But how do you enter? He lets out a shout.

no-gate is the Dharma-gate. Is there anyone who can enter this gate? Looking at the assembly, he said: “A snake does not move without a head.”
Xingfu points to the three gates: the stone bridge locks to the east, and the ancient stream flows from the west. The portals of the Buddhas and Patriarchs stand wide open through all time.
Do you see? The auspicious qilin and the lucky phoenix have all entered this mountain.

Dharma Words on the Method of Incense Offering in the Buddha Hall by Chan Master Mimian Jie at Jiangshan Temple: "Because of me, you receive my prostrations; I have traced the source to its very bottom.

In the Guangxiao Buddha Hall: Śākyamuni has already passed away and Maitreya has not yet been born. Within these two thousand years, who is there to preach the Dharma?
Who is there to cause it to be practiced? Yunmen’s nose is straight; Deshan’s eyes are askew.
At Yangshan’s Buddha Hall, the "Little Śākyamuni of the Eastern Land" pointed to the Buddha statue and said, "Look at this—it is you. [Yangshan] asked: "I venture to ask:

when [Maitreya] dreamed of ascending to the Tuṣita Heaven Palace and spoke of transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations, what principle was he clarifying? To regulate them by means of ritual."

Chan Master Yuansou Duanshi’s Inscription for the Buddha Hall of Zifu Monastery: The jade-white tuft of light shines universally throughout the ten directions; the golden hue radiates everywhere across the thousand worlds. [Having said this,] he prostrated himself.
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun’s Inscription for the Buddha of Ruiyan Monastery: This Buddha is a person of the household. If you can understand him directly, then [you will realize] Xuansha...
To the very bottom.
Chan Master Liaoyuan Yu opened the Buddha Hall at Kaifu. When the World-Honored One held up the flower and Kāśyapa smiled, it was thanks to Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra;
a kettle for brewing tea is not the same as a small saucepan.

The Buddha Hall of Original Enlightenment: the nature of enlightenment is wondrously luminous; original enlightenment is luminously wondrous. Cast off the "hawk-odored" robe; take down the "fat-cheese" cap. The Buddha Hall of Lingyan:
the World-Honored One’s samādhi—Kāśyapa did not know it. This single assembly on Vulture Peak remains solemnly present even now.
Chan Master Da’an Zhuang burns incense at the Buddha Hall of Jing Mountain:

"The Buddhas of the three periods are now, right where the incense smoke rises, emitting light and manifesting auspicious omens while turning the Great Dharma Wheel. The cat and the white ox let out a great laugh;
the pillar and the lantern let out a great laugh."
Chan Master Weian’s inscription for the Buddha Hall at Shengshou Monastery: "The Dharma-body, Reward-body, and Transformation-body are all this very thing.
Ultimately, by what means is it verified? "When the mud is thick, the Buddha is large. [The Master] then prostrated.
To clarify the words of Chan Master Yongzhang Jun regarding the Universal Compassion Buddha Hall: "Not clinging to seeking the Buddha; not clinging to seeking the Dharma. What kind of talk is this?
There is only the Buddha’s Bodhi as the true place of refuge. Having said this, he prostrated.
At the Buddha Hall of Suiryam: "This very mind is the Buddha; neither mind nor Buddha. If the mind is right here, where is the Buddha?
He raises his sitting mat—almost missing it right before one's face.
Chan Master Chushi Qi consecrated the Buddha Hall at Fuzhen; the old woman east of the city did not wish to see it.
The bhikṣu Devadatta was constantly angry and resentful; he took a stick of incense in his hand and offered it—this too is like practicing the ordinances of spring in winter.
The Tianning Buddha Hall: "This is me; this is you. Scattering earth, scattering sand, entering and exiting through the same gate—these are enemies in life and death.
The Fengshan Buddha Hall: Upon the golden hall sits the Old Śākyamuni; it is improper to defecate here.
[He spreads his sitting cloth] and says: "For now, let us prostrate and cover it over."
The Buddha Hall of Original Enlightenment. "Buddha" means awakening. Who is it that awakens? Brought from the Western Heaven to this land, a lotus fiber pulls Mount Sumeru.
In the Buddha Hall of Guangxiao, do you still recognize the Buddha? His face is like the full moon, his eyes are like lotuses; throughout heaven and earth, all...
With reverence, Chan Master Tieguanshu Puzei would utter the word "Buddha" whenever he spoke of the Buddha in the main hall; for three years, he would rinse his mouth [afterward]. Why?
In a world of purity and peace, one must strictly avoid corrupt speech.
Chan Master Guyan Ji, at the Buddha Hall of Mount Jing, looked left and right and said: "Planting a single blade of grass, one builds a palace of jade and crystal;
picking up a single blade of grass, one makes it the sixteen-foot golden body. Upon the mountain there is a carp; at the bottom of the well there is swirling dust."
Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun at the Buddha Hall of Central India: "Two thousand years ago you had skill while I lacked it;
two thousand years later I have skill while you lack it. Why? Because when entering the water, one sees a tall man."
Chan Master Nan Shiyou’s Universal Gate Buddha Hall: The Buddha-body is unconditioned; it does not fall into any numerical categories.
A tortoise bows its head to the Sumeru pillar.
Jing Mountain Buddha Hall: "Buddha" has the meaning of awakening. What is the meaning of awakening? Above the head is heaven; beneath the feet is earth.

The Buddha Hall of Lingyan: The Buddha has no coming or going; he manifests immediately in response to conditions. When spreading out the sitting mat, let none among the assembly say they do not see him.
Chan Master Lingxing of Folang said of the Buddha Hall at Shushan: "The entire realm of empty space is this very jewel hall. After all, which one is it?"
"This is the Buddha. He roared and said: "Look beyond the heavens! Who is like me?
At Tiantong’s Buddha Hall, the Dharma-body, Reward-body, and Transformation-body—the "zhi-hu-ye-zhe"—are all regulated by ritual propriety (*li*). Above heaven and below heaven.
Chan Master Shiwu Hong’s Inscription for the Buddha Hall: "Because of me, you receive my prostrations; Falling down by yourself, you must rise by yourself.
The magpie cries atop the tree; Its intent lies within the hemp field."
When Chan Master Miyun Wu entered Tiantong Monastery, he went to the site of the ancient Buddha hall and said: "The void serves as the hall;
the sun and moon serve as the lamps. Tell me, whose realm is this? Do you understand?
If you do not yet understand, then watch the new elder unfold his sitting cloth and perform three full prostrations."
Chan Master Zhuo’an asked at the Buddha Hall of Jinshan: "Because of me, you must pay homage. You vulgar, low-born fellows, gathering in crowds and bands!
Mañjuśrī is Mañjuśrī himself; Samantabhadra is Samantabhadra himself. Two by two they do not form a pair; three by three they are not so."
Today, this new elder wishes to manifest the marks of a Great Man. Spreading his sitting cloth, he performs nine prostrations.
At the Leuze Buddha Hall, Deshan broke it; here, I raise it up. Even a clod of mud emits radiance;
I, this mountain monk, spread my sitting cloth and pay homage.
Master Huìtán, receiving the incense at the Buddha Hall, said: "It is neither the Dharma-body, the Reward-body, nor the Transformation-body;
it is also not an image of gold, wood, or clay. Suddenly manifesting before one's eyes, it is difficult to know—yet it is the model for all people and devas throughout the ages.
He then unfolded his sitting cloth and prostrated three times.
In the Buddha Hall of Chan Master Yun’ao Yu, the ancient Śākyamuni and the new elder look at one another; it is most fitting.
Nevertheless, ritual proceeds from the outside; lacking these, the three prostrations cannot be omitted. Thereupon, he spreads his sitting mat and performs the salutation.
Chan Master Hongjue Meng’s Buddha Hall Inscription: "Buddha" means awakening. Under the Bamboo Forest Mountain, a whip made of bamboo fibers;
a three-legged donkey prances about on its hooves. "Three pounds of hemp. The one at the bottom of the hall. The elder is like an elder brother, the younger is like a younger brother.
But tell me, what is the meaning? One stroke splits Mount Hua into two paths; the perennial flowing stream knows nothing of spring.
In Master Muyunmen’s Buddha Hall: Mañjuśrī rides a lion; Samantabhadra rides an elephant king;
and Old Śākyamuni sits upon a jeweled flower pedestal. Each claims to be supreme. Since this mountain monk has entered their protective society, I cannot help but manifest a bit of spiritual power.
Spreading his sitting cloth, he says: "What is it?"
In the Buddha Hall, amidst fine mountains on three sides, stands a solitary King of Emptiness Hall. With a shout, he drives away "three catties of hemp";
he opens up the "dry dung pellet. Where can one meet the ancient Buddhas? He strikes a circle with his sitting cloth and says: "Connected!"
At the Buddha Hall of Chan Master Zhaozong Ren, he held up his sitting cloth and said, "Is it bowing, or is it not bowing?
Since you are an old acquaintance, why need one act so abruptly? He then bowed.

A Dharma Talk on Incense Offerings in the Hall of the Temple Deities by Chan Master Yuan Nengren of the Primordial Abiding at Fuyan. Upon entering the hall of the temple deities, he saw a great many earthen figurines and could not help but laugh aloud.
He then lit incense and said: "In small hermitages, small dwellings, and small monasteries, why should there be eight or nine guardians of the land? If..."

"Understanding that they come in turn to offer their tribute, so that they may not be ground into a heap of dust. (That evening, the deity appeared in a dream to a lay patron before the mountain, wishing for things to be as instructed.
"Only Chan Master Anran is the sacred life-force of the monastery; upright and intelligent, intelligent and upright.
To manifest the orthodox and crush the heterodox—by whose power is this achieved? (He lets out a shout.)
Chan Master Folang said to Chan Master Shushan at Galan Temple: "I possess the six supernatural powers; you possess five. Tell me, what is that one power?
No one recognizes the merit of the sweating horse; once again, the achievements that cover the age are debated.

Chan Master Nanxiu pointed to the local deity at Lingyan Temple and said: "Wondrously penetrating heaven and earth, turning the axis of creation and transformation—all is nothing more than these few drops.
Why is this so? When a drop of wine falls to the ground, all the deities become intoxicated."
The Bao’en Monastery is empty yet spiritual, still yet wondrous. Heaven covers all without partiality; the sun shines upon all without partiality.
At the Land Deity Hall and the Dragon King Temple of Chan Master Chushi Qi, their fame is majestic and their spirit is pure. The phoenix towers of former dynasties endure;
this dragon court lasts through ten thousand ages. After the rain has passed, the mountains of Wu stand green, piercing the heavens.
Master Miyun Yuanwu, while offering incense at the Shrine of the Local Deity (Tudishen), said: "O Guardian Deity of the Monastery, Lord of the Forests!
This single offering of incense—raising it with both hands—he immediately burned."
Chan Master Zhuo’an asked at the Hall of the Temple Guardians at Mount Jinshan: "The true does not conceal the false;
the crooked does not hide the straight. You cannot escape my circle; I cannot escape your circle."
Chan Master Hongjue Wen is the guardian of this monastery. His entire being pervades the universe, never hidden. Since he knows of one’s coming and going beforehand, what hindrance could there be?
Rather than waiting for him to appear later and add a fraction more, it is better to offer incense directly before his face.
The Shrine of the Land. Calamities do not come alone; blessings do not arrive in pairs. As for the misfortunes that afflict the monastic groves, they fall only upon you and me.
Meeting here, we clap our hands atop the high platform, leaving it to Pāpīyān to look on with cold eyes.

The Chan Master Muchunmen is the guardian of this monastery. We look up with reverence as you protect these ancient halls and lofty forests. The reflections of the pond and the radiance of the mountains are reflected on the left and gazed upon from the right.
But what is it that you are looking at? "The eternal abode of a thousand years rests in a single morning monk; he lifts the lamp of Lingfeng to illuminate the night."
Dharma Words for Incense Offerings at the Patriarchs’ Hall:
Chan Master Weian Ran at Shengshou Patriarchs’ Hall. You lot, this whole crew, have no backbone at all.
Six ears conspiring together—what good plan could there possibly be?
This is used to manifest the ancestral hall of Zen Master Yongchang at Ruiyan: transmitting mind with mind, and transmitting Dharma with Dharma.
One dog barks at the void; a thousand monkeys gnaw at reality. Bodhidharma did not understand Zen; the Sixth Patriarch did not understand the Way.
From where was this transmitted Dharma obtained?
Chan Master Tieguanshu’s Universal Ferrying of the Patriarchs’ Hall: A horse’s jaw and a donkey’s whiskers; a nailed beak and an iron tongue.
The four sevens and two threes—turning a tortoise into a turtle.
Chan Master Chushi Qi said: "If it were not for this group of fellows, the Buddha-dharma would not have reached the present day;
yet if it were not for this group of fellows, the Buddha-dharma would not have reached the present day. Now tell me, do you approve of them or not?"
The Ancestral Hall of Original Enlightenment: Master Bodhidharma was not the patriarch; at midnight he descended upon Jambudvīpa while the sun was at its zenith.
The Ancestral Hall of Guangxiao: "One flower, five petals. There must be a cause for what arises—tell me, from where does it arise?
On the bank, hoof meets hoof; in the water, beak faces beak.
The Hall of Master Yuyan Ji and Patriarch Puci: In Kunming Lake the sword is lost; at the head of Qujiang River the saw is found.
Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru the waves overflow the heavens; from the bottom of the great ocean the dust rises like a gale.
The patriarchs, great and small, have no teeth in their mouths.
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun’s Hall of Patriarchs at Guangfu: The chestnut thorn and the diamond circle are cast back and forth between this land and the Western Heaven.
At Zuiyan’s Hall of Patriarchs, heart meets heart and eye meets eye; it is all one and the same aged, rotten tangle. Six.
The six [categories] remain as the thirty-six.
Chan Master Nan Shi-xiu established a monastic community at Bao-guo Zu-tang to transmit the essential mind of the Buddha.
He walked barefoot yet wore black boots; he left his head exposed yet donned a straw hat.
The Patriarchal Hall of Baoguo: Forty-seven, twenty-three. The direct pointing of the single transmission. Clouds rise on the Southern Mountain; rain falls on the Northern Mountain.
At the Patriarchal Hall of Jingshan, rising from bowing and gathering the sitting mat, he says: "From patriarch to patriarch it has been maintained—this one point alone.
It illuminates the past and soars through the present, filling the ditches and blocking the ravines."
Chan Master Folang’s Inscription for the Patriarchal Hall of Shushan: "Seventeen hundred patriarchs from India and this land— Black beans have changed people's eyes.
Now, throughout the great earth, all have hidden their traces; With bellies drummed, they sing aloud in their own Great Peace."
The Patriarchal Hall of Tiantong: From the time the ancestral masters established the Dharma community, the eastern house was made into a donkey and the western house into a horse;
their nostrils were pierced with utter ease. Taibai’s entire pen has been brought under control.

Chan Master Miyun Yuanwu’s Ancestral Hall Inscription states: "The seven patriarchs of the Western Heaven and the two or three patriarchs of this Eastern Land are all here, silently deliberating upon a matter.
Today, they are all caught in one fell swoop. Tell me, what serves as the proof? He inserts an incense stick and says:
"This serves as the proof."
Chan Master Zhuo’an asked at the Ancestral Hall of Jinshan: "In the Western Heaven and the Eastern Land, what kind of 'nose' are this pack of old, frozen fellows looking for?
If you, Venerable Upadhyaya, wish to give voice on behalf of the Ancestors, take up the incense and say: 'One, two, three, four, five.'"
Huitan succeeded the Chan Master at the Patriarchs’ Hall; from Kapilavastu to the land of Liang, his influence reached countless ordinary people beyond measure.
Today, as the precepts are implemented at Shouliang Monastery, everyone’s nostrils are pierced by a single incense stick.

The Patriarchal Hall of Chan Master Hongjue Wenyin: At Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, the secret entrustment was bestowed; It has spread throughout the west and the east. How long indeed is the radiance of this flame!
A thousand lamps continue on, beyond measure. [Offering incense: A single burner of incense scatters through the white clouds.
The Patriarch’s Hall. Four hundred and seventy-two [generations] from east to west—each one a white-robed thief and a rogue. This mountain monk need not brandish his spear;
as soon as they enter the room, I capture and defeat them. But tell me, where does the proof lie? Holding up the incense, he said: "The stolen goods are here before your eyes."
The Patriarchal Hall of Chan Master Muchunmen: The wind and moon of Shaolin; the model of Baizhang.
For a thousand or ten thousand years, it has turned out there was someone who knew where it was. Who was that person? [Inserting incense, he says: "Six ears do not share a secret."

The Dharma Words for Occupying the Room and Burning Incense by Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin at Chongning: Occupying the Room: Pointing to the Abbot’s quarters, he said, “For the practitioners of our school, even the palaces of demons and the dens of tigers are places where they dwell in peace;
how much more so the locations where they benefit sentient beings and engage with others! Do you know this room? It is surrounded by all the devas.”
Guarded by the witness of all the sages, that spiritual friend sits upright within this space, untangling the entanglements and removing the bonds of others.
Since such a sublime manifestation exists here, how shall I, this mountain monk, provide for it? If one does not enter the startling waves, it is difficult to find a fish to one’s liking.
What is the phrase for entering the gate? When the waters return to the great ocean, the billows are stilled; when the clouds reach the azure sky...
Wu’s demeanor was leisurely. He entered immediately.
Zen Master Dahui Zonggao of Yuyang pointed toward the abbot’s quarters and called to the assembly, saying:

"This place is the great furnace for smelting Buddhas and patriarchs, the cruel tongs and hammers for forging the living and the dead. Do not take offense that the host has no face; the Dharma is thus."
Therefore, it is not a matter of forced effort. Since the Dharma is thus, it is also not a matter of forced effort. But tell me, how is it with the very first phrase?
Do you understand? "The fishing pole is worn out, so plant bamboo again; do not calculate the labor, and when the opportunity arises, simply rest."
Chan Master Ying’an Hua sat upon the seat at Kuangxiao Temple and said: "The public case is already accomplished; it cuts off all confusion.
To provide a mistaken commentary is to break your own back. To 'lift the robe and go' is like a terminal illness—one must be a man of exceptional talent to have a different way of life.
What if a swift falcon suddenly comes charging through the clouds? A net spread across the heavens, a hundred thousand layers deep."
Gui-zong took his seat and said, "Anyone who serves as a *shanzhishi* (good knowledge) and occupies this room must first commit the five acts of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya-karma*).

Only then will I show them the boiling cauldrons, the burning furnaces, the mountains of knives and trees of swords, and the pestles and grinding stones—what is called pulling out nails, extracting wedges, untying adhesions, and removing bonds.
If you are of inferior nature, you will surely turn back in dismay at the precipice. It is only those who..."
Only then can one draw near to the true son of the Dharma King. At such a time as this, what is it like?

[He] lets out a shout and rises. Donglin takes his seat and says: "The four or seven patriarchs of India and the two or three masters of the Tang land all drove their stakes and rowed their oars right here.
I, the new Donglin, will untie your moorings and set you free for all of you. Without even mentioning transcending the school or possessing extraordinary eyes, if you can..."
Gazing at one another with brows level, it may also be arranged beneath a bright window. If one were to act in such a manner, how could one avoid having their cheek slapped away?
Baoren, sitting firmly upon his seat, said: "O assembly, this chamber is deep and vast; day and night it constantly emits golden light. This is...
This is the realm of the Great Being Mañjuśrī; it is also called the "Heavenly Net. For those who can penetrate through it, a blow is struck even behind their heads.
For those who cannot penetrate it, they may as well walk alone in the crimson sky. Why? Because to kill a man, one must see blood.
"One must act with thoroughness when acting for others.
Chan Master Mianjie of Huazang sat upon the seat and said: "The lion teaches its cubs the secret of hunting; as soon as they intend to leap forward, they have already turned their bodies.
At the point where patterns are formed and blades cross in combat, even the hawk-eyed veteran loses his track in the moment. The ancients...
To speak in such a manner is like Xu Liu carrying a single plank.
When Chan Master Xueyan Qin occupied the hall at Longxing, he said: "This is where old Yuanwu severed the life-root of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
How should his unworthy descendants act today? He then folded his hands and said: "What leisure do I have for such things?"
Husheng occupied the chamber; he severed his own arm and stood in the snow; he carried stones and trod upon the pestle; he took people’s hearts and livers. Truly, one cannot bear such things!
As for Husheng, you may not show your face or commit theft within his domain. With his hand, he beckoned them, saying: "Withdraw! Withdraw!"
Guangxiao occupies the room: if you have one zhang, I give you back one zhang; if you have one chi, I give you back one chi.
If you merely bite down with determination and refuse to turn back, there will be a thunderbolt in broad daylight under the blue sky.
Chan Master Weian Shengshou occupied the abbot’s quarters. Holding up his staff, he said: "To grant is up to me; to take back is also up to me.
Even those with iron brows and copper heads must pass under my scrutiny. He struck the floor with the staff.
Chan Master Zang-sou Zhen of Mount Jing occupied the room, saying: "Is this place where you stand by my side after having made your inquiries and burned incense?
You dull-witted fellow! It may be tolerable for you to be at a loss yourself, but do not come here to put me to shame."
Chan Master Yuansou Duan occupied the room at Fengshan. Grasping his staff, he threw open the locks of the golden hall and struck the bell of the jade tower.
One who is not of our own lineage stands atop the highest peak and walks upon the deepest seabed; yet even such a person is not yet a monk of true standing.
When a lion cub lets out a roar across the *ṭhāsa* ground, it stands like a sheer cliff ten thousand fathoms high—yet even behind its head, there is still...
He missed one blow. Leaning on his staff, he rose.
Chan Master Chushi Qi said: "Fuzhen occupies this room; three feet of ground at the corner of the meditation seat is where all people beg for their lives.
To let them off by one move makes it even more unbearable. You have immeasurable transgressions, and I too have immeasurable [transgressions]."
What a transgression!
Tianning occupies the room, yet here there is no secret dharma transmitted in a private chamber.
A painful blow and a hot shout under the bright sun and clear sky—if you hesitate even for a moment, you go to Western Qin while I remain in Eastern Lu.
Fengshan occupied the room. When Linji received sixty blows from Huangbo, it was as if he had been brushed with a bundle of mugwort.
Is there any such monk today? Even if there were, you must still put him through the test before you can accept him.
Fundamental Awakening occupies the chamber: seizing the tiger’s head and grasping the tiger’s tail. Under the first phrase, the fundamental principle is clarified.
Even if you manage to clarify it, that is already the second phrase; if you do not clarify it, continue to investigate for another thirty years.
Guangxiao occupies the room; it is one zhang wide and ten chi high. Why is it that you all cannot enter and act within it?
An iron wall, an iron wall!
When Chan Master Yuguan occupied the abbot’s quarters at Jingci Temple, he scraped tortoise hair from the back of an iron ox;

morning after morning he struck three thousand blows, and evening after evening he struck eight hundred blows, cutting off the rabbit’s horns at the waist of a stone woman. Pointing east and drawing west, drumming his lips and wagging his tongue, he remained outside the gate.
With the spark struck from flint and the flash of lightning, he crossed the nine *ākalpas* upon the edge of an icicle, walking upon the blade of a sword.
The Master picked up the whole body [of the broom] and gave it thirty strokes with the handle. "If you do not come in this manner at all, what then?
He took up his staff and said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ!"
Chan Master Tianmu Li occupies the room at Guangshou: Śākyamuni shuts his room; playing with the false to represent the true. Vimalakīrti remains silent; playing with the true to represent the false.
Guangshou wields a single white staff: he strikes even if it is the Buddha who comes; he strikes even if it is the Patriarch who comes.
"Why is it thus? One, two, three, four, five. Jingci occupied the room [and said]:
"All the ancestral masters of antiquity and the old worthies of the world have been cutting off the horns on horseheads and plucking out the feathers from tortoise shells.
But what about the new Baoen? He picks the willow flowers—picks the willow flowers!"
Tiantong occupied the room; he shook the earth like a peal of thunder and flashed lightning.
A yakṣa’s head, a bodhisattva’s face—where, you all, will you meet him? He let out a shout.
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun occupied the abbot’s quarters at Guangfu; with a single blow, he was settled. He seized his topknot and went straight to the yamen without requiring a single blow;

though he may have been one who "embraces the stolen goods while crying out for injustice," and even if he were capable of hitting the mark a hundred times in a hundred shots, releasing both ends simultaneously—none of this is of any use beneath my Lingyan gate.
Holding up his staff and drawing a line, he said: "Three unbroken lines for Qian; six broken lines for Kun."
When Suīyán took up residence in his quarters, he said: "In my place, everything is merely ordinary.

If you come here to toy with mechanical devices and boast of your nimble hands, you are rubbing an itch on the head of a venomous snake or unfastening a bell from under the chin of a fierce tiger. My staff has not yet struck you! Why?
Because only when there are gnarled roots and knotted joints can sharp tools be applied; only when there are silver mountains and iron walls [can they be scaled]."
"Bring forth your tongs and hammers!
Chan Master Zhuang Da’an of Daming Temple occupied the abbot’s quarters at Jingshan Monastery. Holding up his staff, he said: "If it comes from the bright side, meet it with the bright side;
if it comes from the dark side, meet it with the dark side. If you can speak, twenty blows of the staff; if you cannot speak, twenty blows of the staff."
Why is this? Under a heavy reward, there must surely be brave men. [Master] Zhuo held up his staff.

To manifest the realization of Master Jun Chan’s universal compassion, he took up his staff and said: "If there were no one in this room who could attain realization by grasping the tip of the staff, I would swear that this staff of mine shall never be called a 'staff.
Is there such a person? He then issued the imperial decree to point out the flying dragon horse; [the horse] was lame.
The turtle pokes its head out.

Chan Master Folangxing of Shushan occupies the room; his mastery over killing and giving life is free and unrestrained. Across ten feet in every direction—above, below, and the four quarters—there are silver mountains and iron walls.
Leaning his staff across them, he says, "Just to open up a single thread," and with a back-splitting blow from his black cane, he lets out a shout.
"Ha! Master Shiwu Hong took up residence in the hall, held up his staff, and said:

"All the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past, all the old monks of the world—they have all been tossing dust upon the bottom of the water and plucking willow flowers from within the fire. Now, at Fuyuan..."
"How is it? [The Master] planted his staff and let out a shout.
Chan Master Wuwen Can occupied the room and said: "Today this mountain monk shall open the gates of hell;
I invite all people throughout the great earth to create the karma of hell and realize the fruit of hell. If there should be even one person who becomes a Buddha or a Patriarch, I vow never to..."
He attained perfect enlightenment.
Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun took possession of the room; leaning his staff across it and looking left and right, he asked, "Is there anyone?
Is there anyone? He struck once and said, "No one has bid the price; I shall strike and give him three hundred."
Chan Master Nan Shiyou occupies the room of the State-Protecting [Temple]. How can one who is so coarse and clumsy be fit for carving and polishing?
Even if you possess works of transcendent brilliance, first return to me the official certificate of your own Way.
Jingshan entered the room, laid his staff across it horizontally, and said, "By merely doing so, you have already been left behind by me.
What is the use of further wagging your lips and moving your tongue? He drew a line with the staff and then rose.
When Chan Master Liaoyuan Yu took up residence at Kaifu, the genuine did not conceal the false, and the crooked could not hide the straight. Rocks split and mists collapsed;
thunder roared and lightning flashed. Having turned his body around, he had yet to receive a blow of the staff. He let out a shout.

Benjue occupied the room. Leaning his staff across it horizontally, he said, "There is a hand that does not err regarding the orthodox or the biased, and a function that possesses the simultaneous act of pecking and striking.
All such must be ranked below the wind. He struck the ground with his staff and let out a shout.
Lingyan occupies this room; it is a place where the venerable masters of old have roasted Buddhas, refined patriarchs, forged saints, and melted away ordinary people.
The new elder levels the high and accommodates the low, abandons the cramped for the spacious, and shall allow you all to breathe freely.
Chan Master Miyun Wu took his seat in the room. Occupying this room and exercising this command, he invited the monks of the world to come and beg for their lives;
one by one, he pressed them down headlong. He struck the floor with his staff and then rose.
Chan Master Luo’an asked: "When Tiantai came, he passed through here; when Nanyue came, he passed through here.
Throughout the four great continents, wherever the streets were filled and the roads were blocked, there was no one who did not verify their practice here."
To let go is up to me; to grasp tightly is also up to me. (He plants his staff upright and says: "Today, one must not engage in frivolous discourse.
Master Mumen Chushi occupies this room; he provides the fodder of the fundamental path and does not follow worldly sentiments.
If you point to your chest or your ribs behind my back, this mountain monk will likewise act as if he neither sees nor hears you. But if you are a person of...
The Han [monk] attempted to leap through the Dragon Gate. There, baring his fangs and showing his claws, he could not avoid the thunderclaps crashing in the blue sky.
Why? Unless one enters the waves that startle the world, it is difficult to encounter a fish that satisfies one’s heart.
"Occupying this room, you may leap as much as you wish at the diamond circle cast forth; you may swallow as many as you can of the chestnut thorns thrust out.
Yet I, this mountain monk, still have thirty blows remaining for you. Why? Because in the school of Linji, no order goes unexecuted.
He struck his staff once.
Chan Master Hongjue Wenyi occupies the room; closing the door and sleeping, he receives those of the highest capacity. Those of middling or lower capacity enter the garden to dig the earth.
If one waits for him to raise his whisk or strike the meditation seat, it is all just the "bottom line" of Muzhou. He lets out a shout:
"Eight blows for thirteen—this tally has not yet reached you."
Occupying the chamber, Baiyun descended from his seat; the pestle-head caused the flowers to bloom. When a guest arrives, there is no formal etiquette;
mugwort decoction serves as tea. Although this is so, selling gold will never be equated with mixing it with sand.

**Outline for Entering the Monastery** (When a former master enters the hall, they invariably await an imperial decree or wait for an invitation from the local authorities before proceeding; thus, after taking possession of the quarters upon arrival at the monastery, they simply conduct the formal *shangtang* as usual.
Chan Master Yangqi Huai ascends the hall upon entering the monastery: Mist shrouds the vast sky; wind rises across the great fields. The hundred grasses and trees...
The Great Lion Roar is made by the wooden figure; it expounds the Mahāprajñāpāramitā. The Buddhas of the three periods of time are turning the Great Dharma Wheel beneath the feet of you all.
If you can understand this, your efforts will not have been in vain; if you do not understand, they will be.
"Do not say the mountain ridges of Yangqi are steep; ahead lies yet another highest peak.
When Chan Master Baoning Yong entered the monastery and ascended the hall to teach, he said: "If you wish to ascend this seat, you must first pay homage to Mount Sumeru and King Dīpa.
But tell me, where is Mount Sumeru and King Dīpa? And furthermore, toward what place do you pay homage? Is it with the mind?"
Is it that both mental conceptions and objective referents are forgotten? Is it that mind and objects are one and the same? Or is it that the myriad dharmas are empty and still?
If your understanding is such as this, you have not yet emerged from the common stream. Since it is not like this, then how is it? "A blow strikes the head of the stone man;
*bok bok*, he speaks of the actual reality. Even if one possesses vast learning, a powerful memory, worldly wisdom, and eloquence, and attains the Great Totality—
Possessing complete and unimpeded eloquence, he entered into the direct encounter at the gate of the Patriarch.
Therefore, this matter cannot be sought with a conscious mind, nor can it be attained through a mindless state; it cannot be constructed through speech, nor communicated through silent stillness.

It is beyond gain and loss, right and wrong, the monastic and the lay, the noble and the humble, and the distinctions between ordinary beings and sages, nor is it a matter of emotional capacity or intellectual understanding.
It is beyond the reach of others. When people arrive here, how can they be "just as they are"? If one is a true man of great character, then directly beneath, the real cannot be hidden by the false;
only when one personally consents at the most intimate point does one become truly close. When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, I have already buried [the truth] myself.
Now, is there anyone who will not be deceived? After a long silence, he said: "Throughout my life, my liver..."
He pours out his heart toward others; though they are acquaintances, he treats them as if they were strangers. He then picks up his staff and says: "Countless clouds and mountains cannot conceal him;
yet he carries his cane and enters the marketplace. Knocking at a thousand doors and ten thousand households, today he stands clearly upon the Phoenix Terrace.
With a single strike, he sets the staff down and descends from his seat.
When Chan Master Xuedou Xian entered the monastery at Cuifeng and ascended the hall to teach, many people harbored doubts about the future of Cuifeng;
yet once they arrived in person, they found the entire realm was serene and still—this was no different from Sudhana entering the gates of the pavilions and momentarily withdrawing his thoughts.

There is nothing that can compare to the distinct monastic regulations within Vimalakīrti’s world held in the palm of his hand. It is hoped that all people will be fully satisfied by beholding this sight, thereby providing them with consolation and joy.
Master Wuzu Yan, upon entering the monastery, ascended the hall and said, citing the Patriarch’s words: "I have come to this land to transmit the Dharma."
To save those lost in delusion: one flower opens into five petals; the fruiting occurs spontaneously. Great Master Bodhidharma came with his feet and spoke with his mouth;
yet the descendants of later generations have mostly fallen into calculating deliberation. Do you wish to understand the place where the flowers bloom and the fruit ripens?
Pear trees of Zhengzhou, jujubes of Qingzhou—among all things, nothing surpasses a good source.
Chan Master Zhenjing Wen ascends the hall upon entering his post at Shengshou Monastery: "The green mountains and blue waters cannot detain him;
the white days and red dust he returns to of their own accord. Now there is no place to hide; so let us blend with the mundane and harmonize with the light, with heads ashen and faces like dust."
He laughs at those in the forest retreats; people must also laugh. If you can laugh, it is most wondrous.
Having picked up a tattered cotton robe from the crossroads, he shakes off the dust and shows it to all: "Is it good? Is it bad? Do you understand? Do you not understand?
Let him sing and shout from the butcher's block. He lets out a roar and says: "Turn your heads and look back!"
Upon entering the monastery at Guizong, he ascended the hall and said: "The essential mystery of the Buddha-dharma lies simply in returning to its source.

If one returns to the source, naturally there is neither 'can' nor 'cannot'; everything is fully manifest, and the Sea-Seal radiates its light. Now, together with the great assembly, we have already returned to the source and abide in the fundamental limit of equality.
I dare ask: what is this source? What is this essential mystery? After a long silence, he said: "It is simply..."
To clarify this to the utmost would only cause what is attained to be delayed.
Master Yuechan Yunyun, upon entering the monastery at Cuiyan, ascended the hall and said: "In years past, this mountain monk once visited; today I come again.
Not only has human fellowship increased in joy, but the forests and springs have grown even more beautiful. Now tell me, how can one act without harming the principle of things?"
"How do you express this? After a long silence, he said: "The heavens are high in the southeast; the earth slopes toward the northwest. He then descended from his seat.

When the Dharma Wheel enters the monastery, the Dharma does not arise in isolation; it manifests only by relying on conditions. The Way does not travel in vain; it responds as soon as it encounters circumstances.
However, those who are masters of the universal way surely know where they must return. For those who wander and travel, what prevents them from advancing further?
Is there anyone such? After a long silence, he said: "When the fishing pole is worn out, plant bamboo again; do not calculate the time or effort, but rest as soon as you have attained it."
When Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin entered the monastery of Jia Shan, the green mountains beneath the gate were like dappled ink, and the fine rain along the road was like rich manure.
On the paths of Lingyun, peach blossoms bloomed; everywhere, their fragrance overflowed the eyes. By the cliffs of Xiangyan, emerald bamboos constantly stirred their shadows and swayed in the wind.
Truly, with a single blow one forgets all that is known, and with a single glance all doubt is severed—yet one cannot help but still...

Pause and observe. You have not yet penetrated through form and sound. If you can see the form that is no-form and hear the sound that is no-sound, you will turn the head of the path and overturn the pivot of the lock.
Every phrase transcends Buddhas and Patriarchs; every speck of dust shines from antiquity to the present.

Everywhere, one is detached from form and severed from names; each and every one cuts through nails and hacks iron. Outside the mind there is no dharma; outside dharmas there is no mind. To employ [this]—
The sword in the King’s treasury; the release of a crossbow bolt weighing a thousand *qun*; standing like a cliff ten thousand *ren* high;

sitting and cutting off the ten directions—this is how one may enter the Gate of Great Liberation and transmit the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye. Toward the era of Yao and the sun of Shun, we shall together enjoy peace and prosperity;

with bellies drummed and songs sung, we return home to sit securely. But as for the phrase "arriving home," how do you speak of it? Simply: "I only wish that the spring breeze would exert its full strength."
At one time, it blew into my gate. He further said: "In the past, it was transmitted that Ming possessed a strategy for piercing the heavens and a divine mechanism for spanning the seas;
he caused a tongueless man to speak words of non-meaning. He gathered Lopu, received Qingfeng, discerned Shishuang, and honored Furi.
His 'precipice phrases' were steep, his 'tiger-trapping mechanism' was profound. Like lightning striking and stars flying, like pearls rolling and jade turning, he established this treasure."
The exemplary standards of the monastery remain fully intact, yet this mountain monk is mediocre in all matters; how can he hope to follow in his illustrious footsteps?

Chan Master Chu-shih Qi resided at Fu-zhen. A decree from the Xing-zheng Yuan (Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs) arrived: "On the summit of a solitary peak, he has constructed a thatched hut;
though he possesses a mouth, it is fit only to hang on the wall. At the crossroads of the city, he unties his cloth bag;

only by entering the water can one see the tall man. Why does he reach such a state? The decree continues: "With the very hands that mend the imperial robes and season the soup, he turns the pivot..."
The Tathāgata’s Wheel of the True Dharma.
Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun, while residing at Jiqing Monastery, held up an official notice and addressed the assembly, saying: "With a single bamboo pole, he established a monastery;
all is complete according to his will. With eighty *qing* of consecrated ground, the site was perfected right where it stood. Today, the various officials have respectfully received [this decree]."
Imperial Decree: A memorial has been prepared to earnestly invite you to serve as the founding patriarch. How shall the first phrase be revealed?
The Golden Wheel governs the three thousand worlds; the Jade Calendar extends for ten million springs.

Chan Master Yangqi Huaihui’s Hall-opening Sermon at Xinghua Temple, featuring the Dharma words from the *Fahua Shu* (Commentary on the Lotus Sutra) by Hufa. The Provincial Governor, Lord Longtu, presented the formal invitation document (*shu*) to the Master.
As soon as the Master received it, he held it up and said: "Assembly! The Provincial Governor, Lord Longtu, the Cavalier Attendant, and all the officials have come entirely for the sake of you all."
People say they have understood the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*). Do you all know it? If you do, then the state and the family will be at peace, as one and the same household.
If you do not, trouble yourself to have the Monastic Administrator (*sengzheng*) and the Ritual Master (*biaobai*) recite it for you, so that all people under heaven may come to know.
When Chan Master Longmen Yuan opened the hall at Tianning Monastery, the presiding official presented him with a formal petition. Upon receiving it, the Master addressed the assembly, saying:
"Heaven cannot cover it; earth cannot bear it. It leaks the celestial mechanism, and every word is worthy of love.
But tell me, what are these words worthy of love? After a long silence, he said: "Take this clearly to heart and present it to a master. He then passed it to [the official] Biao.
Baizhang said:
On the day Chan Master Zhenjing Wen opened the hall at Baofeng, he received the memorial from the hand of the Left Minister and addressed the assembly, saying:
"The transmission bestowed by the Left Minister is brilliantly manifest before us; let Lestam present it, and you must clearly realize it. Whether you realize it or not..."

The *jian* (offering) is passed to the *biaobai* (the ritual master). The *biaobai* prepares to receive it, but [the Master] withdraws it, saying: "Has it not been said? 'The authority is in one's hand;
bestowal and withdrawal are according to the occasion. It is not only Lestan who is thus; the various officials of the Left Bureau possess the full power of supernatural transformations.
He then passes it to the *biaobai*.
When Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin ascended the hall, he received the ceremonial proclamation from the hands of the Prefect and presented it to the assembly, saying:
"Every character expounds immeasurable meaning; every phrase is like the udumbara flower. It is the hammer and tongs of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, and the banner of praise for devas and humans."
Held up before the assembly, the patterns are already manifest; it is like adding flowers upon brocade—please state once more how this was done.
Opening the hall, the Prefect Yan Kangdu presented the formal petition to the Master. Having received it, the Master said: "The ready-made public case has been brought to its ultimate conclusion."
The sound of gold striking the earth reveals the ancient tradition of the monasteries; its celestial brilliance emerges from the great brush of a master hand, manifesting the Supreme Vehicle.
Desiring that this be heard throughout the four seas, I request that the Sangha Rectifier proclaim it aloud.

Upon arriving at Nankang Commandery, he ascended the hall and, receiving the formal letter from the hands of the Prefect, addressed the assembly, saying: "Do you see? It is revealed directly before you, manifest and immediate.
A hundred layers and a thousand folds, penetrating in seven ways and open in eight directions.

This is the very core of every master; in every instance, it is the supreme vehicle of the ancestral school. To take this up immediately would still leave something to be desired; yet if you have not yet realized it..."
He requested the Sangzheng to explain it once more.
When Chan Master Dahui Gaofeng presided over the opening of the hall at Mingqing Temple, he held up the ceremonial document and addressed the assembly, saying:

"The Chancellor, the State Protector, has entered the Samādhi of Skillfully Knowing All Arts; from the tip of his hair-pen he radiates great light, and without moving his tongue, he expounds the Dharma."
The forty-two gates of Prajñāpāramitā are now complete. Can you still believe this?
If you cannot yet believe it, I request the表白 (Biao-bai) to once again bring it forth, so that those who have not heard may hear, and those who have not believed may believe.

Chan Master Mianjie received the memorial for his ordination presented by the Prefectural Governor. Upon receiving it, he said: "To exhaust all profound dialectics is like placing a single hair in the vast void;
to exhaust the world’s pivotal mechanisms ultimately does not depart from right mindfulness.
He then held up the memorial and called to the assembly, saying: "Right mindfulness has arisen! But tell me, what is the matter within it? He then requested the official to explain it further.
The announcement was read aloud.
Master [Xuedou] received the memorial submitted by the Prefectural Pacifier, Minister Du, and rising, he said:

"For forty-nine years, Śākyamuni Buddha spoke crosswise and spoke straight; that which could not be spoken is entirely flowing forth from within this very place, encompassing all existence within its fold."

Encompassing the ten voids, one may attain such faith. Thus, the imperial grace and the Buddha’s grace will be repaid all at once. Should this not yet be so, what prevents one from revealing the truth?
Chan Master Chu-shih Qi, while residing at Fengshan, took up the memorial from the Xuanzheng Yuan and said: "White clouds emerge from the mountain peaks; they are originally without [a fixed place]."
Mind! Seeking a pearl in red water, one returns empty-handed to the *wangxiang* (the formless spirit). In myriad ways, preserve this Way; in a single flavor, trust in past conditions.
Residing at Guangxiao, he held up the memorial from the Xingzheng Yuan. Harmonizing yin and yang, he penetrates the workings of creation;
he illuminates the Buddha-sun and universally spreads the true wind. To him, a man of great power, belongs this deed of great power. He called to the assembly, saying:
Look up with high resolve!

Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun’s Preface to the *Nian-yuan* (Picking-up-Courtyard) Collection at Zhongtianzhu states: "This is the phrase by which the Great Chancellor personally received the prediction of enlightenment at Vulture Peak.
It has been entrusted to this mountain monk, so that those who have not heard it may hear it, and those who have not seen it may see it."
When Chan Master Liaoyuan Yu resided at Lingyan, he took up the monastery’s memorial address. With the scales of judgment in his hand, he granted or withdrew as the occasion required.
His governance spread far and wide; like the wind passing over grass, all bowed down in submission.
Chan Master Shiwu Hong held up the memorial draft from the Governor of Guangjiao and said:
"This old Gautama’s unsolved case from two thousand years ago—today, Upasaka Hong shall settle it in the hands of the official of the Guangjiao Prefecture.
He presented the draft, saying: "The contents submitted are true to the facts."
When Chan Master Yuejiang Yin resided at Yuwang Temple, he took up the memorial from the Guangjiao Prefecture;
wielding the halberd of Ruyang, he restored the radiance of the Buddha-sun and caused the Great Teaching to flourish—this stands as the foremost achievement.
Chan Master Ruohan’s Opening Address for the Hall: The Emperor’s decree within the realm; the General’s command beyond the pass.
With a single word, heaven and earth are settled; all monks beg for their lives.

I take up the memorial from the provincial government. Since that time on Vulture Peak, the power of the entrustment has remained unforgotten; suddenly presented before us, it manifests most extraordinary wonders.
Having no way to avoid it, there is nowhere to hide. Where a favorable breeze escorts it, the rain of flowers falls once more in profusion.
Holding up the county memorial: For ages he has buried his head in the mountain valleys; meeting him is not as good as hearing his name.

Now that his reputation has truly become illustrious, it depends on everyone recognizing this. Clouds follow the dragon, winds follow the tiger; listen to the price, not the sound. All are equally masterful hands.

Zhu Qing-shan presented a memorial to the Master for the protection of the Dharma. The Master received the memorial and said: "Having seen it with my own eyes and heard it with my own ears, the words are upright and the speech is precise.

It reveals what was previously hidden with a fresh brilliance, causing the old colors to shine once more. To manifest the orthodox and suppress the heterodox, to discern demons and distinguish the true—this must be done by a person of this caliber before such words can be understood.
But tell me, what kind of words are these? Let the Rector try to proclaim them."
The *Fahufa Shu* (Commentary on Protecting the Dharma). Every inch of silk and every foot of brocade shines with luster and grace upon the stream; thus one may know the propriety of the rite.

As jade turns and pearls revolve, Chan Master Hongjue Man’s *Nianshu* (Excerpts from the Commentary) says: "To hold fast to the 'Great Person' (*shang daren*) and manifest the 'Qiu Yiji'—this relies entirely upon this true mantra.
If you are one who recognizes the tail by grasping the head, you will immediately [attain it] before the hair-pen has even moved."
One can understand the ritual propriety here. Why need one wait until the full brilliance of the patterns is revealed before manifesting the three thousand transformations accordingly?
Even so, though one holds the "Night-Bright Talisman" in hand, how many truly know the dawn of heaven? Please, Venerable Karmadāna, recite it now.
A Preface for the "Discourse on the Extra-Mundane" by Chan Master Yuansou Duan. Vast and profound, within it lies an essence; hazy and indistinct, within it lies a substance.
For those who know before the word is raised, there is truly no need for speech. Yet this embroidered banner and jade-rolled scroll—how [wondrous it is]!
Attained while dwelling here. Stop up your ears and listen clearly.
This is a preface written by Fangwai at Mount Jing: every word reveals the ultimate truth; every sentence flows toward the source.
The Elder Vimalakīrti of old in the Western Heaven; Master Pangyun of today in this Eastern Land.
A Memorial for Chan Master Chushi Qi’s Lay Friends: A single phrase has no "this" or "that. Is there anything hidden from me?
I have nothing hidden from you.
A Memorial for the Chan Master Shuzhong Yun’s Lay Associates: "The nostrils of Confucius and the eyes of Bodhidharma are both right here.
When their fundamental source is discussed, they arise from one origin; when their merits are compared, each possesses eight hundred [virtues].
Yet, there is a certain point of ambiguity herein that no one, past or present, has ever spoken of. The Memorial states: "It is the sword that kills, the blade that gives life."
A Dharma Discourse on the Inscription for the Main Gate at Lingyan, by Chan Master Nan Shi Xiu. Each phrase is a phrase; it does not involve literary artifice at all.
One truly knows that these words from within the house naturally possess neither interior nor exterior.
The Preface to the Monastery Gate: A man of the house speaks the language of the house. When the tea is ready, it is plucked; when the sun shines, the straw sandals are spread out to dry.
The Preface to the Monastery Gate: Hanging the sword between the brows, one throws down the chestnut thorn. Yangqi and Miaoxi were of one mind without prior consultation.
The Preface for the Entrance of Chan Master Shuzhong Yun into Lingyan Mountain on Mount Xiangshan: Before entering the gate of Lingyan, you people are the masters and this mountain monk is the guest.
Once having entered the gate of Lingyan, this mountain monk is the master and you people are the guests.
Now, how do you express the phrase in which guest and host are merged? A cast-iron K'un-lun man beneath a golden incense burner.
Chan Master Liaohan Yu’s Preface for the Monastery Gate: There is host and guest, there is response and challenge;
cutting off the tongue, one blow serves as two.
Preface for the Abbot’s Seat at Benjue Mountain: Before entering the gate, there is a single phrase; having arrived here, not even half a word remains.
Absolutely nothing. Ultimately, how is it? *Sulu sulu*.
This is the preface to the monastic regulations by Chan Master Folangxing: "If one is a member of this family, do not guard the 'roundabout storehouse.
Erect the Dharma banner at the tips of the hundred grasses; clouds follow the dragon, and wind follows the tiger."
Chan Master Shiwu Hong held up the monastery’s introductory statement and said: "The size of the cauldron and the length of the ladle handle are matters of the household;
why must they be measured and deliberated?"

Chan Master Hongjue Wenyin’s Preface for the Mountain Gate: In the case of a sovereign, it is called a decree; in the case of a state, it is called an edict; in the case of an envoy, it is called a warrant;
in the case of this mountain monk, what is it? The Buddhas and patriarchs listen to its authority; humans and devas alike beg for their lives.

Chan Master Yuansou Duan held up the memorial inscriptions from various mountains for his tenure at Lingyin Temple and said: "The eminent elders and renowned figures of this entire prefecture have used these to pierce the nostrils of the patch-robed monks throughout the world.
Yet even the 'Four Sevens' of India could not produce them, nor the 'Two or Three' of this land."
It cannot be concealed.
This is the preface by Chan Master Chushih Qi for the various mountain monasteries of the Two Zhe regions: "The true does not mask the false; the crooked does not hide the straight.
The setting clouds fly alongside the solitary wild goose; the autumn waters share the same hue as the vast sky."

I take up the commentaries of the various mountains. From the north and south of the Yangtze to the west and east of Zhejiang—within the same there is difference, and within the different there is sameness.
The wild colors are no longer severed by mountains; the heavenly light directly communicates with the waters. Do you understand?
If not, look at the notes below.
The Preface by Chan Master Nan Shiyou for the Various Mountains of Pumen: "To study is called 'hearing'; to transcend study is called 'neighboring' [the ultimate].
After a long silence: "The Yellow River flows in nine bends; its waters emerge from Kunlun."
The Memorial for Chan Master Liaoyuan Yu’s Installation at Kaifu by Various Mountains: When a single Buddha appears in the world, each sits upon a lotus flower;
their reflections meet and their brilliance connects, yet they do not borrow from one another.
Master Shuzhong Yun’s Dharma Words for the Preface to the Three Schools at Ruyuan:
Holding up the Preface to the Three Schools of Mingzhou—Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The breeze is clear over the land of the Three Buddhas; the moon is bright upon Mount Siming.
Chan Master Bongseong’s *Commentary on the Three Schools*: In the eastern district, ginger is sold; beneath the great ocean, the fires glow crimson.
In the western county, soapberry pods are peddled; atop Mount Sumeru, the waves overturn the void. The commoner hears the strange customs from next door;
the gentleman shares the same breeze across a thousand miles.
The Dharma Words for the "Preamble to the Lineage" by Chan Master Fulang Xing. This is a ladder provided by the various elder monks of the capital monasteries for someone to climb a tree.
How, ultimately, is it to be judged? He further said: "There are many who praise him, and many who revile him."
Those who know this are not few; they understand that all alike receive it and all alike do not receive it. The great earth, mountains, and rivers are bright with the blazing sun.

This is the Preface to the Chan Master Nan Shiyou’s Founding of a Monastery in the Imperial Capital: he erected the banner of the Dharma in the capital city and fanned the true wind during the Semblance Age.
The Elephant King turns in circles; the Lion roars with vigor.
Master Chanist Nan Shi Xu’s *Jianghu Shu* (Notes on the Rivers and Lakes). An ancient said, "A thousand miles share the same wind. What is this "same wind"?
A sentence on the wind: When Dīpaṃkara was at the Golden Ground, he beckoned from afar; when the Wise One was at Jiangling, he nodded his head in the dark.

A commentary on rivers and lakes: Words of like mind have a fragrance like that of orchids. It is easy to distinguish dragons from snakes, yet difficult for patch-robed monks to avoid being over-simplistic.
The Preface for Chan Master Liaoyuan Yu by Jianghu: With an iron heart and stone entrails, and a river-tongue and ocean-mouth, to praise him is like flowers blooming on a pestle;
to disparage him is to find a hundred flaws in the face of a Buddha. Where praise and disparagement do not reach, he faces south and gazes at the Big Dipper.
Master Folangxing’s “Jianghu Shu” (Roving the World): You come in such a manner, and I am in such a state. Public judgment and personal bias both converge in the primary principle (*paramārtha*).
Amidst the frost and snow where willow catkins drift, white egrets frolic at their ease together.
Chan Master Wuwen Can’s “Jianghu Su” (Draft for the Jianghu Community): “Malicious acquaintances, malicious curses—my whole body is a mouth, unable to offer a defense.
The draft says: ‘The Head Seat shall simply cover it up.’”
On the day of opening the hall, Chan Master Dingyin of Shen Ding pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "Before ascending this seat, my work of transforming conditions was already complete.
Do you all understand? If you understand, you may disperse; if you do not disperse, I cannot help but ascend."
This concludes the second chapter, "Entering the Hall," from this seat. You should not find fault with this mountain monk.
On the day Master Chan Master Baoning Yong ascended the hall, he pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "The Buddhas of the three periods and the patriarchs of all times..."
Everything has been completed here by turning the Great Dharma Wheel. It has now passed beneath the feet of all of you.
Do you see it? If you see it, the eyebrows and eyelashes are constantly emitting radiance. If you do not see it, look! Look!
This mountain monk is entering the mud and the water with every step.
When Chan Master Wuzu Yan opened the hall at Haihui Monastery, after the proclamation of the formal documents was finished, he said: "The documents have all been read at once.
For those who possess the diamond eye, what need is there to repeat the verses? Nevertheless, matters are never absolute."
On the day Chan Master Zhenjing Wen ascended the hall, after he had finished proclaiming the memorial, he said: "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas;
yet the Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him, and he could not attain the Way of Buddhahood. Today, surrounded by the fourfold assembly, does the Buddha-dharma manifest before you?
Is it attained or not? After a long silence, he said: "If one wishes to travel a thousand li, the first step is the beginning. Thereupon, he ascended the seat.
The Seat.
Chan Master Nianguan of Suzhou Beichen ascends the hall for the opening of the assembly. It being precisely the ninth day, he points to the Dharma seat and says:
"An inch of ash within the breast has long since grown cold; a thousand strands of snow upon the head have not yet melted. These aged feet are fit only for walking on level ground."
Not knowing for what reason he ascended once more, he took his seat upon the dais. (When Lord Wei Pi, the Prime Minister, heard of this, he struck his hand-clappers incessantly.
Chan Master Xuedou Xian, while presiding over the Dharma seat at Cuifeng, looked out at the assembly and said:

"If we speak of seeing one another in accordance with the fundamental essence, there is no need to ascend this high seat. He then pointed with his finger and said: "Everyone, follow the mountain monk’s hand and look! There was none.
He measured the Buddha-lands, all appearing simultaneously before him. He gazed at each one with meticulous attention;
yet, as he could not discern their ultimate boundaries, he was inevitably left "dragging through mud and water. Thereupon, he ascended the seat.
Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin, upon ascending the hall, pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "The Buddhas of the three periods turn the wheel of the Dharma here;
the ancestral masters of successive generations have raised the seal of the patriarchs here. If you wish to travel a thousand miles, the first step must be taken;
there is no avoiding the necessity of beginning by sketching out the model."
At the opening of the hall during the Chongning era, [Changsha] pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "O Great Assembly! This one path is known by all the sages of the past.
Walking slowly, one tramples the sound of flowing water; looking out freely, one traces the tracks of soaring birds. But tell me, how does one advance further?
To raise the signless seal of Vairocana, one must walk upon the summit of a thousand peaks."
Standing at Mount Jangshan, he pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "High and lofty, it has no exterior; deep and profound, it has no limit.
