There is no further need to pay homage to the Lamp of Sumeru; with every step upon the stairway, the whole body is present. Now tell me, what is this? Look, look!"
Zhu Tianning pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "The robe of gentle forbearance; the emptiness of all dharmas as the seat. Having donned this robe, one must surely occupy this seat.
Moreover, the Buddhas and the ancestral patriarchs have relied upon these as their ladder and their vessel. Do you see? When there is a branch, grasp the branch;
when there is no branch, follow the precedent."
Pointing to the Dharma seat as he enters, he said: "How could thirty-two thousand lion thrones compare to this simple wooden chair?

It cuts off both the Reward-body and Transformation-bodies Buddhas, transcending hearing, seeing, knowing, and perceiving. It raises high the noble tradition of Vulture Peak and looks up to pray for the Sage Emperor’s long life.
Do you see it? Look at the time when the command is issued."
While residing at Yunju, he first received an imperial decree at Yongxi Temple. Pointing to the Dharma seat, he said:

"Borrowing the precious throne of Yongxi and lifting the golden circle of Yangqi, it is realized directly here and now; grasp it clearly! Do you understand thoroughly? The adamantine true body is revealed in its majestic presence;
every step one takes is nothing other than the Great Dharma Assembly. Standing abruptly atop the crown of Vairocana’s head, what more could there be?"
He took his place before the Lamp-King (Dīpaṃkara). Look, look!
Zen Master Yunfeng Yue, upon ascending the hall at Shanglan, pointed to the Dharma-seat and said: "Is there anyone here who does not suffer deception?
If there is, come forward, overturn the meditation seat, and shout to disperse the assembly! Yet even so, you would still not be a true master. For now...

"I have saved half of you. Is there anyone else? After a long silence, he said, "Since no one has come forward, I shall today spare no effort—though it may cost me my eyebrows—to point out a deer as a horse and turn the sun into the moon.
Do not blame me for this thirty years from now. He then ascended the seat.

When Chan Master Longmen Yuan ascended the Dharma seat at Tianning Monastery to open the hall, he pointed to it and said, "Do the ancient sages come for the sake of the Dharma, or do they come for the sake of the seat?
I have come for the sake of the Dharma, not for the sake of the seat. The Master (Yunmen) exclaimed, "What kind of talk is this?"
Chan Master Dahuai Gao, at Jingshan, pointed to the Dharma seat and called to the assembly, saying: "Do you see?

It cuts off the path of the ancient Buddhas and causes a thousand demons and a hundred monsters to flee in hiding. Even if it were Mount Sumeru or King Lamp-Wielder, one must still quickly prostrate three times. He gave a shout.
Residing once again at Jingshan, he pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "The crown of Vairocana’s head—every person has the aspiration to travel its upper reaches.
Yet when questioned about the path, ten out of twenty do not know where it leads. Do you all wish to recognize this path?
After a long silence, he said: 'Look!'"
At the Dharma seat of Longxing, Master Xueyan Qin said: "Hundreds of thousands of Buddhas and Patriarchs have defecated here;
a sky-reaching stench pervades the Sahā world. The new Longxing cannot help but pour out the waters of the Xiang River to wash it clean.
Yet the mess only becomes greater.
Dwelling upon the Dharma-seat of Mount Yangshan, the precious mirror hangs high and precious flowers scatter about; this is indeed something everyone knows exists.
But tell me, what dharma did Sumeru-dīpa-rāja ultimately preach? He kicks it seven ways and tramples it eight ways.
Chan Master Weian pointed to his seat at Shengshou Monastery and said: "Take one step forward; take one step higher.
Tread upon the summit, and your entire being will be revealed in its nakedness. He then snapped his fingers and said: "Sumeru-dīpa-rāja, go over there!"
Chan Master Yuansou Duan pointed toward the Dharma seat in Central India and said:
"The ancient old bald-headed fellow roared a thunderclap in the blue sky and stirred up waves upon level ground right here. New Elder, you must take a different path.
He took a sudden step forward and said: "One, two, three, four, five."
Chan Master Fuzhen of Chushi Qi pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "Have you come for the sake of the Dharma, or for the sake of this seat?
A magnificent hawk soaring toward the clouds should seize the moment; a weary fish stuck in a shallow pool merely exhausts itself splashing the waves."
I have occupied the Dharma seat at Tianning and finished preaching the Dharma for everyone in the Ling Shan Hall. Did you hear it?
If you did not hear it, you cannot avoid being like someone drawing legs on a snake.
Juzhun Benjue pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "The 'White Snow' of the springtime has a lofty melody that finds few who can harmonize with it;
yet village songs and community dances find their place everywhere. Today, New Benjue shall join you at this table to strike the gavel."
When Chan Master Da’an Zhuang pointed to the seat at Yunju, the former masters of old regarded this position as the ultimate standard.
Yet, Senior Monk Zhuang saw it as merely ordinary.
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun occupied the Dharma seat at Ruiyan. Where there is level ground, he creates precipices; where there is solitary loftiness, he makes it plain and easy.
This is what has been used constantly by those of all ages. Today, I shall certainly not deceive you all by merely following a mold or copying bricks here.
Nevertheless, "if you do not take it when you see it, it will be difficult to forget for a thousand years. For now, let us cut off the very summit of Vairocana.
“How do you express this? The assembly was speechless. He then said, “I should have let it pass.
Chan Master Yuguan Ji pointed to the Dharma seat at Jingci Temple and said, “The entire world of the ten directions is the Lion’s Seat of Universal Radiance.
Buddhas and sentient beings arise and sit upon it together. Why then does this mountain monk today specifically [take it]?”
The ground rises high. I only fear that you all may be ignorant of its origin.
Chan Master Shiwu Gong pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "This is the precious throne of devas and humans; it is a curved wooden bench. If I wish to sit upon it now, I shall sit;
I will not further pay homage to the King of Mount Sumeru. He then ascended the seat.
Chan Master Yuejiang Yin, at Yuyuan Temple, pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "Standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high—there is no need to ascend it.
Blending water with mud, let us briefly open a single thread."
When Chan Master Liaohan Yu occupied the seat at Benjue Temple, he pointed to the Dharma throne and said:

"Treading high upon the crown of Vairocana, not receiving instruction from Śākyamuni—this is the samādhi you all practice constantly. I, this mountain monk, shall now comply with the exigencies of the times and blend the mud and water."
Chan Master Folangxing pointed to the Dharma seat at Tiantong and, looking out over the assembly, said: "A thousand opportunities and ten thousand opportunities are but a single opportunity;

a thousand steps and ten thousand steps are but a single step. Seizing the path and cutting off the ten directions with a lion’s roar—this is the upward road that penetrates everywhere in all seven directions and eight openings.
He let out a shout.

Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun, while presiding at Zhong Tianzhu, pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "Severing the heads of both the *nirmāṇakāya* and *saṃbhogakāya* Buddhas, one does not fall into the stages of the profound and subtle.
[This is the realm of] Dou Ba’s patchwork robe and Yunmen’s ‘the seventh day’."
Zhu Jiqing pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "Wiping away this land and the Western Heaven, sitting and cutting off all distinctions and differences;
leveling the high by means of the low, looking through the hole to drive in the wedge."
Chan Master Nan Shiyou, while presiding at the Dharma seat of Wanshou Monastery, looked to his left and right and said: "Do you understand?
If you wish to raise the formless seal of Vairocana, you must walk upon the summit of a thousand peaks."
Residing at Mount Jing, he pointed to the Dharma seat, saying: "The Tathāgata’s seat is the emptiness of all phenomena. Look, look!
Upon level ground, waves arise.
When Chan Master Jizhou Fazu of Tianning opened the hall, he pointed to the Dharma seat, saying: "This curved wooden bench is the King of Precious Flowers."
The seat. A person such as this must sit in such a manner. (He lets out a shout.
Before the Dharma seat of Chan Master Tianyin Xiu, he said: "If you wish to take the first step, you must hold fast atop the thousand peaks.
Tell me, where does such a person tread? Open your eyes wide! He then ascended the seat.
Master Miyun Yuanwu, opening the hall, pointed to the Dharma seat and said:
"This is the Great Judicial Official, the Great Dharma Protector, who at the autumn of the Dingmao year struck down the iron mountain at Mount Lu’s Kaiyuan Temple.
Today, before this assembly of humans and devas, I shall raise it up once more. Do you see it? Thereupon, he ascended the seat.
Chan Master Zhuo’an pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "The precious Sumeru throne is immeasurably and boundlessly high and wide;
this staff is also immeasurably and boundlessly high and wide. Tell me, where does one set foot?
With a single clap of thunder, wind and rain arise."
Zhu Luezhi pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "It is easy to ascend higher step by step; it is difficult to let go from the void. What is difficult about letting go from the void?
It is that as one ascends higher step by step, one cannot find a place to start. When there is a branch, grasp the branch;
when there is no branch, grasp the pattern."
Chan Master Hongjue Wen was summoned by imperial decree to reside at the Wanshan Hall within the Imperial Palace and was authorized to ascend the Dharma seat. Pointing to the seat, he said:
"When Maitreya ascended to Tuṣita, the Heavenly King spread the seat for him. It is not said: 'The Tathāgata of Renown is heard throughout the ten directions;
among all auspicious things, he is supreme. In the past, he dwelt here in this Maṇi Hall; therefore, this place is most auspicious. With his hand...
He pointed and said: "The great assembly, look! These hundreds of billions of railings and stairways; these hundreds of billions of celestial silks and wondrous jewels;

these hundreds of billions of clouds of fragrant light and nets; these hundreds of billions of supreme adornments—all of these have arisen from the cultivation through accumulated kalpas by our Emperor.
They are collectively accomplished by the roots of goodness and merit of hundreds of billions of asaṃkhyeya kalpas. At that moment—
In the space of a thought, [the assembly] was fully manifested within this hall. Do you see it?
Thereupon, he ascended the dais and offered incense with these ritual words for the Emperor, the Empress Dowager, the Empresses, the Crown Prince, and the imperial family members of the two palaces.

Chan Master Mimam Jue offered incense, saying: "This one portion of incense is respectfully offered to pray for the longevity of His Majesty the Emperor, the Most August Sovereign, whose virtue is as vast as heaven and earth, who embodies the Way and follows the principles of humanity, benevolence, sincerity, and virtue, whose military strategies are like the warp and civil governance like the woof—may his sacred person live ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years!
We respectfully pray that the benevolence of Yao may spread far and wide, and the virtue of Shun may ever renew; may prosperity flourish forever for ten million years."
With sagacious calculation, he lifts the incense:

"This one portion of incense is respectfully offered for the longevity and majestic fortune of the Empress Dowager, the Empress, the Crown Prince, and the Grandsons—the celestial kin of the two palaces—and for their adornment with merit. We respectfully pray that their mountain of longevity may increase."
Stately and profound, the ocean of merit grows ever deeper. Together we clarify the primary cause of Prajñā; together we plant the diamond-seed of *jñāna*.
Master Zenben of Zhongfeng held up the incense and said: "This incense is the embryo of the myriad phenomena and the nurturer of the two polarities.

We reverently pray for the Empress Dowager’s ten-thousand-year reign, for the Empress to live as long as heaven endures, and for the Crown Prince to reach a thousand autumns. May we respectfully wish that [the Emperor] be as vast as heaven and as stable as earth."
Qinghai: "The ocean contains all equally; spring nurtures all equally.
Chan Master Hongjue Myn held up the incense and said: "This one portion of incense was gathered within the Garden of Varanāsa and was about to emerge beneath the Ashoka tree.
I burn it in this burner to honor the Empress, Zhaosheng Cishou Gongjian Anyi Zhangqing."
To the Empress Dowager, and next to the Empress of the Inner Palace: we humbly pray that their longevity may be as firm as a mountain and their blessings as vast as heaven;
that they may manifest enduring auspiciousness and ensure the perpetual prosperity of their descendants.
The Dharma Words for Holding Incense at the Opening of the Hall by Chan Master Zhenjing Wen: Holding up this incense, he said:

"This single offering of incense is respectfully presented to extend the auspicious life of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand ten thousand years. We pray that the wind of Yao’s virtue may forever prevail, equaling the brilliance of the sun and moon."
[The year] Ming. Tang Demi Xin shares in the eternal stability of heaven and earth.
Chan Master Meng’an Xin, upon opening the hall, held up the incense and said: "This one portion of incense is respectfully offered to extend the holy longevity of the present Emperor.
I pray that his governance of the world may equal the blessings of a Cakravartin King, and that he may preside over Heaven as the Honored One of Mahābrahmā."

When Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin received the Imperial Edict of Chongning and ascended the Dharma Hall to offer incense, he addressed the assembly, saying: "His light swallows the ten thousand phenomena;

His spirit transcends all mundane dust. From the time he first 'parted the grass and gazed at the wind' until his later 'entering the marketplace and extending a hand,' he did not wish to manifest [his realization] fully at will, fearing it might alarm the multitude and stir the crowd.
Today, I bring it forth to offer as a prayer for the longevity of the present Emperor."

Yan Shengshou, while at Jia Shan, held up the incense and said: "This single offering of incense is respectfully presented to the present Emperor to pray for his sacred longevity—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years! We humbly pray that his sagely calculations may equal Heaven and Earth, and his holy brilliance may surpass the sun and moon. Long...
May the imperial calendar of the phoenix endure for ten million years; may the jade leaves and golden branches extend through hundreds of thousands of kalpas.
Today, as Heaven Peace Monastery opens its hall, this single offering of incense is respectfully presented to pray for the long life of His Majesty the Emperor.

We humbly wish that the Golden Wheel may forever govern the realm and the precious mandate remain eternally prosperous and flourishing, so that he may honor the North Pole with his majesty and empty the city of mustard seeds.
[The Master] spoke more firmly.
Opening the hall, he held up the incense and said: "O assembly, do you see? This incense perfumes the fivefold Dharma-body and binds together the auspicious hues of the five clouds.
I burn it within this burner to offer prayers for the present Emperor’s sacred longevity—ten thousand years, ten thousand ten-thousand years. [He] prostrated himself.

May his Way equal that of Yao and Shun; may his virtue surpass that of Fuxi and Xuanyuan. May his life span exceed ten million years like Mount Nanshan; may his venerable majesty endure for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges like the North Star.
While standing before the Golden Mountain, he offered incense, saying: "This single offering of incense is respectfully presented to pray for the long and sacred life of the present Emperor."
I respectfully pray that Your Majesty’s civil and martial brilliance may equal the sun and moon, and Your sagely calculations match the vastness of heaven and earth.

May You achieve the merit of restoring the traces of Yu like King Shaokang, and accomplish the enterprise of reviving the House of Han like Emperors Xuan and Guang. May the myriad states submit to Your sacred transformation, and may the eight directions lay down their spears and halberds.
At Yongxi Temple, having received the imperial decree to reside at Yunju, he offered incense, saying: "Before the world of empty space was divided, there was a transcendent fragrance;
once the Flower Treasury (Kusumatalagarbha) had fully manifested, it was uniquely pervasive.

Perfumed by precepts, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation, and gathered from hundreds of thousands of millions of immeasurable, sublime sources—this I burn within the incense burner to offer supreme prayers for the longevity of the current Emperor."

May Your Majesty live for ten thousand years. We humbly pray that Your Virtue and Way may surpass those of the Five Emperors of antiquity, and Your majestic spirit may exceed that of the hundred kings who came before.

May Your Holy Life equal the Southern Mountain, and Your imperial domain match the North Pole. May the Two Sages soon return in their jade carriages, and may the myriad nations together celebrate peace and prosperity.
May weapons of war be forever laid to rest, and may the four classes of people delight in their vocations.
Chan Master Daguang Miaogao, upon ascending the hall at Mount Jing, held up the incense and said:
"This one portion of incense is respectfully offered to the Most Honored One of the Northern Palace, to pray for the myriad years of longevity of the Southern Mountain."
Chan Master Zhongfeng Ben opened the hall and offered incense, saying: "This single portion of incense cannot be contained by empty space, nor can it be supported by the great earth.

I, the monk Mingben, burn it toward this precious burner specifically to pray for the longevity of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years! May Your Majesty be most sagely and most enlightened, like the sun and..."
[The Master] said: "May [the Emperor’s] blessings and longevity be equal to those of the Earth and Heaven.
Chan Master Yuansou Duan, upon opening the hall, held up the incense and said: "This incense has its roots coiled and its joints interlaced before the time of Vipaśyin Buddha (Viyinwang Fo).
Its flames continue and its fragrance link together, standing above the World-Honored One Kāśyapa (Jiawen Shizun). I burn it toward this precious burner specifically for..."
We pray for the long life of the Great Yuan World-Ruler, the present Emperor, ten thousand years, ten thousand ten thousand years!
We humbly wish that Your Majesty may unify the hundred billion fragrant water seas into a single sea of merit, eternal and inexhaustible;
and may you gather the hundred billion Mount Sumerus into a single mountain of longevity, lofty and immovable.
Opening the Hall and Offering Incense in Central India: It embodies the righteous spirit of Pangu opening the heavens—looking up, it is ever more lofty;
piercing into it, it is ever more solid. It matches the great achievement of Yu the Great in surveying the lands—stained by fire yet never blackened, ground down yet never worn away.

As this incense is burned in the precious burner, it is offered specifically to pray for the ten-thousand-year reign of the sacred person of the current Emperor, the Sovereign of the Great Yuan World. Ten-thousand years! Ten-thousand years! Ten-thousand years!
Ten thousand years of longevity! Your Majesty, we respectfully pray that from the west, the east, the south, and the north, all shall return to the realm of universal peace.
May you be sagely and divine, martial and civil, forever enjoying boundless prosperity.
While residing at Mount Jing, he held up the incense and said: "This incense embodies the great harmony of the eras of Tang and Yu; it is vast and beyond naming.
It accords with the fragrant influence of the supreme governance of Yin and Zhou; it is majestic and marks the achievement of success.

I burn this toward the precious burner, reverently offering prayers for the longevity—ten thousand years, ten thousand ten-thousand years—of the current Emperor, the Sovereign of the Great Yuan World."
Chan Master Chushi Qi, upon opening the hall, held up the incense and said:
"This single portion of incense belongs to the realm above and below heaven, and to all that is mundane and supramundane; it is under its illumination and receives its grace.
I burn it within this burner specifically to pray for the longevity of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand ten thousand years! May Your Majesty be sagely and divine, martial and..."
The text reads: Throughout the four seas, all sing of the Way; from the west, from the east, from the south, and from the north, the eight directions all rejoice in non-action.
Chan Master Xiyin Yun, by imperial decree, ascended the hall and offered incense, saying: "This incense is the total embodiment and total function [of the Way].
It was present at the very inception of the great transformation; most noble and most supreme, it flourishes atop the nine heavens. Its value exceeds that of the *cintāmaṇi* jewel."
The fragrance of the *utpala* flower wafts upward; it brings spring to all things and spreads the harmony of the Yang energy across the great earth.

Manifesting auspicious omens in accordance with the seasons, it opens the realm of longevity throughout the eight wildernesses. As I burn this incense before the precious burner, I sincerely pray for the long life of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand ten thousand years!
May Your Majesty’s reign see the *Qianyuan* establish its ultimate principle, may the celestial star shine forth, and may the Three Steps of the Heavens be harmonized.
The celestial calendar is upon his person; the Sage has arisen and all things behold him. His life is coextensive with Heaven, and the myriad nations come as guests.
Chan Master Nan Shiyou, while residing at Baoen Temple, offered incense and said: "Most supreme and most noble, his value exceeds that of a hundred billion Mount Sumerus.

As an auspicious omen and a sign of good fortune, he provides a protective canopy over the great chiliocosm. With devotion, I burn this precious incense in the furnace, solely to pray for the long life of the Emperor."
"Long live the Emperor! Ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years! We reverently pray that the benevolence of Yao be as vast as heaven—so expansive that it can hardly be named.
May the virtue of Tang be ever-renewing daily—so pure that nothing can surpass it. May the imperial lineage endure for a hundred generations, and may there be ten thousand years of longevity."
While at Mount Jing, he held up the incense and said: "The substance of this incense embodies the nine-five yang energy; it is like gold and like jade.
Its leaves cover the great chiliocosm, serving as both canopy and cloud. Its name surpasses that of the *utpala* flower, and its value exceeds that of the *cintāmaṇi* jewel."
Incense was burned before the precious incense burner, and prayers were offered for the Emperor’s ten-thousand-fold, ten-thousand-fold, ten-thousand-fold myriad years of longevity.

It was respectfully prayed that his life-span might equal a hundred billion Sumeru mountains and his blessings those of the ocean of three thousand worlds. May the mountains remain as whetstones and the rivers as girdles, further consolidating the imperial destiny.
Amidst five days of rain and ten days of wind, we look up and sing the praises of Your Majesty’s sacred transformation.
Chan Master Liaohan Yu, upon opening the hall, held up the incense and said: "This incense forms a precious web of silk and disperses as clouds of radiant light.
I burn it in this precious burner to pray for the longevity of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand ten thousand years!
I respectfully wish that his civil and cultural brilliance may equal the North Pole and his years of life may match the Southern Mountains."
Chan Master Hongjue Wen held up the incense and said: "This single portion of incense does not arise spontaneously from heaven, nor is it obtained from a person.
It is rooted in the seeds of great compassion sown by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and nurtured and cultivated by great joy and great relinquishment;
it flourishes and spreads through great vows and great power. Only then is it severed with a golden blade."
With the axe of firm wisdom, it is split apart by the sword of skillful means. When burned in the furnace and formed into a canopy, it covers the great trichiliocosm;
when dispersed as clouds, its moisture flows through the realms of the sands.

We respectfully pray for the longevity of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years! May his merit surpass that of the three sovereigns, and his Way permeate the hundred kings. May he [dance]...

With the *gan* and *yu* dances, he converted the Prince of Miao; the eight remote regions were transformed through his influence. Wearing his robes and sash as he sat, he received the myriad nations in audience; the world turned toward benevolence.
Incense Offering and Dharma Words for the Officials of the Provinces, Courts, Ministries, Censorates, and Prefectures, and for the Military and Civil Bureaucracy.

On the day of opening the hall, Chan Master Shending Yin held up the incense and said: "This one offering of incense is respectfully offered for the Chancellor of the Prefecture, the Academicians, and all the honored officials of the entire commandery.
May you cause the Sun of the Buddha to shine ever more brightly and forever assist the Enlightened Sovereign."
On the day of opening the hall, Chan Master Yangqi Hui held up the incense and said: "This single portion of incense is offered for the Governor, the Dragon-Tu, the Jia-bu, and all officials;
may you remain forever in your positions of honor."
Chan Master Yong of Baoning, upon opening the hall, offered incense, saying: "This single portion of incense is respectfully offered for all the civil and military officials of the entire nation.
May their strategic plans be far-reaching and grand, and may their meritorious achievements flow on in enduring succession.
May the six armies remain forever at peace, and the myriad people eternally secure."
On the day of the opening of the hall, Chan Master Zhenjing Wen held up the incense and said:

"This single portion of incense is respectfully offered for the great patron, the Excellency Minister and Vice President of the Provincial Administration. May his entire clan enjoy a hundred auspicious blessings, and may both the small and the great increase in virtuous joy.
Furthermore, we pray that the Excellency Minister and Vice President, Brother and Elder, shall long remain as such."
This is the defensive wall of the Buddha-Dharma; may it serve as the enduring beams and pillars for the imperial house, generation after generation.

This single offering of incense is respectfully presented for the sake of the Censor-in-Chief, the Vice Commissioner, the Court Gentleman, and all civil and military officials, that they may always abide in their positions of honor.
Furthermore, may the various officials of the Censorate, together with the two Excellencies, have long received the Buddha’s prophecy to manifest as kings.
Your servant [writes]: "The long flourishing of the Buddha-Dharma depends upon such external protection. By means of these causes, all shall attain the fruit of the Buddha-way.

As the Fifth Patriarch, Chan Master Yuan, said when opening the hall and offering incense: "This single portion of incense is offered in service to the officials and magistrates of the prefectures and counties."
I humbly pray that you, being loyal and filial, pure and stainless, may forever serve as the parent of all living beings and eternally act as the protective pillar of the world’s order.
Chan Master Yuanwu Qin, while offering incense at the opening of the hall at Jia Shan, said: "This one portion of incense is offered in honor of the Prefectural Governor."

To the Tongpan Chaoqing, the presiding judges, the officials seated here, and the meritorious nobles of all offices: I humbly pray that your ranks and emoluments may be elevated ever higher, and the foundation of your longevity may remain forever firm.

At this opening of the hall at Tianning, this single incense offering is respectfully presented for the sake of the Prefectural Governor, Pacification Commissioner, Lecturer, and Transport Commissioner, Zhongda.
The Yunkan, Jiantao, Tixue, Shanding, and Tiju Dàfū; the Chengshou, Fengyù, and Tongpan Dàfū—all these high-ranking officials and nobles of merit were present in the assembly.

We humbly pray that you may serve as Fenghou and Lìmù, act as Houjì, Zhòu, Kǔi, and Gāo. To fulfill the expectations of all who look up to you, you shall occupy the Eight Seats and the Three Terraces;
to move the Emperor’s heart, you shall be like salt and plum, or like the rain that falls at will.

Opening the hall, he held up the incense and said: "On behalf of the Minister, the Governor-General, and all the officials of noble rank and merit, I pray that you may be favored by the singular selection of the Sovereign, fulfill the high expectations of the four seas, serve as the Zhou, Shao, Fu, and Shen, and act as the Gao, Kui, Yi, and Zhong."

Standing before the Golden Mountain, he offered incense, saying: "This single portion of incense is respectfully offered for the sake of the Governor, the Pacifier, the Vice-Governor Yan Kang, and the civil and military officials of the entire prefecture.
We pray that their positions may be as firm as a massive boulder and their merit as great as that of the princes who protect the state;
that when they govern the provinces, they shall be like those of Lu, Wei, Jin, and Qi, and when they ascend to the imperial halls, they shall be like Gao Yao, Shun, Ji, and Hou Ji."

While offering incense at Yunju, [the Master] addresses the Left Vice President, the Excellency of the Two Palaces, the various ministers and officials of the court, and all the eminent scholars and noble dignitaries present today at this assembly:
"I humbly pray that you may act as rain and dew for the world, and serve as oars and boats for the people."
"Supplementing the robes was Zhongshan; harmonizing the soup was Yue Shuo.

Opening the hall: this single incense offering is respectfully presented for the Prefectural Governor, the Vice-Governor, the Transport Commissioner, the Palace Secretary, the Prefectural Magistrate, and all honored officials of the entire prefecture, as well as the colleagues present at this assembly.
May you remain ever loyal and filial, serving the state and the people, and serving the Sage.
They are the limbs of the sovereign and serve as the pillars and cornerstones of a bright age.

When Chan Master Longmen Yuan opened the hall, he held up the incense and said: "This one portion of incense is offered for the sake of the Censor-in-Chief, the Academician, the Acting Prefect, the Vice-Prefect, and all the dignitaries of this region.
I pray that their illustrious reputations may spread far and wide and their virtuous governance may be renewed daily. Frequent...
Receiving the grace of rain and dew, I sit here to listen to the decree regarding the salt and plum.

Dreaman Chan Master, upon opening the hall, held up the incense and said: "This one portion of incense is offered for the sake of the Provincial Governor, the Chancellor, and all the officials of the prefecture.
May their lifespans be firm and long, and may their ocean of blessings grow ever deeper, so that they may always serve as the pillars and beams of the Great State."

To perpetually serve as guardians of the Dharma-gate, Chan Master Yuan of Yunju requested that Wang Gong Shao, the Military Commissioner of Xise—who considered his own karmic burden from killing to be heavy—be cleansed of it by requesting a Dharma discourse at Shanglan Monastery.
The Master lit incense and said: "This incense is for the General Who Kills Without Flinching."
The Great Layman, who attained Buddhahood while still standing, was universally praised as "Excellent Shao," and his mind was likewise at ease.
When Chan Master Zhongfeng Ben opened the hall and offered incense, he said: "This incense has a reputation that towers over the various nations; its value is esteemed throughout the Three Han.

I offer it to serve the Imperial Son-in-law, the Grand Marshal, Prince Shen, to extensively provide for his merit and longevity. I humbly pray that within the cosmos beyond kalpas, his golden branches may flourish."
Within the Imperial Garden, under the sun and moon of the world, the jade leaves flourish in the royal court.

On the day of opening the hall, Chan Master Baiyun Endan offered incense as an expression of gratitude, saying: "I respectfully offer this for the Great Awakened Ocean of the past, present, and future."
I universally repay the kindness of all sentient beings, all sages and worthies, and all the spiritual friends and companions on the ancient path whom I have encountered throughout my life—
those who have bestowed upon me even a single word or a single phrase— and I likewise express my gratitude to my teachers,
monks, parents, and all my benefactors and kin.

The Ritual for Burning Incense from the Lap (The incense mentioned above is all for burning; the attendant offers each stick one by one. However, for the "Dharma-succession incense," the abbot should draw it from his lap and personally insert it into the burner.
On the day of Master Xinghua Jiang’s opening of the hall, he held up the incense and said: "This one stick of incense was originally intended for my elder brother, Sansheng.
Since my elder brother Sansheng was too solitary for me, I ought instead to have succeeded to Daqiao. Daqiao was too..."
"Sha! At the feet of the Three Sages, I have attained the 'Guest and Host' phrase. Had I not met my elder brother, the Great Awakened One, I would surely have wasted my entire life.
Under the Great Awakened One, I received a blow of the staff and thereby came to see the principle of how my late teacher Linji received blows from Huangbo.
This single stick of incense is an offering to my late teacher Linji."
Chan Master Shimen Zhao, upon ascending the hall, held up the incense and said:
"From the twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven to the Sixth Patriarch of this land of Tang, all the sages of the past attained the transmission of the robe and the dharma.

From the time of the Sixth Patriarch in the Tang dynasty onward, those who attained the Way have been as numerous as rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds; they did not transmit the robe, but only transmitted the Dharma, using incense alone as the token of faith. Today..."
For whom does this single incense offering convey a message? Although I do not speak, the assembly already knows it fully.
I now burn this single stick of incense and depart.
On the day of opening the hall, Chan Master Shending Yin held up the incense and said: "This incense is not the fragrance of precepts, concentration, and wisdom;
nor is it sandalwood or aloeswood. It is simply the local product of Ruizhou. He then burned it, saying: "I offer this to the Venerable Shoushan to repay the milk of the Dharma."
On the day of opening the hall, Chan Master Yangqi Hui held up the incense and said: "Great assembly, do you know where it falls?

If you do not, I shall provide a commentary for you. To repay the grace of the Dharma-milk from Master Ciming of Shishuang Mountain, this mountain monk cannot help but let it 'fumigate the heavens and scorch the earth. He then burned it.
On the day of his inaugural address, Chan Master Baiyun端 held up the incense and said: "Tell me, for whom is this?
If there is something for which it is intended, it is like adding frost to snow; if there is nothing for which it is intended, the fault would be even greater.
I offer this in honor of the ancient master who first resided at Yangqi and later at Yungai—one who personally saw Ciming. Who would have thought that today, right here," [he continued].
"Let go of three and cast away two.
On the day of his formal opening of the hall, Chan Master Zhenjing Wen held up the incense and said: "O Great Assembly! Do you know where this single portion of incense falls?
Without further concealment, I offer it directly into the burner for the late Chan Master Huanglong Nan."
Chan Master Baoning Yong ascended the hall and held up the incense, saying: "O Great Assembly! This single portion of incense is priceless throughout past and present;
it has not been transmitted by Buddhas or patriarchs. Tell me, from where was it obtained? Do you know its point of descent? If you can know it,"
If you do not understand even this— coming here to meet a true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra)—
then burn [this incense] in the burner as an offering to my former abbot at Yangqi and my later abbot at Yunge, Master Hui.
Chan Master Yunfeng Yue, upon ascending the hall, held up the incense and said: "O Great Assembly! This single portion of incense cannot be covered by heaven nor supported by earth;
even the Buddhas as numerous as dust motes and the teachers of the world have not dared to look upon it with their true eye.
Where, then, do you all seek to grasp it? Yet, while official channels do not admit a needle, private paths allow for carriages and horses. I offer this in honor of the late Master Cuiyan."
Chan Master Zhi, when Chan Master Wuzu Yan opened the hall, held up the incense and said: "This one portion of incense has been sought for a long time.
For more than ten years I have traveled as a cloud upon the sea, seeking an adversary, yet never encountering one. Now that I have arrived at Longshu, indeed..."
Meeting such a person finally accords with my long-standing indignation. Today, before this great assembly, I shall clear my grievance.
I must burn [this letter] for the sake of my late teacher, the Venerable Baiyun Wenda; let it scorch the heavens and sear the earth as it pleases, and let it pass freely through Cai Prefecture.
Let those who possess nostrils discern it for themselves.
At Dongshan, he ascended the hall and held up the incense, saying: "This one stick of incense has been with me for twenty-seven years while I resided at three monasteries in Shu Prefecture;
everyone knows this. I was about to burn it, but then I said: 'No, I must explain it. For fifteen years I traveled on pilgrimage;
first I attended upon Master Xian and obtained his fur, and subsequently I visited venerable elders throughout the four seas and obtained..."
I obtained his skin at the place of the old master Yuanjian of Mount Fu; later, I obtained his bone at the place of Master Baiyun Wenda;
and only then did I dare to receive his marrow and act as a teacher for others.
Today, I am cast into the furnace, letting it smoke the heavens and scorch the earth; let those with ears discern it.
Chan Master Yuanwu Qin, while residing at Chongning Temple, held up the incense and said:

"This single portion of incense was not brought from the Pamir Mountains, nor did it flow forth from my own breast. In the South, I encountered more than thirty venerable elders; finally, I ran into a true master.
He struck me with a single blow and shattered [my attachments]. Today, before this assembly, I shall reveal it for you all: I offer it to the present..."
The Venerable Master Wuzu Yan, residing at Qizhou, offered incense to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk.

Opening the hall at Tianning Temple, he held up the incense and said: "When the thousand Buddhas appear in the world, who can set their price? Beyond the limit of Avidyā (Wei-yin), who can discern the beginning?
In years past, one received this under a single phrase from Baiyun; today, for the third time, I hold it up here in the city of Tan."

[The Master] steps forward. To repay the milk of the Dharma for the late Chan Master Yan, the tenth-generation patriarch of Wuzu Mountain in Qizhou, he opens the hall and holds up the incense, saying:
"In years past, within the mass of white clouds, this first phrase cut off the flow.
Today, before this assembly of humans and devas, this is what I bring forth for the fourth time. I offer it to the late Chan Master Yan, the tenth-generation patriarch of Wuzu Mountain in Qizhou."
Chan Master Yan burned incense in the brazier to repay the milk of the Dharma.
Chan Master Yuan of Longmen, upon opening the hall, held up the incense and said: "Do you know where this single portion of incense falls? The more one seeks to hide it, the more it is revealed;
the more one remains in obscurity, the more it shines forth. Originally, I intended to cast it away in a mountain ravine to mingle with the sand and stones, yet I have been forced by all [of you]..."
Pressed by others, I cannot avoid explaining the origins in detail.

I offer this incense for my late master, Chan Master Yan of Dongshan in Huangmei, Qizhou, to burn in a single burner, thereby repaying the kindness of his Dharma-milk and modestly expressing the ritual of transformation.
Although such great kindness is difficult to repay, I cannot help but let go of three and release two.
Chan Master Hongluo of Huqiu ascended the hall and held up the incense, saying: "This one portion of incense has caused many to harbor doubts.
For thirty years I have traveled from one monastic grove to another community; when encountering the lowly, it was noble, and when encountering the noble, it was lowly.
Finally, I encountered this faceless old fellow who struck me at my very life-vein, causing me to unconsciously let it fall from the void."

Now, unable to avoid it, I bring this forth before the assembly. It is offered on behalf of the Great Master Foguo Yuanwu, the Zen Teacher currently residing at Jìnshān in Rùnzhōu, to repay the kindness of his Dharma-milk.
Chan Master Daguang Miaogao, upon ascending the hall at Jingshan, held up the incense and said: "This single portion of incense—if one looks at it, one's eyes will go dry;
if one smells it, one's skull will split open. When met with the noble, its value is as great as the Sahā world; when met with the lowly, it is not worth a single coin.
Today, before this assembly of humans and devas, I burn it within the incense burner to offer in honor of the Zhaojue [Temple] in Chengdu Prefecture."
At Chan Temple, the Great Master Zen Master Xian Yuangwu, in order to repay the kindness of his dharma-milk, once again took up residence at Jingshan and held up the incense, saying:
"This single portion of incense—when in the Tuṣita Heaven, it is called *siddhārtha*."
In the Heaven of Skillful Transformations, it is called "Seizing the Mind. At the edge of Lake Anavatapta, it is called "Lotus Treasury.
But tell me, what would you call it when it is pointed out by Hand at Mount Jing? After a long silence, he said: "Not only would the Elder Yuanwu have no share in seeing it;
even if all the Buddhas of the three periods of time were to appear, they would not dare to look upon it with a direct eye."
He then burned it.
Chan Master Ying'an Hua, upon opening the hall, held up the incense and said:

"This one portion of incense is offered for the late Master Long, who first resided at Zhangjiao in Xuanzhou and later resided at Yunyan Chan Monastery on Mount Huqiu in Pingjiang. I burn it within this burner."
To repay the grace of the Dharma-milk, let the monks of the world strike the brick as they please.

Chan Master Miam Jie, upon ascending the hall, held up the incense and said: "This single portion of incense has been gathered for a long time; though I wished to conceal it, it becomes ever more manifest.
Today, with the assembly of humans and devas gathered in full, I cannot help but reveal its origin from the beginning. In years past, while traveling on pilgrimage along the Yangtze River..."
He turned westward, intending to go to Siming. Upon arriving at Zhiwei in Wuzhou, he was mistakenly directed by some bystanders and brothers onto the wrong path.
He stumbled into Mingguo Mountain in Quzhou, where he encountered an old monk who was so brusque and unaccommodating that it was truly beyond human measure.
Having already made the mistake, he followed it through and prostrated three times; even to this day, he regrets it.
Although it is so, resentment has its source and debt has its owner.

I burn this incense in the furnace as an offering to the Eighteenth Abbot of Tiantong Mountain, the Great Monk Ying’an, who dwelt there in his final years, in order to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk.

Chan Master Xiatang Yuan, by imperial decree, took up residence at Lingyin Temple and ascended the Dharma hall. After the imperial envoy had descended with incense and offered prayers for the Emperor, the Master held up the incense and said:
"This one stick of incense cannot be concealed even by heaven and earth; it cannot be fathomed even by the Buddha-eye. Wherever it is raised, it extinguishes the barbarian lineage;
wherever it is brought forth, it leaves people stunned and paralyzed. It has caused me to lie across the wild weeds for thirty years."
To this day, I have spent my entire life as a mediocre fellow; yet, there is a certain point of confusion within it that must be exposed before the assembly.
Twenty years ago, I was driven by the winds of karma to the base of Mount Min-e, into a thicket of brambles, where I encountered a solid iron hammer without a hole.
Struck by it, I was half-drunk and half-awake, and I thought—
Mute his mouth, so that it may never be opened for the rest of his life. Twenty years later, he is blown by the winds of karma to the banks of the Zhuojin River, amidst a thicket of entanglements.
There he encounters a "burnt-tail white-cheeked tiger. At that moment, he is personally struck by its single fang;

his courage is lost and his soul flees, yet he finally manages to open his mouth. To this day, he enjoys the fruit of this experience without end. Now tell me: for whom is this incense intended? For the second [case]?
The knowledge realized ten years ago is the very same as the knowledge realized twenty years later. A solitary crane does not perch on two trees;
a single guest does not trouble two households. Have you not heard it said: "If one goes too far ahead, one fails to reach the end"?
Now the thief’s own body has been exposed and the stolen goods are manifest before us. This is offered in honor of the former [Abbot] of Chengdu Prefecture, Zhao... [text truncated].

I honor the Great Master Chan Master Juexian Yuanwu not for his empty talk before the Emperor or his bold roaming upon the seas, but solely for the fact that his breast was devoid of worldly things and his belly held no "Chan.
I burn this incense within the furnace to repay the milk of the Dharma.

Master Meng’an Xin held the opening ceremony of the hall and offered incense, saying: "This single portion of incense—before the assembly of humans and devas has yet discerned its origin, it is fortunate that there is one who can testify to it;
to keep it secret would be a vain labor. I offer this in honor of my late predecessor, Venerable Jing of Xiyu Tang at Shengyin Monastery in Chuzhou, to repay the kindness of his Dharma-milk."

Chan Master Gaofeng Miao, while residing at Tianmu, held up the incense and said: "This single portion of incense does not borrow from the sun and moon within the alchemical cauldron, nor does it come from the spring breeze beyond the kalpas.
Having several times personally encountered its lethal touch, I have been made to become transparent and resonant on all eight sides.
Now, when set down, it causes the earth to shake with six great quakes; when held up, it fills and pierces through empty space. Tell me, when neither held up nor set down—"
"Having uttered a single phrase, what then? He let out a shout, performed a woman’s bow, and burned [the incense] in the incense burner as an offering to the former Abbot of Yangshan—
the old monk with horns, who wore fur, and had no nostrils— to repay the debt of his life-blood in the Dharma.
Chan Master Yuansou Duan, upon opening the hall, held up the incense and said:

"The Patriarch Dahui Daoning would rather take this very body to undergo the sufferings of hell on behalf of all sentient beings in the great earth than ever treat the Buddha-Dharma as a matter of personal favor.
My late teacher at Jingshan, Venerable Zangshou, throughout his life refused to accommodate the people of the four quarters of the world—even were it Śākyamuni himself or Bodhidharma."
When the Great Master arrives, one must step back; that is the rule.
When I was in the attendant’s quarters two years ago, I exhausted every stratagem and employed every skill, yet there was truly nowhere for me to find a foothold.
Thus, I knew him to be the true grandson of Dahui. Now, as I offer this incense to him, I wish for everyone to bear witness.
While standing in India, he offered incense and said: "If one praises this incense, one's eyes will go blind and ears deaf; if one slanders it, one's mouth will become mute and tongue withered.
Even the Buddhas of the three periods and the six generations of patriarchs manifesting all at once have only a share in gazing up at it."
On behalf of the late Great Master Zang-sou, the fifteenth-generation descendant in the direct line of Linji who formerly resided at Mount Jing, [this incense] is offered continuously.
Chan Master Wuwen Can, upon opening the hall, held up the incense and said: "This incense cannot be looked upon; it cannot be grasped."
I cannot bear to discard it; looking upon it with a cold eye, it is truly laughable.

It shall remain for a full thirty years, then be burned within the incense burner, offered on behalf of the late Great Monk Xiaoweng of Ayuwang Da Guangli Chan Temple in Qingyuan Prefecture, to repay the kindness of his Dharma-milk.
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun, upon ascending the hall, held up the incense and said: "When the ancients appeared in the world, they offered incense to repay the milk of the Dharma.
When people of today appear in the world, they offer incense to repay the kindness of the world. I, the monk Yun, am neither of these.
In years past, while traveling on pilgrimage, I went to Mount Zituo to visit an old nun-robe wearer; he had no dharma to bestow, and I had no dharma to receive."

It may be accepted. I simply bring it forth from within the state where there is neither giving nor receiving, to offer to the late Venerable Zhuyuan Dao, who resided at Jianyan Chan Monastery in Kunshan.
This is not intended to repay his virtue or requite his kindness; it is simply so that everyone may understand and realize this.
While at Ruiyan, he held up the incense and said: "This incense has already been offered for the second time.

I burn it in this burner as an offering to my late master, the Great Monk Zhu Yuan of the Western Guangyuan at Zhituo Peak, who formerly resided at Jianyan Chan Temple in Kunshan during his later years, in order to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk. However, karmic creditors and enemies have their own due."
The reason for my coming: today, before this assembly of devas and humans, I shall not hesitate to once again clear away the doubts.

Many years ago, while I was at that mountain seeking instruction from the Old Monk, I went specifically to request his guidance because I could not resolve the koan regarding the dog having no Buddha-nature.
As soon as I opened my mouth, he gave me a shout, which caused my entire body to break into a cold sweat. Because of this...
He presented a verse, saying: "The dog has no Buddha-nature; Spring colors fill the imperial capital. In Zhaozhou’s East Courtyard, A gourd hangs upon the wall.
Then he burst into laughter and said, "How could understanding it in such a way suffice? It is as the saying goes: 'The first arrow is still light, but the second arrow is deep.
He then inserted an incense stick and said, "Even with Boya’s lute, it would be difficult to transcribe the heart's innermost song."
When Chan Master Xian of Western Shu first received the seal of his mind from Master Wuzu Yan, on the day he ascended the hall, he took up the incense of the late Master Shaojue Bai.
His words were as follows: "One is the refinement of the furnace; the other is the perfection of the whetstone.

When these two functions are both manifest, which principle comes first? Have you not heard it said that 'the root is heavy and the branch is light,' and that this can be discerned when facing the wind? This incense—"
On behalf of the late Master Shaojue, I burn this incense within the brazier, so that it may fill the heavens and cover the earth, filling the ditches and blocking the ravines,
leaving no place for the monks of the world to draw breath.
Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun, upon opening the hall, held up the incense and said: "This incense was once received under a single phrase atop the summit of Mount Daxiong;
today it is brought forth before the fivefold assembly on Mount Fenghuang.
I offer it to pay homage to the grace of the Dharma-milk of the late Great Monk Huiji, the Chan Master who previously resided at Jingshan and later resided at Dayang."
Master Nanxiu, upon opening the hall, held up the incense and said: "It did not descend from the heavens, nor did it well up from the earth.
The Buddhas of the three periods have been unable to find its trace; the patch-robed monks of the world find it difficult to recognize its value.
Is there anyone here who knows where it has fallen? If you do not yet know, I respectfully offer this for the former abbot of Wanshou, Master Xingzhong Dahe."

Shangyi burned it in the incense burner and set it aside; he did not yet discuss repaying virtue or requiting kindness, but rather sought to ensure that all people throughout the great earth would know its fragrance.
When Chan Master Tieguanshu opened the hall, he held up the incense and said: "This single portion of incense—the Buddhas of the three periods of time do not dare [to claim it]..."
As for the price: since the time of the six ancestral patriarchs, who has ever caught its scent? It was obtained long ago within the pass of Shimen;

today, before this assembly of devas and humans, I bring it forth. I offer this in honor of the Great Monk Yuweng of Tianchi Xinghua Chan Temple on Mount Moqian in the Zhejiang region, to repay the kindness of his Dharma-milk.
Chan Master Tianyin held up the incense and said: "Diligently buried within ancient trees and amidst heaps of white clouds, it was obtained from within the state of having nothing to obtain;
yet, while in the midst of cultivation and realization, it was not realized. Today, before this assembly, I hold it forth."
I make this offering to my late Master, the Great Monk Huanyou of Yunmen Chan Monastery on Longchi Mountain at Jingxi, to repay the milk of the Dharma.
Chan Master Zhanran Cheng held up his incense and said: "The primary and the secondary are carried together; striking and singing occur simultaneously. Father and son meet."

The way of sovereign and subject is in perfect harmony; this is solely for the purpose of making offerings at the Dajue Hall in Beijing to the Venerable Qingliang Cizhou Nian, the thirty-first generation successor of the orthodox Caodong lineage, in order to slightly repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk.
Chan Master Ruohan asked about the incense offering at the opening of the assembly at Qing Shan: "Twenty years ago, he went out from here; twenty years later, he enters here.
Although his coming and going have their times, how can one say there is any turning away or facing toward? Since there is no turning away or facing toward, tell me:
is it the one who goes out, or is it the one who enters? Without sparing his eyebrows, he spoke before the assembly of gods and humans.
I burn this single incense stick to honor my late Master, the Great Monk Shengtian Xiayin,
the thirtieth-generation successor in the Linji lineage at this very Qingshan Hall, in order to repay the milk of the Dharma.
Holding up the incense, he said: "This single offering of incense would not be considered excessive enough to leave the world in doubt;
it would not be considered poisonous enough to erase the world from existence. In the past, there was a fundamental basis upon which to rely; now, it pervades the entire realm without concealment.

No matter how clever a *ṛṣi* may be, who dares to look directly at it with their true eye? I offer this in honor of the former abbot of Jingxi Qingshan and the later abbot of Baoguo Temple in Huzhou."
To repay the grace of our late Master, the Great Monk, who concealed himself beneath heaven, Chan Master Sōnyu Mitsu offered incense, saying:
"This single portion of incense was subtly shifted one step forward before the Hall at Hakuryō."

Within the books of Mount Ying, he sat and cut off all common winds; even axes and hatchets could not split him open. His kindness was as deep as that between father and son, such that those outside the circle did not dare to discuss it.

When the merit returns to the minister, he burns incense in the furnace specifically to make offerings to Master Bo-shan on his high seat—none other than our late Great Abbot—to repay the milk of the Dharma.
Record of the Essential Teachings of the Successive Patriarchs,
Volume Twenty-three and Volume Twenty-four.
Compiled by Xingyue of Loudong, Abbot of Lian’an Chan Monastery at the Eighteen Streams in Wulin.
After the mallet was struck, Chan Master Linji Xuan spoke as he took his seat, saying:
"The Provincial Governor, Attendant Wang Changshi, and the various officials have requested that I open the hall.
This mountain monk, having no choice in the matter today, has conformed to human sentiment to ascend this seat. However, if one were to speak according to the school of our ancestors—"
To extol this Great Matter is to find one’s mouth unable to open; there is no place for you to set foot.

Today, at the earnest request of the Attendant, I have brought forth the essential thread of the ancestral school. Is there any master warrior here who can immediately deploy the battle array and unfurl the banner?
Let him bring evidence before the assembly and see!
On the day of opening the hall, Chan Master Daowu Zhen said: "If you can perceive it in this very way, you will find immediate liberation.
But as for the profound mystery, whether you see it or do not see it, it is all at once blind."
In the North Chan Hall, he ascended the seat and said: "The green mountains are steep and lofty; the white sun passes like a shuttle. No guests at the Dragon Gate;
many people in the bustling market. You all, tell me: how many tax-paying commoners are there right now at the head of the vegetable row?"
Chan Master Fahua Ju ascended the hall and said: "Now, the primary truth (paramārtha-satya) is not something that can be explained by intellectual discernment nor measured by the mind’s machinations.
It is a separate transmission outside the teachings, where no words or letters are established. Having arrived at this point, how is it further?
You must directly cut off Vairocana and allow for neither ordinary nor sage. Can you do so? If you have not yet attained this, I, this mountain monk, shall [speak] again."
Having spoken these verses, he departed. He did not seal [himself] with the Vairocana mudrā; how could he propagate the mind of the ancient Buddha? A bright moon illuminates the secluded valley;
cold waves assist the night mortar. Do you all understand this thoroughly? Each of you should hope to pose a question.
On the day of opening the hall, Chan Master Dayu Zhi said: "Is there anyone who thoroughly understands the point of landing?

If you understand it, you will benefit beings according to their capacities and respond through transformation without fixed form; appearing and disappearing, rolling up and unrolling between heaven and earth, you will move with sovereign ease in every direction."
If you still do not understand where it falls, Śākyamuni, the Buddhas of the three periods, the twenty-eight patriarchs, and all the old worthies of the world have been cast into the furnace at once;
now listen to this old monk’s rambling talk.
Chan Master Ciming Yuan, upon opening the hall at Nanyuan, said: "Great assembly, do you understand? It is like the fine waters of Yiyang and the stone bridge of Mount Heng.
If you do not understand, it will merely deceive you all. Therefore it is said that Bodhidharma came from the West to transmit a phrase outside the teachings.
But tell me, what is this phrase transmitted outside the teachings? It is to point directly at the human mind, see one's nature, and become a Buddha."
Indeed, all of you here are people pointed out by the Patriarch himself. Do you believe this?
If you can believe it, you will study alongside the Patriarchs and Buddhas; if you cannot believe it, you may be said to have brought about your own discouragement.
This assembly today is no small matter. I offer this single incense burner for my late Master Wude Chan. Now tell me, do you recognize him?
"Is there no Chan Master who has attained [this]? If you do not recognize it, ask your questions if you have doubts.
On the day Master Yunfeng Yue opened the hall, he said: "If the patriarchs and ancestors did not resolve it, the calamity falls upon their descendants.

When matters reach such a state, how can one allow for any further justification? What is called the matter of leaving the world to benefit sentient beings is termed the Gate of the Primary Meaning (Paramārtha). However—"
Much that is spoken lacks true meaning. If you people were to understand thoroughly, this mountain monk’s work in appearing in the world would be finished.
If this is not yet so, then please ask whatever doubts you have.
On the day Chan Master Zhenjing Wen opened the hall, after the mallet had been struck, the Master called to the assembly, saying: "You must observe for yourselves.
To observe in this way is called right observation; to observe otherwise is called wrong observation. While the distinction between the wrong and the right has not yet been made—"
I have a doubt and ask for instruction.
After the Venerable Master opened the hall and struck the gavel, he remained silent for a long while and then said: "Do you understand? On the peak of Shaoshi, this was once revealed;
on the banks of Gaoyuan, who has transmitted it again? If there is a seeker among you, do not follow the example of Shen Guang and abandon your practice."
The year passed. [One day], he suddenly shouted, "If you have doubts, ask them.
After Bao Ning had finished opening the hall and striking the gavel, he extended one foot and said, "O Great Assembly, is this one or two?"

After a long silence, he said: "The person of superior capacity resolves everything in a single decision; those of middling and inferior capacity hear much but have little faith. He then invited questions.
After the gavel had been struck on the opening day of Master Baiyun’s formal assembly, he looked to his left and right and said: "If it were simply like this, you would all disperse."
Go! From antiquity to the present, they are as numerous as hemp and millet.
If you say there is anything more to it—“how” or “what”—then the single path of Caoxi will sink into oblivion.

Therefore, all the sages of the past emerged from within the flames and extended their hands, desiring only that everyone’s eyes be horizontal and noses straight. Is there anyone here today who extends their hand? Come forth!
"Come!
On the day Chan Master Baoning Yong opened the hall, after the mallet had been struck, he looked at the assembly and said: 'Do you understand thoroughly?
If you do not understand thoroughly, it is like drawing legs on a snake. Before the ancient Buddha’s cliff, a thousand flowers compete in splendor; atop the source of Caoxi, ten thousand [waves]..."
He sent him back to his own school. Is there anyone who would ascend precipitous peaks or wade through vast, surging waters? Disregarding danger and death, please come to meet me.
Zen Master Wuzu Yan opened the hall from all four sides and said: "If we discuss the primary principle, the twenty-eight patriarchs of India..."
The Sixth Patriarch of Tang stood downwind from the soil; the entire Great Canon of the teachings is ten thousand miles of white clouds.
Mahākāśyapa’s closing of his room and Vimalakīrti’s silence are but dreams; the appearance of the thousand Buddhas in the world is no more than unfinished sleep-talk.
Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra twist the crooked to make it straight. Therefore it is said: even if one attains realization before words, it is still being stuck in the husk and lost in the seal.
Even if one is thoroughly proficient in the words [of the teachings], one cannot avoid encountering wild views wherever one goes.
If you can instead firmly maintain the boundaries [of reality], what need is there to mention the saying that "the grass before the Dharma Hall is ten feet deep"?

Only when the paths of ordinary and sage are cut off, such that even birds cannot fly across, and no monk in the world has a place to draw breath—among this assembly, is there anyone who does not agree? Come forth and meet me!
After the opening of the hall and the striking of the gavel by Haihui, he said: "The golden arrowhead is accustomed to leveling the ancestral path;
the iron whip possesses great strength, yet it laments having no enemy. Is there any monk who disregards danger and death? Come forth and meet me."

At Dongshan, after the opening of the hall and the striking of the gavel had concluded, he said: "One should contemplate the primary truth (*paramārtha*). A precious sword has a blade as sharp as frost;
it flashes like lightning across three thousand worlds. It is supreme and beyond compare. Only the eye can discern it and the hand can grasp it intimately. Come forth and let us test one another!"
When Master Xuedou Xian opened the hall at Wanshou Monastery, after the mallet had been struck, the Master said: "When the Dharma-vehicle is proclaimed once, the Tripitaka ceases its interpretation.

When the Patriarch’s command is put into action, the ten directions are cut off. If there be an enlightened person who does not shrink from birth and death, raise your eyebrows and come forth from the assembly to meet me."
While presiding at the opening of the hall at Xuedou, after the mallet had been struck, he said: "The Tathāgata’s Treasury of the True Dharma Eye is entrusted to this very day.

If one lets it go, even tiles and pebbles will radiate light; if one holds it fast, even genuine gold loses its luster. The authority rests in my hands; killing and giving life are applied according to the occasion.
Should there be any who are true practitioners, let us bear witness to one another."
On the day Master Chanyuan of Longmen opened the hall, after the mallet had been struck, he said: "Contemplation is not the one; the one is not contemplation.
Where, then, is the gateway of the primary principle?"

When Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin ascended the hall for his inaugural sermon at Chongning Temple, after the mallet had been struck, he said: "Drawing a crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt, one strikes and departs immediately;
piercing through the Iron Ring Mountains, there is no room for deliberation. Within a single word, killing and giving life are fully revealed;
within a fraction of a momentary response, the myriad phenomena are encompassed. You must be pierced directly at the head so that your thousand eyes may open all at once. Furthermore, if..."
Looking about in hesitation, he immediately began to search the heavens and grope the earth. One who had grasped the truth came forward from the assembly to meet him.
Jiashan entered the monastery and ascended the hall, saying: "A wild ape carries its young back to the green peaks; A hidden bird holds a flower as it passes over the azure cliffs.
In years past, I was a guest in this place; Now, as the host, I am ashamed to have no cause for shame. "Is there anyone among the assembly who can discern [the truth]?"
"Have you attained the status of a monk who is both guest and host?
Upon entering the monastery and ascending the hall, he said: 'The scorching heat of midsummer departs from the green peaks; the solemn, clear autumn crosses the azure marshes.
The ancient hall is majestic and the pines and cypresses are dense; in this dustless golden ground, there is sufficient coolness. Having arrived here, do you still possess your original [nature]?"
"Is there any monk of color? Come forth and let us verify it together.

While residing at Yunju, he first opened the hall for teaching in Nanjiang Prefecture. After the mallet was struck, he said: "Encompassing the myriad existences, its sound shakes the great chiliocosm.
Whether Buddha or Patriarch, the crown-center is opened; whether god or man, the square inch of the mind is vast. And so it was.
This has been presented; it is not without its essential brevity. If you hesitate, you will fall into the secondary gate.
Is there any monk whose arrow-tip meets another’s? Come forth and let us stimulate one another.
After Master Hujiu Long finished striking the gavel while residing at Kaisheng, he said: "The fishing line is cast across the four seas, seeking only the leviathan.
If you can speak the Way while remaining three inches away from the hook, come forward and speak!"
Chan Master Daguang Miaogao was residing at Mount Jing. After the gavel had been struck, he said:

"According to the long-standing precedents of all quarters and the constant protocols of past and present, even if the thousand Buddhas and World-Honored Ones were to appear in succession and ascend this seat, they would still not receive so much as a single ladle of foul water from me.
Is there anyone here who can avoid this? Come forth and provide proof!"
Chan Master Ying’an Hua entered the monastery at Mingguo to open the hall. After the mallet was struck to signal the start of the formal session, he said:

"To realize the emptiness of the primary truth is called the lion’s roar. Now that the lion has roared, foxes and wolves have hidden their tracks and those of different species have vanished from sight.
Is there anyone here who can join hands with me? Come forth and meet me."
While residing at Jiangshan, after the gavel had been struck, he said: "If one were to discuss the primary meaning (paramārtha), it is like a single speck of snow upon a red-hot furnace.
If you cannot hear the sound when it is heard, nor transcend form when it is seen, what prevents you from coming forward from the assembly to resolve your doubts?"
When Chan Master Mimuan Jie opened the hall at Lingyin Monastery, after the mallet had been struck, he said: "The true command has already been enacted;
all divergent paths have been erased from their traces. From this point on, Buddha to Buddha have handed it down, and Patriarch to Patriarch have transmitted it.
If you can understand it thus, you may respectfully bow to Śākyamuni and not prostrate before Maitreya. Should you still linger in listening and watching, what question will you bring forth?"

While residing at Lingyin, after the mallet had been struck to signal the assembly, he said: "The primary truth (paramārtha-satya) is empty and void, without form; inside and out it is one and the same.
Both Buddhas and sentient beings are merely superfluous designations (adhivacana). Now, how do you observe this? If there is an observation performed with a mind, it belongs to deluded thought."
The contemplation of a mindless state belongs to the view of nihilism; the contemplation of a mind that is neither existent nor non-existent is a vague and superficial grasping of Buddha-nature.
Let any monk who has truly penetrated the eye of the critical barrier come forth and display it for all to see!
When Chan Master Liaojueyuan opened the hall for the formal assembly, the head monk finished the ritual of striking the gavel. The Master remained silent for a long while and then said:
"Even if Aniruddha’s divine eye could not yet discern clearly, and even if the Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara were present, how could he possibly lift it up?
Is there no one among you who feels this is unsatisfactory? Come forth, overturn the meditation seat, and scatter the assembly with a shout! Even so, it is still not [enough]."
These are true masters. For now, let us grant some breath to the monks within the second gate.
When Chan Master Jinshan Weizhong ascended the hall, after the head monk had finished striking the gavel, the Master looked to his left and right and said:
"Do you understand? A lion’s vigorous display, an elephant king’s circular turn. If you can realize this clearly, it will not fail to save you effort. But if you do not..."
However, I have a doubt and ask for instruction.
When Chan Master Yizhang of the Upper Hall opened the hall, after the head monk had finished striking the gavel, the Master said: "Before the gavel was struck, observing 'one' is not it;
after the gavel was struck, observing 'two' is also not it. Arriving at this point, even those with iron eyes and copper pupils must [look further]."
"Shattered into a hundred pieces! Is there any monk who does not avoid peril and death? Come forth and see!
Thus did Chan Master Yuansou Duan, while presiding over the opening of the hall at Fengshan, say: "To seize upon one pivot is for a thousand pivots and ten thousand pivots to arrive all at once;
it is like carving human excrement to produce the fragrance of sandalwood. To bring up a single phrase is for a thousand phrases and ten thousand phrases to flow toward the source; it is like..."
"Take a conch-shell ladle and measure the waters of the great ocean. Is there no one who is pure, naked, starkly bare, solitary, liberated, and without dependence?
Come forth and provide mutual verification!"
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun resided at Ruiyan. After the gavel had been struck, he said: "The Buddhas appearing in the world is the second head;
