Xuan said, "I have long known that the Master possesses this essential pivot. Wujiu said, "Since you do not understand, watch how the monk behind you responds.
When Shao was about to step forward, Wujiu struck him, saying, "There is no difference in the soil within the same pit. The Master said, "Everyone..."
The Waymaster’s use of the *wujiao* (marking nut) was like a thunderclap at the end of a battle;
yet he failed to realize that his very life and nature had fallen into the hands of the two monks, like a defeated general casting aside his spear and scattering across the field.
When Chan Master Yuguan Ji entered the monastery and ascended the hall to preach, the sun shone with lofty brilliance and the sea and sky stretched vast and wide.
Peaks surged like the ocean, and pavilions opened like the heavens. Every single thing is the unsurpassed wondrous gate; everywhere is the adamantine true body.
The Buddhas appearing in the world have passed down errors as truths; the Patriarchs coming from the West have taken mistakes as correct. The entire Tripitaka is but a deception.
It illuminates the villages and hamlets. Even an enlightened monk cannot save himself; he can only achieve it by being without mind regarding affairs and having no affairs within his mind.
Then one will see the wind of Yao sweeping vast and the sun of Shun shining bright; heaven will be clear and earth peaceful, the people healthy and all things flourishing.

This mountain monk’s Way is thin and his person insignificant, yet he has received the command of the monastery from afar. Crossing the three rivers and nine dams, sailing over the seas and climbing the mountains, he comes to serve the state.
The Master proclaims the fundamental tenet; there is not a single thread of deception toward you all, nor do you all deceive this mountain monk by even a single thread.
I hope that each of you will maintain sincerity so that we may fully understand one another. Again, he cites a monk who asked Baizhang, "What is the extraordinary matter?
Baizhang replied, "Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak. The monk bowed, and Baizhang struck him. The Master said, "How great and small was Baizhang!"
The Master had no choice but to claim supremacy where there was no Buddha. Today, if someone were to ask, "What is the extraordinary matter at the new Longjiao?
one should simply say to him, "All of you shall become Buddhas. If he then prostrates, say further to him:
Simply cultivate a heart of resolve, and you will certainly not be deceived.

Upon entering the monastery and ascending the hall, I, Puci, lament that my spiritual practice has not been perfected, bringing shame upon the ancients; whether in action or withdrawal, in departure or staying, I merely follow conditions as they arise.
I pity myself that my past karmic debts are difficult to evade; once more I board an iron ship upon the vast blue ocean.
Alas, the Great Dharma is in decline, and we dwell in this age of the Dharma’s semblance. Though the new Elder has exhausted his spiritual powers, how can he further provide for us?
I venture to request that Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra ply the oars and rock the rudders for Puci; that Śrītara and Avalokiteśvara hoist the sails and grip the helm before our eyes.

The supreme stream flows on, with voices chanting and harmonizing with one another. If one can simply share in the same virtue and the same mind, then naturally there will be nothing that is acceptable and nothing that is unacceptable.

Dwelling neither on this shore, nor on the other shore, nor in the middle stream, one shall directly cause all sentient beings throughout the dust-motes and hair-pores of the ten directions—the ignorant, the base, the poor, the suffering, the weary, the foul, and the impure—to spontaneously flow into *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge).
The ocean is the reliance and the refuge. At such a time as this, how would you express the single phrase: "The wind is calm and the waves are still, together enjoying peace and tranquility"?
Holding up his whisk, he said: "The heavens are high and the myriad forms are upright; the ocean is vast and the hundred rivers flow toward it."
Ascending the hall upon entering Jingci Monastery: Magnificent is this Southern Ravine, a supreme field of awakening; resplendent is this Yongming, a lofty and expansive seat.
This mountain monk is of meager talent and thin virtue—how could he dare to ascend? Yet, as the Dharma encounters conditions, it must be realized; it is difficult to decline such an opportunity.

The lake’s light glistens and the mountain colors are hazy, expansively revealing the realm of True Suchness (Tathatā). The Mirror of the School is suspended on high, and the sun of wisdom shines bright.
Radiant! The tradition of Shaoshi is expanded and magnified; every detail soars through the present and illuminates the past. At every turn, jade rolls and pearls revolve.
Truly, Śākyamuni and Maitreya rejoice together in the age of Yao, while Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra alike bask in the sun of Shun.
Although this is so, it still has not stirred the single opening above. *Katsu!* When the clash of arms has finally subsided, the four seas delight in the rising of the Way.
"Ordinary. The Master again cited Zen Master Zhijue of this mountain, who addressed the assembly, saying: "If you wish to know the purport of Yongming, there is a lake before the gate.
When the sun shines upon it, radiance arises; when the wind blows, waves emerge. The Master said, "Do you all see the Patriarch? (He struck his staff and) said:
'If you wish to discern right from wrong, his face and features are present now.'"
Jing Mountain ascends the hall: From top to bottom, it is utterly beyond the net; encompassing the earth and pervading the heavens, there is no trace.
It cannot be known by consciousness, nor can it be grasped by wisdom.

Since the picking of the flower and the smile, and the facing of the wall and the settling of the mind, we have seen only the five petals flow with fragrance and the thousand lamps continue their flames. To investigate this further is merely to create artificial complications. Even if one were to...
Above, there is nothing to grasp or look up to; below, one’s own body is cut off. With the constant light appearing before one, one stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.
How is this different from a mangy horse tied to a withered post, or a black ox lying in stagnant water?

Even if one were to possess brand-new suns and moons and a peerless standard of conduct—crossing the nine *ākalpas* upon the edge of an ice ridge, or picking up one's whole body upon the blade of a sword—it would still be right to strike three thousand times in the morning and strike [three thousand] times in the evening.
Eight hundred. Have you not seen how Master Yunmen said: "The entire universe and great earth, without a single hair’s breadth of fault—this is still a 'turning phrase.
Only when you do not see a single color is it half-revealed. You must know that there is yet a time for the full revelation."

Nevertheless, although he has always proceeded in this manner, how could the Dharma Hall not have grass over a fathom deep? Public authority does not admit even a needle, yet private paths allow for carriages and horses.
The Five Peaks rise abruptly and the Double Path winds around; the Great Enlightenment National Teacher’s vow-power was vast and profound.
Fuyou Dragon King, by virtue of pure conditions and a timely opportunity, has established this as the preeminent monastery of the Chan forest and a veritable famous mountain of the world.
It is fitting that you all hang up your alms-bowls and break your staffs, so that the eight directions may enjoy peace and tranquility, and the myriad people may sing songs of joy.
May the cawing of crows and the chirping of magpies all accord with the True Source; may the movement of wind and the rising of dust both clarify the Buddha-work. Raise [the banner]!

To propagate the sublime transformation and repay profound kindness that is both requited and unrequited—at such a moment as this, how shall one present the single phrase for the opening of the hall to bless the Emperor?
[The Master] strikes the whisk: "May the common people find immediate rest from the three calamities; may the sagely calculations extend for ten million springs.
Again, he cites a monk who asked Chan Master Yin of this mountain: "When the breath is stilled like ash, what then? Yin—

The monk said, "It is still like this; what about human effort? Yunmen said, "After the effort, what then? Xian said, "A farmer tills the field but does not sow. The monk said, "Ultimately, how is it?
Xian said, "When the grain ripens, he does not go to the threshing floor.

The Master said, "Master Xian answered the dialogue in such a way that he labored in vain without merit. If that monk had been a true man, he certainly would not have relied on another for his understanding. Later..."
Master Ying’an said: "The incense has faded in the phoenix pavilion; the snow-nest is cold at night. A bright moon fills half the window, and a serene harmony pervades.
At such a moment as this, tell me: does Guizong and Jingshan have any share in meeting one another, or not?—*shout*."
Even if you were to meet [the Buddha] face-to-face, it would still be making a living inside a toad’s den.

To see the extraordinary adaptability that extends in all four directions and eight facets, you must first apply a different kind of eye. Does the new Jingshan have no excellence? [He] strikes the meditation seat and says:
"Striking out the five-colored marrow of the phoenix; smashing to pieces the bright moon-jewel of the black dragon. For ten thousand ages, Mount Hua remains."
At your feet: it must have been Pan Lang, riding his donkey backward. Long standing, take care.
Master Chan Shi Qi, Fuzhen, ascends the hall upon entering the monastery: "Before leaving Tuṣita Heaven, he had already descended into the royal palace;

before emerging from the womb, his work of saving beings was already complete. Thus it was with the Buddhas of the three periods, the patriarchs of successive generations, and the old monks of the world."
To speak of mind and speak of nature, citing the ancients and the present, is all but ripples without wind. Truly, such sincerity deserves twenty blows of the staff.
New blessings arrive today; it is not that the Dharma is exhausted and there are no people to uphold it.
Failing to meet a true master at the outset, one ends up as nothing but old junk in the end. If you understand this thoroughly, cast off the cap of dripping fat and strip away [the robes].
"The foul-smelling cloth robe. If this is not yet so, there will be great matters to attend to tomorrow and the day after.

Again, he raised the public case of Linji’s address to the assembly concerning the "mass of red flesh. The Master said, "If Linji had not had those subsequent words, he would have been caught breaking Cai State.
Nevertheless, if one has the 'Diagram of Bai Ze' in the home, such monsters will surely not appear."
Ascending the hall upon entering Yongzuo Monastery: "In the past, I received my ordination on this very mountain as a *śrāmaṇera* named Tuobai.
Without cause, I was pushed out by others and, before the assembly of devas and humans, was called an 'Elder. Could a mud-pig or a scabby dog ever avoid such treatment?
Today, I am brought forward to this curved wooden seat to point east and draw west. This is the very first step of entering the gate."
"A single ladle of foul water. When one arrives here, having no other recourse, one must break through the mask of formality and employ some entanglements—this and that, this and that.
Thus, when the Old Śākyamuni was before Mount Prabhūtaratna at the moment the morning star appeared, he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
But tell me, what did he realize? Today, as I open the hall to preach the Dharma, I shall speak further.
"What is it? [The Master] could not help but pour a second ladle of foul water over everyone.
He took up his staff, struck it once, and let out a shout. He then raised the public case of the Sixth Patriarch and the wind and banner, saying:
"All you Zen adepts, 'the wind moves, the banner moves, the mind moves'—I have cleared this away for you. Where do you see the Patriarch now?"
Ascending the hall: Solitary and towering, steep and majestic—sages and worthies have no recourse. Vividly surging, luminous and vast, it leaves nothing remaining throughout its circumference.
There are worlds where radiance constitutes the Buddha-work; there are worlds where adornment constitutes the Buddha-work.
There are worlds where the Buddha-work is performed through fragrant food; there are worlds where the Buddha-work is performed through sound;
there are worlds where the Buddha-work is performed through silent stillness. Now tell me: here at Baon’en, what constitutes the Buddha-work?
It is the inconceivable that constitutes the Buddha-work. That is to say, the appearance of the Buddhas is inconceivable, as are the karmic fruits of sentient beings.
It is inconceivable. The formation and destruction of worlds are inconceivable; even this inconceivability is itself inconceivable.
Therefore, the one becomes the infinite, and the infinite becomes the one. Within the great, the small appears; within the small, the great appears.
"Upon the tip of a single hair, he manifests a jeweled king-realm; sitting within a mote of dust, he turns the Great Dharma Wheel.
[The Master] lets out a shout. He then cites Nantang, who said: "The sovereign is clear-sighted; the generals are alert.
Once victory is won, the six states are at peace. The Master says: "Even so, even the sovereigns Yao and Shun still had their 'transformations' (hua) remaining."
"A great merit does not stand upon reward"—how do you act upon this single phrase? "The autumn wind blows over the Wei River; fallen leaves fill Chang'an.
When entering the monastery to ascend the hall to report to the state, the Buddhas of the three periods—whether speaking horizontally or vertically—have never uttered a single word.
The six successive patriarchs fully raised and partially raised [the Dharma], yet they never succeeded in receiving a single person.
Although they received no one, each had eyes askance and a straight nose; although they spoke not a single word, every utterance rolled like jade and turned like pearls.

Releasing both and gathering both, living together and dying together; fully manifesting light and fully manifesting darkness, possessing both killing and giving life. When Deshan entered the gate, he struck him with his staff.
Linji would shout as soon as someone entered his gate; Muzhou would say, "A ready-made case," upon seeing a monk;
Zifu would turn back as soon as he saw the flagpole from across the river. To their heels, they deserve thirty blows!
An eighty-year-old entering the examination hall—this is truly no child’s play. If you can make a clear decision before the assembly, I, this mountain monk, will [grant you] my portion.
He entrusted him with the bowl bag. He further cited Master Baiyun Yuan’s address to the assembly, saying:
"If you can truly experience a single bout of breaking into a sweat, you will manifest a palace of jade and crystal upon a single blade of grass.

If you have not yet experienced a single bout of breaking into a sweat, even if there were a palace of jade and crystal, it would be covered over by a single blade of grass. The Master said: "Set aside that blade of grass."
The stalk of grass—where are the jade halls and crystal palaces? When you reach the end of the land of Jiang and Wu, mountains lie beyond mountains.

When Benjue enters the monastery and ascends the hall, he takes a step forward from atop a hundred-foot pole; the sea is vast and the sky is wide. Amidst a crowd of ten thousand people, he seizes the high banner;
with eyes keen and hands ready, the self prior to the empty kalpa is none other than the self of daily life.
The self you employ in daily life is precisely the self prior to the kalpa of emptiness.
The unspeakably, unspeakably many seas of fragrant water and the Floating Banner King lands are all entirely upon your eyebrows and eyelashes in the Hall of Universal Radiance.
This is originally Vairocana together with Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteśvara, Maitreya, Maudgalyāyana, Śāriputra, Aśvaghoṣa, and Nāgārjuna.
"I have finished expounding the Dharma-gate of the Mind-Ground for each of you. Do you hear it? If you do, you may go forth and save sentient beings wherever you are.
If you do not, Mount Shouyan’s affairs are many and I have no leisure to speak with you.
He then raised another case: A monk asked Caoshan, "How was it before all Buddhas had appeared in the world? Caoshan said, "Caoshan."
"Not as good. The monk asked, "How is it after he has appeared in the world? Shanshan said, "Not as good as Caoshan. The Master said, "Great indeed is Caoshan;
his mouth is sweet, but his heart is bitter. Suppose someone were to ask Shoushan, "How was it before all Buddhas had appeared in the world?
You would say to him, "Good. "How is it after they have appeared in the world? "Good. Giving him three "Goods"—just listen to this for a lifetime of study.

Chan Master Shiwu Hong enters the monastery and ascends the hall for the formal address. When he holds fast, not even a trace of his sharp edge is revealed; when he lets go, the ten directions are traversed in every direction.
Meeting in the depths of the waters and clouds, yet it is upon the peaks of a thousand mountains; meeting upon the peaks of a thousand mountains, yet it is in the depths of the waters and clouds.
Today, within Fuyuan Temple, the Dharma is expounded as the hall is opened; yesterday, at Tian... [text fragment]
Beside the lake hermitage, one tills the soil and cultivates amidst the mist. Thus it is said: "The Dharma has no fixed location; when conditions meet, the source is found.
This allows the wind of true stillness to be transmitted and assists the transformation of non-action. At such a time as this, how is it? [He] takes up his staff, strikes once, and says:
"When the nine-myriad-li Peng bird spreads its wings, the three-thousand-year-old crane soars aloft."
Chan Master Yunfeng Gao ascends the hall upon entering the monastery at Jiangshan. Before the world had taken form, heaven and earth were in profound stillness;

before the Buddha and sentient beings were manifested, the entire body was manifest as the absolute truth. Without cause, the Great Being Jingrong leapt forth from the eagle’s nest and split open his own face;
he had already been subjected to the scrutiny of others’ brushstrokes. Furthermore, the toothless old barbarian did not abide by his own standard, but gazed afar toward the East...
The land of China possesses the capacity for the Mahāyāna. You have come from ten thousand *li* away; your intention was to cut in line and seize the market.
Now, you have reached the drum-beating Phoenix Hall and the bell-sounding Azure Pavilion. Yet, every turn of your tongue strikes a taboo, and wherever you plant your feet, there is no door.
The entire nation finds you difficult to follow, and you have been exposed once more. I, the new Jingshan, having no choice, have boarded another’s boat and entered another’s territory.
A new official does not attend to old affairs. But in the end, what of it? [He] strikes the meditation seat and says: "The watchtower is silent, storing the moonlight of a thousand peaks;
the frontier grass lies idle, spreading the autumn across ten thousand li."
Ascending the hall upon entering Jingshan Monastery: Five peaks stand steep and high; only those who are truly such as they may reach them. A single mirror hangs in the void;
there is nothing that does not receive its illumination. The ancestral patriarchs’ legacy remains as it was; the livelihood of the patch-robed monks has never undergone change.
Precisely where one cannot lay a hand, there is the need for awakening; precisely when there is no door through which to set foot, there is the fitness for treading.
Directly, the mountain clouds are limpid and the stream waters flow murmuring. A single melody is impartial; the myriad realms enjoy their vocations.
At such a time as this, to whom does the merit belong? From antiquity, the chariots and books have shared the same script and tracks; today, the four seas are one family.
Chan Master Daian Zhuang received an imperial decree to reside at Mount Jing and enter the hall to open the Dharma assembly. This mountain monk’s Way is insufficient to compare with the sages of old;
his traces are mingled among the monastic groves as he passes his time according to natural spontaneity, seeking only to hide his ineptitude.

Little did he expect that the venerable elders of the capital would mistakenly take up his hollow reputation, deeming him worthy of inclusion among the ranks of eminent monks. Having been graced by the benevolence of the Sacred Sovereign, he was summoned to the Forbidden Palace to receive the Emperor’s personal audience.
Your sagely favor has bestowed upon me the special gift of Dharma robes. This brings glory to the ancestral tradition of Shaoshi.

As this gracious mandate is repeatedly conferred, I am now appointed to preside over the seat of the First Patriarch of the State. As it is said in the teachings, "I originally had no mind to seek [this];
now these great jewels of the Dharma have arrived spontaneously. At this moment, my humble heart knows only joy and gratitude. As for what is called the propagation of the Buddha-dharma:
To repay the imperial grace: how shall the Buddha-dharma be propagated, and how shall the imperial grace be repaid?
At this point, it is necessary that all of you understand and realize this together. [The Master] strikes the whisk. Ten thousand streams and a thousand brooks are all the Bohai Sea;

the seven golden mountains and five sacred peaks are all Mount Sumeru. He then spoke a verse: "Personally receiving the imperial decree, I emerge from the inner palace; Ascending the peak of Mount Lingxiao,"
Singing of the profound mystery: a single phrase for repaying kindness can be entrusted to you.
Having attained the highest degree in the field where Buddhas are selected, Chan Master Shuzhong Yun ascends the hall upon entering Guangfu Monastery.

The profound purport of Vulture Peak and the true mystery of Shaoshi are such that the sun and moon cannot suffice to illustrate their brilliance, nor can empty space suffice to illustrate their vastness. Lofty and sovereign in its solitary operation, it is expansive and boundless.
I reflect upon it and find it flawed; I deliberate upon it and find it erroneous. Throughout the five thousand and forty-eight fascicles, he speaks of food only to direct it toward others;

for one thousand seven hundred fascicles of entanglement, he holds a conch shell to measure the ocean. Today, throughout all quarters, there are none who do not say that he drives away their plows and robs them of their sustenance, valuing only that the ancestral style not fall into decline.
Yet they fail to realize that this is precisely like pouring fire upon those who are thirsty or trying to ward off the cold with ice.
Giving him ice only increases the severity of his ailment. New Lingyan speaks thus not to suppress the worthy and degrade them to the lowly, nor to invite the ridicule of the world.

It is like knowing how to treat a physician after one’s arm has been broken three times, or understanding physiognomy after having observed many people. Those who are clever need not ask "how" or "what if";
they should simply draw the single blade directly and sweep away the chaos of war. To sit and enjoy the peace of the era—is this not joyful?
Alas! Having just begun to waver, the white clouds have already stretched ten thousand miles. [The Master] again raised the "Old Lady of Mount Tai" koan and commented:
"The old lady was like insects eating wood, where characters happened to form by chance; Zhaozhou, seeing what he deemed right, acted with courage, yet ended up making a display of it."
"Do you all understand? When the clouds have gathered and the rain has cleared, the vast sky is wide open; a pair of mandarin ducks cannot be captured in a painting.
Chan Master Wumen Can ascended the hall upon entering Ruanfu Monastery. "The heavens are high and the earth is deep; the sun waxes and the moon wanes.

To fully raise [the teaching] or to raise it only halfway is as far apart as heaven and earth. Master Can has spent his entire life only knowing how to put on his robes and eat his meals. When he hears people..."
To speak of the two words "Buddha-Dharma" is like the wind passing over the treetops or water poured upon a stubborn stone.
Today, having stripped away my mask and called myself an "Elder," I wished to discuss this with you all;

yet, having needlessly braved the great heat of the fifth or sixth month and traveled two thousand li on a long road, it has all been lost at once. Nevertheless, there is still this staff to rely upon.
The Master was present. Holding up his staff, he said, "Staff, try and say something. He struck it once. "In this world of clarity and peace, one must strictly avoid false speech.
He then cited San-sheng, who said, "When I meet people, I come forth; when I come forth, I do not act for others. Xing-hua said, "When I meet people, I do not come forth;
when I come forth, I immediately act for others. The Master composed a verse, saying: "The brothers' capital..."
Much contention! Together they board the official boat, each rowing for themselves. Rowing away and rowing back, they look behind; as before, they have not emerged from the reed-flower marshes.
Chan Master Liaoyuan Yu, upon entering Kai-fu Monastery, ascended the hall and said: "To erect the Dharma-banner and establish the school’s fundamental tenets, one must expand [the path]..."

This is the supreme and wondrous gate that reveals the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*). What is vast about heaven? What is narrow about earth? The green mountains are not green; the white clouds are not white.
The tipsy old man at the crossroads is wide awake even in his dreams; the stinking monkey in the village of three houses possesses a truly remarkable bearing.
He overturns the nest of right and wrong and cuts off the tracks of both ordinary beings and sages. This is the staff of Deshan.
The head fully manifests the great function; beneath Linji’s shout, there is a wind-like elegance that sheds all traces of the body.

The Sage Son of Heaven, with his robes hanging and his garments properly adjusted, continues the transformation of Tang and Yu. The worthy Prime Minister, cultivating culture and laying down arms, pours forth rains like those of autumn. Thus it is said:
"A single hair manifests spiritual transformations; all Buddhas speak of this together. Even after passing through immeasurable kalpas, one cannot reach its limit.
He let out a shout and said, "I thought there would indeed be such talk as this.

He took up his staff and said, "Setting aside for a moment the question of how this staff pierces through the nostrils of everyone present—how, ultimately, did the Venerable Bao of Liang ride the Buddha Hall out through the mountain gate?"
"What have you attained? He strikes the ground with his staff and says: "A thousand-fathom whale spouts, and the great waves fly;
a single clap of thunder shakes, and the pure wind rises. He then cites the Patriarch, who said: "I originally came to this land to transmit the Dharma and save deluded beings.
One flower opens into five petals; the fruiting occurs naturally. Master Wuzu Yan said: "Master Bodhidharma truly walked with his feet."
The letter says: "Later generations have all turned this into mere calculation. Do you all wish to understand where the blossoms open and the fruit ripens?
A pear from Zhengzhou, a jujube from Qingzhou—among all things, nothing surpasses a good source. The Master said: "Bring forth the tongs and hammer of one's own fundamental share;
shatter the nests of emotional understanding. Return it to the old man of the Fifth Ancestor; only then will you see where the blossoms open and the fruit ripens."
Then it is far indeed. Do you all understand the place where flowers bloom and fruit ripen? Cast aside the pears of Zhengzhou; set down the dates of Qingzhou.
Stepping out the door, one is upon the road to Chang’an. I have stood long; take care.
Ascending the hall for the inaugural address at Lingyan: The rocky gate is perilous and the iron barrier is secure; Looking up, it is clearly ten thousand fathoms high.
Having returned here once more after forty years, From beginning to end, not a single hair’s breadth separates us. Good assembly! The deep, shimmering lake reflects like a polished mirror;
the green mountain colors reach upward into the clouds. This is the very place where Zhizhao manifested his presence.
This is truly a place for the sublime seclusion of perfect illumination. To follow in these fragrant footsteps, I am truly ashamed of my lack of talent;
yet I cannot help but proceed toward the pores of Samantabhadra’s body, expanding the world within the palm of Vimalakīrti.

I shall directly cause the four classes of sages and the six realms of ordinary beings to assemble in infinite layers, so that the wind does not rustle the branches and the rain does not break the clods of earth—wherein heaven is clear, earth is peaceful, the times are prosperous, and the Way is flourishing.

Repaying the profound kindness of both requital and non-requital; propagating the teachings of both manifestation and non-manifestation. Grasping up the iron caltrop, the pearl of the black dragon is shattered to pieces.
For ten thousand ages, all is dark and vast; the ditches and ravines are filled, yet no one understands. *Hehe!* (A shout).
Chan Master Yuejiang Yin ascends the hall upon entering Yuyuan Monastery. "The Buddha-dharma pervades all places;
throughout all mountains, rivers, and lands, there is no distinction between other regions and this land, nor any difference between the past, present, and future.
As the Great Master Yunmen said: "All of you who carry your alms-bags and travel on pilgrimage do not know that the Buddha-dharma exists even upon the Buddha Hall."
Even the *chīwén* (roof-ornaments) seem to know there is Buddha-dharma. Above is heaven; below is earth.
The sun, moon, stars, and myriad phenomena each abide in their fixed positions. What do you call "Buddha-dharma"?
Master Mazu said, "Since I first began my chaotic wandering, for thirty years I have not lacked salt and sauce. Can this be called Buddha-dharma? Damei said, "Leave it to you."
"It is neither mind nor Buddha; I am simply 'mind is itself Buddha. Can it be called the Buddha-dharma?
Yangqi said, "The diamond ring you must pass through; the thorny jujube you must swallow. Can it be called the Buddha-dharma?
Dongshan Wuzu said, "Under the gate of Baiyun, I bit through a single iron tart until its hundred flavors were fully realized."
To call that which is fully endowed "Buddha-dharma"—is this permissible? For now, let us say there is no connection.
You must know that before even the Buddha or sentient beings were fully formed, eighty-four thousand śarīra-radiations were constantly entering and exiting the gates of the faces of all of you.
It is simply that you people have failed to perceive or realize it, and you have avoided it right where you stand. What could I possibly say when I arrive here?
It can be attained. Therefore it is said: "When I sit, you must stand; when I stand, you must sit.
When I howl like a jackal, you shall roar like a lion; when you howl like a jackal, I shall roar like a lion.
In this way, one may glorify the Sun of the Buddha, greatly shake the profound breeze, establish the banner of the Dharma, and manifest the fundamental tenets—at this very time, when autumn is high.
"May your spirits be clear. I humbly wish that the various mountain masters and the entire assembly of the Great Monastery each enjoy ease and well-being. [He raises his staff.
"In the mountains of Eastern Zhejiang and the waters of Western Zhejiang—within the imperial transformation of the four seas and five lakes. [He strikes the ground once with the staff.]

I am deeply humbled by the overflowing radiance of your grace, all the more so as you have arrived here with your elephant-mounted carriage.

Now, having offered prayers for the Emperor and opened the hall to expound the Dharma for the assembly, these Buddhist rites for the season have fortunately reached their conclusion. I respectfully dedicate this superior merit to nourish the vast mountain ranges and the borderlands.

I prostrate myself and pray that the Sovereign may rejoice in prosperity and the myriad nations may enjoy universal peace. May the eminent officials present at this banquet, upon seeing this, [be inspired].
Having realized the principle of non-arising, he manifested before the assembly of the wise and erected the most supreme banner throughout the heavens.
I have troubled you with my protracted standing; I pray you, take care of yourself. Resuming his seat, he said:
"In the past, the Great Master Linji arrived at the banks of the Hutuo River and stayed in a small courtyard called Linji. He had some three hundred followers under him. One day, he addressed Puhua."
Kefu said, "I wish to establish the school of Huangbo here; you two must assist me.
He told the two of them, "Be careful," and they went down. Three days later, Puhua came up and asked, "What did the Master say three days ago?
Linji took up his staff and struck him. Three days later, Kefu came up and asked, "Master, what was the reason for [your striking] three days ago?"
He struck Puhua severely; Jue also struck him. The Master said, "One guest, one host; one push, one shove.
Cast from raw iron, forged with a blunt hammer. To establish the school of Huangbo and reveal the marrow of the ancestors, one must be such a person as this.
Yet I regret that these two men withdrew with such care, for Linji did not cut them off on the spot, which led to..."
Latter-day people play with their vital spirits three days before and three days after; today, this mountain monk, seeing injustice on the road, cannot help but exterminate them for them.
O virtuous ones! This mountain monk also wishes to establish the school of Tiantong right here.
I dare ask you all: how would you go about stripping this mountain monk of his dignity? Or would you rather say, "Please take care"? [The Master] descended from the seat.
Did he depart? Or did he come up after three days? Or did he pass from east to west? Or did he remain silent for a long while?
Or did he shake out his sleeves and leave the hall? Or did he circumambulate the seat three times and perform a woman’s bow?
Or did he raise his eyebrows, blink his eyes, point a finger, and clench his fists? Or did he overturn the Dharma-seat and shout?
"Is this dispersing the great assembly? All that has been performed above does not go beyond playing with one's spirit.

Ultimately, how will you produce a hand and eye to establish the fundamental tenet together with this mountain monk? Do you understand? A crane with nine peaks finds it difficult to spread its wings; a horse lacking a thousand-li stride vainly pursues the wind.
[The Mace is struck. "Observe closely the Dharma of the Dharma King; the Dharma of the Dharma King is thus. The Master descends from his seat.
Chan Master Feiyin Rong ascended the hall while residing at Tiantong:

"Entering the Great Jewel Realm, ascending the Great Dharma Altar, blowing the Great Dharma Conch, beating the Great Dharma Drum, and expounding the Great Dharma Meaning, he proclaimed the principles of the Linji lineage and upheld the path beyond the ordinary.
While pointing out the tracks may involve ten thousand variations and a thousand differences, to penetrate and transcend them is, in truth, a single word. Before reaching this point..."

The Master’s countenance is manifest before us; his majestic style remains as it was in antiquity. Thus, the Dharma follows the practice of the Dharma, and the banner of the Dharma is established wherever he goes.
Encountering conditions, he immediately establishes the school; wherever he is, he acts as the master. He subdues the heterodox and restores the orthodox, relying on the truth to weed out the false.
Truly, the four seas boil with excitement and the five peaks dance; at that time, the Buddhas and Patriarchs shout for joy, and the dragons and elephants hasten from afar.
They gallop forth; even those who are noble or base, sages or ordinary folk—the fourfold assembly gathers everywhere in one place.

Humans and devas meet face-to-face, each able to see the other. Everyone is taught so that their spiritual capacities accord with the single transmission; every person awakens to what they originally possessed.
Thus, within this great jewel-land and great dharma altar, bells and drums resound to the heavens, and the thunder of the Dharma shakes the earth. The spirits...
The sublime assembly of the mountain appears as if before my eyes; I am deeply bathed in imperial grace, no small matter indeed.
On the day Master Shiqi Yun ascended the seat to open the hall at Xuedou, he said: "A single move facing the sun is revealed without obstruction;
it is brilliant on all eight sides and vast throughout the ten directions. With clear-eyed witnesses present, how could I dare conceal it? It has reached the point where even jade..."
The jade palaces atop the towers are fully revealed upon the tips of a hundred blades of grass; the thousand-fathom reward-body suddenly appears amidst heaps of rubble.
Dust mote by dust mote, world-system by world-system, the "True Person of No Rank" emerges, clarifying this ready-made koan.
Even if all the Buddhas of the three periods and the ancient masters of successive generations were to arrive, each would have no choice but to step back. It is precisely at such a moment...
What of the present moment? When water returns to the great ocean, the waves and billows are stilled; when clouds reach Cangwu, the atmosphere becomes serene.
As Master Xian Chan of Fushi ascends the hall upon entering his monastery to repay the kindness [of his patrons], he said:

"Even if one were to carry [the scriptures] upon one's head for kalpas as numerous as motes of dust, and offer one’s body as a seat throughout the three thousandfold world-system, if one does not transmit the Dharma to deliver sentient beings, there would ultimately be no way to repay that kindness. He then cast down [his whisk].
The Subdirector said, "Xin Baoen has now completed the transmission of the Dharma; the assembly shall all together take up this responsibility.

Regarding the entry into the monastery and the taking up of the administrative guidelines (*tígāng*), Chan Master Yue of Yunfeng took up residence at Yunfeng and ascended the hall. An ancient said: "The wind moves, the heart wavers, and the tree [shakes]. The clouds...

The nature of birth gives rise to dust; if one clarifies the affairs of today, one obscures the person of original substance. Setting aside the affairs of today for a moment, what is this person of original substance?
After a long silence, he said: "A crane may have nine gao of open space, yet its wings find it hard to soar;
a horse may lack the thousand-li stride, yet it vainly pursues the wind. Be careful.

Chan Master Xiqian Shun was stripped of his robes by the Magistrate of Nankang due to a private grievance. Later, Emperor Renzong issued an imperial edict restoring him to the status of a monk and granting a special decree for him to reside at Qixian.
Upon entering the monastery and ascending the hall, he said: "For no reason, I was slandered and unjustly beset by misfortune."
Having been a layman for more than half a year, today I return to Sanxia Temple. How much joy, how much anger!
Chan Master Foyuan was invited by Prefect Qian to reside at Baoshan Temple; ascending the hall, he said: "The mandate of the ruler is weighty."
"Manifesting and descending upon Xue Luo. No room for stillness. *Svāhā*! The tunic and straw hat are most shabby and pitiable;
Yet one goes before others to chant 'Li-la. 'Li-li-la!'—clap once. 'La-li-la!'—clap once again. He says:
'The plum tree of last year, the willow tree of this year— Their colors and fragrance remain as they were. Man grows old, yet the waters flow on long. The Way is without mind.'"
The head is joined; the seat is lowered.
Chan Master Dahui Zonggao, having been appointed as the abbot of Jingshan, ascended the hall for his inaugural sermon. An ancient said: "Going, going, yet truly not going;
on the road, do good deeds well. Coming, coming, yet truly not coming; on the path, do not fall into peril. I dare ask the assembly: [What is this?]
Since he did not go, what was there to be well-managed? Since he did not come, what loss or peril was there?
It has been eighteen years since Miaoxi left Mount Lingjiu; today, having returned, I see neither anything well-managed nor anything lost or endangered.
"The three gates remain open to the south as before. Why is this so? After a long silence, he said: "Now the four seas are as clear as a mirror;
let the traveler not treat the road as an enemy."

Chan Master Ying’an Hua, having been appointed to reside at Guizong, ascended the hall upon entering the monastery and said: “The Great Way has no fixed location; it dwells at ease throughout the vast seas.
For many years I have longed for a place of seclusion, yet true peace and joy are found here on Mount Lu. Thus, I shall continue to uphold the traditional customs of my former home;
how could I dare recklessly alter the path? Once again I pay homage to the exquisite features of Yaśas, and once more I gaze upon the compassionate countenance that wipes away the eyes.”

It is simply that when the sound is harmonious, the echo follows; when the form is straight, the shadow is upright. Therefore it is said: "When you lift it up, heaven turns and earth revolves—you must fold your hands and surrender.
When you let it down, the grass bows and the wind blows—it is essential to withdraw your whole body to avoid harm.
Whether there or here, there is fundamentally no gap between them; going and coming—how could they have two distinct marks? Nevertheless, this is still karma.
Consciousness is vast and boundless. Furthermore, regarding the phrase "the wind is calm and the waves are still," how would you express it? When the clouds settle, the sun and moon shine bright;
when the snow clears, spring fills the world.
Chan Master Yuan’an Ji resided at Mount Jing for many years. This mountain monk, receiving his retribution according to conditions, has unworthily assumed this vacancy to sit here.
I am burdened by past karmic obstacles and have vowed to seek seclusion.

Now, having received the unwavering instructions from Mount Ling on the part of the Censor-in-Chief, the Grand Marshal, and the Chancellor, who have united their hearts to draft this petition and restore me to the position of abbot, I find it difficult to decline.
I can do nothing but follow established precedent and ascend to this seat. I reverently burn precious incense to pray for the long life of the present Emperor.

Peace! May the Empress’s years be as long as those of the Emperor; may the Crown Prince live for a thousand autumns; and may the ranks of civil and military officials likewise increase in their emoluments and longevity.

We reverently pray that the imperial domain remain forever firm and the Way of the Emperor flourish far and wide. May arms be laid down and letters cultivated; may the rivers be clear and the seas calm; may the winds and rains be timely and the crops and people prosper.
If we were to disperse just like this, having brought this period of affairs to its conclusion, would it not be entirely excellent and perfect? Furthermore, let us...
What could this mountain monk possibly say? Although it has been exactly two years since I left these mountains, morning and evening my eyebrows have been intertwined with yours.
When walking, I walk with you; when sitting, I sit with you.
Not even a single thread of a principle that constitutes a separation or obstruction can be found. Today, returning here, I rely upon...
Yet they are merely people of old, not changing their former ways of conduct. Therefore it is said: "Going and returning are boundless;
movement and stillness share a single source. Coming and going do not rely on forms; movement and stillness do not rely on the mind.

If one seeks even a hair’s breadth of the marks of movement, stillness, coming, or going, they are utterly unobtainable. If you can believe this, then each may simply settle into their own home and enjoy their own work.

Expanding the ancestral fields and gardens of his forefathers, he plays the holeless flute and sings songs of Great Peace. He drives away Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra; he dispatches Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
Within the tip of a single hair, he beholds the Jewel-King Buddha-land; sitting within a mote of dust, he turns the Great Dharma Wheel.
He moves with effortless ease, following conditions with sovereign freedom. Although it is thus, from the standpoint of a patch-robed monk, one must...
Furthermore, you have not even dreamed of the stench of his sweat.
Have you not seen how, in the past, the Great Master Ma of Jiangxi sent Xitang Zhizang to deliver a letter to Chan Master Daqian of Mount Dangshan? Upon opening the seal, Daqian saw a perfect circle;
he took up a brush and placed a single dot within the circle. This may truly be called the gallop of dragons and tigers, the turning of jade and pearls.
Return! A fine hand presents itself before a fine hand; a red heart is met by a red heart within.
For what reason did National Teacher Zhong of Nanyang say, "Master Qin was still deluded by Master Ma"? Later, Xuedou said:

"Setting aside the fact that Jingshan was deluded, if you were to present this to the National Teacher, what other skillful means would you employ to avoid being deluded? I dare ask: [What would you do?]
It is said that the elder monks of the world each possess the adamantine eye;
even if they were to extensively manifest supernatural transformations and miraculous changes, could they still escape [this critique]? I, Xuedou, wish for all of you to know my perspective:
at the very moment Master Ma drew the picture, he was already deluded. But tell me, when Xuedou delivers such a critique, can he himself escape it? No, Master Shan.
The Sangha celebrates and praises this today at the midday meal, presenting it to all of you. Taking his whisk, he draws a circle and says:
"Is there anyone here who is not deluded? He lets out a shout. Again, he cites Master Ying’an’s discourse upon returning to Guizong: "Ascending the hall..."
When Master Nan departed from the city and returned to the mountain, he presented a verse to the assembly, saying: "When departing, a stream of flowing water saw me off;
Upon my return, a valley full of white clouds welcomed me. My single body’s going and staying are neither going nor staying;
These two things are insentient, yet they seem sentient. Ying’an said: "Master Nan’s verse is fine, but he simply loves what is convenient. Guizong also has one:"
The verse was presented to the assembly: "Leaving, one braved the rain through the night; returning, one carried water and trailed mud.
I marvel at my own lack of stability throughout this life; I am constantly buffeted by the winds of karma.
Today, Fuyan (Yuanwu) has settled at Mount Jing, and he too presents a verse to the assembly: "When departing, one must repay past debts; when returning, those past debts..."
Originally empty, the carp leaps upon the mountain peak; the National Teacher displays a smile.

Chan Master Hongjue Mian, having been installed as the abbot of Tiantong, ascends the hall for the inaugural sermon: "The gate of the vast heavens stands wide open; even the thousand sages cannot reach up to it.
The great tradition of the lineage flows on majestically; the sentient beings who rely upon its shelter are beyond measure. Therefore, from...
Among the former masters of old, there were none who did not provide shelter for and nurture the myriad sprouts of sentient beings. The King [of Dharma] possesses the three realms;

as a patriarch who has attained Buddhahood, he has given rise to ten thousand schools. Yet, while many dwell within the thatched huts of their practice, the multitude who wander outside the gates is vast.

Consequently, the grand regulations have failed to be transmitted, and the great enterprise has fallen into desolation. Among the assembly, there is none who is a true son of the Dharma King capable of upholding his lineage.
"Ma! He stepped out from the assembly to meet them. While the assembly was engaged in conversation, another monk came forward; the Master took up his staff and struck him, then let out a shout.

"You must know that the seas and mountains submit to the enlightened sovereign; do not believe that there is another heaven within the universe. He planted his staff firmly and descended from his seat.
That evening, Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin gave a small sermon at Jiangshan Temple. The outline: "When meeting, do not bring it forth; as soon as you intend to act, one knows it exists.
Before a multitude of ten thousand people, he reveals his blunt and coarse nature. It is not the mechanism before one's eyes, nor is it the matter before one's eyes. Three thousand miles away."

Externally, all flaws and deficiencies are admitted; one must simply reach the point where throughout the entire expanse of heaven and earth, not even a single thread of dharma can be grasped by the intellect.
In profound stillness, free from all contradiction, even the thousand sages dare not speculate. This is placed upon the crown of all Buddhas.

Reaching this state, what more need be said of wielding the staff or shouting, of discussing the orthodox or the deviant? Whether with speech or silence, it is utterly beyond the mystical and the ineffable.
Exquisite! Releasing both and gathering both, dying together and living together; making one’s livelihood within the nest. At this very moment, how shall you investigate?
How shall you grasp it? How shall you manipulate and wield it? How shall you realize and enter it?
If there is even a single thread of artifice, you will see spirits and ghosts; do not create another.
These are but the tricks of a silkworm’s cocoon; they cannot avoid falling into the realm of "nothingness.

Within this matter, it is like the world with its heavens, earth, sun, and moon existing within Master Huguang’s gourd. Thus, Zen Master Xuefeng said, "To grasp the entire earth and bring it forth, it would be no larger than a grain of millet.
He also said, "The entire earth is the single eye of a śramaṇa. Guishan also said, "Empty space serves as..."
Taking Mount Sumeru as a drumstick—what kind of person could strike it? Nanquan said, "Old Wang does not strike this broken drum.
Fayan said, "Old Wang does not strike. Xuansha said, "Deep in the mountains and on rocky cliffs for a thousand or ten thousand years."
"Is there still Buddha-dharma in places where no one goes? Master Yunmen said: "Coming and going during the day, one distinguishes people by the light of day.
Suppose you were suddenly told to take up an object in the middle of the night; where neither sun, moon, nor lamp exists, you have never been to such a place. How would you take it?
If you do not penetrate this thoroughly, and there is even the slightest obstruction, then it will be like mountains and peaks. Or...
If you can penetrate this with your whole heart, you may act as you wish; what more is there to doubt? Nevertheless, you must truly reach such a state before it will do.
Let go at the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom precipice; advance further from the top of a hundred-foot pole.
But tell me, how is this matter to be thoroughly understood? When meeting a fellow traveler on the road, pass each other shoulder to shoulder. You!
"Facing Xiangxiang, I face Qin. He descended from his seat.

On the evening of that day, Chan Master Dahui Zonggao, while residing at Mount Jing, gave a small-scale sermon (xiaochan). "The Great Way is right before one's eyes, yet it is difficult to behold within those very eyes.
If you wish to recognize the true essence of the Great Way, it is not separate from sound, form, voice, and language. Raising his whisk, he said:

[The Master] said, "This is form. He struck the meditation seat and said, "This is sound. Right now, as this mountain monk speaks with my mouth flapping open, what is the true essence of the Great Way?
He let out a shout and said: "This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing;
there is no further sound or form to present to you. If one understands within this, there is nothing at all; essence and function do not hinder one another."
To divide or not to divide? If one were to divide it: when it rains, the earth becomes wet; when the sky clears, the sun comes out;
a short month has twenty-nine days, while a long month has thirty. If one does not divide it: the Vajra and the Earth God rub his back together until, with a single scrub, the bone is exposed.
Again he said: "The ancients said, 'The final phrase is where one first reaches the secure barrier. One must block the vital ford."
Pervading both the ordinary and the sage—what is this final phrase? After a long silence, he said, "Do not speak of dreams," and struck the meditation seat before descending.
On the evening of his arrival at Daolin, Chan Master Xueyan Qin gave a small lecture: "The Way of Jibei arises from the ordinary."
In speech and silence, in movement and stillness, the entire essence is fully revealed. The Three Mysteries and Three Essentials: the pine is straight, the thorn is crooked.
The Four Guests and Four Hosts: the duck is short, the crane is long. Thus, when Old Yuanwu spoke of the place where all Buddhas emerge, he said:

"A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool. This brings misfortune upon Miaoxi, who loses his nostrils—nowhere in the universe can they be hidden. The mountains are green.

Azure. The waters stretch boundlessly, leaving no trace of footprints; all attempts at direct engagement are severed. Beyond the bamboo fences and thatched huts of the river village, a returning sail hangs upon the distant bay as the sun sets.
Again, he raised the case of Magu visiting Linji. Linji asked, "Of the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion, which one is the true eye?
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Magu dragged Linji down from his meditation seat and sat back down himself. Linji rose and said, "How do you do? (Farewell).
Tang raised an objection. Jie dragged Tang down from the meditation seat and sat back down himself; Tang then departed. The Master commented:
"When these two great elders thus engaged in such spirited debate, although hundreds of thousands of hands and eyes were revealed all at once, how could they avoid being called 'two blind fellows'?
Tell me, is there anyone who can pass inspection? Blind!"
Zhuzhu Guangxiao said: "The Buddha-dharma originally has no 'many children. It is majestic and manifest within the midst of daily life;

it is only because one lacks self-confidence that one treats what is easy as difficult. Tonight, I cannot help but employ this expedient means to open the doors and windows for you all and shatter your knots of doubt.
He struck his whisk and said: "The stars are on the scale, not on the pan. He then raised [the case].

The Great Master Yunmen’s discourse on the story of "Awakening to the Way upon Hearing Sound. [The Ancestor] held it up and said: "This limping monk, out of fondness for his beloved child, always goes to the trouble of exposing his guts and entrails;
yet he merely fabricates things in haste, leaving behind some sticky, tooth-clinging remnants. Master Qin, however, is not like this: 'Upon hearing sound, one awakens to the Way;

upon seeing form, one clarifies the Mind.'* He then planted his staff and said: 'Every household contemplates [it]. *(Note: This is a well-known Zen phrase often used to express the simultaneous realization of both the sensory and the spiritual through ordinary perception.)*
Shiyan said while staying at Yangshan: "The Buddha-dharma pervades all places; how could it exclude Fujian or Zhejiang?
Whether Jiangdong or Jiangxi, there is no difference—it is simply one and the same: night is dark and day is bright, spring is cold and autumn is hot. Within this, suddenly—
A versatile master of broad learning clapped his hands once behind the elder’s back and cleared his throat, saying:
"Elder, you thought that because he had come from Cold Spring Pavilion, he must have new words and extraordinary insights.
It turns out his skill is merely this. He slapped his own cheek and said, "Yangshan, you are at fault. He then cited a monk who asked the former Yangshan:
Mount [Yangshan] asked, "Does the Dharma-body still preach the Dharma? Yangshan said, "I cannot preach it; there is another person who can.
The monk asked, "Where is this person who can preach it? Yangshan pushed out his pillow. When Guishan heard of this, he said, "Jizi (Yangshan) employs the business of the sword's edge.
The Master comments: "The Dharma-body preaching the Dharma has already flowed forth at the very point of the question."
"Penetrating. [The Master] pushed out his pillow; it was simply a matter of "faithfully receiving and practicing. Old Man Guishan employed the business of the sword's edge;
although one might say he arranged it into sections and chapters, as for the main text itself, I dare say it does not fall into any fixed position.
Chan Master Yuansou Duan, while residing at Zhong Tianzhu, said: "All dharmas fundamentally lack self-nature and likewise lack the nature of arising.
Names such as *bodhi* and *nirvāṇa* are derived from pure phenomena; names such as greed, hatred, craving, and grasping are derived from defiled phenomena.
One should not rely upon either of these two extremes—purity or defilement—for there are merely empty names, and even those names do not exist."
The various names and phrases, the diverse meanings of the sentences, and the three baskets and twelve divisions of the teachings do not, in total, transcend this fundamental principle.
Therefore, the ancient sages have said: "If the mind conceives and thinks, the myriad dharmas that arise are all false and unreal."
If the mind itself does not exist, how could it give rise to all phenomena?

It would be like a person taking a sound and placing it inside a casket, or like blowing into a net to make it full of air. Such is the statement of ultimate truth; to take it as being real is a great error.
The founding patriarch, Venerable Baozhang, was one thousand seventy-two years old.
There were no names, phrases, or meanings among the Three Baskets, the Five Vehicles, and the Twelve Divisions of the scriptures that he had not thoroughly practiced or fully mastered.
Later, in the city of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, he encountered the "toothless old barbarian," whereupon he suddenly realized the Great Dharma; this was by no means easy. You must simply...
"Listen closely. He then recited the verse of Master Baozhang: "Emperor Wu met his Guide; he investigated Chan and realized the mind-ground.
Drifting through the two provinces of Zhejiang, he further exhausted the finest mountains and waters. The Master also spoke a verse: "Investigating Chan requires only realizing the mind-ground.
When the mind-ground is realized, all dharmas are empty. Last night on the South Mountain, the sun was at its zenith; the white-jawed tiger bit it to death."
The "Cinder-Tailed Insect.
On the evening of his arrival at Tianning Monastery, Chan Master Chushi Qi gave a small-scale sermon (*xiaochan*).
He cited the case of Master Tong’an Pi, who, when asked by a monk, "What is the master’s house style? replied: "A golden rooster cradles its chick, leaving the mists and heavens; a jade hare..."
The fetus enters the Purple Microcosm. The monk said, "If a guest were to arrive suddenly, how would you receive them? Huian replied, "The golden fruit was plucked by the monkey at early court;
the jade flower was carried back by the phoenix at evening. The Master said, "In the mutual interplay of the orthodox and the deviant, not a single hair's breadth of the blade is struck."
In his question-and-answer sessions, Master Tongxiong was naturally brilliant and noble; Old Man Tong’an was well-versed in finding such opportunities.
Once, when someone asked Tianning, "What is the house style of the Master? he replied, "The steamed rice in the alms bowl. When asked again, "If a guest suddenly arrives, how will you receive them?
he said, "A cup of tea after the meal. Tell me, are these the same as or different from the ancients?
Abiding in the clouds of fundamental enlightenment, one cannot allow sand to enter the eyes, nor can one allow water to enter the ears.
Those who come in such a manner do not face away from a single person; they are able to place Mount Sumeru within their eyes and the great ocean waters within their ears.

Those who depart in such a manner do not turn their backs on a single person; they manifest speech where there is no speech, accomplish affairs where there is no affair, and act where there is no Buddha.

The Buddha saves sentient beings from the place of non-arising. Rolling up and unfolding, he establishes heaven and earth beyond the square; traversing vertically and horizontally, he hangs the sun and moon within the realm.
Gain and loss are both lost; right and wrong are forgotten in the distance. He turns back the upper pivot and blinds the eye at the crown of the head.
He casts aside the palace of the Empty King and sheds his original garment. Yet even this is not yet the place where a patch-robed monk finds true utility. Do you understand?
"A house without even a minor servant cannot produce a gentleman. Again, Master Zhizhe Qian addressed the assembly, saying:
"To strike the profound pivot, one must possess integrity and be utterly resolute; only a man who can cut through nails and sever iron—a person of stark, unyielding resolve—will succeed.
As for those who fear the blade and avoid the arrow, they may look on, but they have no share in this. The Master said: "Great or small, it is Zhizhe."
Exhausting one's own mind to make others laugh until their mouths split—Mount Shou has nothing particularly extraordinary about it.
At dawn, wash your face with warm water; at dusk, take off your socks and sleep. In the great ocean, the fish leap as they will; across the vast sky, the birds fly as they please.
After Zhubao Guangxiao finished recounting the story of Linji’s four shouts, the Master gave a shout and said:
"Now tell me, where does this one shout land? Is it the Vajra King’s Precious Sword? Is it the Crouching Lion?
Is it the Probing Pole and Shadow Grass? Or is it that one shout not functioning as one shout? Try to discern it. If...
It cannot be distinguished; I have already annotated and shattered this for you in the *Bao'en*. The Diamond King’s Sword can be verified right before one's eyes.
If you hesitate or deliberate, you will fall into pits and ravines. A lion crouching on the ground is the very thing right here and now.
Smash the skull and pull out the teeth. Is the probing pole and the shadow-grass good or not? Sometimes with the left hand one raises them up, and with the right hand one pushes them down. At times—
A shout is not used for the purpose of shouting. Mazu and Linji were merely talking in their sleep. Even if you understand it in this way, you still lack one shout.
(He lets out a shout.)
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun’s informal sermon at Lingyan on that evening: "Lingyan is steep and precipitous; those who reach it must find it difficult.
Those who have already arrived enjoy peace and security, while those who have not yet arrived are solitary and exposed. Those who are solitary and exposed should take a step forward;
those who enjoy their arrival must further retreat to examine themselves within. Thus it is said that matters do not always follow a single direction; sometimes..."
Turning the head into a tail; sometimes turning the tail into a head—whether gathering or releasing, whether horizontal or vertical, how could there be any fixed track?
At Mahākāśyapa’s room was closed, and at Vaiśālī words were silenced; though these are called the full implementation of the true command, they still have not reached the ultimate.

He called to the crowd, saying, "I cast down this meditation cushion; the Dharma is preached wherever one is. Suddenly, he let out a shout and struck his staff once on the ground.
Again leaning on his staff, he said: "Today, as I ascend the seat within the Maitreya Hall, I shall once more cite an ancient precedent for the sake of the great assembly.
In the beginning,布袋和尚 (Pūrnaghata) also traveled as a wandering monk just like the new Baegunsa [Baoen]. He often recounted his own life’s journey, saying:
'A single bowl for the food of a thousand households; a solitary body for travel across ten thousand miles. Later, out of compassion..."
There is a saying from the "Discourse on Falling Grass" that goes: "Maitreya is truly Maitreya; he manifests a thousand, ten thousand, and a hundred million bodies.
From time to time he reveals himself to those of this age, yet the people of this age do not recognize him. Alas! This master’s compassion is indeed great, yet his stinginess is also slight.
Today, at New Baoen, since we share this karmic affinity with the assembly in this single gathering, let us once and for all open the sack.
He has departed without revealing his head or hiding his tail. Listen attentively, Great Assembly! Maitreya is truly Maitreya; he manifests a thousand billion emanations.
Across his forehead run two horizontal eyebrows, and upon his face stands a single nose. Aha-ha! He laughs without ceasing.
Lifting up his lips, layer upon layer of skin reveals many rows of teeth and bone. Extending his hand, he says: "Everyone, give me one!"
"Patterned coins. I have one more phrase to say for you: Ten fingers, eight of them forked. Who is ordinary and who is extraordinary?
He threw down his staff and descended from the seat.
The Master Yangqi Huai, upon returning from his visit to the Ministry of War, ascended the hall to offer a formal address of thanks for the provisions provided by the temple.
"Śākyamuni Buddha acts as the vanguard; Maitreya Bodhisattva serves as the rearguard. Is there anyone among you who can exert their strength? Come forth and assist Yungai!"
Look with all your might! If there is nothing [to be seen], then Cloud-Cover (Yungai) has gone off to display his own supernatural powers.
For three or five days, watch the head seat and the assembly as they come and go. You tell me: is there still any principle of obstruction here?
Elder, when the bowls are spread in the Sangha hall, they are spread together with you; when they sleep, they sleep together with you; when they stand, they stand together with you.
Standing on the same ground as the Elder, the long one has a long Dharma-body and the short one has a short Dharma-body.
Where is there any separation between Maitreya’s application and his coming and going? Even so, tell me: is Yun-gai at the bow of the boat or at the stern?
Is there any sharp-witted monk among you who can see this? After a long silence, he said: "People!"
Everyone says the level ground is perilous; only upon ascending the tower does one realize the distant mountains are green. *Chan*.
Master Zhengen Wen, having returned from his tour of the prefecture, ascended the hall and said: "Matters of the mountains and the city do not know one another.
There is a single phrase that I have not yet dared to leak its secret; I shall wait until I have visited every quarters one by one to deliver it face-to-face. It is truly imminent."
At that time, each person must exert their own brilliance; do not let it slip away.
Upon returning from the prefecture, he ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said: 'Going, going, yet truly not going; on the road, act with goodness. Coming, coming, yet truly not coming;
on the path, do not fall into peril. The ancients did not see through to liberation, so they needlessly created complications to delude others."
Later generations [have misunderstood this]. Dongshan, however, was not like that. When coming, he simply said "coming"; when going, he simply said "going. What fault is there in that?
When I entered the prefecture, I would stay for the evening and depart at dawn.
Furthermore, what was so skillful about that? On the road back, I would rest when tired and eat when hungry. What harm or peril was there in that? Now, here in the forest among the practitioners...
People meet one another; what further matters are there? After the formal session, we drink tea.

Upon returning from outside, we enter the hall for the sermon. Having returned, it is the intercalary second month; all is silent within the Jewel Mountain. The ears and eyes of the city walls have reached their limit.
The myriad affairs of worldly toil are empty; the spring waters are green, the wild flowers are red. One must believe that the Way of the Chan school is inexhaustible.
Picking up a blade of grass at random with one’s hand, one wields life and death as one pleases, east or west.
Upon returning from outside to ascend the hall, the ancients said: "The movement of things is the common nature of humanity.
If such sentiment does not arise, then this old monk’s coming and going, whether in motion or stillness, is free from the notion of departure or arrival. Thus, human affairs are naturally fulfilled.

Furthermore, what hindrance is there to sporting within the treasury of spiritual powers, the joy of Dharma, and the bliss of Zen? In this way, one dwells together with the great assembly in the state of the Tathāgata.
"Ultimate awakening in the ocean of quiescence. [The Master] let out a shout and descended from his seat.

On his return from Zhuang Village, Chan Master Baoning Yong ascended the hall. He said: "I recall that one day after the monks had finished cleaning up, the Master of Goose Lake did not go to the hall.
Instead, he went into the abbot’s quarters and slept. After the midday meal, the administrators came and said, 'Master, why..."
He did not go to the hall. Guoshan said, "I have been eating oil-cakes at the manor. Later that evening, when the manor master arrived, he said, "Today I thanked the Master for the oil-cakes.
"Venerable assembly, is this the wondrous function of spiritual power, or is it simply the nature of reality as it is?
To act so strangely on level ground—since it is not thus, how would you do it? After a long silence, he said, "This public case..."
Let the people of the world under heaven judge this for themselves. Baoning possesses neither supernatural powers nor miraculous functions; he has no knowledge of past lives or the minds of others.
The monastery is located in Jiangning Prefecture, and its estate belongs to Yixing County. It is one thousand *li* by water and four hundred *li* by land.
A solitary boat passes through every wild crossing; willow trees by the embankments and flowers on the cliffs bloom from time to time.
I departed last month and returned yesterday; at the manor, I never ate their oil-cakes.
I simply steamed white rice and boiled wild vegetable soup, satisfying my hunger according to the family’s means, whether abundant or meager. Even so, there is yet another matter worth noting.
Anecdote: Every grain of rice was filled with worms. [He] entered the hall after his morning walk.
The frosty wind howls and the leaves fall in profusion; at dawn he enters the door of an old villager in a deep village.
Upon meeting, they simply sit together in silence; there is nothing else to discuss. After a long while, he said: "It is easier to enter the mountains and capture a tiger than it is to..."
It is difficult to speak openly to others.
Chan Master Xuedou Xian ascended the hall at his monastery; how remarkably dignified he appeared! Do you know him yet, all you venerable practitioners?
The patriarchs and Buddhas could not proclaim it; heaven and earth could not encompass it. Upon hearing it, those of the Two Vehicles’ hearts would burst;
reaching this point, even those of the Ten Stages would be struck with terror. Yet when enlightened practitioners engage in mutual refinement, they encounter a decisive confrontation;

with one pressure and one push, the essential style is briefly revealed. If the words stagnate, they stand like a mountain piercing the void; if the source is lost, clouds spread across the wilds. Therefore, the former sages—
The Way. As soon as a single word is uttered, a thousand carts share the same ruts; it encompasses even the finest motes of dust—yet this is still but a teaching of transformation.
How should you, a monk, seek it? When you know for yourself, then descend from the seat.
