Compiled by Xingyue of Loudong, Abbot of Lian’an Chan Monastery at Shiba Jian in Wulin.
A Sermon upon Returning to the Monastery after Expressing Thanks:
Master Wuzu Yan’s Outline for the Hall Discourse upon Returning from the Prefecture. "There is no idle work on the boat; from time to time, circumstances differ."
"Yesterday morning he was within the city walls; today he is amidst the white clouds. Tell me, where is the Immovable Honored One?
He said himself, "His breath is like a bellows; it makes one feel endearingly."
Chan Master Milmun Je returned from his official residence and ascended the hall.

"In one exit and one entry, in one movement and one stillness—whether in wine shops or teahouses, amidst the dust and clamor of the marketplace, or right at the butcher’s stall—suddenly striking and bumping against things, like a tiger with its horns, a chilling wind arises.
Yet when he returns and we meet, it remains as before: the eyebrows are still thick and rugged. Tell me, tell me!
"Is this the Dharma of the Buddha or the Dharma of the world? Master Xuedou replied, "The ordinary person possesses the Dharma of the ordinary person, yet the ordinary person does not know it;
the sage possesses the Dharma of the sage, yet the sage does not understand it. He struck the meditation staff and said, "First, they do not know; second, they do not understand.
East, west, south, and north—they flow forth in profusion."
Chan Master Meng’an Xin returned from his travels and ascended the hall. After being away for many days in the countryside, he had spoken at length of the cold skies and warm sun;
now that he has returned to the monastery today, how could he avoid speaking in both Chinese and barbarian tongues?

Since you know that every word reveals the ultimate truth and flows toward the source, you will then understand that every phrase cuts through like a chisel striking iron. If you can grasp this, then for both speaker and listener, the effort will not be in vain.
To fail [in this] would mean that both host and guest lose their advantage. [The master] descends from his seat.
Chan Master Yuansou Duan ascends the hall upon returning from Chengdu: "When departing, the summer heat permeated my robes; Upon returning, the autumn wind fills my face with coolness.
In the mere snap of a finger, such a difference arises— How long can the hundred-year span of life truly last?"
Returning to the hall from the city: the flower-lined streets and willow alleys expand the local scenery of one’s own ground;
the wine shops and tea houses reveal the very core of the patch-robed monk. Every person is brilliant on all eight sides; every individual is unobstructed throughout the ten directions.
Why wait until the eastern outskirts of the City of Enlightenment to see Mañjuśrī? Why must the gates of the pavilions open before one may attend to Maitreya? Holding up his staff, he said: "Three."
The child embraces a flower-drum; do not come to block my path to the ball-gate.

Chan Master Chu-shih Qi, upon returning from holding tea in the Imperial Examination Hall, ascended the hall and said: He cited Feng-xue’s sermon given within the provincial administration office at Yingzhou, which said:
"The Mind-Seal of the Patriarchs resembles the mechanism of an iron ox: if it moves away, it is sealed; if it stays still, it is sealed."
[The Master] broke [the silence]. "Just as there is neither going nor staying, is the seal applied, or is it not applied?
At that time, the Elder Lupi came forward and asked, "I possess the faculty of the Iron Ox; I request the Master not to apply the seal.

Fengxue said, "Accustomed to hooking whales and leviathans in vast depths, you instead sigh over the toad’s steps rolling in the mud. Lupi stood there lost in thought. Fengxue shouted, "Elder, what [are you thinking]?"
He did not respond. Xué prepared to deliberate, when the Master struck him with his whisk and said, "Do you still remember the *huatou*?
Try to bring it up. As Xué was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him again with the whisk. The Herdsman said, "I know that the Buddha-dharma and the royal law are the same.
Xué asked, "What principle have you seen? The Herdsman replied, "To hesitate when one ought to decide brings only misfortune."

As he was about to leave in disorder, Xué stepped down from his seat. The Master said: "The spark struck from flint, the flash of lightning—whether you grasp it or fail to grasp it, you cannot avoid losing your life.
Xué stands like a thousand-fathom cliff, cutting off the tongues of Lúpō.

If Lúpō were a man of true caliber, before he had even reached the Herdsman’s inspection, as soon as he heard it said that 'the Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs is like iron,' [he would have known better]."
"The mechanism of the ox. He let out a great laugh. If you try to deliberate upon it, he gives a single clap and departs.
Without cause, you invite the Master not to grant you the seal. Leaning on his gate and relying on his wall, you are needlessly called a "lord" by people of this age.
Now, if there were someone who could act as the true host for Fengxue, I would ask him: "Where is the Heart-Seal?"
The Master ascended the hall upon the return of the official who had been touring the monasteries with various mountain masters. He raised the following case:
When Zen Master Shimen Cong went to visit the provincial officials, he encountered the Elder of Yanqing on the road. The Elder asked, "When we meet midway, how do you speak this one phrase?
Shimen replied, "I have my share of paying respects to the Master. The next day, during the tea talk at the monastery, Yanqing said, "Yesterday I heard that you..."
Shi said, "The Master of Shimen is 'new. The Master has been at Shimen for a long time; why do you call him 'new'?
Shimen replied, "Palms joined behind the head. Shi asked, "When coming there is nothing; when going, it is empty. Both paths are lost. How can one avoid being lost?
Shimen replied, "Half a catty on the head of the scale; eight taels on the tail of the scale. The Master said, "Shimen spoke thus..."
"Such-and-such a person has the right to pay respects to the Master; even Yanqing does not know when he is being robbed. Do you wish to recognize Shimen?
Third Elder Li Jing has long experienced the ranks of battle. Nevertheless, even so, he cannot avoid using his power to deceive others."
The Marshal returns from his reconnaissance; ascending the hall, he says: "The army follows the seal’s turn; Ji Xin ascends the nine-dragon palanquin. The general pursues the talisman’s movement;
Huo Guang sells the city of counterfeit silver. Thus, where there is a talisman, there must be a general; where there is a seal, there must be an army."
"The soldiers are here; where is the seal? After a long silence, he said: "Today Baoen has encountered something great while making only a small excursion.
On his return to the temple at the beginning of winter, he ascended the hall and said: "It is easy for a single hair to swallow up the mountains, rivers, and the great earth;
it is difficult for the mountains, rivers, and the great earth to swallow up a single hair. It is neither difficult nor easy: spread out a tattered mat and sleep in the sun. He then laid down.
Imagine the Tuṣita Palace above; there is no such thing as the sun scorching one’s back here.

Again, he raised his hand and pointed to a green creeper winding its way straight up to the crest of a cold pine tree, where white clouds drift and vanish amidst the vast void. "All phenomena are fundamentally still, yet it is people who create the clamor.
Huanglong asked, "What is there to clamor about? The Master said, "Do not say that there is nothing to do."
Ascending the Dharma Hall upon returning from the Imperial Capital: the wind does not whistle through the branches; the rain does not break the clods of earth; the people do not lose their dwellings;
and on the roads, nothing is left to be picked up. At such a time as this, what a season of Great Peace!

Recently, this mountain monk received an imperial mission and traveled far to the capital, where he stood face-to-face with the Dragon Countenance and personally heard the imperial edict. A meeting of wind and clouds, a celebration of fortune once in a thousand years—now that I am returning.
How shall the mountain repay [this]? It does not go beyond this very moment.

When the Buddhas appear in the world and the Patriarchs come from the West, when the old monks throughout the land point directly or speak circuitously, none of it ever goes beyond this very moment. Therefore it is said:

"If you wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the conditions of time and season. When the time and season arrive, its principle will manifest of itself. For now, let us simply act as such.
"What is this principle that manifests itself? The imperial domain matches the North Pole; the Sage’s longevity equals the Southern Mountain.
Master Shiwu Gong ascended the hall upon returning to his monastery and said: "The old ox has stolen a moment's leisure for half a year;

the fields of the ancestral estate are overgrown with weeds. Having returned, he is too lazy to repay his debt again; the plow and harrow are once more placed upon his shoulders in the spring breeze. "It is so, indeed."
The ancestors have not yet reached resolution; it is difficult to escape the constraints of past karma. Four hooves plow the white waters; two horns point toward the blue sky.
(He strikes his knee once and says: "What a pity no one understands this meaning. Before the wind, it makes me remember Nanquan."

Chan Master Yuan’an Jiqi went out to the Zhuang estate and returned to request that the Guest Prefect ascend the hall. "Yesterday I passed through the southern village; this morning I am again at the eastern gate.

In movement and stillness, in going and coming—how has there ever been any separation? Yet when one moves, one enters the realm of worldly toil; when one is still, one sinks into the land of昏醉 (delusive intoxication).
When both movement and stillness are extinguished, one falls into emptiness and oblivion. When movement and stillness are practiced together," [the Master continued].
Thus, the Buddha-nature is vast and indistinct—thirty-seven, forty-eight. "The pleasures of the road are not as good as being at home.
He lets out a shout and says: "Who is there at the painted tower where wine is sold? Come, let us be invited to drink Zhaozhou’s tea."
Chan Master Wumen Can entered Zhejiang and upon his return, ascended the hall to address the assembly: "I have been away for five or six months, traveling three thousand li back and forth.
Trusting my feet, I have kicked it; trusting my hands, I have lifted it up. I have never casually shown it to others; I have hidden it deep within the folds of my sleeves."
"Returning, we invite the entire assembly to perform a 'joyous rite of entry. What is it? The mountains of East Zhejiang and the waters of West Zhejiang.
Master Liaohan Yu ascended the hall; having entered the city and reflected upon his teaching, he returned to present this to the assembly.
"I only fear that if one does not hear the matter truly, one cannot help but mistake a bell for a water jar. He then descended from the seat.
Chan Master Nan Shiyou ascends the hall from his return to the capital, simultaneously expressing gratitude to the Secretary and the Chief Administrator. His movement is like drifting clouds;
his stillness is like the spirit of the valley. Having no mind for "this" or "that," how could there be any form of coming or going?

Last year, in the fifth month, I, this mountain man, responded to the summons to enter the Wenyuan Pavilion to collate the *Yongle Encyclopedia*. Moving in and out of the imperial court... [the waves].
Poxieqie continued to attend the great assembly, where he was granted the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. It took him eight months to complete the journey;
upon his return to Gusu to visit old friends, another two months passed. When he finally reached the mountains, it happened to be mid-spring. Now tell me: did he have a mind for this or that?
Was he without a mind for this or that? Did he have a form in coming and going? Or was he without a form in coming and going?
Indeed. A sharp and discerning monk, before a word is spoken, has already grasped the meaning; before a movement is made, he already knows it.

Thus, he can extend the Buddha’s hand, sweep past the patriarchs’ barrier, extinguish the lineage of the old barbarian, and restore the groves of monasteries for a thousand ages. Nevertheless, the sovereign’s grace is profound and weighty, beyond the reach of thought or speech.
I have respectfully composed this verse to express my humble sentiments: The Sūtra was specially bestowed from the inner treasury.
People return from within the nine-layered city; on the Five-Tufted Peak, the spring sun is warm. Mountains, forests, springs, and rocks all radiate brilliance.
Chan Master Yuezhao Wenzhan ascends the hall and says: "Before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja, the mind of nirvāṇa was easy to understand. King Bhīṣma...
After the King of Sound, the wisdom of differentiation is difficult to clarify. How is it that "Today it rains; yesterday it was sunny" is the mind of nirvana?
How is it that "Yesterday it was sunny; today it rains" is the wisdom of differentiation?

Suddenly, if a patch-robed monk comes forth and says, "Master, for you to speak in such a manner is not without merit within the gate of proclaiming the teaching, yet you have not even dreamed of a true patch-robed monk."
The fundamental matter is present. But what is this fundamental matter of the patch-robed monk? Only when returning to the courtyard in leisure does one find it:
the tender green has already crept over the wall.
Chan Master Muyunmen ascends the hall upon his return from a temporary absence. "Going away, truly he does not go; on the road, may you do good.
Coming back, truly he does not come; on the way, do not suffer peril. This mountain monk has been abroad for five or six days.
I respectfully wish that the head officers, the administrative staff, and the great assembly may each enjoy ten thousand blessings. I recall last evening at the donor’s house..."
At the juncture when Yang (the sun) was about to return but had not yet returned, the Mulberry Forest was vast and open, and the Milky Way was wide and clear.
My secluded thoughts were deeply satisfied, and unconsciously I composed half a gāthā: "This night’s moon is exceptionally fine; The light clouds are as thin as autumn.
Before I had finished speaking, a great wind suddenly arose from the northwest, followed by a sudden downpour of rain and two thunderclaps crashing down. I do not know—
"Is there still this very message here? A monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "I have exhausted you to the limit," and immediately descended from his seat.
He addressed the assembly, stating the essential principles for going on a mission.

Zen Master Wuzu Yan addressed the assembly before departing on a military expedition, ascending the hall and saying: "Tomorrow, with a single horse and a solitary spear, I shall go forth to battle for the sake of the nation.
On the day I return victorious with my spear lowered, there will be songs of joy along the entire road.
Great assembly, what is this one song of joy? He then said: "Lo-lo-li, lo-lo-li. "Is there anyone who can harmonize with this? After a long silence, he said: "The embroidered mandarin ducks."
"Look directly for yourself; do not pass the golden needle to others.
Zen Master Yuanwu Qin gave this small-scale sermon while on military patrol: "He opens the forge of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and employs the tongs and hammer of the ultimate path.
If you hesitate even for a moment, you are a thousand miles away; if you realize it upon meeting the challenge, you cut off the vital ford. This is still..."
Regarding the teaching of the gate of transformation: if we discuss it according to reality, this mountain monk has a mouth but no place to speak;

all you people have ears but no place to listen in. Even the sun and moon are insufficient to provide illumination; empty space is insufficient to provide breadth; heaven and earth are insufficient to provide greatness;
and the myriad phenomena are insufficient to provide multiplicity. When one arrives here, there is only a single squeeze, a single press, a single nudge, and a single push.
The essential point is to see the matter of one's own fundamental portion. For now, let me ask: what is this fundamental matter? The great chiliocosm is but a bubble in the sea;
all sages and worthies are like a flash of lightning.
Chan Master Meng’an Xin went out into the world to address the assembly before ascending the hall: “Within long streets and short alleys, we turn the Great Dharma Wheel;
this requires everyone to lend a hand. Amidst wine shops and fish markets, we establish the Buddha’s work; one must not advance alone.
Now, let us enter the marketplace together, wishing to behold the joyful Buddha Ratnākara. He then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Miam Je ascends the hall after leaving his native village. The midsummer heat blazes like fire; who knows that the cool place surpasses ice and snow?
Amidst the clamor of the dusty marketplace, he awaits a person of true caliber; the ritual protocols of the Seven Buddhas have all been revealed. Announce this to the Dragon King!

One must rely on the protection of merit. To gather the great trichiliocosm into a single pinch constitutes the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*). A single word fixes all things, yet ten thousand functions flow through;
naturally, this brings forth the majestic spirit of the Shaolin tradition. Again, regarding the public case of the World-Honored One’s command to Ānanda to carry the bowl, the Master said:
"The Great and Small World-Honored One was lightly leaned upon by Ānanda; he could not help but mistake the bell for a jar."
On the first day of the seventh month, Chan Master Yuejiang Yin ascended the hall while walking on the path and said: "For thirty years I have resided at Zihu;
The strength of my two-meal rice and gruel has been coarse. With nothing to do, I go down the mountain for a stroll; I ask you people of this time: do you understand?"
Why do you, my son, so greatly resemble one who is aged and solitary in heart? Yunfeng is not like this: for three or four years he has resided at a monastery;

twice daily he partakes of gruel and rice with vigorous strength. When the communal labor calls him down the mountain for a turn, the fragrance of the tilled and weeded fields spreads across ten thousand acres.

Chan Master Yulin Xiu addressed the assembly before departing on a tour, ascending the hall: "In the Western Heaven, the Buddhas and Patriarchs mostly practiced itinerant teaching rather than establishing formal monasteries;
in this Eastern Land, the masters of knowledge mostly established monasteries rather than practicing itinerant teaching.

Although these two approaches differ according to their respective regions, if one examines them closely, they are both merely adhering to a single corner and failing to excel in adaptability and transformation. New Baoren..."

That is not so. To establish a *bodhimaṇḍa* does not preclude practicing transformation according to the times; indeed, practicing transformation according to the times is fundamentally for the purpose of establishing a *bodhimaṇḍa*.

Now tell me, who is this person at Xin Bao’en? One who possesses such power relies solely on a single heart of gratitude, offering up body and life entirely to serve the dust-motes and lands of the universe. Having said this, he struck his staff and departed.
Chan Master Fenshan of Jianmen ascended the hall to preach after having established Jianmen Hermitage. The old monk himself composed this inscription:

The stingy ghosts have vanished without a trace; The donors have opened the gates. In the Buddha-land we dwell together in peace. How great! Forever firm and solid, The benefits shall be inexhaustible.
From ancient times to the present, there is no other path. For a long time I have not descended from the mountain; Tomorrow I shall go down the mountain. From [here].
Whether rich or poor, he brings it forth without any evasion. [He] descends from the seat.
Master Wuzu Yan, returning from a military expedition, ascended the hall and said: "I have been away on expedition for half a month; my eyes could not see my own nose."
Forgetting the Zen of the Patriarchs, one picks up a piece of antiquity. Tell me, where shall it be placed?
One part is offered to Śākyamuni Buddha; one part is offered to the Stūpa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha.
Returning from his alms-round, he ascends the hall at Baiyun Haichui Monastery. There is plenty of water as well as firewood and charcoal; we lack only hemp and wheat.
Everyone has clearly seen this, yet while you personally go to solicit donors, you neglect the Arhats. I hope for your great compassion.
"Look at the Buddha’s face one by one. "Great assembly, the Buddha-body fills the Dharma-realm; how then do you look?
I say: not separated by so much as a single thread.
Chan Master Foyuan returns from his travels; ascending the hall, he departs through the gate as the sun rises. He has already begun to encounter the mist and fog;
braving the moonlight, he gazes toward the mountains on his way home. Heavy dew dampens his dhyāna robes. His heart is silent and still; his steps are slow and measured.
The unperforated flute is blown again and again: *li li ro ro ro li*. The traveler, hearing it for the first time, finds his travel-sleeve moistened; the lady still sings the "Cui" melody.
Lower your brows. Listen further. Do not be suspicious. What tune is this? Return to the hall.
Chan Master Dahui Gaofeng, upon returning from his travels, ascended the hall and said: "Master Zhao says: 'Movement is like drifting clouds;
stillness is like the spirit of the valley. Since there is no mind regarding self and other, how could there be any form of coming or going? Master Xiu then said: "To go..."
When going, there is truly no going; one should practice what is good along the way. When coming, there is truly no coming; do not fall into peril on the road. The Master said:

"It is a pity that these two old fellows did not live at the same time as I am at Jing Mountain. Had they been contemporaries, I would have bound them together as a single bundle and cast them into the Qiantang River.
Why? Because the mountains and rivers of past and present are the same, and the sun and moon of past and present are the same."
Now, regarding human relations: when it is cold, the entire heavens and the entire earth are cold; when it is hot, the entire heavens and the entire earth are hot.
As for coming and going, moving and resting—what fault is there in that?

Suppose a monk were to come forth and say, "If Mount Jing says such things, I would tie them up in a bundle and cast them into the Qiantang River. To this, I, the mountain monk, would simply say: "It is hot!"
He warmed a cup and offered tea for him to drink. Why is it so? A true man plucking a tiger’s whiskers—how could this be considered extraordinary?

Upon returning from his journey outside the village, he ascended the hall. He cited the Elder Wuzu, who, upon returning from a military expedition, addressed the assembly, saying: "Half a person went on the expedition."
The Moon: The eyes do not see the nostrils; one has lost the Zen of the Patriarchs and picked up a mere antique.
Tell me, where shall it be placed? One part is offered to Śākyamuni Buddha; one part is offered to the Stūpa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha.

Casting a Buddha: A monk asked, "What is the golden Buddha that does not pass through the furnace? The Master said, "Fill the ditches and block the ravines."
The student asked, "How is it that the wooden Buddha does not pass through fire? The Master said, "It is precisely at this time.
The student asked, "How is it that the clay Buddha does not pass through water? The Master said, "East, west, south, north—eighty thousand miles. He then said: "The clay Buddha has been soaked;
the wooden Buddha has been burned; the golden Buddha has been melted; and the true Buddha has been scrutinized and seen through. — Zhaozhou.
This old man has been dismissed from the monastery; once gone, he will not return again. *Duḥ!* [Heavenly shout!
Entering the hall to pay homage to the ten thousand Buddhas: "Night after night one embraces the Buddha in sleep. What do you call this "Buddha"? "Morning after morning one rises together with him."
Do not mistake the scale for the moon. Rising and sitting, it follows you at all times. After all, who is this? Whether speaking or silent, dwelling together;
neither one nor two, not even a hair’s breadth apart. It is like the relationship between a body and its shadow.

This single expanse of empty space—how many people fail to grasp it? No matter how refined the pure gold through a hundred smeltings, or how clever the myriad schemes devised, it cannot be cast [into form].

It cannot be cast by casting; it cannot be carved by carving. As soon as Master Fatai opened his forge, its spirit was revealed, shining across the earth and heavens, transcending the present and illuminating the past. Nevertheless, he too could only capture half of it.
From morning until evening, as you all enter the hall, pass through the door, spread out your mats, and unfold your bowls, what concealment can there be for your original face?
"Place! Do you see it yet? If you do not investigate the source now, you must wait until that year when you ask Maitreya.
While presiding over the assembly, he raised the case of Nanquan calling for the courtyard master. When the master responded, Nanquan said:

"Please, Maudgalyāyana, employ your supernatural powers to lead the craftsmen there three times to carve a Buddha image.
They managed to carve thirty-one of the marks, but why was the mark of the Brahma-voice (*brahmasvara*) not carved? The Abbot asked, "What is the mark of the Brahma-voice?

He attains the mark of the Brahma-voice. To those who are to be liberated by a Buddha-body, he manifests a Buddha-body and preaches the Dharma for them.

Even to those who are to be liberated by the bodies of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth—he manifests all such forms and preaches the Dharma for them. Moreover...
"What dharma does the Way speak of? Having said this, he descended from his seat.

He ascended the hall to consecrate a statue of the Thousand-Armed Great Compassionate One, stating: "According to the teachings, the deluded perceptions of sentient beings do not depart from the sensory objects before them."
When opening the eyes, one sees light; yet this light is not light. When closing the eyes, one sees darkness; yet this darkness is not darkness.
Passing in front of the Buddha hall, one does not see what is behind it; passing behind the Buddha hall, one does not see what is in front of it.

All of these belong to deluded perceptions obstructed by external objects (*viṣaya*). If one were separated from these external objects, there would be no Buddha to be seen. According to Yongzuo’s perspective, [this is] great.
"Pitiful! A Bodhisattva originally has no body, nor hands or eyes. Yet some say, 'I understand! I understand!
Give them twenty-nine blows and drive them out; keep one blow for yourself. Is there anyone who can bring down their hand?"
As it was, Ma-zu lost the advantage today. Mazu raised the question that Gu-ku had asked Lin-chi: "Of the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion, which one is the True Eye?
Lin-chi said, "Of the thousand hands and eyes of Great Compassion, which one is the True Eye? Speak quickly! Speak quickly!"
Dagu pulled Huairang down from the meditation seat; Huairang sat back down. Dagu said, "How do you do? Huairang then shouted. Dagu pulled Huairang down from the meditation seat;

When Master Xueguan Yuan’s sandalwood image was completed, a donor invited him to ascend the hall. Zhaozhou said:

A Case for Use. Caoshan asked a monk, "The Buddha’s true Dharma-body is like empty space; it manifests forms in response to things, like the moon reflected in water.
How do you explain this principle of 'responding'? The monk said, "It is like a donkey looking down a well. Caoshan said: [The monk was struck.]
"The Way! Truly, what a way it is! Yet he has only managed to express eighty percent of it. The monk asked, "How about you, Master? Caoshan said, "It is like looking down a well at a donkey.
This mountain monk says: In skillful modeling, none equals Cao Shan; in skillful carving, none equals Old Zhao.
Not a trace of the blade's mark is revealed—truly, his craftsmanship is sublime. If you can understand "like a donkey looking down a well," then you will comprehend the stem.
Grass is transformed into a golden body. If you can understand it like looking at a donkey in a well, then you will know that the sixteen-foot golden body is right within the grass.
Maudgalyāyana’s exercise of supernatural powers was in vain; King Udayana’s laborious craftsmanship was for naught. Danxia’s true command is applied directly to one's head.
Who says that descendants are either worthy or unworthy? Nevertheless, while principle has no duality, how can it be that the Dharma does not have a single direction?
Ding Lan carved a wooden figure to serve his parents; when he pricked it with a needle, blood flowed. This is no different from the Tuṣita Heaven palace descending below.

When the image goes out to welcome the Buddha, the Buddha comes to welcome the image. If you use conceptual consciousness to falsely create distance between them, it is like scratching an itch through a boot—your gazing upward will be in vain.

"What merit is there? He planted his staff upright and said: "Seeking no tainted blessings of humans or devas, Great Filial Piety fully manifests the Mind of the Ancient Buddha.
On the birthday of the Great Being Chan Master Mimi of Songshan, when the image was completed and its eyes were opened, he ascended the hall. The spring air was clear and mild; the assembly...
The birds sing; along the misty village, willows trail green. Within this mass of form and sound, it is clearly manifest.
To touch upon it is for one’s entire being to become the eye. All you people, if you can understand it thus: when hearing sounds, wondrous wisdom is born;
where seeing forms, perfect penetration appears. Holding the handle of sovereign power, the great mechanism operates in secret. It penetrates above and reaches below, encompassing heaven and earth.
Nothing can contain or cover it. How could the myriad things possibly conceal it? It is manifest yet not exposed; hidden yet ever more clearly revealed.
It is no different between past and present; those who attain it follow the same path. Do you all wish to know what this "same path" entails? After a long silence, he said:
"When Bole once passes by, even the feeble horses all neigh. He then descended from his seat.

An Outline for Inviting the Tripitaka (Inviting the Case, Welcoming the Scriptures, Opening the Scriptures, Reading the Scriptures, Drying the Scriptures, Repairing the Scriptures, Sunning the Scriptures).
Chan Master Chushi Qi ascended the hall to give a discourse on the newly acquired Tripitaka. He cited the following:

One day, while Xuefeng was leading a communal work party to carry firewood, he encountered a monk on the road. He then threw down a piece of wood and said, "The entire Great Tripitaka speaks of only this."
Later, Zhenru Zhe said, "The entire Great Canon of Teachings does not speak of this. The Master asked, "What is this very thing?
As for speaking or not speaking, where do you all see these two great elders?

The Sage clarifies the ordinary by using the new to perceive the old, and makes the sutras manifest through the cases.
How fitting that each and every dharma established therein is both-and-yet. Though both-and-yet, it does not involve duality; what is established is capable of all things.
This great gate of liberation is deeply understood only by the wise. Thus, Master Shitou said: "Within light there is darkness; do not look for it through the aspect of darkness."
"When there is darkness, there is light; do not meet light with light. Light and darkness face one another, like front and back steps.
He then picked up his staff and said, "Tell me, is this light or is it dark? To leap out of it is truly marvelous; if you cannot leap out, you remain within light and darkness.
Yet even this very light and darkness is difficult to clarify. He then struck the incense table and descended from his seat.
Chan Master Zhuo’an Welcomes the Tripitaka to the Mountain and Addresses the Assembly: Jade rollers and golden cases—the ancient Buddha-mind;

Ten thousand years of perpetual blessing for the sagely sovereign. In these woods and springs, we are fortunate to receive your grace; Throughout the vast days, all is tranquil—thanksgiving for the peace of the age.

When the whale swallows the sea water until it is gone, the coral branches are revealed.

It is said: "Breaking through the two layers of barriers; a person from Sizhou sees the Great Sage.
Chan Master Zhu-yun Tan, while roasting scriptures, ascended the hall and said: "The numinous texts of the ocean-store of the Dharma transcend and encompass heaven and earth;
their jade-encased volumes turn like jewels, filling the valleys and filling the ditches. What the Tathāgata did not speak, he spoke—beating out the five-colored marrow of the phoenix. Kāśyapa..."
Hearing upon hearing, he shattered the pearl from beneath the jaw of the black dragon. The flame preaches the Dharma for the Buddhas of the three periods;
its meaning shines like a bright sky, lifting up the earth’s foundations. The Buddhas of the three periods preach the Dharma upon the flame;

not a trace of a character remains as the Dharma-realm becomes empty. Within the *tūla* cotton, the jade turns and the pearl revolves; amidst the civil and martial fires, the stars shift and the lightning rolls. Line after line...
Casting out golden characters upon yellow paper, flower after flower blooms upon white jade lotuses. Deeply tranquil and unmoving, the True Person (Arhat) does not rely on external aid.
But what of the saying: "The sutras return to the treasury; Chan returns to the sea"? How is this so? Five thousand scrolls of paper, scarred by the brush;

the Dharma is a vessel for ascending high to the other shore; the Dharma is the eyes that open for humans and devas. O virtuous ones, let us set aside for a moment the fact that the benefits of the Dharma are inexhaustible and its praises can never be fully told.
Consider this: prior to the empty kalpa beyond the limit of majestic sound (Vibhāvasu), even the names of the Three Jewels did not yet exist.
At the moment of naming, does the Buddha precede the Dharma, or does the Dharma precede the Buddha? If the Dharma preceded the Buddha, who was the one to proclaim it?
If the Buddha preceded the Dharma, then [the Buddha] would still be ignorant of the path of cultivation.
If you can here burst open a single eye and personally see the source of the Buddha-Dharma, then the Dharma is itself the primordial Dharma; it does not flow forth from the Buddha.
The Buddha is the Buddha from the very beginning; he is not accomplished through the cultivation of dharmas.

Since he is not accomplished through the cultivation of dharmas, he did not depart from Tuṣita Heaven before descending to the royal palace, nor was his work of saving sentient beings finished before emerging from his mother’s womb. It is not from the Buddha that [this teaching] has spread.
From the land of Prabhāsa at the beginning until the river Vārāṇasī at the end—during these two intervals, not a single word was ever spoken.
If this is so, then Zhou Jingang may take the *Qinglong Shuchao* and burn it all with a single torch;
Xiao Shijia may regard the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* as entirely the words of Māra. What further fault could there be? If you have not yet reached this realization, then upon the tip of a single hair—

Regarding the framework for construction—clearing the weeds, laying the foundation, setting the foundation stones, and erecting the pillars—the Chan Master Jianmen Fen said:
"Brilliant and luminous, lacking nothing; though there are a thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions," [it remains as it is].
Nengju established a hermitage on the summit of Mount Hushan, where he cleared away the weeds. He asked with a smile, "Do people see it?

I ask you all to cut down the thorns and remove the rubble. The original site is already clearly visible, yet there remains only that tree in the center."
No one has been able to pull it out. Today, this mountain monk cannot help but employ another expedient means: with a sharp blade, he shears away all the profuse branches and leaves;
with a blunt hoe, he deeply digs up the roots of perversion. The work on the ground of reality becomes a single whole; the pickaxe of the mountain-dweller leaves no trace.
Chan Master Yuansou Duan ascended the hall at the request of Puqing Monastery. "The Dharmakāya is formless, encompassing the ten voids;
the Dharma-eye is flawless, containing all phenomena. It is pure and naked, beyond any claim of attainment; it is bright and unadorned, without any deficiency."
Like the heavens universally covering all, like the earth universally supporting all; directly realizing that the one is the infinite and the infinite is the one;
manifesting the great within the small and the small within the great; manifesting the Jewel-King Land upon the tip of a single hair;
sitting within a mote of dust while turning the Great Dharma Wheel—at such a time as this, is there anyone who can meet you, Elder Yunen? If...

From beginning to end. Should you hesitate even for a moment, listen further to this verse: In the realm of the Unsurpassed Jewel King, who among those present can truly perceive it?

Those who bury their heads in the burning house—throughout ancient and modern times, they have been muddled and indistinct.

Chan Master Fen of Jianmen held up a pillar and said: "The Dharma-gate’s preeminent ridgepole and beam, loftily stabilizing the foundation of blessings for all living beings.

across the vast and boundless universe, how many people know it?"

Touch it! Observe how his every action surpasses the pavilions of Vairocana; he lightly places it upon the summit, allowing it to be grasped horizontally or vertically as one pleases.
Do you see, Great Assembly? May the Sage’s life be boundless, and may the myriad people live in peace and happiness.

Within the brows and eyelashes lies the Land of Awesome Sound; May the rains be favorable and the winds harmonious—congratulations to the Sage’s brilliance!
The Lifting of the Beams for the Great Hall at Lake Tai: Supporting heaven and propping up earth, the gateway stands firm; Picking it up with a casual hand, its application is intimate.
A jade palace and a crystal tower are but a single blade of grass; Throughout the heavens and across the earth, radiance is released.
After a long silence, he said: "Arise! Covering the sixteen-foot golden body."

Gently place it upon the crown of the head; from all four sides, the pure breeze stirs through the vast void. Do you see, Great Assembly?
I take up this useless thing and show you the supreme point beyond. *Shout!* (Hei!)

With the sound of the Dharma, may we for a thousand years pray for imperial grace.

The Sangha must adapt to the times and accord with the seasons; for now, they must blend with the mundane world and harmonize with the light.

Just now, because we encountered the "Leaning on the Beam" (pāo liáng) [chant], how could we avoid following the current and drifting with the waves? As it is said: "The Dharma does not arise in isolation; it arises only by relying on conditions.

It is perfected wherever it is encountered and established according to what is appropriate. I dare ask you all: tell me, what is being established right now? Have you not heard it said: "Leaning on the Beam to the East"?
The Chan Gate is a distinct school with its own style. As incense of agalloch smolders by the shores of the vast sea, may the Sage King’s divine years be forever without end.
Casting a beam toward the West, at Shaolin, branches sprout anew from the joints. After the single flower has unfolded into five petals, the fruition is perfected, wondrous in every place.
Casting a beam toward the South, Sudhana—on that day he needlessly sought instruction; having worn out his straw sandals, he returned home.
Calculating the days: a thousand peaks remain as ever, their color like indigo. Throwing the beam northward—Zhaozhou’s courtyard cypress is difficult for people to recognize;

its verdant hue cherishes the heart that endures the cold of winter, yet though one tries to identify it, it remains ungraspable as before. Throwing the beam upward—regarding Buddhist matters, there is no single direction within the gate;
the *yakṣas*, demonic hordes, and *asuras*, along with the eight classes of dragon-deities, all look up in reverence. Throwing the beam downward—

A single piece, solid and without seam or fissure. The Earth Deity lifts it forth, towering toward the heart of heaven; it shall forever stabilize the vast ocean and sing of the Sage’s transformation.
Great Assembly: It pervades all four directions, above and below. Then, drawing a circle, he said: "Now, as for this steamed bun, where would you cast it?

Originally there is no person who is deluded or awakened; one simply requires this very day. Once you have understood this day, you sit thus, cutting off the heads of both the *nirmāṇakāya* and *saṃbhogakāya* Buddhas.

Furthermore, how is it that one cuts off the various sense-faculties? Letting down a single thread of the Way to pass through a message—do you understand this yet?
It is like obtaining sweet rain during a great drought, or attaining coolness amidst intense heat. There is also a verse that says: "The myriad peaks wind and turn, the halls are deep and vast;

This ancient monastery was renowned for its fame.

May [the Emperor] be protected. May the myriad blessings of humans and devas be shared equally; may the altars of state and the mountains and rivers be made firm; and may the celestial mandate forever preserve the Imperial person.

We reverently observe that Your Majesty’s sagacity and wisdom are innate, and your divine martial prowess is bestowed by Heaven. Governing the eight extremities of the world, you have discerned the subtle sentiments of the people and things;

you have swept away the multitude of rebels and restored the orthodox succession of the Founding Ancestors. Consequently, since your accession to the throne, auspicious omens have repeatedly descended, and the seas...

Its value is unknown; it remains for the world to illuminate the night.
The late masters have left behind their writings.
Upon the arrival of the letters from Master Zhigai of Yungai and Master Sishin of Huanglong, he ascended the hall and said: "A great misfortune has befallen the Dharma gate."
The Dharma-banner is toppled; within the mountains of the five aggregates, they are transformed into ashes. Last night, the clay ox passed through a single thread;
from this moment, Huanglong enters the cycle of saṃsāra.
Master Longmen Yuan’s letter from the late Master Sishin of Mount Huanglong has arrived; [he] ascends the hall. Sishin’s mind...
He is already dead; though his heart has died, he still lives. He snaps off the horns of the Yellow Dragon and turns his body over to walk upon the earth.
This old man has from the start worn his robe inside out and carries his scholar’s hat upside down. His speech is coarse and blunt, yet his heart is gentle and harmonious.
He inspects the monastic groves and rebukes the students; although he transmits the Way of Huìtáng, he loves to employ the Chan of Yúnmén, using it to scold the wind and scold the rain.

Yu acted as a teacher for his disciples, making the cultivation of vegetables and greens his primary task. He brought about calamities and sent down misfortunes; he was seldom joyful and frequently wrathful.
When fools saw him, they knit their brows in displeasure; when the wise saw him, they nodded in agreement. Whenever he wished to leave, he would depart immediately—truly a master of the Way.
Tengshen was originally a Miao person; in his sleep, he lost the old man of the "dead heart. Alas! What a tragedy for the Dharma gate!

Upon the arrival of the late Master Huanglong Lingyuan’s final letter, he ascended the hall and said: "In the past, he engraved the 'Continuation of the Orthodox' (Zhengxu); now, he reveals his true return."

He proclaimed: "The single path to the gate of Nirvana—both in practice and in teaching, he has personally reached it. He brightly kindles the lamp of Linji and skillfully sings the song of Huanglong.
The empty ocean has long been clear and still; now the clouds and waves surge vast and wide.

Swallowing the great sea at once and piloting a high-riding iron ship, he whose hidden and manifest states share a common source and whose unfolding and rolling back are boundless—who is this if not Lingyuan? This Chan Master dwells in the stage of ultimate realization."

The realm of original enlightenment (*prakṛtistha-gotra*): though it is said to manifest birth, in reality there is no birth to be manifested; though it is said to manifest extinction, in reality there is no extinction to be manifested.
It is luminous and profound, profoundly and secretly luminous. Since the true and the transformative do not shift, what hindrance is there to appearing and disappearing?

Therefore, the final words were made as instruction, and the true message was proclaimed for all to hear. The tasks of his life have reached their beginning and end, and this single period [of his ministry] is now concluded. Yet, I, [the author], in the past...
At the beginning of my travels this year, I encountered you in Longshu. We pledged a friendship based on a mere half-glance; our spirits were compatible and our bonds moved me deeply.

Though the jade may be hidden within the mountains of Jing, it has already met with one who possesses true discernment. Since then, we have been like oysters opening their shells to reveal pearls or voyagers finding their swords upon the boat.

Meeting again at Mount Ou, our long-cherished wishes harmonized even more perfectly. Our joy and sublime aspirations were as if joined by matching tally-strips. From that first meeting until now, three...
For ten years, our principles have been in accord and our styles shared; the sublime resonance has remained uninterrupted. Why must we part so suddenly? You have specifically sent this urgent letter;

my gratitude for your presence and my remembrance of your passing make these feelings all the more poignant. Nevertheless, such is the nature of things: the Buddhas are inconceivable, and none are permitted to dwell long in this world.
Let the great assembly reflect deeply: in the end, it is simply this. Thus, once Ziqi had passed away, Boya broke his strings.

The lute strings were snapped; it was likely because he lamented that there was no one who could truly understand his music. How much more so regarding this Ultimate Way, which transcends perception and surpasses emotion, flowing in perfect harmony with the mind—what words can express it?
Long ago, someone asked Changsha, "Where has Nanquan gone after his passing? Changsha replied:
When Shitou was a śrāmaṇera, he visited the Sixth Patriarch. [Later, someone] asked: "I am not asking about Shitou’s visit to the Sixth Patriarch when he was a śrāmaṇera;
where has Nanquan gone after his parinirvāṇa? The śrāmaṇera said: "I tell him to go and reflect upon it. The Master then laughed heartily and said: "Do you understand?
When the water rises, the boat floats higher; when the mud is deep, the Buddha is larger. Together they went before the altar.
No need for further observation or listening.
A letter from Master Fojian of Jiangshan has arrived; he ascends the hall and says: "Aha! Aha! Elder Brother, Elder Brother, you appeared before me;
you have departed ahead of me. Aha! Aha! Elder Brother, Elder Brother, you appeared before me; you have been permitted to drive side-by-side with me."

We stand shoulder to shoulder. You have departed ahead of me, leaving me with but a single wing to soar alone. How could I not think of these beings lost in the ocean of suffering who have not yet been delivered?

Moreover, scholars from the Five Lakes have come to this assembly, carrying their books upon their backs; how can they suddenly abandon their boats and oars when there is no one to ferry them across the vast river?
Yet, the principles of the Buddha-dharma possess their own causes and conditions. This is simply because sentient beings lack protection and their merit is meager.
Forever separated from the monastic community, the torch of the Dharma has no one to transmit it. I have heard that the Tathāgata manifested his parinirvāṇa at the Twin Śāla Trees;
I have also heard that Bodhidharma departed for the West with a single shoe. From Buddha to Buddha, from patriarch to patriarch, their Way has been continuous and far-reaching.

Moreover, my Dharma brother Fojian of Zhongshan possesses wondrous capacities, appearing and disappearing without interval to respond to conditions. As for his coming and going, his birth and death—what concern is that of mine? Yet, as for me, toward my teacher...

This gate is the most profound point of resonance. Within the ranks of the geese, we are as inseparable as brothers; our bonds of righteousness are as firm as metal and stone, and our spirit reaches the clouds and heavens.
Hearing these lingering tones, how could I bear it? Reflecting upon this decaying body, I realize it is not enduring. With a shared heart and mutual illumination, what more need be said?
I still clearly remember when the Tathāgata entered parinirvāṇa. Ānanda asked Kāśyapa, "What dharma did the World-Honored One transmit besides this golden robe?
Kāśyapa said, "Ānanda! Ānanda responded, "Yes. Kāśyapa said, "Throw down that banner pole in front of the gate! [The Master said:
"Great assembly, if you do not have this public case, birth and death will burn fiercely. Master Bāiyún said: "Gold..."
Beyond the outer skirt, what further transmission remains? That a younger brother responds to his elder brother’s call—how could this be by chance?
Turn over the banner-pole at the gate, lest it continue to lean against the wall as before. “Great assembly, do you understand? Leaning against the wall, leaning against the wall;
within the light of quiescent extinction, one pays homage to the white lotus.”
Chan Master Dahuì Gǎo received a letter from the late Master Tiāntóng Jué. Upon receiving the letter, he said:
"The ancients said, 'The final phrase at the end reaches the secure barrier; it blocks the vital ford, allowing neither ordinary person nor sage to pass. Holding up the letter, he said:
'This is the message of Master Tiāntóng’s final blocking of the vital ford and his total upholding of the Way. Do you understand?"
If you have not yet fully understood, I ask the *vinaya-dhara* (Venna) to explain it clearly for us. Having finished the proclamation, he ascended the seat and said:
"The Dharma banner has fallen; the Dharma beam has broken; the Dharma river has run dry; the Dharma eye has been extinguished. Even so, this is precisely Tiantong’s true teaching.
But tell me, what is the matter being taught? Once the one who knows the sound knows it, who else can know it?"
Chan Master Miman Jie received the posthumous letter from Master Mugwan. Holding up the incense, he said: "Venerable assembly, do you recognize this compassionate one?
Although we were born of the same lineage, we do not die of the same lineage. It has long been heard that he raised dust and winnowed soil throughout the Seven Min regions;
though his mastery of the ancestral wind was unsurpassed, today I joyfully behold the path of clarity and peace. Clear.
On the level path, having already seen the extraordinary, what ultimately was it? Tea is poured for three libations; incense is burned in a single burner.

We humbly pray that you still partake. The late Master Fohai of Lingyin’s final letter has arrived. At the mouth of the Valley of the Calling Monkeys, empty space splits asunder; even crows cannot fly across.
Whether walking or speaking, he struck the celestial bell of the Thirty-three Heavens. To forge a blade, one must rely on the smiths of Binzhou.
"Metal! He gave a shout and descended from his seat.
When Zen Master Yuansou Duan received the letter of late Master Yunwai of Tiantong, he ascended the hall and said: "I cite the case of Master Yungu Ying of Yunju.
At the time of his passing, he asked his attendant, 'What day is it today? The attendant replied, 'The third. Yunju said:"
After thirty years, he simply said, "It is just this," and then, sitting upright, he passed away into stillness. The Master said:
"Yunju attained the direct transmission of Cao-Dong and served as a model for the school of the lineage for a hundred generations.
Yet, why was his final total presentation such a failure? (He struck the whisk and said: Within the seamless stupa, clouds swirl; upon the sprout-less branch, the moon is full."
The letter from Chan Master Yuyan and the late Master Shishi of Yuyuan arrived; he entered the Patriarchs’ Hall and ascended the seat.
For fifty-three years, he played with cleverness until it turned to clumsiness; he trod through empty space and walked barefoot.
The myriad phenomena and the ten thousand forms laughed without ceasing. "O Great Assembly! This is the final phrase by which Master Shishi of Yuyuan benefited others," he said. It is clear.
Like the bright sun, as vast as the great void, both provisional and ultimate, illumination and function, are fully present; seizing and releasing, killing and enlivening, are all complete.
It can ferry the four modes of birth across, and serve as a bridge and vessel for the nine realms of existence. A mosquito attempting to bite an iron ox finds no place to insert its mouth.
(He plants his staff and says: "If you see it here, there is not a single place where you do not behold the compassionate countenance, nor a single moment when you do not..."
Listen to the preaching of the Dharma. If this has not yet occurred, shortly after descending from the seat, there shall be a communal recitation of the sutras to adorn the stages of practice;
at the place where the incense smoke rises, let everyone gaze upon it freely.
Upon receiving the letter from Master Changxi of Jinshan, Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun addressed the assembly: "The Great Dharma has become subtle;
it relies upon us to propagate it within this Sahā world. Though this illusory body has perished, we must continue to inspire and uplift others within the ocean of nirvana."
Linji said, "Do not extinguish my treasury of the true Dharma-eye. Da-jue said, "I must entrust you with a single arrow.
This was truly because his resolve to propagate the Dharma was so weighty and his compassion for sentient beings so profound that he spoke these words of descending into the weeds.
Do you all see where Jinnshan extends his hand? He capsizes the bottomless iron boat and returns once more to Dongshan’s waters.
Practice. A letter from Master Dugu of Lingyin arrived; he ascended the hall and said: "The spiritual mechanism is beyond expectation and does not involve coming or going.
Wondrous function is without fixed direction—how could it abide by rules? When Damei heard the sound of the flying squirrel, he buried his own self. Puhua..."
Wearing a straight-cut robe, he deceives and deludes others. How can he compare to our Master Lingyin, who, according to conditions, makes his arrangements without falling into the realm of merit?
For seventy-four years, he has outshone those before him and surpassed those after; it is enough to make Flying Eagle Peak dance and Cold Spring Pavilion leap.
Do you all see this old man’s marks of a great being even after his nirvana? His vast body lies stretched out across the three worlds.
Outside the realm, he strides alone with majestic dignity, a presence before the kalpas.
Upon the arrival of the letter from the late Master Guzhi of Donglin, he ascends the hall. Taking up the "hare-horn staff," he strikes out the very marrow of the Buddhas and Patriarchs;
grasping the "blow-sheathing sword," he sweeps away the tangles of the past and present. As he approaches the path of departure, who will hear this final word? It blazes forth!
It blazes through the void. Like Linji extinguishing the Eye of the True Dharma, San-sheng immediately took it up;
when Pan-shan addressed the assembly seeking the transmission of the truth, Pu-hua alone understood by performing a somersault.

Long-xiang pays his respects with such lamentation—among you, is there anyone who would beat their breast with their hand? (He strikes the whisk) and says: "Vast and empty are heaven and earth; there is no one to understand."
Hearing the lingering echoes, I let the empty strings snap.
The late letter from the Abbot of Mount Jing has arrived; he ascends the hall and says: "In the past, when the Patriarch Miaoxi arrived at Jiangshan, Master Ying’an ascended the hall and said:
'Among the venerable elders in the world who possess the great eye, there is only my Dharma-uncle alone. Now I...

Dharma Uncle Jingshan was a second incarnation of Miaoxi. Your humble nephew had previously heard from the Chaoqing that he was to be the founding patriarch of this monastery, yet his wish remained unfulfilled.
Now that these posthumous letters have suddenly arrived, it is as if one beholds the arrival of the Elephant Vehicle itself.

His majestic and upright form appears as if a golden staff were held across his shoulders; his resonant Dharma voice is heard like the ringing of a bell through the void. The fourfold assembly looks upon him with longing and attachment.
How unbearable this grief! Since birth and death are without interval, we cannot avoid the meeting of guest and host.
To transmit the family lineage, there is only this Vajra King; it is left as a standard for descendants.
Upon receiving the posthumous letter from Master Tánfāng of Lóngxiáng, Chan Master Chǔshí Qí ascended the hall and said:
"The mind is identical to the realm of empty space; it manifests dharmas equal to empty space. When one realizes empty space, there is neither 'is' nor 'is not.
Since there is neither this dharma nor that non-dharma, then all Buddhas attain equal and perfect enlightenment, turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma, and enter parinirvāṇa."
It is like a dream. The venerable Master Fohai Tánfāng repeatedly presided over famous monasteries and personally received imperial favor.
Just as he was taking his leave of Jìngwǔ, he immediately took charge of Lóngxiáng. At the end, the brilliance of his entire-body śarīra—eight *hú* and four *dǒu*—was not even considered much.
Let me pick up a single grain for everyone to see. (He raises his whisk and says: "The Sea God knows its value."
Its price is unknown; it remains among men, its light illuminating the night. [The Master] threw down his whisk.
Chan Master Liúyǎn Yù of Tiānníng in Xuānzhōu delivered a letter, which led to this address to the assembly: "The Iron Ox roars, shattering the moon over the Double Creek;
The Stone Woman holds her flute, her sorrow never ceasing. Hawk-eyes and Dragon-gazes both remain ignorant; The deaf man hears it personally, yet the mute speaks."
The Master said: "Twenty years ago, I personally saw Old Man Caoting at the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff pick up a broken length of rope.
Everywhere he went, he pierced the nostrils of the patriarchal masters of the world.

Now that he has appeared in response to conditions at Tianting to bring auspiciousness to the age—where water reaches the channel and wind bends the grass—he wishes once again to use this rope to pierce theirs."
The nostrils of all the monks in the world have been [familiarized]. Having completed his mission of transforming conditions, he has suddenly returned to the truth.
Casting off his hands there beyond, there is no trace whatsoever. Thus it is said: "Before sound, it is not sound; after form, it is not form.
A mosquito on an iron ox—there is no place for you to bite. Today, this mountain monk cannot help but issue this command in reverse. In a moment, he will descend from the seat and proceed to...
Burn a stick of incense and light a cup of tea before the sacred image. I wish to pass through his nostrils for him. Why?
Because when you take a punch, you must remember the moment the punch was struck.
Upon receiving the news of the passing of Master Xibai, he ascended the hall and said: "When one has not yet realized that objects are but the mind, all manner of discrimination arises.
Once one realizes that objects are but the mind, discrimination no longer arises. Within this state where nothing arises, one’s original face is revealed in its nakedness.
This is truly to be free from characteristics and names, absolute and beyond all relativity; it shatters the dust and pierces the target, penetrating both form and sound. Thus he spoke.

Master Baoguo attained this samādhi; dwelling in mountain retreats at two locations, he single-handedly transmitted the authentic seal, sweeping away erroneous interpretations and upholding this school.
Having completed his great task, he let go of his hands over there. In his final moments, he fully raised [the Dharma], manifesting a profound brilliance. Now tell me:
is this the same as or different from him [Baofu] pressing his chest against the assembly and displaying his crossed feet within the coffin? (He strikes the meditation seat.)
It is said: "The antelope hangs its horns atop a thousand peaks; yet there is another antelope upon the highest peak.
When the letter from Master Xianyan Zhongmou arrived, he ascended the hall. At the summit of Mount Ducha, he strikes the phoenix and nets the dragon;

by the waters of Huangchi, he spreads his shrimp net to catch the turtle. Having reached the point of returning home in embroidered robes, he employs a single flavor that cuts through nails and severs iron. It is like this:
Now the puppet strings have snapped; the five-colored auspicious qilin strides upon the celestial shore. What harm is there in having companions?
Why not return once more to settle the old public case of the former master? But how is that public case of the former master to be settled? [He] plants his staff and lets out a shout.
Master Hongjue Men, the Abbot of Tiantong, while observing the seventh-day memorial rites, again received the news of the passing of Chan Masters Xiancheng Ermu and Bianshan Jiumo.
The Master established an altar for the spirits and offered this memorial: "The west wind rises from the level ground, Blowing down the Hall of the Empty King.
There are also banners of the Good Dharma, Tumbling one after another into ruin. The life of wisdom hangs but by a thread; Heaven and humanity..."
How can one harbor lingering attachments? Reflect upon this with meticulous care. Nothing compares to the ease of a monk: the mud ox at the bottom of the sea has long since left no trace;
there is no need for straw sandals to travel through villages and counties. Do not lament that the world is so desolate;

you must believe that the imperial decree has formed a single expanse. O fine monk—do you realize it or not? If you have not yet reached the source here, burn a stick of incense and drink three cups of tea.
The offerings are set down; beating one’s breast, one can do nothing but cry out to the blue heavens. The Demon King claps his hands in unrestrained jubilation.

The letter of the Dharma-protector has arrived, providing the essential framework for the announcement of the passing of National Instructor Shi, Chan Master Mianjie. Upon receiving the news of the Master’s death, he ascended the hall. As the wind blows, the grass bends; as the water flows, the channel forms.
Accomplished. Trusting your feet, you come thus; clouds gather and mists roll away, and spring is everywhere. Trusting your feet, you go thus;
the sky is clear and the sea is tranquil, and things and self are as one. Therefore it is said: coming and going are not by means of form; movement and stillness are not by means of the mind.
In this way, majestic power is universally manifested in every atom and every land. Form and sound are transcended; not even a speck of dust can be established.
Enmeshed yet unwilling to dwell, called upon yet refusing to turn back. The ancient sages made no arrangements, and to this day there are no tracks left behind.
But tell me, where is Master Shi, the Censor, right now? After a long silence, he said: "The yellow beam has just ended the dream. ZHU.
A flower blooms in the kingdom. He further spoke in verse: "In years past we met and discussed the ultimate truth; Today, ascending the hall, we speak of coming and going.
In a single thought, all is vast and open, without front or back; On the iron tree, the spring blossoms bloom of their own accord."
Request for the Head of the West Hall to Announce the Outline (for both Orders).
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun was requested by the West Order to ascend the hall. Within the Tathāgatagarbha, not a single dharma is retained;
how could there be many variations within the gate of the patch-robed monks? Master Lingshu said: "My head seat has been born! My head seat acts!"
It is also the foot. Not a single stroke is applied to this one character. Do you understand? Have you not heard it said: "When guests arrive, there is no tea; mugwort soup prepares the ritual"?
Master Yuejiang Yin invited the head officers to the hall. "Excellent!"—three strikes of the board—and all the kalyāṇamitras come to study.
Since you already know the proper timing well, I shall not repeat myself three times. When the ancients spoke thus, it was very much like pressing a cow’s head down to make it eat grass.
Yunfeng, however, does not do so. How excellent! When the board strikes three times, he draws up his feet and ascends the meditation seat.
With a backbone forged of cast iron, he passes through the Patriarch’s barrier; in a single breath, he turns the entire Great Canon, and with his back turned, he sweeps away Mount Sumeru.
Mountains. In the seven locations where the mind was sought, no mind could be found; in the eightfold analysis of seeing, no seeing could be returned.
Entering the celestial palace in a dream, one has not yet awakened; the golden rooster flies atop the jade balustrade.
Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun invited the Head Monks to ascend the hall. Illuminating the present and shining upon the past, the True Eye of Mahesvara is clearly revealed.

Forging the sages and melting the commoners, the upward-pointing tongs and hammer are subtle and profound. To determine the phrases that constitute the fundamental principles of Buddhas and Patriarchs, one must be such a person;
to deploy the mechanism of the mutual interchange between host and guest, one must seek a true adept. Thus it is said: "To build a great mansion requires more than one man."
Wood can indeed form [a boat]. When crossing a vast river, how could it be saved by a single oar?

Only when illumination and function occur simultaneously—like shooting stars and rolling lightning, where both the person and the environment are stripped away, and the resonance of jade and metal is heard—can it be so. At such a time, everyone’s nostrils are in this old monk’s hands.
But tell me, where are this old monk’s own nostrils? He throws down his whisk and says: "Drag them along as you please."
[The assembly] was drawn forward.

The two Hall Heads were requested to invite Chan Master Zhenjing Wen to serve as the Head Seat, the Rector, and the Director of the Hall for the morning session. Three virtues and six flavors are offered to the Buddha.

And as for the Sangha: in the Fragrant Accumulation Kitchen, skillful seasoning is held in hand; the Buddhas of the three periods of time respond to one another with every strike upon the sounding block.
But tell me, what is it that they correspond with? After a long silence, he said: "Go ask the First Seat in the Hall."
I invite the Head Seat, the Steward, and Venerable Xiaoyao to ascend the hall. Without moving from the true limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), one establishes a locus for all phenomena.
Yesterday was the name of the Chief Administrator; today is the title of the Head Seat. Conditions respond in a hundred thousand ways; in every established place, there is wondrousness.
The steward grasps the handle of the ladle, arranging everything according to the occasion. If the multitude’s mouths can be harmonized, then they share in the state of Xiaoyao.
A single path. The locus upon which all dharmas are established has now been revealed. How can one explain the principle of "not moving from the true limit"?
[He lets out a shout and descends from his seat.]
Please ascend the hall, Head Seat. One part is new; one part is old. The new and the old must support one another to achieve fulfillment.
All you practitioners of Zen, tell me: what is it that is achieved? Is it the achievement of Buddhist affairs? The achievement of the site of practice? Or the achievement of the monastic community?
If it were achieved in such a manner, how could there be a "separate transmission outside the teachings"? [The Master] then took up his staff and said:
"Is this within the teachings or outside the teachings? Is it new or old? It cannot be called a staff; it would be best to simply take hold of it.
Having said this, he threw it down and left the seat.
Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin requested that the Head Seat ascend the hall. [The Master said:

"It harmonizes the thousand differences, encompasses the ten thousand existences, aligns the comings and goings, seals the past and present, merges existence and non-existence, and unifies life and death. It issues commands that cannot be transgressed and carries out teachings that need no words.
It equalizes the unequal and levels the uneven. Herein is established; herein is clarified; herein lies the governing framework; herein is the leadership."
What dharma cannot be accommodated? What matter cannot be accomplished? What virtue is not perfected? What mind is not in accord?
Furthermore, regarding the phrase "the wind blows and the grass bends," how do you speak it? To build a mountain, one climbs nine *ren*; to hold soil, one must fix a thousand *jin*.
Chan Master Yuansou Duan invited the Head Seat to ascend the hall. There are clouds and billows reaching the heavens, capable of accommodating fish that swallow ships;
there is a wind spanning ninety thousand *li*, capable of bearing wings that touch the sky. Thus one erects the banner of the Dharma and establishes the fundamental tenets.
"If it were not for the right person, how could they be entrusted with such a matter? Striking the meditation seat, he said: "When there is spirit, one adds to that spirit;
where there is no elegance, there is elegance nonetheless."
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun invited the Head Seat to ascend the hall. He opened up the eyes and the mind’s eye of humanity, restoring the majestic standards of antiquity.
Seated, he cut off the dust of emotions and conceptual thoughts, falling neither into the subtle nor the mysterious mechanisms of the mind.
With renewed sun and moon and a distinct heaven and earth, such a person alone is capable of undertaking such a task—just as Lingshu left the first seat vacant to await Yunmen.
It is for this reason. [The Master] pats the meditation seat: "Do not take offense at his lofty spirit; his house has already trodden upon the highest barrier.
On the request of Chan Master Yuyan Ji, Changguo Jixiang invited Yuan Chongshouzuo to ascend the hall and preach. Linji—
In establishing the Huangbo school’s fundamental tenets, Puhua exerted his full strength to bring them to completion without cause. Yangshan said, "This man has a head but no tail;
he has a beginning but no end. In years past, when I was serving in my temporary capacity at Haishan, you, Master Yuan, laid down your body to assist me.

Now that I am fulfilling my duties at Dang Temple, I am again indebted to you for sharing the seat to preach the Dharma. Yet, you do not seem like the Yangshan who said, "This man has a head but no tail."

For a person to have a head but no tail is to have a beginning but no end. Observe the Buddhas and Patriarchs with discernment: each appeared in the world to guide and transform beings according to their circumstances;
there were none who did not fully embody both guest and host, or fully embody both host and guest. Their great functions were manifested in unison, and their great capacities responded universally.
Circulate the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye and manifest the wondrous mind of Nirvana; directly attain the state where clouds move and rain falls, and water reaches the channel of its own accord.
It is only those of transcendent capacity who can undertake tasks of transcendent magnitude. (He plants his staff upright and says:
"When the dragon finds water, his spirit is enhanced; when the tiger encounters mountain scenery, his fierce majesty grows."
Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun requested the Head Seat to preside over the assembly and express gratitude to the two elders, Jixiang and Chongjiao, as they ascended the hall.
To cleave apart Mount Tai and Mount Hua is for the Great Spirit to vainly display his prowess; to pierce the willow leaves at a hundred paces is for Yi You to still fall short of hitting the mark.
Therefore, he succeeded Yunmen and inherited Xuefeng; he directed Linji to study under Huangbo. In Muzhou’s eyes, there was nothing...
With sinews, he pulls the rake and drags the plow to farm for his food. Yangqi lacked strength in his wrists; Longxiang, in his ordinary dealings, did not dare to employ people lightly.
Yet when it came time to act, one man was equal to a hundred. He was like Emperor Gaozu of Han, who was not skilled at leading soldiers himself but was skilled at leading generals.
This was not merely to establish the regulations of the monastic community, but to serve as a model for future generations. Furthermore, there is a difficult younger brother.

The difficult elder brother comes and goes, responding and chanting in turn; it does not hinder striking the phoenix or weaving the dragon. Three thousand fathoms of spider-silk from a tortoise’s hair form a net.

On the occasion of the First Seat ascending the hall at the request of Chan Master Muchun: the sun is at its southernmost point as the winter solstice arrives; the season reaches the "cloud-writing" [marking of the calendar]. The Will of Heaven...

I saw him again. Supporting the Yang (the vital principle) and suppressing the Yin (the passive), with a purple silk cloth bound around his forehead and an embroidered skirt at his waist, he possessed a most distinguished bearing.

His bright red cotton skirt had not been replaced for some time. Since his household has no goods that stagnate and does not hoard them, he knows that to smelt gold and carve jade, one must rely on the hammer and tongs of active practice.
To uphold the Teaching and support the Dharma-lineage depends entirely upon brothers of the same essence. May you brandish the Buddha-sun even as it sets in the west. Return...
"The turbulent waves have already collapsed; is this not the time when the Way of the gentleman flourishes and the Way of the petty man wanes?

The middle can both kill people and bring people to life. To kill people, one must have the sword that kills;

Yin asked further, "Who knows? The Master replied, "He who knows it knows; after him, who else would know?
Yin pressed, "In that case, the water flows cold from the side of the rock, and the wind comes fragrant from within the flowers. The Master replied, "Idle talk. Yin asked, "What is Deshan’s staff?

The Master replied, “Do you hear it now? The student advanced and said, “I recall that in the past, when Master Linji addressed the assembly, he said:

The respondent said, "One must take care not to wound the blade or injure the hand. The questioner asked, "What is one shout that is like a crouching lion?"
The Master replied, "Truly, how pitiable. The student asked, "How is it that one shout serves as a 'probing rod' and 'shadow-grass'?

The Master replied, "One must not be in front or behind. The student asked, "How is it that one shout does not function as a shout? The Master replied, "You must investigate this before you can understand.

*Thump.* The Diamond Precious Sword. *Thump.* The Lion Crouching on the Ground. *Thump.* The Probing Pole and Shadow-Grass.

To flourish the Śākya lineage and inherit the family tradition, one must carefully examine the original school: what is its defining character?
Have you not seen how Linji struck Huangbo three times, receiving sixty blows of the staff each time as if they were like the branches of Mount Song being brushed aside?
And have you not seen how Deshan attained sudden enlightenment at Longtan when the paper candle was blown out? When the Way exhausts all profound sophistry, it is as if—
To place a single hair in the vast void, or to exhaust the pivotal mechanisms of the world, is like casting a single drop into a great abyss.

These two great elders may truly be said to have exhausted the very marrow of a thousand sages and penetrated the source of all dharmas; they caused their fragrance to flow through future generations and established enduring models for the monastic communities.
Those who study the Way today must likewise possess a measure of the "sinews of the eye" to see through them.
It is only at the point where the ancients failed that one may truly begin.

If you can see through this, you will realize that although Huangbo and Longtan were like the golden-winged bird cleaving the sea to seize and swallow the dragon, they nonetheless could not avoid acting as a physician treating a dead horse.

To claim the title of a patriarch for a hundred generations is not yet possible. Within the gate of this Dharma hall, we do not speak of whether one has "seen through" or not;

Now that we have gathered here for a brief moment, I, Venerable Qin, cannot help but borrow the majestic radiance of the Elder in the Hall to overturn the seas and mountains and smash the Great Void.

Regarding the stage of the feet: either one's practice becomes intermittent and fails to achieve continuity; or, having experienced some degree of joy, one ceases to apply further effort to seek authentic awakening;

This requires nothing more than keen faculties and superior wisdom—to strike and immediately turn, to seize and immediately act. Only then will you be able to be one with the old fellow Zhaozhou.

The single eye and the single mind are identical in their function; they encompass the essentials of ten thousand variations and a thousand differences, opening the gates of those very thousands of differences and ten thousand variations.

They are entirely guest and entirely host, entirely essence and entirely function, entirely releasing and entirely gathering, entirely giving life and entirely taking it away—all of which does not lie outside of this.
