With an iron spine, he sits upright upon the long couch with his meditation cushions thickly spread, making his three hundred and sixty bones and eighty-four thousand pores into a single "Mu" (無).

To hold it firmly and keep it bound; furthermore, one must not listen to what others say.

It suffices to experience and examine it within the hearing of sounds and the seeing of forms, and to take responsibility for it in every bowing and rising, every movement and gesture. To speak is to hit upon it; to take a step is to tread upon it.
At the gates of the six sense organs, a single ray of divine light never ceases day or night. This is called the fundamental karma of birth and death.
This mass of ignorance must be swiftly severed into three pieces. Furthermore, do not listen to what others say: that all phenomena are established from the root of non-abiding;
that fundamentally there have never been mountains, rivers, the great earth, light, darkness, form, or emptiness;

If one merely twists and fashions it bit by bit, measures and weighs it bit by bit, and discriminates it bit by bit—attempting to fathom the inconceivable, great, perfect circle of the Tathāgata’s ocean of enlightenment with the conceptual mind—it is like trying to burn Mount Sumeru with a firefly; it will ultimately never succeed.
It is so. Even if you were to stuff your belly full of leftover soup and rancid rice, would there still be even a single bit of it that could be put to use?
Could you possibly deceive everyone else? Even if you could deceive others, could you possibly deceive yourself?
Even if you could deceive yourself, could you possibly deceive the lanterns and the pillars? Since you cannot deceive them—
One cannot avoid being laughed at from a cold place by the myriad phenomena of the universe.
Take, for instance, how Master Qin tonight exhausts his mouth and tongue with such idle chatter, speaking of sevens and eights; tell me, can he even escape this one laugh?
If you say it cannot be produced, you have not yet escaped being counted among the ninety-six types of heterodox paths in India.
If you say it can be produced, alas, there are bystanders watching. Tell me, where is this bystander’s eye? It is late at night; we have stood for a long time.
I pray you, take care of yourself.

After entering the room for formal instruction, [the Master] gave a general discourse on Chan Master Xueyan Qin’s discourse following his entry into the room. "Brothers, gather here for a short while;
I shall twist your nostrils and split open the great void for you. Although this is like gouging a sore from good flesh, it must be done.
In the end, the blade is iron. Do you yet know that within a single phrase there are three mysteries (*xuan*), and within a single mystery there are three essentials (*yao*)?

Furthermore, do you yet know that within the guest there is the host, and within the host there is the guest; that sometimes the guest is entirely the host, and sometimes the host is entirely the guest?
Moreover, do you yet know that within killing there is life, and within life there is killing; that sometimes it is entirely killing?
Is it that when life is preserved, one preserves it entirely, and when there is killing, one kills? Furthermore, do you yet know that opening the mouth does not reside upon the tongue?
Moreover, do you yet know that one hand lifts while the other hand presses down? If you cannot discern this clearly, you will not distinguish between the black and the white;

you will not escape the state of merely saying "it is right" when others say it is right, and "it is wrong" when others say it is wrong. This is precisely what is called "a short man looking at a banner."
Playing about, one follows others up and down. How could one have known that within the blue cloth curtain there was originally someone?
As for this talk, do not say that those who have not yet cleared their ground cannot grope for it;

even among those ten or five out of ten practitioners of the Way who wear blue cloth robes, most simply swallow the dates whole. Do not speak of using the conscious intellect to calculate or measure with mouth and ear.
Those who follow conventional practices merely give rise to interpretations based on words and engage in forced, pedantic analysis of every phrase;

they must know that this is a sublime excellence beyond categories and free from the dust of the mundane, which cannot be reached through deliberation or conjecture, nor does it involve seeing, hearing, sensing, or knowing.

Furthermore, they must know that everyone is fully endowed with it and each individual is perfectly accomplished; it is only because for immeasurable kalpas one has been tossed about by birth and death that [this truth] has not been realized.
This clarifies that the karmic consciousness is shrouded and obscured, such that [the Way] cannot manifest before one nor be utilized.

Now, if you wish to turn this over once and for all prior to King Vaibhūṣaṇa, you must believe that this single point of the Path is truly a thing originally possessed by yourself, and that it is certainly not obtained from another.
Only then, exhausting the body born of your parents and the heavens and earth...
Take the vital energy you have received and, with a single breath, blow it into a sharp, keen sword.
Cut your own solitary life-force into two pieces and cast them down over a precipice ten thousand fathoms high.

Only when all phenomena, from the myriad forms of the universe to the very ground, have utterly subsided into stillness, can it be called "attaining the headship of mind-emptiness" and "the radiance of the ocean-seal samādhi. If one deviates from this—even if one were to engage in intensive investigation—[it will not suffice].
I have filled my belly and sewn together a cloth bag; on the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, I shall inevitably find myself flustered and frantic like a crab falling into boiling water.
When I was under the guidance of Wuzhun and Chijue, there was a friend who frequently offered a word or two that has become a classic among people;
he also exhausted himself in the ancients' methods of indirect striking and hidden blows.
He understood the point of arrival, yet he simply had never performed his own practice upon the meditation cushion (*bōtuán*).

Later, while serving as a library director (*zàngzhǔ*) in various regions, his temperament was haughty and his conduct superior to his peers. One day, due to involvement in several frivolous legal disputes, the case was not resolved and he was defeated by others.
Consequently, he became consumed with resentment and vomited blood, leading to an illness that could not be saved. At the time of his death—
At that time, he had undergone thousands of births and ten thousands of sufferings, yet though he sought death, he could not find it.

Whenever he saw a friend come to inquire after his illness, he would say, "I have practiced Chan my entire life, yet I have never performed any work upon a meditation cushion. I do not believe there is a gate of awakening;

I request a long cord; with a single lift, he strides beyond the clouds of the nine heavens. In a casual step, he topples the City of the Dharma King. The novice shaves his head;

He addressed him, saying, "Welcome. O benevolent one, for what purpose have you come? He replied, "Does the Master not recognize me?
The Master said, "I regard Buddhas and sentient beings as equal; I view them all as one—how could I make distinctions?

The deity said, "This principle is profound and obscure to my ears. I merely sought the Master’s precepts so that I might become your disciple."

The Way. To pass through it means that although one has been fully sustained and has not yet died, once one has reached the head, one must seek an exit.

If one cannot find the exit, then in the end one dies and has never truly lived. Therefore it is said: "It is easy to emerge from within the gate; it is difficult for the body to depart from within itself.
If one is a man without private interests beneath one's feet, then when the red thread is severed, the ten landscapes vanish; the divine colt crosses the South Sea. Five.
The auspicious qilin strides upon the celestial shore;

the venerable Zhi Xiu Jing has risen from his funerary niche. Having spent many years composing his verse, he now returns to his native village. Fearing that his song before others might be empty and hollow, he lets out blood-stained cries through the night like the soul of a cuckoo.
His longing for home cannot be restrained as it mounts the brow’s peak. Spring has departed; the green— (Note: The final character "綠" [lǜ] appears to be a fragment or an incomplete line.)
A profusion of blossoms fills the thickets; along the road, after wind and rain, where can horse hooves avoid the remaining petals?

For the purpose of raising the coffin of Chan Master Rong of Nan-yuan in Baoqing: Springtime has no feet yet it traverses Jambudvīpa; the songs of birds and the fragrance of flowers pervade the entire world.
How could the lush grasses fail to bewilder one on the ancient shore? The golden rope is severed at the head of the iron ox. Forget the pipes.
Carrying it with you, severing all confinement; taking leisurely steps south toward heaven and north across the earth, what place could possibly lack elegance?
For the sake of Master Yunzhang Yunchan, the coffin is raised: upon the waters of East Mountain he travels without ceasing; amidst the flames, the wooden horse gallops through the pure wind.
Because the nose-ring was severed, the golden tether snaps; the eight-cornered millstone rolls freely through the void.
Chan Master Tianru Ze prepared a medicinal broth for Elder Cong. To remove the dull and promote the bright, he offered this bitter-tasting, excellent medicine.

Yet Zen monks have an ailment deep in the *gao-huang* (the vital organs), where it is locked at the throat so they cannot swallow it down. Elder Cong, you now forget both the medicine and the illness;
feel free to swallow it or spit it out as you please.
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun prepared bone-tea for Secretary Man. Man had his belly full of literary compositions, yet he carried a wooden board across his entire body.
When it came time to be pressed and probed, however, his skin was pierced through and his bones were laid bare.

Had Nan Biadou not been subjected to the bitter, lethal hand of Ciming, he would have inevitably been drowned in the stagnant waters of Lestam. He was a man standing at a painted pavilion where wine is sold.
"Come together to drink Zhaozhou’s tea.

Regarding the carrying of the staff and holding the torch for a deceased monk (*qingui* states: "For Buddhist services such as locking and opening the coffin, the *vinaya-master* (*weina*) consults with the *first seat* (*shouzuo*).

These may be performed by inviting a senior official (*tou-shou*) according to seniority. However, for the specific act of holding the torch, one must invite the Abbot to preside over the service. Nowadays, various quarters also appoint senior officials for this; I fear this is not the ancient Way.)
Chan Master Wuxiang addressed the assembly: "Does the great assembly know the origins of the Junior Rector Jing?
His parents gave him birth on the banks of the Yanling Rapids; he changed his robes atop White Reed Peak and arrived here. Yet, he has missed the jewel atop the Tathāgata’s head."
With a belly full of wind and thunder, he sought to inherit the patriarch’s estate; his wings brushed the clouds and heavens, yet he escaped from both ends only to achieve nothing at all.
Returning home burdened by illness, it was known beforehand that he would not survive. Today, Old Lushan extends a hand for him, causing him to realize his true home directly beneath:
with his body hidden within a flame, he passes through the thorn-brake with a mere snap of the fingers; in a fleeting turn of the head—
Riding backward upon the bell tower, one enters the Buddha hall. I ask the great assembly: at such a time as this, is there still anyone who acts with both illumination and function simultaneously?
The single path of Nirvāṇa is neither arising nor ceasing; look directly at the ice-flower within the fire.
Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin performed the cremation for a deceased monk: Atop the mountain of the five aggregates lies the path to nirvana;
In the four directions and eight corners, there is no barrier. The entire body is entirely adamantine eyes; A single grain of numinous elixir burns within the flames.
Chan Master Dahui Zonggao said to the rector Yan: "This venerable elder has realized that the nature of the five aggregates is empty and awakened to the selflessness of all phenomena.
As soon as he perceived that the four elements were in discord, he knew it was the ripening of his past causes.
Two or three days prior, he bathed and shaved his head, personally wrote his final testament, and asked me for a handful of fire, showing no concern for what lay behind him."
A divine light spanning ten thousand *li*—how could it begrudge the golden lock at the mysterious gate before one's eyes?
This mass of ignorance, karma, and deluded consciousness—I shall examine each and every part from the very beginning. How many monks who have thus settled their affairs can there be in this world?
Since the Venerable Yanwei has spoken thus, there is yet one more matter that must be disclosed: if you travel to visit Tiantai and Yandang, convey my words to Mount Song.

Pozhuo said, "For the sake of the Dharma-lamp’s *jian-si* (supervisor of the kitchen), I shall use fire. Holding up a torch, he pointed toward the shrine and said, "This is the Dharma-lamp that has already been extinguished.
He then raised the torch again and said, "This is the fire of untainted wisdom (*anāsrava-jñāna*). The fire of untainted wisdom kindles the Dharma."

A lamp: it may be lit, or it may be extinguished; there is nothing that cannot be. Does Attendant Lamp know? After the ashes fly and the smoke vanishes, a single udumbara flower shall serve as fuel for Attendant Chan’s fire.
Everyone possesses the four great elements, but Attendant Chan alone possesses five: earth, water, fire, [wind, and]... [the fifth].
As a supplement to the preceding discourse on wind, there is yet another instance of the magnitude of a hat. Within this hat, it is empty inside, empty outside, and empty both inside and out.

It encompasses the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm; even the vast Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains, the rivers, and the great oceans, as well as the myriad phenomena of the universe, are all contained within it without any crowding or constraint.
Now that the four elements have fallen into disorder, only the magnitude of this hat remains.
The Town Headman is here; his hat is large and very strange. Chanting once, twice, three times—whether at a high price or a low price, he will not sell.
After all, what is it? He strikes and enters the *samādhi* of fire-light together with Master Chong.
I perform the cremation for one who has transcended dhyāna. On the mountain below, the wheat is golden and the silkworms have ceased their work; a procession of the dead escorts a living man.
This living man’s body is like an adamantine vajra; now he enters once more the red furnace to be smelted.
Chan Master Ying’an Hua performed the cremation for the Secretary Nan; at Donghu, Guangling, and Guizong, a brilliant radiance soared from the forge.
Iron eyes and copper pupils could not withstand the smelting; the very core of the patch-robed monk is well worth circulating.
When Chan Master Tianmu Li was at Nanchan, he held up a torch at the gatehouse during a rainstorm and pointed out the way:
"North, south, east, west—Alas, you fellow Meng Babang! You go right ahead like that. It is not that going is not possible;
however, suppose there are yakṣas and rākṣasas ahead, a turbulent sea and a precipice behind, and a fire pit that traps people in between. When you arrive here—
Furthermore, how is it? A torrential rain pours down as one steps out the door.
When Chan Master Yuansou Duan served as the rector (dīnà) for Ding, under a single stroke of the mallet, his true eye was opened wide.
For kalpas as vast as grains of dust, this has been the gate of great tranquil concentration. Looking left and right, he said: "Last night, where did a fire break out that burned this forth?"

The ancient tomb serves as the funeral pyre for this senior monk. If this illusory body were not subject to the six sense objects, it would be impossible for a cricket in the fire to swallow up the mountains, rivers, and the great earth. Now, where does this illusory body reside?
"Light the fire for the Elder on the road. The Way is neither within nor without. The great ocean does not harbor a corpse;
a fierce flame does not tolerate a mosquito. Having said this, he threw down the fire.
He is the fire of the foremost elder; a *nāga* in great meditative concentration. Motion and stillness are eternally true; birth-and-death and coming-and-going are like a playful sport.
He turns his body upon the edge of a sword and gallops his horse through the midst of flames.
He performed the cremation for Head Seat Xuán. He had shattered the steep and lofty, and melted away the profound and subtle. Within the Tuṣita Heaven, there was no longer any dream or thought;
upon the road of weary existence, he forever ceased his galloping. A fire-tortoise with horns upon its head turns over and topples the five Sumeru mountains.

"You are the one who swims in the fire of wealth; you are the one who divides pounds and ounces upon the scales. You are the one who arranges thousands horizontally and hundreds vertically along the abacus.
Now tell me: as you swim and play within the sea of birth and death, are you yourself or are you not? [The Master] threw down the firebrand and said:
'Within this mass of blazing flames, recognize it clearly!'"
Chan Master Gaofeng Miao performed the cremation for the Elder Ruoqiong. Holding up a torch, he said:
"If you can realize it here, a single blade of grass is a jade palace; otherwise, a jade palace is but a single blade of grass."
He cast down a cloud of fire. He raised his eyebrows and said, "Look within the fire!
Ming Shan, the Manager of the Fire Department, drew a circle with fire and said: "If you can see it here, then you will see that the mountain is the mountain and the water is the water.
A spark flies from the bottom of the great ocean; waves rise upon the peak of Tianmu. Otherwise, he cast [the fire] away.
The Lower Fire said: "Before every door is a torch. The Elder Fata is fire;
your name is Gautama, and the Buddha’s name is Fata. I have pointed this out clearly for you;
if you have doubts, seek another teacher. He threw down the fire and said: "A fire burns within a cave in the midst of the great ocean."
Chan Master Zhongfeng Ben was the *zhisui* (head of the work-staff) for Maoshi. In other quarters, the *zhisui* hands the torch to the abbot;
today, the abbot hands the torch to the *zhisui*. Tell me, what matter does this clarify?
Tomorrow the *udumbara* flower will bloom in full splendor, and Prince Siddhārtha will be born in the palace of King Śuddhodana. One must take up the responsibility from right here. A thousand...
Ancient and eternal, *alala*. Mastering the abbot’s quarters is the fire;
returning to the source is the single flavor of Chan. Yangqi’s three-legged donkey—two layers of public cases, one phrase that shatters them all.
But tell me, which is that one phrase? Throwing down a torch, he says: “A brazier of fire amidst a heap of winter snow.”
The Master of the Circular Bath takes up a torch and draws a circle in the air, saying: "Does the Master of the Circular Bath see it? To call it a 'circle' is to turn one's back on it;
not to call it a 'circle' is to commit a transgression. To pass through these two barriers is to return to one’s own kin.
The Lotus Peak thrusts forth the pestle-tipped flower; the handle of the ladle overturns the lion’s paws. The fragrant waters, deep and profound, are dried to the very bottom."
The entire assembly is called upon to strain their eyes in unison; tell me, what are they looking at? Throwing down a torch, he says:
"A shell-shedding divine tortoise soars into the heavens; the formless true person bathes in the fire."
The Auspicious Firewood Head. Holding up a torch, he says: "Does the Auspicious Firewood Head see it? Ten thousand auspicious clouds drift across the earth;
the branches and leaves of the forest are carried on one shoulder. Today the two ends of the carrying pole break—cut for a thousand days, burned in a single day."
Chan Master Wuyong Kuan served as the director of the ordination platform and presided over the cremation. The four great elements are fundamentally empty; there is no obstruction whatsoever.
Turning the body within the flames, one stroke wins both prizes.

The record mentions the temple master’s fire. Since it has already been recorded, there is no need for further use. A handless man strikes down empty space, startling Mount Sumeru until it topples upside down.
Throwing out the fire, he says: "Right within this mass of fierce flames, let go of tortoise hair and rabbit horns. *He lets out a shout.*
The ancient Chan Master Meiyu served as the head of the administrative staff (karmadāna). When Xinghua struck Kebin that year, Yangshan held the torch—there was no partiality toward kin or stranger.
Having traveled extensively to study under various masters, his practice was earnest; he cast off his hands and went forth, for his eyes possessed the vital sinew.
Whether remaining in this very body or departing from it, a rocket flies upon the terrace of nirvana; let the falling leaves return to their roots as they may.
Chan Master Tianru Ze yielded the position of Rear Hall Head to another, yet preached the Dharma in the Tuṣita Palace;

he yielded the position of First Seat to another, yet turned his body toward the shore of Nirvāṇa. He seized the primary pivot, transcended the four propositions, and cut off the hundred negations; amidst the fierce flames, he alone further manifested his brilliance.
The *weina* takes up a torch and draws a circle in the air, saying: "Yunfeng broke the barrel hoops; it was somewhat like this.
He then strikes with the torch, saying: "A single blow and it shatters into a hundred pieces. Tell me, what is this? The nature of fire is true emptiness;
the nature of emptiness is true fire.
The Head Seat Purifies the Fire: The pure and wondrous Dharma-body is fundamentally without appearing or disappearing. Pointing to the funeral bier with his hand, he said:
"As for this—neither mind, nor Buddha, nor thing—it is the 'True Person of No Rank' (muga jinjin) given a provisional name.
He is called the model for the monastic community. Even when the kalpa-ending fires blaze forth, they cannot burn him."
The Abbot of Yan was strict with fire; the family tradition of Tiantong was not so strict. The Abbot of Yan had two oil lamps;
the Administrator of Nanshan obtained the right person, remaining steadfastly single-minded throughout his life. Do you wish to see where the Abbot of Yan was single-minded?
On a piece of dead wood, the fire glows bright red, manifesting the three eyes of Maheśvara.
Praising the Head Seat: A sword hangs from his brow; he is one who should be reviled, not praised. Cutting off the cat:
he is one who should be praised, not reviled. Suddenly, praise and revilement proceed together—what principle is this ultimately? Fire burns the Persian’s beak in the South Sea.
The fire at the Abbot’s Quarters of Rui. A single stroke that illuminates heaven and reflects the earth; oil leaks from the bottom of the cup and cannot be contained.
Sparks fly upon the eyebrows and eyelashes, shattering both nirvana and birth-and-death. Holding up the torch, he said: "Do you all see?"
"I have seen the Lamp-Light Buddha; the original radiance and auspicious signs were just like this.
Neng the Elder said, "This fire has dragged a corpse here; its nostrils do not meet its mouth. Both subject and object are utterly gone.
A shrimp cannot leap out of a measuring bucket. He threw down a torch and said, "Now it has leaped out! Fire burning beneath the water, scorching the void."
"Empty! The entire forest roars like lions.
As for Elder Long, fire does not conceal a dragon; dead water cannot hide a dragon. Have you understood yet? If you have understood, try entering the fire-light samādhi."
Chan Master Yuguan Ji was serving as the Chief Administrator (Dusi) of the Lamp Hall when a fire broke out. Holding up a torch, he said:
"The leaking lamp-cup illuminates the dark alleys of birth and death throughout kalpas. The entire world of the ten directions is this very gate of Great Nirvana.
Looking to his left and right, he said: "Where did the fire come from last night? It has burned out the graves of the ancients."
To purify the Lord of the Hall’s fire: upon the lapis lazuli hall, thorns reach the heavens; at the head of the Gate of Victory, a pure breeze sweeps the earth.
Casting forth the fire, he says: "This dilapidated house has no one to repair it; on the head of the Fire Official rides a wind-chariot."

For the sake of his successor, he performed the cremation for Master Zang; his lineage was about to inherit that of Huqiu Long. With the treasury of teachings overturned, his spirit soared like a rainbow.
For twenty-seven years, his entire reality was fully manifested; the Southern Mountain burned charcoal while the Northern Mountain glowed red.
To supervise the lighting of the fire for the vehicle: throughout the lands of the ten directions, there is only the Single Vehicle Dharma (*ekayāna*).
When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the worlds are all destroyed, only the vajra-circle remains unharmed. Is it not this very Dharma?
Holding up a torch, he said: "If you can speak, it is merely adding grass to the flames."
Acting as the master of the auspicious bath for the fire, he made the essence of the firm Dharma-body drip down in thick drops; neither fire could burn it nor water could wash it away.
Throwing the fire, he said: "I have seen the lamp-light Buddha; its original radiant auspiciousness was like this."
Record of the Essential Teachings of the Patriarchs,
Volume Thirty-Four and Volume Thirty-Five. Compiled by Xingyue of Loudong,
Abbot of Lian’an Chan Temple at the Eighteen Streams in Wulin.
The Abbot carries the torch for a deceased monk (raising the bones, cremating the bones, enshrining them in a stupa, and scattering the ashes).
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun performed the cremation for the Prior Nai. Urging him on during the evening discourse, he said, "This is the art of death.
Holding up the torch, he said: "When the flames reach Mount Kunlun, jade and stone are burned together; only true gold remains unrefined by the fire."
For the sake of receiving the fire of the monastery head, he received harsh blows of fists and kicks, yet was immediately able to transcend life and death.

The leaking oil lamp shook the earth as it emitted light; the diamond ring was not worth a single coin. Amidst a mass of blazing flames, he buried his fishing line and hook, and caught a carp one foot long.
The fire for the merit-distributing *karmadāna* was at the eastern edge of the City of Merit, no different from it is today.

You only exhausted your skillful means and extinguished your active delusions because you headed toward the spot where the wooden barrel hoop exploded. Holding up a torch, he said: "Light this fire and look:
how thick is your skin?"
When the fire for the abbot’s quarters was being prepared, Yangqi looked at Baiyun and burst into laughter. "This is very much like forcing a live snake to transform into a dragon;
it is entirely a path of death, neither of them a way of life. He cast down the fire and said, "I call this fire; you must not call it fire."

There is one who oversees the fire: he sets aside the leaking lamp and releases the originally inherent spiritual light, which pierces through the night of the dark alleys of birth and death throughout kalpas.
The moon does not wait for the wind to be cool; the sun does not wait for fire to be hot.
"Regarding the fire at the Abbot’s quarters: though you have left the dust of the world, you do not understand the ultimate meaning; this is because emotional attachments have not been severed.

Though you are advanced in years, you have not realized the emptiness of nature; this is because the great matter remains unresolved. Now that the four elements have already separated, you have not yet severed what was to be severed, nor have you realized what was to be realized.
Yangqi’s burden has been broken and burned as firewood; amidst the mass of blazing flames, snow flies crosswise."

Hail! Chan Master Wumen Can served as the master of the funeral pyre for Master Zhu. Before every household door were torches; when applied according to the occasion, there was nothing that could not be done.
Within the ocean of fragrant water, he shook the earth and emitted light, illuminating the very headway of birth and death all at once.
"Broken. Does someone still see it? Holding up a torch and drawing a circle, he said: "Be careful not to call this 'a single bright pearl.

Setting fire beneath the ginger root; working with all one's might at the plow and hoe. Without intention, the beard and hair are removed; as one grows old, the will becomes even firmer. *Sheng* (Birth).
Ginger does not lose its pungency. Suddenly the great earth is turned over by the plow. Once dead, one does not live again. Look, look!
Kaixian today shall bring you back to life! [He throws down a torch and says: A fire-snake comes crashing against the face; empty space is stripped bare to its very bottom.
Chan Master Da’ān Zhuang served as the master of the treasury of fire. Those who enter through the gate do not possess the family treasure.
The scriptures of the Three Vehicles all lack true meaning. To call it "fire" is to burn you to death; not to call it "fire" is to freeze you to death.
"Master Yizang presides over the fire. That which comes and goes with you is the treasury; that which does not come and go with you is also the treasury.

You must clarify the primary truth (paramārtha-satya). Be most careful not to fall under the sway of others' words. Holding a torch, he drew a circle in the air and said: "The moon is cool without waiting for the wind;
the sun is hot without waiting for the fire. He then cast the torch down.
The Abbot of the Medicine Hall sets fire [to the weeds]. Administering medicine according to the ailment, he settles the case based on the facts.

The diamond circle and the brambles—those who cannot penetrate them or swallow them are all dead men. A fierce tiger before the mountain chases the wildcat; a cricket in the flames swallows the snail’s nose.
Master Ji’s treasury of the fire overflows with eloquence like the Milky Way; his writings are strung together like pearls and gems. Yet, at the brink of birth and death, none of these are of use.
The entire Great Canon of Teachings is the character "left" (之); the Patriarch’s coming from the West is the character "right" (右). Holding up the fire, he said:
The eminent Hoten penetrated it thoroughly; the lad Bingding recited "Mahā.
When Chan Master Tieguanshu performed the cremation for Supervisor Chao, he shattered the golden circle and transcended birth and death.
A torch in broad daylight under a clear blue sky!
Chan Master Nan Shiyou performed the cremation for the newly appointed senior monk Yue, the monastery steward.

Although he has served as a steward for many years and is not one who has newly entered the monastic community, if the great matter of birth and death remains unclarified, listen now as the flames preach the Dharma for you.

I performed the cremation for the guest-master Mǎo. He had not yet realized that the adventitious afflictions were blazing and flourishing; once he had understood the single truth, the universe was cleared and purified.
Thus, from the very head of dead firewood, the flames rose up and let out a true roar.
For the fire of the Elder Jing: His pure wisdom is wondrously perfect; his essence is inherently empty and still. Entering birth and exiting death is like fire burning ice.
For the fire of the Head Seat Daxingkong: Chanting praises atop the bell tower, growing vegetables beneath the bed—this is direct realization.
Penetrating through, there is no doubt regarding birth and death. The true fire of the nature of emptiness; the true emptiness of the nature of fire. A gnat swallows the peak of Mount Sumeru.
For the sake of the Abbot Cheng, the fire flares up and scatters the fragments of firewood; the waves of the *kṣetra* subside into clarity.

One thoroughly knows that there is neither Buddha nor Patriarch—who would say there is death or birth? A diamond statue molded from mud runs amidst the clouds; a Bodhisattva drawn with a brush walks through the flames.

Acting as hall attendant, storekeeper, or server, and maintaining the purity of the fires—these are matters on the shore of birth and death. Grinding rice in the mortar house is a matter on the shore of birth and death.
Announcing to the assembly in the corridor is a matter on the shore of birth and death. How can you emerge from birth and death? "Two arises from one."
Do not cling even to this "one. Within the flames, the wagtail opens its smiling mouth.
When Chan Master Folang Xing performed the cremation for the Abbot Miaojian of Tiantong, it was settled in a single stroke:

birth and death are beyond description. He became the master among masters; what need is there to debate whether he was sublime or not? Having brushed aside the diamond circle, his constant radiance is pure.
Silently. He makes a circular gesture with a torch and asks, "Do you understand? Amidst a mass of fierce flames, turn quickly;
above, there is another aperture that pierces through to heaven."
For you, Qiongdu, this is the fire of the monastery. Upon a single hair-tip stand jade towers and crystal palaces; on this side and that side are the faces of the sun and moon.
Wiping away Yangqi’s three-legged donkey, what need is there to worry about birth and death as urgent as a flying arrow?
Refine yourself once more within this great mass of fire; it is the majestic, authentic body of adamantine flame. (He lets out a shout.)
For the sake of the Lingchun Monastery fire, with a single breath I cause the first turn; spring light pervades the great earth.
Letting go of the leaking oil lamp, birth and death are like a game. Coming and coming, yet truly not coming; going and going, yet fundamentally no going.
The fire of the nature of true emptiness is the patience of non-arising—this is the highest rank at the Dragon Flower Assembly.
For the sake of the ultimate benefit of the monastery’s stewards, through the power of supreme compassion and meditative concentration, how could there be the illness of birth and death?

When walking at night, do not step on white; it is neither water nor stone. Whether public or private matters, do not concern yourself with them; shatter the cave of ignorance. Striking a circular form with a torch, he said:
"The wisdom-fire of the Vajra-body; the great trichiliocosm is like the rising sun."
Chan Master Shiyufang addressed the fire-head attendant Hai: "Up until now you have been burning the fire; today, the fire shall burn you.
If only you can realize that the nature of fire is empty, your own nature will likewise be so. Has the fire-head Hai understood yet? A surge of windless waves arises;
though the ocean of wisdom is deep, its bottom is ultimately visible."
Chan Master Hongjue Wenyin said: "The fire-head [attendant] has reached the root. Whether the stove is cold, apply the fire; whether the stove is hot, apply the fire.
As for the causes you have created, you shall receive the corresponding fruits. Knowing the cause, one realizes that the fundamental substance is unborn.
This would make Mount Songshan’s 'Broken Stove Falling' laugh to death."
To extinguish the fire of the Venerable Zhixiu, one must turn the light back in a single thought: "Before my parents were born, who was I?
With the four corners collapsing to the ground, the eternally true, solitary original person is revealed. Furthermore, knowing when to stop, one can stop; knowing when to rest, one can rest.
Like the incense burner in an ancient temple, or like a single length of white silk—though it may receive the alms bowl from another house, one need not forcibly attach a handle to it.
The mold on the rice has grown white and level; yellow clumps gather at the corners of the mouth. Eating alone, one chews the food in the cauldron until it is soft.

Because one’s breath is suppressed like ash, one is able to treat birth and death as if casting off a garment. Yet if you simply proceed in this manner, I fear you will merely guard the cold crags where strange grasses turn green, or sit amidst the white clouds—this lineage is not subtle.
When I, this mountain monk, have reached this point, I cannot help but pivot for you with another turn of the mechanism. I wish to wait...
Lying crosswise within the triple world—please consult the Brahmin Śūramgama. He casts down the fire-torch and burns it away;
this is the fire of the Seal and Mantra Chief Administrator. Most difficult to invade is the ancestral field; let the nine rats and three snakes burrow through it at will.
How many times has the kalpa-fire been clearly extinguished? Yet the wind through the pines still reaches the bamboo slopes. Thus, the ancients said:
"The substance is exhausted and the form dissolves, yet it does not perish; the metal flows and the ore scatters, yet it remains forever. This is precisely what that means.
If this is so, what more need be said of the river flowing east thirty years ago, or the river flowing west thirty years hence? Nevertheless, as for the world—
The formation of the world has no connection with this; the abiding of the world has no connection with this;
even the destruction and emptiness of the world have no connection with this. But tell me, what is this? [He] throws down a firebrand and says:
When it strikes the face, one realizes it directly; the precious seal in the void matches the azure sky.
A miraculous omen for the monk Huo—whom would say that the winding does not conceal the straight? One must believe that within life there is death; now, having died, one returns to life.
Behind the crown of the head, the divine light extends ten thousand miles. Holding up a torch, he says: "Look! Look! I see the lamp-light."
The Buddha’s original radiance and auspicious signs are like this.

It is for the sake of ordinary Chan practitioners raising the torch: do not cling to ordinary sentiments, and you will immediately manifest the sacred sentiment. The mountains of Wu and the waters of Chu compete in their towering majesty;
now the Yellow Crane Tower has been toppled by a single fist, and before the Isle of Parrots, the moon is shining brightly. Look with urgency! Be alert!
Awakened! When all traces of news have vanished, the whole body is revealed: an iron snake chews cold ice amidst the flames.
For the sake of the Zen practitioner Hengche, [I say]: Prajñā is like a great mass of fire; one cannot enter it from any of the four sides.
Prajñā is like a cool, refreshing pool; one may enter it from any of the four sides. Even if you can enter, there is nowhere to go; even if you cannot enter, there is nowhere to go.
Go! But as for one whose entire body remains within—how is that? Casting off the hands beyond the thousand sages, returning to the source is fit to be an ox in the fire.
I have prepared the firewood for the hearth from the start; I envy you for entering the monastic life so late. Your practice is mostly pure and diligent. When it rains, you beat your straw sandals;
when the sun is out, you hope to find some wood. You serve as the provider of fuel for the kitchen, daily hacking at the green mountains.

Holding a clumsy axe in the right hand, you trim the branches; with the left, you twist the hemp rope to bind them. Carrying the load along the path of birds, you tread upon every height and depth. This samādhi is truly majestic.
The Enjoyment Body (saṃbhogakāya) has been inherently endowed with wondrous, brilliant clarity from the very beginning; yet, for no apparent reason, the burden was broken this morning.
How joyful and truly liberated throughout one's life! How could it compare to Pòzào Duò of Mount Sōng?
How could it vie with Pǔhuà shaking his bells? A-he-he! Joyful or not joyful? A cricket in the fire swallows a large insect; ten thousand miles away across the sky, a single *yún* bird soars.
Chan Master Zhuo’an asked about the fire at the office of Vice-Abbot Wen: "From hearing, contemplating, and practicing, one enters samādhi;
the golden lock is snapped asunder and the entire body shatters into a hundred fragments. Within the flash of a stone-fire, one realizes intimacy; with a long cry, a pure wind arises."
The fire for Master Cheng’s attendant was witnessed and heard firsthand within the Bamboo Grove Monastery; it is the very same as today.
That which was personally realized and verified in the Shiqing Mountains is the very same as today. You have never turned your back on me, nor have I ever failed you.
From morning until night, you held the towel and the water pitcher; this single stream of brilliance covered heaven and earth, undisturbed by the eight winds.
Unshakable, neither praise nor blame can affect him. He sweeps past the five Mount Sumerus and overturns the four great oceans;

he snatches the crest-jewel from the jaws of the black dragon and parts the murderous claws from the whiskers of the fierce tiger. Thus, with eyes that see clearly and hands that act decisively, he blazes forth as the most eminent of his time.
In the end, having cast off the shackles and escaped the hook, he is truly able to cut off all continuity. It is no mistake to say he is one among the lions in the lion’s den.
Lion! You are truly what is called "sandalwood within a sandalwood grove. Since your task is complete, what regret could my heart have?
Having reached this point, you have passed through the final, weighty barrier at the top of a hundred-foot pole. But tell me, is there still further progress to be made?
Since the darkness of the mundane world was shattered by its brilliance, it has been clearly manifest throughout the entire realm, never concealed. Thus he cast down the torch;

the fire of the Patriarch’s barrier follows the flame of the Zen practitioner. The light of the Hall of Wisdom shines upon the entire world, and the fierce flames at the Basin for Washing Bowls extend across the heavens.

With both the environment and the physical body fully adorned, he surpasses the blind, shaven-headed Chan practitioners of all quarters; yet this does not hinder his ability to outshine the past and illuminate the future.
For those who would rest in their own meditation, he teaches them to rest, though they refuse to do so. Having exerted every effort in supporting the assembly, he now raises his two eyebrows.
I could not have believed that this day would come. If you can truly believe it, what separation could there be between life and death? I raise high the banner of radiance;
for your sake, I strike this wedge once more.
The Cremation of Zen Practitioner Hantang. "Venerable Hantang, from where have you come? And to where will you go?
Your place of coming is precisely your place of going. If you recognize the place of going, you will not fail the place of coming.
But as for the one who comes from nowhere and goes nowhere—how is that? Look! The fire has broken out!"
Chan Master Wuwen Can presided over the funeral rites for the Elder Yi. The ultimate pivot of the Dharma fills one’s eyes and ears;
it is like a gale-force wind that allows no landing, like a long sword leaning against the heavens that brooks no deliberation. Why?
Because if you turn your head or twist your brain, you will be a corpse lying ten thousand miles away.

The Venerable Huì raised up the bones; the Sun of Wisdom hung high in the heavens. Shining throughout the heavens and across the earth, it pierces through the eyes of Buddhas and Patriarchs and reveals the very core of the monk’s nostrils.
Although this is the total manifestation of reality when confronted directly, if you recognize it as such, it remains incorrect as before. Why?
Because to err by a hair’s breadth is to lose the mark by a thousand miles.
Chan Master Gaofeng Miao forged the bones of the two Senior Monks Zheng. As for Senior Monk Zheng: two do not form a pair, nor does one form a solitary unit.
His teeth are distinct; he is truly possessed of bone. Within the furnace of ten thousand refinements, his color shines with perfect brilliance.
The earthen ox butts through the cave of the azure dragon.
When the Elder Guangshe was cremating his bones, he could neither grasp them nor let them go. At such a moment, how can one truly comprehend?
*Pfft!* Raise your eyebrows and look into the fire: there, clearly visible, is a set of golden bones.
Chan Master Daguang Miaogao was interring the remains of the two Chan practitioners, Yi and Zhao. Holding up a bone from his left hand, he said, "This is Yi of Meizhou.
Holding up a bone from his right hand, he said, "This is Zhao of Raoyou. One understood Chan; the other understood the Teachings.
Although each followed their own path, in the end they arrived at the same time. But tell me, what does it mean to arrive at the same time?
"What is this matter? In the pond of a private villa belonging to whom? A pair of mandarin ducks cannot be painted.

For the sake of Chan Master Wei Yue’s entry into the stupa, [the Master] held up the remains and said: "At Vulture Peak they spoke of the moon; at Caoxi they pointed to the moon. Today, Miaoxi holds up the moon.
If one investigates this thoroughly and minutely, one has not yet attained total eradication. Why is this? Rather—"
This master has completely exposed all his secret mechanisms. Since they have been exposed, look! It is already the Mid-Autumn Festival;
there is nothing that can compare to it. Let him speak for himself.
Master Gumengyou, the Zen Master, performed the enshrinement for Attendant Chuan. The tree has fallen and the vines are withered; the flames of the red furnace have been extinguished.
Having exhausted all antiquities, there is no further leakage. Striking him back into the pagoda courtyard, he is as pure as ice and as pristine as jade.
Attendant Chuan has pulled open the vast earth to reach the secure barrier—like clear lapis lazuli containing a precious moon.
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun composed this for the interment of Official Ming: "Clearly knowing it is this very thing, one cannot open one's mouth to speak;
clearly knowing it is not this very thing, one can indeed open one's mouth and speak. Having cut off both barriers, his natural wind-bone is revealed.
A hundredfold hits, the sage’s arrow leaves the string; seven-pierced and eight-perforated, from south of Xiang to north of Tan. For your sake..."
How many times did he descend into the Blue Dragon’s Cave?
Chan Master Zhuang Da’an performed the enshrinement for the Head Seat, Lü. One who has truly practiced enters life and death as if in play.
Furthermore, when the sword hangs from between his brows—how is it? If you hesitate to respond, your skull will be struck.
At the site, Chan Master Nan Shiyou was interred in his stupa by the administrative head, Yin. Because of delusion there is birth; because of birth there is extinction.
When quiescent extinction manifests before one, the eyes within the skull are alive; the lotus flower blooms within the thorny chestnut burr. Amidst the seamless stupa, clouds swirl.
[The Master] circled [the grave]. Chan Master Tieguanshu entered the stupa for the sake of Abbot Cidu. [He uttered: "Baoji, Ci, Ge, 'Juice from Dry Bones,' the 'Diamond Circle,' the 'Mud Ball.
Casting down the bones, he said: 'A clear pool does not permit the azure dragon to coil.'"
Chan Master Gaofeng Miao enshrined his esteemed dharma heir in this stupa. To realize the meaning is to forget the words; to act in reverse is to transform others in accordance with them.
Always on the road, yet never leaving home. With a snap of the fingers, he said: "The stupa door is open!
Throughout the entire world, there is nowhere for a skull to hide. Here, let go of everything entirely."
Chan Master Zhongfeng Ben composed this for the interment of Dharma Hall Attendant Xian (posthumously titled Wugai; he resided at Qianqing Temple).

Having lived in poverty to the very marrow for thirty years, he has constantly formed a karmic enmity with the Buddhas and Patriarchs. When the Great Spirit crushes the bones of empty space, the great function manifests before every single speck of dust.
I respectfully venerate the deceased: before Lion Rock, you attained a single phrase; atop Lotus Flower Peak, it was as if...
Emptiness merges with emptiness. At the summit of Lotus Peak, one awakens to a single pivot; before Lion Rock, it is like a mirror reflecting a mirror.

Whether on this side or that side, its application is never lacking; across thousands and tens of thousands of miles, wherever conditions meet, it is the very source. Cast aside the water-and-fire jewel.
Put down the straw-sweeping fan. Here, the entire ten directions of the world are the adamantine true body;
the entire ten directions of the world are the seamless gate of the stupa. To go out is unimpeded, and to enter is unimpeded.
But tell me, how shall one proclaim the phrase of neither going out nor entering? An iron horse bursts open the green stone gate; a jade rooster pecks through—
The Golden Egg. Regarding the late Head Seat Jian’s entry into the stupa:
that final word was already spoken long before you had even set foot on the eighteen-thousand-li road to Duan.
Today, Ancient Mirror radiates its light, revealing the lightning flashing across the clear sky. It is perfectly round.
The seamless pagoda door opens; grasp the three-foot sword between the brows.
(Yunnan person) When the guest master Hong enters the pagoda and the rector is absent, you must strike the mallet. With one blow to the head, rouse the grand regulations.
Tear open the seamless pagoda and shatter the jade glass. This is precisely the moment of laying down the entire body.
Chan Master Tianru Ze entered the stupa as the Great Elder. The entire earth is this Great Elder;
the entire earth is this skull of death; the entire earth is this seamless stupa.
But tell me, from where does one enter? He let out a shout.
When Chan Master Huanyou enshrined the remains of the assembly in the Universal Common Stūpa (Pútóngtǎ), the entire world of the ten directions was itself this seamless stūpa.
Furthermore, where could one seek a place of entry or exit? It is only because people falsely calculate that there is entering and exiting.
Today, we take no account of whether these are the bone-slabs of Zhang San, nor do we take account of those of Li Si.
[The Master] said, "Whether it be Xu Wu’s or Xie Ba’s, [I do not care]. Raising his staff, he pointed to the door of the pagoda and said, 'Bring them all here for me;
place them all within this. Suddenly, he recalled the words of Śākyamuni:
'I observe the three-thousandfold world system, and even within its midst, there is not a single spot the size of a mustard seed that was not abandoned by me.'"
The locus of body and life. Heh! To offer this body and mind to every dust mote and land—this is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness.
When Chan Master Ruohan asked about the enshrinement of Chief Seat Chè, [he said]: "The path of the noble is naturally distinct from the outset.
From beginning to end, what is born and what ceases? A heart and liver forged from cast iron; a backbone tempered from refined steel. This is it."
You are one who has always stood alone with a distinguished character, a model for gods and humans. You have cast wide open the hands of ultimate poverty and raised high the nose of the vast heavens.
Although you have not yet fully displayed your total majesty, you have already caused flowers to bloom upon the iron stake. You laugh at Xiangyan’s climbing the tree for its needless fuss;
you deride the plucking of flowers at Vulture Peak as merely exhausting superfluous effort. Indeed, you have taken this up with empty hands; you are no mistaken patch-robed monk.
The monk’s breath has ceased. Today, when this mountain monk arrives here, there are words difficult to utter and a mind impossible to fathom.
[He strikes a circle with his staff and says: "I raise the great Dharma banner of the monastic community to leave it as a standard for future generations."
The Attendant Hong enters the stupa. Meeting on a narrow path, he is suddenly struck by a scorching shout; the thatched hut is burned down. Together they emerge and together they vanish;
Mount Sumeru is toppled, leaving no place for his entire body to rest. Yet he refuses to settle for this, choosing instead to be buried alive.

Time and again he travels from the south of the Yangtze to the north. Now tell me: does the mountain monk owe you, or do you owe the mountain monk? *Throwing down the bones, he says:* "Great lamentation!"
Suddenly, three days of rain poured down. Where there was no elegance, there was elegance.
When the monk Yong entered the stupa, people said, "I am alive; the Venerable Upadhyaya is dead. The mountain monk said, "I am dead;
the Venerable Upadhyaya is instead alive. How can this be verified? Pointing to the stupa, he said, "Enter. (This occurred on the occasion of the Master’s fiftieth birthday.)
The Jade Chan practitioner enters the Universal Cremation Site (Pūtóng). The perilous Jianxia Gorge is not truly perilous; the deep Gutang Gorge is not truly deep.

Emerging from one monastic community and entering another grove of trees, he feels the bottom of the bowl—how high and towering it rises! He peers through the windows and doors—it is difficult to fathom or grasp.
Today, he suddenly collapsed. He was sent back to a pit ten thousand fathoms deep. Pointing his staff at the stupa, he said:
"Coming and going everywhere leaves no trace; it is better to find rest here."
Chan Master Hongjue Mian composed this for the interment of the Chan practitioner Weifan at Shaolin. At Shaolin, it was said that one may attain the skin or the marrow;
at Nanyue, the eyes, tongue, and mind were likewise distinguished. Passing directly south of Xiang and north of Tan, it is everywhere said that the entire land is filled with gold.
Lifting up the bone lining, he said: "At Tiantong, it is not like this at all. Within the presence of all ordinary and sagely beings, we wrap them all together;
let the withered bones be made to roar like dragons."

Chan Master Shiyufang, Qiyanyan, Panming, and Shanming entered the same stupa together. In the Land of Constant Quiescent Light and the Land Where Ordinary Beings and Sages Dwell Together, one hand shields while the other reveals.
Since the enlightened spirits of these three—Qiyanyan, Panming, and Shanming—already share the same life-force and the same vessel, from now on there is no need for mutual concealment.
Should there be a need for concealment, those of the same breath will naturally seek one another out.
Their voices harmonized as one. He picked up a bone and said, "Duo.
He then moved the old collective remains of Bao-shou into the new collective stupa. Zen of the Tathāgata and Zen of the Patriarchs both rely entirely upon the spring wind of the second month.
To the east, waters and clouds; to the west, waters and clouds. The partridges cry and fallen flowers fly. Depart from the assembly.
"O awakened spirit, do not move! Although you do not eat the provisions of the Empty King, you must let everyone know that you are held in high esteem.
[He] cast down the bones and said, "Send them off.

For the Unmarked True Chan Master, acting as the Director of the Monastery in the Capital, the bones were scattered. Sixty-three years of a dream-like and illusory body—within this, [the essence remains].
To whom can this news be entrusted? When the iron ox has finished plowing, it turns its body; it pierces through the clear pool, and the night moon is renewed.
Inspector Jing traveled extensively throughout all quarters in his youth; now returned in his old age, he follows conditions as they arise, moving with natural spontaneity.
He is exceptionally carefree and remains alert to the very end. Although he is free to go or stay, alas, this one still remains. Is it thus?
At this moment, do you all still know where it has fallen? A single stream flows from the heart of Lake Anavatapta; a flash of lightning illuminates the three thousandfold world system.
For the nun’s passing, we request the funeral rites: [raising the coffin], [holding the torch], and [entering the stupa].
Chan Master Yuansou Duan raised the coffin for the eminent nun Miaojingjie. He saw that the body has no reality—it is the Buddha-body;

mountains, rivers, and the great earth are utterly devoid of external conditions. He realized that the mind is like an illusion—it is the Buddha-illusion; grasses, trees, and forests possess no separate dharma.
Therefore, this certain person, manifesting in the form of a bhikṣuṇī, accomplishes the deeds of a great man. She casts aside the jade tower.
The Golden Hall: Directly heading toward this school, it stands forth like an iron wall and a silver mountain, clarifying one's own nature alone.

It clears away the clouds and mist from the sky of the nature and sweeps away the dust and darkness of the mind-ground. Penetrating sound and penetrating form, it is brilliant and unobstructed in all eight directions; spanning from antiquity to the present, it flows freely throughout the ten directions.
Without fixity or necessity, it can be both supple and firm. Its Way accords with the two courts of North and South, and its fame fills the East.
To the west, in the two regions of Zhejiang, the numinous mechanism is agile and free; even Liu Tiemo was not yet able to fully behold its splendor.
The mirror of wisdom is empty and perfect; even Ling Xingpo must take a step back. The whole body is this great ocean of liberation; the whole body is this wondrous mind of nirvana.
There is no arising or ceasing to be sought, and no birth-and-death to escape from. When the hundred skeletal members disintegrate, it stands forth alone and solitary. Part four.
At the moment of great separation, all is profoundly still and eternally tranquil. At such a time, let us not speak of going out from within the body; how about coming forth from within the gate?
One has always traveled upon the crown of Vairocana’s head; in the Land of Peace and Bliss, one may go or stay as one pleases.
Chan Master Hongjue Wen raised the coffin for the nun Xi’an. With every lifting, it was ever new; firmly guarding the profound pivot, he sat and brought others to their end.
When the Northern Dipper is lost and the Southern Star appears, if you wish to behold the flying dragon beyond the thousand worlds, a single secret step is the thoroughfare.
The assembly, consider this: as for that which cannot be pushed forward and cannot be pulled back—what then?
"How so? He struck the shrine once with his staff and said: "Stretching out three legs of an iron donkey, riding backward upon a jade elephant to pursue the qilin.
Master Nian’ao Duan has performed the cremation for the Nun Neng. Her karmic conditions are now exhausted; her life’s work is complete. Four...
"Let us set aside the matter of the five great aggregates for a moment. As for the bhikṣuṇī Xing turning a single thought into arhatship—what evidence is there for this at all?
He threw down a firebrand and said, "A blazing mass of fire; if you touch it, it will burn you to death."
Chan Master Hongjue Wen performed the cremation for Nun Benyou. After the four elements had dispersed and all conditions were utterly abandoned, one gazes toward Mount Nirvana;
the smoke and grass are lush and dense. The steep peaks are ravaged and the profound mystery incinerated. The skull is completely parched, yet the mother-born eyes remain;
ten thousand miles away, a divine light shines from behind the crown of the head.
Chan Master Wuyongkuan has enshrined the Daoist nun Cishou in her stupa. She manifested as a young girl in Jambudvīpa;
she never mistook the markings on the scale. Having been refined in the fire, she still radiates brilliance; within the *stūpa*, it is spring in all four seasons.
Chan Master Zhuo’an asked: When a nun enters the Universal Common Cremation Ground, it is like jade carved by white stone and gold cast from yellow metal;
hundreds of thousands of Buddhas participate together, walking hand-in-hand within the Hall of Universal Radiance. This is neither nirvana nor rebirth in the future;
where one lays down body and life, all traces vanish. Yet, as before, she faces south to gaze at the Big Dipper.
The Uposatha Layman’s Passing: A Record of the Buddha’s Affairs (Raising the Coffin, Holding the Torch, Raising the Bones, Entering the Tomb and Scattering Earth, Consecrating the Tablet).
Master Shimen Gang performed the rite of raising the coffin for Du Junyu: "Fifty-odd years have passed since that dream of returning home;
A fine person has departed so swiftly—truly it is a cause for sorrow. Upon the Lan River, the cold plum bears dew; It seems as if the grieving one sheds tears. Respectfully.

It is said that such-and-such a person was a man of distinction in his province and possessed a fine reputation throughout the four seas. In his youth, he inherited the legacy of his uncle; in his prime, he excelled in the ancestral enterprise of his forebears.
With two sons and two daughters, he rejoiced in having wives and a household; with one husband and one wife, it was fitting to wish him longevity and prosperity.
Yet, who would have expected him to be infected by a terminal illness? How could he so suddenly suffer such a calamity to his very vitals?

In grief, we suddenly see the boat shifted to the night’s ravine; forever parted from the span of natural life. It is truly as when flowers bloom only for rain to fall, or the moon shines bright only for clouds to veil it.
Relatives wail in lamentation and wives and children suffer in pain. The widowed parent in the hall has lost their support; brothers and sisters, like branches of the same tree, are wounded in heart.
At such a time, one should well employ the sword of wisdom to sever the net of affection and tread open the path beyond birth and death.
The Path. Leaping out of the pass of right and wrong, reflect inward and turn the light back upon yourself. Realize that one’s original nature is nothing other than Buddha-nature.

Return to the truth and abandon delusion; understand that the ordinary mind is itself the holy mind. Depart from the burning house and mount the great carriage; take a single step backward from the midst of the dust. Seek the tomb in the shade;
when it is time to return to the inner chamber, simply invite tranquility while facing the streams and mountains. This is no different from the Pure Land—what more is there to say?
Obstruction! You must awaken with fierce introspection; do not hesitate any longer. Even so, tell me: how can one express the single phrase of "stepping out the door"?
Heh! Trusting one’s feet as they step out the door is the Great Way; in this realm or other worlds, one may wander at ease.
Chan Master Tianmu Li served as the torch-bearer for Commander Chen. One version says: "The warhorses at the frontier urge him on;
several times he has returned with songs of victory. Now that he is old and his body is of no further use, he lies listening to the 'Plucking the Plum' melody played atop the city wall.
His loyal heart is easily broken, yet his indignant spirit is difficult to crush. This final, most secure stronghold—the Southern Mountain shall break it open for you. Chen.
Commander! You must quickly look at the "biting the arrowhead" before the trigger; a fire-arrow comes splitting one’s face from the sky.
