The Torch-Cloud. For eighty years, this person has relied solely upon this to establish their home and build their career. Through diligence in the granary and frugality in the storehouse, they have accumulated a surplus;
through benevolence in dwelling and righteousness on the path, their conduct has never been exhausted. For eighty years, they have relied solely upon this to honor virtue and admire the good.
Whenever the mind is raised, it never obscures the true nature; wherever one is touched by it, the whole body is expedient means. Eighty years...

Coming here, we rely solely on this to educate our children and raise our grandchildren; the eminent scholars stand tall, continuing the illustrious footsteps of their ancestors, while the tinkling of their jade rings and pendants shakes the noble gate.
For eighty years, we have relied solely on this to gather the causes and bring forth the fruit:

the surface of the cauldron overflows with a shimmering green, and beneath the Hall of Good Fortune, the flowers bloom one after another. Reaching this point, the original face is revealed—pure and true in every encounter with things.
One’s own mountain home is not more than a few paces away. The eighty-four thousand pores are in mutual communication with the true fire-pore of intrinsic emptiness;
the three hundred and sixty joints are mutually supported by the empty space of intrinsic fire.
Radiance hangs down and disperses into the forest of merit and virtue; its brilliance flows and is gathered back into the gateway of light. Now tell me, what is this thing?
Brandishing a torch, he drew a circle and said: "Rotating in perfect circles, it becomes a great round mirror; every single branch reflects forth coral boughs.
All the people of the world do not see them; only Master Feng alone knows them."
The funeral pyre of Chan Master Gumeng You and Layman Wuwei: Ten thousand leaves fall as golden rain; a thousand peaks stand as a chilling mountain.
With a single turn of the body, he ascends directly to Mount Nirvana. Ultimately, on what does he rely? From the beginning, his nostrils have hung down with great dignity;
whether entering or withdrawing, acting or concealing, one must seek them out. Cease seeking! Atop the mountain, the stone tiger’s roar has gone dry; at the bottom of the sea...
The clay ox butts its horns until they break; it is like sand in the eyes of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.
If one does not achieve perfect enlightenment in a single thought, then even though it is so, how ultimately is the final word? Master Juetong: "Aha!
Riding an iron horse backward up Mount Kunlun, let the red furnace smelt the empty shell as it pleases.
Chan Master Gaoping Miao performed the cremation for Layman Zhiguang. Drawing a circle with his hand amidst the flames, he said:

"The waters of Gusu and the mountains of Tianmu— All are the non-dual barrier of Vimalakīrti. When one turns their head within this fierce blaze, It is as if the human world were still faintly visible."
Chan Master Hongjue Wen: Human strength is like wearing a firebrand on one’s back; his life was spent with bare shoulders from dawn until dusk.

He constantly bore a load of over a hundred and twenty catties upon his shoulders. Today, he has personally broken his扁担 (flat shoulder-pole). His carefree wandering is like clouds across the sea and sky. Lin Zipei, do you know it yet?
Because you did not cultivate merit in past lives, you have encountered suffering at every turn since birth. [The current flow continues...]
Separated from waves and splashes in countless ways, with no one to rely upon or protect, you take refuge in the forest groves as your support.
In the morning you hack at the green mountains; by evening you have lost your way. Your whole body is drenched in profuse sweat. Why is your life so stingy—so solitary and fragile?
Not yet having reached thirty, you die young. Is it that the August Heaven truly lacks kindness? Listen to my words: cease your resentment and anger. By...
He struck a circular shape with a fire-torch and said: "Only this one matter is vast and uniform: the wealthy have no surplus and the poor lack nothing.
It rests upon your own person without deficiency or ruin. Like a great, majestic *māṇi* jewel that emits fire, when it rains down treasures, precious things pervade the world."
"The kalpa may be burned, yet the channel remains unimpeded. Neither increasing nor decreasing, it is inherently vajra-like. The body departs and the body arrives, eternally in samādhi.

A spade upon the shoulder; a plow in the hand. He lets out a shout and says: "This time, everything is entrusted to the old man Bingding. With a single stroke, the debts of the impoverished ghosts are wiped away.
Having said this, he throws [the fire] down and sets it ablaze.
Chan Master Tianruze said: "The clouds and valleys, the rocks and ten thousand households, arise from the bones. While alive, one is enfeoffed as a marquis for his strategic military merits;

when dead, he shall partake of offerings in the temple to manifest his spiritual intelligence. He stroked the bones and said: "Furthermore, turn yourself around from this very place; in every dust mote of the Buddha-land, there is a path that leads through.
Such a person was invincible in valor, profound and still in counsel, possessing both martial strategy and literary wisdom, naturally entrusted with the green [robes of office].
Among those of the forest was Feng Yi. With a loyal heart and a spirit of righteousness, he constantly held in mind Zhou Yu of Chibi.

His worth was extolled by his friends, and his kindness was felt by his soldiers. Carrying out the royal mandate to suppress the Yao and Tion tribes, he strove with reckless disregard for his own life;

wielding military authority, his prestige shook the barbarian wastes, and those who heard of him were disheartened. When the news of his victory first reached the heavens, he suddenly grew weary of men upon his return journey.
In an instant, he performed a somersault before the Qingshang Monastery and departed; on the Wusong River, he welcomed his reliquary casket back home.

Heaven and earth changed countenance for him; mountains and rivers shed tears for him. His work being accomplished, what regret could there be in death? The entire nation calls him a true man of great character.
Twenty-four years of following the teachings have been like a dream; the lineage relies upon this extraordinary son to carry it forward.
My son, for hundreds of thousands of millions of lifetimes, your fragrance shall flow on. Upon reaching this point, exert your spirit and discern the message anew.
Tear asunder the web of affliction and smash through the barrier of birth and death. The illusory form and its shadows come and go like drifting clouds emerging from a valley;
the true nature and true luminosity do not shift nor change, like the bright moon suspended in the sky. It is precisely this—
This is the root of one’s own being; this is one’s native land and field; this is the place where one establishes one’s life and sustenance;
this is the very moment of becoming a Buddha and an ancestral patriarch. This is certainly so. But tell me: does there still arise any auspicious omen as you now raise your bones?
Last night, the heavenly wind stirred the snowflakes, sweeping the road for your western return.
Chan Master Wuxiang presided over the interment of the late Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, Yan Baisan. O Great Assembly!

The late Vice Minister Yan Baisan was a brilliant star whose radiance illuminated the four directions. He was about to grasp the lofty branches within the moon, and intended to act as a rain-bringer for the world.
Yet time did not grant him this; he has suddenly followed the receding waves. Relying now on this "stripping away of the body" (tieti) to awaken the mind, one must see the original source.
The face and eyes of the present moment: today at Lushan, the expedient means are opened wide to point directly to the essential ford.
O you who possess the hundred and three secret provinces, proceed thus to the very bottom. One enters all, and all enter one; walking alone in the Great Square, one sports in samādhi.
Although it is thus, you must further turn back from every place before you have attained it. If you turn back from every place...
It cannot be so. To die together but not be born together; if one attains transformation in all places, one is born together but does not die together.
At this very moment, do you wish to understand the phrase of "transcending birth and escaping death"? "Austere and heroic wind, its use inexhaustible;
Behold the orchids and jade, spreading the family’s renown."

Chan Master Ying'an Hua performed the earth-covering ceremony for the Retainer, the Grand Councilor and Senior Statesman. Heaven is high and earth is deep; the sea is vast and the mountains are distant.

He manifested the supreme faculty and revealed the true mark. Thus, our Retainer, the Grand Councilor and Minister, has expanded the orthodox eye of the crown of his head and displayed the numinous talisman behind his elbow.
By this he serves the state and the people; by this he achieves the utmost loyalty and filial piety.
One may say that great merit lies in the absence of a master; truly, we see a master at work here. At the very end, he fully raises the banner;
the ten directions of space are completely severed. In the field of non-arising, there is sowing and harvest; upon the vessel of Prajñā, there is a ferry and a crossing.
One attains the state of soaring far beyond all things and treading alone upon the Great Way. At such a time, how do you speak a single phrase of total reverence? You must be careful.
Looking beyond the clouds: A single sword leans against the heavens, cold.
Master Yuansou Duan performed the earth-covering ceremony for the layman Zhu Yuxuan of Bohai. The entire world of the ten directions is a single great treasury of radiant light;
from antiquity to the present, not a single dharma has been added. Throughout the void of the ten directions...
This is a great gate of liberation. From antiquity to the present, there has not been a single dharma that can be diminished.
Thus, our fellow countryman, the Layman Yue-xuan of Bohai, was a virtuous gentleman of his locality and a man of refined spirit within the three realms.

As for his Confucianism, he was a divining stalk and a mirror for the Confucian garden; as for his Buddhism, he was the rampart and moat of the Buddha-gate. Although he manifested the performance of conditioned phenomena...

They engage in worldly affairs without destroying the characteristics of the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*). Although they demonstrate the study of unconditioned dharmas, they do not discriminate regarding the names of the conditioned (*saṃskṛta*).
Although they manifest fame, glory, wealth, and honor, they are not bound or entangled by such fame, glory, wealth, and honor.
Although he manifests the karmic retribution of worldly afflictions (*kleśa*), he is not submerged by such afflictions. He recovers the primordial ground and reveals his own family tradition;

he sustains his ancestors with poetry and the classics, and delights his kin and friends with propriety and righteousness. In his relationship as husband and wife, they are like the *qin* and *se* lutes in harmony;
in raising children and grandchildren, they are like the *feng* and *lin* phoenixes and qilin. Through the practice of various skillful means, he brings all things to completion.
Through various causes and conditions, in years past, the whole body came thus: a snake appearing as a reflection in wine. This morning, the whole body goes thus:
a wild goose leaving a trace upon the sand. Since the snake in the wine has no real substance to remain, how could the goose’s trace on the sand have any true mark worth clinging to?
Penetrating in all directions without obstruction, amidst ten thousand distinctions and a thousand variations—there is nothing to grasp.

There is absolutely no obstruction whatsoever. At this very moment, when one has returned to the root and attained the essential meaning, how can one uphold and display that final phrase of ultimate glory?
A single mound of yellow earth covers a lifetime; a thousand ages of pure wind stir the mountain caves.
Chan Master Qianguan Chang performed the interment for Old Man Lou Qing. How could Heaven disregard human sentiment? Amidst a mass of snow and rain, he selected a clear day.
By cultivating merit, one naturally invites a karmic reward; before life and after death, his radiance is revealed.
"Do you all see this patch of ground right before you? This was personally prepared by my late friend, Old Man Qing."
That which has been attained is inexhaustible to enjoy while alive, and inexhaustible to enjoy at death; it will likewise be inexhaustible for one's descendants to enjoy for generations to come.
If those present here can observe this model and learn from it, each should return home and cultivate that very plot of land;
it is truly excellent. Otherwise, I, this mountain monk, shall further spread flowers upon brocade for you. Worldly people—!
There was an eminent and heroic man who had accumulated goodness and cultivated virtue; a single phrase of his accorded with the path shared by a thousand chariots.
On this day, I respectfully honor our late patron, the Elder Layman Qing, the Former Court Gentleman. He was of the lineage of National Teacher Zhizhe, a venerable elder from Yiwu County.
For eighty-four years, life after life has been fundamentally unborn. To practice is to preach, and to preach is to practice.
For eighty-four years, death after death, yet there is no dying. From son to grandson, and from grandson to son, the three-year mourning period is filial piety;
the funeral rites today are the ritual propriety. The purity of Heaven is the purity of the Elder. It is like the Palace of Śakra and Brahmā atop the neighboring Pure Abodes. As for the earth—
Thick! How thick is this virtue! It expands the realm of the true and eternal within the mind-ground; from the mud and mire, the nostrils protrude. Within the skull, the eyes open wide.
Contemplating form as empty, one realizes Great Wisdom and does not abide in birth-and-death.
Contemplating emptiness as form, one realizes Great Compassion and does not abide in Nirvana. Since one abides neither in Nirvana nor in birth-and-death, it is right now.
The Elder Qingweng has honored this single phrase with his whole being; how do you speak it? [He] scatters earth, saying:
"The spirit-casket may be closed, but the name cannot be concealed; the traveler on the road has a mouth like a monument. With these words, I take my leave. I pray you, cherish yourself.
For Lou Wen’ung’s entry into the tomb: Birth and death are the constant of the world; waxing and waning are the way of Heaven.
Man is the most spiritual among the myriad things; one ages while another does not. We respectfully contemplate the honored spirit of the late donor, the Director Lou Wen’ung:
both wealth and longevity were fully realized, and both reputation and conduct reached their pinnacle. Eighty-five years ago, you possessed nothing more than the skin-sack bestowed by your parents.
My son, after eighty-five years, this skin-bag born of one's parents will ultimately return to the earth.

During those eighty-five years, there was seeing, hearing, knowing, and perceiving; there were joys, sorrows, anger, and pleasures; distinctions were made between noble and base, and between good and evil.
In affairs, everything was orderly; in principle, every step was without error. You served as a mature elder of the village and community, bringing up your children and grandchildren...
Managing a household, manifesting as an elder in a sagely age, and exerting oneself as a great official among men—all these are brought forth by the Master from within this skin-bag.
Now, this Master has cast off the skin-bag and is contained within a coffin.
Tell me, is his countenance the same as it was before his parents were born, or is it different? It is one and the same.
The three threes are but one; from this emerge a thousand transformations and ten thousand changes. The golden crow flies through the heavens night after night;
every morning, the round sun surges forth. The World-Honored One said: "Physical form belongs to the four great elements; the nature of mind returns to the six sense objects.
Since the substance of the four great elements is each separate, who is it that brings them together? Lay Brother, even this is still a matter belonging to the shore of birth and death.
How is it to transcend birth and escape death? [The Master] picks up some earth and says: "The entire great earth is but a single pinch of soil;
within that pinch of soil, heaven and earth are vast. Heaven and earth are but a single spiritual coffin; a pair of eyes are vividly alive.
Turning one's head, one encounters what is one's own: bright moon and clear wind—how can they be compared? Shining through antiquity and soaring through the present, it is only—"
This is it. The old man is advanced in years; I humbly pray that you will provide for his needs.
Chan Master Tianru Ze was interred by Cao Gong of Ju-zhu; having escaped birth and death, one must know where he has fallen.
Since the place of descent is clearly manifest, it falls down from the void. After letting go, what then? Heaven opens and earth parts as the whole body appears;
a jade phoenix perches at night upon a shadowless tree. This person is the son of Counselor Mei-zhu and the grandson of Professor Shou-zhai.
In the distant past, his lineage has been recorded in the annals of history since the time of Prince Wuhui; in more recent times, he is descended from Lord Wen-gong.
His descendants have filled his lineage, leaving no commoners among them; everyone admires such prosperity, yet the Master did not consider it a source of honor.

When he first took up the post of a local schoolteacher, he grew weary of the autumn maples of Wujiang and shook out his sleeves to return home. Later, when summoned by a provincial decree, he cherished the bamboo groves by the steaming stream and shook his head, refusing to rise for office.
His conduct was such that he remained undisturbed by wealth and honor, never succumbing to their allure. There was none... [who could compare].

He intended for fame and merit, yet fame and merit arrived of their own accord. With weapons in his left hand and ritual vessels in his right, he certainly did not forget the ancestral reputation of the Cao clan.
By day he indulged in poetry and wine; by evening, he attended to the zither and books, wishing to emulate the refined demeanor of the men of Jin.

He once cut flesh from his thigh to blend with the soup in order to cure the illness of his great-grandfather; he also once removed his own clothing and gave away his food to provide for the needs of destitute scholars. As for his treatment of friends...
With friends, he was earnest and encouraging; toward his kinsmen and clansmen, he was broad-minded and open.

The disciples of Confucian learning looked up to him as a great master of literature, while the officials of the Jixian Academy hailed him as a pure and reclusive scholar. Throughout his life, all matters were already complete;
at the final moment, his realization reached even higher heights. From the crown of his head, the diamond eye was revealed; in every step, he manifested the ancients.
This is the pivot of the human gate. From the tip of the brush, the precious treasury of the *Lotus Sūtra* manifests; at every turn, the treasures of one’s own house are revealed.
There is no obstruction whatsoever regarding words and letters; neither nirvāṇa nor birth-and-death can hinder one another.
Previously, you only said, "Come out! Come out! Come out quickly! Alas for the burning house of the triple world! Only now do you know: "Go back! Go back! It is better to go back."
Depart! It is as if we were once again at the assembly on Vulture Peak. Since you have realized where you belong, why is it that there is something which cannot be taken away?
Since it cannot be taken away, it ought to be concealed. Since it is concealed, what evidence is there for it? [He scatters earth, saying:
"The provisional city and the precious abode are without distinction; every inch of soil has always been an inch of gold."
Chan Master Hongjue Wen covered the earth for the layman Huang Wanzhong. Holding up his staff, he said:
"This patch of ground has, from the very beginning, been in essence without front or back; its realm transcends all directions and corners. It existed prior to the self-arising of the Buddhas."
Its adornments lie beyond the limit of Vīkūṇa; it is not something the three calamities can reach, nor can it be shifted by the four modes of change.
This is truly because its ground and field are stable and profound; thus it is named the Jewel Monastery of the Vajra King, and also the Fearless Lion Banner.
In its concealment, the Buddhas of the three periods cannot encroach upon it; in its secrecy, the ancestral masters of successive generations and the elders of the world [cannot fathom it].
The Master has transcended the Gateless Barrier. Now, this mountain monk shall take back the original contract and deliver it with both hands to the layman Huang Wanzhong.

I pray that you will immediately set your four corners firmly upon the ground and cast your whole body down, returning to the great mansion of Nirvana and taking the entire ocean of Dharma as your home.
There will then be no more distinction between this world and other realms; who would dwell as a transient guest in a foreign land? Bamboo.
The pines extend along the banks, constantly revealing the local scenery of the original ground; at the tips of the hundred grasses, the great matter of one’s own feet is fully manifested.
It is such that it is like the moon descending upon the autumn waters, shining brilliantly everywhere; or like a wild goose passing through the vast sky, its traces sinking away without a mark.
Therefore it is said: "True in every place, true in every place; in every mote of dust is the person of original nature. When speaking of this reality, the sound—
"Not seen. The majestic, upright essence has vanished from the body. I venture to ask: since the body has vanished, what is this majestic, upright essence?
"The land of Han does not contain it; Qin does not oversee it. Riding a donkey backward toward Yangzhou."
Chan Master Shiyufang acted as the "eye-dotter" for the lay practitioner Ge Qizhan of the Taichang Academy.
With mountains high as his brush and waters long as his ink, the Master’s character could not be fully captured by description; it is the Way of Heaven. What does Heaven say?
It is his very literature—unadorned by a single dot. Nevertheless, the Master of Hunan has become a figure of ten thousand ages; his spirit and the moonlight remain faintly present.

Regarding the various rites for a laywoman’s passing— requesting the Buddha’s presence, raising the coffin, the tea-offering torch, cremating the bones, enshrining them in a stupa, scattering the bones, and establishing the spirit-tablet (zhǔ)—
Master Wuyuan performed the rite of raising the coffin for the Lady of the Kong family. Wuyuan’s words were entirely without fixed limits.
Meeting face-to-face, the shout of the Way arises.
For the sake of Lady Zhou, the coffin is raised. Fundamentally, there is no mark of male or female; the four elements have provisionally combined.
Appearing within the mundane world, one undergoes suffering and joy, adversity and favor. *Hè!* Leaping out of the barrier of birth and death, the pure wind resounds through the universe.
Chan Master Tianyin raised the coffin for the practitioner Yan. Holding up his staff, he struck the coffin and said:
"Delusion has continued from vast kalpas until this very moment; casting off one body to receive another, you cycle through illusory existence.

If you can realize it here and now, karmic obstructions as massive as mountains will be shattered into a hundred fragments by a single blow. True nature is like the ocean; with a moment’s reflection, all conditions vanish."
Empty. Should this not yet be so, listen again to the verse of an ancient Buddha: "By borrowing the four elements, a body is formed; The mind is originally unborn, arising only because of objects.
If the external object is absent, the mind is likewise non-existent; Sin and merit are like illusions—they arise and then perish.
Since it is thus, how do you speak the single phrase upon leaving the gate? Pointing with his staff, he said: "A fragrant breeze from the south."
"Come. Let us return to the forest.
Master Yuansou Duan lit the funeral pyre for the lay attendants. "It is not the wind that moves; it is not the banner that moves.
This is the phrase by which Layman Lu cut off people's tongues; it is like a great mass of fire—approaching it, one is...
The face-gate is incinerated.
Chan Master Gaofeng Miao acted as the fire-attendant for Zhizu; while alive there was insufficiency, yet in death there is abundance.
As the ashes fly and the smoke vanishes, the entire body is revealed. If it is simply thus, what restriction is there? In the blazing heat of the sixth month, there is but a single furnace of fire.
To clarify the Way for people, I shall speak only of this one point: from ancient times to the present, there has been no transmission of it.
Only those who clearly understand the Way can preserve it from beginning to end; like an iron ox performing somersaults amidst the flames.
Chan Master Wuyong Kuan performed the cremation for the Daoist Cishan. Breaking through the "deadly barrier," his entire being was filled with exhilaration.
Letting out a roar, he cast fire beyond the kalpa of Wei-yin, saying: "Fire breaks out on the mountain peak; one stroke wins two prizes."
For the sake of compassion, he kindles the fire of the pure person; the fire beneath the waters blazes up and consumes the void. The great earth, mountains, and rivers are but a single dream;
thus, before the trigger is pulled, one attains liberation of the body. A stone tiger on the southern mountain bites the clear wind.
On behalf of the Wang family’s Daoist nun Ci, the elder sister-in-law of the Wang family from the eastern village went to Huzhou to purchase a bamboo basket. She hurried home in great haste;
upon waking, she was unaware of what had transpired. Throwing down the fire, she said, "It has been burned."
Chan Master Zhuo’an performs the cremation for the laywoman Xingzhu. A mani-jewel long buried has today begun to shine with brilliant light, piercing through the vast void.
Even the icy river erupts in flames. Whether she attains realization or not, let us enter the red furnace once more to undergo further smelting and refinement.
Chan Master Gaofeng Miao forged the bones of the lay attendant Zhizang. The entire Great Canon of the Teachings is fire;
if one possesses the numinous bones of Lingnan, one may well shoulder this burden naked. Nevertheless, one must enter the red furnace once more to undergo further smelting.

Master Gumeng You performed the enshrinement for the practitioner Rong Dao. As the ashes flew across the great wilds and the skeletal remains returned to the mountain, a single "pop" resounded from the earth;
only then did he reach the secure barrier. For the practitioner Rong Dao, this single point of numinous light is neither internal nor external:
the stupa is empty, locked in the idleness of white clouds.
Chan Master Shiyufang, acting as a thunderclap for the Dharma, escorted his mother Jingyuan into the stupa. White clouds leave no trace; green waters have their source.
Both abide nowhere—so who is Jingyuan? Those who understand it: male and female forms alike return to An-yang. Those who do not understand:
they merely seek temporary peace within the seamless stupa. But tell me, what is this seamless stupa like?
Seeking comfort in negligence: Last night the flower branches fell away entirely; at dawn, as before, the north wind is cold.
Master Wuyong Kuan performed the bone-scattering rite for the practitioner Ciqing: "In life and in death, who can distinguish them?
The skeletal joints emit light that shines upon the crown of the head. Scattered into the vast waves and deep waters, it is as if they had never existed from the start."
Chan Master Zhuo’an was asked by the layman Wu Baihán to perform the ritual of "pointing to the title" for his late mother-in-law.
The Master took up his brush and said, "Does the assembly understand? This is the uninterrupted life-blood of all Buddhas and Patriarchs from antiquity;
all beings among heaven and humanity receive this power of grace. Today, on behalf of the late Lady Jiang, mother of Mr. Wu, we perform this rite before the altar."

He points [to the incense burner], causing all present—sons and grandsons alike—to know their own origins. May this entire assembly together penetrate that great matter, never before seen or heard, wherein all traces of the extraordinary are severed.
He then points to the main [incense burner] and says: "A single leaf of blossoming flowers fills the golden realm;
ten thousand mountains of clouds bow toward the jade pavilion."
Preface to the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* Assembly (Prior to the Summer Retreat).
Chan Master Cheng of Jingyin ascended the hall for the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* assembly. Holding up his staff, he said: "The fundamental nature is pure and still;
how is it that mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? Look, look! Pūrṇa has passed right through the nostrils of Old Śākyamuni. Śākyamuni...
Kālacitta has pierced through the belly of empty space. Tell me, where are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth?
Throwing down his staff, he called to the assembly, saying: "Empty space performs a somersault and departs for the kingdom of Silla.
You all must take care not to mistake leaves for a crying child, nor seek the sword by marking the boat."
Chan Master Longxiang Gui ascended the hall for the assembly. "When one perceives that which is perceived, that perception is not true seeing.

Even seeing is already detached from seeing; it cannot reach it. The falling flower has the intention to follow the flowing water, yet the flowing water has no sentiment to cherish the falling flower.
All things that can be returned to their source are naturally not you. That which cannot be returned to its source—what is it if not you? One harbors long resentment that spring departs without..."
He searched for his whereabouts, not knowing that he had entered into this [state]. He let out a shout and said:
"Thirty years from now, do not say that Nengren has ruined people's sons and daughters."
Chan Master Xiang of Jingci ascended the hall for the inauguration ceremony. An ancient said, "When a single film obscures the eye, empty flowers fall in confusion.
Holding up his staff, he said: "Jingci raises this staff—is this not 'a single film obscuring the eye'?
Within the tip of this staff, the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas all manifest bodies sixteen feet tall, of purple-gold hue, traveling through their lands."
Traversing the ten directions and preaching all dharmas to deliver all sentient beings—is this not like the chaotic falling of flowers from the sky?
Right now, is there anyone who can cut it off while the staff has not yet been lifted? Come forth and meet with Jingci!
As for "non-existence," one must by all means avoid falling into the trap of regarding emptiness as the original absence of flowers or the eye as originally free from cataracts.
[The Master] suddenly threw down his staff and descended from the seat. *Liejuzu Tigang Lu*, Volume 35.

*Jiejia* (Retreat Schedule) for the Establishment of the Retreat.
Chan Master Jiao of Langye ascended the hall at the commencement of the summer retreat and said:
"All of you who are here spending the summer, I shall point out five kinds of illnesses for you. First, do not go to a place where there is not a single blade of grass ten thousand miles away.
Second, do not stay alone on a solitary peak. Third, do not draw bows and set arrows. Fourth, do not seek refuge beyond all phenomena. Fifth, do not..."
Stuck between life and death. Why? If one is obstructed in a single place, it is difficult even to save oneself;

if one is unimpeded in all five places, only then may one be called a true guide. You people, if you travel to various regions and encounter those with clear vision who act as creators, convey this message to them so that the ancestral wind does not fall into ruin.
If you are merely ordinary practitioners, then cease your journey. Why? Because of the country of Huanxing (Ankle-Shaped).
"Pretentious in their clothing and ornaments; I suspect you are utterly ignorant of the times.

Master Yunju You addressed the assembly at the commencement of the summer retreat: "Within the light of formlessness, there is a True Person of No Rank who appears and disappears within the three realms and wanders through the five paths.
He does not abandon the ten evil deeds, nor does he fall into the body of the five aggregates, nor does he eliminate affliction."
Afflictions are obstacles; one does not realize nirvana. One does not harbor hatred toward those who violate the precepts, nor does one fail to respect those who uphold them.
Not passing through winter and not exceeding summer—do you all know where these go? After a long silence, he said: "Within the ninety-day mirage, the fivefold Dharma-body is perfected."
Cenyan Daowei Chan Master, at the commencement of the summer retreat, said: "The beginning of the *anju* (summer retreat) is named 'forbidding the feet.
The intent behind forbidding the feet lies in advancing on the Path and protecting living beings. But for us patch-robed monks, what living being is there to protect?
What Path is there to advance upon? Spit! With one spit, I spit across the face of Old Śākyamuni. Take a step! With one step, I tread upon Old Śākyamuni."
Zi Jigū: You are still just one who follows along and keeps pace with the crowd; you have not yet become a monk of the true portion. What is a monk of the true portion?
With boundless elegance, he is too weary to put it on display, so as to avoid being pointed out by others as a "fine young master."
Chan Master Zhenjing Wen ascended the hall at Dongshan for the Summer Retreat. "The ten directions assemble; once every three months we enter retreat.

This is to stifle the mind of arrogance and delusion, to eliminate the heat of suffering and affliction, to attain supreme coolness, and to realize great nirvana. Reaching the shore of *pāramitā*, one leaves the tracks of birth and death.
It is because of this sacred regulation that [this practice] is not established in vain. Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas neither see nor hear of it. Three...
The Buddhas of the world can only know this for themselves; even Zen monks cannot leap out of it.

To be caught within its intricate patterns is to urinate on one’s bed upon opening one’s eyes, or to speak dreams within a dream. For now, seek a way to live for ninety days under the gate of Dongshan.
Ascending the hall: Today marks the beginning of summer, the morning when the monastic community enters the retreat.

The Bhikṣu Kewen of Lestan Mountain, together with this pure assembly, mounts the Bodhisattva vehicle and cultivates the practice of quiescent extinction. We take Great Perfect Enlightenment as our monastery.

The body and mind abide in peace at the fundamental limit of equality. Because the self-nature of *nirvāṇa* is without attachment, I now respectfully request that you do not follow the way of the *śrāvakas*, but rather enter the three-month *varṣā* retreat together with the Tathāgatas of the ten directions and the great Bodhisattvas.

For the sake of cultivating the great causal conditions for the unsurpassed, wondrous enlightenment of a Bodhisattva, may you maintain pure *brahmacarya*, free from all defilements. If you are able to...
It is so. It is as the lotus flower is not defiled by water; the purity of mind transcends that.
Chan Master Wumen Yan, while observing the summer retreat at Sishen, ascended the hall and said: "In observing the summer retreat, I have nothing with which to make offerings to the Great Assembly."
Acting as the host for a family banquet, he looked after everyone. He then raised his hand and said: "Luo-luo-zhao, Luo-luo-yao, Luo-luo-song.
Do not take my lack of refinement as an offense. I humbly pray that you all will cherish yourselves."
The Summer Retreat at Haihui: Ascending the Hall. This summer I dwell at Baiyun; Zen practitioners have gathered by chance.
During these three months of ninety days, those of high and low status rely upon one another. Whether the rice porridge and tea are fine or coarse, we endure them according to our lot.
Following our inclinations, we study the scriptures; as we practice, we cultivate samādhi. We who are all children of the renunciant life—let us simply let our bellies grow large!
Ascending the hall at the commencement of the summer retreat: The early summer heat gradually increases; I humbly wish that the Head Seat and the assembly are enjoying ten thousand blessings.
It is as if peach blossoms amidst bamboo—flowers upon a brocade, flowers everywhere. Do not let your eyes wander. This is the annual custom; there is no need for formal inspection.
Upon descending from the seat, the assembly shall pay their respects and tea will be served throughout the quarters.
Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin ascended the hall for the summer retreat: "Transcending the ten stages without passing through kalpas; things and self as one, body and mind in equality.
Not taking companionship with the myriad dharmas, not treading the same path as the thousand sages.

Vividly, the constant radiance manifests before you; everywhere, it stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high. Even if you could penetrate beyond the time of Wei-yin, you would still be this [person]."

These are matters of the phenomenal side. When principle follows the transformation of phenomena to respond to things and adapt to capacities—whether manifesting the ten kinds of *parabhogakāya*, or appearing as three feet or one zhang and six chi;

whether at times gazing toward the clouds from the peak of a solitary mountain, or at other times traversing shallow grass and level fields in horizontal and vertical strides—all these are likewise matters of this side. It is just like [the case of] not moving a single step, yet...
Expansive as the entire realm of sand-grains, he is one who pervades the ten voids without giving rise to a single thought.
Tell me, does he still observe the summer retreat for the ninety days and three months? "The clouds atop the ridge peak have no leisure; the water flowing down the ravine is far too busy."
Ascending the hall at the commencement of the summer retreat: A single mote of dust contains the boundless Dharma-realm; yet, if one examines it closely, there is still room for deficiency.

Within every billion hairs, a lion appears; within every billion hairs, they manifest all at once. Even if one were to weigh and measure this with earnestness, it would not yet be the talk of the ultimate limit.
If we speak of the fundamental matter: the great person possesses great vision, and great wisdom attains great function. Suppose...
Even if one were to exhaust the boundless seas of fragrant water and traverse unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds, it would all still be merely one’s own place of dwelling.

"How does one enter the gate of the Prajñāpāramitā? [The Master] raises his whisk and says, "A mirror.
Master Chan Master Ruo’an addresses the assembly at the commencement of the summer retreat: "Everyone suffers from the sweltering heat; I love the lengthening days of summer.

A fragrant breeze comes from the south, bringing a subtle coolness to the halls and pavilions. After a long pause, he says, "Everyone is right here," and suddenly strikes the meditation seat with his hand.
The Seat. One must believe that within the vast expanse of misty waves, there is naturally something else to be considered.
Ascending the seat for the Summer Retreat: this is a ready-made koan, utterly free from error. Dropping off the shoulder-bag, the Great Matter is already accomplished.
The Buddhas and Patriarchs could not speak of it; today I speak of it. The Buddhas and Patriarchs could not practice it; today I practice it.
It reaches the point where Deshan’s shouts are like thunder and Linji’s staffs fall like raindrops;
even here, one must retreat three paces. The Ten Sages and Three Worthies are at a loss; the wild foxes peer about but find no way in. If you step with a false foot, you will be caught.
If you see that a single brick remains eternally constant, you will immediately perceive its two halves as distinct.

How much more so when comparing the ancient with the modern, praising the long while disparaging the short, stirring up rumors of right and wrong to delude the men and women of this house? Whether one’s allotted time is long or short, whether one is on this side or that, it is merely a waste of straw sandals and a squandering of years and months.
When you stand before Old Yan at a later time, he will strike the backside of your ghostly bones. Now tell me: [what will you say?]
Who is it that can inherit this? Twenty years ago, while wandering by waterside and beneath the trees, I encountered a faceless old man.
Not even a single drop of water ever touched him. Today, before this assembly of devas and humans, I dare to speak out on behalf of this old man.
Our paths as kinsmen have converged; pressed in by you venerable elders, you demand that I [speak].
"I am observing the summer retreat for the sake of the assembly. Let us set aside the matter of the retreat for a moment: where will you place this mountain monk’s staff? Do not move it;
if you move it, your head will split and your brain will burst. He planted his staff in the ground and said, "This is my formal announcement."
The Master ascends the hall for the opening of the retreat and says: "Forcing the monkey up the tree; painting a tiger that turns out to be a wildcat.

Peeling the finest lychees; striving for cleverness only to end up clumsy. 'Today is the third,' 'Tomorrow is the fourth'—branch upon branch sprouting. Biting through the head-phrase until the nostrils are torn apart.
On level ground, one falls into pits that trap the men and women of the household. Even if you were to realize it before the word is even raised—"
You are still people standing on the ground who have died; brothers, fortunately do not become such creatures.
How do you speak that single, direct phrase right before the light? Autumn wind and autumn rain chill the bones; with rotting leaves piled like clouds, simply close the door.
The Opening of the Retreat: An Address to the Assembly. Whether speaking in curves or straight lines, in the dust or across the lands, the teaching of the three periods of time occurs all at once.

Yet the tongue does not leave the mouth. Here, clear-eyed monks must join hands together; this is for the sake of ensuring that the ancestral style does not fall and that the teacher’s dharma has a firm foundation.
If you merely follow old paths and guard against tracks, how could you avoid burying your entire life? As the ninety-day period begins, the Sage...
When the regulation was first established, those who struck the head did not encounter a true master; by the end, it had turned into nothing but antiquities.
If you wish to avoid falling into this trap, a single phrase transcends hundreds of billions: in the sixth month, the Yellow River freezes through to its very bottom.
Ascending the hall for the commencement of the retreat: A single dharma is not existent; the myriad dharmas are not non-existent.

We do not speak of the Tathāgata’s Chan; we do not clarify the Master’s intent. Guest is guest and host is host; ritual is ritual and music is music. Spring wind fills one’s face as it splashes across the painted railings;
the deep locks of the Brahmā King’s palace are opened. Even those who sit and enjoy the Great Peace cannot do without you.

"Grasping above and lifting below is the very bottom; one cannot do without it even slightly. Within this, should there be any half-acceptance or half-rejection, I, this mountain monk, simply let it pass.
Clouds emerge from the mountain peaks without intent; water fills its hollows and flows on.
It must stop when it encounters a high mountain, and only rest when it reaches the great ocean. He struck the meditation staff once and said: "Long periods and short limits are all entirely..."
A matter of leisure. One must cause every person to reach the ultimate end.
On the occasion of the opening of the retreat, the assembly ascends the hall: Lingyun saw the peach blossoms and fell into a pit; Xiangyan heard the bamboo strike and rode upon the echo in the void.
This ready-made field allows for movement in all directions; in a wasteland of ten-thousand-rod fields, one does not weed the grass, but simply picks it up with the hand as it comes.
"Come here! Now tell me, what is this? When the sky is clear the sun shines; when it rains the ground becomes wet.

The spring mountains are layered with chaotic greens; the spring waters overturn the azure void. 'Since you have not yet returned, you shall return as soon as you can. It cannot be seen, nor can it be heard.
If you hesitate for even a moment, I shall strike you across the spine. At this time, if you do not investigate the source, you must wait until the future to ask Maitreya."
Chan Master Lin Gao Preaches Upon Entering Retreat: This year’s summer retreat is no ordinary one. Firewood fills the stacks, and wheat fills the granaries.
Take heed, you guests from the five lakes and the waters: Gently wave the *pú*-fan, and you shall have sufficient cool breeze. (He lets out a shout.)
Master Mùyúnmén ascended the hall for the summer retreat. "Tiantong, as we enter the summer retreat, our straw sandals are hung high.
There is no interior and no exterior; there is no high and no low. Taking Great Perfect Enlightenment as my monastery, body and mind dwell in peace within the Wisdom of Equality.
O Assembly! If you take Great Perfect Enlightenment as your monastery, then there are ten billion Mount Sumerus and ten billion suns and moons."
From the ten billion sets of four continents, up to the entirety of the Flower Treasury World and its boundless seas of fragrant water, none can pass the threshold of the Celestial Youth’s gate.
Body and mind dwell in tranquility within the Wisdom of Equality; one simply eats when hungry and sleeps when weary.
When walking, one merely walks; when sitting, one merely sits. Awakening and affliction, birth-and-death and nirvana, wisdom and ignorance—[are all one].
The Buddha-nature of the suchness of delusion—when you are at the heels of a person, there is absolutely no need to stir it. At this very moment, how is it?
A yellow oriole sings in the green trees; listen well to the mystery within. Descend from the seat.
Chan Master Hongjue Wen ascended the hall for the opening of the retreat. Raising his staff, he said: "Look, look!
Upon the tip of this mountain monk’s staff, precious buddha-lands are opened wide, gathering all the various schools.
From among them, Vairocana Tathāgata has been invited to serve as the Hall Head (Dharmasvāmin), Śikhin Tathāgata as the Chief Administrative Officer (Karmadāna), and Śākyamuni Tathāgata as..."
As for the presiding master: Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva was the head seat; Maitreya Bodhisattva was the *karmadāna*;
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva was the secretary; Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva was the vice-abbot; and Samantabhadra Bodhisattva was the steward.
Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja was the Librarian; Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata was the Guest Master;
Bodhisattva Anantagātra was the Steward; Bodhisattva Śāntendriya was the Chamberlain; Bodhisattva Sūradatta was the Bath Attendant; Bodhisattva Prajñottara was the Personal Attendant;
Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita was the Head of the Quarters; and Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha was the Hall Master. Śubha... [text continues]

The Bodhisattva Cai served as the leader of the assembly. Together with all beings throughout the ten directions and three periods of time, exhausting the entirety of the dharma-realm—whether ordinary or sagely—they all universally entered the monastery of Perfect Enlightenment (*pariniṣpanna-avabodha*).
Each dwelt in peace within the wisdom of the equality of natures (*samatā-jñāna*).
Thereupon, the Tathāgata Vairocana expounded the Dharma for the multitude, saying: "To protect life, one must kill; only when killing is exhausted..."
During the summer retreat, he finally grasped the meaning within this: "An iron boat floats upon the water. Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva presided over the whisk for a small-scale *can* (sermon), saying:
"The ten directions gather together; each and every one studies non-action (*wuwei*). This is the field for selecting Buddhas;

with an empty mind, one returns having passed the imperial examination. He then called out, "Great assembly! If you can thus believe and understand it thoroughly, then right now I shall grant you [the seal of certification]."
The various sages have participated together. In the future, you shall succeed him as the Great Preceptor (Upādhyāya) to Vairocana Tathāgata.
Should you still linger in observation and listening, even slightly indulging in hesitation, then each person will remain merely a person, and this staff will remain merely a staff.
As it is, the distance from the Sage remains vast, and the True Dharma is on the verge of extinction; within these ninety days, you must most urgently apply yourself with diligence.
Excellent! Long standing, take care.
On the occasion of the summer retreat, Master Chan Master Tiandong Qi ascended the hall and said:

"Twenty years ago, on a certain day, I casually gathered the life-force of all sentient beings within the three thousand great thousandfold world-system and contained it within a single minute speck of dust."
Not a single person among them knew of it. This is what is called "hiding a mountain in the sea" or "hiding a boat in a ravine.
At midnight, a strong man carries it away, yet those who sleep do not perceive it. Today, this mountain monk proclaims this to the great assembly: can you believe it?
If you can believe it and see it through, then you may well rest and cease from striving. If you cannot believe it and do not see it...
Chè: "It does not hinder morning attendance or evening attendance. Once you have attended until there is no place to attend, you will look around left and right and say:
'Only then do I know that there is nowhere that is not my home mountain.'"
