Volume Thirty-Six and Volume Thirty-Seven.
Compiled by Xingyue of Loudong, Abbot of Lian’an Chan Temple at the Eighteen Streams in Wulin.
The Essential Outline of the Central Lands:
Chan Master Oukan Ti. Ascending the hall in the Central Lands: The blazing sun of the midsummer heavens; Empty space recklessly proclaims new Zen.
With ears to hear, it would be difficult to listen to this as it blows in the wind; Not falling into various conditions, it is transmitted at random. Do not ask about the East.
To the west, he sits firmly atop the peak of Mount Miaogao; let there be no distinction between self and other. He devours the heads of both *nirmāṇakāya* and *saṃbhogakāya* Buddhas whole;

when cold, he feels no concern for the cold, for form and emptiness are non-dual. When hot, he feels no concern for the heat, for mind and object are as one. This Great Chan Buddha treats others as if they do not exist.

The wandering monk makes his body a lodging-house for travelers; the old bhikṣu who has extinguished his mind cannot avoid knitting his brows. Even Vimalakīrti, who kept his mouth shut, must have let out a cold laugh.
But tell me, what was he laughing at? Where there is intentionality, every application is an error; when one looks without intent, it is perfectly as it is.
Chan Master Xueyan Qin ascended the hall for the summer retreat. He said: "The forty-five days that have already passed are gone;
the forty-five days yet to come are still in the future. He struck his staff and said: "Right now, on this very day, tell me:
do the characteristics of past and future still exist? Furthermore, is there even a single hair’s breadth of a characteristic that neither goes nor comes?"
There is none. If you can settle your mind within this, you will attain certainty. At the fifth watch, one washes the face; at dusk, one sleeps.
When it is announced that there is a meal at noon and gruel in the morning, day after day is the same and evening after evening is identical.

If this is not yet so, Baoen has already prepared for the midsummer retreat yesterday; today, the drum is struck and we ascend the hall, as the Prefectural Office welcomes and honors Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
The assembly hall was prepared for offerings, and a ritual site for praying for clear weather was inaugurated.
During the first forty-five days of midsummer, one knows how to advance but not how to retreat; during the latter forty-five days, one knows how to retreat but not how to advance.
On this very day, both advancing and retreating are forgotten. In the extreme heat of late summer, the warm breeze brings its own coolness.
Zhuo leaned on his staff and said: "At that moment, one hears the fragrance of a cluster of lotus flowers.
Chan Master Gaofeng Miao ascended the hall during the summer retreat and said: "Where did you go during the first forty-five days? A tawny tiger enters the bustling marketplace.
Where will you come from during the latter forty-five days? A three-legged donkey mounts a high platform. He was brilliant.
A hawk or a swift falcon ought to seize the moment; a lame tortoise and a blind turtle labor in vain with their leaping and jumping.
Entering the hall in Central China, he held up his whisk and addressed the assembly, saying:
"At this point, you cannot take even one step forward, nor can you take even one step back. It is also not permissible to do neither. Ultimately, what is it? No.
"Attainment and non-attainment.
Master Zhongfeng Ben addressed the assembly during the summer retreat: "O Great Assembly! Forty-five days prior, in the morning one was drowsy and in the evening distracted;
forty-five days later, in the morning one is distracted and in the evening drowsy. Right now, on this very day, it falls within these forty..."
Within these five days, try bringing forth your dullness and distraction for this old monk to see.

Since there is no place for you to bring them forth, then even such things as True Suchness, Bodhi, Nirvana, and Liberation have no place for you to bring forth. Do not say that you cannot bring them forth;
even if one were to summon the Old Man Śākyamuni from two thousand years ago out of the Great Samādhi of Quiescence, [there would still be nothing to bring forth].
I dare say there is no principle by which it could be brought forth. Since it cannot be brought forth, what do you call "dullness and distraction"?

And what do you call "quiescent illumination"? At this very moment, when the sentiments of sage and ordinary are exhausted and the obstructions of subject and object are emptied, one is directly without dependence and, in the immediacy of the occasion, beyond all relativity.
One does not see the forty-five days as being before; one does not see the forty-five days as being behind.
Afterwards, the three periods of time are equalized in a single path of empty stillness; even now, if you try to find this "Middle Kingdom," it cannot be found.
Nevertheless, this is still merely a matter of being on the road. As for the news of arriving home, it is still a hundred thousand leagues away from the Western Heaven.
O practitioners of Zen, when you first resolved your will, you intended to address the great matter of birth and death; it was not something that could be settled by mere words.
Stop! You must arouse a resolute spirit that disregards both life and death.

Whether you are forty-five years old now, or forty-five years hence, or exactly forty-five years old, or not forty-five—regardless of whether you are right or wrong, long or short—raise up the koan with explosive intensity, even if it means being utterly blind to everything else.
Blindly striking and enduring—no one cares whether in this life you strike through thoroughly or not.

Even if one were driven upon the mountain of knives and trees of swords by a wheel of glowing iron, circling it hundreds of thousands of millions of times in a single day, one could never be made to let go of the kōan one is investigating for even a moment.
Possessing such resolve, one desires to surpass the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
It is not difficult. That we have failed to reach the level of the ancients in the past was simply because our aspirations were not sincere and our footing was not firm.
Thus the ancients said: "To cross a river one must use a raft; to study the Way one must use a resolve.
Śākyamuni and Maitreya initially had no special talents; they were merely ordinary people capable of establishing their vows. Once there was a monk...
He asked an ancient worthy, "If not a single thought arises for even a moment, is there still any fault? The worthy replied, "Mount Sumeru.
Now tell me, how far apart is this from Zhaozhou’s "A monk's robe from Qingzhou"?
If you do not yet understand, come back forty-five days from now and reveal a message.

Master Chan Wansong Wei addressed the assembly during the summer retreat: "Bodhidharma came from the West specifically to point directly to the human mind, so that one may see one's nature and attain Buddhahood.
But tell me, what is this 'nature'? With a single shout, right here and now, let the mass of doubt shatter into a hundred pieces."
Behold: the lush green bamboo reveals True Suchness; the green willows and red flowers manifest pure clarity. The wind rises and the tiger roars; the stone dragon sighs;
the swallows chatter and the orioles sing—these resolve your doubts for you. The monk’s life is lively and vibrant; from his full breast he casts forth the night-bright pearl.
Even the treasure-offering Persian merchant would find it difficult to discern. He lays down his robes and goes to sleep; let Heaven do as it will.
The earth may collapse or split apart, yet this [truth] shall not fail to be so. *Zan*.
Master Chan Shi Qi addressed the assembly on the first day of summer retreat: "The forty-five days that have already passed are gone;
the forty-five days yet to come have not arrived. Right in the midst of these forty-five days, the present moment cannot be found."
Therefore it is said: "The past mind cannot be apprehended; the present mind cannot be apprehended; the future mind cannot be apprehended.
This non-apprehension itself cannot be apprehended. One pours out one's liver and gall toward others throughout life, yet those who know one are as if they did not know one at all.
Master Gumengyou ascended the hall during the summer retreat: "The ninety-day period for restraining the feet has already passed its halfway mark.
If you have not yet clarified the ground of your mind, it is like pulling a fire-drill—do not let this time go to waste. Settle these idle cases;
to catch a thief on level ground without cause—the old monk comes forth to settle them for you."
To illustrate this, Master Zhongxia ascended the hall and gave a discourse. He cited the case where Linji went up the mountain during the midsummer retreat to pay his respects to Huangbo.
Seeing Huangbo reading a scripture, Linji said, "I thought you were a man of realization; it turns out you are just an old monk who chants 'Oṃ' like a black bean.
After staying for several days, Linji took his leave. Huangbo said, "You arrived after the summer retreat was already underway; why did you not stay for the full duration?"

"Go! Go! I have come for a moment to pay my respects. Huangbo then struck him and sent him away. After traveling several *li*, Nanquan Jie felt doubt about the matter and returned once more to spend the remainder of the summer there.
The Master [Zongmi] commented: "He would not come when summoned; he would not leave when driven away. What kind of person is this?
If Ruiyan had been in Huangbo’s place, when Nanquan returned again, even if his staff were broken, he would not have let him go. Why? Because the truth cannot be achieved upon the staff.

Master Wencan of Longmen ascended the hall during the first half of the summer retreat. Regarding the Dharma-gates practiced and the vows cultivated during this first half of the summer, I, the mountain monk, have already expounded them for you all while at West Mountain.
As for the Dharma-gates to be practiced and the [vows] to be cultivated during the second half of the summer...
Regarding practice and vows: I, this mountain monk, am now at East Lake expounding them for you all. What is practiced at East Lake differs from the West Mountain;

yet what is preached at the West Mountain is no different from that of East Lake. It is like pointing at a locust tree to scold a willow, or taking a tortoise as evidence to prove it is a soft-shelled turtle.
Koṭivimśa would prick up his ears to listen, while the spirit Śūnyatā would be so startled that he sticks out his tongue.
Chan Master Liaohan Yu addressed the assembly on the occasion of Midsummer: "The first half of summer has already passed; the second half of summer has not yet arrived.
Right now, at this very moment, it is called 'midsummer. O Great Assembly, the past is gone and the future has not yet come—how is it with the present matter?
Is it that one should not stand upon either of the two extremes, and need not settle upon the Middle Way? Such talk as this—"
This is the leftover soup and stale rice you have already chewed up. Why is it that when pressed, ten out of every five or six find the nose-string in another’s hand?
Tell me, where does the point of danger lie? A single film over the eye;
empty flowers falling in confusion.
The Outline for the Construction of the *Ullambana* Assembly, by Chan Master Shiyu Fang.
Entering the Hall for the *Ullambana* Assembly: Today is the day when Maudgalyāyana rescued his mother and the Earth Deity pardoned transgressions.
Gathered here to repent, the deceased may transcend to rebirth, and the living may obtain blessings.
These are the parents of this world. Yet, in the supramundane realm as well, each person likewise has their own parents;
they can nurture your Dharma-body and sustain your life of wisdom. Great assembly, do you know them?

These parents cannot be sought through physical form, nor can they be seen through distance or proximity, nor will they respond to being called out. Nevertheless, among you there are those whose parents are both present.
Among those in mourning, there are also those whose parents are both still living. Tell me, how does one perform repentance so that they may attain transcendence?
How does one provide protection so that they may obtain blessings? Is there anyone who can give a definitive answer? [The Master] strikes the meditation seat once and descends from it.
Unfurling the Main Pillar at the Conclusion of the Retreat:

Chan Master Jia of Dongshan addresses the assembly. "Brothers, as the early autumn approaches and the summer retreat ends, whether you go east or west, you must head toward a place ten thousand *li* away where there is not even an inch of grass before you will succeed.
He further said, "As for that very place ten thousand *li* away where there is not an inch of grass—"
"How shall one go?
Thus spoke Chan Master Shishuang Quan, upon ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat (*varṣā*). "Yesterday you were an infant; today your years are already old.

Failing to understand the 'three eights and nine,' it is difficult to tread the path of the Ancient Sovereign. With hands blazing, the Yellow River is dried up; with feet kicking, Mount Sumeru is overturned. Floating...
One is born with a body like a dream or an illusion; human life is difficult to preserve even for a single evening. Both heaven and hell are created by the mind alone.

The pines on the southern mountains and northern ridges, and the grasses on the northern ridges and southern mountains—moistened by a single rain, their roots and sprouts flourish while others remain withered.
The seekers from the Five Lakes merely ask the empty sky for answers. When dying, one sheds the summer shirt; when born, one dons the winter robe. To distinguish them...
"A man of no affairs gives rise to afflictions out of nowhere. With a shout, he descended from his seat.

Master Yunfeng Yue held a formal assembly upon the conclusion of the summer retreat. "The sun and moon flow on; time passes in an instant. We have just seen the commencement of the *an-gu* (summer retreat), and now it is time for the *zi-zi* (self-examination).
This summer, I am glad that the members of the great assembly have each maintained their physical well-being. However, having left the household life..."
This kind of person is expansive, unimpeded, and free from attachment. At the end of summer or the beginning of autumn, they may go east or west, leaving one grove of trees and entering another.
Suddenly, someone might ask the Elder, "How did Master Cuoyan guide others this summer?"
When confronted with such a question, how could one possibly respond? Do not say, "Nine times nine is eighty-one.
Do not say, "Once the snow has melted, spring will naturally arrive. Do not say, "The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night. Do not say, "Shut that dog's mouth!
Do not say, "Let out a shout, give a slap, strike the meditation seat across the mouth, or shake the whisk and depart immediately. None of these will suffice.
"Zen Master, you have gone so far as to expose yourself by visiting Cuiyan. Since that is not the case, how else would you reveal it?
Try saying something before this assembly; is there anyone who can speak? The assembly remained silent. The Master said, "If you go to other places..."
"Do not say that I have come from Cuiyan," and he immediately descended from his seat.

Chan Master Da Jue Lian ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: "The autumn wind rises; the courtyard paulownia leaves fall. The patch-robed disciples scramble about, looking for auspicious omens.
Zhang San and Li Si peddle nothing but clamor and dust. Shi De and Han Shan vie with one another over cheapness and value. Meeting face-to-face..."

There is no difficulty or ease here. Amidst the stalls, railings, and tiled markets of the four-way crossroads, filling the void of space and covering heaven and earth—this is Linji’s bare flesh-ball;
Xuefeng’s South Mountain turtle-nosed snake; Xuansha seeing the tiger; and Juzhi pointing his finger.
All are brought forth at once and bestowed right before your face. If you hesitate even for a moment, there are a thousand mountains and ten thousand waters. He said again: "Pass!"
Cenian Master Baiyun, upon concluding the summer retreat, cited Chan Master Dongshan Wuben, who said:

"At the beginning of autumn and the end of summer, you must go to a place ten thousand miles away where there is not a single blade of grass. A monk recounted this to the Hermitage Master of Liuyang, who said:
"As soon as you step out the door, it is all grass. The Master [Baiyun] said: "If you can see the Hermitage Master, you will see Dongshan; if you can see Dongshan..."
Shan saw through the abbot immediately; it was easier for him to see Dongshan than it was to see the abbot.

It was because he did not allow himself to be bound by the constraints of serving as an abbot. As it is said: "The clouds at the mountain peak have no leisure; the water flowing down the ravine is too busy."
Chan Master Baoning Yong ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: "The autumn wind has just stirred, and the sack’s mouth is opened.
Those who come do so of their own accord; those who leave do so of their own accord. Jianghuai and Liangzhe possess a full measure of family style; Hengyue and Lufeng offer even more secluded charm.
Amidst this bustling toil, this ceaseless wandering, and this constant drifting, you must know that the Immovable Tathāgata has never taken a single step."
Furthermore, tell me: how do you express the phrase "without moving a step"? After a long silence, he said: "Just now I came from the hall;
now I am returning to the hall.
Chan Master Changqing An, at the conclusion of the summer retreat, ascended the hall and said: "What is it that all of you have come to seek from An?"
If you wish to become a Buddha, you are yourself already a Buddha. Yet you carry this "Buddha" about as you run from house to house, like a thirsty deer chasing a mirage;

when will you ever attain true correspondence with reality? If you wish to become a Buddha, simply be free from these many inverted attachments, delusive thoughts, and evil perceptions—the defiled and pure mind of a sentient being—and you are immediately the Primordially Enlightened Buddha. Where else would you need to go?
A separate discussion. This is why I have lived at Mount Mui for thirty years, eating Mount Mui’s rice and defecating Mount Mui’s excrement, yet not studying Mount Mui’s Zen;
I have simply watched a water buffalo. Whenever it falls deeply into the grass, I pull its nostrils back;
as soon as it offends the crops, I whip and subdue it. After a long time, this poor creature comes to accept its lot.
People speak of it as such, yet now it has transformed into a white ox in the open air that is always before one’s face.
Day and night it stands exposed and clear; though you try to chase it away, it will not go. Each of you possesses a priceless great treasure:

from the gateway of the eyes, light is emitted, illuminating the mountains, rivers, and the great earth; from the gateway of the ears, light is emitted, perceiving all sounds, whether good or evil. It is like this.
These six gates constantly emit radiance day and night; it is also called the Samādhi of Emitting Light. You yourself do not recognize its grasping:
its shadow resides within the body of the four great elements, supporting it from both within and without so that it does not lean or fall.
It is like a person carrying a heavy burden crossing a single-plank bridge, yet never losing their footing. Tell me, what thing is it that provides such sustaining support?
It is so. For now, not even a hair’s breadth can be seen. Have you not heard the Venerable Master Zhigong say:
"Searching within and without, nothing at all is found; yet the functioning within the realm is entirely present. Take heed!
Chan Master Zhennjingwen ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat and said: "This matter cannot be learned, cannot be taught, and cannot be transmitted;
it must be realized by the person themselves before it can be attained. Once realized, it is vividly present, relaxed and at ease, perfectly clear and bright, distinct and penetrating.
All supernatural powers and transformations are spontaneously complete within it; there is no need for anything external."

Qiu then took up his staff and held it crosswise, saying, "Holding the Mohe sword crosswise, the true command is fully established; throughout the realm of Great Peace, he slays the dull and obstinate.
He then cast the staff down. After a long pause, he let out a shout and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Daomiao Zhe ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat and said: "The ten directions gather together; each and every one studies non-action.

This is the field for selecting Buddhas; with an empty mind, they return as top graduates. Under the guidance of Master Huixian, one is directly uprooted and elevated without passing through the formal stages of examination.
Since you have all arrived here, the winds and clouds are spread across the earth and your fangs and claws are already formed; you merely lack the sound of thunder to set it ablaze.
"Tail! Now, for all of you, I shall strike the thunderbolt! With his staff, he struck the meditation seat and descended from it.

Zen Master Wuzu Yan ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat and said: "When a single speck of dust arises, the whole earth is gathered within it. When a single leaf falls, the entire world knows autumn.
Where the golden wind stirs, it awakens the chirping of crickets by the steps; when the jade dew falls, it draws forth the song of cicadas in the forest."

Chatter fills the air; distant smoke rises from secluded bays as gulls and egrets vie with one another in flight. On sheer cliffs and perilous peaks, monkeys and langurs everywhere compete in their howling.
Furthermore, one sees fishermen raising their oars and woodcutters singing songs; the sound of several pipes from the *qiang* flute accompanies the play of the cowherd boys.
A single sail on the horizon, a solitary traveler’s dream—this can serve to manifest the ancestral way and establish the patriarchal style. Ninety days of practice yield no fruit wasted;
a hundred kalpas find their application in the present moment. When discussed in such a manner, the patch-robed monks knit their brows. Have you not heard it said:
"When not a single speck of dust remains, one has finally returned home; were there even a hair’s breadth remaining, one would not be a member of the family."
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: Three months of ninety days pass in the blink of an eye. Those who are busy are truly busy;
those who are idle are truly idle. In every matter there is no end—ten thousand ages of white clouds upon the mountain.
Ascending the hall: The three-month summer retreat is now complete. How have you fared during these ninety days of restraining the feet? In the West, the wax seal was tested by the sound long ago;
here in this land, those who speak of the goose’s pearl are many. In this degenerate age of two thousand years, distant intentions are mixed like water and milk, accumulating into a river.
May the bodhisattvas of the forests and springs all uphold and protect [the Dharma], ensuring it does not fall into decline or become ensnared by the various demons.
Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat. The autumn light is clear and shallow; the autumn dew is ethereally congealed;

the autumn wind whistles and sighs; the autumn colors are limpid and pure. Thus, Śākyamuni’s work of protecting living beings is complete, and the monastics' method of the *kṣetrasaṃvara* (retreat) is fully perfected.

If you can inwardly forget your own views and outwardly realize the emptiness of phenomena, such that the internal and external are one and the same—ethereal, congealed, and limpid—[you will attain liberation].
In stillness, the entire mind is Buddha, and the entire Buddha is the mind. You walk hand-in-hand with all Buddhas and share the same realization and application as the Patriarchs.
Having reached this point, what more need be said of bondage? What more need be said of liberation?
Throughout the twenty-four hours of the day, you are pure, naked, and radiant; though you wear clothes all day long, not a single thread is ever attached. All day long you eat...
In eating rice, he never bit a single grain. As it is said: "When moving, he is like drifting clouds; when still, he is like the Valley Spirit. How could he have any concern for this or that?
How could there be any image of coming or going? Encountering him everywhere, his entire capacity is uniquely liberated.
At such a time, how is it? "White clouds are originally mindless things; they appear and disappear at will within the great void. He further said: "Nine."

On this day, the ten days' merit is perfected; there is no need to further test the wax figure. Although for ten thousand miles there is not a blade of grass, the mouth of the sack has been untied this morning.

Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: The monastery of Perfect Enlightenment has its doors and windows thrown wide open; the ocean of lands of the Flower Adornment Sūtra faces the central dais.
To condense hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas into a single thought-moment—how could it be limited to the long period of one hundred and twenty days?

To extend a single thought-moment into hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas—what need is there to discuss this life or future lives? Just as we first see the golden metal melting and the stones glowing, suddenly the jade dew falls.

Hanging Pearls: "The seasons do not yield to one another; the nature of things undergoes change and renewal. When the summer retreat (varṣā) is entered, it is entered simultaneously throughout the heavens and across the earth.
When the retreat is concluded, it is concluded simultaneously throughout the heavens and across the earth. At the time of entry, there is originally no mutual attachment."
At the moment of understanding, they are initially not separate. Upon reaching this point, one penetrates a single thread and awakens to a single mechanism.
You act for me, and I act for you; the long remains long and the short remains short; the clear remains clear and the turbid remains turbid.

Within this, there is neither coming nor going, nor is there any shifting or turning. Vast and profoundly balanced, all returns to a single consistency. Only then can one release and gather, seize and let go.
Having attained great liberation, what more can be called "you" or "me," "long" or "short"? All at once it is cut off.
For now, let yourself be free; how would you express this in a single phrase? "The clouds atop the ridge never rest; the water flowing down the ravine is too busy."

Ascending the hall upon the conclusion of the retreat: Usually, there is nothing that surpasses the simple and straightforward; sitting and cutting off all manifold distinctions requires one to raise one’s eyes even higher.

Where the cliff stands ten thousand fathoms high, it is utterly bare and naked; amidst the level fields and shallow grass, it is steep and perilous. To be at ease in that very place is to drag through mud and water;
to probe deeply and strike with painful precision is to risk injury to the hand and wound the blade. If you wish for these two not to obstruct one another, you must act thus.
Each of you, please cease your efforts and put down your fishing lines. Now, how would you express this: "Receiving rewards during the nine months of summer"?
One must never fail to maintain awareness and discernment in dangerous places; even when walking on level ground, one must remain vigilant.
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: At the tip of a single hair, jeweled temples are vast and spacious; ten ages neighbor the void, and past and present are infinitely remote.
Seeing through, one sees nothing; hearing through, one hears nothing. Reaching this point, it is not merely that Sudhana could not perceive for seven days after concentrating his mind;
even if Mañjuśrī were to exert the great power of wisdom and manifest boundless spiritual functions for a hundred kalpas, he still could not catch a glimpse of it. Only...
All of you, for ninety days, each of you shall traverse this entirety.
Emerging and submerging, rolling up and unfolding, extending and contracting, moving east and sinking west—should you suddenly come to know this with perfect certainty, then you shall depart.
It is well not to fail to tread upon the solid ground step by step, and to accord with and realize the ordinary mind in every thought.
If this is not yet so, today the mouth of the bag is opened. Do you understand? After a long silence, he said: "There is no need to say that the clear autumn possesses many superior charms;
lingering and turning back, one simply continues to press down on the clouds."

Chan Master Yuanyuan of Longmen ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat. With a single grain of mustard seed, he struck the cave of the asuras and sat in meditative composure within for ninety days.
Brandishing his six-ringed iron staff, he ascended Mount Sumeru and remained in strict retreat for three months.
Leaning against a tall pine tree, he made his vow; pacing by the green waters, he practiced walking meditation. As he traveled through towns and villages, his every movement was serene and detached.

Residing within the monastic groves, one’s dignified deportment is majestic; what need is there to discuss cities, walls, or villages? One makes no distinction between sacred sites and precious monasteries.
The moon of the mind is solitary and full, the divine pearl is brilliantly radiant. The six sense-gates are empty and still, and all phenomena are as they are.
In such a way of protecting life, what "life" is there to protect? In such a way of upholding the precepts, what "precepts" are there to uphold? A wax seal within a bag...
The person’s entire body is cold as snow; truly worthy of celebration—how great is this joy!
Upon ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: the Seer Viśvāmitra took Sudhana by the hand, and instantly beheld as many Buddhas of the past as there are motes of dust.
When they let go of their grasp, it is exactly as it was before. The Elder of Longmen, leading the great assembly, took up residence here for the summer retreat (*varṣā*).
When the retreat concluded, it was exactly as it was before. Sudhana remained in his original place within the motes of dust; the Buddhas, encompassing all, have their place of return.
The great assembly remained in their original places for three months; for ninety days they gathered and withdrew without a trace. Do you understand?

Within a single hair-tip, oceans of lands are concealed; within a mustard seed, Mount Sumeru is contained. Without departing from the conditions of seeing and hearing, one transcends directly to the ten stages (*bhūmi*).
The four modes of birth and the six realms of existence are the very nature of one’s own mind; the three miserable paths and the eight difficulties everywhere manifest as the form-body (*rūpakāya*).
Abiding in the midst of the Flower Treasury Ocean (*Huazanghai*) and dwelling within the inconceivable, such a principle is indeed the constant lot of our own kind.
"Do you still believe this?
On the occasion of the end of the summer retreat, he ascended the hall, picked up his staff, struck it once, and said: 'Perfect, luminous awareness does not depend on mental thought;
yet to insist on speaking of it is to fall into pits and ravines. After all, how is it? He then leaned his staff against the seat and descended from the platform.

Master Zeyin ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat. The ancients said, "At the beginning of autumn and the end of summer, there ought to be thirty blows of the staff for failing to meet expectations.
Zeyin, however, did not think so. At the assembly on Vulture Peak, the World-Honored One held up a flower and Kāśyapa smiled.
At such a time as this, thirty blows of the staff are well-deserved. Why is this so? Because in times of great peace, one forcibly raises the sword;
yet it is taught that one should blow the Great Dharma Conch and beat the Great Dharma Drum. When taking a step, golden lotuses tread beneath one’s feet;
when sitting upright, the precious steps are majestic and towering. Brahmā leads the way before, surrounded by fragrant flowers, while Śakra follows behind.
Thereafter, dragon-elephants (great masters) thronged together; down to the present day, their descendants have successively imitated one another.
In groups of threes and twos, they all claim to possess extraordinary style and bearing. Wandering from kalpa to kalpa, they refuse to return home to sit in peace.

Their flapping lips and wagging tongues are like bells, stone chimes, panpipes, and flutes; their brandishing arms and pointing at their chests exceed the number of rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds. They further boast of their travels through the mountains.

Playing in the water, parting the grass, and discerning the wind—though one may speak before others until the stones nod their heads and flowers fly from the heavens to cover the ground, they too deserve thirty blows of the staff.
But tell me, when rewarding those who have sat through the summer retreat for their labors, how should one bestow the recompense? After a long silence, he said:
"When the myriad treasures have achieved their work, what thickness or thinness is there? When the price of a thousand-jin weight is set, it naturally rises or falls."
Chan Master Hongzhou Huqiu Lingyun ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat and said: "Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; above, there is nothing to grasp or look up to.

Where there is no Buddha, pass quickly by; below, cut off all personal involvement. From the beginning, there has been neither facing nor turning away; fundamentally, it is free from all nets and cages.
Stepping out the door, you bump into Subhūti—where even an inch of grass does not grow for thousands of miles. This is simply the long-beaked bird; do not speak of it."

The fragrant tree provides no place to perch; they merely prattle on about Chan and the Way. Mañjuśrī, even if your mind were suspended from the treetop, you could not avoid your body sinking to the bottom of the sea.
Do not move! To move would incur thirty blows—let that be for now. Regarding the phrase for the *pravāraṇā* at the end of the summer retreat, how do you speak it?
The green mountains and blue waters remain as they ever were; the bright moon and clear breeze belong to one and the same house.
Chan Master Daguang Haoyun’s discourse on the occasion of the end of the summer retreat, regarding the public case of "the fifteenth day of the fourth month.

It is only on the fifteenth day of the seventh month that the summer retreat is formally concluded. Yet here now, among this great multitude, every single person has a principle that is difficult to vindicate.

Is there anyone in this assembly with eloquent and sharp辩才 (discerning speech) who can come forward and vindicate it? Try coming forth and vindicating it! Even if you were able to vindicate it—*even so*...
"One must touch one's forehead to the ground before it is attained.
Upon ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat (*varsā*), he held up his staff and said: "For one hundred and twenty days of summer, there has been no moment of vacancy.

The pillar displays its supernatural powers; the lantern reveals its ugliness and clumsiness. Whether you have penetrated it or not, come now and I shall resolve it for you upon this staff. He struck the floor once with the staff.
Descending from his seat, he ascends the hall to mark the end of the summer retreat. For one hundred and twenty days we have observed the *kaṭhina* period; for thirty-five days we have been abroad.

Though the iron cauldron for boiling tea and the iron kettle are not the same, the clay ox can still let out the roar of a lion. Today, the year of the Dharma has reached its full completion. [He] lifts up...
Having gained the nostrils, one loses the mouth. Taking Great Perfect Enlightenment as the monastery, the forty-nine days of the seven-week period follow as before.
Announcing the end of the summer retreat to the assembly: "Dongshan’s 'ten thousand miles of a single iron bar'—Liujiang struck it once and it shattered into a hundred pieces.
Yunmen’s 'Gate' character is ever-present before him. As for Cuiyan’s eyebrows, are they there or not? He then raised his whisk and said, "Yunmen’s Great..."
"The Master comes! Do you see him? (He strikes the whisk and says: "One win, two wins.

Addressing the assembly at the conclusion of the summer retreat: "When monks meet, do not harbor doubt or suspicion. The knot of the sackcloth bag is untied today. The candela, wearing its robe, departs for Nanyue;
The lantern, removing its hat, ascends to Tiantai. (Suddenly picking up his staff, he says: "There is only the clouds..."
The Venerable Sengmumen remained for his entire life without going or coming. At one time, leaning alone against the side of an ancient screen, he saw through the horse-stand before the gate.
He cast down his staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Ying’an Hua ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat and said:

A monk asked Yunmen, “At the beginning of autumn and the end of summer, if someone on the road ahead asks me something, I do not know how I should answer him. Yunmen said, “Have the assembly step back.
The monk asked, “Where does the fault lie? Yunmen said, “Return my ninety days’ worth of rice money! The Master said: This monk had a way of meeting [the challenge].

The blade’s edge is the strategy; Yunmen possesses the means to both kill and give life. Nevertheless, if one is under the gate of Baoen, one must still undergo further examination before being accepted. Descend from the seat.
Chan Master He’an ascended the hall at the conclusion of the retreat and said: “Treading boldly through tiger dens and demon palaces, Destroying monks and slandering Buddhas without hesitation.
Ignorance and the three poisons strike fear into people; Yet this enemy of mine is strangely adept. Do you understand?
When the true command is upheld, the grass before the Dharma Hall grows ten feet deep. When false teachers err, how many have been drowned in the pickle jars?”
His origins were extraordinary, and in the end he attained his ground; his spirit swallowed the Yunmeng marshes, and his radiance pierced the Oxherd Star.
Taking the Dharma-realm as a monastery, dragons and snakes are easily distinguished; taking the sands of the Ganges as a vast assembly, the patch-robed monks cannot deceive him.

To scramble for food from a tiger’s mouth is not due to a fiery temperament; to wrestle before a horse is it truly a matter of heroic spirit? Throughout the nine months of summer and the three autumns, he fully wielded the Great Function.
The boundaries of all directions have never been reached before; he has overturned them to their very depths. He has completely cut off the tongue that neither Buddhas nor Patriarchs can utter.
Who could leap across his self-indulgence? What is this "protecting life"? His nose is straight and his eyes are askance; his spirit is lofty and his resonance far-reaching.
One who enters the chamber of Nan-chuan and emerges through the gate of Nan-chuan does not treat the path as an enemy; having picked up the dead snake, they know how to play it alive.
It is just as when Layman Zhao opened the mouth of the bag: seeing him daily and becoming more intimate with him day by day—what further need is there for explanation?

After a long silence, he said: "Truly, this is genuine seed-grass for upholding the family lineage; it is not like the short-term peddlers and wandering monks. He then cited a monk who asked an ancient worthy:
"The ninety-day retreat for restraining the feet is now coming to an end; what is the function of the *pravāraṇa* (self-indulgence) ceremony?
The worthy replied: "A monkey chasing a butterfly, taking a rest every nine steps. He then asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The worthy said: "Two..."
A child carries a wooden drum; striking it on this side, he dances on that. In an instant, he manifests a hundred thousand forms;
I show each one to you—look and see! The Master said: "This monk has poked his head out too far.

The ancient worthies competed in poverty and wealth, yet they had not yet reached full maturity. Suddenly, someone asked Nanzen: "The ninety-day retreat for restraining the senses is now complete; when shall we hold the *pravāraṇā* ceremony?"
What is the mechanism of this? Simply say: "If you wish to go, then go; if you wish to stay, then stay. Do not inquire whether one understands or not.
If they ask, "Ultimately, how is it? then reply: "A face of cast iron—knives cannot cut into it.
Blind ignorance and temperament have already spread throughout all quarters. This is so, but take care not to misrepresent it.

Chan Master Mimang Jie ascends the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: "Today, Wugu concludes the summer retreat, following the discourse of the Yellow-Faced Old Man from two thousand years ago.
The wax figure is thoroughly pure as ice; the pearl of the precepts is protected without a single flaw.
Yet, only the lamp-stand and the pillar refuse to enter this protective community. Why? Because from the beginning, their hearts have been like iron."
At the end of the summer retreat, he ascended the hall for the formal address.
Before the fifteenth day, one is bound by ropes of one’s own making; after the fifteenth day, the feet grow lean while the straw sandals remain wide.
On the fifteenth day itself, heaven covers all without partiality and earth sustains all without partiality; the wind does not rustle the branches.
The rain does not break the clods of earth; the great householders clap their hands in joy at this era of peace. Let them fall to the east or be struck down to the west as they please.

(He lets out a shout and descends from the seat. Ascending the hall for the conclusion of the summer retreat: On the fifteenth day of the fourth month we bound ourselves; on the fifteenth day of the seventh month we are released. It is like these six dice.
A basin full of red. For the most part, this is merely for the sake of spectacle. *Haha!* [The Master] takes a sip.
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: When a single gourd falls to the ground, the gourd-vines all over the earth topple over as well.
If you wish to recognize the Chan of direct transmission and pointing directly, today’s assembly has come together most perfectly.
Chan Master Wuzhun Shanfang ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: "The summer has already ended; nothing remains unresolved.
Thus, he sets aside his bowl from Suifu and his ceramic cup from Qiongzhou."

Chan Master Gaofeng Miao, at the conclusion of the summer retreat, addressed the assembly: "For ninety days, we gripped the rope-head with such firmness that not even a hair’s breadth of movement was permitted.
It reached the point where every single person was stripped to the bone, reduced to a scattered mess.

Looking upon this with cold eyes, it is truly like digging through the earth to seek the sky—a thousand errors, ten thousand mistakes. Today, arriving here, I cannot help but let loose a single thread for both you and me."
Without constraint or restriction, one moves freely and spontaneously in all directions—east, west, south, and north. In the heavens above and the human realm below, one dwells in carefree joy.

Yet, even though this is so, tell me: if one suddenly encounters the cauldrons of boiling water, the furnaces of glowing coals, the sword-trees, and the mountain of blades, where will one find a place to rest?
After a long silence, he said: "Evil!"

Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the retreat: The mouth of the hemp-sack is opened; whether it feeds donkeys or horses, if you wish to ride, you may ride; if you wish to dismount, you may dismount.
But if you go to Jiangxi or Hunan and encounter a "burnt-tail tiger," do not say that you spent the summer retreat on West Peak.
Ascending the hall to conclude the summer retreat: Throughout this entire summer, you all have been full of *maluo* (shame/embarrassment), and I, this mountain monk, have also been full of *maluo*.

Meeting *maluo*, we have both avoided letting it pass in vain. Today, as the sacred regulations of the retreat come to an end, I cannot help but speak some more *maluo*-Chan, so that everyone may win the state of being fully *maluo*.
What is *maluo*-Chan? *Duh!* (A sharp rebuke). It is like a fierce fire frying oil.
Upon concluding the retreat, he ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he struck it once and said: "The mouth of the sack is opened; hundreds and thousands of oxen are let loose.
They roam freely among the fragrant grasses, never to be caught by others again. One day they shall return, and we shall meet face to face—half with smiles, half with shame.
"Assembly, let the shame cease for now. But what, ultimately, is there to smile about? He struck the staff once more.
"Stop! said Chan Master Wanfeng Wei as he ascended the hall. "A single leaf falls, and the world turns autumnal; a single mote of dust rises, and the great earth is gathered in.
Unfastening the mouth of the sack, the patch-robed monk attains freedom. From head to foot, wind and clouds arise; scattering soil and raising sand."
Rolling into the stream, it fills the void without leaving a trace; the weeping oriole is already at the tip of the willow branch.
Ultimately, how do you employ it? *He*.
Chan Master Tianru Ze gave this instruction to the assembly upon the conclusion of the summer retreat. Striking the meditation seat with his staff, he said:

"The monastery of Perfect Enlightenment is shattered into a hundred fragments by a single blow! On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, the formal commencement of the retreat was originally without anything to commence; on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the conclusion is likewise not a conclusion.
Westerners test the wax man in the ice, creating complications for themselves; Easterners test the iron ball."
You are accustomed to playing with empty tricks. Here, I am entirely straightforward and honest: if you have a staff, I give you a staff;
if you have no staff, I take yours away from you.
Chan Master Weian ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat. He cited the words of Cuiyan, who addressed the assembly at the end of the summer:
"Throughout this entire summer, I have been conversing with you brothers; look—do Cuiyan’s eyebrows still remain? Baofu said, "The heart of a thief is always anxious.
The Master remarked, "Good news does not leave the door. Changqing said, "They have grown! The Master remarked, "Bad news travels a thousand miles."
Yunmen said, "The barrier. The Master said, "Wrong. This group of fellows only knows how to protect their eyebrows;
they do not realize they have lost their nostrils. Today, Longfeng intends to settle the case for them according to the facts.
Do you all understand? The summer heat departs with the clouds and rain; the cool breeze penetrates the courtyard. (He lets out a shout.)
Chan Master Yongtai Ren ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat. The pine wind is piercingly cold; withered leaves fall in profusion.
The willows by the bank are withered and decayed; monkeys cry out from the distant peaks. If you can skillfully observe the seasons, you will then be in the company of the sages.
Yet, you have not yet mastered the livelihood of a patch-robed monk. O worthy ones, at this very moment, it is best to carry your staff across your shoulders and hang your alms bowl high.
"Carrying my bag, I shall go everywhere to rouse the abbot’s door and meet this old barbarian face-to-face.

If not a single word of accord is reached, I shall simply strike him with my sitting mat and depart. Would that not be most delightful? Since I first began my travels as a wandering monk, I have never encountered even one or half of such a person.
Why is this so? After a long silence, he said: "The land is vast and the people are few; those who meet [such a person] are rare."
Chan Master Shu’An Zong ascended the hall and raised the following case: Chan Master Yue-lin Zhen addressed the assembly, saying, "The mouth of the cloth bag is open;
is there anyone who would buy it? A monk said, "There is. Yue-lin asked, "Without making it cheap and without making it expensive, how would you buy it?"
The monk remained silent. Lin said, "The old monk has lost.

The Master said, "Yuelin set up this question with great ingenuity, yet when confronted by another’s single word 'Yes,' he was left with nothing but to cover himself here and there, unable to conceal his tracks fast enough.
Huguo said, "Today the mouth of the sack is open; is there anyone who will buy it? After a long pause, he said, "Though the railing is shared by all..."
Leaning against [the wall], the mountain colors appear differently depending on one's perspective.
On the occasion of the end of the summer retreat, Chan Master Jing of Xueting ascended the hall and said: "For those who truly know, ten thousand years pass as if they were a single day."
For those who do not know [this], a single day passes as if it were ten thousand years. Have you not heard the words of Master Sītacitta?
"This mountain monk has been traveling on pilgrimage for over thirty years; he reckons ninety days as one summer. One cannot add a single day, nor can one subtract a single day.
It cannot be grasped, nor can it be relinquished. Within this state of non-attainability, it is simply attained. —Cuiyun.
Furthermore, this standpoint is not so. For thirty years since I first set out on my travels as a monk, who has cared for him whether it be one day or ninety days?
There is neither attainment nor non-attainment. Everywhere one comes to see Maitreya. But tell me, where is Maitreya?
The golden wind blows over the Wei River; fallen leaves fill Chang’an.
Master Gumeyou ascended the hall to give a discourse at the conclusion of the summer retreat. "Three months of summer seclusion—this is a deliberate mistake.
Three months of peaceful dwelling—this is binding oneself without a rope. The cloth bag is untied; heaven and earth are vast and empty. Letting go is like seeking tortoise hair;
gathering it back is like hanging rabbit horns. Try hanging both eyes upon the void; a gust of cool wind arises from the corner of the hall."
Chan Master Tieguanshu ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat. "On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, he releases a fierce tiger that roars like a golden-maned lion;
it swallows Buddhas and patriarchs. Great assembly, since this is a fierce tiger, why does it let out the roar of a lion?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: Guishan asked Yangshan, "What have you accomplished this summer, my son?
Yangshan replied, "I cleared a patch of fallow land and sowed a basketful of millet. Guishan said, "My son, you have not spent this summer in vain.
[Yangshan] then served poisoned wine at the banquet. Later, Yangshan asked Guishan, "What have you accomplished this summer, Preceptor? Guishan—
Yangshan said, "I eat but once at midday and sleep but once after nightfall. Yangshan replied, "Master, you have not spent this summer in vain either.
In the space of a casual conversation, he brandished his spear and halberd. He called to the assembly, saying, "Do you understand? Two humpbacked camels have met face to face."
"In this world, there are currently no upright people.
Master Yuejiang Yin, upon concluding the summer retreat (*xiazhe*), said: "At the beginning of autumn and the end of summer, you brothers go east and west;
like a strong man extending his arm, you do not rely on external force; like a lion roaming, you seek no companion. This was because he was acting for the sake of others.
Beneath the heels of every person lies a living path that reaches through the heavens.

The Buddhas of the three periods, the six generations of patriarchs, and the old monks of the world all walk hand-in-hand with you. Have you not seen how Master Yunmen asked Dongshan, "Where have you recently come from?
"Chadu," he replied. "Where did you spend the summer? "At Baoci in Hunan. "When did you leave there? "The second day of the eighth month."
15. Yunmen said, "I let you off three blows of the staff. The next day, [Dongshan] went up to the abbot's quarters and asked, "Yesterday I received the Master’s gift of three blows of the staff;
I do not know where my fault lay. Yunmen replied, "You rice-bag! You go off to Jiangxi and Hunan acting just like this!
At these words, Dongshan attained great enlightenment. Yunmen brandished a sky-reaching long sword—how awe-inspiring!
Divine blades are not easily avoided. Dongshan cast himself nakedly into their midst to charge through those white blades. At such a moment, what is it like?
The golden crow pecks through the lapis lazuli shell; the jade hare pushes open the gates of the azure sea.
Chan Master Zhengfaming ascends the hall at the conclusion of the retreat: Leaves fall in profusion; heaven and earth announce the early autumn.
This is clearly the meaning of the Western Patriarch—what need is there for further seeking?

If you can understand it thus, you will finally believe that the Way of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is fundamentally level and even, and that the Great Gate of Liberation has never had a lock or key. It encompasses the universe and fills the void.
Its measure is inexhaustible and its wisdom cannot be fathomed.

If one has not yet clarified this essential meaning and does not penetrate its source, then even if one cultivates merit for a hundred kalpas and refines one’s practice through a thousand lifetimes, it will only lead to weary toil with no connection to the truth.

If, however, one deeply clarifies this essential meaning and thoroughly penetrates its source, one will realize that in every movement, stillness, action, and exertion—whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—every single instance accords with the Way.

Reflecting on the primary source, did our Patriarch not say: "Deluded beings are in a state of chaotic stillness; awakening is free from likes and dislikes. Let gain and loss, right and wrong, be cast off all at once.
If this is so, who is deluded and who is awakened? Who is right and who is wrong?

It is only because you all have individually given rise to divergent views—observing the great and the small, clinging to existence and clinging to non-existence—that your own spiritual luminosity shines forth alone, yet you refuse to accept it. This is the moon of the mind.
To be solitary yet claim perfection is a contradiction; how is this different from abandoning one's father at home or forgetting a pearl within one's clothing?
It causes thorns to grow into a forest upon the path to Bodhi, and misty clouds to shroud the sun in the sky of liberation.

Fortunately, on this day, the mountain monk has encountered the *pravāraṇā* ceremony of the assembly, the patron has returned to the mountains, and these virtuous superiors have taken the trouble to visit me in person. I must not remain silent.
This is a bit of a tangle, but I have made a circuitous effort to provide a slight opening of expedient means for this present age.

You must all look closely and observe each of you with discernment. If you further attempt to deliberate or reflect upon it, ten thousand miles of white clouds will intervene. [The Master] then took up his staff and said:
"If you can understand this clearly, the assembly on Vulture Peak is solemnly present before your eyes. If this is not yet the case, wait until tomorrow morning for the instruction."
Chan Master Zhengtang Bian ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: "Before the fifteenth day, you must not depart;
the single shoe of Shaolin has no place to be hidden. After the fifteenth day, you must not remain; the fragrance of the cassia seeds blends with the rain and dew.
As for this very fifteenth day—how is it? Aha-ha! Elegance does not depend on wearing many garments."
Chan Master Tuian Xiu ascended the hall for the opening address. "At the time of the summer retreat, my left eye was half a catty; at the time of the summer's end, my right eye was eight taels.
In vain you claim it is a ninety-day period of *an-gu* (sitting in seclusion); all you gain is a belly full of delusive thoughts.

Even if you were to pierce through seven holes and eight openings, you would still not escape this mountain monk’s staff. Nevertheless, a crossbow of a thousand catties does not fire for the sake of a field mouse."

People must not misquote [the Master]: "Mountains of Langzhou, waters of Liuzhou; the four seas and five lakes are all within the Imperial Transformation.

With satchels at their waists and straw hats upon their heads, there are tens of thousands of them; when questioned, they all speak only of mountains and waters. Suddenly, one who cannot bear this comes forward and says:
If the mountain speaks only of the mountain and the water speaks only of the water, what fault is there? After a long silence, he said: "One should not yet cast away one's whole heart;
when meeting people, speak but three parts of the truth."

Ascending the hall to mark the conclusion of the retreat: For ninety days we shared the same restriction of the feet; today is the day of *pravāraṇā*. In this temple, evening rain falls by the green lamp;

A west wind blows across the white stone bridge. With a solitary body and the three robes, I carry a single light bundle for ten thousand miles. If you should arrive at the place of Muzhou, You must beware of the knife hidden within a smile.
Ascending the hall to conclude the summer retreat: This morning is the fifteenth day of the seventh month. A cool breeze opens my bamboo door;

atop the ridge, one or two flecks of white cloud are blown by the wind until they are scattered in all directions—horizontal and vertical. Lightly drifting, floating and shimmering, they seem about to disperse yet do not, about to gather yet do not.
The old monk beckons toward the white clouds: "White clouds, white clouds, why do you not stay?"
"In the end, one must surely return to the mountains. Wandering abroad at the ends of the earth and along the roads. (He lets out a shout.

Chan Master Yuansou Duan ascends the hall for the *jie-xia* (conclusion of the summer retreat). "On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, we enter; [he raises his staff] and strikes it once to the left.
All those who come from every direction observe the *jinzu* (foot-binding) and dwell in seclusion here. On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, we conclude. [He raises his staff.]

He struck the meditation desk once. To those present, he said: "The summer retreat has ended with the *pravāraṇā* ceremony. Before the empty kalpa, there was no name for Buddha and no name for sentient beings.
What more is there to bind? And what more is there to unbind? Leaning on his staff, he descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: The autumn mountains are carved from jade; the autumn waters are polished bronze.

The living path runs through north, south, east, and west. A pair of straw sandals is as vigorous as a tiger; a single iron staff is as fierce as a dragon. Suddenly, one bumps into Elder Ding, who asks:
"How far apart are the 'true person of no station' and the 'not-being-no-station true person'? One must take care not to fill [the void] with silence."
His face flushed red.
Upon the conclusion of the summer retreat, he ascended the hall and said: "When the mouth of the sack is tied shut, the myriad phenomena have no place to breathe.
When the mouth of the sack is untied, the mountains, rivers, and the great earth attain great liberation. It is tied, and it is tied; it is untied, and it is untied. All of you..."
"Go east or west as you please. Should anyone suddenly ask about your future path, do not say that you spent the summer retreat in Central India.
[He] descended from the seat.
At the conclusion of the summer retreat, he ascended the hall and cited Master Dongshan’s address to the assembly: "A hundred-forged gold cast into an iron ox... Ten...
"Dividing the high price to repay others; before the courtyard, there are no flowers smiling. Once again, Dongshan has rested for a summer. The Master said:
"Jingshan, following the coarse woolen cloth, also has a verse: 'Old and without heart to cast an iron ox, Before my eyes, I repay as circumstances allow.
Leaves fall before the courtyard as the west wind rises; I am glad that Lingxiao has rested for a summer.'"
Chan Master Chushi Qi ascended the hall for the conclusion of the summer retreat. "Today is the end of the summer.
From South India to North Wutai, one may roam freely in all directions. Suppose someone suddenly asks you, 'How have things been at Yongxue lately?
How would you respond? Simply say: 'When I came, I was not told to deliver a message. This will surely cut off the tongues of everyone under heaven."
Head. Although so, this one belongs to Yongzuo; which one belongs to the Senior Seat?
Upon ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: the entire world of the ten directions is the true human body.

Awakening and affliction, birth and death, nirvana, the conditioned and the unconditioned, the sages of the past and the sages of the future, the commencement and conclusion of the retreat, long periods and short periods—truly...
In terms of the ultimate reality, there is no meeting point. Xuefeng went to Touzi three times and to Dongshan nine times;
finally, at the Inn on Mount Aoshan, he lost his nostrils. Dawsui studied under more than sixty spiritual friends;
Changqing sat through seven broken meditation cushions; and Xinghua, through the staff of Dajue, deeply realized the intent of Huangbo, overturning it completely.
Mountains and seas lay down their arms; it is as if one were to exchange a thousand pounds of valley echoes for ten thousand petals of floating flowers.

Beyond the limit of awe-inspiring sound, prior to the empty kalpa—wherever there are words and explanations, none possess true meaning. How can you speak that single phrase which pierces the nostrils of all people under heaven?
When the Great Peng spreads its wings, it covers the Ten Continents; the swallows and sparrows by the hedge but chirp in vain.

Chiu. Again, [the Master] raised a case where a monk asked Yunmen: "At the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, if someone suddenly asks you about the path ahead, I wonder what you would say to him?
Yunmen said, "The assembly, step back! The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie?
Yunmen said, "Bring me back the payment for my ninety days' worth of rice. The Master said: "It cannot be let pass; I wonder what he would say. Simply..."
He said to him, "Seventy-two blows have turned into one hundred and twenty. Where does the fault lie?
He replied to him, "You simply take the blows; I want this saying to circulate."
Chan Master Da’an Zhuang ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat. "The sacred regulations have reached their completion; it is precisely this day.
In the monasteries of all quarters, they speak of Chan and speak of the Way in a great clamor. Here, with me, it is solitary, remote, steep, and lofty.
Even if there were Buddha-dharma, who would cast an eye to look upon it? He struck the meditation seat and descended.
Ascending the hall: After the summer retreat, whether going east, west, south, or north, you must stand upon the peak of the highest mountain and walk upon the floor of the deepest sea.
If there are things from the inner chambers that you cannot let go of, you will inevitably fall into pits and ravines.
(He strikes the whisk. At the gate, he plants no more thorns, so as to avoid being entangled by those who come.

Chan Master Guyan Ji ascended the hall to address the advancement and retirement of the two orders at the conclusion of the summer retreat. There is advancing and retreating; there is binding and unbinding.
Moving left and right with refined elegance, he said: "Reciting hymns atop the bell tower, planting vegetables beneath the bedposts.
Then, the Head Seat Sheng declared, "A fierce tiger sits blocking the road," and striking his staff, he said: "One rain universally nourishes the three types of grass and the two kinds of trees."
Ascending the hall for the conclusion of the summer retreat: On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, the mouth of the sack is tied shut;
how many are there who move freely in the ten directions? On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the mouth of the sack is untied; how many are there who bind themselves without a rope?
*Hè!* (A shout). Neither bondage can be found, nor has liberation ever existed. With both bondage and liberation perfectly transcended, one faces south and looks at the Big Dipper.
Descend from the seat.

Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun delivered a formal lecture upon the conclusion of the summer retreat: "Monks, as you conclude the summer retreat and depart for the east or west, do not merely say you are carrying your satchels to catch the early cool.
The three realms are blazing like a house on fire; who knows where one’s true hometown lies?"

At the conclusion of the summer retreat, the Master ascended the hall for a discourse. He raised the following case: A monk asked Jiufeng, "In the Western Heaven at the end of the summer retreat, there are many who attain the fruits of the Way.
I wonder, is there anyone here in this land who has done so? Jiufeng said, "There is. The monk asked, "Who is it?

Jiufeng replied, "One whose head bears the midnight moon and whose feet tread upon the golden earth. The Master said, "The Western Heaven and this land do not differ by a single step. To attain the Way..."
The fruit is like a phoenix entwined in golden chains. This assembly of mine is not at all like that; we do not practice cultivation, nor do we possess a single grain of merit.
Yet, these ninety days have not been spent in vain. Now that the heat has subsided and the cool air arises, you may walk, sit, or lie down as you please.

Do not inquire about the karmic conditions of the Patriarchs—they are all nothing but the saliva and drool of wild foxes. Even those with the eyes of a hawk or the pupils of a dragon would see it thus.
He pressed down from the head and released the great tiger of Changsha; it startled Pòzào Duò of Sōngshān.

Chan Master Shùzhōng Yùn, upon ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat (*kṣetra-vāsa*), cited the occasion when Master Dégǔn Yuǎn ascended the hall at the end of the summer retreat.
A monk asked: "The ninety-day period of restraining the feet has now concluded; what is the ritual for the *pravāraṇā* (self-reproval) ceremony? Dégǔn said: "A monkey."
"Chasing butterflies; take a rest at every nine steps. A monk asked, "I do not understand the meaning of this;
what is its intent? Deshan showed him with a verse: Two children carry a wooden drum; The left strikes it, the right dances.
In a single instant, they manifest a hundred thousand forms; I show them clearly to you—take heed! [The Master] comments: The answer has been given; the verse has been sung.
It is understood. Yet, how can one help the fact that this monk has not yet been willing to nod his head?
Lingyan, seeing injustice on the road, wishes to meet with Deshan. The occasion for self-indulgence is today; there is a flower right before one’s face. One phrase settles the confusion:
a monkey chasing a butterfly—the butterfly flies away, nowhere to be found. Sitting in meditation in mid-air, threading a needle at the bottom of the sea. Suddenly, he picks up his staff.
Looking around to his left and right, he said, "Is there no one among this assembly who can celebrate and praise through the merit of this vegetarian feast?
He struck the meditation staff and said, "Do not let your idle learning and intellectual understanding bury the mind of the Patriarchs."
Ascending the hall: In summer there is the untying of knots; the Dharma has no fixed characteristics. The meaning of existence and non-existence is like a bubble-flower in the sky.
Whether one treads upon it at the heels of those here—South India or North Wutai—if you cannot tread upon it, leave it unsaid.
If, on the road ahead, someone suddenly asks, "Where have you come from? by all means do not say, "From Ruiyan. Let him harbor doubt for thirty years.
Chan Master Wumen Can ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat and presented the public case concerning an old master who did not speak to his monks for an entire summer.
The Master offered this verse: "A single word once uttered is as hard to recall as a horse in flight; Having spoken it, how can one repent?
In the silence, he was exposed by another; His jaw clenched tight, his mouth weary to open."

Chan Master Liaohan Yu ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat. The Buddha rejoices; the monks perform the *pravāraṇā*. The fragrant elephant crosses the river, cutting through the current and departing.
Whether there is gain or no gain, one does not leave the marketplace. At the tip of the staff, there is another world.
[He] planted his staff and gave a shout.

Chan Master Nan Shiyou ascended the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat. "The *Awakening of Faith in the Mahāyāna* can give rise to all phenomena, yet no phenomenon has ever been apart from the *Awakening of Faith*.
Ants know the rain and seal their burrows; the *shichong* insect responds to the season and raises its blossoms.
How many are there with hands and feet stuck to things? How many are there with the ten directions crisscrossed?"

Upon concluding the retreat, the donor relinquishes the meditation benches, mats, and dharma robes; [the Master] ascends the hall. During the nine-month summer retreat, not even a trace of Mara has arisen.
The conduct and hidden virtues of the assembly’s eminent practitioners are light and efficient. Those who drink from the camphor-scented well find their thirst quenched;

those who eat the rice from the tidal fields remain free from hunger. Mount Yang burned the slash-and-burn fields to plant millet; Mount Wei slept at night and ate during the day; Baizhang rolled up [his sitting mat].
Bowing upon the mat, he faces Mazu. The World-Honored One encircles Kāśyapa with his *kāṣāya*. After a long while: "The golden qi has responded to the coming night;
coolness reaches much of the bamboo bed."

Chan Master Shouchang ascends the hall to conclude the retreat: "The three-month summer retreat and the ninety-day prohibition were not for seeking the Buddha, Dharma, or Sangha, nor for the merit of humans and devas.
To speak of 'vowing that all sentient beings together realize Bodhi' is much like crying out for one's father after he has already died.
But how is it, ultimately? Only a Persian could bite off the arrowhead. Take care!"
Chan Master Poshan Ming ascended the hall at the conclusion of the retreat: "The east wind thaws the frost, and the hundred grasses sprout their buds.

Wandering monks are as numerous as millet and hemp seeds. They drag through mud and water, their straw sandals fierce as tigers; they blend with the mundane and harmonize with the light, their staffs as lively as snakes.
One must not dwell where there is a Buddha, and must swiftly pass by where there is no Buddha—only then can one be called [a true practitioner]."
A talented writer must never go to a place where there is not even an inch of grass for ten thousand miles; otherwise, one’s life will be spent in vain.
My assembly, consider this: here at my mountain monastery, we have observed the ninety-day retreat and refined our minds for three months.
Today, as we conclude the retreat and prepare to depart, what single phrase can be spoken? Pluck the willow blossoms! Pluck the willow blossoms!
Chan Master Ruohan ascends the hall to mark the conclusion of the retreat: "The wondrous function of spiritual power is played with at ease;
in movement and stillness, coming and going, there is neither sorrow nor joy. Eons of dust are not distant, and a single instant is not brief. Day after day, the mouth of the hemp sack is untied."
The deity of peace and bliss manifests from time to time; why must one attend upon Maitreya in the morning and pay homage to Śākyamuni in the evening?

Within the meaning of conventional truth (*saṃvṛti-satya*), the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*) is truly realized. One turns the Great Dharma Wheel amidst the flames; the ancestral seal is fully revealed at the tips of the hundred grasses.
With the crown of the head suddenly opened, the stream of sensory stimuli is cut off. Transcending the realms of humans and devas, one remains unchanging while following conditions. Great!
"The ocean receives the rivers"—in one phrase, how do you say it? "The days grow long, the daylight lasts forever; spring has deepened, the green shade is vast.

At the conclusion of the retreat, he ascended the hall and raised the following case: San-sheng asked Xue-feng, "What does the golden fish that has passed through the net eat? Feng replied: [He ate the mud on the bottom of the net.]
"I will tell you when you come out of the net. Xuefeng said, "A spiritual friend of fifteen hundred people, yet you do not even recognize the pivot of the teaching.

Yunfeng said, "This old monk’s administrative duties are too numerous. The Master said, "Sansheng and Xuefeng held hands, standing atop the highest mountain peak and walking upon the deepest ocean floor;
this was the way they sang in harmony as companions, their rhythmic steps following one another."
I, this mountain monk, am not like that here. Suppose someone were to ask, "What does the golden fish that has passed through the net eat?

I would tell him, "Today is the end of the retreat. If he further says, "You do not even recognize the teaching topic of the Great Master of fifteen hundred disciples," I would simply say, "Be skillful on the path.
Now tell me, is this the same as the ancients, or is it different? [The master] descends from his seat.
Chan Master Muyunmen ascends the hall to conclude the retreat. On this occasion of the Upper Yuan Festival, the weather is clear and bright.
Here at Tiantong, we open wide the gates to let forth all the Bodhisattva children to go out and play.

From the first ground, the second, the third, and the fourth, through the fifth and sixth grounds—joyful, radiant, and unable to be detained—they cultivate further stage by stage, intent upon the Far-Reaching Path. How firm!
Only the eighth stage, the Immovable Bhūmi, remained. The Buddha Candrasūryapradīpa could no longer restrain himself;

he rose into the air to a height of seven tala trees and, one by one, bestowed the prediction of enlightenment upon them by touching their heads with his hand. Those who depart do so down a slope; they do not run, yet such a swift opportunity is difficult to encounter again.
The dweller has his eyebrows knotted and his nostrils pressed together. Go! Go! Go! Stay! Stay! Stay!
Son of a Bodhisattva, do not speak of the sick deva-boys; their words have no foundation. Tsk!
Chan Master Chanshi Leshi ascends the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: "Today is the fifteenth day of the seventh month. A single phrase is entirely guest and entirely host.
Having untied the mouth of the sack, let it go as it will—east or west. Where there is no Buddha, pass by swiftly; where there is a Buddha, do not dwell.
When meeting people three thousand miles away, do not speak of this in error. He lets out a shout.

Chan Master Jing of Dongyuan, upon concluding the summer retreat (*jie-zhi*), took leave of the assembly and ascended the hall to speak. Gazing alone from the solitary pavilion, the spring mountains stretch afar;
The nine bends of the clear stream flow on day and night. How joyful it is that the splendor of the season flows on inexhaustible— Willow branches line the embankment as the moon rises.
Great Assembly: One binding and one unbinding are the time-honored customs of a thousand ages; one dwelling and one acting require nothing less than the mastery of the pivot.
"It has its own conditions. Today, I, this mountain monk, hand it over before the assembly. This staff intends to go toward the peaks of ten thousand mountains.
The assembly repeatedly entreated him, saying, "For the sake of the Dharma, please remain for a long time.
The Master said, "Assembly, speak a single phrase from the tip of my staff, and I shall stay. As the assembly hesitated, the Master struck once and said, "From here..."
Come and dwell together; no one shall recognize you. Let out a long, piercing cry and go your way! [The Master] descends from his seat.
On the day of the lifting of the retreat, Chan Master Xian of Gushan ascends the hall and says: "Today the retreat is lifted. Brothers, you will inevitably be heading east or west.
I, this mountain monk, have three phrases to entrust to you. First: when you step out the door, do not drag a corpse along."
Go! Second, when you arrive at someone’s house to eat a meal, do not let your lips touch the food.

Third, do not dwell in a place where there are ten thousand miles of land with not a single blade of grass. If you can avoid violating these three points, then on a future day, lighting a single stick of incense to make offerings to this old monk will not be considered an extraordinary act.
