"At the beginning of the thirty-six hundred days, at the start of the seventy-two seasonal signs—let us set aside for now the final phrase; as for the very first phrase, how would you speak it?
He raises his staff and says: "On the first day of the year, one grasps the brush; all matters are auspicious. Swiftly, as if by imperial decree! "O assembly, this mountain monk..."
"Proposing and chanting in such a manner—tell me, does this still contain the meaning of the Patriarchs? After a long silence, he said, "I remember Old Black Li from the eastern village;
year after year he personally writes his name upon the gate. He then planted his staff on the ground and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Fennan ascends the hall on New Year’s Day: To indulge in empty pretenses is merely to waste one's effort. Neither cold nor heat can alter true reality.
To stand so upright yet suffer such indignity is truly pitiable. How many times has the first day of the first month come year after year?
Brandishing the "knife that kills," a single stalk of grass rises ten thousand fathoms high. Lowering the "sword that gives life," it is neither noble nor base.
Moving freely and striking decisively, killing and giving life at will—like a lion emerging from the forest, the tracks of the foxes vanish. Every year is a good year;
every day is a good day. A great phoenix does not fly like an old crow; the Yellow River’s nine bends flow straight as a thread.
(He lets out a shout and descends from his seat.)

The Outline for New Year’s Day: Master Sifan Duan’s Hall Discourse for the New Year. A new year, a fresh spring, and the snow falls thick once more; the myriad phenomena of the universe are all the same.
When meeting one another, do not mistake this for the truth; perform a full somersault to manifest the ancestral wind. He then performed a somersault.
The Master descended from his seat.
On New Year’s Day, Chan Master Wuyong Kuan ascended the hall. At Lake Tai and Mount Liangshan, he turned everything over completely.
With a single handle-less whisk, he struck open the Three Barriers of Huanglong. "Great assembly, each of you may now rise and enjoy much merit. He planted his staff.
[The Master] said, "Just look at Zhaozhou’s 'Mu' (No). There is no need to divinate here and there. He descended from his seat.
On the New Year’s Day, he ascended the hall and said: "On Mount Taihu, we celebrate the New Year; The myriad phenomena and the ten thousand forms laugh aloud, piercing the heavens.
Startled, the earthen ox swallows the stone tiger; In every dust mote and every world-system, all is naturally at ease. He gave a shout and said, "May the winds be harmonious and the rains timely."
"May the Great Yuan Dynasty be blessed. [The Master] descends from his seat.
Zen Master Tianru Ze addresses the assembly on New Year's Day: "The Elder Kauṇḍinya beats the drum; Mount He Shan’s Ox-tail speaks Chan.
With a black lacquered staff, he utters words and speaks Chan, saying: 'The thirtieth day of the twelfth month passed yesterday. [He] sits upright.
The first day of the month arrived today. He gave this instruction: "Night is dark and day is bright; who is it that departs? Heaven is high and earth is vast; who is it that arrives?
This Lion Grove Monastery has a fine assembly for the formal lecture, yet they have already been told everything beforehand;
in the end, it all boils down to merely performing a bow, burning incense, and drinking tea.
Chan Master Yangshan Jian ascends the hall on New Year’s Day: The new laws have just been distinguished; the rosy light announces the dawn.
The weather is about to warm yet remains cold; the climate shifts from winter to spring. For the signs of the vast chaos (*hongmeng*) have just arisen, while the freezing cold has not yet withdrawn.
Time passes in an instant, and we already belong to the Lord of the East. Do not weary yourselves; let us together celebrate this passing of the year. Firmly.
There is one person who does not fall within this limit. Heaven and earth have no means to cover or support him; how could cold and heat cause him to shift?

The sun and moon cannot harmonize their illumination upon him; yin and yang find it ultimately difficult to transform him. If one were to force this person to undergo the passing of the year, he would never be willing to accept it;
yet when the season arrives, how can it be avoided? Now tell me: between the person who undergoes the passing of the year and the person who does not, which is it?
When family members meet one another, how do they offer congratulations? After a long silence, he said: "The cold follows the night away; spring pursues the fifth watch.
Upon the New Year’s Day, Chan Master Weian ascended the hall and said: "The first day of the new year begins its reign; all things flourish and prosper. He then suddenly took up his staff and said:
"Last night this staff sprouted branches; this morning it has put forth buds. The flower blooms in five petals, and its fragrance pervades the great universe."
"Thousand! Now tell me, is there any Buddha-dharma at the head of the New Year? [The Master] plants his staff and lets out a shout.
Master Tianguan Shu ascends the hall on the first day of the year to give thanks to the Prior. He raises his whisk and says:

"The Buddhas of the three periods, the Patriarchs of the six generations, and all the old monks throughout the world—all of them are celebrating the auspicious occasion of the New Year upon the tip of this whisk."
Pushan took a thorn from a jujube tree and offered it to everyone equally. "If you can swallow it, swallow; if you can spit it out, spit.
If you cannot swallow it nor spit it out, you will inevitably lose your body and forfeit your life. (He lets out a shout.)
On the New Year’s Day, Chan Master Shiwu Hong ascended the hall. On the bell tower, hymns were chanted; beneath the meditation platform, vegetables were planted.
Senior Seat Holder Sheng remarked, "A fierce tiger sits blocking the road. At this place, Fuyuan, at the mountain gate, there is singing and chanting for the New Year;

within the Buddha Hall, there is the recitation of sutras to offer blessings to the Emperor. All these are but sounds, yet they hold infinite meanings—some are worthy of being heard, and some are not.
"Have any of you ever been able to examine this thoroughly? He gave a shout and descended from his seat.
On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and said: "Jingqing said, 'In the new year, there is Buddha-dharma. Mingjiao said, 'In the new year, there is no Buddha-dharma.
To say it exists does not necessarily mean it exists; to say it does not exist does not necessarily mean it does not exist. It is like Zhang Gong drinking wine."
Master Li was intoxicated; Zhaozhou hung his gourd on the eastern wall.
Chan Master Yuansou Duan, ascending the hall on New Year’s Day, said: "Yesterday is called the New Year of today; today is called the Old Year of yesterday.
But what is the meaning of 'the non-transmigration of things'? He struck the whisk. "The cold plum blossoms atop the ridge."
No sooner has the snow melted than the willows by the city walls already hold mist.
On the occasion of the New Year’s Day lecture: The old year was sent off yesterday; the new spring is welcomed today. Auspicious vapors rise through the nine heavens;
joyful sounds pervade the ten thousand lands.
Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun delivered a lecture on the New Year’s Day: "The beginning of the year inaugurates the reign; all things are renewed.
The world rejoices in unison, and humans and devas celebrate together. Truly, the stone woman rides backward upon an iron horse, trampling through the void;
the wooden man cracks his whip, driving the clay ox to plow the azure heavens. A-he-he! Do you understand? When one has spirit, let the spirit increase!"
Where there is no elegance, there is elegance. On the New Year’s Day, he ascended the hall: “The adamantine true body is revealed in full majesty; the myriad phenomena are the radiance of prajñā.

The mechanism of coming and going is extinguished, transcending the present moment; the principle of yin and yang is fully manifest. The wooden cock cries out at dawn in the deep alley; the stone [dragon]..."

The maiden welcomes the spring as she emerges from her bridal chamber. All rejoice that the Dragon Lake abounds with auspicious vapors; the celestial breeze occasionally wafts the fragrance of the imperial incense burner.
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun delivers a lecture on the first day of the New Year: "At the beginning of the New Year, there is a single phrase which I shall present to you all."
This single phrase is the very phrase that existed prior to the birth of one’s parents. One must not take it upon oneself at the point where it is raised;
one must not speculate within the realm of the mental faculty. Simply see the imperial wind as a single expanse, and you will not know where the boundaries lie.

Ascending the hall on New Year’s Day: At the start of the new year, the Buddha-dharma is manifest everywhere. Guests hurrying to offer New Year greetings arrive, and he welcomes them by rushing out from his sandals.
He points laughingly at the fine weather; the wind and sun are still mild and bright. "The fields and rice must surely ripen," he says, "and we shall sing of peace with full bellies.
"Great assembly, if a superior man of the highest caliber were suddenly to arrive, how would you receive him? Qingyuan.
Wine. Zhaozhou’s tea. Three cups, two goblets, and one sleeps drunk amidst the mists and clouds. For the most part, this is the true style of a master of the house.
On New Year’s Day, Chan Master Zhuang of Daaan ascended the hall and said: “Heaven attains the One and becomes clear; Earth attains the One and becomes tranquil;
the Sovereign attains the One and brings about Great Peace. When a patch-robed monk attains a single drop of water, ice forms. He took up his staff and said: “As for this very staff...”
How is it when the staff-holder attains it at once? He directly reveals the Buddha-dharma of the new year: striking the wind and beating the rain, he moves with total freedom.
Leaning on his staff, he ascends the hall on the first day of the year and says: "All insentient things possess Buddha-nature. Rising early in the morning, we celebrate the New Year."
To strike a pillar in the Dharma Hall—what could be wrong with paying it three prostrations? The Mountain God of Anle was groundlessly irascible and struck a gong;
the Venerable Dianxiong, atop the foundation of the Buddha Hall, prattled on about right and wrong.
To both of them, I give twenty blows of the staff and drive them out beyond the Pass of Zhaozhou. Have you not heard it said: "The Master of Three Thousand Edicts"?
This is the practice of giving.
On New Year’s Day, ascending the hall: at the beginning of the year, one must not engage in entanglements with others. Set aside the staff of Deshan and the shout of Linji.
You say that Master Zhaozhou makes use of the twelve hours of the day; is there anyone who can verify this?
There is no place for it. [The Master] strikes the whisk. Before the door of every house, the sun and moon blaze;
in the Great Peace, there is no need for the majesty of a general. On the occasion of the New Year’s Day, ascending the hall:

before this old monk has even opened his mouth, at all times and in all places, the patterns of the Universal Radiance Mind-Seal are fully manifest. By the time you try to look with your eyes, it is already obscured. Today, specifically...

To point this out, he calls upon everyone to bear witness. Suddenly grasping his staff, he strikes it once and says, "In the new year, when one takes up the brush, all affairs shall be most auspicious.
He leans on the staff and descends from the seat.
Chan Master Tianmu Li ascends the hall on New Year’s Day: "Yesterday was the remnants of snow; today is the New Year.
We exchange greetings and perform our formal courtesies. Only at Nengren do we remain until old age without distinguishing the passage of time. Lifting one's head to gaze beyond the heavens."
It is entirely the old mountains and rivers.
On the first day of the new year, Chan Master Chu-shih Qi ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said:
"This mountain monk’s single staff has never been used to strike people indiscriminately. Today, on this New Year’s Day, it is opened and sent forth. Śākyamuni the Elder, Bodhidharma..."
The Master said, "It is unacceptable to let this one pass. As for the rest of their kind, they could be measured by the cartload or the peck. A sharp sword does not slay those who are already dead.
Suppose someone were to suddenly step forward and say, 'What about the Elder?'—he would strike him across the spine with his staff. This is not because he wishes to live in discord with others;
it is simply that, generally speaking, the distinction between the ordained and the laity must be clear. Relying on his staff, he descended from the seat.

On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said: "If there is a Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year, I do not dare grant that even this staff possesses it.
If there is no Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year, I do not dare grant that even this staff lacks it.

To transcend the four propositions and sever the hundred negations—all of these are merely old stories from all quarters; I do not dare grant that even this staff is such. He drew a line across the air.
The New Year begins its reign, and all things are renewed.
Ascending the hall on the first day of the year: This year’s year is last year’s year; how many years have passed as the old year went and the new came?
Yesterday’s day is today’s day; the sun rises and sets, yet it is not merely one day. This very thing has neither coming nor going, neither entering nor exiting.
Every year is a good year; every day is a good day. The four oceans flow toward the East Sea—this is the *prajñāpāramitā*.
On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall. The Patriarch said: "When the fruit is full, bodhi is perfected; when the flower blooms, the world arises. Holding up his staff, he said:
"The one flower has bloomed—is it a peach or a plum? Today is the head of the New Year; yesterday was the tail of the Old Year. Do you recognize this?"
Attaining one's original person, there is neither sorrow nor joy. He gives a single strike and says: "At every turn, green willows are fit to tie the horse;
at every household door, one penetrates to Chang'an."
On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and cited Xiangyan, who said: "Poverty last year was not yet poverty; poverty this year is true poverty.
Last year’s poverty had enough ground to stick a锥 (chui—a small awl) into; this year’s poverty has not even a 锥. Zhenjing said:
"Wealth last year was not yet wealth; wealth this year is true wealth. Last year’s wealth consisted of nothing more than a single piece of coarse black cloth robe."
This year I have acquired an additional cassock of a hundred patches. On New Year’s Day, I shake it out before the assembly of Zen practitioners.
Truly, this may be called the "wind-and-water style" (fengliu) of one who has mastered the house. The Master said: "Xiangyan was not poor, yet he still had a whole body remaining.
Zhenjing was not rich, yet his private property could not help but be fully exposed. Here at Fengshan, we do not speak of being rich or poor."
Speaking of poverty: according to the family’s abundance or scarcity, one treats the distant and the kin alike. He raises his whisk: when gathered in, it is as long as a hare's horn;
when let go, it weighs nine catties more than tortoise hair.

On New Year’s Day, he ascends the hall. At midnight, he rises to proceed to the Provincial Hall to offer incense and prayers. Having finished the incense and prayers, he performs the formal greetings with the Chancellor’s office and the various government departments.
Once these greetings are concluded, he returns to the main hall to burn incense, scatter sand, recite incantations over the earth, and circumambulate the corridors while practicing the Way.
Subsequently, the monasteries of the various mountains send their congratulations and prepare to receive the official. If it is held as a Buddhist assembly for the New Year, he enters.
"Hell is like being struck by an arrow.
On the first day of the New Year, he ascended the hall and said: "The beginning of the three hundred and sixty days; the start of the twenty-four solar energies.

The handle of the Dipper turns toward spring, and the radiance of the light dazzles the eyes. Sometimes the days are short and the nights long; sometimes the nights are short and the days long; sometimes the summer heat departs..."
When cold comes, or when heat comes and cold departs; the root of the flower is fundamentally vibrant, and the tiger’s coat is originally striped.

Although one does not change from who one was in former times, it cannot be avoided that everyone adds another year. He called the assembly together and said: "This very year, once added, will reach its end."
How could the future limit even be reached?
Master Yuguan gave this discourse while ascending the hall: "The new year begins its reign; all things are renewed. At the bottom of the well, dust and weeds obscure the sun;
atop the mountain, the carp grasps the clouds. Yet, how shall one speak a phrase that does not involve temporal conditions? He then raised his staff.
Zhaozhou said: "The staff says: 'Today my staff has gained another year; picked up as before, it remains black and weathered. Liaonan Yu Chan Master ascended the hall:
"The new year replaces the old year; broken, yet it is complete again. Although the patch-robed monks do not realize this, their nostrils already reach the heavens.
Look, look! A night market is being set up upon the eyelashes of a gnat, and on the tongue of a tiger."
Swinging on a swing. *He!* Ascending the hall for the New Year:
"The moon gives birth to one. From this, the Tathāgatas of the three periods emerge. "The moon gives birth to two. The intent of the Buddhas and Patriarchs suddenly manifests.
"The moon gives birth to three. The myriad phenomena of the universe vie with one another to seek realization. (Tapping the meditation seat) The Imperial Foundation!
Majestic and vast across the three thousandfold world-systems, the precious calendar opens a new epoch for ten million years.
Ascending the hall: As the New Year begins at dawn, a single phrase is fully upheld; all myriad functions cease, and not even a thousand sages can carry it away.
Purple mists shroud the imperial palace; sagacious calculations are equal to Heaven itself.
Ascending the Hall. On this New Year’s Day, it coincides with the Gengshen day. Tang Cheng’s virtue was ever-renewing; the Great Yuan has opened the Phoenix Calendar for eighty-four thousand springs.

Ascending the Hall on the first day of the year: the new reign begins at the start of the cycle. Mounting the horse, one sees the road ahead; all things are renewed, and everywhere there is a passable ford.

I respectfully address the head monks and the great assembly. Though you may be like dead snakes, you must still be brought to life through skillful manipulation. May each and every one of you enjoy ten thousand blessings in your daily lives and physical well-being.
Like the lion’s roar and the elephant king’s circling, with tigers bowing their heads in homage, may the Son of Heaven live for ten thousand years!
On the occasion of the New Year’s Day, Master Zhongjun ascended the hall and said:

"At the moment when the old year is about to depart but has not yet departed, and the new year is about to arrive but has not yet arrived—this is already to leak the celestial mechanism beneath words and reveal true wisdom before the assembly.
Today, as we begin the day by beating the drum to gather the multitude, tell me: what Dharma must be spoken? After a long silence, he said: "Great!"
"Assembly! A candela is one year older than a great lantern; a great lantern is one year older than an ancient Buddha; an ancient Buddha is one year older than empty space. Stop! Stop!
Had I not shouted 'Stop,' I would have nearly counted all the way back to myself. Then he descended from his seat.
On the first day of the New Year, Chan Master Nan Shiyou ascended the hall and said: "The beginning of the year inaugurates the reign; all things are renewed.
The year is new, the moon is new, the days are new, and the times are new. The great earth, the mountains, the rivers, and every creature, large and small, animate and inanimate—all are new.
But tell me, within the realm of the patch-robed monk, is there still anything new or old? With a shout, he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Yuzhi assembled the community for the New Year’s Day discourse: "The fleeting light of the passing years is like a swift arrow;
today once again marks the first day of the first month. On every door, peach-wood talismans are pasted; great ghosts and small ghosts have all fled and hidden away.

Yet there remains one man who does not conform to the cycles of Yin and Yang—his ancient countenance is majestic and grand, leaving no trace of his path. He is brighter than the sun and darker than lacquer."
Yulei’s eyes cannot see it; today he has been caught and defeated by this mountain monk. I have come specifically to deliver this news to you all.
*Pah!* In the Buddha Hall they offer prayers of praise; before the Sangha Hall they gather like clouds.
Chan Master Wququ (Wuqu) addresses the assembly on New Year’s Day: "Today is the first day of the three hundred and sixty days of the year.
In every household, the New Year is celebrated; throughout the empire, the imperial spring decree is put into practice. The officials of the entire realm offer prayers for the longevity of the Sage."
Upon the nine-layered halls of the Great Ming, before the ancestral shrines and administrative offices of the eight directions, clusters of brocade robes and rows of elegant jade pendants appear.

They bow deeply and turn respectfully, moving with measured grace; they dance amidst rising dust as the shouts of "Long Live! resound. The three hundred dignified gestures and three thousand ritual observances manifest all at once.
If one were to deliberate upon these as state ceremonies, it would not only betray the Tathāgata, but also contradict the Buddha’s own teachings.

Furthermore, there is no other Buddha-dharma. If one attempts to comprehend it through the lens of Buddha-dharma, one not only turns one's back on the Son of Heaven, but beyond that, there is no longer any national etiquette.
Ultimately, how can this be resolved? Only when ritual and dharma are brought together and flow as a single path can it be achieved.
Thereupon, he raised his whisk, bowed, and said: "The imperial domain is firm and secure; the Emperor’s Way flourishes afar. With the whisk, he struck once in a circle.
The Inscription: May the Sun of the Buddha increase its brilliance; may the Benevolent Wind forever spread.
On the New Year’s Day, Chan Master Mimi ascends the hall: A new year, a new moon, a new sun, a new season. The Elder has also donned a new Dharma robe.
Holding up the robe, he says: "This is the robe. What is the Dharma? He then lays down the robe and says: "Nine."
Nine hundred, one hundred, seven, Zhao, eight. It is still cold in the first month of spring; one must not expose the bones.
*Haha!* (A shout) Descend from the seat. Zen Master Ruohan asked: "As I ascend the seat for the New Year, I have a phrase that I did not speak last year."
I did not say it last year; I did not say it the year before last. Now that we have fortunately encountered this auspicious occasion and conditions, how could we simply cast it aside in indifference?
All you venerable seniors, stand firm and listen as I, the mountain monk, relate it for you.
Holding his staff horizontally, he said: "In the land of the Great Ming, fifteen years of the reign of the Sagely Son of Heaven, Emperor Chongzhen, have passed."
The sequence of the year meets its proper beginning; today is the first day. Ascending the hall on New Year’s Day:
he emerges as the foremost among all things, and the myriad nations are all at peace. In the morning, upon washing his face, he touches his nose; a fine breeze comes, clearing the doorway.
The lanterns listen intently and the pillars lean in to hear. Let forth the wood-gatherers and the cowherds.
Transverse and vertical, surpassing adversaries and startling the multitude; let it be—standing atop the highest mountain peak, walking at the bottom of the deepest waters.
Everyone holds hands in joyous peace. But as for this phrase "hold hands," how can one be certain? This year the silkworms and wheat have ripened.
Rāhula’s son was given one coin.
On the New Year’s Day, he ascended the hall and said: "The Patriarchal Heart-Seal is like the mechanism of an iron ox: when it moves, it is sealed; when it stays still, it is broken.
On the solitary peak, amidst the piercing cold, the bare hand is fully raised. As soon as you think, 'I am thus,' I am not thus. You..."
"In such a way, I am indeed in such a way. Here, host and guest interchange, and provisional and ultimate reality are both revealed.

To a clever monk, the distinction between black and white is naturally and utterly clear. Yet, if one were to swallow the whole date at once, one would inevitably fail the ancient sages and obscure one's own spiritual brilliance.
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth would obstruct the eye’s vision; light, darkness, form, and space would fill the breast. [This is] the thorny plum.
How can one swallow the brambles? How can one leap over the vajra-ring?
Linji’s Three Mysteries and Dongshan’s Five Ranks have been turned into superfluous teachings. Thus it is said: "To attain this in the mind, even the *eranda* tree becomes a sandalwood tree."
To miss the essential point is to treat ambrosia as a garden of thorns.

At this juncture, if there were suddenly a man to emerge who could take the head for the tail and the tail for the head—one capable of being a teacher to the Buddhas and Patriarchs and fit to serve as the eye for devas and humans—[he would truly have found it].

He hands over his *keng* (stone chime) and staff with both hands. "Is there anyone here? At the beginning of the new year, blessings are bestowed; all things flourish. May you receive protection in accordance with the season;
may there be no occasion for lack of celebration. With a shout, he descends from the seat.
Ascending the seat on New Year’s Day: penetrating to the very marrow, cutting off the myriad peaks, severing iron and chopping nails, he refines a single phrase.
By this he serves the state; by this he blesses the people; by this he benefits all living beings; by this he unfolds the ancestral laws of the house.
Directly, it is like the dragon’s roar that stirs the mist and the tiger’s cry that raises the wind; the myriad phenomena revolve in clarity, and the forest of existence shines with brilliance.

In every instance, reality is fully manifested; in every dharma, the truth is completely revealed. One thoroughly penetrates the supreme pivot of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and broadly displays the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye for humans and devas.
Even when letting go, not a single hair is moved; even when holding fast, how could its radiance ever be concealed? How clever!
Had Han Xiang possessed even one eye of insight, he would have been able to shoulder the fundamental principles and uphold the Great Dharma;
he would have assisted his teachers and supported the monastic communities. He could have taken a mustard seed and made it Mount Sumeru, or turned the long river into ghee and curd.

Thus, he would have celebrated the sagehood of the sovereign and delighted in the tranquil purity of the four seas, joining in the support of non-action and together illuminating the sun of transformation.
"Not something outside of one's capacity. But tell me, at such a time as this, is there anyone like that? He plants his staff and says:
"A single point of spring harmony provides the vital energy; the ten-thousand-year pine displays its form amidst snow and frost."
On the first day of the New Year, Chan Master Hongjue Mên ascended the hall and said: "The beginning of the year opens the reign; all things are renewed.

I respectfully wish that the Head Seat and the entire assembly may each enjoy ten thousand blessings in your practice and daily life. Suddenly, he clapped his hands and laughed heartily, saying, "A good laugh!
A good laugh! It makes one's bowels and sinews nearly snap. Tell me, what is this mountain monk laughing at? Yesterday..."
At the beginning of the fourth watch of the night, the Great King Yu, King Tang, and King Wu of Zhou joined together to pay their respects and celebrate the New Year.

Thereupon, they held a grand banquet atop Mount Yunmen in the Palace of the Jade Gate of the Great Heaven. When the wine was half-drunk, King Wu rose and urged them to drink, proposing a game of chance.
The theme for the rite was titled "Capturing the Scene of the New Year" and "Creating Wind at the Banquet. The victor—

He was exempted from drinking; those who carried the wine were punished by being made to drink it. Thereupon, he recorded these words: "Heaven opened in the month of Zi; Earth was laid open in the month of Chou; humanity was born in the month of Yin.
The Zhou calendar establishes Zi as its first month, representing the lineage of Heaven. The Shang calendar establishes Chou as its first month, representing the lineage of Earth.

The Xia calendar establishes Yin as its first month, representing the lineage of Humanity. Among the Three Powers (the Three Talents), Heaven is the head, Earth follows, and Humanity follows again. The King of Shang bore the penalty."
The Great King Yu of Xia was heavily intoxicated and ought to have drunk three large bowls of "Youth from Qingzhou.
As he was about to raise his cup, King Tang said, "I, Your Majesty, should not receive this penalty. The *Yi* says: 'When Qian is above Kun, it is called Pi (Stagnation);
when Kun is above Qian, it is called Tai (Prosperity). Does this mean that King Zhou of Zhou desired stagnation and did not desire prosperity? King Yu of Xia replied, "I, too, [desire prosperity]."
He should not be punished. The Book says: "Heaven sent down its people; it appointed for them rulers and teachers.

The Xia calendar begins with the month of Yin (the second lunar month) so as to facilitate the affairs of the common people. Therefore, when Yan Yuan asked about governing a state, the Master said, "Practice the time reckoning of the Xia.
Unaware that his words were loud enough to cause a commotion, he startled Shi Chenbo, who was sleeping in a mountain cave. Startled awake, Chenbo gave a great yawn.
He yawned and loudly chanted: "Within the cave there are no clouds; it is a world apart. Peach blossoms are like brocade; willows are like mist.

The immortals do not concern themselves with winter or summer; even when the rocks crumble and the pines wither, another year has passed. When the Three Emperors heard this, they found no ground for shame or embarrassment;
they immediately ordered the Cheshaja (Imperial Carriage Office) to turn the carriage and depart. Have any of you ever attained such [realization]?
"Do you understand yet? He gave a shout and said, "Except for Master Chen of Mount Hua, who among men does not walk about burdened by right and wrong?
On New Year’s Day, Chan Master Chaozong ascended the hall and, holding up the incense, said: "This one portion of incense is offered to prolong the life of the present [Emperor]."
"May the new Emperor’s sacred life be boundless. We humbly pray that he may clear away the demonic vapors of the four seas and fulfill the virtuous achievements of a great restoration.
(The dialogue is not recorded. He then said: "If one discusses this matter, it is like an old man and a young man passing a festival together;
it is all the same scene of New Year's Day. If it were a young man, he would perceive himself as..."
At present, the entire human realm has been transformed into something entirely new; even those things one previously loathed and discarded have suddenly changed their appearance.
All share in this celebration with immeasurable joy. This is truly what is called "a realm that cannot be described to others" and "a realm that cannot be presented to others.
If it were an old man, having experienced much already, although he too would join [in the celebration]...
In celebrating this occasion, one cannot help but maintain a state of universal equanimity. Thus it is said: "Though all under heaven may rejoice in their prosperity, I alone am unwilling. And again:
"An eighty-year-old elder entering the examination hall—this is truly no mere child’s play.
This is precisely the pivotal juncture from beginning to end for those who have come before. If you can penetrate these two barriers, then naturally...
"I have personally seen where the ancients stood. Nevertheless, what kind of person is it who is neither old nor young?
He suddenly said, "The Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the New Year cannot be spoken of too much.
Wait until you all have passed through these two barriers, and then I shall speak further to you. He then descended from his seat.
The Outline for the Day of Establishing Spring.
Chan Master Yuan of Changqing ascended the hall on the day of the commencement of spring and said: "The cold air is about to end and the spring day has arrived;
the tetherless iron ox leaps and bounds everywhere. Striking the nostrils of Kunlun, he topples Mount Sumeru into a heap of refuse. The cowherd boy—"
The whip has been cast aside; there is no need to blow the holeless flute. Clapping my hands, I laugh "he-he. Go back! Go back!
In the depths of the misty clouds, I lie down with my clothes on. After a long while, he said: "Be careful not to fall asleep!"
On the first day of spring, Chan Master Zhong’an Kong ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he struck it once and said, “First, strike the head of the spring ox.
He struck it again and said, “Afterward, strike the tail of the spring ox. Startled, the void enters within a lotus fiber;
Śākyamuni has no way to hide his tracks, and Maitreya flees in haste for a thousand miles. Only Mañjuśrī knows where it lands; clapping his hands, he laughs aloud.
He laughs with joy. But tell me, what is it that he rejoices in? "Last night, the spring breeze entered the gate;
immediately, a thousand blossoms sprang from the tip of the pestle.

This was the verse spoken by Chan Master Duanqiao Lun on the occasion of the Spring Festival, ascending the hall. He then cited Chan Master Daguan Ying’s address to the assembly, which began: "The Seven Buddhas..."
"This place is a slave; the myriad dharmas are the mind's servants. But tell me, where is the master?
He struck himself with his hand and shouted, "All Buddhas from the seventh patriarch downward have shown their heads! Then he answered himself, "Each attends to his own post.
The Master said, "He calls the seven Buddhas 'nature-slaves' and points to the myriad dharmas as 'mind-servants. Daguang claims for himself a way to emerge, yet when it comes to striking himself..."
"I accept. Furthermore, this is a matter concerning slaves; when has the master ever even dreamed of such a thing? "Assembly, do you wish to see it?
With his whisk, he makes a single sweep and says: "A spring breeze stirs at dawn, causing every kind of flower to bloom throughout the gardens."
Chan Master Xueyan Qin ascended the hall on the first day of spring: "The spring breeze blows vast and wide; the spring days shine with joy. Flowers bloom with smiling faces;
willows unfurl brows of delight. Everywhere purple swallows warble; everywhere yellow orioles sing their clear, melodious notes.
'Three pounds of flax,' 'a dried-up shit-stick,' 'the cypress tree in the courtyard'—if you can see it here, principle and phenomena are both complete, and there is neither right nor wrong."
Seated at the summit of Jiyun Peak, everyone celebrates together in this era of Great Peace.
On the occasion of the Spring Equinox, Master Chan Master Yuejiang Yin ascends the hall and says: "On the day of the Spring Equinox, all things are most auspicious.

Peach talismans are nailed to the gates; the pi-li flute is blown by the fences. As for those who study the profound mystery beneath the forest trees, they have mouths that hang only on the wall. The clay ox is whipped..."
Rising to pursue the spring plowing—his entire being is nothing but golden bone.
Master Chan Master Miyun Wu gave this lecture upon the arrival of Spring Equinox: "A single point of spring upon a shadowless branch; alas, the great earth is entirely buried in dust.
The old debts of years past were settled last night; it is a mistake to say that today is yet another new beginning. *He let out a shout.*
He said, "Lifting one's head to gaze beyond the heavens—who is such a person? He then gave a shout and descended from his seat.
On the Spring Equinox, Chan Master Yulin Xiu held a small assembly for private instruction on a certain matter. He said: "The spring wind blows; the spring rain moistens.
Suddenly, the gardens and groves are lush and lovely. Even the rootless tree blooms its flowers. Let us ask: do those of the Chan school understand this or not? He looked around.
The attendants said, "If you can understand this, the groves of the Buddha-dharma will flourish from time to time.
If you do not yet understand, there will be many sudden gales and torrential rains in the Zen forests during the late autumn. Brothers, take good care of yourselves;
do not be turned about by the force of the wind. He struck the meditation staff.
Chan Master Muyunmun ascended the hall and said: "Human Day and the Beginning of Spring: the universe is newly renewed; the snow melts and the ice dissolves, and the myriad trees flourish with joy.
At this very moment, the True Person of No Rank suddenly emerges from the face-gate, seizing hold of the entire world."
It is such that the sun and moon are not sufficient to be called bright; space is not sufficient to be called vast; Mount Tai is not sufficient to be called high;

and the rivers and seas are not sufficient to be called deep. When the black, vast earth fills the ditches and blocks the ravines—how then is there a single phrase that permits the letting go while not destroying worldly phenomena?
"The auspicious air urges the yellow birds; the clear light turns the green duckweed. Descend from the seat.
Ascending the hall on the Start of Spring: The subtle pivot of the spirit moves, and the four seasons shift. Between heaven and earth, it is like a bellows;
look, look—winter has arrived, and immediately the spring breeze comes. What you have learned upon the long meditation couch is the secondary mechanism.
As for the primary mechanism, not even the old patriarchs of the world have ever brought it forth; how then could this mountain monk?
To conclude: [The Master] raises his whisk and says, "Look! Look! A head painted in five colors, with a golden dot upon the forehead.
He strikes once more and says, "A fine spring ox has been smashed to pieces by a single whip from Mount Sengshan. Those who hear one and know two may manifest their bodies throughout the world;
those who mistake the shadow for the substance may let their eyes remain blurred with rheum as they please."
Small Assembly for the Start of Spring: Five nines make forty-five. A destitute man dances in the street. He dances—yes, he dances—and yet there is still the spring breeze of forty-five.
If one were to propagate this as mere worldly truth, a fine scripture would be ruined by a crooked-mouthed monk reciting it.
After all, what is the ultimate point? [He lets out a sneeze. "A sneeze on a spring morning brings good fortune in all matters."

I only wish that the eastern wind would exert its full power, So that spring’s beauty does not reside solely in Jiangnan.
Great assembly, when the fifty-nine days of winter end, spring arrives once more. In the blink of an eye, the peach blossoms turn crimson and the willows turn green; the white peony and the red...
The peony and the *bimba* fruit of the civil official—there will come a day when they bloom throughout the gardens and groves.
However, I do not know when the flower of the people's minds will manifest its brilliance.

Above, the heavens are vast and majestic; below, the earth is boundless and wide.

Within [the assembly] there were food jars and within them were vessels of broth; they were intoxicated by the eastern wind. "I pray that the eastern wind will swiftly manifest its power!
Hu-lu hu-lu! Now the eastern wind has already arrived; let us wait and see if it can exert its strength for everyone.
He took up his staff, descended from the seat, struck everyone at once, and returned to the Abbot’s quarters.
On the Lantern Festival Day, Master Wuzu Yan ascended the hall and gave this instruction: "Tonight is the fifteenth day of the first month; heaven and earth are one single expanse.
The gate of Samantabhadra stands wide open, yet though we meet, we do not see one another. He then asked: "In whom does the fault lie?"
Ascending the hall: This morning is the fifteenth day of the first month. I meet with all of you here; the tender wheat grows new sprouts, every grain of which shall become flour.
Whether it is offered or not, it relies entirely upon the fanning of the spring breeze.
Chan Master Dahuì Gǎo ascended the hall: "Today is the fifteenth day of the first month. There is an old public case:

light several bowls of lamps and strike the drum for a general invitation to look. Looking is not without its purpose; yet when suddenly the oil runs out and the lamp goes out, you must take care not to bump into a pillar in the darkness."
Ascending the hall: On this auspicious festival of the Lantern Festival, all share in joy; everywhere, endless lamps are lit.
The blazing firelight pierces the face of the Fiery Heat Deity, while the Night Goddess suddenly suffers from a cold headache. *Chan*.

Chan Master Ying’an Hua ascended the hall on the first day of the New Year and said: "Before the fifteenth day, they draw water and set fire; after the fifteenth day, the sparrows chirp and the crows caw.
On this very fifteenth day, the wind is calm and the waves are still; rain follows the season and wind is harmonious; the people are at peace and the state is prosperous.
There is a single phrase that reaches you—it would silence my mouth; yet there is not a single phrase that does not reach you."
"You! I will blind your eyes! For three copper coins you wed a black wife; she neither combs her hair nor washes her face.
Who knows whether she is a sage or a commoner? He suddenly struck the meditation seat once and said: "If one does not enter the startling waves, it is difficult to find a fish to one's liking."
Ascending the hall on the first day of the First Month: Last year there was no such snow; this year there is this snow.

Everyone laments this snow, saying they cannot see the lanterns and the moon of the Lantern Festival. Do not lament the snow; it is simply that people lack the power of discernment. Can you truly discern?
A single expanse of pure light rests in profound stillness.
On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, Chan Master Mimi Jie ascended the hall and said: "Today is the Lantern Festival; everywhere lanterns are hung.

One lamp kindles hundreds of thousands of lamps; from lamp to lamp they continue in succession, layer upon layer, inexhaustible like a net of precious jewels. Thus it is with the Buddhas of the three periods..."
The Buddha appears within the light and shadow; the six generations of patriarchs preach the Dharma and deliver sentient beings within the light and shadow;
the four sages and six classes of ordinary beings emerge and submerge within the light and shadow; the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are established within the light and shadow.
If you can believe this, you will find that the source from which these lights and shadows come is utterly unobtainable. Then, at once—

Seated, he cuts off the heads of both the *nirmāṇakāya* and *saṃbhogakāya* Buddhas. If you do not believe this, throughout the twelve periods of the day, you will be driven by shadows and light until you are thrown into sevenfold or eightfold confusion.
Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "Today is the fifteenth of the first month; let us all join in the communal request to look. The Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara of the past is within you."
All of you, do you see the light radiating from beneath your own feet that shakes the earth?
If you can see it, then even amidst these god-like and ghostly countenances, there has always been someone present. If you cannot see it, take care not to crash headlong into walls and barriers.
Shangyuan ascended the hall and said: "Before the fifteenth day, if brightness comes from the front, strike it with brightness.

After the fifteenth day, if darkness comes from the back, strike it with darkness. On the very fifteenth day itself, one lamp kindles hundreds of thousands of lamps; lamp after lamp continues on, penetrating and illuminating both the holy and the ordinary.
When Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva buys sesame cakes with money, why does he drop them as soon as he puts them down?"
Yet it is but an iron sour jujube. If one attempts to deliberate upon it as if it were the Buddha-dharma, it is truly beyond the reach of a spoon.

If one does not deliberate upon it as the Buddha-dharma, it will cause countless people to fall into a pit on level ground. To treat it as neither of these is likewise to suffer a heartache from overeating.
Descend from your seats.
On the Lantern Festival, Chan Master Wuyong ascended the hall and said: "This single point of luminosity has never been deceived by people throughout kalpas.
You of meager roots and shallow virtue merely seek it within the texts and commentaries of the scriptures, counting characters and tracing lines."
Piercing through confusion, piercing through confusion! Even if one possesses unimpeded eloquence, it is merely the attainment of dry wisdom;
one has wasted their time. Though there may be a thousand or ten thousand ways to do good, the Old Man today will not spare his verbal karma.
I strip away the lower skin for you and speak the matter through to its core: I bid you rest, I bid you cease. A single thought for ten thousand years;
ten thousand years within a single thought. This will not only be your sustenance for one lifetime, but will spare you from falling forever into the Yellow Springs.
Clever practitioners, lift up the lamp of the mind and illuminate the infinite and boundless! *He strikes his staff once and lets out a shout, saying:* "Investigate!"
The Master rose from his seat and departed.
Chan Master Xueyan Qin ascended the hall on the Lantern Festival. "On this auspicious occasion of the Lantern Festival, we are fortunate that the sky is clear.
High silver candles are lit to illuminate the radiance of the Buddha. At Jiyun Peak, not a single lamp lacks oil; it is most brilliantly radiant, far surpassing ordinary circumstances."
Why is this? I have seen that the lamp-light of the Buddha is such a manifestation of his original radiance and auspicious signs.
On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "Last year on the Lantern Festival, there was no oil to light the lamps;

this year on the Lantern Festival, there is the moon shining upon the high pavilions. Thus, the Bhaisajyaguru Vaidūryaprabhā Buddha manifests his dignified and wondrous form, each and every aspect appearing before all.
A great radiance is emitted from the eyebrows and eyelashes of human beings. Do you see it? If you see it, you are obstructed by seeing;
if you do not see it, you are obstructed by non-seeing. Cast away seeing and eliminate obstruction. The three gates face the Buddha Hall.
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: A lantern in the rain, a moon amidst the clouds—how most distinct and how brilliantly pure!
You people, hearing this being said, will likely think it is a dream within a dream. Little do you realize that within the thicket of brambles, there is a field and garden entirely apart.
Tell me, how far is this from the case of Yangshan? Different carts, yet the same ruts.

Chan Master Gaofeng Miao ascended the hall on the Lantern Festival and said: "To practice Chan, one must be a man of iron. When the hand touches the heart, judgment is made instantly. But consider this:

when snow covers the thousand mountains, why is the solitary peak not white? How do you judge it? He threw down his staff and said, "The Lantern Festival is certainly the fifteenth day of the first lunar month."
Chan Master Zhongfeng Ben’s Address to the Assembly on the Lantern Festival:
"Last night, the Tathāgata Sumeru-dīpa-rāja and the Buddha Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha met at the crossroads. They went hand in hand to view the lanterns of the Turtle Mountain (Àoshān).
Suddenly, they encountered an old man with bushy eyebrows and a snow-white head, who, before a hundred thousand people, spoke these four lines of verse: 'Only...'"
"The mind is itself Buddha; Buddha is nothing but the mind. This saying has been passed down from antiquity to the present. Facing it, one does not know that the lamp is fire;
in vain, one seeks only outwardly. At that moment, the two Tathāgatas could no longer restrain themselves and said in a stern voice:
"You are right," [the Master] said. "It is simply that you lack awakening. This very mind is Buddha; this very Buddha is the mind. To say it is so would be understood even by a three-year-old child.
Yet, alas, you do not awaken. To speak of food does not satisfy hunger. [The student] asked, "Please tell me the news of the moment of awakening.
The Master replied, "Let me try to clarify this with a metaphor. Suppose there is a person who has lost a pearl the size of a finger-joint. Although they search for it in a hundred..."
A thousand taels of gold would not suffice to weigh against its value. Had this jewel not been obtained, even ten thousand deaths could not have repaid it.
The resolve to seek it was engraved upon my lungs and liver, carved into my heart and marrow; it manifested in my dreams and permeated all that I saw and heard.
Moment by moment, I never forgot it, striving diligently without ceasing. If it were not obtained for a single day, the thought of it would occupy me for that very day.
Without ceasing, if one does not attain it in one year, the resolve for that year is not abandoned. One becomes increasingly diligent as one does not see progress;

one becomes ever more courageous and vigorous as one gains nothing. Eventually, emotions dissolve, conceptualizations are exhausted, the mind suffers, and the spirit is spent. Cold and heat are both forgotten, and sleep and food are entirely neglected.
After many years and accumulated months, right at the point where there is nothing to grasp, suddenly it is caught in hand—perfectly round and whole.
The light of *tathatā* (suchness) shimmers forth; at that moment, the mind that had for thirty years pursued [the truth] is suddenly and completely stilled—this is called awakening (*bodhi*).
When one searches for this pearl within the heart during a state of mental exhaustion and physical ailment, is this not "investigation" (*canyu*)?

When this pearl suddenly and abruptly manifests before the spirit and the intellect becomes clear, is this not "awakening"? If it were not for the difficulty of such investigative seeking, how could there be awakening?
There was this joy of realization and attainment. As we were discussing this, suddenly someone who could not tolerate it from the sidelines let out a shout that shattered everything.
Thereupon, the lamp was seen simply as a lamp, and the fire simply as fire; the towers and pavilions stood abruptly before one, while carriages and horses passed by in a blur.

Flowers bloom in orderly rows like golden lotuses; flames continue in endless strands like jade candles. Hu Zhangsan and Li Sisi—drunk, they are supported home from amidst the sea of ten thousand people.
Cha-sha Ghost and Da-zhailang—madness has not yet ceased in the arena of a hundred performances.
At such a time, how can one present the phrase for "joyfully sharing the bottomless ground," which does not involve awakening or delusion? It is filled with lapis lazuli.
The belly harbors the bright moon; his lotus-like body radiates precious light throughout.
Chan Master Wuwen Can ascended the hall on Lantern Festival and, raising his whisk, said: "Fat, yet no surplus flesh; thin, yet no exposed bone.

[The Master] sighed: "To say 'it is not the mind, not the Buddha, not a thing'—this is it.
Chan Master Baizhang of Foguo Monastery ascended the hall and said: "The past has already passed; do not calculate the future.

"It is not non-existent. After all, what do you call the moon? Cease seeking it in the heavens; do not look for it in the water.

Chan Master Fatai ascended the hall and said: "Today is the middle of the first month. Everywhere the lanterns and torches flicker in confusion; throughout the city, silks and brocades are gathered in dense crowds.

Zen Master Zhūquánlín ascends the hall for the Lantern Festival: "Today is the Yuanxiao Festival; the snow has cleared and spring reveals its brightness. The Dharma...

Chan Master Tianmu Li ascended the hall on the Lantern Festival. "The fifteenth day of the third month, the Lantern Festival: Lanterns are lit to dispel the chill of night.
The people of the entire city enjoy it together, Singing and rejoicing until dawn. The ancient Buddhas bustle about as they light their lamps, Yet not a single person recognizes them.
Tell me, does Guangshou recognize them or not? He then said, "Not recognized, not recognized."
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: Last night, Dharma Master Madhyāntika lit lotus lamps everywhere to assist the Buddha’s radiance, until even the Real Person of Good Faith lost his luster.

Then the Dragon King Taibai came forth and said, "Since the time of the Buddha King of the Dragon Seed, I have dwelt upon this mountain; I have never heard such news. Thereupon, amidst the air, [he] struck—
A flash of lightning transforms into a sky filled with black winds and torrential rain. Do you understand this thoroughly? I see that the lamp of the Buddha is bright;
its original radiance and auspicious signs are just like this.
Chan Master Yuansou Duan’s Hall Discourse on the Lantern Festival, and the Expression of Gratitude to the Receiver of Offerings, the Bath Master, and the Rector:
"A thousand grains and ten thousand grains are born from a single grain. From where does this single grain arise? A thousand lamps and ten thousand lamps arise from a single lamp.
From where does this single lamp arise? If you understand this one lamp, then the thousand lamps and ten thousand lamps—lamp after lamp—are not [separate]."
Doubt! Once you recognize a single grain, then a thousand grains, ten thousand grains—grain after grain—is without obstruction. A three-legged donkey trots along, kicking up its hooves;
it tramples through the boundless seas of fragrant water. I take up my staff and strike it once: even at the crown of the head, one cannot do without this single blow.
At the Lantern Festival, the Master ascended the hall and said: "The entire earth is a single lamp.

step back, and you break the spine of Bodhidharma. Neither advancing nor retreating, sit still upon the heights of Linji and Deshan."
At the tip of the nose. Furthermore, how can one attain evenness and breadth? After a long silence, he said: "When the ocean dries up, its bottom will finally be seen;
when a person dies, their mind is not known.

On the Lantern Festival, Chan Master Shikong of Dinghui gave a discourse from the high seat: "The first month moon is full, and the reflections in the hundred rivers are clear; a single lamp is lit..."

If one can attain such a state, one may dwell amidst clamor and enter into the secular world, deploying the light of great compassion throughout the *sahasra-lokadhātu* and opening the eye of the Universal Gate for all living beings.
How could this be limited merely to the thirty-two kinds of wondrous and unimpeded responses of the Great Being Avalokiteśvara? It is fully [attained].
Each and every one of the bound ordinary beings can open the eye of the True Dharma.
Nevertheless, even so, it must be a man who cuts through nails and chops iron before he succeeds. If it were otherwise, then *svāhā* in a quiet place!
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun ascended the hall on the Lantern Festival: "The moon is full in the heavens; the lamps shine brightly among men.
This reality from kalpas past is not separated by so much as a speck of dust. Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell; where there is no Buddha, pass quickly by."
Invitation to the Head of the Rear Hall for the Lantern Festival: A single bowl of lamp-light since vast kalpas past— How many have known it to illuminate heaven and earth?
If you wish to see the inexhaustible place of transmission, It is at the moment of awakening from the dream within Tuṣita Palace.
Chan Master Yuejiang Yin ascends the hall on the Lantern Festival: "Today is the fifteenth day of the first month. Everywhere there are village songs and community dances.

Startled, the carp of the Eastern Sea swallows the fierce tiger of the Southern Mountain. I report to you all: do not be so reckless! I...
Seeing the lamp-light of the Buddha, the original radiance of the auspicious omen is thus.
This was used by Zen Master Jun to ascend the hall for the Lantern Festival. Before lighting the lamps: form and emptiness, light and darkness, are both without partiality.

After lighting the lamps: the great earth, mountains, and rivers run topsy-turvy. At the very moment of lighting the lamps: amidst ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences, there is a single path of clarity. Fire.
The illuminating fire is like broad daylight; light swallowing light reveals the true lamp. [The Master] strikes the whisk and descends from the seat.

Lantern Festival, ascending the hall: The Buddha takes one ray of light and disperses it into hundreds, thousands, ten millions, and billions of rays—this is called manifesting an auspicious sign (*śubha-nimitta*).
Ruyuan takes hundreds, thousands, ten millions, and billions of fundamental rays of light and gathers them into a single ray—this, too, is called manifesting an auspicious sign. Ancient...

Today’s moon and sun; the mountains and rivers of past and present; the light of past and present (the auspicious omens of past and present). Tell me, are the light of the lamp and the Buddha-light the same as, or different from, the light of Ruiyan?
In Guangnan, one enjoys the cool air on New Year’s Eve; on Mount Wutai, it snows in the sixth month.
Chan Master Chushi Qi ascended the hall for the Lantern Festival: "From within the furnace of blazing flames, one scoops up the moon;
this moon is utterly without waxing or waning. From the bottom of the great ocean, one strikes a golden lamp; this lamp is not subject to darkness or light.
Precisely on the fifteenth day of the first month, neither heaven nor earth can encompass it. Black as lacquer, yet bright as the sun—who has known it from antiquity to the present?"
"Who gains and who loses? All are the constant portion of my own mind; there is nothing borrowed from external arts. (He lets out a shout.

**Lantern Festival, Ascent to the Hall:** "Today is the fifteenth day of the first month. Lanterns and moonlight are in disarray. Not a single thing exists before one's eyes—beat the drum and let everyone come to look!
He spoke again: "Pierce through the eyes!"
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: All moons take the single moon as their reality; all lamps take the single lamp as their essence.
One is all, and all is one. From where does this "one" arise? To even attempt to provide a commentary here would be a mistake.

Ascending the hall for the Lantern Festival Repentance Assembly: There is a person who possesses the great icchantika nature, commits the karma of immediate retribution, abandons precepts, concentration, and wisdom, and practices greed, anger, and delusion.
They plant thorns in the field of the three realms of existence and sow brambles upon the ground of the one true reality;
they even slander the Buddha, destroy the Dharma, and break the harmony of the Sangha. It would be better for such a person to sink into the depths for eternal kalpas than to seek [the Way].
"Noble Liberation! One must wait until all sentient beings have attained Buddhahood before awakening the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
I do not yet know how this person should perform repentance. After a long silence, [the Buddha said]: "The cauldrons of boiling water and the furnaces of burning coals shall be blown out;
the sword-trees and knife-mountains shall be shouted down into ruin."
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: First we celebrate the New Year’s dawn, and now it is the midpoint of the first month.
Look and see how the hundred grasses grow; in a flash, the three seasons have changed. Worldly affairs are as dense as hemp; time passes as busily as a drill.
