Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Today is once again the Dragon Boat Festival. Mañjuśrī and Sudhana are in a state of constant bustle. The medicine that kills and the medicine that brings life are both ineffective;
it only adds three catties of iron behind one's head. Suddenly grasping his staff, he struck it once on the ground and said:
"The wondrous power of Avalokiteśvara’s wisdom can save the world from suffering. He then threw the staff down and asked: "What is this? An iron snake drills into the earth."
Chan Master Ying’an Hua ascended the hall on the Dragon Boat Festival: "The fifth day of the fifth month is the Dragon Boat Festival.
When a matter of great significance is manifest before one’s eyes, it cannot be concealed. Guizong thrusts his staff out from the tip of his head; idle gods and wild ghosts are all extinguished.
The cold spring at the foot of the steps suddenly flows backward; the white clouds atop the ridge dare not be white. He then cited the story of how one day Mañjuśrī commanded Sudhana...
Mañjuśrī said, "Gather whatever you consider to be medicine and bring it here. Sudhana searched everywhere; there was nothing that was not medicine.

He returned and reported, "There is nothing that is not medicine. Mañjuśrī said again, "Bring whatever you consider to be medicine. Sudhana plucked a single blade of grass and presented it to Mañjuśrī.
Mañjuśrī held it up and showed it to the assembly, saying, "This medicine can both kill and can also bring life."
The Master said, "Great Mañjuśrī has had his eyes changed by Sudhana. He descended from the seat.
On the Dragon Boat Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "One, two, three, four, five; five, four, three, two, one.

Examining this from beginning to end, it makes Vimalakīrti laugh to death and brings trouble upon Li Huzi, whose whiskers get soaked as he sprays water. The ritual of sprinkling purity is now complete. Next...
"Smṛti-pāramitā. Thus spoke Jiangshan. "Who in ten thousand ages can recognize it? Whether recognized or not, where can it be sought?
It is fit to serve as a model for the monastic community. Suddenly he took up his staff, struck it once, and said: "Swiftly, as by imperial decree!"
Chan Master Antai delivered a lecture on the Dragon Boat Festival: "Today, throughout the world, is the Dragon Boat Festival; originally, the enlightened nature has no gate or door.
Wild ghosts and idle spirits vainly show their heads; red mouths and white mouths are but empty old crones. In ordinary life, we do not further nail up peach-wood talismans;
our command is simply to beat the 'poison-coating' drum. If you hear its sound with your ears or see it with your eyes, you may take it for certain—"
Transcending Buddhas and Patriarchs in every direction:
Chan Master Miam Jie’s Dharma Hall discourse on the Dragon Boat Festival. On the fifth day of the fifth month, the Dragon Boat Festival, dark clouds gather and sweet rain has not yet fallen.
The King has bestowed precious incense; the prayers offered by those beneath the forest trees are most earnest. May the dragon deities grant their protection and blessings.
The Seasons: May a single rain well nourish what is parched and withered; may its pervasive coolness dispel vexation and heat. I recall a monk asking Qianfeng:
"The Bhagavāns of the ten directions all share the one path to the gate of Nirvāṇa. I wonder, where does the beginning of that path lie?"
Qingfeng drew a line with his staff and said, "It is right here. Later, a monk requested further instruction from Yunmen.
Yunmen held up the fan in his hand and said, "This fan leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens, striking the nose of Śakra.
An eel from the Eastern Sea receives a blow of the stick, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin. "O Great Assembly! Qingfeng shakes his head; Yunmen wags his tail."
From antiquity to the present day, it has hung upon the lips and teeth of men. At Jingshan, there is a branch to grasp; he brandishes his staff and hurls it down, saying:
"If you understand this, look at the clouds and thunder rising from the earth."
Chan Master Doushuai Huizhao ascended the hall and, raising his whisk, said: "On the fifth day of the fifth month, Long’an also rows its oars;

amidst the clouds of the green mountains, one finds carefree ease. With hunger satisfied and thirst quenched, there is infinite joy—who would love to vie for first place and snatch the silken banner?"
Yet he rows his boat upon dry land; waves rise atop the high mountain peaks. He beats the jade drum in broad daylight and unfurls the iron banner in the dark.
With a single cup of calamus tea and several sugar-filled *zong* dumplings, let us move from North Uttarakuru to come and compete for the forehead-mark with South Jambudvīpa.
[He struck the meditation seat and descended.]
Chan Master Xueyan Qin ascended the hall on the Dragon Boat Festival and said: "The sky is vast and distant; the clouds drift on and on.
Bottomless waves roll like snow as dragon boats race against one another. At such a time, it is truly laughable that the Great Official of Chu, Sanlu, is being drowned in stagnant waters.
Drowned he may be, yet he cannot be killed. Through ten thousand generations, the Xiang River remains wide and expansive."
Chan Master Tieguanshu ascended the hall for the Dragon Boat Festival: "Today is the fifth day of the fifth month. The drum that shakes the heavens is struck.
I raise my whisk, and set out a bottomless platter, filled to the brim with golden millet. Zen followers, your teeth are as hairless as wooden boards; reaching this point, how will you swallow it?
If you can swallow it, then Grand Master Bodhidharma was not the Patriarch."
Chan Master Zhongfeng Ben’s Address to the Assembly on the Dragon Boat Festival: In the records of Spring, Autumn, and Summer, the month of the fifth lunar month is not recorded.

Those who compile the annals have thus doubted a textual omission. Whether it is an omission or not, the "Stone Gendan" at the crossroads of the ten directions will unrestrainedly display its demonic antics before people:

riding backward upon a tiger made of mugwort up to the high towers, with divine talismans hanging from its back as it employs wondrous incantations to restrain malicious speech and eliminate calamities.
A white-tongued man collected five-colored coins from every door, thinking no one could discern their true value.
Suddenly, the Master Wu-shou split open his chest and seized him, dragging him into the eye of a gnat. Yet he has leaked much of the True Mechanism;
but where did this leakage occur? A single pomegranate tree in the courtyard—when the morning sun shines upon it, it blooms as if drenched in crimson.
Blood.
On the Dragon Boat Festival, Chan Master Qianyan Chang ascended the hall and said: "In summer, eating wheat porridge; atop one's head, a thatched hut;
the latrine is dripping with rain; there is nowhere to set foot. Within it dwells an old *dhūta* practitioner—how could he be called a venerable elder? It may be so.
I pity all you fellow practitioners of meditation; you insist on crowding together. Although there is nothing to enjoy, I am glad that you are harmonious with one another.
The healthy work together to complete the tasks, while the sick are served water and beans. Today is the Dragon Boat Festival; there is neither wine nor meat.
I bring forth a single cup of tea, overflowing with the jade-like calamus. Tell me, what business is accomplished by this? If human relations are good, it is enough.
The water one drinks is sweet.
On the Dragon Boat Festival, Chan Master Weian ascended the hall and said: "Eat a bowl of yellow-rice *zong* dumplings; drink half a cup of calamus tea.
This is the auspicious season for a patch-robed monk (*na-seng*). Let us all meet and eat our fill, snoring contentedly. Free and easy in every direction. Thus it is.

They delight in freedom. To speak of Yangshan’s clearing of the wasteland, Muzhou’s wild ox, Heshan’s beating of the drum, and Xuefeng’s rolling of the ball—all these are merely the miscellaneous plays of children;
they are certainly not the ancestral lineage of the former worthies. As for the single phrase, "On the fifth day of the fifth month, the calamity is concealed"—how would you handle this?
When there is nothing strange before one's eyes, there is no need to paste up a Zhong Kui.
Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth Festival: Everywhere else they drink calamus tea; I alone pour the wine of Qingyuan.
In a state of wild and chaotic madness, I knock down the Southern Dipper along with the Northern Dipper. [He] throws down his staff and descends from the seat.
On the Dragon Boat Festival, Chan Master Nan Shiyou ascended the hall and said: "In every household, people hang mugwort and tiger figurines;
Lingyan, however, simply drinks calamus tea. Do not say it is bland and lacks flavor; after all, this is the true style of one who has mastered the house."

Chan Master Liaoyuan Yu ascended the hall and said: "To awaken to the Way upon hearing a sound, or to clarify the mind upon seeing a form—when magpies chirp, crows caw, the wind stirs, and dust rises—to speak of dreams before a deluded person is not permitted.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Zhaozhou replied, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. A deep mountain hides a solitary tiger; shallow grass reveals a swarm of snakes.
The annual Festival of the Heavens. Finely slice calamus and steep it in strong tea.

[The Master] descends from his seat and ascends the hall. On the fifth day of the fifth month, the Festival of the Heavens: no talismans are written, no secret hand-gestures are formed. Let the mind-ground be released so that it is vast and level;
a hundred monsters and a thousand demons will naturally vanish. Have you not seen how Mañjuśrī once commanded Sudhana to gather medicinal herbs?
Sudhana said, "There is nothing that is not medicine. Mañjuśrī said, "Bring me some of this medicine.
Sudhana plucked a blade of grass and handed it to Mañjuśrī. Mañjuśrī accepted it and showed it to the assembly, saying, "This medicine can both kill people and bring them to life.
Master Tiandong Huihua said, "How great Mañjuśrī was! He had his eyes changed by Sudhana."
"Great assembly! The old man Yanguan might well be called a patriarch for a hundred generations, yet he only knows one thing and does not know the second.
This mountain monk says: 'A single hand cannot clap alone; both hands together ring out a resounding clatter.
A board-carrying Chan practitioner has the breath of an ox, yet when he lifts his head, he only says the world is too narrow. *He!* "
Ascending the hall: Time and season allow no indulgence; today is the fifth day of the fifth month. To the east, peach talismans are nailed; to the west, mugwort tigers are hung.
Even atop the solitary peak and its highest summit, one must still rely upon a single path. Raising the Mount Sumeru mallet, let us strike the drum of empty space.
With a turn of the body, we leap over the Gate of Ghosts; throughout the great earth and its mountains and rivers, there is not a single inch of soil. *Hè!* (A shout) — he descends.
The Seat.
Chan Master Guanghui Baolin ascends the hall on the Double Fifth Festival. Today is the fifth day of the fifth month; who among you does not behold the numinous sprouts of the hundred grasses?
When Shancai gathers medicinal herbs with Mañjuśrī, killing and giving life are applied according to the occasion, each acting as host to the other. You followers of the Chan school, do not...
Rough and coarse. Look well, raising your eyebrows for a moment. Picking it up at random with the hand, you know there is no rejection;
the sweet is sweet and the bitter is bitter.
On the Dragon Boat Festival, Chan Master Yuandao of Yuansou gave this discourse: "The fifth day of the fifth month is the Dragon Boat Festival; the mugwort tiger and peach talisman."
Stop speaking altogether. Fengshan is simply this Vajra King; all manner of monsters and demons are utterly extinguished.
In Jiangnan and Liangzhe, it is cold in spring and hot in autumn. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva buys sesame cakes with money; when he lets go of his hand, they turn out to be nothing but cast iron.
Ascending the hall on the festival of the fifth day of the fifth month: "Zhongfeng, today is the fifth of the fifth month. There are no peach talismans nor mugwort tigers.
Directly facing reality, one immediately knows the pivot; Sublime function is纵横 (transverse and vertical), beyond all location. You practitioners of the patched robe, do not be reckless!
The sweet melon is sweet through to the stem; The bitter gourd is bitter down to the root."
On the Dragon Boat Festival, Chan Master Shuzhong Yun ascended the hall. He said: "Master Longya once said: 'To study the Way, one must first have an awakening;
it is like competing for speed in a dragon boat race. Though it may be old ground and an empty field, only after winning it once can one finally rest.
Great and small, Longya’s realization was not yet free; he sat right there. This mountain monk does not begrudge his own eyebrows."
For his sake, he cleared away a path. Immediately, one sees that his merit transcends all and his Way is beyond words and names.
He then said: "Delusion and awakening have always been entirely free; one must simply row a boat upon level ground. Heaven and earth are vast and undivided, without past or present;
the pure breeze of a thousand years never ceases. Suddenly, someone came forward and said: "Ruigan is merely nailing down a stake and shaking it."
Lü. A-he-he! I thought there was no one here. [He] then descended from his seat. Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth:
On the fifth day of the fifth month, the Dragon Boat Festival, The songs and pipes resound by the riverbanks as the boats race.
Patch-robed monks together sip calamus tea; Boundless fragrance arises upon their lips and tongues. A hundred ailments are eliminated; A thousand demons are utterly destroyed.
Mañjuśrī instructed Sudhana to gather medicinal herbs. Sudhana picked up some grass and handed it across to Mañjuśrī, who planted it upon a rock where flowers immediately blossomed.
Mañjuśrī received it and showed it to the assembly, saying, "This medicine can both kill people and bring them back to life. He then drove a wooden stake into the air.
Looking around to his left and right, he said, "Is there anyone here who can act as a witness for Mañjuśrī and Sudhana? He let out a shout.
This was used to illustrate Zen Master Yongchang’s Dharma hall discourse on the Dragon Boat Festival. He cited the Fifth Patriarch’s public address on the same occasion:

"In the past, there was a scholar who composed a treatise denying the existence of ghosts. As soon as he finished writing it and set down his pen, a ghost appeared and, raising its hand, struck the scholar."
"You say, 'What can you do to me? If Baiyun had seen him at that time, he would have made a hand into a magpie's beak and said to him, 'Gu-gu-gua' (the sound of a magpie).
[The Master] picks this up and says: "The theory of no ghosts is established; the ghost has manifested its form. Set it aside and do not ask.
Wuzu making a hand into a magpie's beak was likewise following the heterodox and pursuing the evil. In the house of Ruiyan, there is no *Bai-ze* (White Deer) talisman.
Illustration. Furthermore, there were no such demons or spirits.
On the Dragon Boat Festival, Chan Master Tianmu Li gave a lecture from the high seat. "The moon reaches the month of Ruyin; the festival arrives at the Double Fifth.

We do not race dragon boats, nor do we beat the clamor of the *táo* drums. Here in the mountains, I pluck medicinal herbs as they come to hand. Holding up his whisk, he said, "Do you see? It was also thus.
It can kill a person and it can also bring a person to life. If this were not so, then calamus would float in bitter tea and *jiaoshu* would grease human teeth.
(He strikes the whisk once.)
Chan Master Xiaoyin Yun gave this Dharma talk on the Dragon Boat Festival: "The entire great earth is medicine; it is the grass one picks up with the hand at random.
Manjusri and Sudhana—one falls down together, then another falls. If you can apply the principle and transform through understanding, then ask further of Old Zhongfeng:
whether hungry or full at midday, or plagued by mosquitoes and fleas at night—seeking such things as one pleases only adds to one's daily vexation."
Annoyance. It is better to have no affairs than to have affairs that do not go well.
On the Dragon Boat Festival, Chan Master Chu Shi Qi ascended the hall and said: "Today is the fifth day of the fifth month.

If we do not beat the hoeing drum, our own fields will fall into ruin and the master of the house will lose his flavor. I inform all of you: do not be reckless! Let the malicious mouths and slanderous tongues be entirely exhausted."
Elimination. The True Person of No Station breaks into a sweat like rain.

Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth Festival: Today is the fifth day of the fifth month. The mugwort man rides upon a mugwort tiger; he dashes about in every direction—north, south, east, and west—and returns to say:
"All sentient beings throughout the great earth are suffering. That is to say: the suffering of birth, the suffering of old age, and the suffering of illness.
From the suffering of death to the suffering of the five aggregates in their fullness—all such sufferings can be healed.
Only the mental illness of a Zen practitioner is most difficult to heal; it cannot be treated with arsenic, rock honey, licorice, or tangerine peel.
How, then, can it be healed? I have an ancient prescription that there is nothing it cannot cure. A monk asked Zhaozhou: "A student has just..."
When a monk entered the assembly to beg for the Master’s skillful means, Zhaozhou asked, "Have you finished eating your congee? The monk replied, "I have finished eating my congee.
Zhaozhou said, "Go wash your bowl. Having finished the congee and washed the bowl, there is no need for doubt. When the whale swallows the ocean until it is empty, the coral branches are revealed.
[The Master] clapped his hands and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Yuguan Jie ascended the hall on the Double Fifth, the Duanwu Festival. "In my decrepit old age at Mount Jing, I have no dharma to speak.
Everyone, drink this cup of calamus tea; its single flavor should not be distinguished. As for making distinctions, that is up to you all.
But tell me, what is its ultimate flavor? After a long silence, he said, "If human feelings are good, even drinking water is [enlightenment]."
Féi. On the Dragon Boat Festival, Chan Master Wén Càn ascended the hall. No talismans were inscribed; no herbs were gathered.

To raise the dead and ward off misfortune—he held up his staff and said, "Fortunately, there is this. With a thud, he struck it down: "Throughout the entire monastery, the fragrant breeze blows as the summer days grow long. People—
At the Lotus Fragrance World Monastery, Chan Master Dongsou Ying ascended the hall. He struck the drum, and the assembly gathered; their ears heard together and their eyes saw together.
Transcending heaven and earth and surpassing past and present—why is it so? The fifth day of the fifth month is the Dragon Boat Festival.
On the Day of the Dragon Boat Festival, Chan Master Xiaran Bao addressed the assembly. He cited Master Dahui Zonggao’s discourse from the hall: "Today is once again the fifth day of the fifth month.
The great ghosts clap their hands and the small ghosts dance. Suddenly they run into the deity of the peach-wood talisman;
both hands beat upon their chests as they cry out in grievous suffering. The Master said, "Great Assembly, when Dahui spoke in this way, it was as if he were lacking something essential."
[The questioner asks: "What do you mean by this? Xiangqian said: "In the midst of the blue sky and bright sun, one sees gods and ghosts.

Xiaoyan said: "I am not like that. This very day is the fifth of the fifth month. Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. I, this mountain monk, wish to gamble with all the great sages and ordinary beings present here from the ten directions.
Picking up whatever comes to hand at the tip of a hundred grasses—what is sweet is sweet, and what is bitter is bitter."
He held up his staff and said: "Suddenly emerging is this one single thing that pierces through all the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past.
You people here before me possess everything in a hundred ways; why is it that you alone lack this one thing?
Suddenly, someone from among the assembly—a man of righteous courage—might spring forward in indignation and say: "Master, do not speak in your sleep! As for this..."
"This is one thing. I dare say that every person present here lacks not even a hair’s breadth. The Master set down his staff and smiled, saying, "You simply do not understand.
You are adding a point to an arrowhead; you are piling more earth upon a mound."
Chan Master Zhanyan Cheng ascended the hall on the Double Fifth Festival: "The fifth day of the fifth month, the Midsummer Festival.
Red mouths and white tongues are all extinguished. Peach-wood talismans and *ài* tigers fill one’s head; realgar and calamus are mixed with wine and swallowed.
Drunk and intoxicated, one knows not that the years and months pass by. A thousand monsters and a hundred spirits are all driven away. Who cares whether demons come or Buddhas come? All together—"
Lift up the forehead! O assembly, why is it so? Have you not heard it said: "To protect life, one must kill; only when killing is exhausted does one dwell in peace"?
Do you wish to know the principle of this killing? Seizing this auspicious occasion, take mugwort leaves for banners and calamus for swords;
with a fierce and sharp mind, summon the courage of a hero, and disregard right and wrong, gain and loss, or sage and ordinary person.
Regarding truth and falsehood, and even all the bandits of affliction—greed, anger, ignorance, and craving—one must raise the sword and cut them through both ways at once.
Only then can one attain a state that is utterly pure, naked, and bright; perfectly round and lively.
Become such a great man of the mundane and supramundane realms. Brothers, is there anyone like this? Is there anyone who has truly attained such a state? If you have not attained it...
"Mòdì! I, this mountain monk, have a protective talisman to send along with you. He picks up his staff and says, "Look, look!
The Most High Lord Laojun’s urgent decree, swift as the imperial command!"
Chan Master Zhuo’an ascends the hall on the Dragon Boat Festival: "The divine blade is sharp and piercing; a precious sword stands guard at the pass.
A hundred monsters hide their tracks, and all demons vanish from sight. This is not something created by effort, nor does it belong to any contrived arrangement.

It does not pass through stages of achievement, nor does it follow any path. Moving forward, it is pitch black; retreating, it is perilous. With a single stroke, enter directly; manifesting the essence, it is fully raised. No matter how many times it is broken..."
Cast from the very essence of the Great Unity, the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are all phenomena; light and darkness, form and emptiness are all phenomena.

Dust upon dust, world-system after world-system, they encompass all existence and unify the six voids. What do you call "mountains, rivers, and the great earth"? What do you call "light and darkness, form and emptiness"?
At times they are alert and awake, at times they are tranquil and still; internally and externally they are fused and transparent, manifesting throughout.
It is like being inside a cave. Upon arriving here, the Buddhas of the three periods of time and the black oxen and white cows are simultaneously attained and simultaneously lost;
they are simultaneously illuminated and simultaneously employed. Whether you people recognize this or not, it is perfectly manifest beyond the limit of Vipaśyin Buddha;
even now, at the threshold of affairs, there has never been a different path. This mountain monk, without hindrance, responds to the times and seasons, and for your sake—
All the people go forth together, hand in hand. [The Master] picks up his whisk and says: "The chrysanthemums and hibiscus are red as fire; the mugwort and artemisia are green as a carpet.
This was the sermon given by Chan Master Muchunmen on the Double Fifth Festival. On the fifth day of the fifth month, the Dragon Boat Festival. Composed by Xinyue Yuzhu.
Though one may not taste the *jiao-shu* (zongzi) of Chan-joy, one must guard against choking on the rice from the *du-tian* fields. Set down the chopsticks;
the belly is already full. At midday, the sun’s orb is shining brightly. Picking up the *pu-jian* (rush-sword), one cuts off the head of the snake;
idly watching children fight with the hundred grasses, one finds a single stalk in the hand of Sudhana—one that can kill and can bring life, no ordinary thing.
The fundamental medicinal herbs cure all ailments; there is none that they do not benefit. They reside solely upon the mountain monk’s staff—there is no need for you all to seek them elsewhere.
On the occasion of the Double Fifth Festival (Tianzhongjie), Chan Master Hongjue Man invited the Head Seat to ascend the hall [and preach]: "Lone loyalty has yet to be understood by the sovereign."
Clutching my resentment, I would rather willingly sink into the waters of the Chu and Xiang rivers. The fire-house is ablaze and I am lost as to the way out;
how could this single mind not turn back in alarm? There is a certain way of speaking: the three realms are like flowers in the sky, and the four modes of birth are like dreams and illusions.

Fundamentally, there is no person capable of escaping, nor is there any place from which to escape. It simply requires realizing emptiness and penetrating the illusory nature of dreams and awakening. The mountain monk says:
"Excellent! How does one awaken from a dream? How does one penetrate an illusion? How does one realize emptiness? Exert yourselves together; do not be dilatory.
Cut through the surging waves like flying arrows and dance upon the dragon-ship that spans the sea.
Only when you have won the brocade of Vulture Peak shall you truly believe that a man must strive for himself. He let out a shout. He then raised the case of how one day Mañjuśrī commanded Sudhana:
Wenshu said, "As for this medicine, go and gather it. Sudhana looked everywhere across the great earth and found nothing that was not medicine.
He returned and reported, "There is nothing that is not medicine. Wenshu said, "Then gather whatever is medicine and bring it here.
Sudhana then plucked a blade of grass from the ground and handed it to Wenshu. Wenshu received it, held it up, and showed it to the assembly.

He said: "This medicine can kill a person and it can also bring a person back to life. The Master said: "A medicine that has efficacy is not spiritual; only when there is no illness is it truly sacred.
Let us set aside for now the matter of Sudhana’s heated deception of Mañjuśrī and Mañjuśrī’s heated deception of Sudhana. [The Master] then raised his whisk and said:
As for this single blade of grass, where does its benefit or harm lie? It can both kill a person and bring a person to life.
Do you wish to recognize the source and understand the details? Go ask the first seat in the hall.
The Outline for the Green Sprouts Assembly (June; with the Opening, the Dispersal, and the Attached "Roasting Egg") Chan Master Tong of Huazang ascends the hall for the Green Sprouts Assembly:
"Shatter a single mote of dust and the Great Sutra emerges; the soaring kites and leaping fish become even more distinct.
If you do not look with your eyes but look with your mind, you have already struck ice within the fire once again. [The text ends with: *Yanhei* (Drowned in Black).
Soybeans. Having been ignorant of them all my life, I must now speak of a bountiful harvest beyond the kalpas: the white snow is spun into thread as the mulberry turns green again;
the yellow clouds are harvested until the rice stands a fresh green.
Chan Master Daomeng Tai ascended the hall at the Qingmiao Assembly. Deshan, upon entering the gate, would immediately strike—creating a mound where there was no ground.
Linji, upon entering the gate, would immediately shout—raising waves where there was no wind. Jueyi merely held up a single finger, which cannot avoid being called superficial.
Xuefeng rolled out three balls, which was but the play of a child. Arriving here, none of these are of any use; how can they compare to this?

In the third heat-wave period of the sixth month, sweet rain nourishes all things universally. The waters suffice the eastern marshes; the grain turns green in the southern fields. Farmers drum upon their bellies and wood-gatherers sing aloud.
The ancestral style of the ancient Buddhas remains as if present before us. If one realizes this at such a time, we may together rejoice in the peace and prosperity of the age.
Whether liberation has been attained or not remains uncertain. One only knows that affairs pass before one’s eyes, yet fails to realize that old age creeps upon one from the head.
Master Yuejiang Yin ascended the hall on the occasion of the Green Sprouts Festival and said: "It is easy for the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita to sell his heart and liver to study Prajñāpāramitā;
it is difficult to break open a single mote of dust to reveal the Great Sūtra. To break open a single mote of dust and reveal the Great Sūtra—"
Rolling it up is easy; to condense the *Mahāsāhasrapramardana Sūtra* into a single minute speck of dust is difficult.
A handful of water can swell into waves that surge to the heavens; a single basketful of earth can form a mountain nine *zhang* high. It is neither easy nor difficult:
the green mountains always accompany the white clouds in their leisure.
Chan Master Wumen Can, while reading the *Qingmiao Jing* (Sutra of the Green Sprouts) and expressing thanks to the Head Seat, ascended the hall and said:

"The essential teachings spoken by all Buddhas are like rice, hemp, millet, and grain. If one can chew through even a single character or a single phrase, one will forever be free from hunger and emptiness, and its utility will never be exhausted.
Such words as these, since I have encountered superior people at Kaixian, I must also bring forth and display. He then spread out his arms.
Shouyun said: "This morning is precisely the first day of the sixth month.
Chan Master Liaoyuan Yu is presiding over the assembly to ascend the hall. For two or three days in the mountains, the Green Sprout Assembly (Qingmiao Hui) has been inaugurated.
Whether with eyes open or closed, all is the ocean of Dharma-nature. The Three Worthies certainly do not know it; how could the Ten Sages have ever realized it? Only..."
There are presiding deities of the harvest who have realized this great samādhi; each, riding upon the power of their original vows, universally responds to the realm of sentient beings.
As long as the realm of sentient beings is inexhaustible, these vows shall never falter. I bow my head to the Teacher Vairocana; I pay homage to Avalokiteśvara.

Chan Master Hongjue Wen hung up the bell and board; standing upright without any dependence, he manifested within a state where horizontal and vertical movements are utterly severed from conventional expediency.
In his expansion and contraction, his shifting transformations were the wondrous, natural measure of transformation; in movement and stillness, he revealed the root and sprout of the Dharma King.
Thus, when he held fast, the scorching sun turned to frost and the four oceans were drained of water; when he let go, the cold...
The ice-flames have burst forth and the great earth is suddenly bathed in spring warmth. This is precisely the present day.

Setting aside for a moment the fact that he holds the scales of the Buddhas and Patriarchs high above gods and men—how would you express this single phrase of establishing new rules and issuing new decrees? He then struck once and said:
A clap of thunder resounds through the universe; the heart-flower blooms everywhere in the spring of Shaolin.
When Chan Master Shiyufang of Baoshou hangs the bell and sounding board, he follows the old regulations: "Let the plum blossoms bloom all night long.
Yet with his new decrees, he allows not even a traveler to carry away the spring. Even those with copper heads and iron jaws—upon reaching this point, what can they do?

"It must be forged again. "Whether it be a dragon soaring or a tiger galloping, there is no hindrance to following the teachings and practicing them. Now there is a secret mantra; who will join in its chanting?
After a long silence, he said, "If there is none, then I shall trouble the two Senior Monks to go. Thereupon, he struck the bell and the wooden board.
Hanging the Wooden Fish:
Master Wuguan of Liangshan ascends the hall and hangs the wooden fish. It is not like a fish; it is not like a sea-sprite.
It pierces through empty space. A handle is added to the alms bowl. Starving, one encounters the royal banquet yet cannot eat; at the gates of the Kingdom of Fragrance, he issues his commands.
He gave a shout and said, "Riding backward along the corridors day after day; with one leap through the Gate of Yu, the wind and waves rise high.
He struck his staff once and said, "Watch your eyebrows! Then he descended from the seat.
**The Method for Making Drums** Chan Master Baiyun Yan ascended the hall to speak on the method for newly tanning a dharma drum: "Many years of stubborn hide do not resound when struck;

As soon as the new hide moves, it thunders like a celestial peal. If there is no obstruction, do not say it merely follows the momentum; When there is sound, who would claim it does not come from the uneven? How!
Thus it is. With both eyes one does not hear; with both ears one does not see. Upon this single, level road, who lacks the skillful means?
On the first day of the year, Chan Master Dahui Gaoming ascended the hall to strike the newly stretched Dharma drum. Striking the new drum on the New Year, he universally bestows [the Dharma].
The new rain of the Dharma falls; all things are renewed. Each and every one conforms to the standard. The Great Being Samantabhadra rejoices;
seizing the opportune moment, he opens the gate and releases the White Elephant King, who vanishes across the earth with no trace to be found. [The Master] picks up his staff and says:
Only this one thing does not belong to the old or the new. Casually opening the mouth, one swallows the Dharmakāya. [The Master] throws it down and says:
"What is this? Within a thousand-year peach pit, there is still the original kernel."
Chan Master Shuzhong Yun ascended the hall to beat the newly tanned Dharma drum. He simply dismissed them as they were; it was already three *ke* late.
Why further point east and draw west, speaking of yellow and describing black? Those with clear eyes will surely grit their teeth.

Nevertheless, when there is a handle, grasp it; when there is none, follow the precedent. Have you not seen how Yanguan addressed the assembly, saying: "Take empty space as the drum, and Mount Sumeru..."
[It is used] as a mallet. What kind of person beats it? [The mallet] is buried deep in the ground. Nanquan said, "Master Wang does not beat this broken drum;
this is a case of essence recognizing essence. Fayen Bie said, "Master Wang does not beat it; he is whetting his axe at the gate of Master Ban. Lingyan has newly stretched the Dharma-drum:
it uses wood for its body and leather for its face. When one wishes to beat it, one beats it; when one wishes to cease, one ceases.
Rest! There is no need for all this fuss. It simply must not be heard. To hear it is to lose one's body and life.
But who is it that loses their body and life? The rotting straw sandals beneath the bed; the bald broom made of reeds at the base of the fence.
Chan Master Tianzhen strikes the Dharma drum and ascends the hall: "This drum resounds like thunder and hangs like the sun and moon.

Struck and moved within the land of Zhendan, it is preached universally throughout the Tuṣita Heaven Palace. It preaches in every atom and in every world-realm, preaching the Way with blazing intensity.
Eight-armed Nātha smashes the Imperial Bell; three catties of iron behind the Diamond King’s head. The sea-gate is cut off."
Beyond the threshold lies heaven and earth; yet I laugh at Heyshan for leaking it so easily. From now on, the springs and rocks shall increase in brilliance, and all shall be filled with joy.
*Qie qie qie!* Every single one has heard it fully and penetrated through. [With the whisk, he strikes the air and says: *Dong dong dong!*
